The crystals created within us a new need, a new hunger. An insatiable craving for more crystals. But it's a vicious cycle, the more we acquire, the more we crave.
Soon there's nothing left but the aching need for crystal shards. You can see now why most of my brethren are mad. Consumed utterly by their hunger for the crystals.
But not you?
Ha ha. Oh I crave the crystals. You have no idea how badly I crave them. Each minute is a struggle. Each thought is laced with desperate desire for more of them.
But I resist. I remember what I...what we... once were and I use that knowledge to hold on. But I am slipping and it just takes one moment of weakness to fall forever.
What are the crystals?
Simultaneously they are our salvation and our doom. They were natural growths on Tarddiad. We used them in our tools and architecture.
But it wasn't until Seren came that we saw their true potential. Seren was a beautiful goddess of crystal and these crystals resonated with her.
Her songs, and ours, caused these crystals to absorb the tiniest sliver of her nature. Her essence, if you will.
Not enough to cause her harm, or even for her to notice, but just enough to be special. They contain just enough essence to hold back the Sickness as well.
Though not enough to it off completely. But you can clearly see the profound side effects that they have on us physically, though the mental effect is far worse.
Can I help them?
Perhaps Player, perhaps. The crystals that we crave can also be our salvation. If I can slowly them off the crystals, then they might become as cognisant as I.
Perhaps then, helping one another, we might help each other to find an alternative to these crystals.

o: Perhaps the elves on Gielinor can help.

pages.x: Perhaps the elves on Gielinor can help.
We would look like monsters to them and what could they do but watch us suffer? No, let us not create feelings of guilt for them or curse my kind with pity.
Perhaps in time our people can reunite, but that time is not yet here.
I could gather more crystals. I need to gather them for the elves back in Gielinor anyway.
Yes, that would help. I could ration them and help my brethren get back on their feet.
Will you be able to resist the temptation to use them yourself?
Honestly I could not say. But I have resisted this long, with a clear goal in mind I believe I can prevail.

o: Perhaps the elves on Gielinor can help.

pages.x: Tell me about Tarddiad.
What would you know?

o: What happened to the elven civilisation?
What was the religion before Seren?

pages.x: What happened to the elven civilisation?
When Seren left us and took the majority of our people with her, what remained was barely enough to maintain a civilisation.
We drew inwards, becoming a number of small communities rather than the great cities of old. But without her light to guide us and to protect us, we became sick.
Then we found the crystals. We began to care less about maintaining our society and more and more focused on simply finding more crystals.
Soon there weren't even villages, we became wanderers. Nomads. Searching for the next source of crystals.
What are these crystal growths?
Yes I heard your Gielinor did not have them. But to us they are as natural as the trees and rocks. They have always been part of my world.
What was the religion before Seren?
Do you know, I have no idea. I suppose it just stopped being relevant. I'm not even sure we had religion before her.
We worked with the land, venerating what was, rather than the intangible.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Run faster! Faster!
Excuse me?
Oh, sorry, I didn't notice you there.
I take it you're a coach?
That I am. Now get to the point, I'm very busy!

o: What's the History of Gnome ball?

pages.x: What's the history of Gnome ball?
Be more precise, stranger.

o: What is the ball made from?

pages.x: How did it all start?
Strangely enough, by accident.
Accident?
Don't interrupt!
Sorry.
A great many years ago, before I was even born, there were two young Gnomes. Brothers to be exact.
They were always arguing with each other over the most trivial things - who was the faster runner or who was the tallest.
One day they were up at the swamp throwing stones at the toads.
As you do.
Yep. You know nothing tastes better than toasted toad?
Anyway, they decided to compete to see who could kill the most toads. This gradually became a daily game, to which they invited friends and family to join in.
It all evolved from there.
Creating a playing arena, making up teams and leagues.
Interesting.
Anything else?
What is the ball made from?
Toads of course
Toads?
What with the swamp nearby, and their robust skin, there is nothing better to stretch over some common sand.
I'd never have guessed.
Well, of course. You humans know nothing! Anything else?
Those nets are strange.
Ah, made from the finest thread in all the land.
And that is?
Gnome hair.
You're kidding, right?
I have no time for jokes. It's a serious matter, we go through plenty of nets every day.
So that's why you don't see many Gnomes with long hair?
Exactly.
The world makes sense at last.
Anything else?
Are there any special tactics?
Well of course, like what?
How about passing?
There's the good old one-two tactic.
And that is?
You don't know anything do you? You pass the ball onto a team mate, giving him all the attention of your opposition, and giving you the chance to run further ahead.
Then what?
Well, he passes back to you and you've made an advantage. It's useful in a variety of situations!
I'll remember that one.
Anything else?
How about teamwork?
Well, don't forget that you can block the opposition whilst a team mate has the ball. Very useful if you want to stop or slow down anyone approaching him.
Block for team mates. Got it.
Anything else?
What about my personal physique?
You'd look better if you were shorter.
I mean in regards to scoring more goals!
I see. Your agility is important if you want to avoid being tackled, so that would be a good attribute to improve.
Also many Gnomes say that being able to attack well with a ranged weapon makes you better at scoring goals.
I suppose I should go away and work on those skills.
Yes, although playing the game itself will improve these skills too.
Also you should remember that your distance from the goal affects your chance of scoring, so get close enough and your ranged ability won't matter as much.
Any information would be appreciated!
Hmm, some general facts?
Please!
OK. Have you noticed the different colour clothes for your opposing Gnomes?
Nope.
The colours correspond to their skill level. The red ones are the professionals. They've been playing since before you were born!
The orange ones are in the middle of their careers, whereas the yellow players know very little. Just like you!
Thanks... Anything else?
It's always good to get a group of friends to play with you.
That way you can score goals more easily, and if you take it in turns to score the goals you'll all reap the rewards.
Does the game bring fame?
You mean you've never heard of Speedy Sam The Striker or Norda 'Steal Arms' van Druman?
Afraid not.
Not even Great Thunder Legs MacKnee?
Nope.
Well, they're all richer than you'll ever be!
Good for them.
Indeed, anything else?
Yawn.
I beg your pardon?
Erm... thanks, catch you later.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hey, yooman, what you wanting?

o: So, what's Summoning all about, then?
Can I buy some summoning supplies?
Are you interested in buying pouches or scrolls?

pages.x: Whatchoo talkin' about, yooman?
Yes, I think so.
I gots da pouches and spirit shards, but no charms. Yooman gotta get dem himself. Yooman just gets a club and yooman goes whackin' things till monsters drop charms.
Der'es loads of things that gots charms. Dere is loads of charms all over da place, gold, blue, green, crimson...even some real rare ones like obsidy-un charms as well.
I'll be sure to keep my eyes open for them.
If yooman wants to learn Summonin' good, den yooman needs to make da Summonin' pouches.
Yooman also gets learnin' from da Summonin' and da scrolls and da splittin' Summonin' pouches. Da Summonin' pouches is da bestest way of learnin' of them all.
Yooman got it, or yooman stoopid?
Sure!
Hah! Yooman is smart for a little ting! Da last ting is da pets. Da more summony you is, da more you understand der birds and der bees and der rocks and stuff.
Der bigger yooman's summonyness is, da stronger der pets yooman will be able to keep. Real big summoners gets to raise animals like lizard tings, including dragons!
Now if yooman's brains isn't gonna pop, does it wanna know about somefin' else?
Summoned familiars are da main ting in Summonin', as if yooman didn't be guessing. There's all kinds of tings yooman can summon.
Der bigger der yooman's summonyness, der bigger der tings yooman can summon. Ting is, dem familiars not really, REALLY animals, if yer get me.
Dey are really REALLY spirits dat are stronger than der real animal, wiv all kinds of powaz dat der rest don't.
Dat's why dey are not runnin' around all da time - it's cos der summoner puts dere Summonin' skill points inta summonin' em, and keeping em here.
So Summoning skill points are like food to dem - sorry, them?
Yah! Dat's right! Der bigger der ting, der more ya gotta feed it, and der more often it gets hungry.
Dat's why only der big summony types, like me, have enough Summonin' skill points for der biggest familiars.
And der bigger der yooman's Summonin' level, der easier it is to be feedin' der littler tings for longer.
I'm starting to get a little hungry now.
It's like if yooman be holdin' bags of wheat. Der bigger der bags yooman be holdin', der bigger der yooman's arms get, so de bigger bags dey can hold next time.
If da youman feeds a little ting den dey will have lots of wheat left over too!
Great! So, what can these familiars do?
What can dey not do, more like? Dere is a load of dem - tons, lots and lots - and each of dem is not like der uvvers.
Well, can you give me some hints, then?
Well, Bogrog only calls on der ones dat fight! Dey hang around until Bogrog be fightin' and den dey leap in!
I suppose yooman like you will be wantin' the ones that just make yooman more skilful, or dem ones dat lug around tings dat yooman's arms too puny to lift.
Amazing!
Now, if yooman's brains isn't gonna pop, does it wanna know about someting else?
If you cuts up one of dem Summonin' pouches, over at der obelisk, den da energy gets mushed up real good, transformin' into a big stack of scrolls.
Dese scrolls can den be used to make da familiars do a speshial move! Hur, hur, hur!
Der spirit wolfies, fer example, dey can make little tings run away real good if dey perform dere Howl speshial move.
Or longer, in the case of that giant wolpertinger!
Hur hur hur, me hearing about dat from da spirities!
Yooman can't mix up der scrolls, though - spirit wolfies get real growly if ya try to make 'em perform dreadfowl speshial move!
So, what sort of special moves are there?
Dere is lots of dem - like da familiars!
If yooman's confoosed, den just think of dis; the attackin' familiars got a lot more of der attackin' speshial moves, and der soppy, non-attackin' ones gots da non-attackin' speshial moves.
Yooman will want da non-attackin' ones to heal dem, or get dem stuff, or make dem better at uvver tings.
Are the special moves and the familiar's normal abilities similar?
Naah, dem's mostly diff'rent. Da spirit wolfies' are sim'lar though. Dey's got da Howl speshial move, but dey's also got a howly normal ability.
You can get der spirit wolfy to use Howl on anyt'ing you see, but it can only uses its howly normal ability on tings you is fightin'.
If der familiar with the normal ability is fighting with a yooman, den it makes der normal ability when it sees an openin'.
Der speshial moves though - dey never use dem unless yooman tells 'em to wiv a scroll.
I see. Thanks for the information!
Now, if yooman's brains isn't gonna pop, does it wanna know about somefin' else?
Der petties? Well dey's not real summony stuffs, but if yooman trains hard, then yooman gets to be friends wiv dem.
Der summonier der yooman gets, der more like nature der yooman gets, so da little petties like yooman better.
So, der petties dat would be runnin' away don't, and even der nasty petties get real quiet too.
An' when dey not runnin' or bitin', den da yooman gets ta feed 'em and pet 'em and keep 'em.
So what will I need to do to raise the animals?
Dey just walk behind da yooman, so yooman just gives dem food, more food and good foods. Da bestest summoners wants to pet themse'ves a dragon!
Wow! Imagine riding around on a dragon, and fighting with it!
Yooman is too stoopid.
What?
One, you too puny to make a dragon do as you sez. Two, when yooman gets a pet, yooman remembers it's still alive, an' yooman's friend.
Pets are not like der spirity familiars - dey die if you kills dem! What friend pokes his friend in der head and says 'We go fight now.
I gets on your back and you fights for me'?
I didn't realise.
Dat's 'cos yooman's stoopid. Petties not toys or clubs, or ridy-tings. Dey is livin' tings dat yooman be raisin' from birthyness. If you a bad, petty yooman, I club you!
I'll take good care of them.
Now, if yooman's brains isn't gonna pop, does it wanna know about somefin' else?
Can I buy some summoning supplies, please?
Hur, hur, hur! Yooman's gotta buy lotsa stuff if yooman wants ta train good!
Are you interested in buying pouches or scrolls?
Des other ogres's stealin' Bogrog's stock. Gimmie pouches and scrolls and yooman gets da shardies.
Ok.

conversations.section: In Canifis

pages.x: Hello there!
Greetings traveller. Welcome to 'The Hair Of the Dog' Tavern. What can I do you for?
Can I buy a beer?
Well that's my speciality! The local brew's named 'Moonlight Mead' and will set you back 5 gold. Whaddya say? Fancy a pint?
Yes please.
Actually, no thanks.
Eh, suit yourself. You're missing out on a genuine taste experience.
Can I hear some gossip?
Well, I dunno... The village is kind of on the fringe out here, I dunno how up to date the stuff I hear about is...

o: Tell me about the land of Morytania.
Tell me about the shopkeepers here.
Tell me about the temple to the West.

pages.x: You want to know about Canifis? I dunno why, not a lot happens here. We're just your typical everyday down at earth werewolf folk, after all...
So... everyone here is a werewolf?
Yep. We are as Zamorak made us!
You mentioned Zamorak...
Tell me about the land of Morytania.
Tell me about the shopkeepers here.
Hmmm? Why, who did you want to hear the gossip about?
Tell me what you know about Sbott the Tanner.
Hey, I won't hear a word said bad about that guy! He's an honest and hard-working wolf if I ever met one!
He charges a lot for his job, but he's one of the best tanners I've ever seen - and I'm over four hundred years old! You
need stuff tanning, I recommend him!
Know anything interesting about Rufus the food seller?
Ah yeah... good old Rufus...
He's kind of getting on in years and doesn't like to come out of his wolf form so often, but let me tell you this: that guy is a hunter through and through.
You seen how much food he catches in a day? That
takes real dedication!
Some of the young pups think that just because a wolf has a bit of grey in his fur then he's past it, but I've seen him put those pups to shame in a hunt!
He's a real inspiration to us all!
Got anything to share about Barker the clothes seller?
Eh, I don't like the guy much, but you can't knock the quality of his stock. They're some fine quality threads that you can get yourself there.
What's wrong with him?
Eh... I can't really tell you to be honest. Something about the guy just gets my hackles up everything he opens his yap, know what I mean?
No, not really.
Lucky for you. I can't really explain it, I just don't like the guy. Does great clothes though, you got to give him that.
I bet you have some juicy gossip about Fidelio the general store owner.
That nut job? Oh sure, we all know about him. He was a real firebrand daredevil when he was much younger, always taking risks to make himself a quick buck...
he got himself caught up in the smuggling trade, sneaking over the
border into Misthalin and pretending to be a human so he could buy exotic items to sell.
Exotic items? From Misthalin? Like what?
Oh man, you name it! Flour... buckets... tinderboxes... chisels... he could get the lot! He's been doing it so long now though, his nerves are shot.
Nowadays he's a disgrace, he can barely string a sentence together and jumps at his own shadow. Makes you feel ashamed to be a werewolf.
Tell me about the temple to the west.
Well, I'm not old enough to remember the full story behind it, but it was a terrible day for our kingdom when it was built there.

Apparently Morytania had a once strong kingdom, with lands spreading far further west than they do today, and south into the desert, until the day when a sneak attack by the hated human forces who worship Saradomin burned
our villages and slaughtered our peoples in mass.
They then cursed the river, so that it would burn our kind should we touch it! Can you imagine? To make an entire river poisonous to us?
So you hate humans too?
Absolutely! If I ever met one I would gobble him up where he stands! And then chew the bones for dessert!
Um, okay, thanks, bye.
Can I hear a story?
A story? Heh, well the only one I can think of right now is the one my dear old mammy told me as a pup...
Now how did it go... Ah yes!
Once upon a time a brave young wolf was walking through a forest, when he came upon a human dressed all in red.
'Aha!' he thought to himself, 'Here's a nice easy meal!' But the human talked to him, and he was always taught to
be a polite wolf, he spoke back to it.
Well, this cunning human told him that there was a better meal that would not run away in the house in the woods.
As the brave young wolf could see that this human was not fully grown, he figured maybe he'd better get a better
meal at this house, so he ran as fast as his paws could carry him to the house the human told him about...
inside he found an old human lying in bed, and although she was a little tough, as the human was older than he
thought, he had a good meal and decided to sleep it off in the house for awhile. He had not been asleep long though, when he was woken by a knocking at the door.
The human in red had followed him to the house! Suspecting a human
trap, the brave young wolf put on the old humans clothes and jumped into the bed, so that he could pretend to be human and escape from this terrible trap!
Well now, this human dressed in red came into the house, and pretended
to believe the brave wolf was really a human, and began to talk to him.
But then the human started asking strange questions of the wolf, because the human knew that it was not a human at all! The brave young wolf decided to
try and escape, for it was only a young human, and not very strong, so the brave young wolf said he would eat the human if they did not let him escape!
As he said this however, the human in red shouted at him: 'Aha! You
are a wolf!' and as the human shouted this another bigger human ran into the room from outside!
This bigger human was much stronger and was carrying an axe, and the poor young wolf died in this terrible trap made for him by the
humans.
And do you know what the moral of this story is?
Um... no, not really.
It's 'Never trust humans' of course! My dear old mammy told me that story when I was a pup, and I'm still alive and well to tell it you today!
Pretty good story huh?
Um... yeah. It was great. Really.
Nothing thanks.
...I don't know why you talked to me if you don't want anything then...

conversations.section: After Contact!

pages.x: Hello, Jex.
Hello, Player.
Jex rubs his head tenderly.

o: Could you tell me more about the minor gods?
Why is your temple still in such a state?

pages.x: Are you okay?
Some degenerate clubbed me and gave me a lump the size of an egg on the back of my head.
I'll keep my eyes peeled for suspicious characters.
I have a fairly good idea who did it.
Who?
That linen merchant, Siamun; she's never liked me.
I'll keep an eye out for her.
Could you tell me more about the minor gods?

o: Could you tell me more about Scabaras?
Could you tell me more about Het?
Could you tell me more about Crondis?
Could you tell me more about Apmeken?

pages.x: Could you tell me more about Scabaras?
I think you'll have gathered most of the relevant details from elsewhere, but general knowledge isn't always the most accurate.
Are you claiming I've been misinformed?
Not really; there are simply details of Scabaras's fall from grace that are only known to we priests.
Such as?
Some of his supposed faults can be forgiven. I just can't explain why at the moment.
I'm not sure whether I should thank you for that bit of confusion or add to that bump on your head.
Could you tell me more about the minor gods?
Could you tell me more about Het?
Het is the least strange looking of our deities to foreign eyes; he looks just like us.
I suspect this is why his shrines are particularly targeted by the infamous Templeton.
What does his patronage cover?
He is the very incarnation of health and strength in both mind and body.

o: Could you tell me more about Het's influence over the desert?
Could you tell me more about Het's followers?
Could you tell me more about the minor gods?

pages.x: Could you tell me more about Het's influence over the desert?
When I was young, I thought of Het as a strong virtuous knight: brave, daring, and, perhaps, just a little dim.
Sounds like every knight I've ever known.
But, as I grow older, I'm not so sure.
It is clear that Het's influence is felt all over the desert; his strength can be felt on the serrated edges of the Menaphites' blades.
His nerve is in the tip of every spear wielded by the soldiers of Al Kharid.
He fortifies each steel cuff that constrains a slave. He is the very tug in the river Elid that drags many to their deaths.
Yet, we have enfeebled slaves and weakened villages. Even in this very city there is a plague sapping us of our strength.
So, you feel that Het has turned his back on your people?
No, I wouldn't say that. We mortals are too quick to blame our problems on the gods. Without weakness there is no strength, after all.
Could you tell me more about Het's followers?

Het originated in the north, so he is worshipped fervently by the people of Al Kharid; however, he is a popular god across the desert - his powerful image of strength and health make him a popular god amongst soldiers and leaders.
Could you tell me more about the minor gods?
Could you tell me more about Crondis?
Crondis is a ferocious lady with the head of a mighty crocodile.
That must be awkward when buying helmets.
Enough flippancy: remember she is a deity, and this is her place of power.
What kind of people follow her?
She embodies modesty, diligence and resourcefulness, so Crondis is worshipped by the desert's subsistence farmers and hunters.
Conversely, she proves unpopular amongst society's elite.
How so?
Crondis teaches that people should take no more than they need and make do with little, which, as you can imagine, conflicts with the values of many in the richer echelons of society.
In Menaphos, she is particularly frowned upon, although that is hardly surprising.
Why?
The Pharaoh of Menaphos is a greedy, cruel man whose lack of restraint is beyond even Crondis's help.
Excuse me, I should not have spoken that way. It is unwise to speak ill of one's betters.

o: Could you tell me more about Crondis's connection with crocodiles?
Could you tell me more about Crondis's followers?
Could you tell me more about Crondis's influence over the desert?
Could you tell me more about the minor gods?

pages.x: Could you tell me more about Crondis's connection with crocodiles?
Crondis was once a crocodile. Many people believe that those that hunt in the waters of the River Elid embody her very spirit. They were her most beloved supporters.
When I was young, people were wary of them, revered them even, but were not afraid of them. With the recent crocodile attacks, that has changed.
I'm afraid that the growing lack of restraint of the crocodiles along the River Elid is only further proof that not all is well with Crondis.
Could you tell me more about Crondis's followers?
Crondis is worshipped by those who rely upon their ingenuity to survive: sailors, engineers and rogues hold her in high regard.
Due to her popularity amongst seafarers, word of Crondis has spread far and wide and her followers can be found in a great number of exotic places.
Could you tell me more about Crondis's influence?
Crondis hopes to inspire resourcefulness and unassuming modesty. While this has always been her goal, her methods vary more than most.
I'm confused. What do you mean?
Crondis may save a struggling harvest by bursting the clouds, or she might set swarms of locusts upon a bountiful crop to stop complacency.
Could you tell me more about the minor gods?
Could you tell me more about Apmeken?
Goodbye, Jex.
Goodbye. May the gods be with you.
Why is your temple still in such a state?
The minor gods aren't particularly revered in our fine city. Icthlarin holds sway here and, although a fine deity indeed, he's not the most jolly of sorts.
I thought you were a priest of Icthlarin?
Well, yes and no. I am primarily a priest of Icthlarin, certainly, but I have been trained in the rites of the minor gods as well.
What would it take to repair this temple, then? Money? Materials? Manpower?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. Most of the natural worshippers are in Menaphos; of course, and the local economy is rather depressed.
In addition, that Templeton rogue made off with some of the damaged stonework. We should hunt him down like the jackal he is.
I'm sure you'll think of something; you'll be able to count on me when you do.
Goodbye, Jex.
Goodbye. May the gods be with you.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / With the little book o'piracy or having completed Rocking Out

pages.x: Yer standin' in me light stranger. Can I sell ye somethin' that'll make ye move?

o: Probably, let's see what you have.
That depends on if you have any cutlasses.
(If you have a broken barrelchest anchor in inventory:) I have this anchor, can you fix it?

pages.x: Probably, let's see what you have.
I doubt it.
Then move on stranger.
That depends on if you have any cutlasses.
Cutlasses! Think yer a pirate now lad?
Well, yes.
Well, I have some cutlasses.
I have Brass Hand Harry's Cutlass. Well, a load of them to be honest.
Then there's Unlucky Jenkins' Lucky Cutlass. Lovely blade that.
I've also got Gentleman Mallard's Rapier. Not a cutlass I know, but the finest blade ever wielded by a privateer.
Now, which would ye like to hear about?
Brass Hand Harry's Cutlass.
A good choice!
Ye may end up meeting Brass Hand Harry if ye hang around long enough.
He lost his right hand to a canister round, but that didn't stop him much.
Then he lost his replacement right hook fightin' the excise men off the coast of Karamja.

Not bein' the sort to lie about mopin', he asked me to make him a cutlass with a brass gauntlet fixed to the handle, and rig it up with a load of straps so he could keep on fightin' without losing his hand again.
He's a great man is Harry, but he keeps snappin' the straps while he's at sea, so he sells the cutlasses back to me in exchange for a new one.
It's quite a good blade, but the big, brass gauntlet is what makes it worthwhile.
It's big enough to fit over even a real gauntlet, so ye get extra protection to yer sword hand.
I can sell ye one fer 1,040 coins.
Interested?
Yes.
No.
Well I'll still be here if ye change yer mind.
Unlucky Jenkins' Lucky Cutlass.
Arr, tis a sad tale to this sword.
Jenkins was the lookout on the Jonah, a cursed vessel if there ever was one.
One day his ship were attacked by another group of pirates durin' a fierce storm.
One of their bowmen took a shot at the Cap'n of the vessel, but it were deflected off his compass and hit Jenkins in the back.
How unlucky!
That weren't the worst of it lad. He survived the fight, and the ship's surgeon was trying to get the arrow out when... Are ye familiar with the spell bones to bananas?
Yes, why?
Well, due to a blow to the head he took in the fight, the surgeon cast that spell, thinking it was some sort of new healing spell.
And he did so while touching Jenkins' ribs.
And that killed him?
No lad! See, he survived, his bones turned to bananas, as a huge storm blew up and the crew debated what to do with him.

But you see, the storm was actually the tail end of a hurricane that had swept the nearby jungle islands, and when it approached the ship it petered out, droppin' all manner of strange things onto the deck and into the ocean.
The worst part was when the ship was bombarded with ravenous, hunger-crazed monkeys, the majority of which landed on Jenkins as he lay recoverin'.
And that killed him?
No [lad/lass]! See, what happened next, after the monkeys had had their way with him was...
Look, I don't want to hear any more. Why would I want to buy his cutlass?
Well, after the poor man passed on...
In a final, terrifying, mashed potato coated tragedy...
His shipmates found his cutlass was completely untouched.
See, having been exposed to all the bad luck that Jenkins went through, the thing is unlikely to ever see anything that bad again.
Hence, it must be lucky.
Ye can have it fer 2560 coins.
Interested?
Yes.
No.
Well I'll still be here if ye change yer mind.
Gentleman Mallard's Rapier.
Well, I'll tell ye the story, but it'll take a great deal of convincin' for me to sell you this rapier.
See, gentleman Mallard is a legend in these parts. His family had been rich, shipping all sorts of goods up and down the coast.
Then their rivals got together and had their ships sunk, one after the other, and his business partners were all either bought off or had...accidents.
With no money and only one ship left, he took to the life of a pirate, but no brigand was he.
He took only from those men that had brought about his downfall, was fair with his men, and generous with his loot.
Why, this island would have been wiped out by the shakes if he hadn't turned over his stash to buy medicine.
One day his ship was attacked by a huge sea creature that swept the decks of men with its tentacles.
The crew took to the lifeboats, and the last they saw of him the gentleman was stabbin' at the thing as it hauled the ship under the water.
A week later about ten foot of tentacle washed up on the beach, with his rapier embedded in it to the hilt.
I took it, cleaned it up, and I've been lookin' after it ever since.
I can't let it go for less than 25600 coins, and even then that's a bargain.
Ye think ye have what it takes to wield it?
Yes.
No.
Well I'll still be here if ye change yer mind.
I have this anchor, can you fix it?
Well, this is a very unusual job. This thing looks more suited to bashin' peoples heads in than securing a ship.
Where did ye get it?
You wouldn't believe me if I told you.
Stole it eh? Well I can sort it out for 230000 coins, if you like.

conversations.section: Before The Tourist Trap

pages.x: Yeah, what do you want?
What is this place?
It's none of your business now get lost.

o: Perhaps five gold coins will make it my business?

pages.x: Perhaps five gold coins will make it my business?
Well, it certainly will help... -- The guard takes the five gold coins. -- Now then, what did you want to know?
What is this place?
It's just a mining camp. Prisoners are sent here from Al Kharid. They serve out their sentence by mining. Most prisoners will end their days here, surrounded by desert.
So you could almost say that they got their ... 'Just Desserts'
You could say that... -- There is an awkward pause -- But it wouldn't be very funny.
When they talk about 'the silence of the desert', this must be what they mean.

o: Can I take a look around the place?

pages.x: Can I take a look around the place?
Not really. The Captain won't let you in the compound. He's the only one who has the key to the gate. And if you talk to him, he'll probably just order us to kill you.
Unless...

o: Does the Captain order you to kill a lot of people?

pages.x: Does the Captain order you to kill a lot of people?
-- The guard snorts. -- *Snort* Just about anyone who talks to him. Unless he has a use for you, he'll probably just order us to kill you.
And it's such a horrible job cleaning up the mess afterwards.

o: Not to mention the senseless waste of human life.

pages.x: Not to mention the senseless waste of human life.
Huh? Them's your words, not mine.

o: It doesn't sound as if you respect your Captain much.

pages.x: It doesn't sound as if you respect your Captain much.
Well, to be honest. We think he's not exactly as brave as he makes out. But we have to follow his orders.
If someone called him a coward, or managed to trick him into a one-on-one duel many of us bet that he'd be beaten.
And how could I trick him into a one-on-one duel?
Like all cowards, he likes to be made to feel important. If anyone insults him outright, he just gets us to do his dirty work.
However, if he thinks he's better than you, if you compliment him, he may feel that he can defeat you.
And if he initiated a duel, all the men agreed that they wouldn't intervene. We think he'd be slaughtered in double quick time.

o: Can I have a bet on that?

pages.x: Can I have a bet on that?
Unless what?
Unless he has a use for you. He's been trying to track down someone called 'Al Zaba Bhasim'. You could offer to catch him and that might put you in his good books?

o: Where would I find this Al Zaba Bhasim?

pages.x: Where would I find this Al Zaba Bhasim?
Well, he could be anywhere. He's a nomadic desert dweller. However, they say that he's frequently to be found to the west in the hospitality of the Tentis.
The Tentis, who are they?
Well, we're not really sure what their proper name is, but they live in tents so we call them the 'Tentis'.

o: Is Al Zaba Bhasim very tough?

pages.x: Is Al Zaba Bhasim very tough?
Well, I'm not sure, but by all accounts, he is a slippery fellow. The Captain has been trying to capture him for years. A bit of a waste of time if you ask me.
Anyway, I have to get going, I do have work to do.
What are you guarding?
Well, if you have to know, we're making sure that no prisoners get out. -- The guard gives you a disapproving look.
-- And to make sure that unauthorised people don't get in. -- The guard looks around nervously. -- You'd better go soon before the Captain orders us to kill you.
What are you guarding?
Get lost before I chop off your head!

o: Perhaps these five gold coins will sweeten your mood?

pages.x: Okay, thanks.
Yeah, whatever!
Perhaps five gold coins will sweeten your mood?
Well, it certainly will help!

o: The guard takes the five gold coins.

pages.x: Now then, what did you want to know?
What is this place?
It's none of your business now get lost.
What are you guarding?
Get lost before I chop off your head!

conversations.section: In Prifddinas, after Plague's End

pages.x: What do you want?

o: Can we talk about items and incentives?

pages.x: Can we talk about assignments?
I suppose we can. What do you want to ask about?

o: Do you have any special assignments for me?

pages.x: About your challenge...
Hmmm. Let's see how you are progressing.

o: If you wish to concede defeat, tell me now, and I'll let you off the hook.

pages.x: I need another assignment.
Can we talk about items and incentives?
Well, which is it? Items for sale or incentives?

o: Do you have any other rewards?

pages.x: I have plenty of slayer equipment - take a look.

o: How do I earn co-op points to spend on rewards?
Where can I use the co-op food and potion rewards?

pages.x: You'll gain co-op points if you complete at least half of your contribution to a task with a friend.
That means you need to be in a group for most of the time you're working on your task, but it doesn't matter if your friend beats you to the majority of kills!
You'll still have been in a group for most of your contribution, so you're still entitled to a co-op reward point.

o: Where can I use the co-op food and potion rewards?

pages.x: The rewards can be used in most of the areas we commonly send you to complete your tasks.

o: How do I earn co-op points to spend on rewards?

pages.x: Do you have any other rewards?
For my more able students, I have a special challenge that I offer, and there are some small rewards - besides the glory - that I offer for completing it.
Each time you complete the challenge, I will pay for a free retune of the Max Guild portals - although I won't pay for more than 30 in advance.
I will also allow you to carry special black crystals which have a debilitating effect on you, to make your slaying more challenging.
What are black crystals?
Black crystals are corrupted crystals that have resisted our attempts to cleanse them. The corruption is too strong.
Like the dark crystals, they have debilitating effects when carried. Some of my braver students have taken to carrying some to make their slaying more challengeing.
I allow people to carry them only if they have proved their worth by completing my challenge.
Is there any benefit to carrying them?
There is no material reward. But, the glory! The challenge! Are these not good enough for you?
Let's talk about you.
My favourite subject. What do you want to know?

o: Tell me more about your background.
So what's in this dungeon then?

pages.x: Tell me more about your background.
I am Lord Iorwerth's nephew. The old Lord Iorwerth, that is. I was raised as a leader in our clan.
I looked up to my uncle; it was he who appointed me as our clan's Head of Intelligence.
It was my duty to amass knowledge of our enemies - their strengths and weaknesses - and how best to defeat them.
I was also in charge of interrogations and assassinations.
How did you become a slayer master?
My duties gave me cause to travel far beyond the borders of Tirannwn, though always in disguise of course.
In my travels, I made the acquaintance of a lovely young lady by the name of Kuradal.
She taught me much about the wider world, and I her about the many mysteries of this world closed off to her.
She is a remarkable woman. I found myself fascinated by her and what she does, and so I decided to turn my talents and knowledge towards slaying.
We have to find our place again among the other clans. Some of us still begrudge how things played out, but I intend to embrace this change.
My own knowledge of slaying has now surpassed even Kuradal's...theoretically speaking, of course. She is more suited to practical application...
Only theoretically?
Oh, I could easily kill any beast if I so desired. I've certainly done plenty of it in my time...but there are always others willing to do the dirty work.
I prefer to watch these days - to study and learn.
Despite what you may think of the Iorwerth, I feel there has been enough blood spilled during the civil war.
I have always preferred to only kill when absolutely necessary.
About Clan Iorwerth...
Look, I was never a fan of that whole Dark Lord business. I have my own interests, and I am still able to indulge them.
But as an Iorwerth, I am duty-bound to my lord. We take duty seriously, something the other clans are less concerned over.
So you were just following orders? Like that's a justification.
I cannot speak for the actions of others, but I always ensured that my own actions - my orders - were just.
Within any war, each individual must draw their own lines. I can hold my head high knowing I remained true to my beliefs.
Weren't you an assassin and interrogator?
Wars require both. All of my targets were of military value, never civilians or innocents, and I never once resorted to the use of torture.
Again, I can only be held accountable for my own actions, not those of others.
Do you think a massacre is justifiable?
No, of course not, and I am glad that you put a stop to it.
Don't paint all Iorwerth with the same brush simply due to the actions of my uncle.
He was wrong, that much is clear, and we must now find a way to once more live among our brethren.
There is need of someone such as I to ensure the safety of all the clans, the Clan Iorwerth needs a leader with a more... palatable outlook.
This is why I have waived my right of lordship over to lestin. He is an unconventional choice, but a necessary one.
Some of the older Iorwerth diehards are having a hard time accepting him, but I will keep them in line.
They respect me, and for as long as I support Iestin, they will follow his lead, or they will not be welcome here.
So what's in this dungeon then?
Since the regrowing of Prifddinas, I've tasked the lovely Kuradal to supply me with creatures for my...collection.
To what end?
A challenge, but only for the most elite of slayers!
Can I go in there?
Is that all?
Can I use your dungeon?
Er...nothing...
