conversations.section: In Prifddinas

pages.x: Greetings Player, it is good to see you again. I suppose you have many questions.
Tell me about yourself.
What would you like to know?

o: I hear you can do powerful magic.
I'd like to ask about something else.

pages.x: What was elven royalty like?
It was a society born in haste, from Seren's destruction. Glarial and I took the throne after Seren's shattering.
The elves needed a ruler and the two of us were the most experienced.
To alleviate tensions between the clans, we elevated several elves from various clans to roles as advisors and administrators.
From these would come the first of the elven aristocracy.
As is common with positions of powr, many let their status get to their heads and acted with prejudice to those of 'lower class'.
Something that gave the Iorwerth a platform on which to seed their dissent.
It is easy to point those with little at those with great wealth and say 'this is why you suffer'. In many ways the uprising was inevitable.
Iorwerth merely spearheaded it.
I hear you can do powerful magic.
Yes. I know spells that can move mountains, or summon the trees to fight as an army. But this is not magic I will teach.
Why not?
Because such force could disrupt the balance of power in the world. It could create tyrants and topple kingdoms.
It is magic intended to make the world a better place, but the world is not ready for such change yet. Perhaps in time.
What will you do now?
I will remain here, in Prifddinas. Perhaps a time will come again where I can be useful.
Tell me about Glarial.
She was radiant, both in beauty and in temperament. I loved her from the moment I saw her. A terrible cliche ... perhaps fitting for a king. We courted for a full decade.
I showed her parts of the world that no other elf had been. I taught her the ancient magic, and she was a quick study. I thought that we might change the world together.
But then I left on that foolish crusade. I wanted to see the world and found a new glorious city.
My arrogance and hubris gave the Iorwerth their opening and from there I lost everything. ... I would burn the world to ash for just a few more moments with her ...
Ask me something else Player. Don't make me dwell on what could have been.
Tell me about elven history.
Is there anything that you do not know?

o: Tell me about the elven expansion.
Tell me about the Iorwerth uprising.

pages.x: What happened after Seren shattered?
Our civilisation fell into chaos. Understand that we were utterly devoted to Seren. Our entire culture revolved around her words of wisdom.
Without her guidance there was panic. The streets were filled with terrified people unsure of what to do.
My beloved Glarial, always the voice of reason, encouraged me to take control of the situation.
The Cadarn warriors helped to police the city, establishing order and Glarial and I spoke to the people.
It was not a swift thing, of course, but between us we brought order to chaos. From then we worked on what was needed and we tried to figure out what we should do next.
Without Seren's words to guide us wer were lost. We turned to each problem one at a time, never seeing the big picture.
It was Glarial who saw the wider vision and helped us to pull our society back together. For a while we returned to peace.
But our city was so magnificent, our culture so strong, that we could not limit ourselves to a single region. It was then that we looked to expand the elven lands.
Tell me about the elven expansion.
We had just done the impossible. We had rebuilt our civilsation after Seren had shattered herself.
As a nation we felt unstoppable and so we decided to expand our civilisation beyond the single city.
We spread our civilisation out across Kandarin and even into Misthalin. Such was our confidence. We forged lasting alliances with several races.
Our old friends the gnomes were first. It had been so long since we had seen each other that we held a great feast lasting a full week.
With the gnomes help we forged treaties with the human tribes dotted around the region. They were wary of us, but peace is preferable to war and so we flourished.
The goblins and ogres were less willing to agree to peace. They were so locked into their own civil wars. Still, they were no match for us, so we ignored them.
We prospered for a long time. I was genuinely proud of our accomplishments ... then Tirannwn sell silent.
Tell me about the Iorwerth uprising.
It began with silence. Tirannwn, the heart of our empire, could not be reached. I sent messengers, both elven and animal.
I summoned powerful scrying spells to see what was happening... but there was nothing but darkness.
We of course knew that something was afoot and I sent five of my best scouts to investigate. Only one returned, but he was able to tell me of Iorwerth's treachery.
Prifddinas had fallen. The Iorwerth had seized absolute control, by some terrible power. Glarial and I knew we could not let this stand.
So I rallied our warrios and mages behind us and left for Prifddinas. Thought it broke my heart to leave her behind. We were so arrogant.
We thought our knowledge of magic might be enough, but with the clans behind us how could we be stopped?
Had we known that Iorwerth would be wielding the power of Seren, twisted as it was in the form of the Dark Lord, we might have been less confident.
Shadows assaulted us and darkness blinded our archers. The Lord Iorwerth laughed as our unprepared forces were torn apart. But our will could not be broken.
We withdrew and we lay siege to the city. A long protracted war.
Somehow the walls withstood my magic, as if some dark force just drained the magic right out of my spells as they approached. We fought and we fought ...
but in the end we knew that we had failed. The Iorwerth had won. We withdrew back to the east ... but found only ruin.
The Iorwerth, not only able to hold off a five year siege, had destroyed everything else we had built.
They had rallied the goblins and ogres against our defenceless cities. They had bribed weak-willed human armies to turn on us.
And amongst all of that sadness I lost all hope and all will to fight ... because she was gone.

o: Tell me about when you went to the falls.
I'd like to talk about something else.

pages.x: Tell me about when you went to the falls.
At first I went there to end it all. My grief was so strong that I could not bear it. But I still had that most painful of afflictions... I still had hope.
Hope that one day, Glarial and I might be reunited. So, I hid the shard, that was mine to ward, in a statue of my beloved and then I transformed.
It is an ancient spell, intended to imprison my enemies, but I was my own worst enemy. Once the spell was complete I was just crystal and then I waited.

o: What do you think of Seren.
What do you think of the current elves?

pages.x: What do you think of the current elves?
They have achieved much. The new society is as strong as we ever were. Even the Iorwerth seem to have redeemed themselves.
Do you intend to retake the crown?
No. No. My time as king is over. I shall advise and I shall serve, but I shall no longer rule.

conversations.section: In Varrock / Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello! I'm Ernie the urn collector!
Hello, I'm Player.
Do you have any urns?

o: Why would I want to give you any urns?
I'd like to ask some other questions.

pages.x: What are urns?
You don't know what an urn is? Inconceivable!
Urns are big, magical pots. You keep them in your bag, and they collect scraps and wastage while you perform activities that are related to that urn.
For example, a fishing urn collects guppies while your attention is on larger catches.
Once it's full, you can teleport the urn to me!
Sweet little guppies...
Why would I want to give you any urns?
Why wouldn't you, more to the point?
No, why would I want to send you my full urns?
Oh...for a reward, of course!
You see, I've seen a lot in my lifetime; I have some tricks of the trade to share with you.
You send me an urn, I reward you with know-how regarding the skill type of your urn. Some might call it...gaining experience.
That's a strange way to phrase it.
How do I make urns?
Oh, just use some soft clay on the pottery wheel and then fire the results in the pottery oven downstairs. Urns are big, so you'll need two batches of clay per urn.
Before you can start gathering scraps in your urn, you must attach a rune to it. This dissipates when you teleport the urn to me.
Then I gather the precious, wonderful materials.
If you get stuck, just show me where you've got to and I'll give you some advice. You can also hand full urns to me in person, if you'd prefer.

o: I'd like more information about a specific urn.

pages.x: Why do you want urns?
Why? WHY?
Yes. Why?
Oh, I...couldn't possibly say.
I'm sure you could tell me.
No, no. It's a secret, tasty experiment. You must never know.
I'd like more information about a specific urn.
Certainly. I am a bit of an expert, after all.
Prayer urns scoop up the ashes left behind when you slay demonic creatures.
Weaker demons leave impious ashes behind. Scarier demonic beasties leave accursed ashes, and the most dangerous demons leave infernal ashes. Scrum-diddly-umptious.
With lower Crafting levels, you are able to create impious urns, which collect impious ashes.
Get your skill level up and you'll be able to make urns that collect a smorgasbord of ash types.
Ah, fishing urns! These collect my favourite little fish: guppies!
All you need to do is keep the urn in your bag when you are fishing, and it'll gather up the delicious little guppies each time you make a catch.
Cracked fishing urns, made with lower Crafting levels, only collect guppies when fishing at level 10 or below.
Higher level urns collect the brave guppies that swim around higher level fish.
When you are a master crafter, you will be able to make decorated fishing urns. These collect guppies from any kind of fish that you can think of!
Cooking urns collect lip-smacking food scraps while you are cooking on a fire or range.
Cracked cooking urns, made with lower Crafting levels, collect food scraps from meals that require a Cooking level of 10 or below.
Decorated cooking urns, made at the very highest Crafting levels, collect scraps from even the most complex of meals. These scraps are integral to my experiment!
Experiment?
Who told you about my experiment? Whatever you've heard is a lie!
Magical mining urns! These collect slivers of ore from the rocks you mine.
Cracked urns, made at the lower end of the Crafting scale, will magnetically attract slivers of ore that require a Mining level of 1.
Higher quality urns collect slivers of ore from higher level ores.
When you're skilled enough to make decorated mining urns, you'll gather slivers from any ore that you could swing a pickaxe at!
Smelting urns collect metal scraps while you smelt bars.
Lower level urns only collect metal scraps from bars that require a Smithing level of 1.
The highest level urns collect metal scraps from any bar, high level or low level, 'cept for chocolate bars. Trust me, I've tried.
A note to you: I prefer better quality metal scraps. They contribute a more distinctive taste to my delicious experiment.
Woodcutting urns! Wonderful things! These collect tasty woodchips when you chop wood.
While you are a crafter at lower levels, you will only be able to make cracked urns. These collect woodchips while you chop wood up to a Woodcutting level of 10.
When you are a master of the crafting art, you'll be able to make decorated woodcutting urns that collect from even the hardiest of logs.
Woodchips from magic trees make my lips tingle. I thought you'd like to know.
Wonderful divination urns! Wonderful things! These collect memory fragments.
While you are crafting at lower levels, you will only be able to make cracked urns. These collect memory fragments up to a Divination level of 10.
When you are a master of the crafting art, you'll be able to make decorated divination urns that collect from even the greatest of memories.
You might also want to know that these will collect extra special fragments when you deposit memories into a crater!
Runecrafting urns collect rune remnants when utilising rune essence.
Lower level urns will collect remnants from anything up to level 9. The highest level urns collect remnants from almost anything!

o: I have a few questions about urns in general.

pages.x: Ah hunter urns! These ones collect integument iotas from little critters.
Cracked urns, made at the lower end of the Crafting scale, will be able to collect iotas from creatures that require a Hunter level of 11.
If you manage to catch some of the big guys, you'll find my urns filling up in no time!
Farming urns collect the left over cuttings when farming.
The lowest level urns will work for anything up to level 12.
That's all, thank you.
Good bye!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello.
Hmm? Oh, pardon me, human. I was tracking the movements of warbands out in the Wilderness.

pages.i: What would you like to ask?

pages.x: Warbands are gathering under the banners of the pretender gods, looting and hoarding, and gathering like- minded brigands to their cause.
They are becoming a threat to the balance of this world, and I am sending adventurers to dispatch them.
You look pretty tough. Couldn't you deal with them yourself?
In keeping with the teachings of Guthix, I cannot intervene directly. Rather, I seek to influence events by introduction of a balancing force.
I have the Sight, which allows me to cast my gaze into the Wilderness, spotting any warbands that may be gathering.

o: Why are these warbands gathering out in the Wilderness?
pages.i: What would you like to ask?

pages.x: Recently, there seems to have been a shift in the balance. There have always been outlaws bands living in the wild lands to the north.
A nuisance at worst, but lately...something has changed.
They appear to have found faith.
Faith? Perhaps that's a good thing.
No! Not at all.
Before, they reaved and plundered - yes - but they lacked focus and discipline, and were fettered by infighting.
Now they muster in warbands: hoarding resources; training and marshalling greater forces; committing ever- worse banditry under the banners of the pretender gods.
Brigands and scoundrels still, but all the more dangerous for their renewed sense of purpose.
Men such as these may one day endanger the balance of this world, if left unchecked.
Check in with me from time to time. I shall also announce the presence of warband camps in the Wilderness worldwide.
Once I have located a warband camp, it may be assailed and the supplies in its tents seized.
So we run in and kill everyone, steal the supplies and bring them back here?
No, no. Killing is not always the best option.
Allow me to explain. On arrival, the warband will be on guard and it will not be possible to loot the supply tents.
If you can distract them, you'll gain an advantage and - potentially - additional rewards.
Interesting. Go on.
Each camp centres around a summoning beam: an unstable magical node, crudely manipulated by the warband's mages to draw allies to their cause.
If you manage to position yourself somewhere you aren't being seen - but close enough to the beam, with a clear line of sight - it should be a simple matter to shift its alignment.
Once that's done, you can use the beam again, to summon a force less...sympathetic than the warband would hope.
I see...knock the summoning beam out of whack, summon in another warband, and watch the ensuing chaos!
I prefer to think of it as balance being restored - but yes.
You will receive Prayer experience for shifting the beam, and Summoning experience for successfully summoning aid. After the battle is over, you can loot peacefully.
So I don't have to fight if I don't feel up to it?
No. If you've summoned in reinforcements they can fight for you. When the battle is over, you will be able to loot safely. It'll be quicker if you get involved though!
Never forget that avarice lurks in the hearts of all men, though, and that this is the Wilderness. Be on guard for treachery from your fellow adventurers!
So say I pull this off - I destabilise their beam, converting it to an opposing faction, then use that to summon them in, I just loot whatever I can and bring it back to you?
Yes. However, each camp will have different supplies: usually three different types from Herblore, Mining, Smithing, Construction and Farming.
You can only take 25 items before the camp is empty, but which 25 items you choose to take is up to you.
Be warned, though! Teleportation will not be possible while carrying the items. Even if you can get to the camp quickly, getting out may be a lot more dangerous.
Thanks for the information.
I am glad to help. Anything else?
Peace in balance.

o: I'd like to toggle my rewards.

pages.x: I sense turmoil and strife on the horizon, and it would behove us all to seek a balance of powers.
If you find the camps I sense and bring me back the materials they are hoarding, I shall reward you greatly.
And I can find these rewards in the Wilderness?
Correct. I can sense the camps, but cannot intervene directly. If you are willing to do so in my place, just return here with the spoils should you make it out alive.

o: Tell me about the Task System.
Can I claim any rewards from you?
Could I buy a spare of the reward?

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: For completing the Wilderness set, you are presented with Wilderness sword.
This sword will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You need to complete all the Tasks in the set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Most of the Wilderness set's Tasks are straightforward, although you might find some require quests to be
started, if not finished.
To claim the Wilderness set reward, speak to Mr Ex, Mandrith, Kolodion or myself.
Wilderness sword 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 50,000 coins.
No thanks.
Wilderness sword 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 65,000 coins.
No thanks.
Wilderness sword 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 80,000 coins.
No thanks.
Wilderness sword 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 100,000 coins.
No thanks.
Maintain the balance, Player.

conversations.section: Herblore Habitat / First time dialogue

pages.x: Heh heh heh.
Why are you laughing?
Heh heh heh. Can you not hear her joke? It not one of her best, but it's still a good one.
Whose joke are you talking about?
Why, the vine's joke, of course. Can you hear someone else round here? Perhaps you're going crazy?
Why do you refer to the vine as 'she'?
Because she is female.
How do you know? I mean...she's a plant.
Heh heh heh, she told me that she's a lady. She's telling you now, can you not hear her?
Yes I can hear her.
Oh good, ah am so glad you can hear her. She has been nagging me since you arrived. Between you an' me, she can be quite annoying at times.

o: She's telling me that you should give up all your gold coins.
I thought her joke wasn't that bad.

pages.x: She's telling me that you should give up all your gold coins.
Ah. You sadden me. I had hoped you could hear her beautiful singing, but you clearly cannot. I pay you no ill will, the loss is yours my friend.
I thought her joke wasn't that bad.
Heh heh heh, you should hear her on a full moon. She's always on top form in the moonlight.

o: I'll leave you be for now.

pages.x: Obviously not. You're clearly mad.
Oh, she talks, my friend. If only you could listen.
What is this place?
Oh, I see you have taken an interest in this little vine. I grew this vine from a root cutting of the Jade Vine to the north.
She was a little clumsy and cut me while I took it. I have since imbued the cutting with my own magic, to help make her what she is today.
She grows food for her jadinkos and extends her arms so that they can find home in her shade. And she grows different tings; each ting is nectar to one type of jadinko...
but poison to another. Encourage her to grow different combinations of plants and watch as different jadinkos are drawn into her embrace.
What would be the point of attracting different jadinkos?
Aside from the joy of seeing nature's majesty? Ah suppose you could hunt the jadinkos you attract. They have special properties you could use.
I have some special marasamaw traps that will catch them, if you have the skill. The jadinkos here are part of the vine herself. They are infused with her magic.
Once hunted, they could provide ingredients for powerful new potions, if you have the know-how.

o: So, you say that different plants attract different jadinkos?
Tell me about the potions I can make.

pages.x: What are jadinkos?
Heh heh, that is the name I's given to the strange creatures that live here. It has a nice ring to it, I's thinking.

o: So, you say that different plants attract different creatures?
Tell me about the potions I can make.

pages.x: So, you say that different plants attract different creatures?
Oh yes. The vine is home to many variations of the strange jadinkos that wander here.
Each one is attracted by different combinations of plants and environmental features.
And some can only be attracted by those who have used a special juju potion on the flowers. Drawn to the magic like a moth to a flame, they are.
Most jadinkos, they like the same ting and will always be attracted by that combination.
But there are jadinkos whose tastes are fickle and their requirements change every week or so.
These fickle creatures, when captured, give you ingredients that can enhance your mastery of this strange habitat.
They can be used to make your experience here...more rewarding... ...if you can attract 'em and catch 'em, that is.
Is there any reason to catch them all?
Heh heh heh, of course! If you are skilled enough to catch one of each jadinko type that wander 'ere, come and speak to me. I will have a reward for you.

o: Tell me about the potions I can make.

pages.x: Tell me about the potions I can make.
These potions are different from others you can create. First, they be uniquely tied to you, your essence. No other can benefit from them.
Second, they open up new ways of seeing the world and finding new rewards. Each is different and provides a special benefit.
Perhaps, most important, is the juju hunter potion you can create, for this potion will attract new creatures to this vine.
These juju potions cannot be made in a normal potion vial. They must be made in a specially created juju vial, for only they can hold the power.
Where can I get a juju vial from?
Heh heh heh. I's only one that sells them, strangely enough. Heh heh heh.

o: So, you say that different plants attract different jadinkos?

pages.x: I am Papa Mambo, shaman and protector of this vine. Once, I was the shaman of Shilo Village, and now I's a keeper of this vine.

o: Why did you leave the village?

pages.x: Heh heh heh heh heh. We did not see eye to eye on all tings. Heh heh. Some thought my studies were...unnerving.
But it always seemed such a shame leaving the dead buried, when there was such good work they could do.
I'll leave you be for now.
You may be wanting to visit the druid. He's learning about this habitat, like you, and may be able to share the knowledge he has gained. Goodbye, ma friend.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Oh hello there my
Welcome to our little plot of land on this weird little island.
My granddaughter has roped these old bones into helping expand the Potterington brand to all the corners of the agricultural world.
So here I am, sunning my shrivelled legs on this tropical paradise filled with bloody great death lizards. Could be worse. I used to live in Draynor.
That's a right miserable place I can tell you. So, you ready to help expand our farming enterprise?
Oh me dear? Why there's not much to know really. I'm Great Great Granny Potterington, Petunia's great grandmother.
Come out of retirement to help my great granddaughter manage this new farming enterprise.
Wait? You're granny's great grandmother?
Oh yes dear. I was a grandmother when Granny was just a wee young thing.
Oh dearie me dearie, you never ask a lady her age. It's terribly rude.
But I'll tell you, I'm older than my teeth and younger than I feel. He he he.
I've been living the last few years in Draynor. Nice little village full of thoroughly miserable people.
So when my great granddaughter offered me the opportunity to visit this tropical paradise, why I had to accept.
Like my great granddaughter I have handled a few marrows and potatoes. So I know what I'm doing here on this island.
This farm is a unique environment, it's not suitable for your standard livestock.
Instead this is the perfect place to raise those giant lizards that you see wandering round the island.
I know they might look scary, but get some good grub in them and you'll find them quite manageable dearie.
You'll need to purchase the deeds from the farmer's market and then build the pens yourself using the resources from the island.
After that you'll be good to go.
Well some animals you can get from me. I've got me a few frogs and salamanders tucked away for a modest fee.
For your jadinkos you'll need to get some hunting going.
As for the biggest beasts, you'll either need to get on with murdering some giant lizards, or you can sometimes pick some up whilst hunting them.
Of course, you can also trade any of them with your fellow farmers. The Grand Exchange won't let us trade animals on it, but you can trade with each other directly.
To raise an animal, you first need to make sure you've checked it over.
An unchecked animal could have all manner of diseases, ticks, parasites or curses attached to it and you don't want that.
Then you just need to use the animal on an appropriately sized paddock. Small animals go in the small pen, large in the large, etc.
You can't raise different animals in the same paddock either as they tend to fight.
You'll also need to feed your animals. This is just a simple case of making sure you've put the right sort of food in the feeding trough for the animal in that paddock.
Remember that not all animals will eat all types of food, so make sure you're not trying to feed dragons strawberries or they'll starve.
A starving animal will lose happiness and health, increasing the chance of it becoming sick and reducing the weight, speed and attractiveness potential of that animal.
If your animal gets diseases you will need to examine it. Look over its symptoms and administer the appropriate treatment to cure it.
A diseased animal has lower stats than healthier animals, so it's always worth keeping them healthy.
Animals are fairly chilled out on the farm, so you don't need to keep a constant eye on them. Just pop back every once in a while to see how they're doing.
Oh, that's easy. You just need to get two animals of the same species and put them in the breeding pen.
Make sure that they're of sufficient breeding age and that they have food, then just wait...
They'll get it together on their own time and eventually you should have a lovely baby animal waiting for you.
Despite claims by today's youth, elder animals are quite capable of breeding. So don't worry if your animals get a bit long in the tooth.
They'll still be quite capable of...doing the job.
Animals take time to breed and you'll need to keep them as healthy and happy as possible to get the fastest results.
Also, remember that the breeding pen can only hold 4 animals at a time, so make sure you keep taking the kids out to get new ones in.
Traits are little identifiers that indicate how that animal differs from others.
Some traits mean an animal is much happier than others and easy to keep amused.
Some traits mean that you can harvest them for more materials.
Some traits may do seemingly nothing at all. Whilst others will do strange things.
It's generally always a good thing to try and breed multiple traits into animals as the benefits are cumulative.
And what are perks?
Ah, now for those you first need to buy a farm totem from the farmers' market and attach it to an animal pen.
Then place an elder animal in that pen to activate that animal's perk. For instance, the perk for rabbits is an increase in all animal breeding chances.
If you place a second elder animal of the same type in the other pen of that size - also with an attached farm totem - you'll make the perk more potent!
Pretty much the only way to earn more beans is to sell on some of the animals you've raised.
You'll find buyers showing up on the farm on the beach here quite regularly.
Sell 'em the animals they're after, and you'll soon see them beans flowing in.
Progress will be slow to start, but once we've built up some reputation and a customer base, you'll have more beans than you know what to do with!
Listen close, 'cos there's a lot of nuance to making a great sale.
First up, a buyer will only have interest in a specific type of animal. Take Myfi, for instance - she'll only ever want to buy rabbits.
Each day they show up, they'll only want up to a specific amount of that animal too. They ain't made of beans, so will be on a budget.
The best age at which to sell animals is adolescence. You can sell older animals at a slight discount - they may be past their prime, but still hold fair value.
And while you can sell eggs and babies, you won't get very much for them. That's what people pay us for - to raise them.
Buyers will also have a special request - both a specific breed and specific trait. Match either with any sale and you'll get more beans.
Match both and you'll get a nice little bonus on top.
That said, they'll overlook the specific breed if you're selling 'em a shiny animal!
For all sales, regardless of any special request, there are certain animal traits can affect bean offers.
Anything with the Surly, Nice But Dim or Limited Efficiency traits will sell for fewer beans.
But anything with the Lucky, Fortunate or Unlucky For Some traits will sell for more beans.
It still might be worth selling animals with bad bean traits if it's to a special request. The boost from matching the special request should offset any negatives.
Finally, if you can get hold of one of those fancy farming outfits, you might be able to negotiate better bean prices on EVERY sale! Imagine that...

conversations.section: The Bird and the Beast

pages.x: Here we go again. Warmongering gods, trying to claim the world again.
What is happening here?
The Lumbridge crater has been drained of energy, so the gods are using other methods to gain energy and weaponise it.
It's further proof that the gods are a blight on Gielinor. We can't live in peace while these maniacs stomp about the world.
Who is fighting?
Armadyl and Bandos. Armadyl preaches peace, and yet the faithful flock to join his army. Ironic, yes?
Bandos is out to destroy all the gods - a sentiment I agree with. Unfortunately, he's also a tyrant, and would happily watch us all burn.
They're both guiding their mindless followers onto the battlefield, in order to gain the advantage.
Neither god will stop until the other is dead. It's a welcome outcome, I suppose: the fewer gods, the better.
As you know, the gods are going along with Sliske's game, in an effort to gain their precious Stone of Jas.
Do you want me to help?
Of course! First walk over there and kill Bandos. Then walk over there and kill Armadyl. I would forever be in your debt.
But that might be asking to much. Instead, join an army and help bring down either.
The sooner we remove them, the more likely that humanity survives.
Who should I join?
I cannot speak of the merits of either side. They're both repugnant.
You could join the stronger of the two to ensure the weaker dies, but that guarantees a powerful god's survival.
Joining the weaker god may seem like a folly, but it could help turn the tides. Either way, as long as we bring war to a swift end, we will have succeeded.
As before, the choice remains yours and yours alone.
If you wish to change sides at any point, though, I can help.
Can you give me directions?
Bandos's Tower
This is the way to Bandos's tower
Armadyl's Tower
This is the way to Armadyl's tower
Whose side are you on?
I am on the side of the Godless! Gielinor is our world, and the gods should find their own.
Gods want nothing more than power, and for whatever reason, they feel that Gielinor is worth fighting over.
None of them care about us, we're just pieces on a chess board.
Look at what they are doing now. One day they will be gone. Whether at the hands of my comrade, or my own.
What can you do for me?
The Godless are everywhere; ready in case an opportunity presents itself. But we keep ourselves hidden.
I am known in these lands. My influence will allow you to declare allegiance to either side on a moment's notice.
Be warned: if you change sides, you will lose your progress with your old faction, so choose wisely.
I wish to change sides.
I can change your allegiance to that of Armadyl/Bandos. Are you sure you want to do this?
No
I am here if you change your mind.
Who are you?
I am Kara-Meir, one of the godless. I am waiting for our chance to strike, should one arise.
Why are you with the Godless?
Mortals are made to be free. I am no hurry to be led by an imbecile who craves nothing but power. Why should anyone but me decide my fate?
We've lived too long in fear of these gods. We are many and they are few. It's time we took advantage of that state of affairs, before we become the few.
A mere mortal cannot destroy a god, but in our legions we are stronger. Our first step should be to aid the death of Bandos or Armadyl.
Perhaps if we can manage to kill a god, mortals will be rewarded with the Stone of Jas. Imagine! I could destroy the gods and free us all from their tyranny!
To replace it with what?
Kara-Meir looks away, her jaw clenched
A noble goal.
Kara-Meir simply nods, eyes intent.
I don't believe the stone should be used by anyone.
Kara-Meir Raises one eyebrow, but says nothing.
Wouldn't that make you no better than them?
Kara-Meir looks troubled at the retort, and offers no response.
What do they represent?
Biehn, our leader, set up the Godless in the hope that we might free mortals from tyranny of the gods. We do not need to worship them.
The gods have shown, repeatedly, that war follows them closely. To save ourselves from that war, we need to defeat them.
The sonner we do this, the sooner we can return to peace.
Garlandia has the ear of Biehn. She believes that we shouldn't fight the gods - that, if we stop worshipping them, then they'll have no one to rule. That they will leave.
She is wrong.
The Gods cannot be reasoned with. They crave power, and will not leave if we stop worshipping them - they will merely destroy us.
Look at what they're doing for a simple stone.
I hear you know Sir Theodore?
I... am surprised you have heard of him. He rescued me after my encounter with the Kinshra. He... understood me.
We shared many great adventures. Gunnarsgrunn, Morytania and many more. Those were exhilarating carefree times - no gods interfering in our world.
Were?
Yes, Sir Theodore is no longer with us.
I am sorry to hear that.
I'm fine! It's fine. We were friends. It has not affected my judgement or ability to gut an opponent. What else do you want to know?

conversations.section: Before While Guthix Sleeps

pages.x: Greetings, young warrior. Welcome to the meeting hall of the Warriors' guild. I am Harrallak Menarous, the Guild Master, at your service.

o: Quite a place you've got here. Tell me more about it.}}
You any good with a sword?}}

pages.x: Quite a place you've got here. Tell me more about it.
Yes indeed. What would you like to know?

o: Tell me about the Strength training area.
Tell me about the Attack training area.
Tell me about the Defence training area.
Tell me about the Combat training area.

pages.x: Tell me about the Strength training area.
Ahh, the mighty warrior, [Sloane/Yadech Strongarm], guards the Strength training area.
This intriguing little area consists of two shotput lanes for different weights of shot. It's fairly simple, the referee or [Sloane/Yadech] can explain more.
There's also the store room next door where Jimmy might share his talents with you, but don't tell him that I know he's not on guard duty!
Oh? Why?
Well, he's doing no harm and let's face it, with all these warriors around, the guild is hardly unguarded.
You can find the strength area just up the stairs behind the bank.
Tell me about the Attack training area.
Ahhh, dummies.
I'm no dummy, I just want to know what is there!
Oh no, my dear [man/lady], I did not mean you at all! The training area has mechanical dummies that pop up out of holes in the floor.
The noble dwarf, Gamfred, invented the mechanism and Ajjat can explain more about what to do there.
Oh, okay, I'll have to try it out.
You can find it just down the corridor and on your right.
Tell me about the Defence training area.
To polish your defensive skills to the very highest level, we've employed a most inventive dwarf and a catapult.
You're going to throw dwarves at me?
Oh my, no! I think Gamfred would object to that most strongly.
He's an inventor, you see, and has built a marvellous contraption that can throw all sorts of things at you. Things such as magic missiles...
Mmmm?
...spiked iron balls...
...spinning, slashing blades...
Ummm...
...and anvils.
ANVILS?
No need to be afraid, it's all under very controlled conditions! You can find it just up the stairs behind the bank.
Tell me about the combat training area.
Ahh, yes, our resident magician from foreign lands created a most amazing gadget that can turn your own armour against you! It's really quite intriguing.
That sounds dangerous. What if I'm wearing it at the time?
So far, that's not happened.
You need to speak to Shanomi about the specifics of the process, but as I understand it, putting a suit of armour in one of these devices will make it come to life somehow.
The better the armour, the harder it is to defeat.
Fighting my own armour sounds weird. I could be killed by it...
Indeed, we have had a few fatalities from warriors overstretching themselves and not knowing their limits. Start small and work up, is my motto!
That and go see Lidio for some food if you need it.
Okay, thanks for the warning.
Tell me about tokens.
Ahh, yes! The tokens allow you to spend an amount of time with my 'discovery', located on the top floor of the guild.
Now, the amount of tokens you collect from the five activities around the guild will dictate how long Kamfreena
will allow you in the enclosure on the very top floor. More tokens equals more time.
There are also some bonuses available should you take part in all of the activities around the guild.
Okay, okay. So, how do I earn these tokens?
You can earn them by simply using the training exercises around the guild. The staff will enter your token earnings into a ledger as you play.
Sounds easy enough. What are the bonuses?
Should you take part in all five activities around the guild you can choose to pay for your time on the top floor with tokens of all types.
Should you do this then you'll find you spend less tokens overall and have a better chance of getting the dragon defender, amongst other things.
Excellent, sounds good. So, what's up on the top floor?
Well, without giving too much away, they're big and mean, and you get to fight them for defenders.
If you're really lucky, they'll summon a cyclossus...although that might be unlucky. Still, if you manage to defeat him, you could win his hat.
Interesting...I will have to explore the top floor then!
You any good with a sword?
'Am I any good with a sword'? Have you any clue who I am?
Not really, no.
Why, I could best any person alive in a rapier duel!
Try me, then!
My dear [man/lady], I couldn't possibly duel you, I might hurt you and then what would happen to my reputation! Besides, I have this wonderful guild to run.
Why don't you take a look at the various activities we have. You might even collect enough tokens to be allowed in to kill the strange beasts from the east!
Bye!
Farewell, [brave warrior/fair lady]. I do hope you enjoy my guild.

conversations.section: Talking to Reldo

pages.x: Hello there. How can I help you today?

o: I have a question about the TzHaar language.
I'd like to talk about a pyramid.

pages.x: Me? What do you want to know?

o: Do you have anything to trade?
Do you know any heroic stories?

pages.x: I am the palace librarian.
Ah. That's why you're in the library, then.
Yes.
Although I would probably be in here even if I didn't work here. I like reading.
Some day, I hope to catalogue all of the information stored in these books, so all may read it.
Only knowledge.
How much do you want for that, then?
No, sorry, that was just my little joke. I'm not the trading type.
Oh, well.
Do you know any heroic stories?
Yes, I do.
Years ago, a terrible creature slew King Roald's betrothed and terrorized the people. Varrock sent an embassy to Morytania to open a dialogue with Drakan about it.
What happened?
It didn't end happily. Poor Gar'rth, we didn't know he was... Well, it would be unfair for me to say. That's his secret, not mine.
What about the terrible creature?
It was brought to justice, but not before claiming many innocents.
Go on, tell me about Gar'rth.
Another time, perhaps? I have work to do.
Hmpf!

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?
I'd like to change my teleport point.

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Varrock set, you are presented with some body armour.
This armour will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all Tasks within a particular difficulty set, then you can claim your reward.
Most of the Varrock set's Tasks are straightforward, though you might find some require quests to be started, if not finished.
To claim your Varrock set reward, speak to Rat Burgiss south of Varrock, Vannaka in Edgeville Dungeon, or me.
Varrock armour 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Varrock armour 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
No thanks.
Varrock armour 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Varrock armour 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,00 coins.
No thanks.
I'd like to change my Varrock Teleport point.
Can I change my Varrock teleport point?
Certainly. It's currently set to [the altar in the north of Varrock/the fountain in the middle of Varrock/the Grand Exchange]. Where would you prefer?

o: Fountain in the middle of Varrock.

pages.x: Okay, that's all done.
Okay, that's all done.
Okay, that's all done.
Hello, Reldo. Could you remind me where I could find that book on the TzHaar language?
Of course. It's the TzHaar Tourist Guide. It should be somewhere in the library. I'm not sure exactly where, but if you have a look around, I'm sure you will find it.
Alright, thank you.
I'd like to talk about a pyramid.
How goes the matter of the mummy's personality?
She is reunited with knowledge of her personality now - so overall a happy ending.
Excellent, all too rare to see a good end to matters these days.

conversations.section: At the Runespan / Talking to Wizard Finix

pages.x: Hello. How can I help you?

o: Can you help me find something?
Can you teleport me back to the Wizards' Tower?

pages.x: I'm Wizard Finix. I am a student of runecrafting.
Ah, pleased to meet you, Wizard Finix. I'm Player. What are you doing here?
I'm creating runes by siphoning energy out of the Runespan.
Creating runes by siphoning?
Yes, it's a new way to make runes. I discovered it, actually!

o: Why don't you just use the altars?
How do you make runes by siphoning?
Can you teleport me back to the Wizards' Tower?

pages.x: That is another one of my discoveries! Runecrafting altars will not last forever. One day, the altars will run out!
Run out?
Yes - of course, it is still only a theory. The Runecrafting Guild wizards are still sceptical, but they cannot prove me wrong.
How will humans perform magic if they cannot make runes?
Exactly. That is why learning to siphon energy from the world around us is important.
You mean I could create runes by pulling energy from Gielinor itself?
Theoretically, yes, but there is no runecrafter skilled enough to do this yet. In theory, runecrafting and magic should be a self-supporting cycle.
So how can I learn to siphon energy if it is so difficult?
That is why we are in this area. In the Runespan, energy is still in a very raw state and is not tightly bound to matter, as it is in Gielinor.
The wizards of the Runecrafting Guild have been using their tower to study runic energy in the Runespan for years.
So that means...
...we are outside the Runecrafting Guild - yes!

o: So, how do you make runes by siphoning?
Can you teleport me back to the Wizards' Tower?

pages.x: I can show you around, or I can just explain it to you. Which would you prefer?
This is the Runespan. You can train runecrafting by siphoning energy from here into rune essence.
How do you make runes by siphoning?

o: How do I get rune essence?
Is there anything else to do here?
Why don't you just use the altars?

pages.x: Firstly, you can only train runecrafting here with rune essence found on this plane.
So how do I get rune essence?
There are two ways to get rune essence. If you have no rune essence, then you can use the floating essence to collect a small amount.
If you do have some essence then the best way to get more is to siphon from the creatures that are walking around.
Siphon from the creatures?
Yes. The creatures that you can find here are made up of rune essence that is bound together with runic energy.
If you take away all that energy, then you are just left with rune essence.
If you are in a hurry and don't want to siphon from the creatures then you can chip some of their rune essence away from them using your runes.
I would advise against doing it to the same creature twice, though.
Once you have rune essence from this plane, you can siphon energy from the creatures and pockets of energy that appear randomly on islands in this area.
The energy in the creatures is not as dense as it is in the pockets of energy, so they will give you a small amount of runes and not much experience.
The pockets of energy are the best way to train.
These can be easily spotted because, when one appears, the runecrafting wizards will mark the floor around it to display when energy can be siphoned from it.
The pockets of energy appear in random places and you can find yourself on an island where there are none.
The best way for you to train is to find the most complex type of energy you can siphon, and siphon from that.
Getting around this plane can be tricky as it is made up of floating islands. Fortunately, the Runecrafting Guild wizards have installed crossing points.
For the cost of a few runes, you can activate these points which will enchant you and take you to another island.
Since these are made by wizards, it is not as simple as hopping from island to island, though. The type of runes required are shown on the crossing point.
As you approach a crossing point, the far side will glow to show where it goes to. If you have the runes to use the crossing point, the near side will glow as well.
Not all the crossing points will charge you. If you try to go from a small island to a big island, then the crossing point is free.
This is to prevent you from becoming stranded.
Yes, there are a couple of things you can do here as well.
The wizards have a tendency to get themselves stuck on islands, and once in a while you will hear one of them calling to you.
If you find and help the wizard, he will share some of his runecrafting knowledge with you. There is also a rare chance that a runesphere will form.
This is a complex, multi-layered ball of rune essence.
Each layer of the runesphere is aligned to a specific runic type and you need to siphon away all layers of the runesphere.
This will give you rune dust and impart further runecrafting knowledge to you. The runesphere only appears for a while before it disappears.
If you can siphon away all of its layers before it disappears, then you can hand in the rune dust you gathered from siphoning away the layers to the pure energy inside.
This will grant you yet more runecrafting knowledge.
Sure, what would you like me to help you find?

o: Can you help me find a wizard in yellow robes?
Can you help me find the runesphere?

pages.x: Sure, I've seen him. I will point you in the right direction for a while.
Sure.

conversations.section: In the Fist of Guthix waiting area / After talking to Fiara

o: Who's the weird looking giant earwig?

It comes from the centre of the big cave.

It's very magical.

Something to do with the Fist of Guthix.

This place is special to Guthix, because Fiara is here.
And we know it has something to do with the 'Fist of Guthix' because Fiara occasionally mentions it.
But other than that, we only have theories. Do you want to hear about them?
Well, this is Getorix's silly theory. Listen to it, if you must.
At the end of the God Wars, Guthix returned to Gielinor and was angered by the destruction caused by the other gods in their vanity and quest for power.
So, maybe he punched the ground in anger, leaving an imprint of power on the ground that has lasted ever since.
Because he was angry at the time, the power would have been tainted with aggression, which is why he left Fiara as a guardian, to make sure the power did not escape unfettered.
Do you believe this theory?
No, I think it's rubbish; if it was true, that would mean Guthix's hand would be a very strange shape.
The indentation in the centre of the cave doesn't look like a fist to me. Getorix has just let his imagination run away with him. My theory is better.
Do you want to hear another theory?
This is Pontimer's personal delusion on the subject.
After the God Wars, Guthix found something dangerous here and used his power to protect it.

I don't know for certain, but it must be under that strange impression in the big cave. I think that mark is some sort of ward that Guthix has left to protect the site.

Exactly! That's what I told him. It just doesn't make sense. My theory makes much more sense.

Guthix has left us a test. He deliberately created this site of power as a test of individual strength and balance.
We do know that this place has existed from around the time of the God Wars, so maybe Guthix felt it was important to test one's strength against another in order to face the cruelties of war.
Does Guthix do that sort of thing? And you let anyone into the cave now.
Of course, it wouldn't be balanced otherwise.
How do you know?
I have interpreted the teachings of our Lord Guthix, and the cryptic words of Guardian Fiara.
'Interpreted' - you mean this is a guess?
How dare you question my understanding of the ways of balance!
Do you want to hear another theory?
I'd better get going.
I'd better get going.
Who's the weird looking giant earwig?
Shhh! Give Fiara some respect! She can hear you, you know.
Fiara? It has a name?
Of course, Guthix chooses names for all his guardians.
If...err...Fiara is a Guardian, what is she guarding?
She guards this site. It is a holy site of Guthix.

o: How long has Fiara been here?

pages.x: How long has Fiara been here?
Errr, ages. Since the end of the God Wars I think. She doesn't talk about that much.

o: So what are you doing here?

pages.x: So, what is this place?
I'd better get going.
I'd better get going.
I'd better get going.

Zis iz true, mon ami. 'owever, in ze future, I will 'ave my own entire floor of ze Museum with paintings galore!

Ze bon mot, ze laugh, ze fun of poking at me, eh? I shall 'ave my gallery, you vill see eventually, mon ami. Zen I shall be ze, 'ow you say, laughing last!

JUST a painting? 'ow could you say such a t'ing? When you learn 'ow to appreciate ze wonderful works of art, you may talk to me.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / After joining the Imperial Guard

pages.x: Ah, Player! Back for more, are you? What can I do for you?

o: I want to start one of the activities.
I want to talk to you about rewards.}}
Can you go over the activities again?
pages.i: What do you want to say?

pages.x: I want to start one of the activities.
That's the spirit! Which do you want to do?
Defend the gatehouse!
Good on yer!
Fight the trolls!
Right on!
I want to talk to you about rewards.
Ah, the payoff. Incentive schemes. Points make prizes. Let's talk!
I want to know about the rewards. What's in it for me?
Isn't the glory of the battle enough? The adrenaline rush? The smell of troll sweat in the morning?
Definitely not!
People these days... I suppose I would be willing to impart some expertise to you in exchange for your help. The more you help, the more experience I'll give you.
Just speak to me after you complete the event and I'll give you your reward.
Can you go over the activities again?
Do you want the quick version or the more detailed version?
Every month, you can come back here and help defend the gatehouse.
Why every month? Aren't trolls invading all the time?
Yes, but due to union regulations we can only have each shift work once a month. There are two things you can do to help the gatehouse.
You may only choose to do one to gain a reward. You can still play the other, for practice, any time you like. So, things you can do to help defend the gatehouse...
First, you can fight trolls. You stand alone in front of the gate and fight off as many trolls as you can until you die.
What? Until I die?
Well...maybe not die. Basically, we leave you out there until you 'almost' die, then drag you back in. That way you don't lose any of your stuff.
Okay, what's the other thing I can do?
Oh, that's much safer. Well, you won't die, but Norris did have a nervous breakdown a few weeks ago. I guess the strain of it got to him.
Oh no.
Basically, you run around repairing the gatehouse defences. Keep the oil drums full, repair barricade lines and gatehouse walls...

o: What do you want to ask

pages.x: I want to know more about fighting off the troll hordes.
Ah, after a fight, are you? Thinking of the sweat of battle? Pondering the smell of troll blood in the morning? Good for you!
Fighting troll hordes is all about endurance. It's about showing your moxie. It's about perserverance in the face of unbeatable odds.
Unbeatable?
Well, maybe not unbeatable. More like very, very likely not beatable. The hordes get stronger and more difficult the longer you are out there.
For the most part, the trolls are pretty run of the mill, but there are some that are a bit...unusual.
Some trolls have eaten a few too many wizards and have gained magical powers.
They'll drag you out from your hiding place and beat you to a pulp...like they did to ol' Ralph.
Oh, and there are trolls that ate some druids and now they can summon other trolls - gave Derek a real shock when a troll popped out of the ground between his feet.
That's what you call unusual?
Oh, I haven't finished! There's some sort of flu or plague the trolls have caught and you'll want to avoid touching those ones.
And it might be worth me mentioning that some of the trolls stole some explosives from us and like to use it against the castle.
No big deal, just an explosion here or there.
Explosives!
And I nearly forgot about Cliff! He's a real nasty customer. Other than them, it's a piece of cake. Just make sure to go in prepared for long combat.
You won't lose anything you take in unless you consume it.
I want to know more about defending and repairing the gatehouse.
Ah, deliberating over the defence? Strategising your protective methods? Incentivising your grey cells to safeguard the gatehouse? Wonderful!
Defending the gatehouse is all about speed and multi- tasking. It also helps if you're handy in Strength, Agility, Defence, Crafting, Construction and Firemaking.
You don't have to have any levels in any of those to help out, but it will make your life easier!
Oh, gee, is that all? Why not throw in a few more skills to 'make my life easier'?
Hmm, I suppose we could, but let's see how you get on with these. It'll be easiest if I show you how it all works. Do you want to see?

pages.i: Do you want to see the tutorial?

pages.x: Okay, sure. I'd like to see what I need to do.
No, not right now.
I want to know more about only doing the event once a month. Does that mean I can only do the fighting or the defending? I can't do both?
You can do one a month for reward, after that you can keep going if you wish for training for the following months attempt though.
We in the Imperial Guard recognise that not all guards are cut out for both types of work.
We like to be flexible in your schedules and workload, so you can do it whenever you like the month though.

conversations.section: In Rellekka / After The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Hello again, [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]. I hope your travels have brought you wealth and joy! What compels you to visit me on this day?

o: I just came to say hello.
Can I hear the history of your people?

pages.x: I just came to say hello.
Well met, [brother/sister] [Fremennik name]. It is always good to see your face in glorious Rellekka once more!
Do you have any quests?
Not at the moment, [Fremennik name]. Rest assured, should your services to the Fremennik be required, I will call upon you.
Can I hear the history of your people?
Why, of course, [Fremennik name]! Do not say 'your people' like that, for you are now a Fremennik yourself! What did you want to hear of?

o: Tell me of the finding of Koschei
Tell me of the lands to the North
[Charm] Can I have a new name?

pages.x: I'm interested in finding out about that mysterious warrior I fought as part of Thorvalds' combat trial. His name is Koschei I believe.
Ah... the deathless one... We do not even know if Koschei is his name, when we found him he had no memory, he was simply repeating that single word.
Whatever happened to him must have rattled his soul so hard that his memory ran away from him, and he has not yet found its hiding place.
So how exactly did you find him?
Well, it was a raiding party like any other. We had just struck one of the smaller northern islands to harvest supplies by combat, as our laws allow,
when we saw a figure in the icey waters. As we were at least a 3 week sail from any port, and saw no other ships nearby, he must have been there some time.
We could not leave someone to the cold death of the ocean, even an outerlander, so we fished him aboard. He muttered continually, but his words made no sense.
He had no clothes or possessions with him, and seemed to have been burnt somehow before he had landed in the water.
I cannot help but wonder what burnt him, for as you may have seen, he is incredibly powerful and resistant to damage by any means I know of!
Anyway, we decided to bring him back to Rellekka, for he did not seem of good health or sound mind, and simply repeated the word Koschei over and over.
Yrsa tended to him for many weeks, until one day it was as though a new soul had entered his burnt and broken body.
He suddenly left her house one day, fully healed, and able to speak to us as though nothing had happened to him.
He still had no recollection of how he had come to be in the icey ocean, or of who he was, or where he had come from, but this did not matter to us or him.
He took his trials of adulthood, as you did, and has been a boon to our clan ever since. Someday I fear he may regain his memory, and leave us for his past...
But I will always respect any decision he decides to make should that day ever come upon us. Until then, he is more than welcome to stay here.
So, [Fremennik name], was there anything more you wished to hear?
I would like to hear of the lands across the ocean to the North.
Well, I think the best thing for you would be to go to the docks and ask to join one of our longboats on a journey.
My affairs are concentrated mostly on Rellekka, so my knowledge is not great, but I will happily share what little I do know with you, [Fremennik name].
North of this town the atmosphere becomes bitterly cold. There are a number of small inhabited islands that we have sea routes with.
The largest of these is possibly Miscellania, although I hear that there has been some recent incident with their monarch, but I don't know the details.
There is also of course the island of the moon clan, who change with the tides. They are our bitterest enemies, and we are currently at war with them.
They are an evil people, equally cursed and blessed by the magic in their blood. Beyond those islands, there is the large frozen wasteland we call Acheron.
It is an inhospitable land, and you will need an agile and sturdy body just to keep alive in its perils.
As I say, my knowledge outside of this town is rather limited, and I know no more than this. Was there anything else you wished to hear tell of?
I would like to hear a little of the history between the Fremenniks and the outerlanders.
Ah, now that is something I know a great deal about. Believe it or not, all outerlanders were once orginally Fremenniks.
When first man came to these lands all were Fremenniks, and followed our ways. We lived a happy life, and never settled in one place for long.
We travelled by boat along the coastlines, never taking more from the land than could be regrown by the same time in the following year.
However, many moons past, some of our tribesmen were weary of constantly travelling the lands, and decided to build themselves permanent homes.
Unfortunately, the other races that had also migrated here did not like this. They waged war against us at every opportunity.
We were driven mostly to the coastlines, where we could escape by boat when attacked. Remember, at this time we had no real way to defend against constant attack.
Then one day one of our Seers, whose full name has been lost in the telling of this tale, discovered a cave full of strange rocks.
This rock would never be consumed, no matter how much we took, and sparkled at its peak, and broke off in small and regular sized chunks when mined.
Stranger than this, we found that these rocks would become filled with power when taken to certain places across this land!
There was a terrible argument in our tribe! Some said that we should take as many of these rocks as we could, and use them in defending against our enemies' attacks!
Others said that we had found a place that belonged only to the gods, and that should we steal what was not ours we would find only torment and misery.
We voted on this, and decided that it was in the best interests of the tribe to leave these strange rocks where they lay, for the gods can be spiteful and cruel,
especially to those who do not treat them with the respect they desire. Some of our number refused to accept this ruling by our council however.
They began to mine these rocks, and set up transport systems to the various places of power that enchanted them.
They even created temples at each of these places! This was going too far! We had no choice, but to expel them from our tribe forever!
We turned our backs upon them, and let them know they would never be welcome back to our tribes until they had released themselves from the rocks.
This is the tale of how the outerlanders came about; through stealing from the gods, and from betraying our ideals. This is why we show them no trust.
Was there something else you wished to hear?
Actually, history isn't really my thing.
Well let me know should you wish to hear our lore and histories. We value them highly.
Not that I don't like my name or anything, but can I have a new one?
A new name? That is a strange request. What's wrong with [current Fremennik name]?
Nothing's wrong with [current Fremennik name], I'd just like a new name, if it's not too much trouble.
Very well. From now on you will be known as [new Fremennik name].

pages.x: Tell me about the new dig.
Well, we recently had a large chunk of funds donated to us, so we sent out all sorts of explorers - I'm sure you'll meet them as you go around the world.
People like Simon down in the desert near the pyramid as well as
Aristarchus in Pollnivneach, Varmen and, of course, Anna Jones. Anyway, we think we have discovered an island that has massive archaeological significance.

it. If you have the qualifications and help us out around the Museum, I'm sure we could offer you a place on the dig when we're ready to go.

Tell me about other sections of the Museum.
I'd be delighted to; which areas are you interested in?
Tell me about the Natural History exhibit.

Indeed, I am sure you will recognise some of the
creatures down there. Hopefully, our lectures will teach you some things you didn't know about them!
