Ah, I see. The 'history' refers to that of the species - it doesn't necessarily mean it's died out. After all, we have human history and we're still here!
I guess that makes sense.
Tell me about the Dig Site exhibit.
Ahh, those. We're slowly filling them up with the help of people who have their Earth Sciences exams completed at the Dig Site. If you have, feel free to give us a hand.
We'd appreciate it.
Tell me about the Dig Site find cleaning area.
The cleaning area, yes. Well, we have some really good archaeologists on site right now.
They're cleaning up the finds that are shipped over from the Dig Site to the east of here. If you have the right qualifications, you can help
them clean the finds.
What qualifications?
Level 3 Earth Science exams. You can take them over at the Exam Centre on the Dig Site.
Tell me about the Timeline exhibit.
Ahh, my speciality. Being a historian, matters of the past are my passion. Collated on this floor and the one above are just part of my life's work.
I am still working on updating and finding out more everyday, so if you find any
information on your travels that may be useful, please do let me know.
You can follow the timeline of the history of Gielinor from the creation of the world to the present day, simply by walking around this display.
A wondrous journey, I think you'll agree!
Wow, that's a lot of information. I'm sure in my travels and quests I'll pick up a few bits of information for you.
I have some information that might be of use in your displays.
That's grand! We're always glad to have more facts. Now, tell me what you know...
No thanks.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: It's a rather nice day here in Um! Can I help you with tool storage, or a trip to Winkin's farm, or something else?

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: What can you store?
I can hold onto your rake, seed dibber, spade, secateurs, watering can and trowel - but not those trowels used for archaeology.
I can also store a few buckets and scarecrows for you, and even compost, supercompost and ultracompost.
Of course, compost is essential for good farming, so I can store lots of that for you.
Also, if you hand me your farming produce, I might be able to change it into banknotes.
So, would you like me to look after your farming tools?

o: What do you do with the tools you're storing?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Yes, please.
What do you do with the tools you're storing? They can't all possibly fit in your pockets!
Of course not. I have a toolshed. It is rather curious shed, though. Sometimes, items just seem to appear in there.
So, would you like me to look after your tools?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.
Well, I shall be here if you ever decide that I may be of service.
Actually, I'm fine.

o: Can you take me to Winkin's Farm?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Can you take me to Winkin's Farm?

o: Can you compost patches for me?
Can you stop composting patches for me?
How much have I paid for?
Can I change which patches you compost?
pages.i: What would you like to say

pages.x: Can you compost patches for me?
Sure, I can do it at all of your patches using the compost you give me, if you're willing to pay for the convenience.
500 gold for regular compost, 1,500 gold for supercompost or 2,500 gold for ultracompost. Pay for up to 60,000 upfront, but no refunds.
Can you stop composting patches for me?
How much compost will you use?
We'll use [number] regular, [number] super compost and [number] ultracompost. Want to top up?
Do you want to change some more?
Do you want to change some more?
Do you want to change some more?
Do you want to change some more?
Do you want to change some more?
Do you want to change some more?
Do you want to change some more?

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: How did you come to be a gardener in Um? A lot of people would probably want to stop working after they died.
Well, you see, all my life I'd wanted to be a gardener.
The smell of the soil, the joy you feel when you harvest a cared-for crop...
But, I was afraid of what people would think of me...
All of the gardeners were leprechauns at the time, and I looked nothing like a leprechaun!
You still don't look anything like a leprechaun.
Exactly! So, I never did become a gardener.
After death though, I created this little garden in Um.
When my leprechaun friend over there arrived, I was prepared for the worst...
'There's only room for one gardener in this town', I was expecting him to say. Or something along those lines.
But he's been noting but accepting! As it turned out, he was more than happy to retire after dying.
How lovely.
Anyway, do you want me to look after your farming tools?

conversations.section: Evil Tree dialogue

pages.x: Ain't you noticed the tree yet? Cut it down!
Who are you?
Me? Oo's askin'? I ain't nobody but a leprechaun, innit.
You sound a bit different from other leprechauns...
That's bein' on account a' the fact I was raised by imps, innit. Luvverly chaps, imps. Right geezers.
Anyways, I came across this 'ere root on me wanderin', so I got you geezers wif long legs to 'elp me out.
Now look what I gots on me 'ands. Please, lad!
If ya gimme a hand, I can return a favour.
What is that thing?
That there is an evil tree, innit. The cunnin' geezer starts off lookin' like an innocent sapling.
Later on, though, ooh! It grows into a frightenin' beast, all lashin' roots and 'Look at me nasty teef!'
Some of 'em, I heard from a mate of a mate, are easier to kill than others.
How can I help?
You can't get near the tree while those roots are thrashin' about, so you'll have to cut them with a hatchet. Once they're gone, you can attack the tree itself.
'Cos it's a tree, it don't like hatchets or fire. Use any kindling you gets off the roots to set fires at the base of the tree.
The fires will keep burning and doing damage to the tree while you whack it with a hatchet.
Do ya need more information?
Yes, I'd like some more information.

o: How do I cut the tree?
How do I light fires on the tree?
How do I deal with the roots?
How do I know how much damage I'm doing to the tree?
pages.i: What do you want to know more about?

pages.x: How do I cut the tree?
Ya can only cut the tree when the roots are gone and if ya have a hatchet. The better the hatchet, the faster ya cut the tree.
It looks like ya've already got a hatchet!
No, thanks.
Suit yaself, [lad/lass].
How do I light fires on the tree?
Ya can only burn the tree when the roots are gone. When they've been cut back, use the kindling from the roots on the tree.
You got to have a tinderbox to light the fires.
Do ya need a tinderbox?
No, thanks.
Suit yaself, [lad/lass].
How do I deal with the roots?
Ya have to cut them down to get to the tree. A hatchet or machete should do the trick. The more people cutting them, the faster they'll come down.
Ya can get kindling from them, which ya want to keep to light fires on the tree.
Do ya want a hatchet? I reckon I gots one in me loot-bag somewhere...
How do I know how much damage I'm doing to the tree?
If ya 'inspect' the tree, ya can find out how much damage you've done, as well as a few other bits of useful info.
Ya should also see bark fly off as you cut it, and the fires will flare up when they do damage. Ya should see the tree look weaker the more damage you do.
I'll let ya know how ya doin' as often as I can.
How long will this take?
No, thanks.
Suit yaself, [lad/lass].
Why should I help you?
There's loads of loot in it for ya. Killing one of them will get ya logs, of course.
But that ain't all! You might get seeds or nests, Treasure Trail clues, and maybe a few other surprises.
Also, any logs ya get I'll teleport straight to ya bank. Honest, guv.
I can also make you less likely to fell some trees while you're chopping them, but this'll only work on trees you haven't grown yourself.
Do ya need more information?

o: Player: Can I borrow some tools?

pages.x: I reckon I can spare 'em for ya.
It looks like ya've already got a hatchet!
It looks like ya've already got a hatchet!
Goodbye.
See ya'!

conversations.section: Subsequent dialogue

pages.x: It's the young entrepreneur! How can I help?

o: Can you teach me about the Grand Exchange again?
Can you tell me more about how the system works?
Can you tell me prices for common items, like...
Where did the Grand Exchange come from?

pages.x: Can you teach me about the Grand Exchange again?

o: If the player has an active offer in their first Grand Exchange slot:

pages.x: Sorry, but I can't remind you of the workings of the Grand Exchange while you have an offer active in your first slot.
Hahaha. It would be my absolute pleasure!
Can you tell me more about how the system works?
Oh, I simply love passing on knowledge. Okay, let me hit you with some facts...
The Grand Exchange calculates a guide price for each item that can be traded through it, based on the price people paid for that item over the previous days.
An item's guide price is just a suggested value; you can offer any price you like when setting up your bids.
You'll find various experts dotted around the building. They can tell you the guide prices of common items.
Once you've set up an offer, our clerks will keep looking for players willing to complete the trade, even while you're not logged in.
Item sets! Say, for example, you wish to sell a set of rune armour but you don't want to sell the items individually.
If you speak with one of the clerks, they will do a swap with you: a single item representing the armour set in exchange for all the component parts.
You can then sell this single item on the Grand Exchange! The clerks will also exchange the sets back into their component parts.
Did you know: you can abort your offers at any time by visiting one of the clerks, choosing to exchange in order to view your current bids, right-clicking on the offer and choosing 'abort'.
When you're selling lots of items, your offer may not be completed in a single transaction.
For example, if you're selling 1,000 logs, and someone wants to buy 200, we'll do that trade and let you collect the money.
The remaining 800 logs will stay in the Grand Exchange, waiting for someone else to buy them.
That's a lot of info. I think my brain just melted.
Hahaha. Not to worry: you can ask me as many times as you want.
Trust me, you'll get the hang of it eventually.
Can you tell me prices for common items, like...

o: The prices of weapons and armour.

pages.x: The prices of ores.
By all means, but you can probably get this information quicker by visiting Farid M.
The prices of runes.
My pleasure, but you can probably get at this information quicker by visiting Murky Matt.
The prices of logs.
Sure thing, but you can probably get at this information quicker by visiting Relobo.
The prices of herbs.
Of course, but you can probably get at this information quicker by visiting Bob Barter.
The prices of weapons and armour.
That's easy, but you can probably get at this information quicker by visiting Hofuthand.
Where did the Grand Exchange come from?
I'm glad you ask! I like telling this story. Are you sitting comfortably?
Erm, I'll stand if that's okay.
Fine. *Ahem* I shall tell you a story of hard work, dedication and success. I grew up here in Varrock at my parents' general store.

I got a good feel for how the prices of items would rise and fall depending on supply and demand; I always found it interesting how items would go from one person to another, in this long chain of transactions.
So you've always lived here?
Oh, yes. I'd never consider leaving.
Anyway, as I became an adult, I got to know other shop owners around Varrock along with the rich traders that would exchange vast quantities of items in one go.
How do you class a big quantity?
Well, the quantities are always increasing. I remember the day when you could buy some cooked shark for five coins!
Impossible!
Nope. Straight up. Anyway, I organised a group of us to meet each week to see what deals could be made.
It seemed to work so well and we developed a system that became so popular, that each meeting would see a variety of new people joining.
I kept improving on the system that I had created, but soon it became too big a thing to manage.
I can imagine!
So, in the end, I decided: why not make this a world-wide phenomenon? Make it public and allow anyone to join in.
Up to this point, it catered for people buying and selling large quantities, but I knew it would work on a smaller scale.
And I was also in for a bit of luck. You see, one of the initial patrons had deep connections to the Varrock bank.
Together, I think you'll agree we have a most friendly system.
I feel quite excited now! I have a strange urge to shout, 'Buy, buy, sell, sell!'.
Never mind.

conversations.section: In War's Retreat / Normal dialogue

pages.x: Welcome back to my retreat, Project!

o: Can you tell me about yourself?
I would like to talk about Combat Mastery.
What do you want me to do?
Can you explain the rewards to me?

pages.x: Can you tell me about yourself?
I am War. I was one of the four riders of the apocalypse, before I retired.
Why did you retire?
I got old! There's only so long you can keep up the pace I rode at.
So what do you do now?
Other than a battle Old Boney roped me into, I've been thirsting for combat.
But that's why I've started this retreat! Everyone needs a hobby.

o: What can you tell me about Combat Mastery?
Show me the Combat Mastery tasks I can do.
Do you have any rewards for me?

pages.x: Welcome back to my Retreat, Project! I have new tasks for you.
I have watched your progress with much interest, Project. I want to take your glory to the next level!
What did you have in mind?
I have devised a new set of tasks for you which will further test your mettle. For GLORIOUS BATTLE!
The more tasks you complete, the more rewards I will grant you.
Well done Player, I've kept some rewards aside for you.
Goodbye!
Fight on Project, fight on!
What do you want me to do?
BATTLE!
Do battle?
GLORIOUS BATTLE!
Could you be a bit more specific?
Fight bosses and I will give you marks, return them to me for rewards.
The more bosses you kill the more access I will grant you to my facilities.
Can you explain the rewards to me?
Which rewards are you interested in knowing more about?

o: Can you tell me about the transport options here?
Can you tell me about the altar and adrenaline crystals?
Can you tell me about the campfire?
Can we talk about something else?

pages.x: What are marks of war?
When you defeat worthy foes, I will give you marks to spend. I want combat to become habitual to you, so I will award you up to 1,000 marks an hour.
The more impressive the foe, the more marks I will award you.
These marks can be used to buy combat auras and aura and life refreshes.
You can also use them with logs to upgrade the campfire, so you can warm your heart and sing songs of your battle prowess!
Can you tell me about the transport options here?
If you defeat 10 foes, I can offer you a teleport to return you to this retreat whenever you like.
My portals can be directed to take you to any bosses you can battle, if you've defeated them once before and can pay the price of 100,000 coins.
The first portal, and first redirection is free. I will let you use the second portal when you've defeated 100 impressive foes.
If you've killed a specific boss at least 100 times, you can redirect a portal to it for 50,000 coins.
If you are helping out Old Boney with his reaping, the reaper portal will take you to the target he has assigned you.
The final portal will activate if there is a new foe to battle or an event to participate in.
Can you tell me about the altar and adrenaline crystals?
I can grant you access to my altar to reinvigorate your prayer and summoning after battle...
...and crystals to rouse you for your next one by refilling your adrenaline!
Both of these can be gained by killing 200 and 1,000 powerful creatures, respectively.
Can you tell me about the campfire?
The campfire can be used to warm your heart and boost your lifepoints before an battle.
You can also use 1,000 marks of war with 1,000 logs to upgrade the campfire to improve its effects.
Can we talk about something else?
Of course, Project!

o: I would like to purchase some rewards.
Can you warn me when I'm trying to reattune a portal?

pages.x: I would like to purchase some rewards.
Very well, Project.
Can you warn me when I'm trying to reattune a portal?
MY WARNING SHOUT WILL BE SO LOUD YOUR ANCESTORS WILL HEAR IT!
A simple yes would have sufficed.
Goodbye!
Fight on Project, fight on!

conversations.section: Wizard Elriss

pages.x: Welcome to the Runecrafting Guild.
What is this place?
This is the Runecrafting Guild, as I said.
After the secret of Runecrafting was re-discovered, I set up the guild as a place for the most advanced runecrafters to work together.
Work together towards what?
Towards a greater understanding of Runecrafting, of course.
The basics of Runecrafting may have been re-discovered, but many of the secrets of the first Wizards' Tower remain unknown.
What secrets?
Oh, nothing to interest an adventurer such as yourself, I'm sure.
I'm interested.
We all have our projects, adventurer.
Acantha and Vief are happy to involve junior runecrafters in their feud, but others prefer to keep their research private until it is revealed.
An idea may be subjected to cruel ridicule if it is aired prematurely. you must forgive me if I am not so forthcoming again.
Go on, tell me.
Leave me be!
Acantha and Vief are hardly working together!
Aren't they? They think their debate about orb colour is so important, but do you really think it matters which team you join?
Of course it matters!
Of course it does, of course it does. Be careful which team you join, then. I'll accept your reward tokens, either way.
No, I suppose not.
No. The important thing is that orbs get pushed back into the altars, whatever colour they are.
Where are we, exactly?
You will notice that, whenever you use a runecrafting altar, you enter another place: a self-contained island, or a cave, or some other place, which contains the true altar.
These temples are not exactly in runescape. they are pocket dimensions unto themselves: areas of folded space created by the energy of the rune altar.
so, we're in something similar?
Quite right. This is a shadow of the Wizards' Tower, created by own magic. What better place to study the mysteries of runecrafting?
What does that have to do with the guild?
Don't you see? The Runecrafting Guild exists in a similar pocket dimension, created by our own magic. What better place to study the mysteries of runecrafting?
What can I do here?
Wizard Acantha and Wizard Vief are running The Great Orb Project. It requires a large number of runecrafters, so you should speak with them if you want something to do.
Tell me about Acantha and Vief's project.
The Orb proj...I beg your pardon, The Great Orb Project? It's truly fascinating.
Wizard Acantha and Vief have found that energy energy leaks out of some of the Runecrafting altars.
They are recruiting teams of experienced runecrafters, such as yourself, to force the energy back in. Join one of the teams by speaking to Wizard Acantha or Wizard Vief.
When the Wizards have enough helpers, I will open a portal to the Air Altar. The energy appears in the form of floating orbs.
these can be moved by means of wands that attract or repel them. Acantha or Vief will give you one of each wand.
Your goal is to move the correct colour orb to the altar stone, while keeping the other orbs away.
Wizard Acantha favours the green orbs, while Wizard Vief favours the yellow ones.
You will also have a third wand, which allows you to make magical barriers to block the opposing team's orbs.
After two minutes, the team that has absorbed the most orbs wins that altar. I then open a portal to the next altar in the sequence.
After you have visited all eight altars, you will be returned hear.
What is in it for me?
A fair question. we have agreed on a token scheme that allows you to choose from several rewards.
When you return from the last altar, your senior wizard will give you a number of tokens.
you will get 50 tokens per altar that your team has captured, provided that you contribute to the capture in some way.
you will get an extra if your team captured more altars overall, or 50 extra if it is a draw. You can exchange the tokens for rewards by speaking to me.
you may also find rune essence appearing in your inventory at the end of each round.
this is a side product of the absorption process and you are free to use it as you wish.
Which colour orb is best?
Wizard Acantha believes that the green orbs are best. Wizard Vief believes that the yellow ones are. You should help out the wizard whose team you join.
But what do you think?
Does it matter?
Of course it matters!
Of course it does, of course it does. Be careful which team you join, then. I'll accept your reward tokens, either way.
No, I suppose not.
No. The important thing is that orbs get pushed back into the altars, whatever colour they are.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello there...thanks for helping out Trufitus commune with the gods Bwana. We've been able to return to the village thanks to your help.

o: Is there anything interesting to do here?

pages.x: What do you do here?
Well, I tend the hardwood grove nearby, you can enter if you like and harvest some of the very fine hardwood that grows within.
Apart from that I'm a simple Tai Bwo Wannai villager...I like to try and find out what's going on in the mainland and the rest of the known world.
Is there anything interesting to do around here?

o: Do I get anything for doing this?
Where can I get a machete from?
Where is the fence that needs to be repaired?

pages.x: Do I get anything for doing this?
Yes Bwana, you gain experience in woodcutting. In addition many members of the community will reward you with trading sticks, our local currency, for your efforts.
Trading sticks?
Correct Bwana, trading sticks! It's our form of local currency! Everything you do to help out in the village will give you some favour, but there's a maximum limit!
When you've reached one hundred percent, you cannot gain any more favour, you need to cash in your favour for trading sticks before you can increase your favour again.

o: Who do I get trading sticks from?
Where can I get a machete from?
Where is the fence that needs to be repaired?

pages.x: Who do I get trading sticks from?
Well Bwana, there's a good ten villagers I know of who would show their appreciation for your effort. Who do you want to ask about?
Sharimika is married to Mamma Bufetta, Bwana. They live in the houses just in front of the tribal statue.
Mamma Bufetta lives with her family in the building that faces the stone statue, she lives there with her husband Sharimika and her daughter Layleen.
Layleen is a young girl, the daughter of Mamma Bufetta and Sharimika, she lives with her parents.
Karaday is a young man and his chosen profession is fishing, he follows after his father Safta Doc in that respect.
You can find him usually around the center of the village, that is when he's not off fishing.
Safta Doc used to be a fisherman, but he's just about retired now. He has an interesting profession which you might like to talk to him about.
You'll find him usually near the building with the anvil in it. It's just slightly north of the village statue.
Gabooty is a bit of a mystery, no one's sure where he came from!
He's quite helpful though, you can find him in the middle of the village enclosure, to the south of Sharimika's house.
Fanellaman was a fisherman, he's retired now, but he'll try and regale you with tales of his salty sea dog days. He's often walking up and down the western beach.
Jagbakoba is a wild hunter. He can be a bit aggressive but he'll reward anyone who helps to keep the village in good order.
You'll find him to the south of the enclosure, near the fires.
Ah Rionasta! He's an enterprising man! Had a very good idea and is now much in demand, you'll find him between the blacksmith's and Timfraku's hut.
Murcaily! That's me! Well, what do you want to know?! I look after the teak and mahogany trees and make sure that we get payment of anyone who uses the facility.
And I'm usually standing just about here!
Ok, thanks.
Where can I get a machete from?
You can purchase a standard machete from Jiminua's store. Gabooty has a selection of local items which you may like to purchase, including better machetes.
Also, you may like to chat to Safta Doc, he may have a deal you'll find interesting.
Where is this jungle?
You'll find much of it to the southern end of Tai Bwo Wannai, outside of the village. Some is tougher than others so you may have difficulties cutting it back.
Beware though Bwana, those bushes can conceal a great many dangers or trophies, it could be the death... or the making of you!
What do you mean by that?
It means that you may find something you wish you hadn't but then discover something you never thought you could!
If you find me too vague, go and have a chat with Sharimika about it!
Where is the fence that needs to be repaired?
This is to the South Bwana, you should see that there are sections which are rotten, but some other passers-by sometimes help out repairing it.
You'll need some thatching spars and a machete in order to repair the fence though Bwana.
Ok, thanks.
Ok, thanks.

conversations.section: Talk-to

pages.x: Greetings, desert traveller. Do you require the services of Ali Morrisane's flying carpet fleet?

o: Tell me about this magic carpet fleet.
No, but I had some questions.
(If the player has completed at least the easy Desert tasks) I'd like to see what's lost and found.

pages.x: What? You haven't heard of Ali Morrisane? Possibly the greatest salesman in all the Kharidian Desert, if not all RuneScape?
Can I help you with anything else?
The latest idea from the great Ali Morrisane. Desert travel will never be the same again.
So how does it work?
The carpet or the whole enterprise?
Tell me about how the carpet works.
I'm not really too sure; it's just an enchanted rug really, made out of special Ugthanki hair. It flies to whatever destination its owner commands.
Are they for sale then?
Do you think I'm mad? Do you think that Ali Morrisane would throw his magic carpet monopoly away?
Well, perhaps if I offered the right price.
Not a hope. Could you imagine the mess there'd be if people were constantly zooming through Al Kharid and Pollnivneach? It would be chaos.
This way, we can keep the carpet traffic outside towns and other busy places.
I suppose getting stuck in a carpet jam could get a bit tiresome.
Just think of the friction burns you would get if you were in a carpet crash.
Can I help you with anything else?
Tell me about the enterprise.
It's quite simple really.
Ali Morrisane has hired myself and a few others to set up carpet stations at some of the desert's more populated places and run flights between the stations.
So why has he limited the service to just the desert.
I don't think Ali is prepared to take on Gnome Air just yet. Their gliders are much faster than our carpets.
Besides that, I think we are in the short-haul business, something that would only work in harsh conditions like the desert.
Why is that?
I suppose because people would just walk.
Getting lost isn't too much of a problem generally, but it's a different matter when you're in the middle of the Kharidian Desert with a dry waterskin and no idea which direction to go in.
You're right, I guess. How's the business going?
Not too bad. The hubs are generally quite busy, but the stations in Uzer and the Bedabin Camp could do with a bit more traffic.
A growth market, I guess.
Can I help you with anything else?
I'll help you as much as I can.

o: Is that your pet monkey nearby?
Where did you get that hat?

pages.x: What are you doing here?
Can I help you with anything else?
Is that your pet monkey nearby?
He's his own monkey, he does whatever suits him, a total nuisance.
I detect a degree of hostility being directed towards the monkey.
I shouldn't say this really, but sometimes I begin to question some of Ali Morrisane's ideas. He says that associating a monkey with any product will increase sales.
I just don't know what will be next!
Frogs?
I doubt it; amphibians don't have the same cutesy factor as monkeys.
I'm confused. I thought you didn't like monkeys.
I don't dislike monkeys, it's just THAT monkey. I don't know, I might just be paranoid, but I think he's, well...evil.
Hmm, interesting.
Would you? It sometimes gives me these stares... ~A visible shiver runs down his back.
I would be really grateful if you could get that monkey off my back.
Can I help you with anything else?
Where did you get that hat?
My fez? I got it from Ali Morrisane; it's a uniform of sorts. Apparently it makes us more visible, but I'm not too sure about it.
Well, it is quite distinctive.
Do you like it? I haven't really made my mind up about it yet. You see it's not all that practical for desert conditions.
How so?
Well, it doesn't keep the sun out of my eyes and after a while sitting out in the desert they really begin to burn.
Can I help you with anything else?

conversations.section: In the Fist of Guthix waiting area / Talking to him / After talking to Fiara

pages.x: Welcome to this grand cave of Guthix, traveller.

o: Who's the weird looking giant earwig?

pages.x: So, what is this place?
This is a sacred site of Guthix.
Why is it sacred?
Guthix places guardians in places of holy power. There is one such guardian here.
But what is special about this place?
It exudes a dangerous magical power that we have been entrusted to protect.
Where did this power come from?
It comes from the centre of the big cave.
What's special about the centre?
It's very magical.
Yes, I get that. Why is it magical?
Something to do with the Fist of Guthix.
And what is that, exactly?
The truth is, none of us really know.
This place is special to Guthix, because Fiara is here.
And we know it has something to do with the 'Fist of Guthix' because Fiara occasionally mentions it.
But other than that, we only have theories. Do you want to hear about them?
Well, this is definitely the truth. Don't believe what Alran and Pontimer tell you, they are just making it up.
At the end of the God Wars, Guthix returned to Gielinor and was angered by the destruction caused by the other gods in their vanity and quest for power.
So, maybe he punched the ground in anger, leaving an imprint of power on the ground that has lasted ever since.
Because he was angry at the time, the power would have been tainted with aggression, which is why he left Fiara as a guardian, to make sure the power did not escape unfettered.
Do you want to hear another theory?
This is Pontimer's personal delusion on the subject.
After the God Wars, Guthix found something dangerous here and used his power to protect it.
What did he find?
I don't know for certain, but it must be under that strange impression in the big cave. I think that mark is some sort of ward that Guthix has left to protect the site.
So where does the Fist of Guthix come into this, then?
Exactly! That's what I told him. It just doesn't make sense. My theory makes much more sense.
Do you want to hear another theory?
This is what Alran thinks, for what it's worth...which isn't very much, if you ask me.
Guthix has apparently left us a test. He deliberately created this site of power as a test of individual strength and balance.
Does Guthix do that sort of thing?
Well, no! I agree with you entirely. This theory has so many holes that it makes no sense at all!
Do you want to hear another theory?
I'd better get going.
I'd better get going.
Who's the weird looking giant earwig?
Shhh! Give Fiara some respect! She can hear you, you know.
Fiara? It has a name?
Of course, Guthix chooses names for all his guardians.
If...err...Fiara is a Guardian, what is she guarding?
She guards this site. It is a holy site of Guthix.

o: How long has Fiara been here?

pages.x: How long has Fiara been here?
Errr, ages. Since the end of the God Wars I think. She doesn't talk about that much.

o: So what are you doing here?

pages.x: So, what is this place?
I'd better get going.
I'd better get going.
I'd better get going.

conversations.section: In the Polypore Dungeon

pages.x: Mmmm?

o: I'd like to ask you about yourself.
I'd like to ask you about this place.
I'd like to ask you about these creatures.

pages.x: Hello, I'm Player.
Skip the chit-chat, human.
I'd like to ask you about yourself.
Alright.
I'd like to ask you about this place.
This place? It is my home. What about it?

o: Why is the cave full of fungus?

pages.x: Why is the cave full of fungus?
Fungi are incredibly flexible life forms. I can imbue my powers into them, then grow them all over the beasts of the cave to make new kinds of creature.
When I arrived here, the cave already contained fungi because this is a naturally damp region. I have simply encouraged the growth of these amazing organisms.
What do you do here?
I do whatever I wish! There is no tribe here to make demands of me. My powers are mine to use as I please.
I have learned to imbue my skinweaving powers into the fungus of this cave. By growing it onto the native beasts, I have created new forms of life.
I also make simple garments of mycelium. The merchant sells these upstairs.
If you gather flakes of my fungus from my creatures, you can try to stitch the fungus to the mycelium garments to make protective armour imbued with my magical powers.
Let's talk about something else.
If you must.
I'd like to ask you about these creatures.
My creatures? Alright, go ahead.

o: What loot can I get from them?

pages.x: What are these creatures?
When I first arrived here, they were mindless beasts lumbering around the cave, squatting in slime. They had brute strength, but nothing more.
As I learned to imbue my powers into the native fungi, I was able to grow my fungi onto the creatures, and I adapted their bodies to receive it.
In my creatures, I have achieved a perfect combination of the magical powers of the fungus with the strength and voracity of the beast.
How should I fight them?
When a human sees a strange creature, their instinct is to kill it. Your race is strange indeed!
Nevertheless, you may try to cull them, if you dare; while I enjoy creating them, the fully-formed beasts are of no use to me. You will need skill, human.
My fungus is powerful, and some of the creatures cannot even be harmed except by immensely skilled slayers.
Furthermore, you should know that my fungus makes the creatures resilient to physical attacks. You may have more success using your magical powers.
If you let the larger creatures touch you, their fungus will attempt to infest you. This will kill you very quickly, so keep your distance.
The neem drupes that grow upstairs can be ground up to extract their oil. This is a natural fungicide. You can collect it in a jug.
Splashing the neem oil on my creatures will weaken my fungus for a moment. If you daren't approach the creature to do this, get another human to do it for you.
While the fungus is weakened, the creature will be confused, and it will be unable to cast magical attacks for a short time. Try not to die horribly.
What loot can I get from them?
Spores and flakes of fungus are fairly common. If you collect enough spores, you may be able to grow them on a polypore stick.
Polypore sticks are found on the ganodermic beasts, the large ones. If you grow spores on a polypore stick, you can create a powerful magical staff.
The flakes of fungus can be attached to mycelium garments that I make, turning them into magical armour. The merchant upstairs can sell you the garments.
He is strange, even for a human, but he runs his little shop adequately. Apart from that I have created a special fungus that can be eaten by humans.
I have named it the Gorajian Mushroom. It is imbued with my skinweaving powers.
When you eat a gorajian mushroom, it will restore some of your health immediately, and you will benefit from a healing effect for a short period.
The healing effect makes you take less damage when you are harmed by a human like yourself. You might even gain a little health if the damage was sufficiently slight.
The effect is triggered by the spiritual conflict of the combatants. If you are fighting monsters, there will be no spiritual conflict, so the healing does nothing.
Even if your foe is human, their origin may be too different from yours to trigger the healing effect.
Okay, I'll keep an eye out for those things.
If they don't interest you, maybe you'll be able to sell them on.
Let's talk about something else.
If you must.
I'll leave you alone now.

o: The Ramokee Skinweaver does not appear to care.

conversations.section: In New Varrock / Standard dialogue

pages.x: What is this book of yours?
ZEMO CHORES! YOU DO!
These are your chores? And you want me to do them? Why would I help you?
GIVE MARKS!
You'll pay me to do your chores for you.
YES! YES! YOU DO!
I have some questions for you...

o: I need to be able to talk to cats.

pages.x: BIG ZEMO MAKE DO!
CLEAN AND TIDY! SPY AND EXTORT!
ALL HATE TINY ZEMO! NOT MY FAULT!
He makes you do his dirty work?
YES!
MARKS! EACH CHORE!
For each chore I do, you'll give me zemomarks?
MORE MARKS EACH FINISH!
And each time I finish the quests in this place, I'll get more zemomarks?
NEW VARROCK ARMOUR UPGRADES!
Oh, and upgrades to my Varrock armour? What, like one upgrade for each difficulty level I complete?
YES! YES! YES!
EASY GIVES BETTER MINING!
MEDIUM GIVES BETTER SMELTING!
HARD GIVES BETTER SMITHING!
ELITE MAKES WORK AT ALL FURNACE!
Anything else?
What is it?
ARGH!
What?

o: Tiny Zemouregal is staring at you, unblinking. It's more than a bit unnerving.

pages.x: Why are you looking at me like that?
ARGH!
Never mind.
ARGH!
Forget I asked.
TINY ZEMO!
OR JUST TINY FOR SHORT!
I gathered that much, but where did you come from and what do you do here?
BIG ZEMO MAKE FOR CHORES!
He made you a minion to do chores for him?
YES! ALSO PET!
And you're asking me to do your chores for you?
YES! LAZY!
YOU DO! GET MARKS!
Won't, er 'Big Zemo' find out?
NO! HATE HIM! ... BE FRIEND?
TAKE KITTY TALKER! HAVE FUN!
ARGH!
ARGH!
ARGH!
Never mind.

conversations.section: In Yanille

pages.x: Hello.
Hello, hello, and a most warm welcome to my Hunter Emporium. We have everything the discerning Hunter could need.
Would you like me to show you our range of equipment? Or was there something specific you were after?

o: Okay, let's see what you've got.
Do you have any Hunter wisdom to share?

pages.x: Okay, let's see what you've got.
I'm not interested, thanks.
Well, if you do ever find yourself in need of the finest Hunter equipment available, then you know where to come.
Who's that guy over there?
Him? I think he might be crazy. Either that or he's seeking attention.
He keeps trying to sell me these barmy looking weapons he's invented. I can't see them working, personally.
Do you have any Hunter wisdom to share?
Some creatures can be particularly fond of certain food. If you bait your trap it's more likely that you'll catch the critters.
So, I need to use bait?
Sometimes it's essential. I remember when I was hunting in Isafdar, the animals there wouldn't even look at a trap unless I used bait.
Those pawya and grenwalls aren't easily fooled.

o: How did you find out which bait to use?

pages.x: How did you find out which bait to use?
After watching them for a while I noticed that the grenwalls ate the pawya, so I realised I could use pawya meat to catch grenwall.
But how did you catch the pawya to start with?
That was harder to figure out. I could tell they didn't eat meat, so I tried other baits and found out that they couldn't resist papaya fruit.
Anyway, would you like me to show you our range of equipment or was there something specific you were after?
Thanks for your help.
It's always a pleasure to share Hunter knowledge.
Would you like me to show you our range of equipment or was there something specific you were after?

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?
I'd like to change my teleport point.

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
For completing the Ardougne set, you are presented with a cloak.
This cloak will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Ardougne set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Ardougne set rewards, speak to Ardougne's town crier, Doctor Orbon in East Ardougne church, or myself.
Ardougne cloak 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Ardougne cloak 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
No thanks.
Ardougne cloak 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Ardougne cloak 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,000 coins.
No thanks.
I'd like to change my Watchtower Teleport point.

conversations.section: After Lunar Diplomacy

pages.x: Hello there.
Ah, a visitor from a distant land. How can I help?

o: Have you got anything to trade?
It's a very interesting house you have here.
There is a lunar spell I can't use in my spellbook - can you help me?

pages.x: It's a very interesting house you have here. Does he have a name?
Why of course. It's Berty.
Berty? Berty the leg house?
Yes.
May I ask why?
It just has a certain ring to it, don't you think? Beeerteeee!
You're ins...
Insane? Very.
There's a lunar spell in my spellbook that I can't use. Could you...?
Help you? Certainly. It's one I've just rediscovered! I can teach it to you if you like, but you have to listen to a story first.

o: Okay, I don't mind hearing stories.
I don't really have time right now.

pages.x: Okay, I don't mind hearing sto-
Wonderful!
Well, I was going through some ancient documents recently, expanding my knowledge of our great ancestors...
Hmm, actually, I think I had better go further back, so you will understand.
You know of our ancient war with the Fremennik that you recently healed?
Of course! I am a great diplomat, aren't I?
Some diplomat. Did you even discover WHY we were at war for so long?
Errr... You couldn't see eye to eye about magic, or something like that.
Not too far off; it goes deeper than that.
The Fremennik were actually the first to discover how to make runes, but there was disagreement within the tribe about the implications of making such powerful objects.
Most Fremennik felt we were stealing power from the gods.
They could not see past that to the great things we could do with such power, so we split from them and became the Moon Clan. Our ancient leader, who first
discovered the rune essence mine here on Lunar Isle, travelled far and wide searching for more places of power.
He and his followers built altars all over Gielinor - which you use today to create runes - and at their height
they made runes by the crateful.
They had perfected the process and even advanced it, creating altars that could create any type of rune regardless of the crafter's ability.
But the strife between the Moon Clan and the
Fremennik heightened. The Fremennik had grown strong in body, while our clan had grown strong in mind.
They overpowered our tribe and we retreated to Lunar Isle, where we have lived ever since. The Fremennik then swept
over Gielinor destroying the altars we had made, in an attempt to remove all trace of magic from the land.
That's all very interesting, but what's it got to do with this spell?
I'm getting to that!
The Fremennik were not as thorough as they thought.
They destroyed only the entrances to the altars, for the altars themselves were on a different plane, but they were successful in wiping out our ability to create runes.
That ability has only recently been rediscovered on the mainland, so I hear.
Our people were left isolated on Lunar Isle but we used it to our advantage.
Our control over Magic advanced beyond the need for runes and all knowledge of the altar locations passed from memory. Fortunately, some records
survived... The manuscript I discovered contains the teleportation spell to an advanced altar called Ourania.
It's an altar that allows the user, regardless of their Runecrafting ability, to craft any type of rune upon it.
Ourania is a powerful altar indeed. What state it is in after so many millennia, I know not, but it's interesting all the same.
So, will you teach me the spell?
Certainly.
*Baby Yaga whispers in your ear*
And now you know the teleportation spell, off with you! Go explore.
I don't really have ti-
*Sigh* Very well. Another time, perhaps.
Why do you ask questions if you're going to read my mind anyway?
I was being polite, silly foreigner.
I'm good thanks, bye.

conversations.section: Very rich / Man with a top hat

pages.x: Hello!
What do you want?
I was just wondering what you were doing here?
I ask myself the same question often.
What am I doing down here in these pits along with these filthy dregs of society?
And do you ever come up with an answer?
Always.
I'm here taking their money, that's what.
So how do these rat pits work?
Things work simply in the Ardougne ratpits.
If you have a kitten and at least 100 coins you can challenge someone else who also has a kitten and some spare change.
That sounds simple enough so far.
You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.
So then how do you win the challenge?
I was just getting to that. Both the gamblers' cats are placed inside of the fenced off area, and whoever kills 5 rats first wins.
That sounds vile and cruel.
It's a cruel world and the pits are no exception.
Every day guards are killed for no better reason than to sate the bloodlust of some despicable adventurer.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.
It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.
I agree. Cats have been known to be killed in fights.
Oh how terrible. Is there nothing you can do to save your cat?
Of course there is, you can instruct it to be cautious, and it will leave once it feels as if it is in danger.
Oh that sounds quite wise.
That depends on how you value your cat.
Sorry, I don't follow.
Well if your cat dies or it runs away you lose.
So the longer it stays in the fight the better chance you have of winning.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.
Wow that sounds like fun!
I don't know about that.
One thing I know though is that it's a quick way to make and lose money.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.
Is there a limit to how much you can bet?
Hmmm...let me see. If I'm not mistaken, you can currently bet up to a maximum of [number] coins.
That sounds like a silly amount of money to bet on a cat fight.
You'd be surprised what some people would be willing to bet.
There is a minimum bet of 100 coins too.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.
Can I challenge you and your cat?
No, not now, we don't really bet with outsiders.
But I'm not an outsider, am I not inside in the pits now?
I don't know, maybe once you've done something to win over my trust.
Can it be bought?
What?
Your trust.
No. Regular townsfolk don't like us, which leads us to distrust them and anyone else.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue east of Paterdomus

pages.x: Hello friend. What can I do for you?

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Morytania set, you are presented with some leggings.
These leggings will become increasingly useful as you complete greater difficulties of task sets.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all Tasks within a particular difficulty set, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Morytania set's Tasks are simple, some require certain skill levels, and others require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Morytania set rewards, speak to Robin in Port Phasmatys, the Strange Old Man at the Barrows, Old Man Ral in Meiyerditch or myself.
Morytania legs 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Morytania legs 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
No thanks.
Morytania legs 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Morytania legs 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,000 coins.
No thanks.

o: What is in it for me?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: What do you do here?
I'm here to help maintain the noticeboard nearby.
Mercenaries or survivors of Burgh De Rott usually want safe passage through the Myre and, regardless of their ability, they need assistance.
No one should trek through the Myre alone.
I make sure these people have an advert posted up on the board here so the more heroic types can offer them a secure journey to their destination.
Anything else?
How do I start?
Oh well that's easy, my child. Take a look at the noticeboard just here and pick a person to help.
That's it?
Indeed. The people who leave adverts will have left more information there. Some will be easier to defend than others; some fight, some don't.
You should pick someone you feel comfortable protecting.
Anything else?
What is in it for me?
Other than the feeling of doing good for your fellow man, you'll obtain a variety of rewards.
No doubt the person you take through the Myre will give a token of their appreciation.
That's it?
There is more to it. The people who you guide are just like you, they start off a bit more delicate though.

If you continue to guide the same people you'll find they can gain more experience, becoming better and navigating the swamp - even identifying what events might be next if you want to avoid certain encounters.
Well, that sounds like a nice reward for them. Anything else?
As the people gain experience, they'll know you more and may have unique rewards for you to show their appreciation of your continued support.
Again, they'll put all this up in their advert on the noticeboard so I advise you to check that for the proper details.
Anything else?
Nothing, thanks.
Saradomin be with you.

conversations.section: NovtumberFest / When talked to

pages.x: Welcome to NovtumberFest!

o: What is there to do at NovtumberFest?
Tell me about the bar crawl.

pages.x: We've sent out our cart to travel around Gielinor to spread word of our little get-together.
However, the driver is known to get into the occasional spot of trouble.
If you see him out and about could you check on him and make sure he's safe?
And if he's not, help him out of whatever trouble he's got in to.
So you want me to take care of him?
Oh, he's not that bad, but he does sometimes need a nudge in the right direction.
He's always generous to those who help him out, though.
The perfect thing to go with a cold drink is a nice meaty sausage.
We have only the best sausages at NovtumberFest. Jakob is very particular.
Have a go at cooking some for yourself on the grills.
Just follow your nose and you'll find your way there.
A little more intensive this one.
You too can experience what it is like to be a bar person on a very, very busy shift.
Try to serve all of the customers that you can and get rewarded for your hard work.
I'll warn you - it won't be easy, but it should be fun.
Test your aim! Nice and simple this one.
Just pick your target and fire away at it with arrows.
Just imagine the target is someone you don't like - always cheers me up no end.
A lovely little racetrack inside our freezer-tent.
It's a bit slippery, but that makes it all the more fun.
Just try to stay up on your feet!
To keep the drink flowing we need a good supply of hops.
You should be able to find lots of hops growing around the crater.
If you want to help you can harvest some and then deposit them in the hops crate, over by the glassblowing area.
Moritz is our man in charge of keeping our supply of steins up for our drinks.
A remarkable amount of them get broken during the festivities.
If you head over to the furnace he'll set you up with the equipment you need.
We can never have too many barrels. We always keep losing some.
I know the driver keeps taking some out and about round Gielinor, but he never seems to return with a full cart-full.
If you want to help out with making us more go talk to Lukas by his workbench.
Ah, yes. The wizard. He came to us and asked if we would mind helping him out.
I didn't expect it to cause such a big disturbance though.
Oh well, he seems to be keeping things under control, just about.
Probably best to go talk to Wizard Deedit yourself for more information on the experiment though.
There is no more lovely a way to display your joy at the world around you than with a dance.
Join Mila and Elias on the tables and show everyone how happy you are.
The centrepiece of our little celebration.
Isn't it delightful? I could just watch it go round and round for hours.
Hop on and give it a whirl, it is so much fun.
The lovely Linus. He's the person to go for any cosmetics you might be looking for.
All of the cosmetics for sale in Linus' shop are also available as drops from doing the activities.
Hop on and give it a whirl, it is so much fun.
Portals seem to be all the rage at these kinds of gatherings, so we made sure that we had some too.
They're really handy for zipping around the world.
Leni will be able to keep you up to date with which portals are active.
Of course, they light up when they can be used, so you could just look out for the lights.

conversations.section: Before entering court / Prosecuting

pages.x: I need to ask you some questions about the court case.
If you must.
Goblins.
How do you feel about goblins?
How do you feel about goblins?
Goblins are monsters, and monsters are evil. We can't go on treating monsters as if they are equal to us, and have the same rights to live here.
Monsters have no idea of right and wrong, they're not civilised, and they don't contribute anything to society, if they even know what the word means.
They need to be put down or moved on, pure and simple.
Do you know any goblins personally?
Do you know any goblins personally?
How can you socialise with a lesser species?
So that's a 'no', then.
How can you possibly get to know them? You can't even hold a conversation with them. They are put here for us to kill: you can't deny that.
How do you feel about cats?
How do you feel about cats?
I don't mind them. I prefer dogs, but cats are okay.
Well, cats can talk and have their own culture. By your reasoning, they would also be a target for H.A.M. hatred.
Show me a talking cat and I'll show you a monstrosity. Besides, cats are fuzzy and cute.
The incident.
Would you describe the incident to me?
Would you describe the incident to me?
We were holding a rally, and the speaker was whipping the crowd into a frenzy.
I was keeping an eye on the crowd, being on guard rotation, and heard a call of 'Thief!' from someone in the back row.
I grabbed the thief and threw him in one of our jails. We release criminals back into the surface after they've had some time to stew.
What can you tell me about the allegations that the goblin was beaten?
What can you tell me about the allegations that the goblin was beaten?
We didn't beat anyone, and certainly not a goblin. It wouldn't be...wise, after the recent events with Sigmund.
I handed him over no more roughly than I would any other low-life thief.
Was this an unusual occurrence?
Was this an unusual occurrence?
It was unusual that it was a goblin, but not unusual that someone would steal from us.
Somehow the location of our base has been leaked, and any worthless adventurer can infiltrate and steal from us. We take great pleasure in throwing them into jail.
The stolen items.
What items were missing?
What items were missing?
My fellow H.A.M. members reported the following missing: 1 opal, 1 raw chicken, logs, buttons, thread, 1 bronze hatchet, 1 pair of H.A.M.
gloves, 1 steel pickaxe, and 1 jade.
That list doesn't exactly match what was found at the scene of the crime.
He still stole from us! Hundreds of others attempt to steal from us, so they could have made off with the items.
Was anything of yours missing?
Was anything of yours missing?
Yes, my gloves. They have my initials embroidered on the edges.
Has anything like this happened before?
Has anything like this happened before?
You cannot begin to imagine. As soon as I put on the pink robe and bottoms, it feels like there are hands already in my pockets. It's that common.
Why are both of you in jail?
Why are both of you in jail? Surely, only one of you needs to be?
We countersued, of course, as the crime was clearly against us.
The judge decided that we should all remain in the courthouse until the court date, but they only have these jail cells to stay in. It's not right!
We'll sue them for improper accommodation!
Good luck with that.
I don't have any more questions.
I don't have any more questions.

conversations.section: Talk to / Afterwards / Normally

pages.x: Hi there, Player!

o: What do you have for sale?
I'd like to reclaim my portable telescope.
Do you know anything about starblooms?

pages.x: What do you have for sale?
Oh, all sorts of doodads related to my studies! Runes, gems, telescopes, Mining enhancements...
I should note that I only accept stardust as payment, though. I'm in need of it more than gold!
What are you doing?
I'm studying the skies, building upon the knowledge of the great Scorpius who came before us!
How exciting!
I'm glad you think so too! Astromancy has received a lot of criticism from other wizards in the past.
But since my fellow astromancer, Wizard Chambers, used it to save Gielinor from Tuska they've slowly been coming around to its legitimacy.
My particular specialism is in star sprites, though.
Ever since I first laid eyes on one of the curious little fellows, I fell in love.
I couldn't find a single piece of research on them, so I knew I had to be the one to change that.

o: How can I find shooting stars?
What can I get from shooting stars?

pages.x: What are shooting stars?
Shooting stars are large chunks of rock that occasionally fall down to Gielinor from the skies above.
Well, if I didn't already have a fear of being knocked out from a space rock appearing out of nowhere, now I do.
Statistically, you have nothing to worry about!
Assuming you stumble across a crash star and have managed to avoid getting knocked out cold, you can mine through it to free its inhabitant at its core.
I see, thanks!
How can I find shooting stars?
You can scour the skies for nearby shooting stars using a telescope.
Telescopes can be built in your player-owned house, but you can also find some public telescopes in Varrock Palace library, and the observatory.
What about your telescope over there?
Oh, I wish that beauty was mine! Alas, it belongs to Wizard Rosalina.
He gave me permission to use it, though, so I suppose I can pass that permission on down to you.
I should also mention that not all telescopes are built equally.
You might find that some, due to having been constructed with lower-tiered woods, are a bit less accurate than others.
What does their accuracy affect?
Well, the more accurate a telescope is, the shorter the timeframe it'll give for when the next shooting star will land.
It will also give you a more accurate estimate of the star's size.
That's good to know.
What can I get from shooting stars?
Crashed stars are jam-packed with stardust, I use stardust in my studies, so feel free to bring some to me and I can trade you for some things you might find useful.
If you mine the star all the way to the core, I've also heard that the star sprite inside may aid you with some sort of temporary Mining enhancement!
Intriguing!
Do you know anything about starblooms?
Ooh, starbloom flowers! I've never seen one myself, but I once interviewed a star sprite who cultivated fields of starblooms back home.
They're full of magic and very pretty.
The starbloom flowers, that is. Star sprites are move cute than pretty.
Anyway, some of the stardust I've magically analysed contained trace amounts of otherworldly pollen.
Most of it gets burnt up when a shooting star lands, but over time, it's soaked into Gielinorian soil.
That organic residue is then absorbed by other seeds, or eaten by monsters, that get eaten by bigger nastier monsters, that poop out the indigestible bits of less big and less naster monsters...
And that's how you get starbloom seeds.
So you're saying I can get starbloom seeds by pickpocketing farmers who carry seeds and defeating particularly nasty monsters?
I'm...not saying that? But if that's how you choose to interpret what I'm saying, I guess I can't stop you.
So how would I grow starbloom seeds?
Well, it's not my area of expertise, but starblooms come from an entirely different animasphere.
To tune starbloom seeds to our anima mundi, you'd need to ground them in the magical field of our world's runescape.
So stick a battlestaff in a flower patch, and the starbloom flower will grow up that, like a grapevine frame?
Well...yes, actually. You seem to know more about this than I do!

conversations.section: After In Pyre Need

pages.x: Hail, Player! How are things?
I'm doing okay, thanks. Could I ask you some questions?
What would you like to ask about?
Could you tell me about the phoenix?
The phoenix is an ancient creature - older than either of us can comprehend.
It is a large, powerful avian creature, surrounded by flames and covered in a fiery plumage. It also has strong magical abilities.
Every five hundred years, as it reaches the limits of its lifespan, it returns to its roost to complete a ritual and be reborn.
You see, while not truly immortal, the phoenix can be reborn any number of times, so long as it completes its rebirth ritual.
Thanks to you, the phoenix will live on!
Thanks for the information. Now, back to my other questions.
What would you like to ask about?
Could you go over that ritual once more?
The ritual is not that complicated, really; it just requires certain ingredients and a set of dexterous hands.
In order to be reborn, the phoenix must be burnt alive on a funeral pyre woven from the wood of five particular trees.
You must weave a basket from the fletched twigs of cinnamon, sassafras, ailanthus, cedar and mastic trees.
This basket must be placed on the base of the pyre in the phoenix's roost, and then it must be lit.
You will need to best the phoenix in combat to weaken it so that it can succumb to the flames.
The phoenix will enter the pyre and be burnt to ashes. From these ashes, it will be reborn - young and strong again.
There are specimens of each tree growing inside the phoenix's lair, tended to by the phoenix's thralls in its absence and revived from the trees ashes whenever they die.
Each tree is on a separate level of the lair. You must collect the twigs before moving on.
It's pointless to continue on to a deeper level without having the twigs from all the levels before it.
Only fresh twigs will suffice for the ritual. If you leave the lair at any time, you will have to go through and collect fresh twigs from every tree.
There are some other items required for the ritual that you cannot get from inside the lair.
Oh? What would those be then?
Tools. Secateurs, to prune the trees and gather the twigs, a knife to fletch them and a tinderbox to light the pyre.
I did bring a bunch of the necessary tools with me, but I sold them to a passing trader once the phoenix was saved...
Thanks for the information. Now, back to my other questions.
What would you like to ask about?
Could you tell me about the phoenix's lair?
The phoenix's lair is a lava-filled cave, guarded by its thralls.
You see, the phoenix has power over life and death that is not limited to itself. It has the ability to resurrect lesser creatures.
These revived creatures now roam the phoenix's lair, guarding it from interlopers during the phoenix's long absences.
They attack all who enter, to weed out the weaklings and ensure only the worthy reach the phoenix in its roost, deep inside the cave.
Thanks for the information. Now, back to my other questions.
What would you like to ask about?
The phoenix mentioned granting me the right to challenge her.
Yes, she told me about this a short while ago. I was quite shocked; I didn't realise she was telepathic!
I see. I'm afraid I've forgotten the terms of our agreement.
Worry not, Player! I shall remind your tired brain.
Once a day, you may enter into the phoenix's lair, and if you make it to the phoenix's roost you may challenge her to combat.
You'll need to complete the same ritual as you did when you first helped the phoenix in order for her to appear before you; she will only allow you to fight her if her rebirth is assured.
If you defeat the phoenix, she will give you another two quills, which you can use to create Summoning pouches for summoning the phoenix's essence.
You should take care on your way through the lair, though; the phoenix's guardians will try their best to defeat you now that their mistress is safe.
Once the duel with the phoenix is over and you have said your farewells, you must leave the lair and you will unable to return until the next day.
Immediately after rebirth, the phoenix is small and exhausted. It will quickly regain its former size and strength though, and this is the reason for the day's respite.
I think that's everything.
Yes, you covered everything, and in detail. Thank you. Now, back to my other questions.
What would you like to ask about?
That's all the information I need for now.
Good day, Player, saviour of the phoenix, hero of Guthix!
Farewell!

conversations.section: Poor / Shirtless man

pages.x: Hello!
What are you doing here?
Trying to win my shirt back. I lost it last night in a silly bet.
Well I hope your luck improves. I doubt it can get any worse.
Well I've little left to lose, maybe some more hair and my trousers.
I really think you should try to hold on to them.
So how do these rat pits work?
Things work simply in the Ardougne ratpits.
If you have a kitten and at least 100 coins you can challenge someone else who also has a kitten and some spare change.
That sounds simple enough so far.
You then agree on a wager. It's rumoured that some ratcatchers can talk to their own cats and give them tactics to aid them.
So then how do you win the challenge?
I was just getting to that. Both the gamblers' cats are placed inside of the fenced off area, and whoever kills 5 rats first wins.
That sounds vile and cruel.
It's a cruel world and the pits are no exception.
Every day guards are killed for no better reason than to sate the bloodlust of some despicable adventurer.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.
It sounds a little dangerous for my cat.
I agree. Cats have been known to be killed in fights.
Oh how terrible. Is there nothing you can do to save your cat?
Of course there is, you can instruct it to be cautious, and it will leave once it feels as if it is in danger.
Oh that sounds quite wise.
That depends on how you value your cat.
Sorry, I don't follow.
Well if your cat dies or it runs away you lose.
So the longer it stays in the fight the better chance you have of winning.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.
Wow that sounds like fun!
I don't know about that.
One thing I know though is that it's a quick way to make and lose money.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.
Is there a limit to how much you can bet?
Hmmm...let me see. If I'm not mistaken, you can currently bet up to a maximum of [number] coins.
That sounds like a silly amount of money to bet on a cat fight.
You'd be surprised what some people would be willing to bet.
There is a minimum bet of 100 coins too.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.
Can I challenge you and your cat?
No, not now, we don't really bet with outsiders.
But I'm not an outsider, am I not inside in the pits now?
I don't know, maybe once you've done something to win over my trust.
Can it be bought?
What?
Your trust.
No. Regular townsfolk don't like us, which leads us to distrust them and anyone else.
One more thing...
Thanks for your help.

o: Tell me about the Big High War God.

pages.x: Me dead, but me not go.
Long ago, me have vision of Big High War God. Me chosen prophet of Big High War God.
Me think, when me die, Big High War God take me to reward in Yu'biusk. Every day great battle, every night great victory with feasting.
Big High War God not come. But me have faith. Some day Big High War God come for me, take me to him. Until then me hang on, not let go into death.

o: Tell me about the Big High War God.

pages.x: Me Hopespear of Narogoshuun tribe.
You go to Yu'biusk? What you see?

o: It was everything you hope for.

pages.x: It was a wasteland. It had been so devastated by war that nothing could live there.
All dead? No goblins fighting glorious battles?
No one. It was all empty.
You lie!
I'm not lying. It's what I saw.
Even so. Yu'biusk is place of Big High War God. Land of Goblins. It where goblins should go.
Me happy now old priest bones rest in Yu'biusk. Me sure Big High War God take me to live with him soon.
It was everything you hope for. A paradise for goblins. The Big High War God commands them personally there.
Thank you! I know Big High War God still care for us! I wait for him here. Some day he take me to Yu'biusk to live with him.
Me happy now old priest bones rest in Yu'biusk. Me sure Big High War God take me to live with him soon.
When me die, goblins burn bones and scatter ashes. No more Hopespear bones.
Me stay here, look after goblin temple, wait for Big High War God to take me to Yu'biusk. Me know he come for me someday. Me have faith.
Big High War God greatest of all gods! He take puny goblins from Yu'biusk and make them mighty warriors for great war of gods!
When gods go to war, goblin soldiers so good that Big High War God sell tribes to fight for different gods.
Big High War God fight with different gods, sometimes for one, sometimes another.
Other gods fight for their own reasons, but Big High War God fight for war itself!
Before I have prophecy, goblin tribes fight one another very much.
Long ago we fight other people: beardy-short-people, pointy-hat-short-people, keen-bladed-tall-people.
But other people build cities with walls, and we not able to attack them any more.
There not enough food for all tribes. So tribes with no food attack tribes who have food. Goblin war last many, many years.
Finally, all tribes meet at this place, where temple is now.
It rain many days. But rain not stop goblins. Goblin feet churn up ground with rain and goblin blood. All ground turn to mud. That why it called Battle of Plain of Mud.
Battle last many days. Both sides same size, none win, none lose. Goblin bodies everywhere, many dead.
Me not important general, me not might sergeant. Me just goblin trooper. But one night in tent me have dream.
Me see throne of Big High War God. He shine with light so bright me cannot see him, but me can hear his voice.
He say, 'Stop the fighting!' He say, 'Fighting good, but not if all my followers die! You must not fight one another so much you all die!'
Then he say, 'Today I cannot lead you. But someday I send Chosen Commander to lead you.' And I see Chosen Commander in dream.
He wear shining armour and stand at front of army of goblins.
Behind Chosen Commander, army of goblins stretch to horizon. Many goblins, too many to count, and banners of every tribe. Banners of all tribes, even Dorgesh-tribe.
Other races, they run away from mighty goblin army! Chosen Commander make goblins build siege machines, they break down walls of cities.
Then goblins march in and kill everyone!
And when all dead, Big High War God himself appear and sit on great throne of bronze and rule over all, with Chosen Commander beside him.
Then I wake from dream. I know it true vision from Big High War God. I run to general of my tribe, and he call other generals for emergency meeting.
I tell all generals what I see. They decide to stop fighting so goblins not all die. By this time in battle so many had died that there enough food for all.
Then generals set goblins to work building temple on site of battle. It sink into mud, so they turn it into underground temple, and keep it secret from others.
Goblins write down my vision in goblin holy book, along with history of goblins and commandments of Big High War God.

o: Tell me more about the Big High War God.
Tell me more about the Chosen Commander.

pages.x: Me not know much more. In vision, Chosen Commander wear heavy armour and big helmet that cover face. Me not know what he look like.
I see him give orders, but he far away, me not hear his voice.
Me think Chosen Commander will be great goblin general. But Big High War God chose me to have vision, not great general, so Chosen Commander could be anyone.

conversations.section: Livid Farm / Talk-to / Without witchdoctor camo outfit pieces, with Mambo's potion, or having drunk Mambo's potion

pages.x: Hi Pauline.
Oh, hi. How can I help you?

o: Can you tell me how to work on your farm?
Can I claim some rewards now?
Can you tell me more about why you started this farm?

pages.x: Can you tell me how to work on your farm?
Sure, what part of the farm do you want to know about?

o: How can I fertilise the soil?
How can I cure the diseased plants?
What do I do with the pile of produce?
How do I fix the fences?

pages.x: How can I fertilise the soil?
After I've harvested a patch, I will replant a livid seed and it will need fertilising for it to appear.
I'll get around to this eventually, but, if you cast the Fertilise Soil spell on the patch, you'll get further knowledge in Magic and Farming.
How can I cure the diseased plants?
You will see my plants get diseased quite a lot. It seems they are susceptible to the parasites native to this isle.
Cast the Cure Plant spell on the crop and you'll then have to refine your spell to the particular strain of livid you see growing in that patch.
Then, bingo: Magic and Farming experience are all yours. If you don't manage to do this, I'll do it myself, although there's no reward in it for you if I do.
How can I re-energise you?
Ah, you've noticed how tiring it is running this farm.
Well, you can simply cast the Energy Transfer spell on me, followed by a few encouraging words, and I'll be right-as-rain.
In exchange, you'll receive some Magic and Agility experience. I can recover by myself, but your assistance would be much appreciated.
What do I do with the pile of produce?
When I harvest the livid, I'll teleport it over to the produce pile.
Here, you can grab up to ten livid and then bunch them together with string using the String Jewellery spell. Then, place the bunched produce in the trade wagon.
With this last step, you'll get experience in Magic and Crafting. Be quick, though: like the other tasks, I'll end up doing it myself.
How do I fix the fences?
So, you've spotted that the fences often get into a state of disrepair. I'm not sure if it's those pesky suqah or the sea air, but the wood here doesn't last very long.
Pick up some Lunar lumber from the corner of the farm and use the Plank Make spell to turn them into fence posts. Then, simply use them on the broken fence.
You'll get Magic and Construction experience for your effort upon affixing the post.
What rewards will I get?
Mainly experience in your Magic, Farming, Crafting, Agility and Construction skills. I think you'll find your time and effort is well rewarded.
You can cast all the spells regardless of your Magic level, but you won't get the Magic XP if you don't have the correct level.
I'll also keep an eye on how much produce you're helping to create and, after so much work, it's only fair that I teach you the secrets of some new spells!
Each task enables me to ship more produce over to Chieftain Brundt. Here, let me show you.
Can you tell me more about why you started this farm?
Sure. Like I said, Lokar brought me this strain of vine and asked me to enhance it for Chieftain Brundt's use in protecting the province.
I imagine it would work well as a particularly vicious fence!
I get that, but why help Lokar? He's a pirate. How can you trust him?
A pirate?
I don't think so. He travels the sea in search of treasure and fortune; such an adventurer! I think he's excellent and so exciting.

o: I'm glad you've found someone that makes you happy.

pages.x: I'm not sure that's true. I doubt the innocents he attacks and the villagers he plunders would see it that way.
What? Don't be silly, he's nothing like that. He's travelled to distant lands, experienced the many cultures of our world! He's a fabulous man!
I'm glad you've found someone that makes you happy.
Thank you. I do hope he'll visit me soon.
What of giving away the secrets of the Moon Clan magic?
It's true, our knowledge is most sacred, but, this way they only receive the end-product of that knowledge. It still rests with the likes of me and, to some extent, you.

o: Well, you seem to have it all under control.
I hope Lokar sees this the same way as you do.

pages.x: Well, you seem to have it all under control.
Yes, I know what I'm doing. You should go talk to Lokar at the dock in Rellekka. If you see him, tell him to come and visit me soon!
I hope Lokar sees this the same way as you do.
I'm sure he does. You should go and talk to him yourself at the dock in Rellekka. If you see him, tell him to come and visit me soon!
See you around.
I do hope so.
