I like angry!
I'm sorry I killed you.
I hate sorry! Makes me more angry! WANT TO KILL YOU!
Please try to calm down.
Hate calm! Smash it! Hur hur hur!
I'm not really sorry.
That make me more angry! Uuuurgh!
Is there anything that doesn't make you angry?
No! I like angry! Hur hur hur!
I killed you really easily!
Uhhhhrrr...
Yeah! I could kill you again in my sleep!I think I might go off and kill some other kurask!
Uuuurrrh! Hate you!
What are you going to do about it? Eh? I totally owned you!
Hate you hate you hate you!
What do you think about up there?
Think?
You know, what goes through your tiny stuffed head?
Little bugs...
You have bugs living in you? Eww!
Little bugs! Stomp and crush and stomp!
Yeah! Stomp the bugs!
Stomp crush splat!
Smash! Destroy! Crunch break tear destroy splunch! Hurt wound kill hit punch stab slash kill!
'Splunch'? That is not a word!
I HATE WORDS! Kill all words!
You said 'kill' twice
I like kill! Hur hur hur!
Yeah! Kill smash destroy!
Kill smash destroy! Hur hur hur!
What have the bugs done to you?
Skitter skitter through head noise in ears behind eyes.
HATE THEM! Kill kill kill!
You can't, you've got no feet!
No feet...
Hate lack of feet! Stomp lack of feet! Kill crush destroy smash!
That makes no sense! You can't destroy the absence of something!
Hate requirement to make sense! Smash it kill it destroy kill kill!
You can't physically destroy an abstract concept. It's impossible!
Hate abstract concepts! hate impossible! Kill kill kill destroy smash!
This is getting both surreal and repetitive.

conversations.section: After Nomad's Elegy / In the Soul Wars lobby (if you spared Zanik) / Talk-to

pages.x: Wotcha guv'na!
Hello Zanik.
What? You'd be surprised how many people expect me to say that. Anyway, how can I help?

o: Can you tell me more about Soul Wars?
Can we talk about my own Soul Wars cape?

pages.x: Can you tell me more about Soul Wars?
Such as?
Can I have another tutorial?
Don't you know how to play already?
I forgot.
Well I have a guidebook if you want. I found crates of them if you need a copy.

o: The book sounds good; could I have a copy?

pages.x: I want another tutorial.
Well, according to the notes Zimberfizz left you should be able to reply the tutorial in your mind.
But how do I do that if I can't remember it?
Um, the notes say you have to think really hard about it. Give that a try?
Erm, okay. Hmmmmmm.
No, I don't think that's hard enough. Try again.
Okay, okay. Huuuuuuuuuuuunnnnnnnghhh!
Wait, I can sense seomthing happening! Keep going!
Huuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuunnnnghhh!
The book sounds good; could I have a copy?
Here you are!
How are you feeling?
It's complicated.
On the one hand I'm 'alive' again, and out of that terrible nightmare.
On the other, Death has made it clear that I have to remain here. So I can't see any of my family or friends.
Well, you come here, obviously, but not often enough.
It also means my adventures are over. This is it for me now; the replacement for an imp in a silly hat.
No family, no chance to redeem the Bandosians, no legacy with my own people.
Just me, Zanik, handing out capes.
But I really can't complain, can I? I have a friend who fought for me to drag me out of hell after all.
How many people get a second chance like this? Well third chance. Fourth, if you count the possession thing.
So yeah... taking it day by day I guess.
Can we talk about rewards?
Sure! There is a whole warehouse back here of things you can buy with Zeal.
What kinds of rewards are there?
There are some discarded items related to Nomad.
There are also strange blocks of white powder labeled 'XP'. I don't know what they do but they are in high demand.
Would you like to take a look?
Yes, let's take a look.
No thanks, not right now.
Can we talk about ammunition?
Can we talk about my Soul Wars cape?
Of course. What's the matter?
Could I swap my cape for a different colour?
Really? Changing your wardrobe for the season, Player?
What can I say? I am a creature of fashion!

conversations.section: In the Fist of Guthix waiting area

pages.x: Welcome, adventurer. Have you come to have a look at my fine wares?

o: Yes, I want to see what you're selling.
What currency are you trading in?
Why do all of your wares degrade?

pages.x: What currency are you trading in? It doesn't seem to be regular coins.
You are absolutely right, my friend. I exchange my goods for so called Fist of Guthix tokens.

o: How can I get hold of these tokens?
What are Fist of Guthix tokens?

pages.x: We try to store as much as we can, so that we're ready to use it once we know what it's for.
And what does that have to do with the tokens?
Oh yes, the tokens. Everyone is free to enter the contest we're running here, and the winners are rewarded with tokens which you can then trade in for goods.
If you want to know more, you should speak to Fiara.

o: I want to see what you're trading first.
I have more questions that I want answered.

pages.x: What are Fist of Guthix tokens?
Oh, they're nothing special in themselves. They are just tokens we use as currency.

o: How can I get hold of these tokens?

pages.x: I have to go now.
Can you recharge my items?
By items, I assume you mean items originally acquired from me. If so, the answer is yes, my friend. I gladly spread the power of Guthix, if I am able to.
That's great.
It certainly is. The power of Guthix does not come cheaply, though. So, I'm afraid I will have to charge you some tokens for it.
And I can only recharge items that have been completely depleted of their magical energy.
Sounds fair. So, how do I go about doing this?
Just hand me the item you want recharged and I'll see what I can do.

o: I want to see what you're selling first.
How can I get hold of these tokens?

pages.x: Okay, I'll do that.
Can you uncharge my items for me?
You don't want to keep the power of Guthix? That's strange. But yes, of course I can do this for you.
Please be aware that you won't get anything in return, except the degraded item, and it will cost you tokens to have it charged again.
Yes, I will keep that in mind.
Good. In that case, just hand me the item from which you want the charge removed.

o: I want to see what you're selling first.
How can I get hold of these tokens?

pages.x: Okay, I'll do that.
Why do all of your wares degrade? I have seen plenty of similar items in my days, but they all seem to last a lot longer than yours.
A most accurate observation, my friend.
But the other items you've come across in your travels most certainly have not been directly infused with the power emanating from the Fist of Guthix.
Umm...I suppose not. But wouldn't the power of Guthix have made the items stronger?
Why, yes, they have. Keeping a shop so close to the source of this power has resulted in the items being infused with energy.
This makes them stronger than they normally would have been, but, unfortunately, they are
hardly suitable vessels for such divine power. As they are being used, the power will be spent, and all that will remain is an empty, weakened shell.
When this happens, just come back to me and I will gladly recharge them for you.
...For a small fee.
Haha. Yes, my friend, for a small fee. The power of a god does not come cheaply, not even in small doses.
If we were to give it out for free, we would run out of resources in an instant. Balance must be maintained.
Okay, I will keep that in mind. Thank you.
Now, is there anything else I can help you with?

o: How can I get hold of these tokens?

pages.x: I have to go now.
Sorry, I have to leave now. Goodbye.
No, I'm just passing by.

conversations.section: In Al Kharid / Talking to her / Before unlocking Sorceress's Garden

pages.x: Hello, what are you doing?
Cleaning, cleaning, always cleaning. This apprenticeship isn't all that it was cracked up to be.
Whose apprentice are you?
Oh, Aadeela, the sorceress upstairs, said she'd teach me magic, she did. And here I am scrubbing the floors without a spell to help me.

o: I could cast a Water Blast or an Air Blast spell?
Surely there must be upsides to the task?

pages.x: I could cast a Water Blast or an Air Blast spell to hurry things along if you'd like?
No, no, she'd kill me or worse if she knew I was using Magic to do chores. Her last apprentice - well I'd rather not say.
Oh go on, what happened to them?
They say she turned them into little spiders.
Oh, that's too bad. I had better leave you to it.
Surely there must be upsides to the task?
Nope. Clean this, clean that. When I'm finished cleaning here I have to go help out in the garden.
What garden?
Oh, I shouldn't have told you.

o: Oh, you can talk to me. I can see you're having a bad day.

pages.x: You're right, you shouldn't have.
Well, if you don't mind then, I'm busy and have to get back to work.
Don't let me keep you.
Oh, you can talk to me. I can see you're having a bad day.
You know you're right. Nobody listens to me.

o: I can't blame them, all you do is whine.
A sympathetic ear can do wonders.

pages.x: I can't blame them, all you do is whine.

o: The apprentice is clearly hurt and ignores you.

pages.x: A sympathetic ear can do wonders.
Yes, if I just let my frustrations out, I'd feel a lot better. Now what was I saying?

o: I don't know. You were whining about something or other.
To tell you the truth, I wasn't really listening.
You mentioned something about the garden.

pages.x: I don't know. You were whining about something or other. To tell you the truth, I wasn't really listening.

o: The apprentice is clearly hurt and ignores you.

pages.x: To tell you the truth, I wasn't really listening.

o: The apprentice is clearly hurt and ignores you.

pages.x: You mentioned something about the garden.
Oh yeah, that dreadful garden of hers.
Where is it?
Oh, it's nowhere.
What do you mean?
Well it's here, but not really. You see the sorceress is trying out some new type of compression magic.
Oh, that sounds interesting - so how does it work?
It would take too long to explain and, to be honest, I don't really understand how it works.
Fair enough, but tell me, how do you get to the garden?
By magic! The sorceress did teach me one spell.

o: Wow, cast the spell on me. It will be good Magic training for you.
Oh, that's nice. Well it's been great talking to you.

pages.x: Wow, cast the spell on me. It will be good Magic training for you.
You wouldn't mind?
Of course not. I'd be glad to help.
Okay, here goes! Remember, to return, just drink from the fountain.
Oh, that's nice. Well it's been great talking to you.

conversations.section: Bird and the Beast / Bandosian

pages.x: Speak quickly. We are at war.
Who are you?
I am Bandos, or the Big High War God, if that is your preference.
I am the last of a long-dead species - a proud warrior-race who valued fighting to the death. And die they did. I emerged as their champion.
I have come to this world with a simple proposition: Let the strongest rule the weak.
The other gods are hypocrites. To get what we want, we have to be strongest. They won't admit it, but I tell it how it is.
I am not like other gods. Beneath my banner you fight or you die - there is nothing else. Prove yourself in blood and fury and your rewards will be great.
Fail, and none will mourn you.
Armadyl is deluded. He believes that gods and mortals can exist in peace. A foolish notion.
Where there are gods, there is envy. Where there are mortals, there is fear.
Gielinor is drenched with blood. War will rage across this world until - finally - it is rent asunder.
Tell me about your race.
I was born knowing only war. Glory came from the number of notches on your axe.
On our world, you trained as soon as you could hold a blade. In your tenth year, you were considered ready for combat.
I was a cunning child, and became strategic advisor to my clan's chief. Together we wiped out dozens of other tribes.
In my tenth year, I challenged my clan leader to single combat. When I gutted him, the warriors of the tribe exalted me as warlord.
The other clans fell to my great strategies, and soon no foes remained. But peace did not become us.
We fought each other. Champion after champion fell, until only one was left to challenge me. He failed.
Tell me about your followers.
You may think that I consider my followers expendable.
But they are only expendable if they are weak. If they prove to me that they are strong - if they survive - then they are rewarded.
It is as it should be. The strong are given glory, and the weak die trying.
My followers accept this. They understand this simple, cruel truth.
They are willing to die for their chance to stand at the top of the pile. They are weapons until they prove that they are soldiers.
You can't use people like that!
Then fight me! There is nothing more hateful than sulking. If the world is not as you wish, bend it to your will!
I understand.
Why should I follow you?
I envisage a world where life and death are simple, where greatness is rewarded.
I see a world where there is no need to flatter and deceive: where power is there to be taken by those with the strength to do so.
My philosophy is simple: strength is all. Not only do the fittest survive, they are rewarded - and they govern for as long as they can hold onto power.
If you are weak, you must become strong. Only then are you on the path of greatness.
Perhaps you are strong enough. Join me and you will learn a clarity of purpose, without fear of being tricked or robbed of what is rightfully yours.
Why are you fighting Armadyl?
Armadyl believes the weak and the strong can leave harmoniously.
He believes that the strong will not desire dominion over the weak, and that the weak will be able to withstand the strong.
Can you imagine Saradomin or Zamorak living in such a world? It's a dream, as floating and disconnected as Armadyl's islands.
And does he not lie? Armadyl claims he cannot abide war, yet he stands here with his armies.
I say hypocrite.
He says he wants to give people their freedom, but he still claims them as his own.
I say hypocrite.
(if you have completed Missing, Presumed Death) As you saw at the 'Ascension', Sliske will award the Stone of Jas to whoever kills the most gods.
I intend to simplify this war. I intend to seize the stone.
This is an opportunity to wipe out Armadyl, as a pure example that the strongest will survive.
That's everything.
Get out on the field and bring me divine energy!

conversations.section: Telling your story to Gwir / After Regicide

pages.x: Sure I'll help. Let's start at the beginning?
Sounds like a great idea!
How did this all start for you?
Well, a fair time ago, I was tasked by Edmond of Ardougne to find his kidnapped daughter, Elena.
I've not heard of these people before. You say she was kidnapped?
Kidnapped and taken to West Ardougne, yes.
It was the first time I ever went in, so we had to go through the sewers, but I made it in, and eventually located and returned Elena back to her father.
Great story. It's strange to think how it started so differently for you.
So you had entered West Ardougne for the first time and released Elena from her captors. What happened next for you?
A good question. It was at this point it came to my attention that Elena was, in fact, investigating the plague itself.
I helped her retrieve her distillator from the mourners so she could continue her work.
Let me guess: her work revealed that the plague was a lie?

o: Hey, quit interrupting, I'm telling you what happened.

pages.x: Hey, quit interrupting, I'm telling you what happened.
I apologise, Player, please continue.
Yes, the findings from Elena's sample did reveal the plague to be a lie.
What did you do when you found this out?
I went straight to King Lathas himself.
He admitted the whole thing, but defended his actions by saying that walling off West Ardougne was necessary to contain a much greater threat to the rest of Gielinor.
And this threat was?
Iban. The next step of this story.
So, Iban is where this story continues. Iban is known to us elves - we do not enter the Underground Pass following the losses we suffered there in the times of old.

o: Quit sidetracking things, this is my story.

pages.x: Quit sidetracking things, this is my story.
I apologise, Player, please continue.
What happened to the elves?
Well, I'm not sure how familiar you are with elven history, but we did use to occupy the lands to the east.
The time came when contact between the elves of Isafdar and those who had travelled east was lost.
When that happened, there was a mass exodus back west by those elves who'd left their forest home. They suffered
countless losses on the journey through the Underground Pass and no elf has stepped into it since.
But let's move on. This is about your own trip through the Underground Pass.
So I was saying. King Lathas feared the threat of Iban, and sent me into the Underground Pass to investigate and find a way through to these lands.
What happened next?
I found my way down to the bottom of the Underground Pass where I combined the four elements of Iban with a doll, which I eventually threw into the Well of Voyage.
This defeated Iban and cleansed the area, reopening the well and granting access to the elven lands at last.
And I think the next part of your story is where our fates begin to intertwine...
Then let's continue. You had traversed the Underground Pass and arrived in these lands for the first time.
Yes. After an initial confrontation - an ambush by elves - I navigated the forests here to find Lord Iorwerth's camp.
Iorwerth? The leader of the dark elves?
The very same. Unfortunately, I believed myself to be working on the side of good, killing the supposedly evil King Tyras.
I won't get into it, but I learnt of explosives, which led to catapulting a barrel bomb, killing Tyras in the fire that followed.
Not the greatest moment in history.
Indeed not, but at least the truth came out. On the way back to report this news to King Lathas, I met Arianwyn for the first time.
He revealed the lie and that, in fact, it was good in a way, as I had earnt King Lathas's trust. I
could use that trust to infiltrate deeper into this conspiracy than any elf could.
Well, the journey may have been difficult, but at least it exposed the truth and allowed you to earn their trust. What happened next?

conversations.section: In Tai Bwo Wannai, after Jungle Potion

pages.x: Hello there...thanks for helping out Trufitus commune with the gods Bwana. We've been able to return to the village thanks to your help.

o: Is there anything interesting to do here?
I've been doing some work around the village.

pages.x: What do you do here?
I's not doing a great deal now Bwana, as I'm no spring chicken.
I do my fair share around the village bwana, though, I could tell you a thing or two about the jungle slashing.

o: Ok, tell me about jungle slashing!

pages.x: Ok, tell me about jungle slashing!
Ok Bwana, I will! To begin with you'll need a machete in order to hack your way through the jungle.
There are some better gem edged weapons which you may be able to purchase from Gabooty.
Safta Doc makes them for him. You should be aware that hacking away at the jungle is not without its dangers though Bwana.
Many times you may find some scary creatures lurking inside.
What sort of creatures?
Ok, to start with there are spiders! These are pretty tough but if you defeat it, you can get a good meal from it, if you know how to cook it that is.
My wife cooks them to a turn - Mmmm, delicious.
Ok go on!
Yes Bwana, of course. Then there are snakes...these are dangerous because they're poisonous - so be prepared! However, they're not without their uses.
A bush snake is large enough to have a useful hide.
Once the hide is tanned you get a snakeskin and you're able to make things from it, the same way that mainlanders use normal leather!
However, it's actually still quite small.
You may need several skins in order to make something useful.
Hmm, sounds interesting!
Then there are giant mosquitoes bwana, they're fast and agile. You'll need to be quick if you're to hit them at all! However, it certainly does train your reactions.
They're not very tough, just difficult to hit.
I also believe that their proboscis is useful in someway, I believe Timfraku's sons sometimes use them for hunting.
Ok, that sounds helpful...anything else?
Yes Bwana... and this is serious... The jungle is very ancient and many unspeakable acts have been witnessed on these lands.
Bizarre supernatural curses were placed on criminals and then they were buried alive!
These strange creatures have the curse of the Broodoo on them!
They'll rise from their grave with their heads in their chests and move like crazy spirits of the afterlife.
If they're disturbed they will attack anything in the area with their magical abilities!
They suffer little from being attacked as they seem to be protected by some form of defence.
However... it is said that the means of their death provides the clue to their destruction. So far three distinct Broodoo have been identified.
The Broodoo with a green hued skin is said to have died from poison.
There is a broodoo of yellow hue and a pale skinned broodoo, but little is known of these two!
Erk! Well that sounds pretty scary!
Yes Bwana...
Ok, thanks a lot....
Wait Bwana, there's more!
More... Blimey! Ok carry on...
Some of the local villagers have found strange plants which grow here-abouts.
If you cut away at the jungle and find one, it's considered a blessing, though the useful part of the plant is usually buried underground. And also, you
may find an uncommon rock type which is impregnated with mineral wealth! Well that concludes all the help I can give you regarding the jungle in Tai Bwo Wannai!
I have to say, that's quite a lot of information...thanks very much!
You're more than welcome bwana!
Is there anything interesting to do here?
Ok, thanks.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hi, I can clean your herbs for you at a cost of 200 coins per herb.
If you want me to clean herbs individually please use each herb on me, or I can clean all the herbs in your inventory at once now.
If you want potions decanted into 3, 2 or 1- ose versions, I can do that too.
I charge 2 coins for each normal vial, 2 coins for each juju vial and 2 coins for each powerburst vial I have to supply.

o: Can you convert my flasks into normal vials for me?

pages.x: Please decant my potions.
Would you like them to become 1-, 2- or 3-dose potions?
Make them all 1-dose potions.
Make them all 2-dose potions.
Make them all 3-dose potions.
Actually, forget it.

o: Why would I pay you to clean herbs?
Please explain your fee for decanting potions.

pages.x: Why would I pay you to clean herbs? I can gain Herblore experience by cleaning them myself.
This is true, but many customers want to sell the herbs on without advancing their own skill.
They can get particularly high prices selling those grimy herbs that only the more accomplished herbalist can clean.
Please explain your fee for decanting potions.
If I change your 4-dose potions into 3-dose or 2-dose potions, you may need more vials to hold the same number of doses.
I charge 2 coins for normal vials, 2 coins for juju vials and 2 coins for each powerburst vial.
If I don't need to supply any extra vials, it works out completely free!

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: For completing the Desert set, you are presented with an amulet.
This amulet will become increasingly useful as you complete greater difficulty levels.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
You need to complete all Tasks within a particular difficulty set; then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Desert Tasks are simple, some require certain skill levels, and others require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Desert set rewards, speak to Hassan in Al Kharid Palace, Ali the Mayor in Pollnivneach, the Golem in Uzer, or myself.
Desert amulet 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 25,000 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 50,000 coins.
No thanks.

conversations.section: Conversations / Player-owned head

pages.x: What do you want?
I want to mock you.
All right. Go on then.
You're a stupid slime-witted worm! (This insult will be randomized.)
I'm going back to sleep.
I want to apologise for killing you.
Go on then.
I'm, uh, very sorry I killed you.
Really sorry?
No, not really.
I don't care.
Yes, really.
Really really?
Yes, really really.
Fat load of good that does, I'm still dead.
I'm not THAT sorry.
I don't care.
But will you forgive me?
Of course I'll forgive you!
Really?
No!
I promise not to do it again.
Of course you won't do it again, you can only kill me once.
That's why I won't do it again.
I don't care.
But I won't do it to other basilisks.
Really?
Yes, really!
All right then. Apology accepted. Now leave me alone.
No, not really!
I don't care.
Don't start that again.
Leave me alone then.
Don't push it.
I don't care anyway.
I just wanted to check that you're okay.
Apart from being dead and stuffed and hanging on a wall, you mean?
Uh...yeah. Apart from that are you okay?
Actually there's something blocking my view of the far wall.
I don't see anything.
Perhaps if you were to step to one side of me.
I still don't see anything.
Oh, it's moved away. I can see now.
Nothing.
Leave me alone.

conversations.section: After Smoking Kills

pages.x: I sense you are becoming adept at new Slayer techniques. Impressive.
It was all thanks to your help.
Nice of you to say so, although the cats have definitely had something to do with it. It hints at divine intervention.
It seems I'm the subject of a few too many divine interventions for comfort. It's lucky indeed that I have my feline friend.
Heroes aren't the same as they were in my day. Can I help you with anything else?

o: Could you tell me what's going on?
Can you tell me about the smoky dungeon?
I'd like some information on the remaining guardians.
Are you both in your tomb and the smoky dungeon?

pages.x: Could you tell me what was going on?
The crux of the matter is that you were working for Sumona, who is the Devourer.
I can't say I am happy to have helped her in her plans. She never struck me as a nice type.
Oh, but you didn't help her - she expected you to die. She did promise to reward you, however, so take advantage of that.
What about this twin sister then? Is she a deity too?
Twin sister? It was the Devourer too; she just wanted to watch when the banshee defeated you.
I presume that her being a deity is going to make it awkward for me, having riled her so much.
Her bargain isn't one she can wriggle out of easily, although sending you on Slayer tasks will be far from safe.
You'll also find that you forget her evil deeds when talking with her, such is the power she possesses.
The fake-sister thing explains why she burned that book and what the insectoids were doing there.
Indeed. Thank you for avenging me. It is as much as can be expected by a dead mortal who wishes revenge on an immortal deity.
Can you tell me about the smoky dungeon at all?
You will, of course, be aware that the place is a hive of Slayer creatures. Each of these must be combated within the smoke you mention.
There are no new dangers I should be aware of?
There are four guardians - turoth, kurask, cave crawler and basilisk - that must be slain in order to access the four new areas within the underground passages.
No problem for you, I would suspect, as you were able to easily deal with the banshee mistress. Is there anything more I can help with?
I'd like some information on the remaining guardians.

o: I'd like to know about the mightiest turoth.
I'd like to know about the kurask overlord.
I'd like to know about the monstrous cave crawler.
I'd like to know about the basilisk boss.
I'm not after anything in fact.

pages.x: I'd like to know about the mightiest turoth.
From what I've heard, the mightiest turoth can summon its offspring to aid it.
These are smaller and weaker than the mightiest turoth but they are essentially unlimited in number.
How can I deal with such an onslaught?
I'd guess that killing the leader first would be wise. If you like infinite carnage, however, then slaughtering the offspring might be pleasant for a few moments.
I'd like to know about the kurask overlord.
As far as I can divine, the kurask overlord in the caves can summon its cohorts to aid it. These are almost the equal of the creature itself.
What would you suggest?
I'd guess that killing the overlord as quickly as you can would be the plan. They are bulky creatures, however, so you may be able to use this to your advantage.
I'd like to know about the monstrous cave crawler.
The cave crawlers are a venomous bunch and their guardian even more so.
Adventurers who have seen it and lived have told of its power to poison, even if an opponent has temporary immunity.
I certainly would not look at it as a feeble pushover. Take loads of some poison cure.
I'd like to know about the basilisk boss.
The basilisk boss is similar to most of its kind, but with a fiercer glare.
Whatever draining effects a normal basilisk unleashes, you can expect the basilisk boss to unleash with more power.
I'm not after anything, in fact.
Are you in both your tomb and the smoky dungeon?
I have a spiritual presence in both places associated with my death - my tomb and the place of my murder.
That must be useful. I wish I could be in two places at once.
I don't think that my position is altogether enviable. After all, I'm dead and can only ever exist in two places. You are alive and can go anywhere your legs take you.

conversations.section: Normally

pages.x: Welcome back, how can I help you?

o: How does the Yak Track work?
How did you become an undead yak count?

pages.x: How does the Yak Track work?
Ah, the Yak Track! It's an opportunity to go on an adventure with your very own yak and earn many rewards along the way!
Simply put, you can complete tasks to progress along the track.
You will be given a choice between two tasks at a time, but you only need to complete one of them to progress.
If you don't fancy doing either of them then you can use a task skip to move on.
As you progress along the track you will earn rewards; Premier Club members and those who have purchased a Premier Pass will earn additional premium rewards.
If you purchase a Premier Pass you will receive any premium rewards you would have been eligible for.
Sounds great!
Are you really a count?
Yes.
But you're a yak.
Yes. Are you really a World Guardian?
Yes.
But you are a human.
Okay, I get your point.
How did you become an undead yak count?
Now that is a tale for the ages. Long ago there was a well respected nobleman.
He was a a philanthropist, sharing his wealth with those less fortunate, ensuring everyone was fed and clothed. And I, I was his leading workyak.
Words of his good deeds had spread throughout the land and he was to be granted the title of count for his generosity.
The preparations were put in place and the final step was a simple signature to make it all official. However, before his signature was taken a great tragedy occurred.
While out on one of our excursions we were ambushed by a group of vampyres. He was lucky enough to make it out unscathed, I however was not so fortunate.
I succumbed to my wounds and a terrible curse befell me. Day by day I found myself growing weaker. My body began to decay and my mind no longer felt like it was my own.
But no matter how far I fell, no matter how much I suffered, death would not take me.
The yak doctors tried their hardest, they poked and prodded me, gave me salve after salve of medicine but in the end there was naught they could do.
The nobleman, stricken with grief, knew what had to be done, however he was unable to do it himself.
With the help of the doctors he drafted a letter to the local vampyre hunters.
He knew the curse would not grant me a release but these specialists could bring an end to my suffering. However, there was a mix up.
Somehow his name made it onto the elimination request to the hunters. And my name was passed on to the royalty to become count.
Oh...
It is said that grief has a great effect on the mind. And in this case one simple error had such costly consequences...
But alas, a lot of time has passed since then. Although I continue to suffer each and every day, I have become accustomed to the pain.
I'm really sorry. Hopefully someday we'll be able to find a cure...
Hopefully doth butter no parsnips. But I do appreciate the kind sentiment.
Is this what led to you opening up the yak track?
In essence, yes. Although I sadly cannot remember his name, I can remember his heart.
My body is weary and broken and I can no longer carry what I used to, but it is time for me to pass on the torch.
Uniting new pairs of adventurers and yaks, forging new bonds through adventure. That's what the yak track is all about.
That's a beautiful thought. We'll do our best to carry your legacy!
Thank you.
Bye!
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: It's still here.
Pardon?
It's still here. The crop circle is still here.
Oh yes, thanks Aery. It didn't go anywhere in the meantime, then?
Nope. It just sat there.
Jolly good. I can come back and visit Puro-Puro whenever I want then. Brilliant!

o: Is there anything else you want to ask?
So what are these implings then?
I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

pages.x: What's in Puro-Puro?
Implings...and wheat.
Erm, anything else?
Not really. Though I have noticed quite a lot of you humans travelling through the portal recently. I suppose you must like wheat.
Well, most of us prefer lobsters to be perfectly honest, but there must be something interesting there.
Oh, I did notice a very serious-looking gnome go into the portal. Maybe he knows what's going on.
Do you remember what his name was?
Errm, Egg-nog, or something like that.
Right, thanks! I'll have a chat with him when I go. Maybe he'll know what's going on.
So what are these implings then?
Well, no-one knows for sure. The mischievous little creatures are probably related to imps. And they fly as well. Also, like imps, they love collecting things.
I'm not sure why, though. They also seem to like being chased.
So how would I get hold of what they are carrying, then?
Catch them, I suppose. I don't know really. Why would you want to?
Well, if they were carrying something useful. Maybe I could catch them with a big net - like butterflies.
Sounds a bit cruel to me, but I suppose that's possible.
I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.
Really? You humans like that stuff a lot, don't you? I don't like really old stuff myself.
Old?
Yes, dragon stuff feels really old.
How can you tell that?
From its magical aura, obviously. Oh, I forget you humans can't feel auras.
How old is old?
Really, really, old.
Can you be any more precise?
Not really. Time doesn't really mean a lot round here. Hundreds, maybe thousands of your human lifespans, I suppose.
Anyway, it would have to be old since it all comes from the Necrosyrtes.
Necrosyrtes? Who are they?
Old and powerful creatures. I don't think there have been any around here for aeons. I haven't seen one. I don't think they are very nice. Not like me.
Anyway, this is all ancient history. Boooring!
While I'm on the subject do you have any dragon stuff I can have?
Oh, I did have loads, but I threw it away.
What?
Only joking. No, sorry, I can't help you there. You'll have to look for it yourself. Although, maybe if you find Necrosyrtes then they'll give you some.
I heard they give dragon stuff away to people they like. Not fairies. We're too nice.
No, bye!
See you around!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Ouch!
Are you alright?
I'm fine, I'm fine. Just a scratch.

o: Do you know anything about this pyramid?

pages.x: Who are you then?
Me? I'm Tarik.
That hat you're wearing doesn't look like it comes from around here?
It was a present, my employer thought it would suit me. I'm not sure what it does, though it does keep the sun off very well.
Who is your employer then?
Simon Templeton, though I haven't seen him since the town gates were closed off.
Simon Templeton ... that name seems familiar?
He's an archaeologist, I worked as an assistant for him. Though I work for myself now.
So what have you been up to?
Simon suggested that there might be riches to be found in that pyramid over there.
So how did you get injured?
I've been investigating that pyramid over there.

o: Player: So what's in the pyramid?

pages.x: Well, I'm not sure. First of all there's something odd about the doors on the place. There's four of them - but three of them lead to an empty tomb.
The other one is guarded by something - I keep getting knocked out. If I make it through the door there's a Mummy waiting.
But which door the right one is seems to change, it's all quite confusing.
What about this Mummy?
I don't think he likes people. However he does allot you to enter some of the rooms in the tomb. They are dangerous though.
Bah, I laugh in the face of danger!
Well, if you go into that pyramid then you'll be laughing a lot then. It's full of poisonous snakes and scarabs, and rather nasty Mummies as well. You could die in there.
I managed to get into one room, but the next room was harder. My lockpicking skills weren't good enough, maybe I should have brought a lockpick.
There are also lots of poisonous snakes in the urns. They'll bite you if they can. You might be able to charm them if you know how.
I'd bring some antipoison anyway if I were you.
It all sounds like fun to me. So is there anything valuable in there?
There are lots of artefacts, you should be able to sell them on the black market, I mean, to a legitimate trader, for some money.
You mean Simon Templeton?
Well, he's a 'legitimate' as you can get, if you can get out of this city and get to him.
I'll find a way. Is there anything else of value in there?
I have heard a rumour that there is a valuable magic sceptre in there as well.
Ah, now you have piqued my interest. What do you know about this sceptre?
Not a lot. It is apparently made of gold and covered in jewels, and used to be owned by one of Tumeken's sons.
Tumeken?
Tumeken, the sun god and head of the gods. His sons were the rulers, chosen by him to rule in his name.
So these sons were rich and powerful then? This sceptre should be pretty good then.
Hmmm. Well it is supposed to have some magical powers.
Magical powers? This sounds good. What are they?
I'll let you know when I find it!
Not if I find it first!
Hey! If you find it I deserve a share of the profits! You wouldn't have known it existed without my help.
I'll think about it... Right, I think I'd better investigate this place.

conversations.section: On Waiko (as Sojobo)

pages.x: Looking for work? I have contracts for you to complete in this region, and I'll reward you for them.
What are contracts?
Hoho! Well, from me at least, they are a form of charity. The organisation that I belong to is altruistic and charitable.
We seek to make Wushanko safe for the just, to protect the innocent and smite evil in all its forms.
My contracts will give focus to any that wish to lend a hand towards these goals, ridding this region of evildoers and gathering supplies for the needy.
Some of my contracts require you to gather materials or fashion them into specific items. I don't require you to give me them to fulfil a contract.
You may donate these supplies to those less fortunate than yourself at your convenience.
There are other, more specialised, contract givers to be found in these parts, whose reasons are their own. My contracts, however, are more rewarding! Any questions?

o: Why do you charge me to re-roll contracts?
Can you tell me about the Gu?
What is the Way of Gu?

pages.x: Tell me about contracts.
There is a limit to how many can be completed on any given day. The Way of Gu teaches us that an excess of charity often leads to a development of selfishness.
Charity is for the sake of others, not for personal fulfillment.
I will only offer you contracts that you are capable of completing, but should you wish a different one, then I shall do so...for a small cost of chimes.
Some contracts can be completed on the various islands of this region, but you will most likely want or need to visit the uncharted islands to do the greatest amount of good.
Completed contracts should be returned to me, at which point I shall reward you with a wealth of the Gu's knowledge and experience.
Why do you charge me to re-roll contracts?
Aha! That money is collected as a charitable donation to the Gu, which we put towards spreading our creed around these islands, training new Gu recruits and such.
In return, we handsomely reward you with our knowledge and experience!
Tell me about the Gu.
The Gu have humble origins - a group of ten like-minded individuals banded together to protect a small town from attack by a group of bird-demons.
Each of the ten brought a different skill to the group, and each of them were pivotal to the success of their defence.
After saving that village, the locals wished for them to remain, to live among them as saviours and friends. Thus the Gu were born.
Those ten saviours became the first of the great Gu sages, each of them seeking to master their disciplines, and teaching their new neighbours of their expertise.
Word spread, and many pilgrims made their way to the village to learn from these great sages.
Before long, the Gu sent out envoys and started to spread their knowledge and charity beyond that village and the island it stood on.
The ten Gu sages created a charter for how these envoys should conduct themselves in the world - the Way of Gu - a guiding principle for all who followed in their footsteps.
What is the Way of Gu?
The Way of Gu are the tenets by which we conduct ourselves in this world.
It consists of ten ways in which one can view the world, and seek to make it a better place for all. Gu initiates must learn all of the Ten Ways at first.
Once they have an understanding of them all, many will choose one particular Way to follow and find a master of that Way to teach them further.
After years of study, a student can become a master, and masters that have tutored many can become grandmasters.
Whenever one great sage passes from this mortal coil, the most senior grandmasters will take their place.
What are the Ten Ways?
The Way of the Warrior is the simplest, to master the martial arts in order to protect those that cannot protect themselves.
The Way of the Scholar is to learn about the world from the written and spoken word, and then to spread that knowledge to others.
In contrast, the Way of the Wanderer is to learn about the world from first-hand experience, through adventure and travel.
Then there are the arts, starting with the Way of the Artist, spreading joy and knowledge through artistic expression.
Of a similar vein is the Way of the Musician, using music and song to remember the past and celebrate the present.
Though those who do not understand it see it not as another art, there is also the Way of the Prankster. Humour is the great healer.
And the last of the arts is the Way of the Orator - actors, public speakers and tellers of stories.
There are also crafts, such as the Way of the Maker - makers of armour, folders of swords, builders for boats.
The Way of the Gourmand is a mix of art and craft, perfecting recipes, but also helping to feed the hungry.
And finally is the Way of the Spirit, experts in ghost-hunting, performers of the last rites and our healers.
Phew! That's a lot to take in! Which Way do you ascribe to?
Aha, but I am unique. I am the Tengu, the embodiment of the Ten Ways, and master of all.

conversations.section: In Sorceress's Garden / When spoken to with a Catspeak amulet

pages.x: Hello, no-fur. What are you doing in my mistress's garden?
Looking for sq'irks.
If it's sq'irks you're after then you've come to the right place. We've got four seasons' worth of them.
I'd be happy to help a friend of the feline.
What do you mean?
The Sphinx gave you that amulet, so she must hold you in high regard.
If I remember correctly, it was the High Priest of Sophanem who gave it to me.
He and the Sphinx are as thick as thieves, but regardless, I think you've a bit of a cat feel about you. Now what are these questions?

o: What are the creatures inside the gardens?
How do you get into the seasonal gardens?
How is it that the gardens are in different seasons?
How do I get out of here?

pages.x: What are the creatures inside the gardens?
Oh, you mean the gardeners?
The strange, floaty creatures.
Yes, the gardeners. Don't let them see you or they'll teleport you out here. They're very protective of their crops.
How do you get into the seasonal gardens?
I get in through gaps in the hedge. You are a little too big to squeeze through. I think you'll have to use the gates.
I think the gates are locked, so you'll have to have good Thieving skills to get in.
How is it that the gardens are in different seasons?
How did you get here?
Magic?
Exactly. The Sorceress likes to have a good supply of in-season sq'irks and herbs at all times.
How do I get out of here?
Take a drink from the fountain.
Talking to cats.
A noble and rewarding past-time.
How did you get here?
Every time I play with spiders in the Sorceress's house, her silly apprentice completely freaks out and teleports me here!
So you've been stuck here since?
No, silly! I drink from the fountain whenever I want to leave.
What are you doing here?
I get this strange urge for sq'irks. It's quite peculiar. I think I may be addicted.
I think I know someone else who may be in a similar position.
Don't tell me. Osman, right?
You know him too?
Oh, he used to come here all the time. Then one day, he just stopped.
Who are you?
Del-Monty the cat, at your service.
Are you a famous adventurer who was turned into a cat by a vindictive mage?
No; as I said, I'm Del-Monty the cat, connoisseur of exotic fruits.
In that case, can you tell me anything about sq'irks?
But of course! Their juice is an excellent source of energy for runners, and in the riper varieties they are known to heighten one's Thieving abilities.
Nothing much.
Yawn! Nice talking to you then, no-fur.

conversations.section: Prosecuting

pages.x: I need to ask you some questions about the court case.
Certainly. I'll do anything to convict those nasty H.A.M. members.
The H.A.M. Group
Do you know who the H.A.M. are?
Do you know who the H.A.M. are?
Yes, we are well aware of who they are and what they did to Zanik. We hate the H.A.M. and everything they stand for.
What were you doing at their base of operations?
What were you doing at their base of operations?
I didn't mean to end up there. I was just exploring Lumbridge and found an interesting mine-shaft.
Suddenly, I was grabbed by people in pink, beaten, and thrown in their jail cells.
How do you feel about humans?
How do you feel about humans?
So far, everyone I've met on the surface has been very nice. I visited some tradesmen who were happy to sell me things, and the citizens were very polite.
It's just the H.A.M. who are cruel and horrible.
The incident
Would you describe the incident to me?
Would you describe the incident to me?
I was exploring the river running through Lumbridge. I saw an intresting-looking mine-shaft, so I went for a closer look.
As I got near, a trapdoor opened and I was grabbed by someone in pink. Suddenly, I was underground and thrown into a jail cell.
They interrogated me, beat me, and wanted to know why I was spying on them. I wasn't spying! I was just exploring the surface, getting souvenirs for my family.
You must have known that H.A.M. were in the area. Why'd you go there?
You must have known that H.A.M. were in the area, based on what Zanik told everyone. Why'd you go there?
I was curious to follow Zanik's trail, and I didn't think I'd be openly attacked!
Did anyone else see you exploring?
Did anyone else see you exploring?
I only think some surface goblins saw me, since I travel mostly at night.
Why?
I'm not used to the sun, and it hurt my eyes. It's nicer travelling at night.
The stolen items
Where did you get the items found on you?
Where did you get the items found on you?
I bought them in Lumbridge. They're all for sale there, and I obtained them all legally!
Where did the H.A.M. gloves come from?
Where did the H.A.M. gloves come from?
I don't remember! I must have picked them up from the floor when I was escaping, or found them in the cell.
Why did you want surface items?
Why did you want surface items?
Surface items are still quite rare in Dorgesh-Kaan. They are worth a lot and make wonderful gifts. I was getting things to take back to my family.
Why are both of you in jail?
Why are both of you in jail? Surely only one of you needs to be.
Well, I accused the H.A.M. of crimes against me, and they brought a countersuit!
The judge decided that we should both be held until the court date, since either of us could be found guilty. You humans have strange laws.
I don't have any more questions.
I don't have any more questions.

conversations.section: In Balthazar's Big Top Bonanza / Subsequent dialogue

pages.x: Ah, my little performer. What can I do for you?
Ah, there is so much that goes into being a true virtuoso! The audience is key to any great performance. You must listen to what they want and appease them.
They love seeing their requests performed. They also hate repetition, so don't keep doing the same safe move. Be dangerous!
Try more difficult moves and who knows, you might succeed.
Everything you can do here is rated by difficulty in relation to your skill levels, but they're only recommended levels.
You're welcome to attempt anything you like, you're just more likely to succeed if you have the relevant skill level.
What if I can't do more difficult moves? I can't help repeating!
Then perform an emote in between moves! That will make the audience happy; however, don't repeat them. Our audiences are very fickle and HATE repetition.
Also, we only give you a point bonus for the first 10 that you perform.
Isn't there an easier way to improve my performance? The audience can be so demanding.
Certainly. Wear crazy costumes - the crazier the better! I will not tell you which clothes to wear, as it is to the taste of the performer, but do experiment.
See what works best for you. For safety reasons, you can only wear the costume we provide for the Agility performance.
Also, keep an eye on where the ticket vendor moves to, and who populates our audience. Different locations have different preferences, and that will give you a bonus.
Thanks for the advice!
Would you like to know about anything else?

o: I want to retrieve a costume.
I want to know more about the rewards.

pages.x: Not that performing isn't great in itself, but what do I get for doing it? You can't expect me to work for free.
What happened to the days when the thrill of performing was enough? Of course I reward my performers, but I work on a performance-related pay method.
The better you do, the better I reward you. Your performance itself is a reward, because you gain more experience than you normally would in the skill you perform in.
At the end of your performance, I review how well you did and I will reward you with extra experience and a part of a costume.
What costume?
Not just one, but several! For those that simply...put in the minimum effort, I reward them with peasant costume pieces and the occasional giant hand.
For those that increasingly put in effort, they get performance costumes.
I give out pieces for an acrobat costume, a clown costume and, for those that are truly amazing (like myself), I give out a ringmaster costume!
That's not too bad, I suppose. I hope mine fits better than yours does.
I'd like to see you find a tailor who can make size 115 trousers!
Never mind.
Tell me about the circus. It's a little odd.
It's a circus. It's *supposed* to be odd. What would you like to know?

o: Why are there so few people here?
How do I leave the circus?}}

pages.x: Why is there hardly any one here? And why am I your only performer?
We are but a new business, and haven't attracted many customers yet. That is why there are so few people in the stands.
But with a performer as good as you, we hope to attract more customers and more performers.
Ah, we exist within the ticket vendor. We fold space in on itself to fit in something smaller than the space we take up.
It's all very complex, but the fairies tell me it's quite easy.
So, I'm currently folded in space? Is it going to hurt to unfold?
No, of course not. It's no different to teleporting normally.
How do I leave the circus? All of the exits are roped off.
Silly little performer, you were given a golden ticket when you entered Balthazar Beauregard's Big Top Bonanza, yes?
Yes, I did.
Well, read it! It says you just need to tear it to leave the circus. Tear the ticket and 'POOF', you are gone. Simple as that.
Thanks.
Never mind.

conversations.section: Northeast of Varrock / Before The Hunt for Surok (miniquest) / Talking to her

pages.x: Yes? Can I help you?
Who are you?
Well, now. Do you always go around asking about people like that? It's very rude, you know.
Sorry! I didn't mean to pry!
That's alright. My name is Louisiana Jones, although most people call me Anna. I'm an archaeologist.
Oh. Do you work for the Varrock Museum?
Hah! No. I used to, but now I prefer to work freelance for independent employers.
I see.

o: Please tell me what you're investigating.

pages.x: Please tell me what you're investigating.

I'm investigating the relative coexistence of convergent entries from two para-dimensional subspaces into a quantum metaphysical universe and the exponential decay of said linear pathways in the event of fluctuations in the space-time cortex.
Gosh, really?
No.
Oh.
What are you doing here?
I'm investigating something for someone.
That doesn't really explain anything!
I never said it would.
So what are you investigating?
I'm afraid I can't say.
Okay, so who are you investigating it for?
I'm afraid I can't say that either.
Okay, so is there anything you CAN say?
I can say that I can't say anything about what you want me to say!
Okay, I think you've said enough!

o: Please tell me what you're investigating

pages.x: Who does this statue represent?
That, my dear, is the statue of the great god Saradomin himself. Stand and admire in awe, for you are in the presence of greatness!

o: I bet Zaros could take him!

pages.x: All hail Saradomin!
Indeed. Saradomin watches over us all.

o: Please tell me what you're investigating.

pages.x: ...Yay Zamorak...!
WHAT?!?!
Uh...I said I've lost my anorak!
I see. I'm afraid I haven't seen it.
I bet Zaros could take him!
Ha! You underestimate great Saradomin's power! He created the very ground you stand on.
If you say so.
Well it's lucky for you I don't have time to set your mind to the right path right now. Was there anything else you wanted?
Okay, I'd better go.
Okay, then!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Greetings, adventurer! How can I be of help?
Who are you?
My name's Dotmatrix. I am a druid from Taverley.
I normally wouldn't venture to these latitudes, but my colleague, Astlayrix, spoke so highly of this place that I had to go and see for myself.
What are you doing here?
At first, I just came to witness the fantastic habitat south of here, but then I thought it would be a shame to go home without setting foot in the jungle.
The plants are so luxuriant, I couldn't help but hope I'd stumble upon a
new herb that would change the face of herblore.
Did you?
Sadly not, but I discovered something even more extraordinary. Would you like the short or the long version?

o: Long! I do like a good story.}}

pages.x: Short, please.
Ever been to the jadinko habitat? Ever wondered where jadinkos come from? Well, all the answers are down this very hole.
There's a network of caves overrun by vine roots that curl up and down, and it is inhabited by jadinkos like you've never seen.
Some, at the deepest end of the cave, are peaceful and seem to operate under a hive-like hierarchy.
The other ones are warped and mutated; vicious and very dangerous. They attack the non-mutated ones and threaten the balance of the habitat.
Anything that can be done to prevent these mutated jadinkos from threatening the colony must be done.
Maverick here will have more practical information if you wish.
Long! I do like a good story.
I was around here, studying the plants, when something that looked like a jadinko, but warped, scrambled out of a pile of rocks.
It gave me a maddened look and threw itself at me! It almost had my leg off!
I ran away and only came back once I'd managed to enlist the help of a mercenary adventurer, Maverick. By that point, the creature had gone.
We moved the rocks and uncovered this hole. Down there is a network of damp caves overrun by roots which move, curl and uncurl.
These rooms are filled with mutated jadinko creatures. They are vicious and very dangerous, but will normally leave you alone unless you attack them first.
Further into the caves, we found a big room which contained a colony of healthy individuals.
They still looked different from the surface jadinkos, but had that unmistakable jadinko look about them.
They operated under a hive-like hierarchy.
From what I could gather in the limited time I spent down there, there is a single queen, intimately connected to the vine, which produces eggs from which babies are born.

Some of these hatch and grow to become guards or males, and the rest eat fruits and climb on the roots to the surface, where they become specialised workers, attracted by a certain combination of plants.
They gather food which they return to the hive.
But there is something much darker in there. The Queen's vines occasionally mutate, leading to the birth of mutated babies, which then go on to become mutated adults.
These are vicious and very dangerous, like the one who almost made off with my leg.
Anything that can be done to prevent mutated jadinkos from threatening the colony must be done. The peaceful jadinkos will appreciate any help they can get.
Maverick here will have more practical information if you wish.
I'm not that interested, actually.
Oh, fair enough. Anything else I can help you with?
Tell me about this place.
There are a lot of things to be said. I can tell you about my observations of the caves. For the more practical information, I gather Maverick can help you out.
Now, would you like the long story or the short?

o: Long! I do like a good story.

pages.x: I'll be okay, thank you.

conversations.section: In the Frozen floors of Daemonheim / Afterwards

pages.x: Shall I return to the surface now, or is there more you would like to ask?

o: There's more I'd like to ask you.
You're going to tell me stories?
What are these stories you talk about?
Why were you frozen in ice?

pages.x: Who are you?
That is the question. I'm Player... No, wrong story, that's your name not mine. Perhaps my name is Ozan...do I look like an Ozan?
No, those aren't my names.
I'm sorry, Player, but I don't quite know who I am.
But how did you know my name? We've only just met.
Oh, I knew your name as soon as your stories flooded the shelves.
Shelves? Stories?
The library of my mind; each book a story, each story someone's life, each life full of hopes and dreams.
When you came close, your books filled a whole bookcase; each story filled with adventure and potential.
Riiight.
Yet, you don't know who you are?
No. The library is empty of my stories, it seems.
I know that I am a teller of tales and a keeper of stories. But beyond that I do not know.
So you're going to tell me stories?
Tell you? No, no, I will do so much more than tell you.
I will show you my stories, let you be a part of them, live someone else's life for a while.
Just come find me on the surface outside of these demon halls, and I will be able to explain it better. These dungeons are too dangerous for me to go into great detail.
What are these stories you talk about?
I know all the stories that have taken place within Daemonheim: every grand adventure, every tragic romance... I know them, and in turn I have lived them.
They are all catalogued safely in my mind's library, to be read at a moment's notice.
So, you can tell me what's at the bottom of Daemonheim?
And ruin the adventure for you?
Spoilers, dear [boy/lady], spoilers.
Could you at least tell me these stories?
I would love to.
But not here. The dungeons are too dangerous for idle storytelling.
Now that I am free from my frost prison, I can meet you on the surface. Come to me there and I will tell you such tales.
At least, I will if you can jog my memory. Find story elements while in Daemonheim and I will happily relate the associated saga to you on the surface.
Why were you frozen in ice?
I honestly cannot remember.
Perhaps it was a cave-in, a flash flood perhaps.
But then again, I vaguely remember laughter...haunting laughter. Hmmm, was it really laughter, or something my paranoid mind conjured up?
How long have you been frozen down here?
What Age is this?
It's the 6th Age.
Oh... In that case, I've been down here for a long time indeed. It may even be centuries.
Goodbye.
Yes, farewell for now, my friend. I will wait for you on the surface, near a nice warm fire if there is one.
Find story elements here in Daemonheim and visit me with them. They will unlock stories that you will scantly believe.
Shall I return to the surface now, or is there more you would like to ask?

conversations.section: After Sliske's Endgame

pages.x: Welcome, Player. What brings you to me at this hour?
Can you talk about Sliske's game?
What is there to say? Sliske is dead and the stone is gone. Good riddance on both accounts.
Ah yes, Armadyl, seeker of justice and would-be unifier of the gods. If foolishness could be given a face, it would be his. The gods will never work together, not really.
Each of us has our own agenda, our own ideologies and they blend together like oil and fire.
Does he really believe that Saradomin and myself could ever be anything more than mortal enemies? Of course he doesn't.
Which means he will have to pick a side and history has already shown me that he will not choose my side.
So he must see me as a threat and we both know what he does to threats. But I am not Bandos. My battles will not be fought by strength alone.
There are rules to warfare and I will win because I will not play by them, whereas Armadyl will be forced to. I love fighting a foe with a code of honour.
It's like I've already won.
Do you really need to ask my opinion on that hypocrite? Saradomin would see the universe as his great empire. Everyone trapped in roles he has chosen them.
What he preaches to his followers is nothing more than a life of moral slavery. He would see free will crushed and removed and his will raised above all.
Yet it is I who is painted as evil. I feel sorry for his followers, I truly do, they do not see that they are forging their own chains and shackling us all.
No. Those wounds are still too fresh, too raw.
Even thinking about what she did, it fills me with an uncontrollable rage and I would rather not level Edgeville in my fury.
Sliske cannot be trusted. Even Sliske doesn't trust Sliske.
Yet here we all are, all forced to play his little game because the situation he has created for us, it's the perfect trap.
I'll give Sliske that compliment, he's a master strategist, if a twisted one. Even his intrigues have intrigues.
He is a mahjarrat wearing many masks, I wounder if he knows where the masks end and he begins?
In many ways Zaros is as complicit as Seren in the fate of the mahjarrat and I do hate him for that, make no mistake there.
But you know that I am bound to aid him in Sliske's game. I do not know how, I do not know when, but I know it will be an act that will cost me greatly.
My only comfort is knowing that I am surely not the only one pinioned in this way. Zaros never puts all his eggs in one basket.
Icthlarin may not be the strongest of the gods, but he is not one to count out of any race. I have seen him lead armies, back when we were his 'Stern Judges'.
I have found myself wondering of late, 'what if'. What if we had never betrayed Icthlarin, what if we had sided with him against Zaros. What could have been?
I would never have become a god, I would never have been able to save my people, by Sliske might never have had a chance to take the stone for himself. Makes you think.
How one action can affect the world so greatly. On this I have based my philosophy and it holds truer each day.
Death is an important function, so Death himself performs an important role.
As a person, I barely know him and I doubt the two of us are going to be having drinks together anytime soon.
The dragonkin are dangerous. Never, ever forget that. However reasonable some of them may seen, history teaches us that they will stop at nothing to destroy us all.
My advice. Next time you find one injured, kill it. Don't hesitate. Don't listen to its pleas. Strike it down or it will end up destroying you.
I know there is one in Daemonheim somewhere. My agents hear whispers. They are planning something to do with 'the echo's link', whatever that means.
My agents also believe that they have got their hands on one of the elder artefacts. So whatever they are doing, it cannot be good.
Honestly I have little to say about Vorago. I know he is a powerful beast that guards the anima, but beyond that I have no further opinion.
It is easy to dismiss Brassica Prime, as a joke, or as irrelevant. But just because something is strange, it does not mean it should be ignored.
Brassica was able to convince Guthix to leave him behind when the edicts came up. Even Seren was not able to do this. He is certainly not as powerful as he claims to be.
But if his boasts are to be believed, his agents are fruits and vegetables everywhere. Laugh at that for a moment and then stop and think.
Are there any kings who do not have such things in their kitchens and then served at their diplomatic banquets?
Even the gods discuss their plans within earshot of assorted plant matter. So what secrets must Brassica really know?
If knowledge is power, he must really be a force to consider carefully. He's a fool, yes, a joke, certainly. But what better mask is there?
I'd...er...rather not talk about her. Just...well just don't let yourself be alone with her in a room for a long period of time. She bites!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello there! I am known as the Makeover Mage! I have spent many years researching magicks that can change your physical appearance.
I call it a 'makeover'. Would you like me to perform my magicks on you?

o: Can you give me some more pharmakos berries?

pages.x: Tell me more about this 'makeover'.
Why, of course! Basically, and I will explain this so that you understand it correctly.
I use my secret magical technique to melt your body down into a puddle of its elements.
When I have broken down all components of your body, I then rebuild it into the form I am thinking of.
Or, you know, something vaguely close enough, anyway.
Uh...that doesn't sound particularly safe to me.
It's as safe as houses! Why, I have only had thirty-six major accidents this month!
So, what do you say? Feel like a change?
Sure, do it.
You, of course, agree that if by some accident you are turned into a frog you have no rights for compensation or refund.
No, thanks. I'm happy as I am.

Can you give me some more pharmakos berries?

No problem, but please remember that the amulet I will sell you is only a copy of my own. It contains no magical powers and, as such, will only cost you 100 coins.
Could you do anything about my voice?

pages.x: So, Player, your curiosity leads you to speak to me?

pages.x: Who are you and what are you doing here?
I am the great Malignius Mortifer, wielder of strange and terrible powers. These lowly followers of mine are dedicated students of the magical arts.
Their business is to follow me and learn all they can.
They don't look very tough.
You may believe that, but even if you strike one down, another will rise up within minutes.
Yeah, right.
Each of my followers is a master of his chosen element. His life becomes bound to that element in a way you could not hope to understand.
And what do you do?
I am mastering a branch of magic that few dare to attempt: Necromancy!
The fools in the Guild of Wizards shun anyone who practices this art, but there are a few across the lands who know the rudiments. Grayzag, Invrigar, Sithik...
Even Melzar studied the methods of necromancy, until an accident affected his mind. Now his spells tend to result in... ...
well, let us simply say that he does NOT raise armies of undead minions.

o: What would you like to say?
Why do you keep making fungi appear?

pages.x: Is this like Summoning? Can you teach me?
The obscure magical art of necromancy has nothing to do with Summoning.
Through necromancy, I may resurrect the bodies of those who have fallen, and bend them to my will, and even command them to tell me hidden knowledge.
I shall not pass on my secrets lightly to any passer-by!
Even a mighty hero like me?
What happened to Melzar?
The forces required to wield power over the dead are very difficult to control. Melzar's concentration slipped, and his spell rebounded upon him.
Although he did not die, his mind broke. Now he dwells amidst the beasts that fill his strange home, and when he attempts to do magic he gets... amusing results.
Why do you keep making fungi appear?
Necromancy is... still not fully understood. So few people dare to study it. Although my spells usually raise whichever undead creature I desire, they sometimes misfire.
As Melzar has learnt!
Thanks, I'll be off now.
I am sure your curiosity will eventually draw you to speak to me again, Player.
Can you teach me something about magic?
Where can I get clothes like those?
Bah! Our garments are an outward sign of our dominance of the magical arts. You cannot simply buy them in a shop!
What happens if I kill you and take them?
Try it and see!
How about if you teach me enough about magic so I can wear those clothes too?
How about if I turn you into a mushroom to make you stop bothering me?
MMMmmph!

Actually, I don't want to talk to you.

pages.x: Actually, I don't want to talk to you.
Bah! Then go away!
