conversations.section: At the entrance to the Grand Exchange / Talking to her

pages.x: Good day! How can I help you?

o: Tell me more about treasure trails.
Where can I get my own clue scrolls from?

pages.x: Across the world there is treasure buried that can be recovered... if you know where to look!
If you're lucky in your adventures you may come across something called a clue scroll.
You may find some monsters drop them when they die, or may discover one while you are training your skills.
When you read the clue scroll, it will point you to somewhere else on Gielinor. The challenge here is deciphering where the clue scroll wants you to go.
But if you can figure it out, head to that location and do what the clue asks of you.
Treasure trails can be multiple steps, so don't be surprised if it leads you to another clue scroll.
Keep going and eventually you will find the treasure you seek!
If you happen to find a clue scroll that you're unable to complete, I'll take it off your hands in return for an easier one.
What type of clue scroll would you like to know more about?
Some of the ways you can get easy clue scrolls include killing various low-level monsters across Gielinor, by pickpocketing members of H.A.M.
(they have a hideout in Lumbridge, don't tell them I let you know!), and as an uncommon drop when defeating evil trees.
Some of the ways you can get medium clue scrolls include killing various mid-level monsters across Gielinor and purchasing one from Stanley Limelight with thaler.

Some of the ways you can get hard clue scrolls include killing various high-level monsters across Gielinor, by pickpocketing dwarf traders and elven clan workers, and purchasing one from Stanley Limelight with thaler.

Some of the ways you can get elite clue scrolls include killing various high-level monsters across Gielinor, by pickpocketing Waiko islanders and elven clan workers, using crystal triskelion keys, and purchasing one from Stanley Limelight with thaler.
You can also get a guaranteed elite clue scroll once a week from treasure chests in your aquarium and by defeating the Skeletal Horror.
Ah, the master clues! The rarest of the rare.
The best way to get your hands on these is by completing treasure trails as you'll occasionally find them within the reward caskets.
There's also a small chance that you will get a master clue from anything that normally gives you an elite clue - it's quite rare though so good luck!
Ha! Well that's a tricky question even for me. Listen, I don't rightly know but there are some curiosities to the whole business.
As far as I can tell, all of this is setup by a fella by the name of Uri.
I've been hunting these clue scrolls for years and his supply of treasures seems pretty limitless.
Of course, if that wasn't strange enough - there's also someone who looks identical to Uri, who seems set on sabotaging the whole thing.
Then there are the wizards that pop up from time to time who may try to attack you.
And even more bizarre than that? All the people that these clue scrolls point to - if you ask them about it afterwards, they have no idea what you're talking about!
Like it never happened!
I know what you're thinking, this all sounds like the ramblings of a mad woman. But I swear, every word I say is true!
Basically, even after all these years I still have no idea. If you ever figure it out, I'd love to know. Just to put my mind at ease if anything else.
The name's Zaida, and this brute here is Nigel.
Do you want some advice? Scrap that, I'm going to give it to you anyway. You don't get anywhere in life without putting in hard work.
I'm a treasure hunter, have been my whole life.
Turns out there is treasure buried across the whole of Gielinor and if you spend the time looking there is more wealth than you can imagine just waiting for someone to discover it.
I can't tell you what to do with your life but I'd give up that adventuring lark and focus on finding these trasures.
After all, we all know that money buys happiness.
May good fortune come your way!
I can exchange any clue scroll you have for one of a lower tier. Just give me the clue you want to exchange.
What do you have for sale?
I have titles, a pet, clue scrolls and more! Let's not forget the Globetrotter outfit that will help you on your trails.
Hi there. I would like to reclaim my Globetrotter outfit please.

conversations.section: In Tarddiad, after The Light Within / Using an ancient elven wedding ring on Angof

pages.x: I found this ring, does this mean anything to you?
Let me look at that...
No...Maldwyn.
He...he is...was...my husband.
I'm sorry.
I don't blame you Player. I imagine he left you little choice and if I'm truthful, I lost him long ago.
It's painful to talk about him, but I'll try. What would you like to know?
How did you meet?
We grew up together originally, before we both lost ourselves to the crystal.
We used to run through the forest together, playing the games that young boys tend to play.
We would keep each other away from the crystals and we supported each other through the most painful times.
We weren't perfect. We failed more than once. But we were there to help the other back again when we did.
Eventually he proposed to me and I accepted.
But that was a long time ago now.
Wait - young boys?
Yes. This body was born, incorrectly, male. I changed that.
You say that as though it is unusual. We are shapeshifters, gender to us is hardly a constant.
Sometimes we are born into a body that is not ours. Without the crystal that would be the end of it, but I was fortunate enough to be able to correct that mistake.
What I was is irrelevant. What I am is all that matters.
Sorry, continue your story.
As you wish, now where was I?
What was he like?
Practical. He knew what we needed and he made sure that we got it.
This is not a world where grand sweep romantic gestures are still relevant.
What was important...what I loved about him...was that he kept us safe, alive and sane.
He had a dry sense of humour and an appropriate sense of comic timing. He knew what to say when I was stressed and when not to say anything.
He could make me forget this horrible life, if only for a perfect little moment.
And now he's gone.
Are you ok?
In many ways he's been dead to me for years. So I'll survive.
But am I ok? No Player, I have not been ok for many...many years.
I'll give you some space.
Thank you.
Oops.
No no, please, make fun of this. You have slaughtered the love of my life. My only light in a lifetime of endless, cloying, darkness.
But no, go ahead, make fun.

conversations.section: During The Bird and the Beast / Armadylean / Gold token

pages.x: Your fight for freedom has been noticed by Armadyl. How can I help you?
How's the battle going?
We are holding back the forces of Bandos, but we are at a stalemate. We need to gather divine energy so our cause can prevail.
Can you tell me about the gods?
Armadyl
Armadyl has proven - time and time again - that he is a great leader who can achieve peace and freedom, as long as we have faith in him.
You might ask why a peaceful god is at battle. This is not something Armadyl wants. Bandos is war personified, so he cannot be allowed to live.
Our tribes have followed Armadyl for as long as I can recall. We kept our faith in him, even when we thought he had died. Finally, our loyalty has been rewarded.
By following Armadyl, we hope to bring peace to the gods. That - in turn - will allow peace and prosperity for Gielinor.
Bandos
Bandos seeks ownership of the world at all costs, even to the expense of those who follow him.
He doesn't do this by subtle means. He starts battle after battle.
You can see that he lusts for combat. Even if he defeats all the gods, that lust will remain.
This is why Armadyl has come to stop him. We can halt the cycle of war and bring peace to all species.
Guthix
Guthix did not favour war. I agree with that notion completely.
But Guthix also neglected to deal with the gods' aggression. He chose to put up a barrier and ignore them. He hoped the problem would disappear.
That approach was always going to fail. Eventually - and tragically - it did.
I have questions about you.
Please, ask.
Who are you?
I'm Taka'ra - high mage of the many tribes that follow Armadyl.
I have led the tribes for ten years. For many of those, we assumed that Armadyl died during the God Wars. Regardless, we continued to follow Armadyl's instructions.
I live for the day that Armadyl's plan comes to fruition.
Where are you from?
My tribe is from Abbinah.
It's a particularly unwelcoming place. Floating islands collide with each other and the only water is found at the planet's core.
We cherish and hate our home in equal measure.
Why do you follow Armadyl?
Armadyl represents a belief that all gods and mortals can live in peace.
Our tribe has experienced the consequences of in-fighting and we strive to bring peace to others.
How is it you survived the aviansie's destruction? (After asking anything else)
The day of destruction was a painful one for the aviansie. I would rather not talk about it with just anyone.
What happened after the God Wars? (After asking anything else)
What happened in those dark days is a matter close to my heart, and something I only share with those whom I trust completely.
Back to the present.
I have a question about my orders.
Continue assisting our caravans, hindering those of our enemy, and claiming territory along the roadways. You are doing well so far.
As you have impressed me, I ask that you spread the word of Armadyl. I'm hoping we get more recruits like you.
I have no more questions.
May Armadyl guide us to freedom.

conversations.section: In Draynor Village / Normally

pages.x: Howdy there, partner.
Hi, Diango.

o: (If the player is missing the golden cracker:)

pages.x: The makers of the world have won an award! Have a cracker, with our compliments!

o: Would you like a golden cracker?
Diango gives you a golden cracker.

pages.x: Thanks, Diango!
Pull it with another person and you'll get a special surprise!
Now, what can I do for you? Want to see my spinning plates or kites? Want to check out my range of party items? Or did you want an item back?
Feel free to collect it later! Now, what can I do for you? Want to see my spinning plates or kites? Want to check out my range of party items?
Or did you want an item back?

o: I'd like to check my items, please.
Can you check my bank for items?

pages.x: Spinning plates?
That's right - there's a funny story behind them. Their shipment was held up by thieves.
The crate was marked 'Dragon Plates'. Apparently they thought it was some kind of armour, when really it's just a plate with a dragon on it!
Wow, a kite!
You're not the first to say that...
Can I have one, please?
Well, I suppose I did order more than I need... It's yours for the bargain price of 100 coins.

o: That's a bargain! I'll take one.
No, thanks, I don't want one.

pages.x: That's a bargain! I'll take one.
No, thanks, I don't want one.
Party items, you say?
Yep!
In a partnership with my pal Party Pete, we've decided to launch a whole range of partyware to help celebrate the Royal Wedding of the King Black Dragon and the Kalphite Queen.
Confetti, bubble makers, fireworks, firecrackers. We even have a commemorative mug!
King Black Dragon and Kalphite... Wait, what?
Er, well, that's what I was told; perhaps our providers got it wrong. Mind you, it wouldn't be the first time.
Like, this once, we were due to receive a shipment of dragon mail, and we got a pile of slightly singed letters instead.
Anyway, we've got all those items on sale, and I even have a suitable bouquet available for those who want to emulate the happy bride!
She had a bouquet? The Kalphite Queen? Big bug, beady-eyed, occasionally flies about when it's not laying eggs... Are we talking about the same creature?
Listen, partner, I'm not the one writing the advertising pitch here. I got the goods and been told what to say in order to sell them.
It's not the most convincing pitch I've ever had to do, but, if you ask me, the products don't need a pitch. They speak for themselves. Have a butcher's.
Sure thing, let me just see what you're missing.
Sure thing, let me see what I can take off your hands.
I'll look through items that I will hold onto, items that could go into a costume room in your house and junk items.

conversations.section: At Kharid-et / After completing the Archaeology tutorial

pages.x: Hey, Player, I'm over here!

o: Why are you the site manager here?
What is this dig site about?
I want to talk about mysteries.
Azzanadra? What are you still doing out here?

pages.x: Ha! I'm something of an expert on Zarosian history, would you not say?
Obviously, I just thought you were going incognito when at dig sites.
I am careful not to tip my trilby, but I have proven to be invaluable to the Archaeology Guild, nonetheless.
Surprisingly, given the finds made at the Senntisten dig, the Guild have lower interest in the Kharid-et site than some of the others that have come to their attention.
It makes a certain sense, I guess. If you already have access to the capital city of the empire, there would be less interest in a tiny little fort.
So, when I requested to manage this site, there was no contention.
If the Guild's interest in Kharid-et is so low, why ask to manage the site?
An astute question, Player. Remember that I KNOW where the secrets are buried. It's something of a cheat, as an archaeologist, to be sure.
Given how powerful you are, though, why use Guild resources? Why not just magic your way where you want to get?
Now, where would be the fun in that? Even entities like me need hobbies! It's not the prize it's the progression.
Archaeology is about telling the story, not jumping to the last page to see whodunnit!
I bet it was the butler. It's always the butler.
So, tell me about this dig site...
This was Kharid-et, a Zarosian fort sat on the frontlines of the Menaphite-Zarosian war. An entire legion was once stationed here.
More than that, it holds particular significance for my people, for this was where the Mahjarrat pledged allegiance to Lord Zaros.
While Tumeken was an honourable leader, we quickly saw that Zaros would be
able to free us in a way Tumeken never could.
It has taken time, to be certain.
There have been many setback and our numbers have dwindled significantly in the interim, but now the Mahjarrat are free of sacrificial rituals and have grown in power immensely.
There's more to your interest here than a walk down memory lane, I'd wager.
Indeed. The last time I set foot here was after Zamorak's betrayal.
Many parts of the empire became immediately vulnerable to our enemies, and Kharid-et was alone at the edge of the empire.
I tasked a trusted loyalist with defending it and its secrets.
She very clearly achieved this task - for the most part - but I would like to learn of the events that transpired here and how she died. I miss her dearly.
So, you're saying there's something here worth finding. Is it powerful? Is it dangerous?
Haha! Oh, Player. Let me just say that there is nothing hidden here that I would not trust you with also.
Much has changed for me since the fall of the empire, and many of the concerns I used to hold have long since evaporated.

o: Which mystery would you like to discuss?

pages.x: Not so loud! I'm not Azzanadra, I'm just filling in for him. Apparently he had more important things to do.
You're not Azzanadra? Who are you then?
Your wisest and most humble friend from Nardah.
Wahisietel?
Shh! Yes. Do me a favour and just pretend I'm Dr Nabanik.
Er, okay. So where is Azzanadra?
He might be inside the excavation. Try the main fortress area.
I'll be here should you need me, Player.

conversations.section: In Prifddinas

pages.x: Hello, Player, how can I help?
Can you tell me about yourself?
It's me, Iestin Edern, the new lord of Clan Iorwerth!
My family falls under the auspices of Clan Iorwerth, but it is unusual for one of my standing to be given lordship over the clan.
It normally passes to an heir within the family. Except that Morvran - the heir apparent - has waived his claim.
It's just as well though. Both Clan Iorwerth and the other clans felt that our clan needed someone more progressive to return us to peace.
For some reason, they thought that meant me! But I'm stepping up to the role, to honour the memory of my brother.
I fear it was an attempted raising of the Dark Lord that led to the creation of the shadows which killed him.
Clan Iorwerth will not be heading down that path again, I assure you.
Can you tell me about Clan Iorwerth?
We are a clan of warriors without a war to fight.
He says right after an elf civil war ends...
Yes, but that was our one and only war. Seren forbade us from engaging those who attempted to breach our borders, during the God Wars.
She protected us, of course, kept them out, but if she'd let us we could have stopped them from trying over and over again.
But we were left to guard a city that was protected from on high - a waste of our talents. We should have been allowed to travel east with the Cadarn.
So it was jealousy?
No, nothing so base.
All of my kind wishes for the ability to return home. Ever since the World Gate was taken from us we've been stranded here.
If the Iorwerth had been given leave to travel beyond the forest, we might have stopped that from happening, or spared our kind from what befell King Baxtorian and Queen Glarial.
To make matters worse, Seren abandoned us. What were we to do?
Seren gone. Baxtorian and the Cadarn gone. Someone had to lead our people. We didn't see anyone else offering.
We just wanted to show the other clans what we were capable of.
So the civil war was for the good of the other clans?
War is for the good of none, but what led towards it started out as noble intent. The other clan elders disagreed with our more militant view.
They reverted the city to seed form to protect it from us, but we were ever only trying to protect them, and to find a way back to Tarddiad.
To the Iorwerth, they were the traitors. They robbed us of our homes, of Seren's light.
Over the years, our clan lost sight of why this all started, and then this whole business with raising the Dark Lord happened. We lost our way.
Can you tell me about Clan Iorwerth's skills?
Clan Iorwerth is comprised of proud and skilled warriors. If the elves were ever to amass an army, its bulk would be comprised of Clan Iorwerth.
Oh, the Cadarn would field their mages and scouts, the Ithell some war singers, and the Trahaearn some of their combat automatons, but Clan Iorwerth would form the backbone.
For the army to break, Clan Iorwerth would have to break, and that's just not something we do.
So your troops are predominantly melee fighters?
Yes - though we do count some trackers and scouts among our number. We've had to become self-reliant, thanks to the civil war.
Our troops favour the halberd for its reach, and twin daggers for close-quarter fighting.
You are welcome to test them in combat. An untested warrior is useless, like a dulled blade.
We also have a slayer master in our ranks - Morvran. Strictly, he should have become the new Lord Iorwerth, and frankly I'm glad he waived that right.
Not so that I could become lord, you understand. He's amiable enough, but he has some odd predilections.
There's just something slightly off about him, and I can't quite identify what.

conversations.section: In Shilo Village / After completing the Shilo Village quest

pages.x: Hello.
Hello Bwana, What can I do for you today?

o: Can you tell me a bit about this this place?

pages.x: Can you tell me a bit about this this place?
Of course Bwana, you look like a traveller!
Yes I am actually!
Well, I am a traveller myself, and I have set up this hostel for adventurers and travellers who are weary from their journey.
There is a dormitory upstairs if you are tired, it costs 35 gold pieces which covers the cost of laundry and cleaning.

o: Buy a pack of 5 Dorm tickets: 175 Gold

pages.x: Very good [sir/madam]!
Very good [sir/madam]!
Very good [sir/madam]!
Very good [sir/madam]!

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.}}
Could I buy a spare of the reward?

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Tasks in the Karamja set, you are presented with a pair of gloves.
Completing each difficulty level of the set will allow your gloves to be improved.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in the set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Karamja set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
You can claim your Karamja set reward from Jackie the Fruit at the Brimhaven Agility Arena, me, or one of the jungle foresters to the south.
Karamja gloves 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Karamja gloves 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
No thanks.
Karamja gloves 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Karamja gloves 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,000 coins.
No thanks.

conversations.section: Armadylean

pages.x: Why, hello there, brave soldier of Armadyl! What can I do for you?
I have some questions about you.
What do you want to know?
Who are you?
Call me Kamiee. I'm the head diviner of the Armadyleans.
I've been experimenting with divination since wisps started popping up. Armadyl noticed me and asked me to help. Very convincing bird he is, too!
I construct items and weapons to assist in the battle against Bandos.
I study it all the time - even in my free time, you know? I'm relied on, you see. It's important we achieve Armadyl's vision of peace between mortals and gods.
Where are you from?
I was born here. I mean, I was born in Varrock. It was tough. We didn't have two slices of cheese to rub together, and we had to make do with our wits and empty tummies.
It was hard, no doubt about that. It got harder when a gang murdered my parents.
I survived on my own. Aubury sneaked me the odd rune to practice with, hidden in loaves of bread. Almost choked the first time!
I'd got a decent grasp on magic. But when divination energy started popping up, I was a natural.
I met Taka'ra, who introduced me to Armadyl. They explained what they wanted to do with the world and... Well, you can't knock it, can you? Peace beats war every time.
Why do you follow Armadyl?
I've been a scrapper all my life. Staying alive by kicking people where it hurts and running away, you know?
But Armadyl showed me that living can't be about running away.
He told me about when he ran away, hopping from world to world when he thought his aviansie were dead. He came to realise that running was achieving nothing.
If he wanted to mean anything, he had to stand.
So he stands against warmongers. And I'm doing the same. He's come back as a phoenix, and I'm back as a phoenix too! At least, if I can get some slightly redder feathers.
This is why I follow Armadyl. He's striving to end the constant wars between the gods, so that one day we can all live in peace. It's a lovely thought.
Can I ask something else?
I have questions about divination.
What do you want to know?
What is it?
Divination is as far as I've got to grips with it - the process of gathering the life juice of Guthix and weaving it into divine energy.
The energy's a kind of magic matter that can be made into various gubbins.
You'll create things like portents, signs and divine locations. Things that can help you with your day-to-day life.
In our case, we're powering a building-sized ritual to stop Bandos. A war-ender. We call it the Divine Focus.
Why are you using it?
Where did it come from?
I'm told that divination has only come about since the death of Guthix. So, some smart fellas are saying that it's Guthix's life force.
Or it could be the barrier that Guthix put up to stop the gods from returning.
Or it could be the energy from the world, and it's been leaking out since the Battle of Lumbridge.
Whatever it is, diviners are putting the lifeforce back into the world and hoping that nothing bad happens.
Can I ask something else?
I have questions about the Divine Focus.
That's all I have to say.
Get divining! In the name of Armadyl!

conversations.section: After Death Plateau

pages.x: Hello Sabbot, how's it going?
Terrible! The missus is still insisting on living on the surface like some sort of...some sort of...
Tree?
Yes! Exactly! Like some sort of TREE!
So, I'm going to sort this place out myself! At least there's room to have a separate toilet down here.
Urgh...that explains the smell.
You shut your cake hole! Why did you come to bother me anyway?

o: Why are you living in this cave?
Do you want me to get anything for you?
I think that's it for now.

pages.x: Cave? CAVE? This is no cave, ya idiot!
This is clearly the entrance hall to the trading post I'm gonna set up with me wife, once the trolls are gone.
We're going to have some shelves over there, and put the store room over there...
Well...you have to admit it's a little...unpolished.
Aye? Well blame the missus for that! The second the trolls came along she packed all the tools up and moved into her fancy-dan little cottage.
But not me. I'm not shifting for some stupid trolls. It's them or me, and I'm winning so far.
One day they'll all be dead.
Then I'll work this place into a proper little home and shop. Then who'll be laughing, eh?
Probably you, in a high-pitched, insane cackle.
I heard that!
Uh, I need to ask something else.

o: Can you tell me where the tunnel is?
Where is your wife's house again?

pages.x: Don't be daft, man. Do I look like I can just magic up a tunnel for ya?
But haven't you lived here a long time? Don't you know?
Well, I've been tryin' to work the place a little, you're right. But all I've got to work with is rocks.
If I had some ores I'd be laughing mind, but there's none!

o: Why are you living in this cave?
Where is your wife's house again?
Do you want me to get anything for you?
I think that's it for now.

pages.x: You can't miss her place. It's a little house to the west of here. You just need to follow the only path in that direction and you'll get there.

o: Why are you living in this cave?
Can you tell me where the tunnel is?
I think that's it for now.

pages.x: No!
But I could get you a pickaxe, or a hammer.
No!
What about some food, or some tea?
NO!
I don't need you, or yer fancy tools. I'm a dwarf! If I can't do it on me own then I might as well not bother!
Do ye think I'd be stuck in this hole, fighting trolls with me bare hands and teeth, eating moss, and chipping the walls with a stone if I didn't think I could do it?
These trolls aren't gonna beat me! I'm gonna outlast them, and when me wife comes to her senses she'll come back and we can set up together!
Aye, we'll set up this little shop, just like we planned. And no trolls are gonna stop us.
Uh...okay.

o: Why are you living in this cave?
Where is your wife's house again?
Can you tell me where the tunnel is?
I think that's it for now.

pages.x: Oh, is it now? Well get yourself out then! Watch your head on the way out, mind.

conversations.section: Talk to / If the player isn't a Player Moderator / In Falador, Seers' Village, Varrock, or Wendlewick

pages.x: Oh, hello citizen. Are you here to find out about Player Moderators? Or perhaps would you like to know about the laws of the land?
Tell me about Player Moderators.
Of course. What would you like to know?

o: How do I become a Player Moderator?
What can Player Moderators not do?

pages.x: What is a Player Moderator?
Player Moderators are normal players of the game, just like you.
However, since they have shown themselves to be trustworthy and active reporters, they have been invited by Jagex to monitor the game and take appropriate
action when they see rule breaking.
You can spot a Player Moderator in game by looking at the chat screen - when a Player Moderator speaks, a silver crown appears to the left of their name.
Remember, if there's no silver crown
there, they are not a Player Moderator! You can check out the website if you'd like more information.
Thanks!
Is there anything else you'd like to know?
What can Player Moderators do?
Player Moderators, or 'P-mods', have the ability to mute rule breakers and Jagex view their reports as a priority so that action is taken as quickly as possible.
P-mods also have access to the Player Moderator Centre. Within the
Centre are tools to help them Moderate RuneScape. These tools include dedicated forums, the Player Moderator Guidelines and the Player Moderator Code of Conduct.
Thanks!
Is there anything else you'd like to know?
How do I become a Player Moderator?
Jagex picks players who spend their time and effort to help better the RuneScape community. To increase your chances of becoming a Player Moderator:
Keep your account secure! This is very important, as a player with poor security will never be a P-Mod. Read our Security Tips for more information.
Play by the rules! The rules of RuneScape are enforced for a reason, to make the game a fair and enjoyable environment for all.
Report accurately! When Jagex consider an account for review they look for quality, not quantity.
Ensure your reports are of a high quality by following the report guidelines.
Be excellent to each other! Treat others as you would want to be treated yourself. Respect your fellow player. More information can be found on the website.
Thanks!
Is there anything else you'd like to know?
What can Player Moderators not do?
P-Mods cannot ban your account - they can only report offences. Jagex then takes action based on the evidence received.
If you lose your password or get scammed by another player, P-Mods cannot help you get your account
back. All they can do is recommend you go to Player Support.
They cannot retrieve any items you may have lost and they certainly do not receive any free items from Jagex for moderating the game. They are players
who give their all to help the community, out of the goodness of their hearts!
P-Mods do not work for Jagex and therefore cannot make you a Moderator, or recommend other accounts to become Moderators. If you wish to
become a Moderator, feel free to ask me!
Thanks!
Is there anything else you'd like to know?

conversations.section: Subsequent conversations

pages.x: Is there something you wish to discuss, human?

o: Ask about the people of Kanatah.
What do your people think of me?
I'd like to talk about something else.

pages.x: You are not accustomed to this title? It is reserved for only one in each of our villages, yes.
The Acca is the wisest of all the Goebies who live there, and above all, has the greatest rock upon their back.
It is the Acca's burden not only to bear the weight of their own rock, but also those of all the Goebies who follow them. That burden is mine, human.
These young Goebies look to me to take care of them. Such is my duty.
The Goebies you see around this camp are some of the bravest you will find. Mm, most of them have lost loved ones, some are even orphans.
Yet they share one thing in common, human. They have each stood up to the Airut. Defying their captors and risking death for a more meaningful existence.
Most of us came from the Airut territory to the north, but this camp is our home now, yes. Kanatah stands as a message that those beasts do not own us.

o: I'd like to talk about something else.

pages.x: This camp is Kanatah. It may not look like much, but it is our home. We chose to build it here, right under the Airut's noses, ha!
Those base-minded animals harry us day and night, hmm. They may be strong but they underestimate us, and we have been learning their patterns.
When they come we hide among the rocks or evacuate to the south, then move back in when they have had their fill of destruction.
True, the camp has to be rebuilt regularly, but their frustration is greatly pleasing to us.
You wish to know more of our broken home? I am unsure why you have even ventured here, Player.
You come in search of treasures and power, but you will find only death and desolation. Hmm...
Perhaps you could succeed where our greatest warriors have failed and defeat the monsters that lie within our old city.
I know little about what remains of our old civilisation. A life of captivity has deprived me of such knowledge.
We sometimes find wreckages on the beach to the east, though. I suspect that other camps like ours existed, but they did not survive long.

o: I'd like to talk about something else

pages.x: Many years ago the great beast known as Tuska came from the sky and tore this world asunder. The Goebies here know only what the Airut have told them.
That Tuska devoured the guardian spirits and temples that gave us power. But I know the truth, human.
Tuska was a destroyer spirit, sent to punish us for using their power. The other spirits hid from her, but they are still here, friend.
I will teach the others to commune with them as our ancestors once did.

o: Tell Acca Kanatah about defeating Tuska.

pages.x: Tuska came to our home planet as well. We were able to defeat her, but it required the might of thousands of champions and even the help of gods.
You defeated the destroyer spirit? I... I can hardly believe it, Player.
I have not heard of these 'gods' you speak of, but they must command the power of many great spirits.
Pah, the Airut, they are mindless beasts! I learned plenty about them in captivity.
They claim their ancestors rode Tuska, using her spines to steer her between planets and wreak havoc as they went.
Sometimes they fight over whose ancestors took the helm and directed Tuska by her very tusks! Haha, the fools! In reality they are nothing but pests.
Tuska shook them from her back as we shake lizards from our rocks.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Before joining the Imperial Guard

pages.x: Hi!
Ah, a new recruit! Good, you're just in time.
Uh, what? I'm no-
It's always good to see fresh blood on the ground. You can take over from Wilkins - he's never been quite right...ever since the explosion.
Explosion? What? I can't take over for anyone. I don't know what to do!
We all feel like that the first few days, lad/lass. You'll come to grips with it soon enough.
But I'm not a new recruit! I don't know what I'm doing! I don't even know who you are!
Why, I remember when I first joined the guard... Captain Murry threw me off the defence into th- Wait, what? You're not a new recruit?
Hmm, now that you mention it, you are out of uniform, soldier.
That's because I don't have a uniform! I don't work for you.
Well, we can fix that soon enough. Lad/Lass. Would you like to join the Imperial Guard and defend Burthope from the most vile of creatures?
Put your life on the line to keep at bay the scum of the earth? Risk your health to-
I get the idea!

pages.i: Do you want to join the Imperial Guard?

pages.x: Yes, I'll join the Imperial Guard.
Fantastic! You are in for the thrill of a lifetime. The adventure of the ages. The journ-
What do I have to do?
Hmm? Oh, of course. I'll make it quick. We can't dilly-dally. Monkey about. Sit on our bu-
*ahem* You were explaining?
Every month, you can come back here and help defend the gatehouse.
Why every month? Aren't trolls invading all the time?
Yes, but due to union regulations we can only have each shift work once a month. There are two things you can do to help the gatehouse.
You may only choose to do one to gain a reward. You can still play the other, for practice, any time you like. So, things you can do to help defend the gatehouse...
First, you can fight trolls. You stand alone in front of the gate and fight off as many trolls as you can until you die.
What? Until I die?
Well...maybe not die. Basically, we leave you out there until you 'almost' die, then drag you back in. That way you don't lose any of your stuff.
Okay, what's the other thing I can do?
Oh, that's much safer. Well, you won't die, but Norris did have a nervous breakdown a few weeks ago. I guess the strain of it got to him.
Oh no.
Basically, you run around repairing the gatehouse defences. Keep the oil drums full, repair barricade lines and gatehouse walls... You got all that?
That's the spirit! Which do you want to do? Remember: you'll only get rewarded for the first activity you complete each month.

o: No, I'd like a little more detail.

pages.x: No, I'd like a little more detail.
Ah, the detail-oriented type. Cautious. Timid? Nah! You don't look timid! What do you want to know more about?

pages.i: What do you want to ask about?

pages.x: Not today, thanks.
Suit yourself!

conversations.section: During Halloween 2015 Event

pages.x: Welcome, adventurer!

o: Ask how for information about the event.
Ask what else you can do at the event.

pages.x: I'm Ka. I'm helping Icthlarin by explaining to all you adventurers how you can help the cause. He made it so everyone here can understand me without a Catspeak Amulet!
Icthlarin is busy trying to hold the gates at the end of the bridge shut, so he needs help rounding all the extra souls up.
You can get on a boat at either of the piers by the start of the bridge and sail around gathering the lost souls.
There are even some special ones that will reward you with experience in certain skills! The ferryman by the pier will be able to tell you more.
Once you've gathered enough souls from the river you'll be able to return to shore and escort them across the bridge.
They need you protection to cross so make sure you skill Amascut's devourers or siphon them using divination!
The reason Icthlarin is holding the gates to the Underworld shut is because Amascut is trying to break through with her avatar - the biggest devourer yet.
Periodically she is managing to break open the gates, at which point Icthlarin will need all the help he can get to bring the giant lion's head down!
If you find you need a break from battling Amascut's forces, there is also a fully functioning ectofuntus down here where you can train you prayer.
That old grouch Necrovarus is here too. He'll be able to give you more information about that.
You'll also notice all your actions gain you Noumenon Favour for helping Icthlarin in his fight.
Talk to Sinn Derkwill just west of me to find out what you can buy with your earnings. He's an odd fellow, but very helpful!
You want to know about me? I'm not sure where to start. Hmm... Well, I was once a priestess in Amascut's clergy. A human, just like you.
The end of the second age was a difficult time to live in the Kharid. Everywhere you looked war was taking its toll.
As a priestess I spent my days trying to help the poor and infirmed. Day by day poverty strengthened its grip on the land.
We prayed to Amascut for out crops to grow and allies to arrive, but they never did. She had left this world with Icthlarin. We didn't know if they would ever return.
When they finally did we rejoiced. Our saviours had returned and brought with them an army of Stern Judges and that would turn the tide of the war.
We were elated, for a time. Parties were held in the streets, crops grew plentifully and the rivers burst their banks, but it was not to last...
What happened?
The Stern Judges betrayed us and the war grew bloody once more.
Icthlarin and Amascut's father, Tumeken, was forced to sacrifice himself to put an end to it, turning the Kharid into a desert in the process.
Soon afterwards Amascut decided to destroy everything she once stood for. She decimated her temples and with them her entire clergy.
Though my memories of what ensued are few, I do remember arriving in this place. The stone bridge stretching into the darkness was imprinted in my mind.
Icthlarin saw what Amascut had done and believed himself to blame. He offered rebirth to each of the priestesses.
We accepted, vowing to stop Amascut before it was too late.
Amascut was once responsible for rebirth, but now Icthlarin must fulfil that duty as well as his own.
This is why it has become increasingly rare for a soul to be reincarnated.
Most of my knowledge comes from personal experience, but it would seem people are usually reincarnated as cats.
You may have heard of Robert the Strong of my friend Neite who was a priestess of Amascut as well. Both of them also became cats after their rebirths.
I wonder how many other cats out there are just waiting for someone with a Catspeak Amulet to speak to them...
There was a time when I devoted my life to her, when she was the Goddess of Rebirth.
Amascut would stand beside Icthlarin at the gates to the Underworld that lie ahead of us, offering rebirth to the few chosen souls that deserved it.
Few know that she was also responsible for destroying the darkest, most evil of souls as well. A burden which must have weighed heavy on her shoulders.
After she left this world with Icthlarin I am sure something happened to her, for once she returned she was not the same - and she never would be again.
I believe her father sacrificing himself to save the Kharid from Zaros' empire was the straw that broke the camel's back. Amascut completed her descent into madness.
The part of her responsible for destroying souls completely consumed her. She became what she is today... The Devourer.

conversations.section: In Varrock Palace / Beacon dialogue

pages.x: I was wondering if you could tell me more about the beacons.
Of course. What would you like to know?

o: I'm here to claim my reward.
What else needs to be done to test the beacon network?
I'd like a few more details, please.
I don't have anything more to talk about, actually.

pages.x: I'm here to claim my reward!
Thank you again, Player. Misthalin is truly in your debt.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask me?
What else needs to be done to test the beacon network?
What *doesn't* need to be done is more like it! We need to make sure the entire beacon network is as robust as possible.
I'd be extremely grateful if you'd help us by trying to keep as many beacons alight simultaneously as you possibly can.
How does that help?
Well, obviously, it helps us verify that all the beacons are in good working order, of course.
The more testing, the better, Player. I have generous rewards for you if you manage to keep six, ten and all fourteen beacons alight simultaneously.
However, I'd be positively delighted if you continued on testing them day and night, over and over, relentlessly and without ceasing!
I see this means a great deal to you.
Oh, it does. The safety of one's kingdom is of paramount importance, you know.
Do you have any other questions for me, Player?
Talk to me about rewards.
Ahem, well. It's all well and good having a network of beacons, but it's important to make sure it works properly...and remains working.
Thus, I'm willing to offer various rewards if you are willing to help me out.
There are rewards available for keeping six, ten and all fourteen beacons alight simultaneously.
I'd like a few more details, please.

o: Why have you created all these beacons?
How will these beacons work in an emergency?
I don't have anything more to talk about, actually.

pages.x: Why have you created all these beacons?
You've already had a glimpse of the dangers we face from Morytania. Further dangers threaten from the Wilderness in the north.
Because of these mounting threats, the southern kingdoms have banded together to take action.
We have constructed a network of beacons that stretch all the way from the source of the River Salve to the northwestern-most edge of the Wilderness.
Should there be any threat from these uncivilised lands, we'll be able to spread the word as fast as the light of the flames can travel.
How will these beacons work in an emergency?
Simple. I've equipped each fire tender with a stockpile of gnomish firelighters. In the case of a real emergency, the beacons will burn with coloured flame.
I see. I don't suppose you have any extra firelighters lying around that you want to get rid of, do you?
Don't bother me with idle chatter. Is there anything else?
Who are these fire tenders?
These are special recruits from all around the civilised world. They've been carefully selected for their sharp eyes and long-distance vision.
Not to mention their dedication and reliability. We couldn't entrust such an important job to just anyone, you know!
I don't have anything more to talk about, actually.
Then begone; I am a busy man.
I don't have anything more to talk about, actually.
Then begone; I am a busy man.

conversations.section: Livid Farm / Talk-to / First time

pages.x: What's going on here?
I've livid to cure, fences to fix, patches to fertilise, I'm exhausted and-
Hold on, hold on. Take a deep breath and start from the beginning.
Sorry, this farming is so new to me. A while ago, I was approached by the dashing and brave Lokar Searunner.
Dashing and brave? I might be thinking of a different guy: a pirate who ferried me to a pirate ship.
No, that sounds right. In a courageous trip to Karamja, he came across a funny chap called Papa Mambo.
Lokar obtained some saplings from a vine that grows in the region and brought them to me. He wanted me to grow and enhance the vine using my magic.
We did an experiment on one sapling and quickly discovered that magic enhanced the tenacious attributes of the plant.
Lokar named them 'livid'.
Livid?
Yes, it likely stands for something clever. But it is clearly quite livid!
Hmm, I might have to pay a visit to Lokar. I shudder to think what he might be using this 'livid' for.
Don't be mean: he has admirable intentions. He plans to transport what I grow to Chieftain Brundt, to help protect their village from wild beasts.
Against wild beasts? The livid do sound vicious, I suppose.
They definitely are. They have a mind of their own, and they carry on living even when cut from their roots.
In exchange for the plants, Chieftain Brundt is kindly giving the Moon Clan some trade produce.
So, how can I help out on your farm?
Let me show you!
There are a variety of tasks you can help me out with here. You can do them in any order or just focus on individual tasks, if you want.
If you don't perform the tasks, I will eventually advance the farm on to its next stage, but don't expect any reward!
First there's fertilising patches. I've buried saplings on these patches and they will need fertilising to appear.
So, cast the Fertilise Soil spell on the patch...
...then the livid will grow and you'll get further knowledge in Magic and Farming.
Eventually, the livid will mature...
...but you will see that my plants get diseased quite often.
It seems they are susceptible to the parasites native to this isle. Cast the Cure Plant spell on the crop and, after a little refinement...
...Bingo! The livid is fine, and Magic and Farming experience are yours.
It's really tiring running this farm, so, sometimes, I'll need some help.
Simply give me a few encouraging words and I'll be able to draw upon your run energy, making me right-as-rain.
In exchange, you'll receive some experience in Agility. I can recover slowly by myself, but your assistance would be much appreciated.
Once I harvest the livid, I'll teleport it over to the produce pile.
It is here that you can grab up to ten livid and bunch them together with string using the String Jewellery spell.
Then, place the bundled produce in the trade wagon. With this last step, you'll get experience in Magic and Crafting.
Why is there a big pile of lumber, I hear you ask? Our fences often get into a state of disrepair.
I'm not sure if it's the pesky suqah or the sea breeze, but the wood doesn't last very long here.
Pick up some lunar lumber from the corner of the farm and use the Plank Make spell to turn them into fence posts.
Then use the post on the broken fence. You'll get Magic and Construction experience for your effort upon affixing the post.
So, there you have it!

conversations.section: 2017 / Build A Beach / When talked to

pages.x: Hello friend, are you here to help with Build-a-beach?

o: What was with the sand pits?

pages.x: Who are you?
I'm Reyna, and I love a good beach party.
So where is it then?
Well I have to keep rebuilding it ready for the party every year.
Some Guy keeps interfering and moving all my sand back to the desert.
Any idea who it was?
Nope, but if I ever catch him, I'll show him what for-ks!
What was that other event in the crater?
Some people moved in and brought all kinds of fluff with them!
I told them there'd be Helter pay for if they didn't.
Well given that it's now free again, I guess you're having another party?
I sure am!
How can I help?
Well, you can help with the Build-a-beach in a couple of ways...
You can gather sand whilst on going about your daily business and bring it to me.
Ordinary sand won't do, but you can find this stuff everywhere. It always gets in the cracks.
And the other?
You can help deliver the sand from this pile here next to me, to one of ones in the crater.
Watch out for the quick sand, and those sandstorms though.
If you drop it all before you get to the piles, just come back here and get some more.
I've also got some rewards including an outfit and a little magic ring I made for you if you help out.
Okay, got it.
What was with the sand pits?
Ah yes, well erm I was trying to teleport the sand from the desert straight to the crater but something went a bit wrong.
At least it's all sorted now.
Lovely weather...
Yes well, that seems to be an unfortunate side effect from when I tried to teleport the sand here.
Take care around the sandstorms for now, they'll give you a bit of a whirl if you get too close, though only whilst carrying sand it seems.
Got it.
Hopefully they'll blow out soon enough before we start the party.
What is The Beach Party?
Why it's only the best event of the year, that takes place in the summer near Lumbridge castle, previously where some Gods fought!
Unrivalled then. What can we do?
Well, there are plenty of activities to do, loads of skilling opportunities and portals that take you to other fun activities.
As well as shops with outfits and items for sale, and lots more!
I can't wait!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello, bold adventurer.
Yes, I use them to transport coal over the river. I will let other people use them too, I'm a nice person like that...
Just put coal in a truck and I'll move it down to my depot over the river.
Would you like a poison chalice?
Take one from my shop. You might consider buying one of my fine pickaxes while you're looking.
Pickaxes?
Yes, I've started a business. It's not going very well so far, but the poison chalices are quite a nice loss-leader.
It's an exciting drink I've invented. I don't know what it tastes like. I haven't tried it myself.

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?
I'd like to change my teleport point.

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
For completing the Seers' Village set, you are presented with a headband.
You will receive a better headband with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Seers' Village set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Seers' Village set rewards, speak to any seer in the village, Sir Kay in Camelot, or myself.
Seer's headband 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,000 coins.
No thanks.
I'd like to change my Camelot Teleport point.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge / Historical dialogue / Case 1

pages.x: Hello there, can I help you?

o: Are there any quests I can do here?}}

pages.x: What kind of quest are you looking for?

o: I fancy a bit of a fight, anything dangerous?
Something easy please, I'm new here.
I'm a thinker rather than a fighter, anything skill oriented?
I want to do all kinds of things, do you know of anything like that?

pages.x: Hmm.. dangerous you say? What sort of creatures are you looking to fight?

o: Small.. something small would be good.

pages.x: You are a brave soul indeed.
Now that you mention it, I heard a rumour about a Saradominist in the Varrock church who is rambling about some kind of greater evil.. sounds demon-like if you ask me.
Perhaps you should check it out if you are as brave as you say?
Ha ha. I personally don't believe in such things. However, there is a man in Draynor Village who has been scaring the village folk with stories of vampyres.
He's named Morgan and can be found in one of the village houses. Perhaps you could see what the matter is?
Small? Small isn't really that dangerous though is it?
Yes it can be! There could be anything from an evil chicken to a poisonous spider. They attack in numbers you know!
Point taken. Speaking of small monsters, I hear old Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower has just had his beads taken by a gang of mischievous imps.
Sounds like it could be a quest for you?
I can tell you about plenty of small easy tasks.
The Lumbridge cook has been having problems and the Duke is confused over some strange rocks.
It's funny really, the cook would forget his head if it wasn't screwed on. This time he forgot to get ingredients for the Duke's birthday cake.
Perhaps you could help him? You will probably find him in the Lumbridge Castle kitchen.
Well the Duke of Lumbridge has found a strange stone that no one seems to understand. Perhaps you could help him? You can probably find him upstairs in Lumbridge Castle.
Skills play a big part when you want to progress in knowledge. I know of a few skill-related quests that can get you started.
You may be able to help out Fred the farmer who is in need of someones crafting expertise.
Or, there's always Doric the dwarf who needs an errand running for him?
You can find Fred next to the field of sheep in Lumbridge. Perhaps you should go and speak with him.
Doric the dwarf is located north of Falador. He might be able to help you with smithing. You should speak to him. He may let you use his anvils.
Of course I do. Gielinor is a huge place you know, now let me think...
Hetty the witch in Rimmington might be able to offer help in the ways of magical abilities..
Also, pirates are currently docked in Port Sarim, Where pirates are, treasure is never far away...
Or you could go and help out Ernest who got lost in Draynor Manor, spooky place that.
Hetty the witch can be found in Rimmington, south of Falador. She's currently working on some new potions. Perhaps you could give her a hand?
She might be able to offer help with your magical abilities.
RedBeard Frank in Port Sarim's bar, the Rusty Anchor might be able to tell you about the rumored treasure that is buried somewhere in the world.
The best place to start would be at the gate to Draynor Manor. There you will find Veronica who will be able to tell you more.
I suggest you tread carefully in that place; it's haunted.

conversations.section: North of Kharazi Jungle

pages.x: Hello friend. You're a long way from civilisation!

o: How do I get into the Kharazi Jungle?}}
Can I get another bullroarer please?
Have you seen any natives in the jungle?}}

pages.x: How do I get into the Kharazi Jungle?
Well, I've not managed it yet but I heard that someone managed to find a way in. But they only just managed to escape the jungle with their lives.
Apparently he was on a mission to map the area. How foolish is that?

o: Well, in fact I plan to map that area myself.
So someone managed to get into the Kharazi Jungle?
Have you seen any natives in the jungle?

pages.x: Well, in fact I plan to map that area myself.
--The forester looks very interested-- Oh, well, that sounds quite good actually... Sorry if I sounded rude before, it just didn't seem like a good idea to me.
I guess I just wouldn't want to do it myself. But a map of that area would certainly be a big task. And it would certainly be very useful...
-- The forester looks very thoughtful --
Hey, if you manage to complete it, be sure to let me take a look! Well, best of luck with it, I'm sure you're going to need it.

o: Do you have any other tips about the Kharazi Jungle?
Have you seen any natives in the jungle?

pages.x: Do you have any other tips about the Kharazi Jungle?
Not really, but I would say be careful, it's a dangerous place. And good luck.
Are you calling me foolish?
No, of course not... Sorry, I have to be on my way...
So someone managed to get into the Jungle?
Yes, he said he was from some place... near the Sorcerer's Tower. Mentioned something about a legend? It meant nothing to me though.

o: How do I get into the jungle?

pages.x: Can I get another bullroarer please?
Hmmm, what we have here is an opportunity for trade! I'm a bit peckish so why not get me a tasty cooked oomlie wrap and we'll have a deal.
What do you do here?
I'm a forester, and I specialise in exotic woods. I've not managed to penetrate the Kharazi Jungle very far but I have found some interesting tree specimens.
If you do happen to get into the Kharazi Jungle, do come and let me know. I'd love to be able to safely navigate my own way in and out.

o: How do I get into the Kharazi Jungle?
Have you seen any natives in the jungle?

pages.x: Who are you?
I'm a jungle forester. Names mean little in this part of the world.

o: How do I get into the Kharazi Jungle?

pages.x: Have you seen any natives in the jungle?
Well, I've heard some funny sounds and I think I've seen a native... but I'm not sure. They generally don't like to be seen I guess.
But I found an item that you might be interested in. You swing it above your head and it makes a strange sound, it seems to attract their attention.

o: Can I have the item please?
How do I get into the jungle?

pages.x: Can I have the item please?
Well, I wish I could give it to you. However, I have grown fond of it. And it may help me in case I get lost in the jungle.

o: Will you trade something for it?

pages.x: Will you trade something for it?
Well, if you have something interesting, let me have a look at it and I'll offer you something in return. OK, I have to go now, but it's been nice talking with you.

conversations.section: Talk to / Starting room

pages.x: Hail, Player. Need something?

o: What can you tell me about this place?
Do I have any rewards to claim?

pages.x: What can you tell me about this place?
Who are you?
A friend.
Okay, what are you doing here, friend?
I'm here to help out.
With what?
Well, let's say you find yourself in need of adventuring kit, and you've a heavy pile of rusty coins weighing you down. I can help you with both of those problems. Savvy?
Ah, so you're a trader.
Keep it down, you fool!
Yes, I'm a trader. But I'm not supposed to be trading here.
If you want my goods, you'll learn not to talk about me.
Right, got you.
Is there anything else you can do for me?
Well, there's the job I'm supposed to be doing down here.
Which is?
Say you chance upon an object you know little about. Show it to me, and I'll tell you what it's used for.
That's good to know.
I can also offer hints about the behaviour of powerful opponents you might meet in the area. I've spent a long time down here, observing them.
I'll be sure to come back if I find a particularly strong opponent, then.
You'd be wise to, Player.
How do you know my name?
Nothing gets in or out of Daemonheim without me knowing about it.
Fair enough. Back to my other questions.
I'm here to trade.

o: What great foes await me in this area?
Can I change my starting items?
Can I access my bound and stored items?

pages.x: What great foes await me in this area?
There are a number of terrible foes known to lurk at this depth of Daemonheim. I have seen one such foe lurking about this floor.
Can I change my starting items?

o: I would like to receive coins.
I would like to receive feathers, rune essence and antipoison.
I don't want to change anything.

pages.x: Very well. Is there anything else you need?
Can I access my bound and stored items?
Which one?
Nevermind.
I'll be here.

conversations.section: In Tai Bwo Wannai, after Jungle Potion

pages.x: Hello there...thanks for helping out Trufitus commune with the gods Bwana. We've been able to return to the village thanks to your help.

o: Is there anything interesting to do here?
I've been doing some work around the village.

pages.x: What do you do here?
Not much really... I run a local shop which earns me a few trading sticks, but that's about it. I keep myself to myself really.

o: I want to ask another question.}}

pages.x: What are trading sticks?
They're the local currency Bwana, it's used in Tai Bwo Wannai, there's usually some odd jobs that need doing around the village which you could do to earn some trading sticks.
Or, if you have something which the local villagers might like, you could sell it to me and I'll pay you for it in trading sticks.

o: What sort of things do the local villagers like?
I want to ask another question.

pages.x: What sort of things do the local villagers like?
Gnome cocktails! It's amazing but we all just love them! Luckily I've managed to get stocks of the gnome made cocktails and I supply those to my favourite customers.
However, many of the customers really like the cocktails
made by the adventurers passing through this way. If you ever happen to have any, bring them my way! I'll give you a good deal on it that's for sure!
How did the villagers ever get to try any gnome cocktails?
I think it was that gnome pilot who crashed his glider, perhaps he had a little mini-bar on board?
Come to think about it, you'd expect the little guy to get his stuff together and move on out of here wouldn't you? He must love the jungle to have stayed here so long!
Ok, thanks.
You run a shop?
Yes, it's the Tai Bwo cooperative... catchy name huh! We sell a few local village trinkets and tools.
Also, there are a few items that we're actually looking to stock for the locals' sake.
If you happen across any of them please bring them to me, I'll pay a good price for them. I'm sure you'll find the prices very reasonable.

o: Can I take a look at what you have to sell?
Why do you only take one sort of Gnome cocktail?
I want to ask another question.

pages.x: Can I take a look at what you have to sell?
Sure you can...which shop would you like to see? The Cooperative or Drinks store?
None thanks...
Why do you only take one sort of Gnome cocktail?
It's funny that actually. I've managed to get a good deal with the pilot of that gnome glider. He can supply me directly now.
However, it's really interesting that the local villagers really like the gnome cocktails made by the adventurers passing through this way.
Why, what's the difference?

I think it may just be that they're made fresher, or there is a slight twist in the flavour of the drink, you know, a little more of this, a little less of that, it all adds up and makes for an interesting tipple!
I want to ask another question.
Sure, what do you want to ask?
Ok, thanks.
Is there anything interesting to do here?
Ok, thanks.

conversations.section: Before Ghosts Ahoy

pages.x: Hello there!
Greetings, traveller. Welcome to 'The Green Ghost' Tavern. What can I do you for?

o: What happened to the folk of this town?
Do you have any jobs I can do?

pages.x: Can I buy a beer?
Sorry, but our pumps dried up over half a century ago. We of this village do not have much of a thirst these days.
Can I hear some gossip?
I suppose, as long as you keep it to yourself...
You see Gravingas out there in the marketplace? He speaks for the silent majority of Port Phasmatys, for those of us who would prefer to pass over into the next world.
But old Gravingas is far too obvious in his methods.
Now Velorina, she's a ghost of a different colour altogether. If you feel like helping our cause at all, go speak to Velorina.
What happened to the folk of this town?
That's a long story, my friend, but you look like you have the time...
Do you know why ghosts exist?
Yes, that is normally the case. But here in Port Phasmatys, we of this town once chose freely to become ghosts!
Why on earth would you do such a thing?
It is a long story. Many years ago, this was a thriving port, a trading centre to the eastern lands.
We became rich on the profits made from the traders that came across the eastern seas.
We were very happy... until Lord Drakan noticed us.
He sent unholy creatures to demand that a blood-tithe be paid to the Lord Vampyre, as is required from all in the domain of Morytania.
We had no choice but to agree to his demands.
As the years went by, our numbers dwindled and many spoke of abandoning the town for safer lands. Then, Necrovarus came to us.
He came from the eastern lands, but of more than that, little is known. Some say he was once a mage, some say a priest.
Either way, he was in possession of knowledge totally unknown to even the most learned among us.
Necrovarus told us that he had been brought by a vision he'd had of an underground source of power.
He inspired us to delve beneath the town, promising us the power to repel the vampyres.
Deep underneath Phasmatys, we found a pool of green slime that Necrovarus called ectoplasm.
He showed us how to build the Ectofuntus, which would turn the ectoplasm into the power he had promised us.
Indeed, this Ectopower did repel the vampyres; they would not enter Phasmatys once the Ectofuntus began working.
But little did we know that we had exchanged one evil for yet another - Ectopower.
Little by little, we began to lose any desire for food or water, and our desire for the Ectopower grew until it dominated our thoughts entirely.
Our bodies shrivelled and, one by one, we died.
The Ectofuntus and the power it emanates keeps us here as ghosts - some, like myself, content to remain in this world; some becoming tortured souls who we do not allow to pass our gates.
We would be able to pass over into the next world but Necrovarus has used his power to create a psychic barrier, preventing us.
We must remain here for all eternity, even unto the very end of the world.
Do you have any jobs I can do?
Nothing, thanks.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hmm? Oh, hello, surface-dweller!

o: Can you tell me about the history of the city?

pages.x: What are you doing?
I'm writing the definitive history of Dorgesh-Kaan!
Actually, I wonder if you could help me...
What is this building?
This is the Dorgeshuun Council chamber!
Whenever a decision needs to be made, the seven members of the Dorgeshuun Council meet here.
The last meeting was when they decided to open up the city to surface-dwellers.
In between meetings, I work here writing up the minutes of the meetings and working on the definitive history of Dorgesh-Kaan.
Can you tell me about the history of the city?
Of course! I've gone through all of my predecessors' notes and compiled the definitive history of the Dorgeshuun! What would you like to hear about?
Can you tell me about the founding of Dorgesh-Kaan?
Of course! *Ahem*
The war lasted for thousands of years, and millions of goblins died. Eventually, the evil god sent the Dorgeshuun tribe to fight a battle that they could not win.
But General Bloodfist of the Dorgeshuun refused to fight in this battle. Instead, he commanded the Dorgeshuun army to march down into a fissure in the ground.
General Bloodfist stood at the mouth of the fissure and defied the might of the evil god.
The evil god smote him with a mighty blast that shook the earth, but that blast also closed the fissure, sealing the Dorgeshuun away from the reach of the gods.
Lieutenant Strongaxe, now the leader of the Dorgeshuun, led the tribe deeper into the caves.
They found this cavern, and here they founded Dorgesh-Kaan, city of the Dorgeshuun.
Can you tell me about the Dorgeshuun civil war?
Certainly! *Ahem*
At first, Dorgesh-Kaan was ruled over by generals, just as the tribe had been when it was on the surface. Each general succeeded the last by defeating him in combat.
The generals were advised by a council of elders, but the Dorgeshuun were no longer an army, and many of the people felt that the Council should have authority.
The people voted to become a republic, but General Bonehelm refused to give up power, and so the Dorgeshuun Civil War began.
The republican faction was larger, but the military faction contained most of the trained warriors and controlled the magical equipment that the tribe had brought from the surface.
General Bonehelm was driven from the city, but dug his own base out of the caves nearby.
General Bonehelm's army attacked the city using archers mounted on giant frogs. There was a bloody battle, and General Bonehelm was driven back again into his base.
But General Bonehelm's mining had weakened the stone around his base, and the retreating army's footsteps caused the roof to collapse, crushing his army.
That was the last time one Dorgeshuun has raised arms against another. Since then, the city has been ruled peacefully by an elected council.
Can you tell me about recent years?
Ah, this is where you come in! *Ahem*
In the twenty-ninth century since the founding of the city, one of the miners broke through a wall into the cellar of a surface dwelling.
The miners blocked up the tunnel and went back into their mines.
Despite reservations from many citizens, the Council eventually voted 4-3 to open Dorgesh-Kaan to surface-dwellers.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Ahhh, hello there, Player.

o: Can you tell me a bit about skillcapes?
May I buy a Skillcape of Strength, please?
I've noticed there are a couple of versions of each skillcape.

pages.x: Can you tell me a bit about skillcapes?
Sure. You can buy a skillcape when you reach level 99 in a skill.
Apart from boosting your statistics in that skill, they can also be used to perform some pretty amazing emotes! Is there anything else you would like to know?
Yes! We, the skill masters, have crafted new versions of all skillcapes! We felt like it was time for a change.

o: Yes, I would like to wear the [new/old] version of the skillcape.

pages.x: Would you like to wear the [old/newer] model for just this cape, or for the Quest Cape and all of the skillcapes you own?

o: I would just like to change the Strength skillcape.
I would like to change all my skillcapes.

pages.x: No problem, you will now use the [older/newer] model for your Strength skillcape.
No problem, you will now use the [older/newer] model for all of your skillcapes!
Great! I'm glad you're still enjoying the [old/new] version!
What can I do here?
Ahh, the shot put is a great test of strength and can be quite rewarding.
Mind you do it properly, though, you might want to dust your hands with some powdery substance first. It'll give better grip.
I'll remember that. What should I use?
I personally prefer ground ashes, it makes a nice fine powder and gives some really good grip.
Okay, what else?
Basically you'll need to go in there, make sure you've got nothing cluttering up your hands, pick up a shot and throw it.
Depending upon your technique, you can get quite long throws.
What was your best?
Ahh, that would be telling.
That's a big axe!
Yes, indeed, it is. Have to be mighty strong to wield it too.
But you don't look that strong!
Maybe, maybe not, but I still had to beat a Barbarian to get it. Mind you, usually they don't part with them. This was an unusual circumstance.
Oh?
I bet him he couldn't catch a squirrel whilst still holding his axe but that I could... and that if I won I'd get his axe.
What happened?
He went running after the squirrel... nearly caught it too...
it shot up a tree and he tried to climb up it, only got a bit tangled up with his axe cause he couldn't hang on to it at the same time and... he fell out of the tree.
Then it was my turn....
I simply went and chopped the tree down with this big old axe, still holding it. The squirrel was so petrified it simply jumped straight out of the tree onto me.
I won the axe and let the poor creature go!
I sense a moral in there somewhere.
Aye indeed. Brawn isn't all you need to wield a big axe, brains are required too!

conversations.section: Bandosian

pages.x: Glory to Bandos! What do you want?
I have some questions about you.
What?
Who are you?
I'm Davosi, the head diviner of the Bandosians.
I use divination to locate the power that will smash those who oppose Bandos.
I am wise, but I still have to practice constantly, so that I can serve our great Big High War God.
Where are you from?
I am from the Wilderness. I was a bandit before Bandos noticed my talent.
My men and I roamed the Wilderness, killing the weaklings who'd wandered too far, helping ourselves to the spoils.
Bandos honoured us by asking us to join his army. He saw greatness in me, and chose me to be his head diviner.
I will follow Bandos until the bitter end.
Why do you follow Bandos?
He's the biggest of the gods, and the strongest too. He must know what he's doing if he has drafted me into battle.
Bandos wants a world where only the strongest survive. This allows us all to discover our true potential.
The wise can use our skills to improve warfare and stomp on the weak.
Can I ask something else?
I have some questions about divination.
Ask and I shall answer.
What is it?
Divination is about retrieving the essence from wisps that float out of the ground. You may have noticed them around the world.
From wisps you get energy, from energy you get things like portents, signs and divine locations. They make me at least two or three times better in battle.
We're using the energy to make something bigger: a weapon to destroy Armadyl for the glory of Bandos. We call it the Scarecrow.
Why are you using it?
I'd rather not say to just anyone.
Where did it come from?
Some people say it's down to Guthix.
I say that gives too much credit to Guthix. He was stupid to stop Bandos from being in the world.
I say it's the planet leaking out. The Battle of Lumbridge tore open the world, and now it's bleeding.
Now we're using that lifeblood to help Bandos become ruler of the gods.
Can I ask something else?
I have some questions about that big siege weapon.
I'm not telling you about the Scarecrow. Not until you've shown you're worthy.
That's all I have to say.
Get divining. Victory for Bandos!

conversations.section: Deathbeard's Demise / When talked to during the event

pages.x: Avast, me matey! Welcome to me shipwreck!
That's a sorry looking ship...
Aye, she's stayin' afloat for now. But I be needin' some help gettin' her back on her sea legs.
What is it you need?
Doubloons! But not any ol' coin. These ones be dead, just like me. Get 'em from everyday frolicks, and bring 'em back to me.
I'm on it!

o: What do you need all these doubloons for?
How long will you be around for?

pages.x: So... you're dead?
You can't just go around asking people if they're dead, laddy/lass.
Sorry. But it's not every day you meet a dead pirate captain.
Aye, tha' be true. I did indeed perish along with the rest of me crew. Somethin' clung to me soul, though. Somethin' dark that let me keep on goin'.
I can feel th' same curse has be laid upon them, as well.
What do you need all these doubloons for?
I plan to mend me ship, sail again to whar we perished to collect me crew 'n take on whatever it was that decided to cross us.
What makes you think you'll win this time?
Death may seem horrific, but it has its... benefits.
What happened to your ship?
She's seen better days, that's for sure. The sea... she hasn'a been herself of late - and no one know's 'er like me.
Angry, she's been gettin', with more 'n more of what be stayin' deep risin' to th' top.
You had a run in with something?
It happened so quickly I couldn't say fer sure. One moment we're sailin' through a serene ocean.
Next, we're thrown from it entirely, spit shine into th' air, me ship in ruins. I woke up on th' shore in this state, 'n not a crew member in sight.
How long will you be around for?
Not forever. This curse 'o undeath has given me a new perspective on... life?
I suppose that makes sense...
'O course it does! Now get ta doubloon huntin'!

o: You appear to be changing your appearance...

pages.x: You appear to be changing your appearance...
Aye - I'm still tryin' ta get used ta me new deathly powers. Whatever it be, it lets me change into a more ghastly version o' myself.
I suppose that could come in handy.
I be treatin' it as a gift. I'll find a use fer it somehow.
AAARGH!
Ye know, not all us pirates feel that's the best way to express ourselves...
Oh... I didn't mean to cause offence.
Arghh, they never do.

conversations.section: First time dialogue

pages.x: What's a gnome doing here?
I'm an investigator. I'm watching the implings.
Why would you want to do that?
My client has asked me to find out where certain missing items have been going.
Who is this client?
I'm not at liberty to discuss that. Investigator-client confidentiality don't you know.

o: What do you want to ask?
Can I catch these implings then?
I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

pages.x: Where is this place?
I've heard it called Puro-Puro. It seems to be the home plane of the implings. I don't think these creatures have a name for it.
As you can see there isn't a lot else here other than wheat.
How did you get here?
The same way you did, I suspect. Through a portal in a wheat field. I followed one back.
I haven't noticed them do that.
That's why I'm the investigator and you're the adventurer.

o: What do you want to ask?
Can I catch these implings then?
I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.

pages.x: So, what are these implings?
That's a very interesting question. My best guess is that they are relatives to imps, which is why there are imps here as well.
Implings do appear to like collecting objects and, as my clients have noted, have no concept of ownership. However, I do not sense any malicious intent.
It is my observation that they collect things that other creatures want, rather than they want them themselves. It seems to provide them with sustenance.
So they feed off our desire for things?
Possibly.
Either way, it seems that they almost exclusively collect things that people want, except their younglings who I infer haven't learnt the best things to collect yet.
So the more experienced implings have the more desirable items?
That is my observation. Yes.

o: What do you want to ask?
Can I catch these implings then?
I've heard I may find dragon equipment in Puro-Puro.
