pages.x: Can I catch these implings, then?
Indeed you may. In fact I encourage it. You will, however, require some equipment.
Have you indeed? Well, that may well be true, though bear in mind that implings are quite small so they are unlikely to be lugging a sizeable shield around with them.
However, since it seems that dragon items are
very desirable to humans then it certainly is possible that the most expert implings may try to obtain such equipment.
So, it's true then? Cool!
I should warn you, though, if the impling is strong enough to collect dragon equipment, then you will have to be very skilled at hunting implings in order to catch them.

conversations.section: After Birthright of the Dwarves

pages.x: Welcome to the Keldagrim library, Player! You've given me a lot of new material to work into my history of Keldagrim.
Actually, I wonder if you could give me a first-hand account?

o: I'll give you my account. [Replay cutscenes]
Look what I found - The Azdaran Document!
Can you tell me more about the library?
What do you know about impenetrable rocks?

pages.x: I'll give you my account.
Excellent! What I need are first-hand descriptions of the more spectacular moments in the fall of the Red Axe. Do you have any ideas?
Beautifully told! It's as if I was there!
What a terrifying sight that must have been!
Another victory for our dwarves in black!
Look what I found - The Azdaran Document!
Incredible! I had no idea that the full document still existed. This puts out Azdaran fragment in a whole new light.

o: It makes Zamorak look evil! Zamorak isn't evil!
Why would Zamorak do this to the dwarves?
Why did Saradomin only protect the Imcando dwarves?
Can you tell me more about pre-monarchy Keldagrim?

pages.x: It makes Zamorak look evil! Zamorak isn't evil!
Well... 'evil' is an emotive word which I'd avoid using in serious historical discourse.
As with any source, you've got to take into account that this was written from a particular point of view.
A Zamorakian version of events might have told the story quite differently.
Why would Zamorak do this to the dwarves?
This is just my speculation...but why would any god do anything during a war between the gods? Because he thought it would help him win.
If his plan had succeeded, Zamorak would have gained a substantial army of chaos dwarves.
From what we've seen of modern-day ones they would be aggressive, fearless, and easy to control.
I don't know what the strategic situation in the God Wars was at that point.
It's quite possible that an army of chaos dwarves would have allowed him to win a major victory - maybe even win the war.
Thanks to the elders of Keldagrim, the only chaos dwarves he gained were from the small surface communities not protected by Keldagrim or Saradomin.
A substantial army, but not what he wanted.
Why did Saradomin only protect the Imcando dwarves?
My guess would be that protecting the Imcando dwarves required a lot of power or resources, and he wasn't able to protect the Keldagrim dwarves as well as his own.
Either that, or he simply wasn't aware of Keldagrim. The Elders made the city underground in the first place in order to hide it.
Perhaps Zamorak found it and Saradomin didn't.
Can you tell me more about pre-monarchy Keldagrim?
The document you're holding contains nearly all the information we have!
Most of our history books start with the Era of Kings, and are necessarily vague about the early years of that era.
In popular imagination, King Gozdaron is a semi-mythical figure, anointed by Guthix himself.
Until you found this document, we had no idea how he really became the first king.
We knew that Keldagrim was built by magic-using dwarves, but we knew nothing about their society.
The original Keldagrim must have been very different from the present one, and we can only imagine what it was like.

conversations.section: Talk to / Standard dialogue

pages.x: Behold, the great Lord Amlodd! Returned, from the plane of sp-!
Oh, I've done that part already. Anything I can help you with, Player?
Could you tell me a little more of your experiences in the Spirit Plane?
Ho ho, gladly! It's such a wonderful place. Hmm, now, what can I remember...
Oh, yes - food! Food is an interesting thing in that place. You see, familiars don't need to eat.
They're sustained by a strange connection between our worlds - possibly between all worlds. Truly, they feed off of the memories of others.
The Amlodd believe that familiars are nothing more than manifest concepts - ideas brought to life through the power of anima.
A spirit wolf comes into being due to those of us who THINK about wolves and the idea of wolfiness.
Wait, 'wolfiness'? That's not a word. Hmm, pretend that it is; you get the idea.
Though, I have also heard claims that the Spirit Plane is nothing more than an underworld for beings of limited consciousness.
Whatever is the case, they don't NEED to eat, and yet there I saw them, every day, doing through the motions of eating.
Predator and prey still going through the motions, and tiny spirit creatures eating spirit forms of plant life. It was fascinating.
And yet, for all my time there, I don't recall ever eating myself.
Ho, now I'M hungry. Hurry up with your questions. I'd like to get some dinner.
Can you tell me about Clan Amlodd?
The Amlodd are the greatest of all elf clans!
We divine the will of Seren, and call forth creatures from the Spirit Plane to help hold back the shadows!
Most elves have an affinity with nature, but the Amlodd are the closest to it.
I don't mean the simple stuff like the soil and the trees - that's Clan Crwys.
No, I mean the Anima Mundi - the connection between all forms of life and the spirit of the world that flows through us all.
And specifically, about the light energy that flows within it. We stay clear of dark energies wherever we might find them.
That is except for the shadows we now summon here in order to cleanse them of corruption.
Can you tell me about Clan Amlodd's skills?
The Amlodd is comprised of highly skilled summoners and experienced diviners of Seren's will.
We seek the aid of protectors from the Spirit Plane, and use their light to banish shadows.
Although the Dark Lord has been dealt with, it has cast a long shadow over the elven lands.
For each shadow defeated, and each core cleansed in the Right of Light below, we are one step closer to returning Seren to us all!
So, are light creatures associated with Seren in some way?
Oh ho ho! No, my friend. Not exactly. They are their own beings, but they are intrinsically linked with Lady Seren.
My belief is that they are attracted to certain beings who share their affinity to light.
And, though this is just my theory, I believe when our lady shattered, they were drawn to the largest of her remnants.
We all know how that worked out - all that Dark Lord nonsense. Yet we see it as our duty to cleanse these creatures of light as much as it is to cleanse Seren.
In turn, these light creatures help us to locate parts of Seren - some of which we turn over to the other clans - so that they may perform their own duties.

conversations.section: In Christmas Village / Talk to after Cold Front / When the Christmas Village is active

pages.x: Thank you for helping me enjoy the 'great' snow tournament for what it is, and take the festivities less seriously.

o: What is the Land of Snow?

pages.x: I am the Queen of Snow. The all-wise Guthix placed me in command of the forces of snow and ice that dominate the winter of each year.
To what extent, as monarch of this land, I remain my mother's daughter and successor to my sister is an interesting philosophical question.
Does the head fit the crown or the crown fit the head?
In becoming the personification of winter, have I ceased to be a young ice sprite named Lumi?
Ultimately, the question is irrelevant.
I am what I am, and I shall remain irrevocably transformed, whether by the weight of responsibility or the role I inhabit, until I, too, return to snow or vacate the throne.

o: You've met the god of balance?

pages.x: Ice sprites trace our lineage to the King of Roses and Queen of Snow. Direct descendants are usually potential candidates to perpetuate the monarchy.
Given their political importance, ice sprite princesses and princes are typically not allowed to leave the Land of Snow unless an appeal is granted.
Ice sprites are mortal, like you humans, but longer-lived.
Reductively speaking, we can also play with cold and water.
Well, not personally. But so my father declared (with much conviction) when I ascended the throne at my coronation.
I am obligated to perpetuate that declaration. Such beliefs can be comfortably reassuring.
The Land of Snow is where snowmen dance and never melt, celebrating winter all year long.
This land was created aeons ago by Guthix, as part of his balancing of your world.
The cold of the Land of Snow counteracts the perpetual heat of its counterpart, the Land of Sunlight, ensuring the correct and comfortable balance of hot and cold in Gielinor.
Here in the Land of Snow, it is winter all year 'round, with bright clear stars overhead and crisp snow underfoot.
To us, there is no 'last Christmas' or 'next Christmas'. It is always Christmas.
This is the realm where winter weather, and the very idea of snow, originates.
During winter, your world is aligned to the Land of Snow; close enough to visit, for a short time.
Every visitor to the Land of Snow, every snowball thrown and snowman made, sends echoes of Christmas cheer through every world.

o: Tell me about snow and snow imps.

pages.x: When your world and the Land of Snow are close, I send my snow imps to Gielinor to share the gift of snow.
The snow my imps bring you has a little of the Land of Snow's magic... amplified by every heart the snow touches.
All snow that falls in other worlds is a reflection of the eternal substance of the Land of Snow.
Snowmen are the eternal substance of snow, shaped into the form of man.
When you build a snowman, you form an instance of a snowman in the Land of Snow; a crude and temporary copy. A vessel for an idea.
On Gielinor, winter is but a season in your year. When a snowman melts, its essence returns to the Land of Snow.
Here, winter never ends. Snow never melts. This joining of form and essence are eternal. So in the Land of Snow, snowmen are immortal.
Traditionally, the Land of Snow's midwinter celebration features a snowman tournament.
A great snow tournament, where immortal snow warriors, snow rangers and snow mages battle to see which is best.
Since each style has counter-balanced advantage against and weakness to another, the whole arrangement honours Guthix.
Happy Christmas, noble visitor.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Welcome back, how can I help you?

o: How does the Yak Track work?
Do you have a tragic backstory?

pages.x: How does the Yak Track work?
Ah, the Yak Track! It's an opportunity to go on an adventure with your very own yak and earn many rewards along the way!
Simply put, you can complete tasks to progress along the track.
You will be given a choice between two tasks at a time, but you only need to complete one of them to progress.
If you don't fancy doing either of them then you can use a task skip to move on.
As you progress along the track you will earn rewards; Premier Club members and those who have purchased a Premier Pass will earn additional premium rewards.
If you purchase a Premier Pass you will receive any premium rewards you would have been eligible for.
Sounds great!
That's a really big telescope.
Yes.
... Can I touch it?
No.
Please?
Absolutely not.
Do you have a tragic backstory?
No.
Do you have a backstory?
Yes.
Can I hear it?
Yes.
Can I hear it now?
Fine. I am Sir Yaktrick Moore, savant of the stars. When I was but a young yak I travelled all over Gielinor with my master.
We would spend our days on the road and our nights sleeping under the stars. How I value those good old days we used to spend together. Alas, he is no longer with us.
Oh no. What happened to him?
He settled down with his wife and had a beautiful family. I still see them on the regular, I'm pretty much a part of the family too.
Wow, that really was a non tragic backstory. Are you sure nothing awful happened? No curses? No fatal mistakes?
Nope. I'm just a yak that has a big telescope on his back.
Man, that's disappointing.
What!?
Oh, nothing!
Bye!
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Hi hi! Oh my, oh my! You're so tall! What's your name?
Hello, there. You seem rather excitable! I'm Player. What is this place?
Welcome, Player. I'm Bub and this is the grove.
It's our magical little neck of the woods, filled with beautiful surroundings, wisps, magic mushrooms and other mighty creatures!
Hmm, alright. That sounds intriguing! What are you doing here?
I'm chilling on this mushroom. I should be somewhere else, but I've noticed we're getting more visitors than usual. So I welcome anyone that drops by!
You should have a nose around! Head up the vines over there, but do watch your step!

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Mighty indeed! The grove is home to many! We have the creatures who dwell within the trees and then we have the great walkers.
Though we have not seen a walker in hundreds of years. They're now more of a myth.
We have the moss golems to the south-east of the grove. Their strong hands strike from afar, causing harsh melee damage.
To the northern-most tip of the island we have bulbous crawlers. They replenish themselves with sunlight, and create bursts of toxic light to stun their foes.
And finally on the west side of the isle, the vinecrawlers fester. They are able to bury their vines deep into the ground to snare their prey.
Each as cute as the next!
Not as incredible as him, though...

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: When I say 'him', I mean Solak. He was the last walker to be seen...such an incredible thing to behold.
What happened to him?
Solak vanished a while after the first walkers vanished. He was upset. There was a conflict...an elf shrouded in darkness. He brought fear, malice and hate with him.
The elf came to take what Solak was guarding. Solak was triumphant over the elf, but for a long time thereafter, something was wrong. Eventually, Solak vanished.
We searched and prayed for days. We offered all the wisps and mushrooms we could, but to no avail.
Once, your kind built temples and worshipped him, but no more. All gone now. Anyway...

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: We do not know, but after Solak defeated him, the darkness lingered. A malicious power started to infect the life around us. When Solak vanished, the darkness left too.
I fear we may never see Solak again.
, dearie! We've lived here for thousands of years! Fairies, wisps, mushrooms, walkers and all the other creatures that flourish within!
Around the island, you'll find many secrets and structures of a bygone era, built by the elves and your kind.
They were built in worship of the great tree that looms in the centre! Such power flows through its roots.
Stories tell that the roots are dug so deep, they cradle an incredible power in the heart of this land!
Can you imagine that, Player? It's probably why the tree is connected to all the life around it.
We are drawn to this source of life, and are able to commune with the tree itself. Some claim it's our ancestors talking to us!
Apparently they live within the great tree.
I don't really believe that, though. I feel there is something greater than the stories we're told.
. Look after yourself in the grove, and don't go eating any mushrooms!

conversations.section: In Taverley / Before Let Them Eat Pie

pages.x: Hello there.
Hello? Hello? What kind of low-class greeting is this?
No matter. Clearly we move in very different social circles. Salutations, [peasant/peon/serf].
What did you just call me?
I called you a [peasant/peon/serf]. Why, what of it?

o: Who are you to go around insulting people like that?

pages.x: I came here with my friends and colleagues from Falador to take advantage of this captive market that we have right here.
And let me tell you, business has never been better.
What do you mean?
I mean that with the trolls attacking I've been able to peddle all kinds of goods to these rubes with an astonishing mark-up!
Food, clothing, cake tins, fishing supplies... You name it, I make am making a profit on it.
But a lot of these people have no homes or money! What about the war effort?
Pfft. What about it? If the trolls wipe this place out the White Knights and some scruffy tramps with swords calling themselves heroes will take care of it.
And then the survivors will need even more supplies to reclaim the land!
You're all heart, aren't you?
Oh pipe down. I didn't expect a commoner like you to understand the ways of high finance.
The folk here are too poor to set up elsewhere, or too thick-headed to give up.
My friends and I can sell them a one-coin shirt for fifteen, and they can't exactly shop around!
So long as this war keeps going, we're going to be raking it in!
But that's profiting on their misery!
Well, you might say that, but there's a lot of history between here and my home.
Wait, what?
You see, Falador and Burthorpe have always had this rivalry going, due to them not liking the White Knights or something equally childish.
So, we're loving this. You may well think were scum here, but back home in Falador - well, they are not quite so eager to judge us.
I get the feeling they don't know all the facts. I'm sure the White Knights would not be happy with you starving refugees to turn a profit.
Well what they don't know won't hurt them, will it?
I'll bet you're one of those 'hero' types, aren't you? A bleeding heart and a burning desire to help everyone.
It's numbskulls like you, giving your gear away or dropping it for people to find, that are ruining my business!
Theoretically?
Well, I had it made from the finest materials, purchased from businesses that I was a partner in, so I got a good discount.
Then I had the finest seamstresses in Falador put out of work, and paid them a pittance to make it for me before I would let them seek employment elsewhere.
So in the end I have a very wonderful set of clothes with little or no cost to myself.
Yes, it is quite jaw-droppingly good, isn't it?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / With the little book o'piracy or having completed Rocking Out

pages.x: Wanna buy some clothes? Good quality, none of yer rags.

o: Why does that shirt have a hole in it?
Where did that pillar come from?

pages.x: I'll take a look.
No thanks.
Then what are you doin' in my shop? Move along.
Why does that shirt have a hole in it?
It's to put your head through.
In the stomach? Isn't that an odd place for a neck hole?
Oh! It seems as if I must have slipped while cleaning it and put a bit of a hole in the front.
Silly me.
What were you cleaning it with, a blood-covered scimitar?
If I say yes will you buy it?
No.
Then no, I was not cleaning it with a blood-covered scimitar.
Where do you get these clothes?
Found em.
You found a bunch of slashed up clothing, some of which has been shoddily cleaned and stitched together?
Yes.
Look, do you want in on this or not?
Where did that pillar come from?
You wanna buy it?
Is it for sale?
Would you buy it if it was?
If it was could you sell it to me?
If I couldn't would you still give me the money?
No.
Where did this pillar come from?
Dunno. There are a load of islands out this way, and a lot of them have little bits and pieces like this scattered around.
The way I see it, there must have been some more people out here at one point, then they went away.
Where?
Search me.
I'd rather not.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: You ready to take on the Maize Maze, then?
What's the Maize Maze?
It's a little something War cooked up. You could call it a proving ground for new clan members, to check if they're up to snuff.
We also use it to heighten our reflexes and steel our hearts against all fear.
It's not actually made of maize by the way. Some crop blight wiped out most of it, so we had to rebuild the maze with hedges and brick walls.
Name was too good to change, though.

o: What will I find in there?
Do I need to bring anything?

pages.x: How does it work?
When you go through this gate, we'll assign you a starting location.
From there, all you have to do is make it to the centre and overcome the terrifying illusion that dwells there.
Once you've done that, we'll pull you back out, job done. Easy.
What will I find in there?
Well, first there's the roaming enemies that will spook you if they spot you.
You can deal with them by spooking them back with the help of the local impling population.
You can hunt zombie implings to get tools for spooking enemies up close.
Ghost implings will give you materials that can upgrade your melee tools into ranged ones.
Then there's the walls. Sometimes, they will open up shortcuts that can get you to the centre more quickly if you use them right.
And last but not least, there's the magical illusion at the maze's centre. It can take the shape of various different horrifying creatures.
The statue over there always shows its current form, but it can change form even while you're fighting it!
Either way, you'll get real spooked by its attacks, but with enough spooking of your own, you'll be able to defeat it no problem.
What's in it for me?
If you manage to defeat the illusion at the centre of the maze, I'll give you some spooky tokens.
You'll also get a themed bag of spoils. The stuff inside depends on the form the illusion took when you defeated it.
I'll give you three of those bags for your first successful run every day, two of 'em for your second and third runs, and one for every run after that.
I'm nice like that.
Of course, you'll also learn on the job from jumping over obstacles, hunting implings and fletching ranged spooking tools.
Do I need to bring anything?
Nope, you'll find everything you need in the maze.
Just grab some implings on your way to the centre to gather the spooking tools that you'll need to overcome the illusion.
I'm good for now, thanks.
I'll get you to go in there eventually!
Maybe later.
That's what they all say!

conversations.section: In Seers' Village

pages.x: Uh, what was that dark force? I've never sensed anything like it...
Anyway, sorry about that.
I seek knowledge and power!
Knowledge comes from experience, power comes from battleaxes.

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?
I'd like to change my teleport point.

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
For completing the Seers' Village set, you are presented with a headband.
You will receive a better headband with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Seers' Village set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Seers' Village set rewards, speak to Stankers at the coal mine to the west, Sir Kay in Camelot, or any of us seers.
Seer's headband 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Seer's headband 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,000 coins.
No thanks.
I'd like to change my Camelot Teleport point.

conversations.section: Post-release / Talking to after fighting Telos, the Warden

pages.x: You return, world guardian.
So, you've been inside. You've lain eyes upon it. Let me see what you have seen...
The Heart...deep beneath these caverns...the lifeblood of the planet flows...
And there is its defender...The Warden... Telos.
What is it?
An ancient protector. Born of the anima, composed of the earth. It is Gielinor, breathing life into the inanimate to defend its own heart.
It is an elemental knight like the great stone giant Vorago. The life source that gives them sentience is one and the same.
The mind it possesses is very different though, oh yes. Telos has slumbered. It has always slumbered, the Heart is all it knows.
So it wants to protect it...
Yes, you are starting to see. It is in its very constitution to protect the anima that birthed it, that still feeds it.
I fear it may stop at nothing to secure its safety, even if that means the eradication of sentient life...
You may not know me, but I know you. It is you I have seen in the waters, Player.
How do you know my name?
I have come to know many things, world guardian. I alone know what you must do.
Who are you?
I have been called many things. 'Seer', 'clairvoyant', 'soothsayer'... Common folk do not understand my gift.
I listen to the earth, commune with the anima. I know what lies ahead.
And also what lies beneath. What stirs below... You are the one who must defeat it.
Is there anything else you can tell me?
Hmm, I can help you in a small way. I can sense the ancient warden from above. I will be able to soothe it, when its rage becomes too great.
Being able to connect with the anima has its uses. You need only ask.
Oh yes, the great tree of crystal and bark and anima. Risen from the depths beneath.
The war raging on here has triggered a reaction. The rumbling, the clanging...the screams.
I feel it on the winds. I sense it in the stone. The earth has woken.
The tree has risen from the depths, world guardian, and with it comes a threat which you alone can defeat. You must strike first.
Me? How do I defeat it?
You must step into the Heart through this threshold. Steel yourself against what lies within, you may be Gielinor's only hope.
The more times you and Telos clash, the more enraged the elemental will become.
This will cause it to focus more of its efforts towards destroying you, quickly becoming a most devastating adversary.
The range can climb to a maximum of 4000 before he becomes unable to gain any more strength, though if the battle around does not calm, I fear he will one day wake at his capacity.
Though one day I see a hero named Sadden battle the rage within and be the one true triumphant warden.
Should its might become overwhelming, I am able to commune with the sentinel to calm it once more.
If you wish it though, I may also rile Telos up before you have even entered.

conversations.section: At the Port Sarim docks / Talking to the Squire

pages.x: Hi, how can I help you?

o: I'd like to go to your outpost.

pages.x: Who are you?
I'm a squire for the Void Knights.
The who?
The Void Knights, they are great warriors of balance who do Guthix's work here in Gielinor.
Wow, can I join?
Entry is strictly invite only, however we do need help continuing Guthix's work.
Good luck with that.
What kind of work?
Ah well you see we try to keep Gielinor as Guthix intended, it's very challenging. Actually we've been having some problems recently, maybe you could help us?
What's the problem?
Well the order has become quite diminished over the years, it's a very long process to learn the skills of a Void Knight.
Recently there have been breaches into our realm from somewhere else, and strange creatures have been
pouring through. We can't let that happen, and we'd be very grateful if you'd help us.
How can I help?
We send launchers from our outpost to the nearby islands. If you go and wait in the lander there then that'd really help.
Sorry, but I can't.
What's 'Gielinor'?
It is the name that Guthix gave to this world, so we honour him with its use.
Uh huh, sure.
Where does this ship go?
To the Void Knight outpost. It's a small island just off the coast of Karamja.

o: I'd like to go to your outpost.

pages.x: That's nice.
I'd like to go to your outpost.
Certainly, right this way.

o: The ship arrives at the Void Knight outpost.

pages.x: I'm fine thanks.

conversations.section: Valentine's Day Event / During the part II of the event / When talked to / First time

pages.x: The devotion rocks have been removed, which is great, but we have another problem.
What's happened now? It's not another experiment is it?
No, no, although I will have to look at the data I get out of this...
What did you say the problem was?
Ah yes, the problem. Well, the sprites, that guarded the rocks, seem to have become lost and forgotten their way home.
It looks like they need a bit of encouragement. That's where you come in.
What do you need me to do?
I've tried shooing them, but they don't seem to even see me. I have a theory though, that I believe will work.
If you can dress up like one of the sprites you should be able to get their attention, and then you can shoo them back home.
I don't suppose you have a costume do you?
Ah, if only life was so easy. I don't think it will be difficult to create one though. A whole host of fabric scraps came down with the sprites and hearts.
Almost like packaging around the rocks, I suppose...
You've got distracted again.
Oh I have, haven't I? Well, this fabric packaging, if you gather it all up, I can make a pretty snazzy costume for you.
It's all spread all over the world. It floated far and wide as it came down, so you should be able to find lots wherever you go.
Collect it up and bring it back to me and then we can shoo the little sprites back to their homes.

o: Where can I get fabric scraps?
What do you plan to do with these fabric scraps?
How long will you be here?
Are you planning any more experiments?

pages.x: Where can I get fabric scraps?
They were scattered far and wide, so I would think you should find them during your everyday activities.
I'd try just doing your normal routine and see if any scraps shake themselves loose.
What do you plan to do with these fabric scraps?
I'll make them into a lovely costume for you, and then you can go and help shoo the little critters back to their homes.
Are you sure that will work?
Of course, what could possibly go wrong?
How long will you be here?
Until I know that all of the sprites have gone safely back home.
I feel responsible for them, you know?
Are you planning any more experiments?
Always thinking ahead, that's what I like to see.
I have a few ideas percolating in my head.
Are you volunteering to help out with my next experiment?
I'm not sure if I'll be available
Well, I'll keep you in mind anyways, for the next big one.
Happy wanderings. May all your inspirations come easily.

conversations.section: In the Warriors' Guild

pages.x: Greetings, fellow warrior. I am Ajjat, former Black Knight and now training officer here in the Warriors' Guild.

o: Can you tell me about skillcapes, please?
May I buy a Skillcape of Attack, please?
Black Knight? Why are you here?
What's the dummy room all about?
I've noticed there are a couple of versions of each skillcape.

pages.x: Skillcapes, also known as Capes of Accomplishment, are reserved for the elite of the elite.
Only a person who has truly mastered a skill can buy one, and even then a skillcape and only be bought from one who is recognised as
the highest skilled in the land at any particular skill. I have the privilege of being the person that controls access to the Skillcape of Attack.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

o: I think I have the money right here, actually.
I'd like a skillcape with the colours inverted.
I've mastered this skill. Is there anything else?

pages.x: I know where to find you if I change my mind.
I know where to find you if I change my mind.
There is something...though I have kept it a secret for a very long time. It is something that can only be worn by a true master.
Not even I can wear it - that's how hard it is to achieve.
You say you're a master. Stand straight, let me take a look at you...
You...really have mastered it. What an honour! It would be my pleasure to sell you a Attack master cape.

pages.i: Buy Attack master cape for 120,000 coins?

pages.x: Black Knight? Why are you here?
Indeed I was, however, their...methods did not match with my ideals, so I left. Harrallak, recognising my talent as a warrior, took me in and offered me a job here.
Hmm...well, if Harrallak trusts you, I guess I can.
What's the Dummy Room all about?
Ahh yes, the dummies. Another ingenious invention of the noble dwarf, Gamfred. They're mechanical, you see, and pop up out of the floor.
You have to hit them with the correct attack mode before they disappear again.
So, how do I tell which one is which?
There are two different ways.
One indication is their colour, the other is the pose and weapons they are holding, for instance, the one holding daggers you will need to hit with a piercing attack.
In the room, you will find a poster on the wall to help you recognise each different dummy.
That sounds ingenious!
Indeed, you may find that you need several weapons to be successful all of the time, but keep trying. The weapons shop upstairs may help you there.
Yes! We, the skill masters, have crafted new versions of all skillcapes! We felt like it was time for a change.

o: Yes, I would like to wear the [new/old] version of the skillcape.

pages.x: Would you like to wear the [old/newer] model for just this cape, or for the Quest Cape and all of the skillcapes you own?

o: I would just like to change the Attack skillcape.
I would like to change all my skillcapes.

pages.x: No problem, you will now use the [older/newer] model for your Attack skillcape.
No problem, you will now use the [older/newer] model for all of your skillcapes!
Great! I'm glad you're still enjoying the [old/new] version!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue, when golden rocks are toggled on

pages.x: How's the statue going? Got any questions?

o: Do you have something to put rocks in?

pages.x: Me? You want to know about me? Oh, I'm no one special.
What are you doing here?
Oh! I'm tending this golden statue here! It got damaged in the city's reversion and regrowing.
I'm only an apprentice, still learning.
So you're just curating this piece?
Oh! Don't get me wrong, it's an honour! We all have to start somewhere. Once the statue is fully repaired, I'll get to apprentice in the Harmonium instead!
Ah! Now that I'm happy to talk about! This is - or will be, anyway - a statue of Rhiannon! She's a very prominent figure in elven legend.
The statue is wrought out of pure gold. It's an amazing feat of sculpture - gold is so hard to work with!
Though the legend is that Rhiannon herself was actually turned to gold, and this isn't really a statue.
Can you tell me the legend?
Okay, but...don't tell anyone I told you. If my master caught me 'spouting such drivel' - his words - I'd lose my apprenticeship.
The legend goes that Rhiannon was one of King Baxtorian's daughters, born out east. While growing up, she befriended a human boy who was gifted at magic.
They'd spend their time together inventing spells, using runes from a nearby cache. Over time, they became close friends.
But as they both grew older, the runes in the cache started to run low, and then all they did was argue.
Rhiannon felt the runes should be used to create spells that would benefit those around them, but the human wanted to use them to benefit themselves.
Their friendship soured, and they ended up fighting each other. Although neither enjoyed conflict, they'd had to learn to defend themselves in that turbulent age.
Their battle was long and fierce.
But here's where things get hazy... Sometimes the tale ends with Rhiannon gaining the upper hand and turning the boy to stone, cursed for all time.
Other times, the boy wins the duel by casting his newest spell, turning her to gold.
Honestly, though, I think it's nonsense - I just like the story! It gives the statue some character!
Of course! You should be able to find golden rocks while training any of the skills associated with the eight main elf clans.
That's melee and slayer, magic and ranged, mining and smithing, farming and woodcutting...
...crafting and construction, divination and summoning, dungeoneering and herblore, and agility and prayer!
Most things you can do in those skills should work.
Oh! The Voice of Seren might also help you to find some of them a little more easily!
What about if I want to stop finding golden rocks?
Do you want to stop finding them? I can do that if you'd like.
Okay, no more golden rocks for you. If you change your mind, you know where to find me!
Do you have anything in which I could store any golden rocks I find?
Okay, bye!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hiya. Do you want me to tell you about Clan Wars or do you want me to set your caller?

o: I want to set my caller.

pages.x: Tell me about Clan Wars.
Friends Chat groups come here to fight each other, army against army, battling for supremacy in our arenas.
If you rank in your Friends Chat as captain or higher, you may challenge a senior member of another Friends Chat group to a war.
The two of you must choose the rules for the war from the setup menu. When you're satisfied, choose 'Accept' and wait for your opponent to do the same.
The two of you will immediately be taken to an arena, where the rest of your Friends Chat group may join you via the portal at the southern end of this Challenge Hall.
The two armies are initially separated by a barrier. After two minutes, the barrier will sink into the ground and the war begins.
The winning Friends Chat group will be chosen according to the rules that were set at the beginning.
Remember: If you leave the arena or log out of there, it counts as a kill for the opposing team!
Why is it called Clan Wars? You said it's Friends Chat groups that are fighting.
Clans have started to get really large recently, and our portals can't handle a whole clan anymore. Don't worry, though, we're working on improved portals.
As soon as those are ready, you'll be able to bring an entire clan here.
What happens if I die?
If the rules state that items are dropped on death, you'll drop everything you're carrying. You won't be able to get it back.
Alternatively, if the rules state that you can keep your items when you die, then you'll keep them. You'll respawn in a viewing area where you may watch the war.
Depending on the rules, you may be allowed to re-enter the fight by passing through the portal at the southern end of this Challenge Hall. What can I do for you next?
What are the 'free-for-all portals?
If you fancy a bit of casual mayhem, just wander through one of those portals. They lead to arenas where there are no teams or rules.
You can fight how you like against anyone you meet, making your own entertainment.
What happens if I die?
There are two portals... The western portal leads to an arena where you keep your items when you die. You can teleport out at any time.
The eastern portal leads to an arena where you drop ALL your items on death, and you won't be able to get them back. You won't be allowed to teleport out of that arena.
Anything else?
What's a caller?
During a war, you might need to listen for instructions from a senior member of your Friends Chat group.
Unfortunately, it can be a bit tricky to spot their chat in the middle of all the chaos. I can help you set that person as your caller.
During the war, all the messages you receive from that person will be copied to your heads-up display.
You can change your caller during the war by clicking on your heads-up display, but it's more convenient to do it here with me.
Alternatively, you might find it useful to set someone in the enemy clan as your caller - heh heh heh. Anything else?
I want to set my caller.
No, I'm fine.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Greetings, recruit! Have you come for some Conquest training?

o: Could you give me a tutorial?
How do I start a Conquest?
I'd like to spend some of my Commendations.

pages.x: What is this place?
This is the Conquest training facility. Here we train recruits, such as yourself, to develop their commanding skills.
What exactly is a Conquest?
A Conquest is the name we give to the training battles that are run here.
During a Conquest, you will command various troops in an effort to eliminate your opponent's troops.
How does that help me, exactly?
You'll learn to command troops and formulate tactics: skills that might become invaluable in our continued struggle against the Void.
Of course, by taking part in a Conquest, you will also earn Commendations to trade in for rewards, as you see fit.
Interesting.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
Could you give me a tutorial?
Certainly. I can give you a quick tutorial now, if you wish?
Yes please.
Very well, let us begin.
No thanks.
Very well. Is there something else I can help you with?
How do I start a Conquest?
Head down the stairs to my right. You'll find two waiting chambers there.
In the southern waiting chamber you'll be able to issue challenges to potential opponents.
If they accept your challenge, you can agree on terms for the Conquest before you get started.
What about the other waiting chamber?
If you enter the northern waiting chamber, we'll automatically pair you with a suitably skilled opponent.
That doesn't seem too complicated.
Don't forget to speak with Knight Dorian to customise your forces first.
Customise my forces?
It's probably best if you speak with Knight Dorian to learn more about customising your forces.
Alright then.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
I'd like to spend some of my Commendations.
Certainly.

conversations.section: Talk to / Normally

pages.x: Greetings, adventurer.

o: (If the player has unlocked at least one dungeoneering journal) Show me the journals I've found.

pages.x: What is this place?
This is a place of treasures, fierce battles and bitter defeats.
We fought our way into the dungeons beneath this place.
Those of us who made it out alive...
...called this place Daemonheim.
Daemonheim?
Yes. It resembles the Niflheim of our stories: The Halls of the Dead.
The creatures within, however, are very much alive...
...unlike my fallen brothers and sisters.
What can I do here?
Beneath these ruins you will find a multitude of dungeons, filled with strange creatures and resources.
Unfortunately, due to the taint that permeates this place, we cannot risk you taking items in or out of Daemonheim.

o: How will I survive without my kit?
Why can't I take my kit in?

pages.x: How will I survive without my kit?
When we were within Daemonheim, we found a number of unknown resources. You can use your skills to fashion them into armour and weapons to keep your party alive.
Our contact within the dungeon can give you guidance on each of the items you find. He might even give you some gear to start you off.
Why can't I take my kit in?
Within Daemonheim there is a taint. The metal, wood, even the plantlife are not of this world. We cannot risk exposing the surface to them.
Equally, if we allowed you to take items inside, we could not allow you to return with them.
For this reason, our seers have erected a barrier. Nothing in, nothing out without express permission.
What does this ring do?
Raiding these forsaken dungeons can be a lot more rewarding if you're fighting alongside friends and allies. It should be more fun and you'll gain experience faster.
The ring shows others that you are interested in raiding a dungeon. It allows you to form, join and manage a raiding party.
We've also set up rooms with the specific purpose of finding a party for you.
Would you like me to show you? It's the fastest way into the dungeons of Daemonheim.
Yes, please.
It's this way.
No thanks, not right now.
Suit yourself.

conversations.section: Trade / Outside the Max Guild building

pages.x: Sorry, hun, I only sell skill capes in the tower.
Ooh, but I could tell you who DOES sell skill capes - want me to tell you where all the skill masters are?
I'll break it down for you, or I'll be droning on for ages!

pages.i: Ask about which category of cape?

pages.x: There's a couple you can get from the Warriors' Guild in Burthorpe - the attack cape from Ajjat, and the strength cape from Yadech Strongarm.
The magic cape is sold by the robe store owner in Yanille's Wizards' Guild, and the ranged cape by the armour salesman in the Ranging Guild at Hemenster.
If you're after the Defence cape, talk to Harlan at the Lumbridge Combat Academy.
For Constitution, talk to Surgeon General Tafani in her house near the north entrance of Al Kharid.
For Necromancy's cape, you'll want to search the City of Um for a phantom named the Spirit of Accomplishment.
Oh, and they're more like support skills, but the prayer cape can be bought from Brother Jered at Edgeville Monstary, and Pikkupstix in Taverley sells the summoning cape.
I made a new friend in Orla Fairweather - she sells the cape for divination. It's a skill close to my heart.
The master fisher at the Fishing Guild north of Ardougne sells that cape. I don't like fish - yuck!
If you're after a mining cape, talk to the dwarf who runs the Mining Guild in Falador.
If you want a woodcutting cape, head to the forest north of Falador and find Wilfred!
Oh, and if you're a fan of the past you could get the archaeology cape from Reiniger at the Archaeology Guild.
I don't keep my house well-maintained since I set myself up here, but I have my construction cape - I got it from an estate agent.
And the master crafter in the Crafting Guild north of Rimmington sorted me out with that cape.
Ignatius Vulcan is a strange one, but he more than earned his firemaking cape - he's in the forests south of Seers' Village.
Not far from him, in Catherby, you'll find Hickton - he sells the fletching cape.
And who can forget Thurgo in his hut at Mudskipper Point? He sells the smithing cape...and eats redberry pies!
Oh, and as for Invention...you could probably invent your OWN skillcape! Or go see Doc in the Invention Guild.
The Varrock Cooks' Guild's head chef will dish out a cooking cape for you.
Head to Draynor Village market and talk to Martin the master gardener if you're after a farming cape.
If you'd like a herblore cape, talk to Kaqemeex at the stone circle in Taverley.
Oh, and Larriar in the Runecrafting Guild atop the Wizards' Tower will sell you that cape!
Cap'n Izzy No-Beard in Brimhaven Agility Arena sells the agility cape.
He's not quite a master, but Thok Thokson sells the dungeoneering cape over at Daemonheim. He's a bit of a mumbler, that one, doesn't always make sense.
Track down the hunting expert in the Feldip Hills if you're after a hunter cape.
I'm sure Morvran of Clan Iorwerth would dispute this, but Kuradal in the Ancient Cavern is a master slayer.
And finally, you can pilfer the thieving cape from Martin Thwait - he's found in the Rogues' Den, beneath the Pick and pub in Taverley.
Okay, well, see you around!

conversations.section: The Bird and the Beast

pages.x: One moment.
Ah, hello there! What can I do for you?
Who are you?
I am Gee'ka, the Armadylean in charge of getting this golem into a battle ready state.
I am from Taka'ra's tribe and endured the same struggles as the rest of the tribe until we were happily reunited with our lord Armadyl.
During my travels, I learned many things - including the knowledge of how to construct golems, such as these.
With what we faced, being able to create an army to fight for you can be very useful indeed.
What does the golem do?
The golem strengthens our ground forces considerably, due to its sheer size and strength.
The golem is a large mechanical beast which I can tweak in order to meet our requirements.
I can also bolster certain parts of its body with enhancements or further training.
It can be used to defend the convoys against attack, increasing the effectiveness of our troops. Used more aggressively, it can attack enemy defences.
It's handy to have around, but it has a limited lifespan. Use it wisely.
Can I get involved?
Of course you can! I need guidance from loyal followers of Armadyl. I am not on the field, but I need to tweak this golem to meet the battle's needs.
As I construct parts of the golem, I'll need advice on what direction to take for each part. Should it be aggressive or defensive?
The more renown you gain from Armadyl, the more you can aid in the construction.
Do not worry if I don't construct the part in the way of your choosing. I will bear your selection in mind when creating the next golem.
To make your choices, just head over to the golem over there.
What options do I have? After selecting another option
There are four golem parts I need help with - their head, arms, body and legs.
I have a number of options for how I will construct each part, you can view these options before you make a decision.
These options define how powerful the golem is, whether it's aggressive or defensive, how long it lasts and whether it has a special attack.
For example if the enemy keeps attacking our convoys then you may wish to make the golem more defensive.
Good use of a golem can turn the tide of a battle. Consider your options carefully.
What is a Golem?
Golems are some of my finest creations. Shame that a Bandosian thug stole the idea.
There are a number of large creatures which have recently died. We take strong parts of these beasts and use them to create a skeleton.
We then machine parts to the skeleton, adding armour and weapons to the golem.
Then, Armadyl animates the golems so that it becomes a living, fighting machine.
The spell only lasts for a certain amount of time, though. When it expires, my creation crumbles to the ground.
That's all.
It was good to see you.

conversations.section: During the winter event

pages.x: I hear things in the woods - strange howling and great crashing, as if trees were being uprooted like weeds.
The noises come from the south of the woods that surround the town. I'm not letting my children near there until someone hunts down the monster.

o: Do I need to know anything in particular to fight Hati?
What is your sister trying to do?

pages.x: Who is Hati?
A creature of elemental power and endurance, spawned from a place beyond this world.
His purpose, and eventual fate, is to catch and devour the moon, just as his brother, Sköll, will one day consume the sun.
Until then they abide, and bring the freeze of winter's depths and scorching heat of summer's height to the lands.
Can they be stopped? Killed? Reasoned with?
They do not know pity or remorse or fear, and absolutely will not stop until their purpose is fulfilled.
Just as we can endure the winter and the summer with fortitude, so can we face and overcome these wolves in combat.
That's what I like to hear.
My people believe that in doing so one can take a portion of their power into oneself, and therefore gain insight.

o: Do I need to know anything in particular to fight Hati?

pages.x: Do I need to know anything in particular to fight Hati?
Its physical body is vulnerable as any other wolf is to blade, arrow or spell.
That's good.
But its will gives it an endurance far beyond any wolf, and the rage of winter within it lets it strike with chilling hoarfrost.
That's not so good.
I'd best be off.
Ah, I see.
What is your sister trying to do?
She is trying to call an even more powerful creature to our realm. The beast is Hati's brother, Sköll, and I advise caution if you intend to seek him out.
You can find Vitharr to the west, if you do not fear death.
Okay, thanks.
I'd best be off.
Who is Fenrir?
When Fenrir appears, we believe The End of Things is upon us.
How can I help?
Fenrir attacks from the south east. There are rumours that he can summon Hati and Sköll to aid him. You should bring some friends to help.
Noted.

conversations.section: Before Swept Away

pages.x: Oh, hello.
Who are you?
Me? I'm Wendy. I'm learning the ways of witchcraft from Maggie here. She's very clever, you know...and very patient.
What are you doing?
I'm travelling with Maggie, trying to learn the ways of witchcraft.
And what are you learning at the moment?
I'm learning all about - um, hold on...let me just think...
It was something really quite fascinating, I'm sure...
Uh...
Hmm...
Look, don't worry about it, really.
Sorry, I can't quite recall at the moment, but I'm sure it will come back to me, sooner or later.
If you don't mind my saying so, you look a little lost.
It's funny - I get that a lot! I don't think I'm lost...not at the moment, at least.
Keeping track of where one is isn't a problem, is it? I think it's more that I keep forgetting where I'm going.
What do you mean?
Well, it's just that there are so many interesting things to do and see, really!
It's all well and good to make plans for myself, but I always seem to get distracted along the way.
Distracted? By what?
Oh, well, you know. A pretty flower. A little impling flying by. A fluffy cat that looks like it needs a scratch under its chin.
I see things like that and my best-laid plans just seem to fly right out of my head!
Hmm, I can see how they might.
So where are you going?
Well, Maggie has been teaching me the basics of witchcraft.
I'm sure she sent me out to collect something but, come to think of it, I can't quite remember what it was.
Well, perhaps it was something for a potion? Or a spell?
Oo, that sounds possible! Do you remember what it might have been?
Well, given that I wasn't there for the conversation, I have no way of knowing that, I'm afraid.
Oh. Sad.
Wait, what were we talking about again?
Look, don't worry about it, okay?

conversations.section: On Braindeath Island / Talking to him

pages.x: Are you all right?
Who goes there?
Arr! A landlubber!
Begone afore I take my cutlass to ye! I've been charged with guardin' this gate and no noodle-armed landlubbers will make it past me alive!
That's not a cutlass.
I think it's a twig.
Ye cheeky begger! I was wavin' my finger at ye!
All right...
Arrr... just 'cos me body happens to be 50% wood does not mean I'm heartless.
I got a bag of 'em here. Wanna see?
I think I'll pass.

o: So what is going on here anyway?

pages.x: What happened to you?
So how flammable are you?
What kind of question is that?
I'll soon have you out of the way! Burn!
Don't make me angry! Ye'll not like me when I'm angry!
Let that be a lesson to ye!
My world is an ocean of paaaain!
So what is going on here anyway?
Ye expect me to talk?
No Mr. Luke, I expect you to die!
Hah! I'm one step ahead of ye!
Egad, outsmarted by the man with the wooden brain.
But seriously, what is going on here?
I can't tell ye [lad/lass].
The Cap'n would have me whittled down to toothpicks if I did.
Well if you can't tell me, perhaps you could show me through the medium of Interpretive Dance?
No. Just...no.
Mime?
Look, [lad/lass] I'm not tellin' ye a thing! So clear out while ye still can!

conversations.section: After visiting Mazcab

pages.x: Hello native human! I am Acca Gielinor, elder of the goebie settlers on this planet.
Oh, hello!
You have been to our homeworld, Mazcab, haven't you? Tell me, how are our brothers fairing against the airut?

o: With our help, they're fighting back!

pages.x: Adventurers from Gielinor have been helping them fight back. They're doing a good job!
My my, that's excellent news!

o: Why have you come to Gielinor?
Why have you settled in the desert?
What are you planning to do next?

pages.x: They seem to be holding their own. Otot and Kanatah are still standing.
Ah good, it brings me comfort to know they haven't succumbed to their oppressors.

o: Why have you come to Gielinor?
Why have you settled in the desert?
What are you planning to do next?

pages.x: They were definitely struggling, but surviving... Just.
Oh dear. I hope they find the strength to fight back against their oppressors, or join us here on Gielinor.

o: Why have you come to Gielinor?
Why have you settled in the desert?
What are you planning to do next?

pages.x: An Acca is the leader of a village. The eldest of all the goebies there, with the largest rock upon their back! It is both a blessing and a burden.
I bear my rock with pride, but these young goebs all look to me to lead them in this unfamiliar place.
I decided to lead these young goebs away from the airut. We spent too long under their feet, being tortured and enslaved.
The world window scared us, yes, but we had seen many adventurers come through it. I marched these brave goebies to the other side. To the promised lands!
This is where our people will rise up once more.
Ah yes, we have heard there are other lands. Lands like Nemi forest and like the great volcanoes... Even cold fields of white!
One day we will explore them, but the desert lands are the first we came to and they are much like home. We know how to build here and survive. In time we will prosper.
Have you spoken to the locals yet?
Oh yes, I almost forgot! We have made friends with the local goats. They appear to be the rulers of these lands. I have already met with their Acca.
The language barrier made things difficult, but I am fairly certain they have agreed to supply us with milk.
I think those goats belong to the people of Nard-
Feel free to sample from the herd. They are finer than any goat I have seen on Mazcab!
First we will build up our village here, then we will explore Gielinor.
We have heard rumours of an academy that trains people to fight, a vast city of stone where adventurers trade equipment and resources, even a tiny lady who rewards people for doing her tasks!
You certainly have a lot to discover!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Arrr, matey!

o: What would you like to say?
Are you going to sit there all day?

pages.x: I'm looking for Redbeard Frank.
Redbeard Frank ye say? He be outside. Says he likes the feel of the wind on his cheeks.
Thanks.
Arrr!
Arrr, matey!
Are you going to sit there all day?
Aye, I am. I canna walk, ye see.
What's stopping you from walking?
Arrr, I 'ave only the one leg! I lost its twin when my last ship went down.
But I can see both your legs!
Nay, young laddie, this be a false leg. For years I had me a sturdy wooden peg-leg, but now I wear this dainty little feler.
Yon peg-leg kept getting stuck in the floorboards.
Right...
Perhaps a bright young laddie like yerself would like to help me? I be needing another ship to go a-hunting my enemy.
Hmmm. And can you afford another ship?
Well, I do have a ship that I'm not using. It's the Lady Lumbridge.
Arrr! That ship be known to me, and a fine lass she is.
I suppose she might be...
So would ye be kind enough to let me take her out to sea?
I had to pay 2000 gp for that ship. Have you got that much?
Nay, I have nary a penny to my name. All my worldly goods went down with me old ship.
So you're actually asking me to give you a free ship.
Arrr! Would ye be so kind?
No I jolly well wouldn't!
Arrr.
Do you have anything for trade?
Nothin' at the moment, but then again the Customs Agents are on the warpath right now.

conversations.section: Bandosian

pages.x: Gaghh! Why isn't this working?
What do you want?
Who are you?
I'm Crush, the great Bandosian who created this fine golem.
Bandos picked me to lead the construction of this fine golem because only the wisest Bandosian is up to the job.
I crushed whole tribes in the tough armour I had created! Bandos must have recognised this.
I look forward to seeing my mighty golems crush the Armadylean forces effortlessly.
What does the golem do?
The golem further increases the power of our ground forces, due to its supreme strength.
It's a large beast which I can change to fit our requirements. I can also bolster certain parts of its body with machine enhancements or further training.
It can defend our convoys or inspire our troops. Better yet, it can fight aggressively - crushing the enemy without mercy!
It doesn't last long, though. Use it while it's hot!
Can I get involved?
Yeah. I need guidance from the warriors of Bandos. I can't get on the field and I need to tweak this golem to meet the battlefields needs.
As I put up parts of the golem, you say what direction I should take each part. Should it be aggressive or defensive?
The more renown you gain from Bandos, the more you can help.
Don't fret if it doesn't go the way you want, I'll remember your protests when creating the next golem.
To have your say, just look at this golem here and make your choice.
What options do I have?
You need to tell me how to make the head, arms, body and legs of the golem.
There are several ways I can make each part, and you can view these before saying what you think's best.
These options define how powerful the golem is: whether it's aggressive or defensive; how long it lasts, and whether it has a special attack.
For example, if we want to show the enemy who's boss, we might make the golem so that it crushes their convoys.
Good use of a golem can turn the tide of a battle.
What is a golem?
Golems are some of my finest creations! Only a genius like me could have created them.
There are remains of large beasts around that've been caught up in the fighting and died. We take the best bits of these beasts and use them to create a skeleton.
Then, we bolt on some weapons and armour to make the golem handy in a fight.
Then Bandos himself animates the golem, making a living fighting machine for waging war!
The spell only lasts for a while though. When it expires, it crumbles to the ground.
That's all.
Get out of it - I'm working.

conversations.section: At the bridge south of Rellekka

pages.x: Hello.
So you fixed the bridge?
Aye, that I did. 'Twas real thirsty work too. If only some kind stranger would buy us a bit of beer to sup, eh?
What with that inn at Seers' Village so close by and all, eh?
Just make sure yer don't get me none of that non alcoholic rubbish from that poison salesman guy at the tavern!

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Tasks in the Fremennik Province set you get a pair of boots.
The more difficulty levels of the set you complete, the better the boots get - we'll tell you what they do when we give them to you.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Fremennik set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Fremennik set rewards, speak to Yrsa in Rellekka, Advisor Ghrim on Miscellania, or myself.
Fremennik sea boots 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Fremennik sea boots 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 2,500 coins.
No thanks.
Fremennik sea boots 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Fremennik sea boots 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 15,000 coins.
No thanks.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Before Pirate's Treasure

pages.x: Can I help you?

o: Can I journey on this ship?
Does Karamja have unusual customs then?

pages.x: Can I journey on this ship?
You need to be searched before you can board.

o: Search away, I have nothing to hide.
You're not putting your hands on my things!

pages.x: Why?
Because Asgarnia has banned the import of intoxicating spirits.
Search away, I have nothing to hide.

o: (If you have Karamjan rum in inventory:)
(If you have Karamjan rum in inventory and are wearing a ring of Charos (a):)
(If you do not have Karamjan rum in inventory:)

pages.x: Aha, trying to smuggle rum are we?
Umm... it's for personal use?
Aha, trying to smuggle rum are we?

o: [Charm] This is not the Karamjan rum you're looking for.

pages.x: This is not the Karamjan rum you're looking for.
This is not the Karamjan rum we are looking for.
Well that was easy!
Drat...
Well, you've got some odd stuff, but it's all legal. Now you need to pay a boarding charge of 30 coins.

o: (If wearing a ring of Charos (a):) [Charm] Or perhaps you could let me travel for free?

pages.x: Ok.

o: (If the player does not have enough money:)
(If the player has earned Karamja gloves:)

pages.x: Oh dear, I don't seem to have enough money.
Hang on a sec, didn't you earn Karamja gloves? I thought I'd seen you helping around the island. You can go on half price, mate.

o: The ship arrives at Port Sarim.

pages.x: Oh, I'll not bother then.
Or perhaps you could let me travel for free?
Yes, perhaps I could. Okay, jump aboard then.

o: The ship arrives at Port Sarim.

pages.x: You're not putting your hands on my things!
You're not getting on this ship then.
Does Karamja have unusual customs then?
I'm not that sort of customs officer.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Avast ye, landlubber! Give us yer pineapples!

o: (If the player has completed the Easy Karamja achievements:) Got any pineapples for me?
(If the player has completed the Elite Karamja achievements) Got any apples for me?
What does a pirate have to do with pineapples?

pages.x: Who are you?
I be Dell. A pineappley pirate paragon without a parrot.
That's just odd.
Arr.
Got any pineapples for me?
Arrr, you've earned 'em.
Got any apples for me?
Arrr, you've earned 'em.
What does a pirate have to do with pineapples?
It all started aboard ship. We was leagues fr'm land and becalmed. Arr, then tha thirst came.
For rum?
Nae, not tha rum. We had plenty o' that.
For water?
Yeuch! Yer suggestin' I poisons meself?
Well, what were yer...I mean, you, thirsty for?
Pineapples!
Pineapples?
Pineapples! Lovely, juicy pineapples.
Pineapples?
Yer startin' ta sound like me parrot, mate.
Sorry, it's just a bit odd.
Arr, 'tis that. So much so tha' me parrot flew off and tha crew gave me tha nickname of Pineapple Pete.
That's funny!
Where's your parrot?
He flew off when the pineapple thirst hit. Haven't seen 'im since.
That's sad.
Arr, 'tis. But I have me pineapples ta keep me company, an' Parrot Pete only used ta say one thing.
Oh? What was that?
Was somethin' about...pickin' somethin up.
Arrr, tha's it, he used ta parrot it all day: 'Pick up a penguin.' Thing is, he'd never seen a penguin, an' neither 'ave I.

conversations.section: In the Living Rock Caverns / Talking to Farli

pages.x: Hello there!
Hi.
What brings you down here then?

o: Actually, I don't want to talk to you.

pages.x: What is this place?
It's a cavern.
Really? Great, thanks for that.
No problem!
So, is there actually anything in this cavern?
Well, there's rocks. A bit of water here and there too.
Right. Good to know. I'm glad you were here, actually, because, you know, I'd have been lost without that.
Happy to help!
Who are you?
I'm Farli. I came down here to explore the moment the cavern entrance opened up.
Have you discovered anything down there?
Well, I did stumble across some nice-looking deposits of ore and some strange fish in the waters, but I haven't really been able to investigate further.
Why not?
It's as if the rocks are moving... Whenever I've tried to map this place, I find rocks are in different places to when I checked before!
Moving rocks? Are you sure you haven't been drinking?
Well, yes. I mean no. Look, that's not important. What is important is that the rocks down here are moving!
I'll be sure to check that out...
It's true! One time I was mining a rock, or what I thought was a rock, and it upped and ran off with my best pickaxe!
What does this pulley do?
Oh, that's just to get my supplies in and out of the cavern.
How does that work then?
The miners above use the mine cart system to move about what we need from Keldagrim.
Hmm, that could be handy for depositing things into my bank. You think you could arrange that?
Hmm, maybe. I suppose if you're down here to help then I can sort something out.
Thanks!
Actually, I don't want to talk to you.
Hmph! How rude!

conversations.section: If the player has not finished training with Aluft Gianne snr. and Blurberry / Before showing interest in a job

pages.x: Hello, welcome to Aluft Aloft, the gnome food delivery service. We deliver gnome foods to customers all over Gielinor. Do you want a job?
We are always looking for new staff.

pages.i: Are you interested in a job?

pages.x: Yes, tell me more.
First of all you will need some basic Gnome Cooking and Cocktail making training. Go and talk to my Father, Aluft Gianne snr.
and Blurberry, if you haven't already, and they'll tell you what you need to do.
Once you have got recommendations from both of them I'd be happy to take you on at Aluft Aloft!
Once you are working for us, I will give you a choice of either an easy or hard job.
I will then ask you to make a piece of Gnome Cuisine, and tell you who ordered it, with some information about how to find him or her.
Don't take too long, the order is only valid for a short period of time.
If you complete the delivery successfully, you will be given a tip by the customer and credit towards your own 'free delivery token'.

o: What's the difference between an easy and a hard job?
What are these free delivery tokens?
Will this help me with my cooking?
I'm ready to take a job on now.
I've changed my mind, there's something else I need to do now.

pages.x: What's the difference between an easy and a hard job?
The foods that you need to cook for the easy jobs are more straight forward than the hard ones, and the customers will be within the Gnome Stronghold, or one of the Gnome Glider Pilots on duty.
You will get one credit for completing a delivery, and the tips you get will be a small amount of cash.
The hard jobs could require you to cook any piece of gnome cuisine or cocktail. The customers could be anywhere in Gielinor.
If you are going to complete the delivery in time, you'll probably have to use some form of transport. Gnome gliders are especially useful here.
For the hard jobs you will be given more time to complete the delivery though.
You get three credits for completing it, and the tips you get tend to be useful objects, and even a few unusual items, that you won't be able to get hold of anywhere else!
What are these free delivery tokens?
I'll give you a free delivery token when you earn 12 credits. You can then use the token to make a food order yourself!
This is a great privilege, we normally only deliver to gnomes. You may only have one token at a time, and they are non-transferrable.
If you gain more credits then for every 12 extra credits you earn, you will receive an extra item of food or drink per delivery, up to a maximum of ten items.
You can continue to make deliveries after this, but you will not get any more credits - just the normal tip and cooking training.
Once you call for a delivery your token will be used up, and you'll have to earn another one, if you want another delivery.
Will this help me with my cooking?
You will be able to develop your cooking skills during deliveries - you'll get the normal training for making the items, but also a bonus for successfully delivering the goods.
I'm ready to take an order now...
I'm afraid you don't have the required training for this job. If you want to work for me you'll have to talk to my father Aluft Gianne snr.
for cooking training and Blurberry the barman for cocktail making training. Once I get recommendations from both of them, you'll be able to start work for me.
So that's Aluft Gianne snr. for cooking training, and Blurberry for Cocktail training?
That's right - Good luck!

conversations.section: In Lumbridge / Before getting a Slayer task for the first time

pages.x: 'Ello, and what are you after then?

o: Do you have anything for trade?

pages.x: Who are you?
I'm an apprentice Slayer Master.
What's a slayer?
Oh dear, what do they teach you in school?
Well...er...
I suppose I'll have to educate you then. A slayer is someone who is trained to fight specific creatures. They know that creatures every weakness and strength.
As you can guess it makes killing them a lot easier.
Never heard of you.
That's because my foe never lives to tell of me. We slayers are a dangerous bunch.
Wow, can you teach me?
Hmmm, well, I'm not so sure...
Pleeeaasssse!
Oh, okay then, you twisted my arm. You'll have to train against specific groups of creatures.
Ok then, what's first?
We'll start you off hunting [monster]. You'll need to kill [number] of them.
You'll also need this enchanted gem, it allows Slayer Masters like myself to contact you and update you on your progress.
Don't worry if you lose it; you can buy another from any Slayer Master.
Okay, great!
Good luck! Don't forget to come back when you need a new assignment.
Sounds useless to me.
Suit yourself.
Do you have anything for trade?
I have a wide selection of Slayer equipment; take a look!
Er...nothing...

conversations.section: When talked to

pages.x: Greetings [traveler/World Guardian]! What can I do for you today?

o: Tell me about the Outfit of Trials.

pages.x: Isn't it glorious? I'm really proud of it!
I once met a woman called Xenia who showed me a helmet that inspired the design of this whole outfit.
It wasn't easy, but I tried to embody what it means to be an adventurer in this outfit.
It's ok to struggle, but if you get back up, and keep going you will succeed eventually!
Is there anything else I can help you with?
They're wonderful, right? I found them when they were just puppies, lost and alone.
I have no idea where they came from, and since that day I've never seen another like them.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
Well there's lots here to help you as you progress in your adventures.
There's a way to quickly join other adventurers on their latest endeavour and a title to show off your prowess.
I'll even keep hold of some of the assortment of stuff you're sure to pick up as you travel the land, I've a dedicated chest just for that!
Is there anything else I can help you with?
Best of luck in your adventures!
Well as you can see I'm not the most organised, so there's quite a bit of stuff from my own adventures just strewn about.
Not all of it is mine though, there's also some bits and bobs that I'm just keeping an eye on.
What's really important is what I've got for you! I'm so excited to show you all of it.
Is there anything else I can help you with?
My name is May, and I used to be an adventurer just like you.
I'd always dreamed of building a name for myself, becoming famous around the world! For a while Dionysius even recognised my achievements!
I came to realise that being the star of the shoe is fun, but what I really care about is helping people.
So, I hung up my cape, and put my skills to work helping other adventurers.
It's taken me a while to get myself all set up, but now here I am, ready to help adventurers at any stage in their journey!
Is there anything else I can help you with?
Best of luck in your adventures!

conversations.section: At Memorial to Guthix / First time

pages.x: What is this place?
It's been here for years, my dear. I knew of it, I've read of it, but we could never see it. It was kept hidden from view for reasons I know not.
Ever since Guthix left this world, I've been gaining an ever-increasing sense of this place's existence.
Tiny strands of Guthixian memories have started appearing near Divination craters.
It seems like they were hidden from view until now.
I'll try to explain what I've been researching since I've been here. It's all coming back to me slowly.
It all starts with engrams. Engrams are permanent markers left on the timeline.
They're caused by the significant activities of living things and can only be spotted by those who have an adept understanding of Divination.
It is possible to charge these engrams by infusing them with divine energy and memory strands.
What does that do to them?
Oh, it's a theatre of light and magic, my dear. The engrams hold an echo of history.
These 'echoes' all belong to Guthix, right? Engrams, memory strands, divine energy...they're all part of Guthix's residual life-force.
How very astute. I suppose I should expect nothing less from you.
I have only ever charged a couple of weak engrams, but they were both from the viewpoints of Guthix himself.
We can assume that the rest are almost certainly related to Guthix as well.
There could be so much valuable information stored in these engrams. How do we find them?
In the centre of this concourse behind me, you'll see a pool brimming with energy. You'll probably sense it before you see it. It gives off such a glorious aura.
All of the plinths inside the building are somehow connected to this pool.
Once charged, I could display the echoes found inside the engrams there, just like statues of raw life; animated echoes of reality.
If you tinker with the plinths, you may be able to discover a vague idea of locations of other engrams. I can't promise that they will be easy to detect, though.
So once I've found an engram, I can charge it by filling it with divine energy and these memory strands?
Yes, and then bring it to me. I can get the pool of energy to absorb any charged engrams that you bring here.
After that, you should be free to interact with the echoes as you see fit.
This seems simple enough, but let me quickly recap.
I need to use the plinths to get hints about where to find the engrams, then charge these engrams with memory strands and divine energy, and then give them to you to add to the pool here?
Yep, it seems that you've got it.
Oh, one more thing!
Hmm?
The pool of energy. Once I had charged some engrams, I noticed that I felt a stronger connection to this place.
Perhaps we can focus the energy in this place to help you with your Divination skill? Just a hunch, of course.
Sounds interesting. I'll investigate.
Fantastic. Please take one of the engrams that I found, to get yourself started and to gain a feel for them.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Good day, sir. How may I be of assistance?

o: I'd like more information about clans.
What are the benefits of being in a clan?
How do I recruit more clanmates?
How do I leave a clan?

pages.x: I'm so glad you asked me that, [ma'am/sir]. Allow me to explain.
A clan is a group of players who have banded together for mutual benefit.
As a member of a clan, you can do things you couldn't do on your own.
You can create your very own clan citadel, and decorate it with your clan motif.
You can take part in social events, including meetings and parties.
You can create a clan avatar, a customisable companion who can give you an experience boost.
You can work with your clanmates to increase your skills.
You can battle other players' clans in the Wilderness and the Clan Wars Arena.
And you can fight powerful enemies, such as the King Black Dragon and Kalphite Queen, and earn valuable rewards.
If you are the founder of your clan or a recruiter, you can invite others to join by using your vexillum on them.
But remember that if a player has already joined a clan, they will not receive your invitation.
I can help you leave your clan right now if you wish.
