Remember, however, that if you are the last remaining member of the clan, leaving will permanently dissolve the clan.

o: Do you want to leave your clan?

pages.x: A clan cloak identifies you as a member of a clan, and displays your clan's motif. The Captain of the Guard can provide you with one, if you wish.
A vexillum is a banner that displays your clan's colours and emblem. It can be carried, displayed, or used to recruit new clanmates.
If you place the vexillum in the ground, others can use it to find out more about your clan, and contact you if they are interested in joining.
You can also use the vexillum directly on other players to invite them to join your clan. Finally, you can use the vexillum to teleport directly here.
It would be my pleasure, [ma'am/sir].

o: The scribe gives you a vexillum.

pages.x: Clan scribe Amos Twinly at your service, sir. I keep a record of all clans, and distribute clan charters to those who wish to start a clan.
If you are a member of a clan, I can also provide you with a vexillum - a banner displaying your clan's motif.
Goodbye, [ma'am/sir].

conversations.section: After Darkness of Hallowvale, up to River of Blood

pages.x: Well, I guess so.

o: I'm lost... Can you help me?
Do you know about the Myreque?
Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?
What do you know about the vampyres?

pages.x: What do you do here?
I'm a black-market trader... Fancy taking a look at my wares?

o: What sort of stuff have you got?
Yes, I'll take a look at your wares!
No, I want to ask more questions.

pages.x: What sort of stuff have you got?
Well then, young [lad/lass], that is a good question.
In fact, I specifically deal in vyrewatch uniforms – they might leave you alone a bit more if they think you're one of them!
Makes it easier to move around the sectors without them demanding a blood tithe every time you dare breathe. So then, do you wanna have a look at my stuff?
Yes, I'll take a look at your wares!
Good on ya, [lad/lass]. Good on ya.
No, I want to ask more questions.
I'm lost... Can you help me?
Well, you're in sector [one/two/three/four/five/six], but if you were hoping for any other help then I'm very sorry. I find it hard enough to help myself.
Life's so very hard here. Before too long they'll be wanting to have another blood tithing and then I'll feel just awful again.
What's a blood tithing?
You must be new here, else you'd know for sure. It's where we have to give a blood tithe to the vampyres.
They do it on a weekly basis, a different sector each week so they don't kill us all off.
Do you know about the Myreque?
It's probably best not to talk about that, friend.
I need to make contact with them. Please don't worry - I'm on their side.
As are we all, but I really can't talk about them. It's not a subject easily broached here.
Can you tell me about the Sanguinesti region?
Yep, that's where we are at the moment. This place, Meiyerditch, is just one large ghetto.
The city is sectioned off so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis. That way they don't kill us all off in one go.
What do you know about the vampyres?
They're monsters, I know that much. I've never known anything else, but I have a feeling it might be nice to not have to live in fear the whole time.
Worrying if I'm going to make the next blood tithe quota.
I know that the juveniles are the lowest form of the vampyres, most likely converted from some sort of bipedal creature, probably human.
Juvinates are initiated juveniles who've had some training and are starting to get some special powers. After that you have the vyrewatch - they're nasty... really nasty.

conversations.section: Prifddinas / After Plague's End

pages.x: Well me Player, it's good to see you again. How can I be of service?
Can you tell me about yourself?
You already know me as a rebel leader, against the Iorwerth that was, but I suppose now is the time to speak more of who I was...and am.
It feels as though I have been fighting most of my life. At first it was with my brothers and sisters.
Oh, nothing serious you understand - the standard sibling rivalries. Trying to prove I was better than them in some way.
My brother Dai was always a bit better than I am at magic - one of the skills held dear.
But there were none who could hold a crystal to my skills with a bow.
I relished responsibility and took every opportunity I could to develop my leadership skills.
Hah, I started from a mere archery trainer and then moved up from there.
The only real competition I had to becoming clan leader was my brother Dai. I was mastering archery, and he was a master of magic.
It drove quite a wedge between us, I'm ashamed to say. So on the day that they announced me as the new lord of Clan Cadarn, my brother left.
Where is he now?
I don't know my friend, I wish I did. Perhaps now that the clans have reunited, we might reconcile.
But enough melancholy. Were there other questions you had for me?
Can you tell me about Clan Cadarn?
We are an ancient clan of defenders. We have guarded and protected the elven people for as long as I can remember, and long before that.
Guided by the will of Seren, our arrows find the hearts of our foes and our magic shatters all but the most powerful defences.
We are the soldiers of Prifddinas; its defenders, and - when necessary - its vanguard.
Where Iorwerth flaunt their brutal methods, we exemplify subtlety and precision.
A single arrow, in the right place, can do more damage than an entire platoon of Iorwerth warriors.
They would be wise to remember that.
Can you tell me about Clan Cadarn's skills?
Cadarn are warriors of precision and discipline. We specialise in ranged combat and magic.
Were - Seren forbid - the elves to be drawn into a war, it would be Cadarn leading the fight - scouting ahead and engaging with the most tactically significant targets.
Oh, Iorwerth would tell you they would be the backbone of such an army... But while they are the spine, we are the hands.
It would be Cadarn making the surgical strikes, taking out the enemy leaders and striking where it is most effective.
Let Iorwerth pat themselves on the back for being able to march out in force and die in force, whilst it would be Cadarn that would actually win such a war.
With magic we can change the battlefield to our advantage, teleporting over terrain, enchanting our weapons or cursing our enemies.
Skill, precision and efficiency. Our clan skills represent these ideals and we endeavour to use them as such.

o: Can you give me another crystal trinket?
I'd like to reclaim the Trahaearn exoskeleton.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / With 53 Prayer or greater

pages.x: Hail, traveler! How can I help you?

o: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I'm done talking to you, now!

pages.x: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Oh, but of course! Allow me to assist you by showing you my map.
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I can tell you about the state of the beacons in either direction, up to the last fires that are lit.
I could probably tell you about the other beacons as well, but I'd need the help of a macaw.
A macaw?
Yes. Macaws have the ability to fly high into the air and see things that are much further away.
They are also highly intelligent and can be trained to provide the exact information I'd need for a complete overview of the beacon network.
How's it going?
Oh, very well, thank you. The time away from the Monastery has given me opportunity to mediate and reflect on my path in life.
That sounds very spiritually fulfilling.
It certainly is. I must admit, it's been very nice to spend some time outdoors. The Monastery is pretty stuffy this time of year, not to mention a bit boring.
Oh?
Sometimes, I really wish I'd followed by heart when picking a career, but mother did want a monk in the family. It would have broken her heart.
Oh, but you won't tell the abbot I said so, will you? He would be so disappointed.

o: It's not too late to take up another profession, you know.

pages.x: Of course I won't.
I thank you.
It's not too late to take up another profession, you know.
Do you really think so?
Of course!
But, my dear mother...
Well, what's to say that you can't be a monk AND do something else?
A monk and something else? I'd never considered that!
For example, you seem to be doing a pretty good job at being both a monk and a professional fire tender at present.
You know, you're right! Thank you, Player, you've given me much to think about. I'm very grateful for your advice.
I'm done talking to you, now!
My, such assertiveness!

conversations.section: Boat tour / With both hands free

pages.x: *grumble* Welcome to Ed's boat tours in the City of Um. Today we'll be rowing around Lake Mnemosyne, while I tell you some fun facts about the sights.
*grumble* First stop, the Well of Souls. A masterpiece of architecture, this vessel harbours all of the souls that live here, in Um.
It was created in the First Age, not long after the City itself, and boasts stone carvings of skulls and Death himself.
If you look close enough, you can even see the individual souls floating about in its bowl.
It really is an impressive structure.
Indeed. I wouldn't get too close if I were you though - there's quite a drop surrounding it.
*grumble* For our second stop, just some of the many shipwrecks in Mnemosyne.
Imagined into existence by the many sailors and pirates alike, these wrecks scatter themselves across the rocky outcrops.
Have you met many famous beings in Um?
Great question. With Um having seen many residents over the years, I have met my fair share of notable Gielinorians.
Like who?
Well, to name a few, Queen Glarial of the elves, Obi'Sooth of the aviansie, and the infamous Count Draynor.
Most of them pass through to the afterlife, but some, such as the legendary fisherwoman Tavia, choose to hang around in Um for a while.
No gods, though, as beings such as them - as well as Mahjarrat and demons - do not pass through the Underworld.
*grumble* The third stop on our tour is the dastardly Rasial's citadel.
Whilst not in the City of Um, the citadel sits high in the sky - with views over a vast array of the Underworld.
I haven't personally visited, but I hear it has an impressive central chamber, complete with an antique organ.
*grumble* I don't get fazed easily... But looking up at that citadel for too long sends a rattle down my old bones.
If you're lucky, you might come across some fellow boaters when exploring Mnemosyne, such as our locals Sammy and Deano.
*grumble* Our penultimate stop on the tour is the graveyard and market of Um.
Rather than honouring the dead, the shrines in the graveyard honour the living.
Many residents light candles within them to look over their living loved ones, while they wait for them to pass.
How thoughtful.
The market is home to a variety of traders, who come from all over to sell their wares on the docks of Um.
*grumble* And our final stop on this tour is the centre of the City itself.
The City of Um was created by Death in the First Age, and has since seen a vast variety of beings pass through - humans, trolls, elves, and more.
Residents that pass through here create the features of the city through their memories.
This leaves most of the structures to deteriorate over time as the residents pass on, and their memories are forgotten.
However, one of the most notable and longest-standing features of Um is its giant hourglass.
This is one of the few surviving original features since the City's inception, having been kept in memory due to the frequent visits by Death.
Now, does anyone have any questions before we end the tour?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello there.
Good day. Can I help you with anything?

o: Yes, I'd like a drink please.
The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.
(After The Feud:) Could you tell Traitorous Hesham that someone has poisoned his drink.

pages.x: What's going on in town?
Well since you gave the two gangs a good kicking, things have improved hugely. Both gangs seem to be spending all their gold here drowning their sorrows.
That's great! So do I get a cut in the profits?
Get out of here, you cheeky rascal. A cut in my profits? As if!
Nothing much really, the same as you would expect of any border town on the edge of the desert.
So can you tell me anything about those two gangs in the town?
Nothing much to really say about them. They're all paying customers so I won't rock the boat if you don't mind.
Is there anything else I can help you with?

o: Yes, I'd like to talk about something else.

pages.x: No thanks I'm ok. Thanks for your time.
The 'Asp and Snake'? What a strange name for a bar.
I know what you're thinking, asps are a type of snake, right?
I admit it is a little confusing, but neither 'The Asp' nor 'The Snake' have quite the same ring to them.
I get your point. I quite like the name.
Could you tell Traitorous Hesham that someone has poisoned his drink.
What! Drink being poisoned in my bar! My reputation could be destroyed if someone died here. Thank you adventurer.
No problem at all.
Here have a beer - it's on the house.

o: Thanks but no thanks, I don't drink.
Faisal the barman gives you a beer.

pages.x: Thanks but no thanks, I don't drink.
Don't say that around here too loud please, it may catch and then I'd be out of business.
You could always open up a non alcoholic fruit juice bar. You'd have less problems with drunken customers.
You might be onto something there, but then what would I do with the drunken sailor?
Who?
Jalal the Drunk. Oh never mind its a long story.
Fine, no need to insult me then.

conversations.section: In the Dwarven Mine

pages.x: 'Ello, Player.
Hello, what's that you've got there?
A crossbow, are you interested?
Maybe, are they any good?
Are they any good?! They're dwarven engineering at its best!

o: How do I make one for myself?

pages.x: How do I make one for myself?
Well, firstly, you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.
Wood fletched into stock... check.

Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.
Which goes with which?
Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials. Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamantite and Mahogany and finally Runite and Yew.
Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?
Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows.
You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.
What about magic logs?
Well... I don't rightly know... us dwarves don't work with magic, we prefer gold and rock. Much more stable.
I guess you could ask the humans at the rangers guild to see if they can do something but I don't want anything to do with it!
Thanks for telling me. Bye!
Take care, straight shooting.
Thanks for telling me. Bye!
Take care, straight shooting.
What about ammo?
You can smith yourself lots of different bolts, don't forget to flight them with feathers like you do arrows though.
There's also the option of tipping any untipped bolt with gems then enchanting them with runes. This can have some pretty powerful effects.
Oh my poor bank, how will I store all those?!
Find Hirko in Keldagrim, he also sells crossbow parts and I'm sure he has something you can use to store bolts in.
Thanks for the info.
Thanks for telling me. Bye!
Take care, straight shooting.

conversations.section: Hosting Genie's Gift

pages.x: Hi there! It's great to see you.

o: What do you want to do?
Ask about organising your won items.

pages.x: You want to know about me? Sure - ask away.

o: What do you want to do?

pages.x: I'm Karima, a representative of Super Happy Wonder Lamp. We provide peerless wish services to mortals of this plane. I myself am from the Vetal caste of Djinn.
We are aligned with the magical power of air. See how I'm floating? That's bona fide genie power for you!
Super Happy Wonder Lamp is proud to provide a superb service to you today! You can trade keys to me in return for some fabulous prizes.
We currently have a special offer on lamps! You'll find a corny... corner... coro... A lot! You'll find a lot of lamps hidden in these chests!
What kind of lamps you ask? All kinds! huge lamps, small lamps, bright lamps, dark lamps.
Every kind of lamp you can imagine, even our prized celebration lamps if you're very lucky!
We've performed an *teehee* aggressive takeover of the Treasure Hunter business previously owned by one... ...Princess Alessandra.
I'm sure she's completely safe, unharmed, totally not toast.
It's very easy - if you've got a Treasure Hunter key, you can open a chest and win a prize.

o: What do you want to ask?
What do Hearts of Ice do?

pages.x: Just click on a chest, and see what you win! It's very simple. One key opens one chest to win one prize.
There's loads of prizes to be won! You could win a falling star for some bonus XP, or some resources to help you train a skill.
If you're really lucky you could win a super-rare prize and show off to all your friends!
You can see the prizes that could be in your next chest on the ticker below the chests.
Keys are all over the place! You can also find them around the world as you adventure.
Not only that, but I'll give you a free key every day you're here - two if you're a member.
You can also buy keys directly, and you can earn them through quests and challenges.
Hearts of Ice are magical crystals that you can use to freeze prize categories.
If the prize in the chest you choose is in a frozen category, I'll give you a prize from an unfrozen category instead.
You can find out more by clicking on the categories button.
You can get them when you buy Treasure Hunter keys directly, find keys around the world, or open at least five chests per day.
I have created a way for you to see all of the items you have won on Treasure Hunter and Squeal of Fortune.
You can find out information on all of the items and then decide if you want to keep them. Would you like me to open the interface?

conversations.section: Upgrading necromancy equipment / Tier 90 / Tank / Before having received the inert necromantic crystal

pages.x: So you've chosen to upgrade to tier 90.
To start, you'll need to fill up this soul urn for me.
The urn will only accept souls from powerful communion rituals, of which I need 50.
Alternatively, you can fill it up by just completing a Soul Reaper task using necromancy.
Next, I need 10 empowered necromantic seals from each of the generals of the Heart of Gielinor.
This is a complex process that's taken a lot of time to perfect, so pay attention.
First off, you'll need to defeat the boss to gain the unpowered seals. Make sure to bring along 25 greater necroplasm too.
Now, once you have a bunch of their seals, they'll each require a different process to empower...
The seals from Helwyr should be empowered through opening a crystal chest.
Gregorovic's seals will need you to craft some miasmic runes.
Vindicta's seals will need you to use Bone Shield against a dragonfire attack.
And last but not least, the Twin Furies seals will need you to restore some Zamorakian artefacts.
That is... a lot of work.
Oh, I'm not finished yet!
I also need a pulsating onyx. You'll be able to craft this by combining an uncut onyx and a special crystal.
Lucky for you, I already have the crystal here with me.
Great!
Unlucky for you, it needs powering up. The energies from defeating TzTok-Jad in the TzHaar Fight Cave should be enough for that.
Great.
So that's it, right? I'll be off now!
Not so fast!
Lastly, I would like a blueberry pie.
A BLUEberry pie?
I'm not sure exactly what Gielinor was like during your time alive, but I can tell you now that we don't have such a thing as a blueberry.
I'm sure you can figure it out. Maybe some inhabitants around the city can help you.
So that's...
A full soul urn, 10 empowered necromantic seals from each of the 4 Heart of Gielinor generals, a pulsating onyx...
... And a blueberry pie.
That's everything!
You've got a lot of work ahead of you, so no need to hang around. Here's the list.

conversations.section: In Keldagrim marketplace

pages.x: What to buy? What to buy? Oh, hello human.
Anything I can help you with?
Only if you can help me make a suggestion on what to buy.
I smell a quest!
No, not really. I just need some advice on what to buy, that's all.
You should buy some new clothes. You can't go around town wearing what you're wearing.
You're right, this is a little drab. I shouldn't really go around Keldagrim-West wearing this, should I?
Of course I still don't know what colour I should get. I don't want to accidentally offend the wrong company of course.
Never mind.
You should get yourself a big mighty warhammer.

o: (After The Giant Dwarf and before Birthright of the Dwarves:)

pages.x: I don't think so. The warhammer shop is run by the Red Axe. I'd rather stay out of there.
You don't like the Red Axe?
They're all a lot of bullies if you ask me.
I don't think so. The warhammer shop is run by the Red Axe. I'd rather stay out of there.
You don't like the Red Axe?
They're all a lot of bullies if you ask me.
But I thought they left the city?
They may have, but I still think that shopkeeper is in league with them, banners or no.
I don't think so. The warhammer shop used to be run by the Red Axe. I'd rather stay out of there.
Get yourself a long piece of rope.
What would I do with a rope?
I don't know. I generally find a rope useful while adventuring.
I don't do a lot of adventuring to be honest.
An oversized hat. In a ridiculous colour.
No one is selling hats here, that's not a very helpful suggestion at all.
Nothing. You should buy absolutely nothing.
Now that's the best idea I've heard all day.
I thought so! Now why don't you give me some of the money I saved you?
No, I don't think so. I think I'd rather buy something with my money after all.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Welcome to the Burthorpe Games Rooms!

o: How do I play board games?
Can I buy a drink please?

pages.x: How do I play board games?
You can challenge someone to a game anywhere in the games rooms by using the right click option.
Choose the type of game and then choose the options you want such as time per move.
If you want to play a particular game there are challenge rooms dedicated to that game.
In the challenge rooms you can see other players ranks by right clicking them, their skill will be displayed instead of their combat level.
Once you have enough experience you will be able to use the challenge rooms on the first floor!
If your opponent accepts the challenge you will be taken to one of the tables in the main room where you will play your game of choice.
Once you have finished your game you will go back to the challenge room where you can challenge again!
What games can I play?
Currently we offer Draughts, Runelink, Runesquares, and Runeversi.
Draughts?
Draughts uses standard rules, apart from: a draw is declared if no piece has been taken or promoted for forty moves.
To play Draughts go to the challenge room in the SW corner.
Runelink?
Yup, you have to get four runes in a row. The challenge room for Runelink is in the SE corner.
Runesquares?
Yes, you take it in turns to add a line with the goal of making squares. Everytime you make a square you take another turn.
The challenge room for Runesquares is in the SW corner.
Runeversi?
Yep, the aim is to have more of your runes on the board than your opponent. You can take your opponents pieces by trapping them between your own.
The challenge room for Runeversi is in the SE corner.
Do you have any news?
There are some notice boards in the main entrance, check them from time to time for the latest news.
Can I buy a drink please?
Certainly [sir/miss], our speciality is Asgarnian Ale, we also serve Wizard's Mind Bomb and Dwarven Stout.
Thanks!
