conversations.section: 2018 Christmas event

pages.x: Ho ho ho! Merry Christmas, Player!
It's great to see you again, Santa! What do you have in store for me this year?
Well, there's quite a lot going on this year, please let me know what you want to talk about and we can go from there.

o: What do you want to talk about?

pages.x: What's that big ol' cracker over there all about?
Ah yes, that is just a little gift that I brought with me here to share with you. It needs to be wrapped up first though before it can be pulled apart!
You can help to wrap the cracker by adding Christmas cracker paper to it.
The paper is earned whilst skilling and killing, with a bonus bundle of paper available for completing your daily challenges!
Once the cracker is fully wrapped, it can be pulled apart to receive gifts galore!
Don't worry if you miss out on the experience, I have plenty more crackers with me which will be used to replace open ones so that it can be wrapped and pulled again!
I must warn you though, in the interest of kindness, you must add at least 100 pieces of paper to a cracker in order to be eligbile for a prize!
So what are you waiting for? Earn yourself some paper and get wrapping!

o: What prizes are available from the cracker?

pages.x: Ho ho ho. I normally wouldn't allow this, but seeing as you asked ever so kindly, I will show you what's on offer!
Thank you, Santa!
Can you tell me more about Winter Weekends, please?
Of course! Every weekend in December, and for the first weekend in January, there will be boosts and buffs to various activities throughout the game.
Each weekend starts from midday on the Friday, and finishes midday the following Monday.
There's also a winter portal just over there, which will help you get to the active locations quicker than ever!
If you would like to see the full list of boosts available, and on which weekends they will be active, open the event tab within the community interface.
I love Christmas so much! Is there any way that I can help you?
Now that you mention it, there is something. My sleigh is fuelled by Christmas spirit but it appears to be dying out this year.
If I can't get enough Christmas spirit in time, I fear that I won't be able to deliver all of the presents that I need to.
If you could help me, by summoning some of your own Christmas spirit, and siphoning it into my sleigh, I would be forever grateful.
I will be able to offer you experience in Summoning or Runecrafting for your time and help. Simply interact with my sleigh to begin.
Do you know of any quests I can participate in?
Yes, of course! I heard a very loud roar coming from White Wolf Mountain when I arrived here, perhaps you should check it out to see what the noise was all about.
I have set up a portal at the very north of the Grand Exchange which will help you to get started. Don't worry, you shouldn't need to bring anything with you.
That sounds intriguing! Thank you, Santa.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: To what do I owe the pleasure?

o: You seem to be pretty welcoming now.
How did you get your nickname?

pages.x: I could tell you, but I'd have to kill you.
Given the circumstances I'm not sure if that's a joke...
Right now, I'm not sure either.

o: I'll, erm, just let you get back to your business.

pages.x: Ha, you're bold indeed.

o: The surrounding bandits give you a worrying glare.

pages.x: Alright, I'll bite. Used to make a pretty penny evicting a few poor souls from their bodies.
An assassin, then.
You'd be surprised how often you'll find 'employment' in a 'civilised' place like Misthalin.
I hadn't thought that someone might eventually take offence. I'm known to the authorities now, a fugitive.
Speaking on the topic, got anyone around these parts you need taking care of? My rates are reasonable.

o: I'll keep your offer in mind.

pages.x: At your service.
I'm getting a good feeling from you. You're marked by your intentions.
You can tell, huh? It is a little thrilling, and a little scary.
Wonderful isn't it? Blood pumping, adrenaline flowing.
We have more trust in someone willing to put themselves at risk. The overly cautious don't belong in these lands.
Well, that's a long story.
Go on.
You see...
my kills have been described as notably rapid.
And my real name?
That's Keith.

conversations.section: If the player meets the requirements to engage in Dominion Tower / First-time dialogue

pages.x: Hello?
Hello.
Woah!
It is intriguing that you took so long before coming to me. Fearful, traveller?
Should I be?
It is my duty to inform you that many warriors fight here, and they all succumb to defeat eventually. If that instils terror in you, walk away now.
There are monsters in the tower?
If that is the terminology you would use, yes. Through the powers bestowed upon me by my creator, I can generate opponents for you based on your memories of them.
Men and women have fought here for generations.
Impressive. So, you control the tower?
The tower is I, and I have control of the tower. I see what happens in any corner of any floor. I am always watching.
So, you believe yourself a mighty warrior?

o: Only the greatest warrior that ever lived!
I'm pretty handy with a weapon.

pages.x: Only the greatest warrior that ever lived!
Intriguing. Such belief in your own abilities...
What?
Your confidence may have a foundation, but judgment will come in battle.
I'm pretty handy with a weapon.
Intriguing...I sense humility in you.
What?
For your sake, I hope 'pretty handy' is an understatement.
My purpose...must never stop...
Sorry? Are you alright?
You must fight in the tower, warrior. Demonstrate your ability to others and learn.
I'd have thought that, as a guide, you'd be a little more welcoming.
You will find I am welcoming enough.
Now, I can offer you more guidance; or, if you overflow with confidence, you can figure it out yourself.
I am the tower, I am ever-present, so come to me if you change your mind.
You are proving to be wise.
Your choice. Come back if you change your mind.

conversations.section: Before agreeing to aid Teelee for the first time / Talk to

pages.x: Greetings! These are some interesting looking mushrooms.
Oh, hello! Why, yes, yes they are!
I haven't seen you around here before. My name's Teelee. It's very nice to meet you.
That's a very...unique name. I'm Player.
So, these mushrooms... Are they just magical mushrooms? Or are they like the mushrooms found in fairyrings?
Ha! Oh, no no no. While these are magical mushrooms, they serve a far greater purpose than that of transportation.
Oh? And what might that be?
...Oh, my dear. This grove is rife with magical energy. Be sure to explore the grove in its entirety. I'm sure you'll uncover a lot of hidden secrets!
Hmm, alright. So, back to these mushrooms. What makes them so special?
The mushrooms are entwined with the tree spirits of the grove. Have you seen the great tree?
If you haven't yet ventured to the north, head that way and you'll see the magnificent tree.
The wisps that dwell here aid our tree with nutrients, allowing it to grow. I bet you've never seen a tree of this size in all your travels!
Perhaps not. You mentioned the mushrooms are entwined with the grove. What did you mean by that?
That's the beauty of our grove! Many forms of magic harbour here. When our great tree requires additional nutrients, it channels its needs through these mushrooms.
The colour of each mushroom informs us which essence we must gather from the wisps.
So you mean you're sacrificing the wisps?
Oh, gosh no! Don't be silly! The wisps have excess energy. We create a mixture from a small amount of energy, and offer it to the great tree.
It's a ritual we perform each week.
So, would you be willing to help me gather from the wisps?
I guess I could. I don't think I'd benefit from it, though, and you don't seem to be that busy.
Actually, I'm guarding the mushrooms.
Usually Bub or I will collect the energy while the other watches over the mushrooms, but she went exploring and still hasn't returned.
She always wanders off when she's due to guard!
I could offer you something in return if you could help me out. What do you say?

pages.i: Would you like to aid Teelee this week?

pages.x: Hmm. Unknown rewards from a complete stranger seem right up my alley. Count me in. What exactly do I need to do?
Excellent! Thank you so much! Right, so you need to take this jar and collect the wisps of the corresponding mushroom colours shown here.
Once you've done that, come back and see me. You'll find the wisps spread out across the grove.
If the mushrooms are the same colours you'll only need to find one wisp of that colour! Best of luck!
Sorry, maybe another time. I first want to take a look around this grove.
Very well. If you change your mind, I'll be right here!

conversations.section: Talk to / On a league world

pages.x: Hello, mortal. What do you seek?

o: Can you tell me what is going on?
Can you tell me about tasks?
Can you tell me about relics?
Can you tell me about relics and blessings?

pages.x: In every League, there are a number of tasks for you to complete. Each task has a level of difficulty: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite and Master.
Completing tasks earns you League Points. The number of points earned is independent on the difficulty of the task.
What do these points do?
Once you have achieved a certain amount of League Points you can unlock a new Relic of mine. These are powerful artefacts to help you in this world.
League Points can also be used to buy rewards from the Leagues Reward Shop once the League ends.
So how many tasks are there?
More than you'll be able to complete, most likely. It's up to you which ones you attempt.
Thanks!
Now, would you like to take a look at the tasks for this League?
Is there anything else you need from me?
Relics are powerful artefacts that grant unique abilities for the entire League.
You may even recognise a few from an older RuneScape.
Relics are separated into tiers, where you can claim only one from each tier.
The first Relic tier is available to everyone. The others must be unlocked with League Points.
League Points are earned by completing tasks.
Once you have selected a Relic, you choice can't be changed for the rest of the League. Make your choices carefully.
Now, would you like to take a look at the relics for this League?
Is there anything else you need from me?
Relics are powerful artefacts that grant unique abilities for the entire League. You may even recognise a few from an older RuneScape.
Relics are separated into tiers, where you may claim only one from each tier.
The first Relic tier is available to everyone. The others must be unlocked with League Points, which are earned by completing tasks.
Blessings are powers and abilities unlocked by completing special combat tasks.
Each blessing is aligned with Order, Balance or Chaos.
As you unlock higher tier Blessings, the gods will cast their judgement on your choices, and new God Relics will be revealed to you.
Once you have selected a Relic, your choice can't be changed for the rest of the League. Make your choices carefully.
You will have limited to reset your choice of Blessings, should you wish to change your mind.
Now, would you like to take a look at the relics and blessings for this League?

conversations.section: Valluta's domain after The Void Stares Back

pages.x: Ah, my deliverer returns. Greetings, Player, mighty being.
I had some questions for you if you don't mind.
Please, by all means, ask Valluta, servitor of Guthix, what you will. I fear I know little outside of this chamber, but I shall answer as best I can.

o: Have you recovered from your draining?
Will there be a new queen in the Void?
Will the portals stop appearing now?

pages.x: What exactly are you?
I am Valluta, protector of weak places. I exist to guard this world against creatures from the Void and beyond.
It was Guthix, balancer of all scales, who placed me here, as he has placed so many other guardians against that which threatens his world.
In this spot is a weakening, a closeness of worlds, and those worlds can be brought into conjunction. I am to prevent this.
A job you performed less than admirably.
Player, strong in reproach, is right to berate me. Of late I have felt echoes, small pulls of duty, but to a place far away from here.
To where Grayzag was opening his portals on the islands in the southern seas...
I could not draw myself back quickly enough when the attack came. Packed around with the leech goo, I was reduced to uselessness as you saw.
Have you recovered from your draining?
My strength returns swiftly. Within the hour I shall be quite capable of performing my purpose again.
Good to hear. And what will you do now?
I shall return to my vigil here, and keep this doorway into our world protected from the pests, voracious and deadly, as Guthix demands of me.
Will there be a new queen in the Void?
Yes. There is always a queen.
And will the new one keep up the attack?
It was once that the queen, slave driver of pests, could not enter this world, for the weakening was too small. Now, I do not know.
I suspect not, and that she would need help again, but Grayzag, twisted and insane, is taken away and cannot help her.
In the event that she doesn't need help, or if someone else helps her...
Valluta, restored and contrite, stands ready.
It was Grayzag making the portals in the southern seas, so they'll stop appearing now, right?
This is not the case. The efforts of Grayzag, impetuous and ambitious, have forever damaged the boundaries on which the portals form.
I fear the brave Void Knights must continue their vigil still. They must be in future as they have been up to now: Valluta. Just as I am.
Just as you are, and the sword you carry.
Vall- Wait, you're saying that we're ALL the Valluta?
Valluta is simply what I am, what I do. Protector. Fortification. Guard against the Void. All who fought here today have done this. All who fought here are Valluta.
That's all, thanks.

conversations.section: Defending the gatehouse tutorial

pages.x: Okay, so here we are behind the gatehouse.
Your job is to keep the castle in tip-top shape. By doing so you keep the morale of our troops up, which means they kill more trolls.
So, repairing the gatehouse equals killing trolls!
First, let's take a look at your information screen in the upper-left - this is your most important tool. It will tell you the overall gatehouse health.
Let's get you supplies!
When you begin defending, we'll attempt to put all the supplies you need into your pack.
But, if there's not enough room, or you lose them, you can always pick up more here.
Looks like your oil levels are running low.
You can pick up extra buckets here, if you need them. Fill your buckets from the well of oil.
Be careful, for while having more oil is valuable to filling the drums, it'll also slow you down as it can quickly get heavy!
We'll go up to the top of the gatehouse to fill the oil drums.
Use the bucket on the oil drum to fill it.
My guards will take care of the rest!
Hmm, your ballista is destroyed! We'd better get that repaired - in the real fight you'll be rewarded with Crafting experience for this.
These parts build a ballista that keeps the trolls at bay. You'll have to build it first, then keep it repaired and the ammo lit.
Your information screen will keep you up to date.
Well, that's the easy jobs out the way. You'll also need to keep the gatehouse in good repair. Trolls will smash and throw rocks at anything they get near.
You need to repair walls and barricades with your trusty hammer.
You can see how many walls and barricades are broken on your information screen - fixing these in the real battle will award Construction experience.
If you start feeling overwhelmed, don't despair! Help is at hand.
As you repair the gatehouse, you will raise the morale of the troops and there is a chance you can build up morale points.
You can use this morale to call on extra help when things get dire.
Let's try one out now. We'll call in extra help to repair these walls and barricades.
Great! Extra help! These guys will make sure the broken things don't add to the castle's degrading health for the next 30 seconds.
Make sure to try out the other boosts and see what kind of strategy works for you.
Trolls also have some special attacks of their own that you'll no doubt find out about during the batt-Oh no! INCOMING!
We're okay, but that's going to cause a lot of damage to the gatehouse! Better make sure you keep things repaired in case of sneak attacks like that.
Trolls have some nasty things up there slee-,er, arms. Always be prepared!
One last thing. You can keep an eye on how many trolls have been killed, thanks to your help, on the information screen.
How many are killed related directly to the reward I'll give you, so work hard!

conversations.section: Talk-to / With a catspeak amulet / After All Fired Up and after A Tail of Two Cats

pages.x: Purrr! Hello there. Is there anything I can do for you?

o: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I'm done talking to you, now!

pages.x: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Purrrr. Sure! Just have a peep at this map of mine.
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
Well, I might be short, but I can see very far indeed. I can tell you how many beacons are lit in either direction.
However, if you want to know about beacons beyond that, I’ll need the help of a creature whose eyes are even keener than mine.
What sort of creature is that?
A creature that can view the world from above and which is smart enough to report back about what it has discovered.
Yes, but what sort of creature, exactly?
Purr…a macaw.
A macaw?
Yes, a yummy, delicious macaw. Purr.
You’re just trying to trick me into bringing you a snack, aren’t you?
No, no.
Sadly, if you brought me a macaw for the purpose of obtaining information about the beacons, my integrity as a fire tender would demand that I not make brunch of it.
How's it going?
All's well, life is peaceful, the flowers are blooming, the birds are singing and it's the most lovely of days today.
Wow, you seem very pleased about things!
I am! I'm so happy, I can't help but wag my tail and bound about recklessly!
It's nice to have such a high purpose in life and to have earned the trust and affection of such a noble human as King Roald.
Wait - you're a cat, right? Not a dog in disguise?
Uh, by 'wag my tail' I meant...um...'purr really loudly'. And, just for the record, I'm, uh, thoroughly indifferent to humans. And aloof. I'm very, very aloof.
That sounds more like it.
Say, you won't repeat what I said before, will you? I wouldn't want any more marks on my cat license.
Don't worry, moggy; your secrets are safe with me.
Purrrrrrr!
I'm done talking to you, now!
Happy trails! Purrr.

conversations.section: In Wendlewick / On a members' world

pages.x: Hello there, adventurer. Are you here to learn about the birds and the bees?
Excuse me?
I can help you with bird trapping and beekeeping. Wasn't that clear?

o: Do you have any beekeeping supplies?

pages.x: Tell me about birds.
Birds are a nuisance. They eat the bees, dig up seeds, and they don't half make some noise with incessant *chirp chirp*.
That's where birdbox trapping comes in! It's how me effectively manage it.
I can teach you if you like? It'd save me having to trek out down to the shrine and beyond every day to reset the traps. You'd be welcome to keep anything you find too.
Tell me more.
It's very easy to understand, you take a log of any type and a clockwork mechanism, craft it into a birdhouse trap, place it on a spot, then fill it with enough seed...
...come back a while later and *poof*. You've trapped yourself some birds, and if you're lucky some bird nests too.

o: Does the type of seed matter?
Does the type of wood matter?
Where can I find other birdhouse plots?

pages.x: Does the type of seed matter?
Not at all! For birds, all seeds are equal. Just a light sprinkling of say... one for your basic birdhouse.
Does the type of wood matter?
Only for experience gained! The better the wood, the better the house, the better the bird!
Higher quality houses will also require more seeds to fill, but also trap faster. You reap what you sow and all that!
Where do I get clockwork?
Craftable at a workbench in your house.
Alternatively, I'll sell you some, but at a premium.
Where can I find other birdhouse plots?
If you head east from here there are three dotted about Marigold Farm.
Then if you head south-east and you'll find another at Eastfold farm.
If you head south from there you can find one near the fairy ring and another at the shrine tender's house.
The final plot is to the west near Dalia's tree patches.
Do you have any beekeeping supplies for sale?
I do indeed!
I'm okay for now.
Ah, maybe another time.

conversations.section: In Pollnivneach / After The Feud

pages.x: Thank you once again. Have you spoken to Ali Morrisane yet?
Yes, I spoke to him already. That tourism idea of yours was really quite good.
Well not to be immodest, but it was all my idea. Well I have things to do, good luck adventurer.

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
For completing the Desert set, you are presented with an amulet.
This amulet will become increasingly useful as you complete greater difficulty levels.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all Tasks within a particular difficulty set, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Desert Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Desert Task rewards, speak to Hassan in Al Kharid Palace, Zahur in Nardah, the Golem in Uzer, or myself.
Desert amulet 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 25,000 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 50,000 coins.
No thanks.

conversations.section: Under White Wolf Mountain

pages.x: Oh, hello.
Hello, what's in those boxes?
Crossbows, are you interested?
Maybe, are they any good?
Are they any good?! They're dwarven engineering at its best!

o: How do I make one for myself?

pages.x: Well, firstly you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.
Wood fletched into stock... check.

Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.
Which goes with which?
Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials, Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamantite and Mahogany and finally Runite and Yew.
Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?
Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows.
You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.
What about magic logs?
Well.. I don't rightly know... us dwarves don't work with magic, we prefer gold and rock. Much more stable.
I guess you could ask the humans at the rangers guild to see if they can do something but I don't want anything to do with it!
Thanks for telling me. Bye!
Take care, straight shooting.
Thanks for telling me. Bye!
Take care, straight shooting.
What about ammo?
You can smith yourself lots of different bolts, don't forget to flight them with feathers like you do arrows though.
There's also the option of tipping any untipped bolt with gems then enchanting them with runes. This can have some pretty powerful effects.
Oh my poor bank, how will I store all those?!
Find Hirko in Keldagrim, he also sells crossbow parts and I'm sure he has something you can use to store bolts in.
Thanks for the info.
Thanks for telling me. Bye!
Take care, straight shooting.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Good day! What do you want to know about Group Ironman?

o: Tell me more about Group Ironman mode.
How do I create or join a group?
What are the different group rulesets?
Can I change my game mode?

pages.x: Group Ironman allows you to enjoy the Ironman experience as a group of 2 to 5 friends. You know, when you want to get away from it all, but do it with someone.
As you work together and grow, you can complete Journey Achievements.

Journey achievements are a set of objectives for the group to complete as individuals and as a group - you will need to level your skills, complete quests, kill bosses and explore all Gielinor has to offer.
Completing Journey Achievements will unlock rewards such as group storage, an upgradable cosmetic armour and unique pose emotes.
Or you can chart your own path and set your own goals as you experience a brand new type of adventure. The choice, as they say, is yours.
It's quite simple really! There are two options: you can either start your own group or be invited to an existing group.
If you want to create your own group, simply click the 'Create Group' option and then choose which ruleset you would like your group to be.
Once that's decided, you can then invite anyone you want to join your group. Each group can be between 2 and 5 players in size.
Each group can have their own unique name so pick one that best represents you.
Then you're ready to go! Confirm your group, and head over the bridge to the portal which will take you to Lumbridge to begin your adventure!
Don't forget to collect a set of armour from the stand next to me; it will provide you some initial protection from any enemies you may face.
There are two different rulesets that you can choose from: Competitive and Regular.
Competitive is a strict ruleset where you can only play with your group; this means all your progress and accomplishments come from within the group only.
In Competitive, a group can only be formed with those fresh to Gielinor so you can set out as a group to prove yourself as the best of the best.
Regular is a more relaxed ruleset that allows you to play with others outside your group, and there are no restrictions on leaving and joining other groups in the future.
Pick whichever mode best represents your group.
Competitive groups can choose to become a Regular group later; however a Regular group can never become a Competitive group once the group has been finalised.
Of course! What would you like to do?

o: Change to Standard mode (permanently leave Group Ironman mode).

pages.x: Very well. I will send you on to Burthorpe where my old friend, Turael, will be able to guide you from this point onwards.
Never means never! Are you sure you want to permanently prevent yourself from leaving Group Ironman mode?

o: Yes, I NEVER want to disable Group Ironman mode.
No, I want to be able to leave Group Ironman mode.

pages.x: Are you absolutely sure you want to permanently prevent yourself from leaving Group Ironman mode? This cannot be reversed.

o: Yes, I NEVER want to disable Group Ironman mode.
No, I want to be able to leave Group Ironman mode.
pages.i: Confirm never disabling Group Ironman mode?

pages.x: So be it, you will always remain a Group Ironman.
Thanks!
Farewell.

conversations.section: At Daemonheim

pages.x: Oh, hello, I didn't see...
Hey. I was wondering if you could help me?
Help? Uh...I'm not sure that I can...uh...

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Who are you?
I'm...I used to be...
Yes?
I just handle the...uh...equipment.
I mean, who are you? Like, what is your name?
A name? I...uh...

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: You are driving me crazy.
I'm sorry. I'm...
Yes?
They called me Ma...
Malcolm? Mandrake? Ma...um...Mango?
Uh, no, those aren't quite right.

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: You mentioned something about equipment?
Yes, I did, you're right. I sell things, mend things. What interests you?
You mentioned something about equipment?
Yes...uh...I did, you're quite right. I sell things, mend things. What interests you?

o: Let's see what you sell, then.
pages.i: What would you like to say?}}

pages.x: What exactly can you mend?
Weapons, I guess. I became good at mending in...there. If you buy something from me, I should be able to repair it if it's...uh...degraded.
Show it to me and I'll see what can be done.
I feel...like I can trust you. Let me tell you something: I have a friend in...there, someone who brings me tools and items from that place.
That is how I can offer you services that others...can't. Don't tell anyone. Please.
I'm done with you.
Fine, fine, fine. I'll be here.

conversations.section: Shifting Tombs / Afterwards

pages.x: Hey, how are things going down there? I haven't been able to find Amascut yet, nor the Kharid-ib, unfortunately.
I hope you're having better luck...or at least having fun!

o: Ozan: Any questions about these shifting tombs?
What are the statues and braziers for?

pages.x: In one word: opportunity! There is a wealth of knowledge and, more importantly, valuable trinkets in the tombs of long-dead pharaohs below us.
These tombs are magically warded to deter grave robbers, though, so you'll find that they are ever- changing.

There do seem to be a few constants, though - the most notable of which are sealed chests - each requires a certain skill to unlock, sometimes one which you might not have...but if someone else unlocks it first, you can search
it for your share of loot.
Also, there is a crystallised form of the corruption to mine through, and lots of urns that you should smash.
It may seem odd, but if you smash enough urns, you become empowered, and can mine through a lot of corrupt crystals very quickly!
Then there are sarcophagi, each sealed with a combination - inspect each sarcophagus carefully, then look for nearby panels to open it.
Finally, you'll need to find the exit. If you don't escape within the time limit, you'll lose out on some of what you found, as it gets lost to the corruption.
Oh, there's actually one last thing! You won't have time to do everything alone...so take others with you.
Together, you should be able to find everything, and everyone can share in the bounty. There is no downside for other people
helping you!
That's where you decide what sort of an experience you'll gain in the tombs.
Each of the four statues you activate will gain the favour of a lesser god, and you'll learn different things from them.
It's the same deal with the braziers in front of each statue, though to a lesser degree.
Those are for different skills that you'll gain less experience in, when within the tombs below.
The tombs will reward you more if you're higher levels in these skills too!
Don't just take my word for it, though. You should inspect each of the statues and braziers, and activate those of interest to you.
Yeah, whatever Amascut is doing down there, it's having some sort of corrupting effect. If we spend too long down there at one time, I fear it might affect us.
I wouldn't spend more than five minutes down there before coming back up for some fresh air.
More importantly, you need to find and use the exit BEFORE your time runs out, else you'll lose out on some of what you've found down there.
Will it affect me?
Hey, I'm sure you'll be fine - just don't risk it and put it to the test. Once your time is up, you can always just head straight back in.
Simply coming back to this area seems to be enough to clear any corruption that's attached itself to me.

conversations.section: In a player-owned house

pages.x: What can I do for you?
Can you take something to the bank for me?
Such tasks seem rather below a guard of the Queen's service, but I will do it. Give the item to me.
Here you go. Service worthy of a monarch, I must say.
You don't have any of those in your bank.
I'm afraid I can't go to the sawmill; I'd need extra insurance you see.
A most excellent choice! One cuppa, coming up.
Do you take milk with your tea?
Certainly.
Serve drinks please.
As long as everything is kept in order.
Can I offer you a drink?
Stay at the entrance and greet guests.
If you like. I am highly trained in greeting etiquette, after all.

pages.i: Do you really want to fire your servant?

pages.x: You're fired!
I shall return to my monarch. It has been a pleasure.
As a member of the Queen's Guard, I cannot be seen handling such... objects.
Excuse me mate, I don't work for free! If you want me to keep working for you, you'll need to pay me 500 coins.

o: Pay servant 500 coins and don't ask again.

conversations.section: In East Ardougne / Talking to him

pages.x: Hello Player, I'm Cromperty. Sedridor has told me about you. As a wizard and an inventor, he has aided me in my great invention!

o: Two jobs? That's got to be tough.
Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence?

pages.x: Two jobs? That's got to be tough.
Not when you combine them it isn't! I invent MAGIC things!

o: Well, I shall leave you to your inventing.

pages.x: Well, I shall leave you to your inventing.
Thanks for dropping by! Stop again anytime!
So what have you invented?
Ah! My latest invention is my patent pending teleportation block!
It emits a low level magical signal, that will allow me to locate it anywhere in the world, and teleport anything directly to it!
I hope to revolutionise the entire teleportation system! Don't you think I'm great? Uh, I mean it's great?

o: So where is the other block?

pages.x: So where is the other block?
Well... Hmm. I would guess somewhere between here and the Wizards' Tower in Misthalin.
All I know is that it hasn't got there yet as the wizards there would have contacted me.
I'm using the RPDT for delivery. They assured me it would be delivered promptly.
By all means! I'm afraid I can't give you any specifics as to where you will come out however. Presumably wherever the other block is located.
Who are the RPDT?
The RuneScape Parcel Delivery Team. They come very highly recommended. Their motto is: 'We aim to deliver your stuff at some point after you have paid us!'
Can I be teleported please?
By all means! I'm afraid I can't give you any specifics as to where you will come out however. Presumably wherever the other block is located.

o: Yes, that sounds good. Teleport me!
That sounds dangerous. Leave me here.

pages.x: Yes, that sounds good. Teleport me!
Okey dokey! Ready?
That sounds dangerous. Leave me here.
As you wish.
Well done, that's very clever.
Yes it is isn't it? Forgive me for feeling a little smug, this is a major breakthrough in the field of teleportation!
Can you teleport me to the Rune Essence?

conversations.section: At the entrance to the Lumbridge Catacombs / After The Blood Pact, before Heart of Stone

pages.x: Hello again, adventurer.

o: I've got a question about my adventure in the catacombs...
You weren't really wounded, were you?
What will happen in the catacombs now?

pages.x: Very perceptive, adventurer. I was wounded, but not as badly as I looked. I took the opportunity to see how you would fare.

o: You risked that woman's life for the sake of a test?
You risked my life for the sake of a test?

pages.x: I was prepared to step in and rescue her if you failed, but I won't always be that ready. That's why I had to do this. The world needs heroes.
I was a hero, once, but I'm not getting any younger. I need to make sure the news generation has its own heroes.

o: You risked that woman's life for the sake of a test?
You risked my life for the sake of a test?

pages.x: You're a born adventurer. I can practically smell it on you. People like you have a habit of coming back from things that would kill an ordinary person.

o: You risked that woman's life for the sake of a test?
You risked my life for the sake of a test?

pages.x: Very well indeed. You're a hero. You're exactly the sort of person the world needs. I'm glad I met you.

o: You risked that woman's life for the sake of a test?
You risked my life for the sake of a test?
What will happen in the catacombs now?

pages.x: Reese managed to complete the ritual with his own death. He's opened the staircase to the nest of undead creatures in the lower level of the catacombs.
Without a necromancer to control them, the creatures won't leave the tomb. I'll warn Father Aereck not to let people go down there. You're an adventurer, though.
If you want to, you can venture into the tomb and fight the creatures.

o: You weren't really wounded, were you?

pages.x: It's something Zamorakian cults do sometimes; a way of swearing loyalty to their leader.
A blood pact doesn't have real magical power, but that kind of thing can have great power over a person if they believe strongly enough.

o: You weren't really wounded, were you?
What will happen in the catacombs now?

pages.x: Dragith Nurn was a wizard. He studied at the Wizards' Tower, but he also studied the dar ark, necromancy, on his own. He had a secret magical workshop beneath Lumbridge.
He would steal bodies from the graveyard and perform experiments on them. Necromancy was like an addiction for him. When I met him he was very troubled; very conflicted.
I convinced him to put an end to it all.
He couldn't destroy all the undead he had created - not permanently - so he trapped them all in the lower level of his workshop and sealed it off.
He converted the upper level into these catacombs. Everyone thinks Dragith Nurn is buried here in the tomb, but he isn't.
He built the tomb to hide the entrance to the lower level. Dragith Nurn is still down there.
He knew that when he died he would rise again as a monster, so he sealed himself in with his creatures.

o: You weren't really wounded, were you?
What will happen in the catacombs now?

pages.x: Farewell, adventurer.

conversations.section: Before Kennith's Concerns

pages.x: Well hello there; welcome to our little village. Pray, stay awhile.

o: Can I buy some fishing supplies please?
You are a bit too strange for me. Bye.
You know, you sound just like the mayor?

pages.x: What do you do here?
I supply the local fishermen with the tools and bait they need to do their job.
Interesting. Have you been doing it long?
Why yes, all of my life. I took over from my father, who inherited the business from his father and so on.
In fact, there have been Lovecraft's selling bait for over ten generations.
Wow, that's some lineage.
Oh yes, we have a long and interesting family history. For one reason or another the Lovecraft's have always been bait sellers or writers.
Hmm, yes well. I'm sure it's all fascinating, but I...
Oh very, very fascinating, for instance my great grandfather Howard...
Yawn. Oh, I'm sorry but I really must be getting on. I think my giraffe needs feeding.
Your?
Giraffe. Sorry, but he gets cranky without enough sugar. Bye now!
Oh right, goodbye.
Can I buy some fishing supplies please?
You are a bit too strange for me. Bye.
Sniff. Yes, everyone says that.
You know, you sound just like the mayor?
Really? That's the nicest thing anyone has ever said. I admire him a great deal. He works so hard for this town.
You look like him as well?
Hmm, I don't think I do.
No really, what with the unhealthy skin tone and bulging eyes. The resemblance is uncanny.
Well, I haven't spoken to him in a while. I don't get out much.
I can see why.
Maybe the Mayor has finally seen how much I admire him and has grown to admire me?
Anything's possible I suppose. Wait a minute, you mean you've always looked that odd?
Hey, I resent that!
I'm sorry, it's just... Nevermind.

conversations.section: After King of the Dwarves

pages.x: Get to work! There's a blockage in channel [blocked channel].

o: What do I have to do here?

pages.x: What do I have to do here?
The lava here is only just above the rock's melting point.
In order to keep the lava flowing, we have to constantly mine the crust that forms on the edges of the channels.
You can mine anywhere you like, but there's usually a blockage in some segment or other, and you'll get experience more quickly from mining that segment.
You can find the blockage using the flow gauges. The lava flows more slowly near the blockages. There are a few...distractions that pop up from time to time.
You might want to keep an eye out for them. Any questions?

o: What do I get out of this?
How can I stand so close to the lava without being burned?

pages.x: What do I get out of this?
You get experience in mining! It's a great way to practise your pickaxe skills without having to carry an inconvenient load of rocks away afterwards.
What do you mean...distractions?
Firstly, ever since the latest chaos dwarf attack, the boilers have been playing up. If you spot one that's broken you can repair it with a hammer.
You might find it gives you Smithing experience. Secondly, there's the Liquid Gold Nymph. She's harmless; she just wants to dress everyone in new clothes.
If she gives you a gold pickaxe, I can remove the gold again if you decide you don't like it. Thirdly, the mine is...haunted.
Sometimes an ancestor spirit will grab someone's pickaxe. If you defeat the possessed pickaxe, it'll give you a boost to Mining experience in the mine for ten minutes.
Finally, watch out for a TzHaar hero and lava monster.
I still don't know what the monster did, but if you can delay it enough for the hero to catch it, everyone in the area will find more gems when mining here for ten minutes.
What's all this for, anyway?
This, my friend, is the power supply for the great city of Keldagrim!
Heat from the lava flows boils water in the pipes, and the power is transferred to all of the city's machinery. It's a marvel of the modern age! Just...marvellous!
How can I stand so close to the lava without being burned?
It's brilliant, isn't it? Just...brilliant! Logically, convection should make the air in this chamber hotter than an oven, and we'd all roast alive.
But for some reason that doesn't happen!
Goodbye.
Goodbye.
A fine day to be visiting Falador is it not? Welcome, ally!
Hello to you as well! What do you do here?
As the Falador herald, I've been put in command of keeping Falador a strong and mighty region within Gielinor.
My fighting days are behind me, but I can still conquer the hearts of the people with marching parades and our herald capes.

o: If you already have a Falador herald cape
If you don't have a Falador herald cape
If you have a herald cape from another city

pages.x: Oh, I already have one of those.
Splendid! You're doing Falador proud with this great service. Thank you, gracious madam! Would you like to customise your cape further?

o: Redirected to Falador Herald Cape customisation panel

pages.x: Herald capes? What are those?
Much as the White Knights dress alike for battle, we provide capes adorned with the lion of Falador to those we trust to show our might and valour to all of Gielinor!
We even allow you to customise your cape if you have been helpful to Falador in the past.
How about it, would you like to take a cape?
Sure, I'll take it!
Stupendous! Let's take a look at the customisations we can do...

o: Redirected to Falador Herald Cape customisation panel

pages.x: No thanks.
More's the pity. Well, I shall remain here until you inevitably return.
I already have a herald cape from another city, though.
Oh my. The Falador herald cape would look finer resting on your shoulders.
Naturally, I can offer to replace that herald cape with a much more respectable Falador herald cape.
Sure, I'll take it!
Stupendous! Let's take a look at the customisations we can do...

o: Redirected to Falador Herald Cape customisation panel

pages.x: No thanks, I'll keep the cape I have.
Wonders never cease! Well, I shall remain here until you return.

conversations.section: In Neitiznot

pages.x: Hi, (Player's Fremennik name), you should speak with Burgher Mawnis Burowgar in the main chambers. Do you have any questions?
Tell me about your husband.
Tell me about your husband.
My husband is a typical Fremennik, being both headstrong and brave.
We fell in love when we were young, but as there was a war between our isles, we were ordered to stop seeing each other by our parents.
This didn't stop Mord climbing the wailing tower, on his side of the channel between our isles, to sing to me every night.
After Mord's voice broke, his singing voice was lost, but I still listened to his terrible sonnets each and every night.
Until one night there was no singing! Then, far below me, I heard a gentle voice calling my name.
Mord had stolen his father's boat to come and fetch me from my prison and from that day forth we have lived in Rellekka.
Tell me about Jatizso.
Tell me about Jatizso.
My husband does not speak of the inhabitants of the isle of Jatizso much.
He has little positive to say about his parents, so he chooses not to speak of them in my presence.
The only thing I've noticed is that everyone on that island seems very sad...
Tell me about King Sorvott IV.
Tell me about King Sorvott IV.
King Sorvott IV follows in the footsteps of a line of kings who have reigned since Jatizso himself passed away.
It is rumoured that the King has no heir and is seeking a bride to bear him children. Given his personality I'm not surprised he hasn't found a bride yet!
What were you saying before?
Tell me about Neitiznot.
To be honest with you, I do not keep up to date with all the goings on here now that I have a home in Rellekka.
However, Neitiznot seems a happy place! The Burgher seems a wiser rule than King Sorvott, although I believe he is worried about the trolls at the moment.
They seem to be a big threat.
Can you ferry me to Rellekka?
Can you ferry me to Rellekka?
Sure.
I have nothing to ask you right now.
I have nothing to ask you right now.
Fare thee well.

conversations.section: Meeting Valdez

pages.x: Hello
H-Hello!
So what's up?
I cannot belive it! You can see me? You understand my words?
Sure can. So why are you hanging around here?
My tale is one of woe... No doubt you will have little interest in hearing it... Though it has been so many moons since last I had company in this endless non-life...
(Start of Curse of Zaros (miniquest))
Well, actually I would like to know what happened to you to turn you into an invisible ghost. If only so I can make sure it doesn't happen to me...
My name is Valdez. I served my Lord Saradomin faithfully for many years, as an explorer of this strange land we had been brought to.
I remember the day this curse fell upon me clearly... I had just discovered a huge temple, hidden below the ground, of one of Saradomin's compatriots.
I am unsure who had built it, or why they had left it seemingly abandoned, but inside I located a great treasure... It was the godstaff of Armadyl.
Oh, how I rue my choice that day!
Choice?
Aye, stranger. I chose that day to take it so that my Lord Saradomin's power and prestige could be increased by its possession. A god-weapon!
Do you have any comprehension of the difficulty and rarity in obtaining such a thing? To find such an artefact of power just lying around, it is almost inpomrehensible...
So it was there in that derested temple that I made my choice. I took the staff, and left that temple for Entrana immediately. This was the cause of my cursed state.
What, you mean you gave it to Saradmin and in return he cursed you??? Seems kind of ungrateful if you ask me...
No stranger, you misunderstand completely...

Firstly my gracious Lord would never treat anyone in such a manner; If he felt it was beyond my bounds as a mere mortal to hold such an artefact, he would simply have commanded me to return it to where I had claimed it, and I being eternallly loyal would have obeyed without question...
And secondly?
And secondly, I never managed to pass the artefact on to my Lord...
The vile thief Rennard accosted me as I made my way to Entrana, and after defeation me with a sneak attack, plundered the staff from my person, and left me for dead...
I do not know what became of the staff, but I can feel in my very bones that whatever its final fate was, it is somehow related to this curse upon me...
Wow. Tough break.
I am sorry to bore you with my tale stranger, please allow me to compound my rudeness by asking you for one favour, small to perform?
Eh, I won't make any promises, but if it's nothing too annoying I guess I can help you out.
Many thanks stranger, this existence tortures me...
I need you to find Rennard and if he has the staff yet reclaim it, or find out what hideous deed he performed to curse me so!
I have nothing I may offer you save this piece of clothing, please take it as a payment...

conversations.section: In the Falador Party Room / Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hi!
Hi! I'm Party Pete. Welcome to the Party Room!

o: What's the big lever over there for?

pages.x: So what's this room for?
This room is for partying the night away!
How do you have a party?
Get a few mates round, get the beers in and have fun! Some players organise parties so keep an eye open!
Woop! Thanks Pete!
What's the big lever over there for?
Simple. With the lever you can do some fun stuff.
What kind of stuff?
A balloon drop costs 1000 gold. For this, you get 200 balloons dropped across the whole of the party room. You can then have fun popping the balloons!
Any items in the Party Drop Chest will be put into balloons as soon as you pull the lever. When the balloons are released, you can burst them to get at the items!
For 500 gold, you can summon the Party Room Knights, who will dance for your delight. Their singing isn't a delight, though!
What's the gold chest for?
Any items in the chest will be dropped inside the balloons when you pull the lever.
Cool! Sounds like a fun way to do a drop party.
Exactly! A word of warning, though. Any items that you put into the chest can't be taken out again, and it costs 1000 gold pieces for each drop party.
I wanna party!
I've won the Dance Trophy at the Kandarin Ball three years in a trot!
Show me your moves Pete!

o: Why's there a chameleon in here?

pages.x: I love your hair!
Isn't it groovy? I liked it so much, I had extras made for my party goers. Would you like to buy one?
Why's there a chameleon in here?
Karma's my pet. I got him for Christmas one year. He keeps the Party Room free of flies, and he loves watching me dance. Karma karma karma cha...

conversations.section: At Pollnivneach / After Smoking Kills

pages.x: 'Ello, I am a Slayer Master now.

o: Do you have anything for trade?
I am here to discuss any rewards I might be eligible for.
I have some questions about your sister and the smoky dungeons.

pages.x: I need another assignment.
Do you have anything for trade?
I have a wide selection of Slayer equipment; take a look!

o: How do I earn co-op points to spend on rewards?
Where can I use the co-op food and potion rewards?

pages.x: You'll gain co-op reward points if you complete at least half of your contribution to a task with a friend.
That means you need to be in a group for most of the time you're working on the task, but it doesn't matter if your friend beats you to the majority of kills!
You'll still have been in a group for most of your contribution, so you're still entitled to a co-op reward point.

o: Where can I use the co-op food and potion rewards?

pages.x: The rewards can be used in most of the areas we commonly send you to complete your tasks.

o: How do I earn co-op points to spend on rewards?

pages.x: I have some questions about your sister.
There's not much to say. She's back in a safe place, where no one will see her again.
She started incinerating things when I freed her, and she said some pretty odd things. I'd prefer it if you gave me some answers.
Am I my sister's keeper? Some things must remain a mystery, known only to the gods.

o: I'd like to know about the inhabitants to the dungeons.
Why are you so shifty when I ask about your sister?
The barriers in the dungeon confuse me.
I'm not after anything, in fact.

pages.x: I'd like to know about the inhabitants to the dungeons.
They are monsters, so they are fit only for slaying. With no thoughts of an afterlife, they live a simple life of kill and be killed.
You should strive for such an existence, for therein lies happiness.
That's quite a grim philosophy.
Why are you so shifty when I ask about your sister?
Shifty? Me? I'm protecting her and leaving no clues to her location.
But why not tell me?
There has already been a kidnap attempt and there may be another. Now, I shall be silent, in case I reveal too much.
The barriers in the dungeon confuse me.
Well, they should be mostly passable. I weakened them for you after you rescued Jesmona. You should be able to sate your destructive appetite upon these creatures.
I'm not after anything, in fact.
Er...nothing...

conversations.section: Talking to him / After completing the tutorial

pages.x: Why hello, Portmaster.

o: I'd like to purchase some goods.
Why do you do what you do?
I'd better be going, things to do.

pages.x: Certainly, Portmaster. No questions asked.
I get a variety of goods from the Wushanko Isles. Goods that have fallen off the back of ships, that others have misplaced, that my contacts have picked up.
I can't guarantee what goods I'll bring here each day. These goods move quickly, my prices are so reasonable.
I'll bring you bamboo from the Arc region and Skull is overflowing with gunpowder.
I'll source mountains of slate from the Hook region and the Scythe is ripe with cherrywood. I'll sell you jade enough to build a palace, directly from the Bowl.
My contacts will even travel to the Pincers to bring you back steel that does not rust. But only if you can pay the price.
What's your price?
Western coin. I only accept western coin.
Well, if we are to work together, portmaster, I should secure your trust. Despite the trade I practise, I'm not a dishonest man.
The truth is almost always preferable to a lie. I once lived in New Heritage - one of the largest isles in the Pincer region. I was a well-off merchant.
I had a wife and two little girls. Slaved rarely ventured to the Pincer Region. The khans there are powerful - they have vast armies, soothsayers and ships.
The exiles and eastern slavers know better than to try their luck. But a ship of slavers did arrive.
Slavers from the west - who knows why they were so far out to sea, when few westerners even dared travel past the Arc.
I watched them pull my wife and my girls onto their ship. I could do nothing. I was just a merchant, and definitely no fighter. Months passed. I was sure they were dead.
I was...preparing...to join them. Then, I got a letter. A letter from their kidnappers. They were demanding coin in exchange for my family. Western coin.
A lot of western coin. I shut up shop immediately and set sail for the west with all my goods. I travelled only with my captain: Lily.
The oceans only know how we made the journey. I sold everything I had to raise the coin and left the money where they wanted it.
A few days later, I got another letter...asking for more coin. And so this pattern has gone on for years.
I pay their ransom and they send another letter, but what else can I do?
Have you considered that your family might be...
But how could I? Considering that would mean losing everything.
I work with a group of exiles: the Blazing Lantern clan. They are sailors who operate in the Wushanko Islands but who have rejected the rule of khans.
A westerner might call them pirates, but that would be a generalisation. The khans who rule the Wushanko Islands are chosen, mostly, for their skills on a ship.
Some men an women don't believe that's a just enough reason to rule. If your island is ruled by a cruel khan, the others won't intervene.
They'll let him operate as he wishes, unless he engages in open warfare. Only then will the other khans step in...and then the ocean boils.
We'll talk soon, Portmaster.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / After completing the Grand Exchange tutorial

pages.x: Hello. Is there anything with which I can help you?

o: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I'm done talking to you, now!

pages.x: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Oh, yes. Perhaps it would be easiest for me to show you on my map...
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I can tell you about the state of the beacons in either direction, up to the last fires that are lit.
I could probably tell you about the other beacons as well, but I'd need the help of a macaw.
A macaw?
Yes. Macaws have the ability to fly high into the air and see things that are much further away.
They are also highly intelligent and can be trained to provide the exact information I'd need for a complete overview of the beacon network.
How's it going?
Not bad, not bad.
So, what are you up to, this fine day?
Oh, the usual.
What's 'the usual'?
Well, I'm keeping close watch for signs of danger and I'm constantly scanning the horizon for the glow of other beacons.
Is that all you think about?
Oh, no. It's quite important to keep the mind active in a job like this. If you get lazy in your thinking, you might get lazy in your observation.
Intriguing... So, what do you think about to keep your mind active?
Oh, I suppose I mostly think about my stamp collection.
Mostly?
I also think about the birds I've seen lately.
Birds? You think about birds?
Yes. I am an avid ornithologist.
You like birdwatching, eh? You must see a lot of birds on the job!
Oh, quite. It's very convenient to have a hobby that integrates so well with one's career.
I'm done talking to you, now!
Then keep your voice down. You'll scare away the birds.

conversations.section: In Prifddinas / Talking to Afenen

pages.x: Gosh, it's a nice day! Now, can I help you with tool storage, or a trip to Winkin's Farm, or something else?
What can you store?
I can hold onto your rake, seed dibber, spade, secateurs, watering can and trowel - but not those trowels used for archaeology.
I can also store a few buckets and scarecrows for you, and even compost and supercompost.
Of course, compost is essential for good Farming, so I can store lots of that for you.
Also, if you hand me your Farming produce, I might be able to change it into banknotes.
So, would you like me to look after your Farming tools?

o: What do you do with the tools you're storing?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

pages.x: Yes, please.
What do you do with the tools you're storing? They can't all possibly fit in your pockets!
Of course not. I have a toolshed. It is rather a curious shed, though. Sometimes, items just seem to appear in there.
So, would you like me to look after your tools?

o: No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

pages.x: Yes, please.
What can you store?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.
Well, I shall be here if you ever decide that I may be of service.

o: Can you take me to Winkin's Farm?

pages.x: Can you take me to Winkin's Farm?
Actually, I'm fine.

o: Aren't you a bit tall for a leprechaun?

pages.x: Aren't you a bit tall for a leprechaun?
I'm not a leprechaun! Why would you ask such a strange question?
Well, you're looking after tools like leprechauns do.
I'm of the Crwys clan. We have a special affinity with nature. It is my duty and pleasure to tend this farming patch.
So, would you like me to look after your Farming tools?

o: No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

conversations.section: In Pollnivneach, before Our Man In The North / After Enakhra's Lament

pages.x: Good day, sir. Are you interested in the history of this area?

o: Yes, I want to know more about the desert!
Why should I care about what happened thousands of years ago?

pages.x: Yes, I want to know more about the desert!
It's good to meet someone so eager to learn.
Now, what would you like to hear about?
Tell me about Enakhra the Mahjarrat.
I have read only little about her. She was one of the Mahjarrat who arrived in Gielinor many thousands of years ago.
She supported Zamorak when he tried to gain power, but her efforts to gain his favour failed, and she retreated to a temple she had built.
This is the last anyone knows of what happened to her, and it took place several thousand years ago.
Tell me about Akthanakos the Mahjarrat.
Like Enakhra, his rival, Akthanakos came to Gielinor with the other Mahjarrat. He took on the aspect of one of the local gods, and is usually drawn with a camel's head.
He was against Zamorak's rise to power, but the last anyone knows of him was that he and Enakhra were thinking of forgetting their rivalry.
Tell me about Enakhra's temple.
Well, sources say that Enakhra tried to gain favour with Zamorak by building him a temple somewhere in the desert.
It is said that when she showed it to him, he was not impressed, and told her he would rather have a weapon that could slay gods than a temple.
After that, it seems Enakhra retreated to that temple. If she hasn't died, she's been there ever since.
Tell me about the Camulet.
I'm afraid I've only heard rumours of it, but here's what I know.
When Akthanakos came to Gielinor and took on the aspect of a man with a camel's head, he made an amulet that allowed him to understand camels.
Using it, he even trained some of the native camels to fight for him. Their name, "Ugthanki", is derived from his.
Since he disappeared, however, it is said that the Ugthanki became more violent, and started attacking travellers.
Why should I care about what happened thousands of years ago?
Because those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it.
Knowing something about history can prevent you from making mistakes that people have made before, you see?
Who are you?
I am a librarian from the great library of Menaphos. I left to travel the desert and learn more of its history.
Unfortunately, the plague of Sophanem prevents me from returning to the library.

conversations.section: After Animal Magnetism / Talk to

pages.x: Hello again; I'm busy with my newest research, so can't gossip too much. Are you after information, an upgrade, another device or would you like to see my goods for sale?

o: I seem to need a new device.
I'd like to upgrade my device, please.
I'd like to see your stuff for sale, please.
I'll just head off, I think.

pages.x: I'd like information, please.
Just a few bits of information before you run away to persecute rock crabs or cows.
Firstly, your new device won't work if you are wearing certain metallic chest armours.
The magnetic attraction required for operation would cause feedback, so the device does not allow such incompatible item equippage.
Secondly, although the device is calibrated to attract only arrowheads, there is a chance that other magnetically active items will be attracted.
The arrow recovery function of the devices is slightly different and relies upon a harmonic bond between your arrows and the chicken's magnet.
You'll thus only recover arrows which you have fired rather than those fired by nearby folks.
You'll also need to move about if you want to collect arrows since the gathering of long-lost arrowheads can't work otherwise.
Finally, the device will only work when worn. It automatically deactivates in other circumstances.
I was worried about what would happen if you were to place it in a bank in its active state, so I've made sure it only works when it's on your back.
I need another arrow-attracting device, please.
Well, luckily for you, they have a habit of returning to me when people lose them, so I have some spares. They are homing chickens, it seems.
I'll need 999 gp, however, for the expenses involved in restoring the poor creature to health, or unhealth, or whatever.
Why 999?
Well, it just sounds less expensive than 1000. Do you want that replacement or not.
Sounds good to me.
I'd prefer not to, actually.
I've better things to do than be irritated by you.
I'd like to upgrade my device, please.
I'd like to see your stuff for sale, please.
Here's my shop.
I'll just head off, I think.
Thanks for the help with my bed; see you again.

conversations.section: At Senntisten Temple / After Heart of Stone / Telling him information

pages.x: I hear you have news on the elder gods?
I discovered a number of living statues that referred to themselves as the mouthpieces of the elder gods. They referred to themselves as Kra, in Tzhaar language.
Fascinating, well found. Where did you find them?
FulKra was found under the Karamjan volcano.
Yes, that makes sense. My research indicates that Ful was closeley affiliated with with the early Tzhaar.
BikKra was found under Entrana.
No accounting for taste, still I imagine those detestable monks came later.
WenKra was found under White Wolf Mountain.
Really? Not where I imagined...which could me more concerning than you might think.
Care to explain?
In time Player, in time. Where were we?
JasKra was found in the Kharidian Desert, east of Sophanem.
Interesting. My studies had suspected as much. Still that's all of them accounted for now yes?
There was one more chamber. In Lumbridge, beneath the catacombs.
But Mah never made it to Gielinor... Unless...No, best not to leap to speculation just yet.
So now we have a starting point, something that may help us find the Elder Halls.
Did you learn anything else?
Xenia was trying to drain the anima mundi from the mouthpieces. She wanted to siphon it off Gielinor.
What? What madness? Where was she siphoning it?
Into the Abyss.
Stupid woman, the consequences...
According to an ancient abyssal entity, she may have set in motion something terrible.
They could already be waking up because of her actions? So time is no longer an ally. We must redouble our efforts.
Did you learn anything else?
I befriended an intelligent golem that learns over time. It was able to track down energy traces and lead us to the mouthpieces.
A most remarkable tool, perhaps we can turn him to our mission?
Did you learn anything else?

conversations.section: After Ali the Trader / When the blackjack seller is selling defensive blackjacks

pages.x: Hello. Could I interest you in a blackjack?
Ah, it's you again Player. Tell me how are the blackjack sales going?
Not too bad, Ali was well impressed by the reaction and demand they had initially but he's a little concerned about how the sales have dropped off of recent.
Maybe you could produce a different range of products?
I'm not too sure, I'm quite happy to stick with what I've got unless, I had a good reason to change.

o: I bet you couldn't knock me out with your blackjack.
Hmmm... I'll get back to you on this.

pages.x: I bet you couldn't knock me out with your blackjack.
I reckon I could.
I'll tell you what, if you can't knock me out with one blow, you should make better blackjacks.
Nah, I don't like the sounds of that. It leaves a lot up to chance.
Ok, ok, how about two blows to the head?
Are you sure? I could possibly kill you?

o: Umm... on second thoughts I might give it a skip.
I'm sure. No gain no gain. Grr!

pages.x: Phew! At last the voice of reason speaks.
Now if you don't mind I'll be getting back to work. Thank you.
I'm sure. No gain no gain. Grr!!
You adventurers are crazy.
Pah, you didn't even draw blood.
You really are truly mad.
Are you going to hit me again? I really want to get this over with.
Yeeeoouch... that hurt! I'm still standing though. You can't knock me down.
Either your head is thicker than it looks or else I need to rework my blackjack.
Umm... definitely the blackjack.
I suppose I'll have to modify the blackjack so that it has a better attack.
So I take it you will be supplying Ali Morrisane with the new variety of blackjack then?
Yes, yes. I'll start shipping it by carpet as soon as the first batch is ready.
Hmmm... I'll get back to you on this.

conversations.section: Talk to / After Shadow of the Storm

pages.x: I regret that I could not assist you in the slaying of Agrith Naar.
Don't worry, golem! You've done enough demon-slaying in your time.

o: Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and may count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this area.
For completing the Desert set, you are presented with an amulet.
This amulet will become increasingly useful as you complete greater difficult levels.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim these rewards?
You need to complete all Tasks within a particular difficulty set; then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Desert Tasks are simple, some require certain skill levels, and others require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your desert set rewards, speak to Hassan in Al Kharid Palace, Zahur in Nardah, Hakeem the Mayor in Pollnivneach or myself.
Desert amulet 1? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 1,500 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 2? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 7,500 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 3? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 25,000 coins.
No thanks.
Desert amulet 4? Yes, but I'm afraid it would cost you 50,000 coins.
No thanks.

conversations.section: Talk to / Until the end of last Sunday with Santa's visit

pages.x: 'Ello 'ello 'ello!

o: What can I get from here?
Do you have anything for me?

pages.x: What's happening here?
Why, this is Santa's Lodge!
Every week. The big man 'imself will come 'ere to hand out presents in person to those deserving.
As long as you've been nice, and 'ave Nice Points to prove it, he'll have some'tin for you each week.
On top of that, the nicer you are, the better chances you'll have at getting his special gift. A black partyhat!
To gain Nice Points, yous need to deliver letters to Santa.
For every 3 letters you post, yous get 1 Nice Point.
Find letters and post 'em in Santa's postbox.
Yous can get 3 letters for each day of the Christmas festivities.
I's will give yous one every day, if yous ask nicely that is.
Yous can get one each day from the activities in the Christmas Village.
The final one yous can get is from doing all 3 of yous Daily Challenges.
If yous miss any days, yous can always catch back up by buying letters from Holly on the other side of the bridge.
She drives a hard bargain so I's suggest getting them when they be free.
What can I get from here?
Gifts!
Okay... Can you tell me any more, or is it a surprise?
Well...
Santa really needs 'is letters delivered.
As such, each letter yous deliver, yous get a present to say thanks.
Then, with the nice points yous get for delivering those letters, Santa will bring yous more gifts.
Each week that you have a Nice Point, he will bring you a guaranteed gift.
Then for each Nice Point, yous has a chance at getting a black partyhat.
Do you have anything for me?
Goodbye!
See ya soon!

conversations.section: In Prifddinas / Talking to Eirlys

pages.x: Gosh, it's a nice day! Now, can I help you with tool storage, or a trip to Winkin's Farm, or something else?
What can you store?
I can hold onto your rake, seed dibber, spade, secateurs, watering can and trowel - but not those trowels used for archaeology.
I can also store a few buckets and scarecrows for you, and even compost and supercompost.
Of course, compost is essential for good Farming, so I can store lots of that for you.
Also, if you hand me your Farming produce, I might be able to change it into banknotes.
So, would you like me to look after your Farming tools?

o: What do you do with the tools you're storing?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

pages.x: Yes, please.
What do you do with the tools you're storing? They can't all possibly fit in your pockets!
Of course not. I have a toolshed. It is rather a curious shed, though. Sometimes, items just seem to appear in there.
So, would you like me to look after your tools?

o: No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

pages.x: Yes, please.
What can you store?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.
Well, I shall be here if you ever decide that I may be of service.

o: Can you take me to Winkin's Farm?

pages.x: Can you take me to Winkin's Farm?
Actually, I'm fine.

o: Aren't you a bit tall for a leprechaun?

pages.x: Aren't you a bit tall for a leprechaun?
I'm not a leprechaun! Why would you ask such a strange question?
Well, you're looking after tools like leprechauns do.
I'm of the Crwys clan. We have a special affinity with nature. It is my duty and pleasure to tend this farming patch.
So, would you like me to look after your Farming tools?

o: No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.
