conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Ello there. I'm Gamfred, the engineer in this here guild. Have you seen my catapult?

o: That's not a catapult, it's a large crossbow.

pages.x: That's not a catapult, it's a large crossbow.
WHAT!? I'll have you know that is the finest piece of dwarven engineering for miles around! How DARE you insult my work!
Yes, beautiful piece of engineering.
Nice to meet someone who appreciates fine work, have you tried it out yet?

o: No, how do I do that?

pages.x: Yes.
What did you think?

o: May I have a shield please?

pages.x: It was ok I guess.
Well I guess not everyone will like it.
It was fun!
Glad ta hear it. Try it again sometime. We have more tests to run.
I didn't like it.
Well I guess not everyone will like it. But give it another chance before you go.
May I have a shield please?
No, how do I do that?
Well ye take the big defence shield in both hands and watch the catapult. My assistant will fire different things at you and you need to defend against them.
To see what might be coming your way and which defensive mode to choose, see the poster on the wall.

o: May I have a shield please?

pages.x: May I have a shield please?
Sounds boring.
Your loss...
No, where is it?
Are ye blind lad/lass? Tis over there in the next room with me assistant working it!
Bye!
Come back soon! My catapult needs more test subjects.

conversations.section: In Keldagrim marketplace / Talking to Hirko

pages.x: Hello there!
Hello, what's in those boxes?
Aha, interested in my crossbows are you?
Are they any good?
They're dwarven engineering at its best. If you've got enough skill in crafting, smithing and fletching, you can even make them yourself.
You can buy some of the parts here and make the rest yourself.

o: How do I make one for myself?

pages.x: How do I make one for myself?
Well, firstly you'll need to chop yourself some wood, then use a knife on the wood to whittle out a nice crossbow stock like these here.
Wood fletched into stock... check.

Then get yourself some metal and a hammer and smith yourself some limbs for the bow, mind that you use the right metals and woods though as some wood is too light to use with some metal and vice versa.
Which goes with which?
Wood and Bronze as they're basic materials, Oak and Blurite, Willow and Iron, Steel and Teak, Mithril and Maple, Adamant and Mahogany and finally Rune and Yew.
Ok, so I have my stock and a pair of limbs... what now?
Simply take a hammer and smack the limbs firmly onto the stock. You'll then need a string, only they're not the same as normal bows.
You'll need to dry some large animal's meat to get sinew, then spin that on a spinning wheel, it's the only thing we've found to be strong enough for a crossbow.
What about magic logs?
Well.. I don't rightly know... us dwarves don't work with magic, we prefer gold and rock. Much more stable.
I guess you could ask the humans at the rangers guild to see if they can do something but I don't want anything to do with it!
Thanks for telling me. Bye!
What about ammo?
You can smith yourself lots of different bolts, don't forget to flight them with feathers like you do arrows though.
There's also the option of tipping any untipped bolt with gems then enchanting them with runes. This can have some pretty powerful effects.
Oh my poor bank, how will I store all those?!
Don't you worry, I have just the thing here, a bolt pouch designed specially for holding 4 different types of crossbow bolt.
Wow, how much?
Take care, straight shooting.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Imp-in-a-box (2)

pages.x: Hey imp, can you hear me?
Of course I can hear ya, ya great big ape. You know, 'veres not even enuf space to swing Bob about in 'ere. How about a breather? You know, stretch me pins for a bit?

o: No, I'm going to keep you in there.

pages.x: No, I'm going to keep you in there. I might keep you as a pet.
Pet!! Nah mate. I fink you'd find dat you'd be my pet!! We is not makin good pets.
Really? Why not?
Coz...errr...
We bite! Yeah we is biting and...and...er...
We is fire risk! Yeah dat's it! We be burning down your housey and stealin' all ya shiny gems. Oh, and da beads!! Mmmm, beads.
Fire risk? How does that work?
Is those wizzies. Dey don't like de imps so dey make us go BOOOM!!
It's not that bad. You've got four big windows, charming company...er...
Yeah, we's love tiny, crampt space. It be magical. But I is a busy imp, innit? Dragons needin' ticklin', shiny relics needin' stealin', you know how it goes.
So, if you's know whas good for ya, you'd be lettin' me go, right?
Don't I get three wishes?
Nah, mate. Dunno what you're chirpin' about.
Well, you're a magical creature aren't you? Surely I get some wishes for capturing you, or releasing you, or something?
I'm finking dat you be a bit confoosed. I is an imp, not some namby-pamby genie or some kinda fairy. Ye can tell by the horns.
Sayin' dat, I don't fancy being cooped up like one of me uncle's pigeons. Tell you what, is there anything you need deliverin' to the bank?
I may not be no cunjerer or sommink like dat, but I can get about nice
an quick like. If you let me scarper, I'll take a couple of fings to the bank for ya. You game?

o: Surely it should be three items?
I've got nothing I need banking right now.

pages.x: Okay, that sounds fair.
Surely it should be three items? Then it's one item per wish.
I've already told ya, I ain't no bloomin' fairy. Besides, you know wot dey say, three's a crowd innit? I don't fink I can hop about carryin' more dan 2 fings.
I've got nothing I need banking right now.
Great, just blinkin great, dat is. I'll just sit about countin' zombie sheep then. One...two...two and a bit...three and a bit more...
I don't fink sheep 'ave dat many legs...

conversations.section: In Prifddinas, after Plague's End / Standard dialogue

pages.x: It's wonderful, isn't it? The crystal spires of Prifddinas...it's more beautiful than I could've dreamed. The stories didn't do it justice.

o: Ask about Lady Ithell and her clan...
Can you make me a crystal hatchet, pickaxe or mattock?
Is there anything I can do for you?
Is there anything else I can help you with?

pages.x: Give me a dragon hatchet, pickaxe or mattock to upgrade, and at least 4,000 harmonic dust, and I'll see what I can do.
If you're looking to upgrade an augmented tool, you'll need to show me that directly.
Well, there is one little favour you could do for me...
You see, the previous Lady Ithell pursued a research project late in her life.
I'm not sure if she ever finished it - she imbued the statue schematic with her memories quite a time before she died.
The version of Lady Ithell in my mind had only just taken the first steps on a long journey of discovery.
She was looking for a way to stabilise crystals, so they do not degrade with use. I want to continue her work.
So what's the favour?
I need crystal seeds. Depleted seeds. As many as possible. Just to study them, you understand - you can collect your crystal seeds any time you like.
Seeds with charges won't do?
No, they need to be reverted to their most basic seed form.
Lady Ithell was sure there's some inhibitor in the basic nature of the seeds - these tiny fragments of Seren - that limits their potency.
Oh, Lady Hefin would throw a fit if she heard me talk that way about Seren. I'm sure Seren wouldn't deliberately restrict her chosen people.
Still, there's incredible power in the crystal seeds, and I believe through crystal singing we're barely tapping their true potential.
So, will you let me look after your crystal seeds?

o: Tell me again why you need crystal seeds.

pages.x: The previous Lady Ithell pursued a research project late in her life.
I'm not sure if she ever finished it - she imbued the statue schematic with her memories quite a time before she died.
The version of Lady Ithell in my mind had only just taken the first steps on a long journey of discovery.
She was looking for a way to stabilise crystals, so they do not degrade with use.
Lady Ithell was sure there's some inhibitor in the basic nature of the crystal seeds that limits their potency.
I want to continue her work, and unlock our full potential.
To do that, I need depleted crystal seeds, reverted to their most basic seed form. As many as possible.
Just to study them, you understand - you can collect your crystal seeds any time you like.
So, do you have any crystal seeds you'd like to loan to me?

o: Tell me again why you need crystal seeds.

conversations.section: Talk to / Only on the first time

pages.x: Hello there, I don't think I have seen you around here before.

o: The stranger looks you up and down.

pages.x: No. You have not.
Well, what brings you to this part of the world?
I am waiting for an individual of some talent of creation.
I have made some things in my time, maybe I could be of some help.
Hmmm. From what I have seen of you around here I think you might be of some use.
Excellent, I always do like to help...
Wait. What do you mean that you've seen of me? I haven't seen you anywhere but here.
Come now. Sight is not necessarily a symmetric relationship. Now back to the matter at hand.
I know of your talents, honed in the cave behind me and I would be willing to commission some work from you.
Oh, that might be a bit problematic, as my inventions run off...
Yes yes, burning the torn memories of a dead god for your own ends.
How very resourceful and ethical of you.
An event, which some would say, was your fault.
That's not what happened!
I tried to save them.
I failed.
It matters not, the result was the same.
Regardless, my powering of such items is not your concern.
If you say so...
So what are you after?
Well, I find that when I drop coins into my coin pouch it makes quite the noise.
I would like it to be quieter.
I have some ideas for how to do that...
...and what else that might be useful for...
Excellent. I eagerly await your return with the requested item.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Greetings, child. What brings you to my humble home?

o: Can you tell me more about Ashdale?

pages.x: Magda is my name - Magda the mystic, as some call me. I see things others cannot.
And I see much potential in you, my child.
This ruin has been my home for many years. No doubt it seems basic to you, but it serves me well, and no-one seems to mind my living here.
Ashdale was built over 400 years ago, which is a small span compared with some of Gielinor's more ancient settlements.
So far it has played no part in the conflicts of mortals and gods, but I suspect that may be about to change.

o: Can you tell me more about Gielinor?
Can you tell me more about the gods?
I'd like to ask about something else.

pages.x: Gielinor is a large place, my child, and I know little of what lies east of Morytania or west of Prifddinas, but I will tell you what I can.

o: What can you tell me about eastern Gielinor?
What can you tell me about western Gielinor?
What can you tell me about central Gielinor?
I'd like to know more about the gods.
I'd like to ask something else.

pages.x: The east of Gielinor is home to the desert lands, Morytania, and Daemonheim.
The desert lands contain the ruins of ancient civilisations and strange beasts found nowhere else in Gielinor.
Daemonheim is the site of an ancient fortress, beneath which lurk all manner of foul creatures.
As for Morytania, it is a dark and dangerous place, and many who venture there do not return.
The west of Gielinor is probably the most diverse part of the mainland, home to elves, gnomes, dwarves, and barbarians, among others.
Unfortunately, these races do not always get along, and the west is often a place of conflict.
Central Gielinor contains the great cities of Falador and Varrock, and a vast desolation known as the Wilderness.
The civilised lands are mostly safe, and contain many opportunities for adventure, but the Wilderness can be a dangerous place.
There are a great many gods, but Saradomin, Zamorak and Guthix are perhaps the most notable.

o: What can you tell me about Saradomin?
What can you tell me about Zamorak?
What can you tell me about Guthix?
I'd like to know more about Gielinor.
I'd like to ask about something else.

pages.x: Saradomin represents order and wisdom. Most of those who live here worship him, and the church that stands to the east was built in his name.
When the way was opened for the gods to return to Gielinor, Saradomin was the first to do so.
His followers see him as a kind figure, but history has shown that it is unwise to anger him.
Zamorak is a chaos god, and is often perceived as evil, but like all gods he is a complex being with many sides to his personality.
He was one of the first gods to return to Gielinor, when it became possible for them to do so.
Of all the younger gods, it is Zamorak who most desires power, and that is why he seeks the Stone of Jas - the most powerful of all the Elder Artefacts.
Goodbye, my child.
Goodbye, my child.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello, and welcome to the Crafting Guild. Accomplished crafters from all over the land come here to use our top notch workshops.

pages.i: What would you like to ask?

pages.x: The upper landing of the crafting guild has everything you need to tailor armour.
In brief, you spin plant fibres into thread at a spinning wheel, then weave the thread into cloth at the loom.
Next, choose a design for your cloth at the pattern table, draft your project at the drafting table, and finish it at a tailor's dummy.
When you've fully upgraded your armour, you can adorn a full set on the tailor's display. It's an admirable experience.
But first, you'll need seeds to plant in flower patches to get the flowers you'll spin into thread.
I don't know much about starblooms. You might be able to find out more at the Wizards' Tower's big telescope.
Alright, I'll ask Wizard Rosalina. It might have something to do with shooting stars.
Another thing you might like to try is crafting and enchanting platinum jewellery.
If you're really good at crafting, you could also have a crack at masterwork magic armour. You can find the recipe on the pattern table beside me.
Remember, cloth on a loom. Thread on a spinning wheel. As for stones of binding, maybe try the Wizards' Guild in Yanille.
And you'll need tectonic and praesulic essence to start crafting pearlescent plates. Platinum normally wouldn't be suitable for armour, but imbuing negates that.
If you've got a fully equipped set of trimmed melee masterwork, masterwork ranged or masterwork magic, I can custom fit it for you.
If it's augmented it'll remain augmented and you'll repair it the same way you repair trimmed masterwork.
What does custom-fitting do?
It will become untradeable.
It will degrade 50% slower so it'll last longer.
It will also never degrade when damaged by your current Slayer/Reaper target.
But the process is irreversable. Once custom fitted, your masterwork will always be custom fitted.

o: I've noticed there are a couple of versions of each skillcape.

pages.x: Yes! We, the skill masters, have crafted new versions of all skillcapes! We felt like it was time for a change.

o: Yes, I would like to wear the [new/old] version of the skillcape.

pages.x: Would you like to wear the [old/newer] model for just this cape, or for the Quest Cape and all of the skillcapes you own?

o: I would just like to change the Crafting skillcape.
I would like to change all my skillcapes.

pages.x: No problem, you will now use the [older/newer] model for your Crafting skillcape.
No problem, you will now use the [older/newer] model for all of your skillcapes!
Great! I'm glad you're still enjoying the [old/new] version!

conversations.section: After Dwarf Cannon

pages.x: Hello.
Hello traveller, how's things?
Not bad thanks, yourself?
I'm good, just working hard as usual...

o: I was hoping you might sell me a cannon?
Well, take care of yourself then.
I want to know more about the cannon.

pages.x: I was hoping you might sell me a cannon.
Hmmmmmm... I shouldn't really, but as you helped us so much, well, I could sort something out. I'll warn you though, they don't come cheap!
How much?
For the full setup, 750,000 coins. Or I can sell you the separate parts... but it'll cost extra!
That's not cheap!

o: Okay, I'll take a cannon please.
Can I look at the separate parts please?
Sorry, that's too much for me.
Have you any ammo or instructions to sell?

pages.x: Okay, I'll take a cannon please.
Okay then, but keep it quiet... This thing's top secret!
Can I look at the separate parts please?
Of course!
Sorry, that's too much for me.
Fair enough, it's too much for most of us.
Have you any ammo or instructions to sell?
Of course!
Well, take care of yourself then.
Indeed I will adventurer.
I want to know more about the cannon.
There's only so much I can tell you, adventurer. We've been working on this little beauty for some time now.
Is it effective?
It short bursts it's very effective, the most destructive weapon to date. The cannon automatically targets monsters close by. You just have to make the ammo and let rip.
I've lost my cannon.

pages.x: Gosh, it's a nice day! Now, can I help you with tool storage, or a trip to Winkin's Farm, or something else?

I can hold onto your rake, seed dibber, spade, secateurs, watering can and trowel - but not those trowels used for archaeology.
I can also store a few buckets and scarecrows for you, and even compost and supercompost.
Of course, compost is essential for good Farming, so I can store lots of that for you.
Also, if you hand me your Farming produce, I might be able to change it into banknotes.
So, would you like me to look after your Farming tools?

o: What do you do with the tools you're storing?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

pages.x: Yes, please.
What do you do with the tools you're storing? They can't all possibly fit in your pockets!
Of course not. I have a toolshed. It is rather a curious shed, though. Sometimes, items just seem to appear in there.
So, would you like me to look after your tools?

o: No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

pages.x: Yes, please.
What can you store?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.
Well, I shall be here if you ever decide that I may be of service.

o: Aren't you a bit tall for a leprechaun?

So, would you like me to look after your Farming tools?

o: No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander, before The Mighty Fall / Casting NPC Contact / Zanik and Evil Dave

pages.x: Hello?
Player?
I’m contacting you by magic!
Hey, Player, do you know someone called Evil Dave? He’s telling me about his plan for world domination, but I’m not sure if he’s being serious.

o: He’s an evil wizard! You’ve got to stop him!

pages.x: He’s an evil wizard! You’ve got to stop him!
Okay, I’ve got this. Stop right now, Evil Dave! If you want to conquer the world, you’ll have to get past me first! He’s casting a spell, Player!
He’s made a magic circle and he’s going to summon something! I have to disrupt the magic somehow!

o: Make him get the words wrong!
Just let him cast the spell.

pages.x: Make him get the words wrong!
Abracadabra! Oogle-boogle, shazam! That’s confused him. He’s made a mistake. Something’s appearing… It’s …A cabbage? Oh.
Evil Dave is taking it up to his mum to make into dinner. I think he’s given up his evil plans for now.
Disrupt the magic circle!
There! The circle’s broken! Something is still happening, though… Evil Dave has turned himself into a fish! He’s flopping around and- Oh, he’s turned back.
He says he’s going to go and have a lie down. I think his evil plans are foiled for the time being.
Just let him cast the spell.
Well, okay. He’s finished the spell. Something’s emerging… It’s a rat! A little red rat with glowing eyes! Aww, it’s cute. It’s eating some cheese out of my hand.
Evil Dave is so disappointed. He says he was sure he’d get it right this time.
I think he’s harmless.
Really? He’s asking me to join his evil scheme. He says I could be his ‘Evil Death-Bringer Assassin of Darkness’.

o: You’d make a great assassin of darkness.
You’re not going to join him, are you?

pages.x: You’d make a great assassin of darkness.
Ha! I bet I would.
I’d stand on a rooftop, wrapped in a black cloak, a crossbow bolt glinting in the moonlight as my target moved unsuspecting below… Um, if I were evil, of course.
Which I’m not. I think I’ve hung around with Evil Dave long enough. I’ll talk to you some other time, Player.
You’re not going to join him, are you?
Of course not. You won’t catch me being part of any evil scheme! Well, except that one time, of course. But I don’t want to talk about that.
Anyway, I think I should leave Evil Dave to his schemes. I’ll see you around, Player.

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander, before The Mighty Fall / Casting NPC Contact / Zanik in Morytania

pages.x: Hello?
Player? Where are you? I can’t see you in the swamp.
I’m contacting you by magic!
I’m exploring Morytania and… Woah! I’m slipping! Wo-o-oah!
Zanik? Are you alright?
I’ve fallen in the swamp! What should I do, Player?

o: Try to swim to the bank!

pages.x: Grapple out with your crossbow!
Okay, I’ll try that… There, the grapple’s caught on a tree. I’m climbing out… I’ve landed in a bush, and… Hey, there’s someone else here! Hey! Lumberjack! Over here!
He’s turning this way, and… Oh. Uh-oh. I think he’s a zombie.
Run for it!
You don’t need to tell me twice! Ha ha ha! Zombies can’t run! Phew! I’ve lost him! I think I can see the wall of the temple here. I’m out of the swamp.
Thanks for the help, Player. See you later!
You can take it! Fight!
It’s not so tough! Its arm's come off, but it's still coming at me! Now, I’ve cut off both its arms, but it’s still trying to bite me! What?
It’s hopping at me on one leg! Why doesn’t it die already? There. I’ve cut off all its limbs and kicked it in the swamp. No zombie is safe from Zanik of the Dorgeshuun!
I don’t think I’ll have trouble with anything else in this swamp. Thanks for the help, Player! See you around!
Try to swim to the bank!
I think I can do that! The bank is just… Hey, what’s that? There’s a head poking out of the water… Eek! Tentacles! It’s got me!
Attack the tentacle!
If I can just reach my dagger… It’s working! It doesn’t like that at all! Phew! It let me go. I’m back on the bank now.
I’m not badly hurt, but I’m covered in swamp slime and monster blood. I’m going to stop here and try to clean it off. Thanks for your help, Player.
I’ll talk to you some other time.
Attack the head!
I hope my crossbow’s still dry enough… Haha! Got it! Crossbow bolt in the eye! It didn’t seem to hurt it too much, but it’s let me go. I’ve got back to the bank.
I think I can see a way out of the swamp from here. Thanks for your help, Player! I’ll talk to you some other time.

conversations.section: Outside Herby Werby

pages.x: Waaaaaaaaaaah.
What's going on down in that hole?
What hole?
That big hole right next to you, with all the roots drooping into the unknown.
Waaaaaaaaaaah. This is where the ritual takes place.
The ritual?
Yes. The ritual. We must please the ball of light in the sky!
The sun? Why must you please the sun?
Waaaaaaaaaaah. It nourishes us, makes us feel warm and helps my kind grow. But lately, something is wrong. Something is off. There has been a big shift. Waaaaaaaaaah.
What's wrong?
A lot of the herbs we offered to the ball of light are sick, they're not right. Not right I tell you.
I've tried telling my kind to stop burning the healthy herbs, but they're so eager to fix the situation down there that they're picking all the healthy herbs and burning them.
If we keep this up, we're going to have no more healthy herbs left and we'll slowly die. Waaaaaaaaaaaaah.
Is there anyway I can help?
You could help us! You can burn the bad, corrupt herbs and stop my kin from burning the healthy herbs. Would you please help?
That's what heroes do.
I don't know the answer to that question, what are you?
I am a human.
I am a human too...
No you're not... You're like some... Mushy potato thing.
I am a mushy potato thing.
Wow, now that sounds harsh, you're like a nice plant creature.
No I'm not. I'm a 'mushy potato thing'. Thank you. Before you we didn't have a name, but from here on out we shall henceforth be known as; 'The mushy potato things'.
Ooops.
What rewards can I earn?

conversations.section: In Taverley, after Wolf Whistle

pages.x: Hello again, Bowloftrix. How are you doing?
Well I can’t really complain.

o: What do you think of Taverley?
How do you like being Pikkupstix’ assistant?

pages.x: Wow...uh...that’s kind of put me on the spot.
Why do you want to know all about me? I mean, you saved me and all, but I’m hardly very interesting.
: Please, just humour me.
Fine...I’m a druid. I, you know, worship Guthix and nature.
I like long walks in the forst and eating vegan food. I mean, what else do you need to hear?
Well I was hoping you might have an interesting story to tell me, or a quest for me to do or something.
Well, do many people have those?
You would be surprised.
I think it is ok. I’m a druid. My family has lived here for generations. In the end I’ve never known anything different.
Well, except that time I went on a fishing trip to Rimmington.
Well, what did you think of it?
Meh. Not enough trees.
Guthix preserve me, this is the most harrowing thing that I have ever done!
: More harrowing than being kidnapped by trolls?
By miles!
That’s scarily impressive.
I mean, you hear stories, right? About how such-and-such fell down the stairs, or accidentally nailed their hand to a table.
Then you get there, and things don’t seem so bad. Before you know it, the guy you’re being trained by gets blasted to ashes by a backfire summon!
Gosh!
He’s a walking disaster magnet, but it’s never him! He never gets a single scratch, or is anywhere near things when they go south!
That’s terrible!
Uh, you wouldn’t mind taking this position for a while, would you? Just while I get myself healed up?
Not a chance.
Be well.

pages.x: Howdy, Player!
Howdy Diango!

o: Can you retrieve a holiday item for me?

pages.x: How are you?
I'm doing pretty darn' well!
Now that the workshop's all set up, the pixies are getting on just fine with preparing all the toys for the children.
Even Toby's tried to chip in with stuffing the imp plushies.
I've got no worries with getting everything crafted and wrapped before the big day. We might even be able to get a head start on next year!
So, what can I do in your workshop?

Aoife needs some assistance keeping the hot chocolate just right over in the kitchen, and Maeve could use some extra hands making the toy marionettes.

What about that room downstairs?

And what about that room upstairs?
Oh, that's just my bedroom. Working from home and all that. Stay out of there though, if you wouldn't mind.
Sure thing.
Could you retrieve a holiday item for me, please?
Oh, you're not joking.
Look, Player, normally I'd be happy to help you out. But right now I'm a bit busy with watching over the workshop.
You know, making sure the imps don't get into the paint and the pixies don't get overexcited.
But-
Come and visit me when I'm back in Draynor, where I'll be happy to help!
Bye Diango!
Enjoy the festivities!

pages.x: Well met, fellow adventurer! How can I help you?

o: I'd like to access my bank account, please.
I'd like to check my PIN settings.
I'd like to see my Collection box.
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Who are you?
How frightfully rude of me, my dear [chap/lady]. My name is Eniola and I work for that most excellent enterprise, the Bank of Gielinor.

o: If you work for the bank, what are you doing here?
I'd like to access my bank account, please.
I'd like to check my PIN settings.

pages.x: If you work for the bank, what are you doing here?
My presence here is the start of a new enterprise of travelling banks.
I, and others like me, will provide you with the convenience of having banking facilities where they will be of optimum use to you.
So...what are you doing here?
The Z.M.I., that is, the Zamorakian Magical Institute, requested my services upon discovery of this altar.
We at the Bank of Gielinor are a neutral party and are willing to offer our services regardless of affiliation.
So that is why I am here.
Can I access my bank account by speaking to you?
Of course, dear [sir/lady].
However, I must inform you that because the Z.M.I.
are paying for my services, they require anyone not part of the Institute to pay an access fee to open their bank account.
But, as our goal as travelling bankers is to make our customers' lives more convenient, we have accomodated to your needs.
We know you will be busy creating runes and do not wish to carry money with you. The charge to open your account is the small amount of twenty of one type of rune.
The type of rune is up to you.
Would you like to pay the price of twenty runes to open your bank account?

o: Let me open my account and then I'll give you the runes.
No way! I'm not paying to withdraw my own money.

pages.x: Yes please.
I don't have the runes on me. Let me open my account and then I'll give them to you.
It's not that I don't trust you, old [chap/girl], but as the old adage goes: 'Payment comes before friends'.
That's preposterous! I'm not paying runes to withdraw my own stuff.
I'm sorry to hear that, [sir/madam]. If you should reconsider, because I believe this service offers excellent value for money, do not hesitate to contact me.

pages.i: It costs twenty runes of one type. Do you wish to continue?

conversations.section: 2015 Halloween event

pages.x: Greetings, hero.

o: I need to get to the other side of the bridge.
Ask about becoming the God of the Underworld.

pages.x: Do you wish to be teleported to the southern bank?
This is not a title I ever wished to possess, mortal. It was thrust upon me by my father, Tumeken. Like a child I resisted.
It was a different time, and I was yet to learn the weight of responsibility. Amascut and I, we had displeased our father.
A memory that I do not wish to recount, though it is never far from my mind. Tumeken's rage burned fiercely.
He scorned us for our failings and sent us to guard the Underworld so that we would learn the error of our ways.
It is here, and in the events that transpired since, that I have learned the importance of sacrifice.
My father sought to teach me of responsibility, of which I have learned tenfold. Amascut's descent into madness has left much me with much on my shoulders.
But the weight I carry is my own. My deeds have brought me here… and my deeds will carry me forward.
The Devourer is not my sister, mortal. Amascut is not herself. When our father gave his life to save the Kharid it changed her.
He left all his responsibilities to me, as punishment for the decisions I had made. Amascut saw this not as my punishment, but as her failing.
She never believed she had earned his forgiveness after being sent to the gates of the Underworld. My sister had been left with nothing.
The pain in her heart drove her into the darkness from which she was never to return. Perhaps if I had done things differently… If I had not left… No, hope is not lost.
I can still bring her back, Player. I can still save my sister. First, though, we must defeat her here.
My father… He taught me all I know of humility and selflessness. I only wish I could embodied them more while he was still of this world.
It was my decision to bring the Mahjarrat to Gielinor that ultimately sealed my father's fate. We were on the cusp of defeat.
I sought to earn his respect by doing the impossible: winning the war.
When our new allies helped us throw the Zarosian forces back I went to Tumeken expecting recognition. Alas, I was only to be greeted by disappointment.
I was filled with anger. Why would I still not afford me the respect I deserved? Why did he still withhold his forgiveness? But he simply saw what I did not.
The Mahjarrat would soon betray us, the sweet victory would turn to bitter defeat in our mouths.
When all hope had faded and the Kharid finally seemed lost, my father stepped forward.
I can still hear my sister's screams as we watched Tumeken stride out into the centre of the battlefield. I was filled with immense pride as a bright light engulfed us.
Our father was gone and with him most of the military forces - friend or foe. The energy radiated across the Kharid, destroying most flora and fauna.
It was my actions that caused all of this. The obliteration of the Kharid. My sister's descent into madness. My father's death.
But his memory survives… and I will live up to it. I will make amends for my mistakes, mortal. I will atone.

conversations.section: At the Ancient Cavern / Talking to Kuradal

pages.x: Heya, can I help you?

o: Can we talk about items and incentives?
Tell me about your skillcape, please.
Can you sell me a Slayer skillcape?
I've noticed there are a couple versions of each skillcape.

pages.x: I need another assignment.
Can we talk about items and incentives?
Of course, what would you like to discuss: items for sale or incentives?
Let's talk items.
I have a wide selection of Slayer equipment - take a look!

o: How do I earn co-op points to spend on rewards?
Where can I use the co-op food and potion rewards?

pages.x: You'll gain co-op reward points if you complete at least half of your contribution to a task with a friend.
That means you need to be in a group for most of the time you're working on the task, but it doesn't matter if your friend beats you to the majority of kills!
You'll still have been in a group for most of your contribution, so you're still entitled to a co-op reward point.

o: Where can I use the co-op food and potion rewards?

pages.x: The rewards can be used in most of the areas we commonly send you to complete your tasks.

o: How do I earn co-op points to spend on rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about your skillcape, please.
This is a Slayer's Skillcape. Only a true Slayer master is permitted to wear one. You need more training before you earn that honour.
Well you have performed well as a student. I guess you have earned the right to wear such a prestigious cape now. That will be 99,000 coins, please.

o: I think I have the money right here, actually.
I'd like a skillcape with the colours inverted.
I've mastered this skill. Is there anything else?
I'd like a master cape with the colours inverted.

pages.x: Not at all; there are many other adventurers who would love the opportunity to purchase such a prestigious item! You can find me here if you change your mind.
There is something...though I have kept it a secret for a very long time. It is something that can only be worn by a true master.
Not even I can wear it - that's how hard it is to achieve.
You say you're a master. Stand straight, let me take a look at you...
You...really have mastered it. What an honour! It would be my pleasure to sell you a Slayer master cape.

o: Buy Slayer master cape for 120,000 coins?

pages.x: Yes! We, the skill masters, have crafted new versions of all skillcapes! We felt like it was time for a change.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Oh, it's you.

o: How does the Yak Track work?
Can you recommend any good music?

pages.x: How does the Yak Track work?
You get to go on an adventure and earn rewards along the way. You can complete tasks to progress along the track.
You will be given a choice between two tasks at a time, but you only need to complete one of them to progress.
If you don't feel like doing either of them then you can use a task skip to move on.
As you progress along the track you will earn rewards; Premier Club members and those who have purchased a Premier Pass will earn additional premium rewards.
If you purchase a Premier Pass you will receive any premium rewards you would have been eligible for.
Sounds great!
Can you recommend any good music?
I've been listening to a lot of 'Panyak! at the Disco' lately.
What's a 'disco'?
I have no clue. But I really like their music. I've been listening to 'Welcome to the Yak parade' on repeat all day...
I'm amazed you convinced a musician to play on repeat for you.
I'm paying them with exposure, you see. If you want to embrace your inner rage, try some 'Yak Sabbath'. 'Yak Veil Brides' are also really good.
Or like, whatever you enjoy listening to. It's whatever.
What's your backstory?
I was refusing to leave my barn, listening to Yak-182 and suffocating under the weight of the misery of life when a dark wizard asked me if I wanted to travel with her.
She was brooding, mysterious, powerful... and had great eyeliner. I knew we were soulmates. So I was all like 'gods yes', you know?
Err... sure.
My mum tried to stop me, because of course she did. She keeps trying to tell me it's 'just a phase'. Like... what the Yak?
Travelling with a dark wizard and being physically altered by the sinister forces they command isn't 'just a phase', SHARON.

o: The Yak angrily blows his bangs out of his eyes.

pages.x: I see. Thanks for sharing.
Bye!
Whatever.

Shot?

Your strength [Sir/Madam]. The stronger you are, the further you can throw the shot, but there are other factors of course, like your technique.

pages.x: Run away!

You should fight them.

You should sneak past them.

You need to shut it down!
Yeah, that’s what I was thinking. Hey, Oldak, Player thinks you should shut it down! Oh no! Oldak! Oldak’s paralysed! I can’t remember how to shut it down!
What did Oldak say? It was either de-align the rune injector, or reverse the polarity on the polarity reverser.
De-align the injector!

Reverse the polarity!

I can’t describe it! It’s literally indescribable! Anyway, it’s gone now. I think I should leave Oldak and Grubfoot to work. I’ll see you around, Player.

conversations.section: On members' worlds

pages.x: Good day! Would you like to have your picture taken?
Yes please!
No, thank you.
As you wish.
The imp sends them to a mysterious web that can be found beyond this material plane. From there, they can be viewed by other adventurers to put a face to the name.
For example, they'll be used to display the faces of adventurers with high skill training accomplishments.
There's an imp in there who uses a spell to take your picture.
He can only do it once every 2 hours at the moment, though, and it will take some time to process the picture. There's a lot of demand, you see.
Why an imp?
Ah, good question! See, I've experimented with lots of ways of making accurate visual representations of things in a magical way.
Most recently, I've been trying to modify scrying orbs to get a still picture.
Because of their shape, though, they always made the subject look fat! So I came up with a scrying cube, but that made things look even worse!
So what did you do?
I tweaked and tweaked the shape until I got a decent picture - took me weeks to make - but then this imp just teleported in from out of nowhere right next to it.
My scrying device fell on the floor and smashed.
Oh, no!
Imps take pictures?
Yes. He wouldn't reveal the exact working of the spell to me, or even why they do it, but the result is very convincing.
That's unfortunate.
But are my belongings safe?
Totally! I've got a few runes, orbs and trinkets in there to ensure of that.

conversations.section: In Keldagrim

pages.x: Come to visit my garden then, have you, human?
This is your garden?
No no, not quite. But I do look after it. It's the palace garden, you see. I keep it tidy, keep it living.
It's hard to grow much on these hard rocks deep beneath these mountains, you know.
I can imagine. Where do you get all your food from? Or even the soil for this garden?
We can grow a little food underground, but most of it comes from the extensive steamcart network that runs beneath the earth.
In the Era of Kings, many centuries ago, it was harder of course.
Our steam technology was not developed as far yet and getting fresh supplies of food was always a problem.
Oh, I'm not boring you, am I?
Not at all! Please, go on!
Oh yes, as I was saying, it was difficult to make a decent living here. I'm afraid this garden was rather neglected during that time.
Why did you dwarves stay so deep under ground, then? Why not simply go above ground?
What, with the wars raging up there?
We dwarves went underground a long time ago, see.
For a while the city of Keldagrim was completely cut off from the surface, simply waiting out the wars of the humans and the gods.
This made it hard, though, to determine when the wars above the ground were over. Perhaps Keldagrim had remained hidden for far too long.
Only when King Alvis heroically defended the city against an invasion of trolls did we dare to venture out and see how much the world had changed.
Of course, after that...
Ah well, enough history lessons I should say. I must really get back to my gardening.
Thanks for the info!
A little, yes. I don't really know what all this has to do with anything.
I suppose it doesn't, really, it's just the mumblings of an old dwarf.
Not really, no.
Oh, alright then.

conversations.section: Conversation

pages.x: Hello Player! Thanks again for your help with the dig.
What have you learned about the artefacts we dug up?
When we examined the blade you dug up, we found that the blade is covered in tiny symbols.
The scribe thinks he has enough of them to begin understanding the ancient goblin language, but it will take a while for him to decipher it.
Oldak examined the axeblade you dug up and found it had a faint magic aura. It looks like the mace wasn't the only magical weapon our ancestors brought from the surface.
In fact, it could be that a lot of their equipment was magical.
This means that either the ancient goblins were skilled magical craftsmen, or some other power was supplying them with magical equipment.
The helmet you helped to unearth has come in useful. I used it as a visual aid when I went to talk to the children at the nursery about our history.
It's amazing that the ancient goblins' eyes were even smaller than a child's!
We used the armour fragment you unearthed to reconstruct the shape of the original armour, and with it the shape of the goblin who wore the armour.
This told us a lot about how the goblin body shape changed from its surface form to that of the cave goblins.
Bartak used the design of the shield you extracted to recreate a shield like it. Even though the original shield was poorly made, the design itself was a good one.
Perhaps there is some important knowledge that we have lost since the early, more war-like days of Dorgesh-Kaan.
I lost the ancient goblin mace.
I know. Zanik says she found it lying around in the caves near the city, almost as if it had made its way back here and wanted her to find it.
If you want it back, I will sell it to you for 1,000 coins. That should discourage you from losing it again.
I lost the ancient goblin mace.
I know. Zanik says she found it lying around in the caves near the city, almost as if it had made its way back here and wanted her to find it.
If you want it back, I will sell it to you for 1,000 coins. That should discourage you from losing it again.
Okay.

o: Tegdak hands you the ancient goblin mace.

pages.x: Look after it well. All the goblins who have handled it say it made them feel uneasy. We want it kept safe, but we don't want it near the city.
No way!
Suit yourself.

conversations.section: Before The Dig Site

pages.x: Hello. Who are you?
Good day to you. My name is Terry Balando, I am an expert archaeologist.
I am employed by Varrock Museum to oversee all finds at this site. Anything you find must be reported to me.
Oh, okay. If I find anything of interest I will bring it here.
Can I help you at all?

o: I have something I need checking out.
Can you tell me anything about the site?
Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

pages.x: I have something I need checking out.
Okay, give it to me and I'll have a look for you.
No thanks.
Good, let me know if you find anything unusual.
Can you tell me anything about the site?
Yes, indeed! I am studying the lives of the settlers. During the end of the Third Age, there used to be a great city at the site.
Its inhabitants were humans, supporters of the god Saradomin. It's not recorded what happened to the community here.
I suspect nobody has lived here for over a millennium!

o: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

pages.x: Thank you!
Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?
Of course! Let's see now...
Trowels are vital for fine digging work, so you can be careful to not damage or disturb any artefacts.
Rock picks are for splitting rocks or scraping away soil.
What about specimen jars and brushes?
Those are essential for carefully cleaning and storing smaller samples.
Where can I get any of these things?
Well, we've come into a bit more funding of late, so there should be a stock of each of them in the Exam Centre's tools cupboard.
We also hand out relevant tools as students complete each level of their Earth Sciences exams.
Ah, okay, thanks.

o: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?

pages.x: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
But of course. Just have a look at my map.
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I can tell you about the state of the beacons in either direction, up to the last fires that are lit.
I could probably tell you about the other beacons as well, but I'd need the help of a macaw.
A macaw?
Yes. Macaws have the ability to fly high into the air and see things that are much further away.
They are also highly intelligent and can be trained to provide the exact information I'd need for a complete overview of the beacon network.
How's it going?
Pretty good, for the most part. I've done quite a lot of looking at the horizon today - it's quite hard work.
Have you seen anything worrying?
Not so far, thankfully, but one has to stay constantly vigilant for threats coming from the north.
Isn't it exhausting, constantly keeping your eyes peeled like that?
Well, actually, staring intently at anything for too long can be a strain on one's eyes.
I take a little break every hour or so and look away from the horizon for a few minutes, just to rest my eyes.
Oh? What do you look at, then?
Well, actually, I'm also using this opportunity to increase my knowledge about local moulds and fungi.
Are you being serious?
Not only can I spot danger from miles away, but I'm the quickest identifier of bread moulds this side of the River Lum!
That's a...unique claim to fame.
I'm quite proud of it, really. I'm hoping to branch out to yeasts next, then mushrooms.
I'm done talking to you, now!
Fine! I'm done talking to you, too, then.

pages.x: Hello!
Woah! Hey there!
What brings you to Draynor on a fine day like this?
It's a bit overcast don't you think?
It may be a bit dark, but you need to see beauty in all things. No matter what it looks like at face value.
You're right, what a lovely day to be out taking a stroll... Looking at all the trees.
The trees are all dead mate.

Not really. But speaking of beauty...

o: Victor lets out a deep sigh.

pages.x: What's wrong pal?
Life isn't easy being a goblin, people look at us and instantly think we're ugly vile creatures. It's not worth talking about as she'll never give me the time of day.
Who?
Wendy, she's the young witch over by the cart. I've always wanted to go over and say something but I have no idea what I'd even say. The way her hair flows...
...to the slight swagger in the way she walks...
...how will I ask her out?
How about; 'Hey, I know this is a bit forward but would you like to join me at the Blue moon inn for a beverage followed up by a nice stroll through Falador park.'
Not a chance... She won't give me the time of day.
Have you tried?
No.
Then how can you jump to that conclusion. You never know until you try right?
You're right but she'll judge me because I'm just an ugly green goblin.
What happened to the 'Beauty in all things'? Perhaps she'll look past all that and agree to a date.
You know what. I'll do it. Thank you... What's ya name again?
Player.
Well, thank you Player for the sound advice. I'll have to practice what I'm going to say.

conversations.section: In War's Retreat / Initial Dialogue

pages.x: Welcome Player! I'm glad to see your thirst for battle has led you to me.
Who are you?
I am War, retired horseman, battle-hardened warrior, blood sport enthusiast and owner of this delightful retreat.
Yes, I can feel the relaxation washing over me.
I'm glad you feel it too, Player, I can see you will fit in here!
Other than this lovely atmosphere we both definitely agree you've created, what is this place for?
WARRIORS!
Nurturing the combat talent of the future is my new hobby.
And you are my next project.
What do you mean? What do you want from me?
I want you to fight and grow as a warrior. Earn my favour by defeating the strongest creatures in Gielinor.
As my new project I shall need a name for you. How about Project?
Well, I suppose it's a functional name if nothing else.
What do I get out of this?
My retreat has various facilities to help the eager warrior.
If you defeat enough foes to earn it, I can offer you a teleport to return you to this retreat whenever you like.
My portals can be directed to take you to any bosses you can battle, if you've defeated them once before and can pay the price.
If you are helping out Old Boney with his reaping, the reaper portal will take you to the target he has assigned you.
Do you mean Death?
That's right, Old Boney!
The final portal will activate if there is a new foe to battle or an event to participate in.
I can also grant you access to a campfire and altar to reinvigorate you after a battle and adrenaline crystals to rouse you for your next one!
Finally, whenever you fight powerful creatures, I will give you marks to spend. They can be used to buy combat auras and aura and life refreshes.
That all sounds good, if a little dangerous. I'll think it over.
Don't think Project.
FIGHT!

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Hello. That hat doesn't look like standard Zamorakian attire.
Shh! They haven't noticed me here yet.
Why are you here? If they catch you here, they will kill you!
Well, the runecrafting wizards have got themselves into a bit of a state over a thesis published by a student.
We're also researching a new branch of Runecrafting at the moment: weapon imbuing.
What did this paper say?
Well, in short, it states that one day the altars like this one could run out of runic energy!
That's terrible! How will humans perform magic if we cannot make runes?
Well, it is only a theory. Hardly any of the Runecrafting Guild wizards believe it to be true.
Still, we have not proved Wizard Finix's theories to be incorrect yet, and - if they're true - this is very worrying.
Wizards have been dispatched to all the known altars to investigate.
So, what can we do if Wizard Finix's theories are true?
Well, there is a new method being explored, which was detailed in Wizard Finix's thesis.
He is the best person to explain it to you; he is currently in the Wizards' Tower, if you want to speak to him.
What is weapon imbuing?
Well, if you bring an inert magic weapon to an altar, you can use rune essence to imbue the weapon instead of binding runes.
This process saturates the weapon with runic energy and thus increases its power. This way, even regular wood can be made into menacing magical armaments!
In theory, that is. During our studies, we only ever managed to imbue eternal magic wood, perhaps due to the strong inherent magical properties that it possesses.
Our fellow wizards aren't proficient enough to properly imbue the wood either. None were able to get more than trace amounts of runic energy to settle in it.
This altar here also doesn't seem to work for imbuing at all.
I saw some Zamorakians try it and it looks like they only had any luck with fully imbued weapons, which dissipated into runic energy whenever they tried to imbue them any further.
I have a theory that certain objects of abyssal origin may yield the same results.
Maybe you should try it for yourself and see if you can get any use out of that effect.
I'm too scared to attempt it myself.

conversations.section: At the ground floor of the Ectofuntus / Talking to them

pages.x: What is this strange fountain?
This is the Ectofuntus, the most marvellous creation of Necrovarus, our glorious leader.

o: Where do I get ectoplasm from?

pages.x: What is the Ectofuntus for?
It provides the power to keep us ghosts from passing over into the next plane of existence.
And how does it work?
You have to pour a bucket of ectoplasm into the fountain, a pot of ground bones, and then worship at the Ectofuntus. A unit of unholy power will then be created.
Can you do it yourself?
No, we must rely upon the living, as the worship of the undead no longer holds any inherent power.
Why would people waste their time helping you out?
For every unit of power produced we will give you five Ectotokens.
These tokens can be used in Port Phasmatys to purchase various services, not least of which includes access through the main toll gates.
Where do I get ectoplasm from?
Necrovarus sensed the power bubbling beneath our feet, and we delved long and deep beneath Port Phasmatys, until we found a pool of natural ectoplasm.
You may find it by using the trapdoor over there.
How do I grind bones?
There is a bone grinding machine upstairs. Put bones of any type into the machine's hopper, and then turn the handle to grind them.
You will need a pot to empty the machine of ground up bones.
How do I receive Ectotokens?
We disciples keep track of how many units of power have been produced.
Just talk to us once you have generated some and we will reimburse you with the correct amount of Ectotokens.
How do I generate units of power?
You have to pour a bucket of ectoplasm into the fountain and then worship at the Ectofuntus with a pot of ground bones. This will create a unit of unholy power.
Thanks for your time.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Ah, hello again, young Player. How can I help you?
Can you tell me about yourself?
I am the lord of Clan Crwys. That, I suppose, is where I should begin, for it is my most important function. Beyond that I am an elf, or I was, or I am?
It's hard to remember, my limbs have been bark for so long that I cannot recall whether my veins should run with blood or sap.
You're an elf. You only turned yourself into a tree as a disguise.
Ha! Yes, I suppose you're right. Or perhaps I am a tree that turned itself into an elf as a disguise to free the wrath of my arboreal brethren.
Tree-kind can be surprisingly brutal to one another. The battle for resources is never-ending, and we do not lift a branch when another falls.
You mean you can't lift a branch...right?
Ha ha ha. Yes, yes, that is what we'd have you believe.
Can you tell me about Clan Crwys?
Where other clans create or destroy, clan Crwys maintains. We create and destroy plant life in equal quantities, maintaining a status quo in which we can flourish.
We are not a clan that revels in luxury and pomp. We are the clan with soil beneath our fingernails and splinters in our skin.
Some would argue ours is a simple life, but they have never spent the seasons watching over a farming patch. Learning to spot the signs of disease or infestation.
Nor have they had to worry about where a tree will fall and make sure that it falls on nothing of import. Hah!
Simple, give them a season with us and we'll see if they still think we live a simple life.
Can you tell me about Clan Crwys's skills?
We focus on the art of woodcutting and the craft of farming. Both serve their role in maintaining the elven culture and civilisation.
Through our farms we provide food and vital herbs needed by the other clans. Without us the city would starve and sickness would run rampant.
Through woodcutting we hold the trees back from rampant overgrowth, which could have untold damage on our fair city.
Through their wood we provide fuel for fires and materials for our artisans.

conversations.section: In Behind the Scenes

pages.x: 'A lovestruck Romeo sings a street suss serenade...'
I've been down here since 2010 and I still haven't gotten used to it.
Gotten used to what?
All the references.
Up in Gielinor there are loads of references all the time, but no one ever talks about it.
Oh yeah, didn't they remove you from the game because you were too blatant a reference?
Yes!
Down here though it's all pop culture all the time.
Why do you think there are so many references in the game?
There's two good reasons and one bad one, I reckon.
Good reason one is to show respect for a source of inspiration.
All art is imitative, and a well-placed reference acknowledges that fact without disrupting the flow of the work.
Oh, like homages?
Yes, exactly. Good reason two is to create a sense of camaraderie with the audience.
Including a reference signals to the audience that the author shares their life experiences and loves all the same things.
What's the bad reason?
When it's used as a substitute for actual content. Using a lazy reference because you couldn't think of a line yourself is as bad as using a cliche.
One other important thing is, the perfect reference is visible to those who get it, but invisible to those who don't.
Hm?
If it's obvious that it's a reference but you don't know what it's referencing, that makes you feel excluded from an in-joke.
You must hate this quest then?
Yeah...
You've put a lot of thought into this.
Surprising, isn't it? I'll be honest though, on any other subject I'm still the same randy old dog as always.

conversations.section: In Taverley / After Wolf Whistle

pages.x: It looks like those troll leaders have fled back to the mountain.
So have all the trolls followed them?
No, it looks like they have been sneaking past in small groups and hiding in the well.
Well hopefully the numbers should be small enough for me and the other soldiers to deal with.
Guthix protect you, take care if you do go inside.

o: How do you think the trolls got here?

pages.x: Of course! I suppose introductions were sort of lost in all the kafuffle.
I’m Scalectrix, although that is my druid name. I was originally from Burthorpe, but came to live here when the trolls invaded.
My home was one of the ones destroyed. The druids took me in and let me live here among them, like the other refugees.
Apparently I have a talent for summoning, so I came to work with Pikkupstix while I got settled and the trolls were repelled.
One day I hope, while working for him, I will attain the level of master and wear a Summoning skillcape too!
The war, mostly. I lived in Burthorpe all my life, and then the major push from the trolls destroyed my house and displaced me down here.
I’d always liked coming to Taverley when I had free time from my work in the games room, and I was lucky that the druids took me in.
A lot of the refugees moved back up once the trolls were repelled.
But I love it here! I never want to leave!
Do you mean in general, or here in this well?
Here in this well.
Well a mass of trolls would have been spotted by the troops, so I suppose they are scouts and stragglers.
If one or two of them at a time slip past the guard through the wells and tunnels, or in the confusion of combat, then they could have found each other.
Although I get the feeling those two leaders were scouts, who must have found this well and let the others know.
That might be why there are more still sneaking in there; the leaders ran off and never told them to stop coming.
Still, now the guards know to look for them, there are patrols of the Imperial Guard from Burthorpe looking around to sweep up any survivors.
And me, of course.
Of course! I’m sure you’ll help keep them at bay!
Be well.

conversations.section: At the Wizards' Tower / Talking to Wizard Finix

pages.x: I hope they let me into the Runecrafting Guild soon. It's cold up here on the roof!

o: What do you do in the Wizards' Tower?

pages.x: I'm a student at the Wizards' Tower. I'm here to see Wizard Elriss in the Runecrafting Guild about the thesis I wrote on Runecrafting.
Well, it explains my theory that the runecrafting altars are not everlasting. They are vast stores for runic energy, but one day they will run out!
I believe that's why Wizard Elriss wants to see me. The Runecrafting Guild wizards cannot disprove my theories and I think it's worrying them!
Luckily I believe I've found an alternative method of making runes: runic energy in the Runespan!
Yes! It's a way to take the energy out of the world around us and place it into rune essence, which in turn makes runes.
It's still a theory, and most of the Runecrafting Guild wizards think it can never be done, but Wizard Elriss thinks that the Runespan might help my studies.
We will see what Wizard Elriss says, I suppose.
The Runespan is the plane in which the Runecrafting Guild was built. It's a chaotic place with runic energy flying around unbound to anything.
You can visit the Runespan by going through this portal next to me.
The wizards have been observing it from the Runecrafting Guild for years, but it's only recently that they've been exploring it.
Silly old wizards. They spend far too much time arguing and not enough time going out and researching into all these theories they come up with.
You can buy wicked robes from me. The hood will give you runes and rune essence and even teleport you to the runecrafting altars.
The rest of the robes will improve the hood and make you ligher.
I can also re-colour these robes for you and provide you with an esteem icon for them to show off how much you've trained energy siphoning.
I can also provide you with staves made of rune essence.
They are ineffective as melee weapons, but they can store the charges for spells which only cost runes, and are good at defending against magical attacks.
Lastly, I can sell you a rune essence pouch that is much bigger than any you would find elsewhere.
This pouch will not degrade as quickly as other pouches, but once it has degraded it will turn to dust.

conversations.section: After Throne of Miscellania / Talking to Advisor Ghrim

pages.x: Greetings, Your Royal Highness.

o: It's good to have King Vargas back.
How do I manage the kingdom?
What am I meant to be doing again?

pages.x: How is the Kingdom faring?
Your approval rating is [number]%. Would you like to collect the resources gathered by your subjects?
Yes, please.
Here is a list of what your subjects have collected.
No, thank you.
Very well, Your Royal Highness.
This is how your subjects are distributing their effort.
What happened to King Vargas?
His Majesty has just set out on his latest great adventure. I do not know when he will return, your Royal Highness.
It's good to have King Vargas back.
It certainly is, and I understand he has you to thank, your Majesty.
Perhaps, now that Queen Sigrid has moved in, he will not be tempted to go on any more 'adventures'.
How do I manage the kingdom?
Your loyal subjects work hard to collect resources for you. Every day they bring what they have collected to the castle.

The resources which they collect are coal from the rocks to the north, maple logs from the trees to the east, herbs from the garden just outside the castle, and tuna and swordfish fished at the port to the south.
Another thing which affects the amounts of resources collected is your approval rating. The more your subjects love you, the more they will be motivated to work hard.
King Vargas would often go and help out his subjects in their daily tasks, when he was still able to do so, and they loved him dearly for it.
Finally, you can choose how much of their efforts your subjects devote to each resource; of course, the harder they work at collecting one, the less time they have to spend collecting the others.

Who are you?

Can you tell me about Seren?

Who is Seren?
Seren is the crystal goddess, beloved of the elven people. She was one of the first to set foot on this land.
When she saw the beauty of Gielinor, she brought the elves to settle here alongside the humans.
But with the end of the God Wars, Seren too was bound by the Edicts of Guthix, and although she did not leave, she is not what she once was.
We honour our lady, though, and we know she will return to her former glory.
Why should I follow Seren?
Seren is a goddess of peace and growth. She has always watched over the elves, and she can watch over you too.
With Seren, we can build a sanctuary, away from the chaos wrought by the other gods.
What does Seren want?
Seren is happy to share the bounty of Gielinor, and does not want to be involved in another God War.
We elves live apart from the rest of the world, and we have our own ways, without needing to force them on others.
All Seren wants is to share the world without needless conflict, where people can live as they choose.
I want to declare my support for Seren!
That’s wonderful! On behalf of Seren’s followers, I welcome you. Please, take this banner to show your support.
I have a gift for you: a book of stories regarding the gods and their followers. Please, read it and learn wisdom.
Although they have lost their way, there is something to be learned from reading of the other gods as well. The book is not yet complete, however.
When you complete some jobs I will give you more pages.

conversations.section: Talking to the head mystic

pages.x: Welcome, my [son/daughter]. Praise the Holy Ones for bringing you here.
What can I do here?
You can help us to gather sacred clay from the primordial realm, for the glory of the Holy Ones. I can teach you how.

o: Please give me a full tutorial.
Just give me a brief summary.
I have some questions about the primordial realm...

pages.x: Please give me a full tutorial.
Very well. Your task in the primordial realm is to gether as much sacred clay as you can. You can transform the clay into items using the creation kilns.
These items will help you gather clay more quickly and aid you in battle against the other team. The clay appears in five levels of quality, called classes.
Clay with a higher class will make better equipment and is worth more points, but is more difficult to gather.
I have some questions about the primordial realm...
Not right now.
Then leave me to my meditations.
The Holy Ones?
The Holy Ones! They are the most blessed of all the gods' creatures. Long ago, they served their gods in the glorious wars.
Even now, when their bodies are gone, they faithfully continue the fight. People today call them the revenants. They may be found in a cave below the Wilderness.
A simple seeker after spiritual things. I see truths that others do not see.
Where does that portal lead?
It leads to a world we call the primordial realm. The Holy Ones guided me to it and I had my followers set up camp around it.
Originally, the portal was in the Wilderness. It has recently moved to this cave, and we have followed it.
While this end of the portal is normally stable, the other end shifts dangerously around the primordial realm.
This means you cannot enter the portal directly, but we will guide waiting adventurers through when the time is right.
In the primordial realm we can gather the very stuff of creation; the sacred clay out of which the gods made all things.
The Holy Ones guided me to it, so that we could use it to build new bodies for them.

conversations.section: In Sophanem / After Dealing with Scabaras

pages.x: Good day, Player.
Greetings, cleric.
How can I help you?

o: Is it okay if I pray at your altar?
Can you tell me again about this enchanted water tiara?
Any word from Menaphos and the slaves?

pages.x: How are things?
It seems that your foray into the depths has stabilised the situation below. In my prayers, Icthlarin has expressed his pleasure.
You can talk with Icthlarin? Can you ask him anything you want?
You misunderstand the way in which the desert deities interact with us mortals. Icthlarin has blessed us with a peaceful afterlife, thus we serve him loyally.
It is not our place to pester him with outside influences.
He won't help you directly, then? That makes him just the same as the deities bound by Guthix's laws.
Have you not learned anything from the trouble with Scabaras.
He was influenced to act in this world and disaster befell him and his followers, and all those who came into contact with them.
Point taken, I suppose but what about the Devourer?
The Devourer is different. Her place is to interact with us poor mortals, or at least it is now. She has changed, and for the worse.
We here are grateful that Scabaras did not fall so far and so permanently as the Devourer.
Can you tell me again about this enchanted water tiara?
I have taught you how to make and enchanted water tiara, by using water runes with a water tiara.
This will protect you from the fierce desert heat, as you have protected the desert from the fierce Scabarites.
So, I just use some water runes on a water tiara?
It is, indeed, that simple. Though, you will use up any and all water runes you try to combine the tiara with.
You should also note that you can only have one such enchanted tiara at a time and that you require at least level 50 in both Magic and Runecrafting to create such a tiara.
And if I want the water runes back?
You will discover that by destroying you enchanted tiara, the enchantment will fade. This will free your water runes for whatever other purposes you might have.

conversations.section: After Deadliest Catch / Talk-to

pages.x: Hi, Jones.
Hi, how can I help you?

o: Can we hunt the Thalassus again?
You said something about deposit boxes?

pages.x: Those cast nets sound good!
They are! Which type would you like?
Use them wisely!
Use it wisely!
Use it wisely!
Actually, I changed my mind.
You said something about deposit boxes?
Yes, they're all around the coastline.
There's one near Eagles' Peak; in Tirannwn; down at Ape Atoll; near Brimhaven; a couple around the settlements in the Kharidian Desert; on Harmony Island; and along the River Salve.
You seem to get around a bit?
Around the coastlines I do. There's some good fishing to be done around the world.
What's your cousin's real name?
You mean what's 'The Guns' really called?
Yeah, he wouldn't tell me.
Listen closely; it's...
Julian.
Interesting...
Actually, nothing.
Fair enough!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Good day, Player. Welcome to my shop. Have you come to help with the crystal urchins?

o: What can I do to help?
Can I see what you have for sale?

pages.x: Who are you?
I am Mhistyll. I am the keeper of the cave that lies behind me.
I also reward those who try and deal with the infestation of crystal urchins in the waterfall above.
What are the crystal urchins?
The rock pool at the top of the waterfall used to be filled with regular urchins.
But a crystal within the caves below extended into the pool, and the urchins changed. Now they are living crystal.
They breed rapidly and cannot be killed by their regular predators.
If something is not done then the waterfall will become a cascade of spiny, crystal death!
That seems a little melodramatic.
Some of them are the size of beach balls. Can you imagine the damage they will cause when they start raining down onto the city?
That's a good point.
What can I do to help?
To help fish out the urchins you will need to climb to the top of the waterfall.
There is a route next to me leading up the side of the waterfall but you will need to bring a crossbow and grapple.
Once there you can fish small, medium and large urchins, if you are a sufficiently talented fisher.
You can then grind them to dust, which can be used to make perfect juju fishing potions.
Or if you don't want to do that then you can trade them to me.
I have lamps that can help increase your fishing skill, as well as the song that can let you create a crystal fishing rod.
Also, if you find a hermit crab in the pool then I have a collection of objects you can use to give them a home.
Can I see what you have for sale?
Certainly.

conversations.section: In East Ardougne / Talking to a Mourner (near the wall dividing East and West Ardougne)

pages.x: Hi.
What are you up to?
Just sight-seeing.
This is no place for sight-seeing. Don't you know there's been a plague outbreak?
Yes, I had heard.
Then I suggest you leave as soon as you can.

o: What brought the plague to Ardougne?
What are the symptoms of the plague?

pages.x: What brought the plague to Ardougne?
It's all down to King Tyras of West Ardougne. Rather than protecting his people he spends his time in the lands to the West.
When he returned last he brought the plague with him then left before the problem became serious.
Does he know how bad the situation is now?
If he did he wouldn't care. I believe he wants his people to suffer, he's an evil man.
Isn't that treason?
He's not my king.
What are the symptoms of the plague?
The first signs are typical flu symptoms. These tend to be followed by severe nightmares, horrifying hallucinations which drive many to madness.
Sounds nasty.
It gets worse. Next the victim's blood changes into a thick black tar-like liquid, at this point they're past help.
Their skin is cold to the touch, the victim is now brain dead.
Their body however lives on driven by the virus, roaming like a zombie, spreading itself further wherever possible.
I think I've heard enough.
Thanks for the advice.

conversations.section: After doing the Grand Exchange tutorial

pages.x: A pirate!
Arrrr, How'd ye be guessing that, [me-lad/me-lady]?
You're kidding, right?
Nay! Now, what is it ye be wantin? I can tell ye all about the prices of runes, or perhaps I could combine the charges on yer teleport jewellery.

o: Tell me about the prices of runes.
Combine the charges on my teleport jewellery, please.}}
I got to go, erm, swab some decks! Yarr!

pages.x: What's a pirate doing here?
By my sea-blistered skin, I could ask the same of you!
But... I'm not a pirate?
No? Then what's that smell? The smell o' someone spent too long at sea without a bath!
I think that's probably you.
Har har har!
We've got a stern landlubber 'ere! Well, let me tell ye, I'm here for the Grand Exchange! Gonna cash in me loot!
Don't you just want to sell it in a shop or trade it to someone specific?
By my wave-battered bones! Not when I can sell to the whole world from this very spot!
Tell me about the prices of runes.
Combine the charges on my teleport jewellery, please.
I got to go, erm, swab some decks! Yarr!
Defer your speech right there!
Quit this derogatory and somewhat narrow-minded allusion that all folks of sea voyage are only concerned with washing the decks, looking after parrots and drinking rum.
I'll have ye know there is much more to a pirate than meets the eye.
Aye-aye, captain!
Oh, come on! Lighten up!

conversations.section: During the 2012 Gielinor Games

pages.x: Hello there. What can I do for you today?

Let me see the reward shop.
I'd like to trade in my previous rewards for points.

pages.x: What would you like to know?
We have a number of events running. Which would you like to know more about?

o: I'd like to talk about something else.

pages.x: Oh, this event is one of my personal favourites. The athlete rolls a wheel of cheese down a hill and then chases after it.
Why?
Erm... Do you know, I've never asked. It's a lot of fun, though.
Manic, naturally, and it's really hard to navigate when you're running downhill at, like, a billion miles an hour.

o: I'd like to talk about something else.
I'd like to talk about something else.
I'd like to talk about something else.

conversations.section: In the Falador Party Room / During the New Year Resolutions event

pages.x: Hi!
Hi! I'm Party Pete. Welcome to the Party Room!
What's all this about New Year Resolutions.
Oh thank goodness, after all those Celebration lamps for the New Year, I'm all partied out!
So I thought that this year I'd make a list of New Years Resolutions.
How can I help?
New Years Resolutions?
Yeah, it's a tradition thing. At the start of each year you choose some things to do.
Now it could be getting fit, or giving up bad habits or trying something new!
Cool thanks, I'll look into it.
What's all this about New Year Resolutions.
Oh thank goodness, after all those Celebration lamps for the New Year, I'm all partied out!
So I thought that this year I'd make a list of New Years Resolutions.
Detox drink?
Yeah, it's my super secret recipe.
I could do with a hand with some of the ingredients though.
What do you need?
I've got a list here, take a look...
Can I see the list again?

conversations.section: Slime is of the Essence / Initial conversation

pages.x: Gods... what have I done?
Hey there, something wrong?
Something wrong!? Do you not see the gloopy monstrosity!?
Yeah... it's kind of hard to miss!
Please help me adventurer...
It's Player.
Peter...
So... uh... Peter... What did you do?
I had a little accident.
You don't say...
Last week I was trying a new secret recipe to make a gourmet, sweetened lime, gelatinous dessert for my finer things club.
... You were making lime flavoured jelly?
Gourmet. Sweetened lime. Gelatinous dessert. But that's besides the point! It all went wrong, embarrassingly wrong, I couldn't bare to let anyone know.
So, late that night while everyone was asleep, I carried my failed experiment all the way to here in Rimmington... And dumped it in the well.
But what does this have to do with this slime?
When I did so I heard some strange noises coming from deep within the well. Strange, gurgling noises.
I didn't really think much of it at the time, thought it was maybe a polar bear or something. But it appears it was something worse, something much, much worse.
So you're telling me whatever it was has fused with your lime jelly...
My gourmet, sweetened lime, gelatinous dessert.
Your girthy, sweet limed, jelly dessert.
and now it's terrorising Rimmington?
Pretty much...

conversations.section: In the Rogues' Castle

pages.x: Have you come to bust me out of here?

o: Why are you locked up here?

pages.x: Why are you locked up here?
I used to be a part of the group of rogues here, until they accused me of having stolen the gold we had stolen from people who had previously stolen it from someone else.
So they locked you up?
Yeah, I kept telling them I didn't steal nothing, but they just refused to believe me.
So, did you steal it?
That's not the point! What's important is that I said I didn't.
Eh...I see.
So, have you come to release me or what?
Yes, I have. The doors were locked but I used this magical ring to travel into a parallel realm where all recent changes are opposite to the other side.
So by closing the doors there, I opened the doors he-
Man, did you break the doors open using your head, or what? Regardless, I appreciate the help, man. If you ever need anything, come see me at my place in Varrock.
I've got a business you might be interested in.
Whereabouts in Varrock?
Assuming it hasn't been occupied by any of the muggers, I've got a place in the not-so-nice parts of town, right behind the archery store. Come and see me there.
Anyway, I've got to run now before my so-called companions realise what you and your thick head have done.
No, I haven't. I'm just here to make sure you haven't gotten your hands on anything to eat.
Aw, man, I keep telling you, I didn't steal the gold. Just let me out.
Uh...no.

MORE MARKS EACH FINISH!

NEW VARROCK ARMOUR UPGRADES!
