You found another hand of glory, didn't you?
I did, and of course I need to add a Luck of the Dwarves on to this one. That's right, isn't it? Sorry to have bothered you.
No need to apologise. It's me who should be sorry for being so curt with you last time, just because I was in the middle of something.
I'm glad to see you know what you're doing now, though.
And at least this is the last of them, given there aren't any other tiers of lucky ring to use.
Actually, there is the Hazelme-
Nope! No other lucky rings. None whatsoever.
Well, I was just saying about the Sig-
NO.
MORE.
RINGS.
Gotcha. This is the last of them. Again, sorry for bothering you. Bye.
Bye. Best of luck!
Now, Meg, where were we?

conversations.section: First time

pages.x: Hello human, and welcome to our amazing Gnomecopter Tours. What can we do for you?

o: Have you got anything good for sale?
Nothing at the moment, thank you.
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: What's Gnomecopter Tours?
The gnomecopters are something Sasquine and I invented. Using a unique blend of gnomic engineering and human magic, we've launched a whole new kind of tour experience.

o: What exactly can these things do?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: How did you make them?
Oh, it's very clever.
Sasquine and I saw some men riding around on big magic carpet thingies in the desert south of Al Kharid and we couldn't resist 'borrowing' one or two.
You 'borrowed' some magic carpets?
Well, we didn't exactly ask permission but they're for research purposes. That's allowed! Anyway, we're going off topic.
Alright, so you stole some magic carpets. What did you do then?
We managed to interface the carpets with the latest in gnome clider technology. My brother's an expert flight engineer; he helped a lot.
The result is what you see here: the gnomecopter.
It doesn't look much like a gnome glider or a magic carpet.
The rotors are mostly made from the fabric of the carpets.
Our expert gnomic engineering makes it far easier to handle than the original carpet and its magic allows the gnomecopters to do things that normal gliders
can't.
What exactly can these things do?
What exactly can these things do?
Nothing at the moment, thank you.

conversations.section: Subsequent

pages.x: Hello again, human. What can Gnomecopter Tours do for you?

o: Remind me what it is you do here.
Tell me how you made the gnomecopters.
Have you got anything good for sale?
Nothing at the moment, thank you.
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Putting it simply, the gnomecopters can take you to see bits of the world you might not get the chance to visit yourself.
Tell me how you made the gnomecopters.
Oh, it's very clever.
Sasquine and I saw some men riding around on big magic carpet thingies in the desert south of Al Kharid and we couldn't resist 'borrowing' one or two.
You 'borrowed' some magic carpets?
Well, we didn't exactly ask permission but they're for research purposes. That's allowed! Anyway, we're going off topic.
Alright, so you stole some magic carpets. What did you do then?
We managed to interface the carpets with the latest in gnome clider technology. My brother's an expert flight engineer; he helped a lot.
The result is what you see here: the gnomecopter.
It doesn't look much like a gnome glider or a magic carpet.
The rotors are mostly made from the fabric of the carpets.
Our expert gnomic engineering makes it far easier to handle than the original carpet and its magic allows the gnomecopters to do things that normal gliders
can't.
Such as letting non-members have a preview of members' areas.
Precisely! So, is there anything else you'd like to know?
Can I buy a gnomecopter?
Oh no, I couldn't part with one of these. They're very hard to make.
Nothing at the moment, thank you.

conversations.section: In Sophanem / After Contact!

pages.x: Good day, Player.
Greetings, cleric.
Hello, cleric. Might I impose upon your time?
Certainly. Ask your questions and I will see if I can help.

o: Is it okay if I pray at your altar?
Do you have any quests for me?
Any word from Menaphos and the slaves?

pages.x: Is it okay if I pray at your altar?
Of course. We Sophanites are believers in many gods.
I, in my position as head priest of Icthlarin, still give praise to Tumeken and Elidinis each day at this very altar.
Thanks, you've a very enlightened approach to this.
No need for thanks. Sadly, this view isn't taken by all Menaphite sects.
How are things?
The town is getting back to normal, thanks to you.
The bank under the Temple of the Lesser Gods has reopened and a number of our merchants have reopened their stalls.
That's good to hear! I'll make sure I visit a couple of them.
Have you been trading more with Al Kharid, seeing as Menaphos still has its doors closed to you?
We're doing a bit. Having Nardah and Pollnivneach nearby helps and we're also getting a lot of trade from adventurers these days.
Still, I look forward to when Menaphos opens its gates to us again.
Do you have any quests for me?
I have no quests available to you until you've increased your skills and performed more tasks for other folk.
I haven't heard anything more since my people returned. Ask them, if you're curious about their time in Menaphos.

conversations.section: In Taverley Dungeon

pages.x: Praise Zamorak for conflict, friend. Will you not test the strength of my chaos druids? I fear they grow weak and deserve to be cut down.
Who are you?
I am Ikadia the Exile, leader of these druids.
I wear the title in honour of my ancestor Urval, who was exiled by the druids above for preaching the truth about Guthix and Zamorak.
Zamorak is Guthix's most perfect incarnation! He brings balance to the world through chaos!

o: Haven't you heard? Guthix is dead!
Saradomin defeated Zamorak at the Battle of Lumbridge.

pages.x: Haven't you heard? Guthix is dead!
Of course I've heard, you insolent little man!
Like all druids, I felt the shiver run through the world. Unlike them, however, I rejoiced! Guthix has shed his old form, just as Urval foretold.
Now he returns in the form of Zamorak, to bring balance through chaos!
Saradomin defeated Zamorak at the Battle of Lumbridge.
Fool! You see only the surface and are blind to the true meaning!
When Saradomin and Zamorak began to fight, Lumbridge became a war zone, did it not? A place of conflict and destruction - a place of chaos!
That's an interesting interpretation.
I'm glad to meet someone who's willing to think independently, rather than blindly accept popular beliefs.
Your beliefs are ridiculous.
I am not here to win converts. Believe what you will.
I'd rather test *your* strength.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Talk to / After completing the Secrets of Amberfell quest

pages.x: Greetings, Player.
How is Amberfell faring?
For now, it is well.
I remain close to reassure them. While I am here, they are safe.
Sorrel's transgressions have been forgiven and the bonds to Wendlewick have been mended. They are all stronger for it.
Has the Sanguine spread closer?
Yes. Each day, it consumes more of the east.
The monsters that attacked us at the temple were a vanguard. A sign of what is to come.
Amberfell itself is safe for now. We will have to take the fight east soon, though, if we are to survive.
What can you tell me about the temple to the north of here?
It is called Moonrise.
Once, long ago, it was a site of great power. This was before I came to be. I do not know what it hides.
I seldom travel there myself. It is watched over by another. One I wish to avoid.
Perhaps it will soon reveal its secrets to you.
May I?
You may.
Briefly.
You have my trust, Player. Do not squander it.
May the moonlight favour you.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Hello. Do you need any help with brewing?

o: What do I do once my drink has matured?
Can you sell me any ale yeast?

pages.x: How do I brew ales?
Well, first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick.
Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's barley cooked on a range, by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide what ale it is you're brewing.
Lastly, you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff!
How can I get ale yeast?
Just ask me! If you bring me a pot I can fill it up with yeast for 25 coins.
How do I brew cider?
First, you'll need some apples. You'll crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush.
Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff!
How can I get ale yeast?
Just ask me! If you bring me a pot I can fill it up with yeast for 25 coins.
What do I do once my drink has matured?
Well, once you've got a full vat of the good stuff, just turn the valve and your barrel will fill up with eight pinks of whatever your chosen tipple is.
Once your barrel is full, you can drain it into an empty beer glass or a calquat keg.
Can you sell me any ale yeast?
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Whose tomb is this? It must have been someone special for the city of Falador to honour them with such a resting place.
My family's history is deeply rooted in the very foundations of Falador, long before a castle even existed.
She served King Raddallin faithfully, and travelled to every corner of each kingdom to help with the unification of what then became the Kingdom of Asgarnia.
During her travels, she learned everything she could from the various tribes and villages she passed through, mastering everything she was taught.
As Asgarnia flourished, she continued to serve her king before eventually passing unto the light of Saradomin. Forever to be remembered.
What was her name?
Her name was Meira.
Before she passed, to mark her place in history and as a gesture of all she did for the king, she was honoured with a cape made of the most magical thread.
The cape was enchanted by someone lost to the history books. However, the enchantment they cast prevents unworthy individuals from wearing the cape.
But you can wear it?
Meira's mastery over all the skills of the world became somewhat of a creed for our family, so we've continued her legacy by passing on what she started.
Then came a time where we'd honour those outside our family with such a blessing.
If I master all skills, can I wear the cape?
If you master all skills and are able to craft a keystone made of rubies, emeralds and sapphires set into some blurite, then place said keystone into that slot you see there on the tomb.
The tomb itself will decide if you're worthy. Then - and only then - will I offer you the chance to wear the cape.
I'll try that!
Oh, and there is one condition.
Hmm?
If one day you do manage to earn the cape. You're not to sell it or donate it to the Varrock Museum. They've been trying to get their hands on this for a while.
It's not a garment to lay unworn and gathering dust.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Oh, hello there, dear. How can I help you?

o: Do you have a spare spade?
Do you have anything for trade?

pages.x: Where are we?
This is Winkin's Farm, dear.
Oh, I see. So where is Mr. Winkin?
Oh, he headed off to the market a while back. We look after the farm while he's gone.
Now, was there anything else you wanted?
Have you got any flags?
Let me check for you.
Do you have a spare spade?
Why, of course. I can sell you one for 5 gold pieces.
Okay, thanks.
Here you are, then.
Actually, I've changed my mind.
Okay then.
Do you have anything for trade?
Of course.
Nothing. I'm fine, thanks.
Okay, dear.

conversations.section: At Troll Stronghold after My Arm's Big Adventure

pages.x: What can My Arm do for you today, Player?

o: Can I get another copy of that farming book, please?
I want to talk to you about the Kyzaj.

pages.x: Can I get another copy of that farming book, please?
Here, have dis one.
Thanks.
How's your farming coming along?
My Arm is getting good at dis. I growin' plenty of goutweed for Burntmeat, an' he very happy.
Good, good.
Anyfing else?
Nothing, thanks.
Dat okay, Player. Come back anytime you like.
Haw haw! Was great! Never seen anyfing like dat! Hope dey put on anuvva one soon.

o: What do you think about Zanik?
What do you think about Graardor?

pages.x: Shame you had ta kill 'er but I guess Zarador made a convincin' argument.
I just 'ope I nevva get chucked in a pit wiv you!
I never 'eard of 'im before this tournament. He's a pretty good fighter.
Nuffin' on you of course!
Naw. It sounds like pretty good adventure but I couldn't just leave. Dese herbs might die if I done that.
Nothing, thanks.
Dat okay, Player. Come back anytime you like.

conversations.section: At the Ancient Door / One week before the release of The World Wakes / Talking to Orlando Smith

pages.x: What's going on here?
Alright, mate? Exciting stuff, let me tell you!
Well, actually, I can't tell you. Not yet, anyway.
Why not?
Gotta be sure first, mate! Can't go making wild statements about world-changing discoveries without any basis.
Can't you even give me a hint?
Hmm... Well, alright - but only because I'm so excited about it m'self.
I believe, this could be...the ancient, original dwelling of Guthix. Where he used to actually live!
Course, I can't be sure until I get in there and 'have a look.
Tell ya what: come back in a while and I'm sure I could use an 'and.
I look forward to it!
Guthix is one of the gods! Some say the most powerful god of them all.
It's believed 'e was the first god to come to Gielinor, shapin' it in 'is vision. He brought us humans in, among others.
Belief 'as it that Guthix lives off balance; he thrives from us livin' in harmony.
So, back in the Third Age, when the other gods came along and started fightin'...well...Guthix just up and banished 'em all!
Course, it could all be legend, but it's fascinating stuff for a historian.
That sounds exciting! Can I help at all?
Tell ya what: come back in a while and I'm sure I could use an 'and.
I look forward to it!

conversations.section: After Dragon Slayer / If the player is carrying an anti-dragon shield

pages.x: Good day to you.
Aye, 'tis a fair day, mighty dragon-slaying friend. That's an interesting shield yer wearing. Could I have a look at it?

o: Can I buy a rune platebody now, please?
Yes, it's a very nice day.
Can I have another key to Melzar's Maze?

pages.x: Here you go.
Hmm...where did ye get it?
The Duke of Lumbridge gave it to me. It's an anti-dragonbreath shield.
Ah, I thought as much!
Feel how it's warm to the touch. This shield must be storing dragonfire and just letting it radiate away.
Now, if there was only a way to get the dragonfire out again...

o: Can I buy a rune platebody now, please?

pages.x: What use would that be?
Why, ain't it obvious? Ye could project blasts of dragonfire from yer shield!
Ye know, I think there might be a way.

o: Can I buy a rune platebody now, please?

pages.x: What way?
I've heard legends of a thing called a 'draconic visage'. It was made by the dragonkin themselves, creators of the dragons, or so they say.
This 'draconic visage' had the power to channel dragonfire. Now, if I could attach the visage to the front of this shield...

o: I will look for this draconic visage!
Can I buy a rune platebody now, please?

pages.x: I will look for this draconic visage!
Good luck wi' that. They're mighty rare, so yer quest will take some time. If any monsters have them, it'll be the dragons.

conversations.section: In Burthorpe during Parcels from the Hedge (May 2018) / When talked to

pages.x: Player! So great to hear from you.

o: What are the postage stamps for?
What's so special about the parcels you send me each day?

pages.x: Any mail for me?
What's with all the parcels?
They're from all the people of Gielinor to all the adventurers to thank them for their hard work!
I'll try to send you one each day for 30 days, and if you don't have enough space, just come and see me in Burthorpe once you do.
If you want more, you'll just have to get out into the world and try doing something. I'm sure some mail will turn up.
What are the postage stamps for?
I'm always sending letters, so I'm interested in any spare postage stamps you may have. I'll even exchange them for an unclaimed parcel.
What's so special about the parcels you send me each day?
I have a couple of lost property packages in the post office, that you can take off my hands should you collect parcels from me frequently.
Wow, that sounds great!
Just check in each day and I'll send any mail your way.
What delivery options are there?
I can send all parcels to you directly, or alternatively I can have them sent to your bank.
I'll send parcels to you directly as my priority.
I'll send parcels to your bank as my priority.

conversations.section: Historical dialogue / First time speaking to the professor

pages.x: Hello.
Hello what?
Uh...hello there?
Hello, 'Professor'. Manners cost nothing, you know. When you're in my classroom, I ask that you use the proper address for my station.
Your station?
Yes. It means 'position', so to speak.
Oh, okay.
Now, what can I do for you, exactly?
What is this place?
This is the Misthalin Training Centre of Excellence.
It is where bold adventurers, such as yourself, can come to learn of the dangers of the wide world and gain some valuable experience at the same time.
What can I do here?
Here you can take part in the Player Safety test: a set of valuable lessons to learn about staying safe in RuneScape.
I can give you a test paper to take and, once completed, you can bring it back to me for marking. Would you like to take the test? It will not cost you anything.
Yes, please.
Right then. Here is the test paper. When you have completed all the questions, bring it back to me for marking.
Okay, thanks.
Not right now, thanks.

conversations.section: In the Thieves' Guild / First time dialogue

pages.x: Hello there. What do you do?
I'm the trainer of safes like these ones.
They don't look like they take much training...
Har-dee-har. No, I train thieves to open them. Wanna hear more?

o: How many hanky points do I have?
I'd like to claim a reward for my hanky points.

pages.x: What are these handkerchiefs for?
Oh, we use them to keep track of our members' training regiment. Blue handkerchiefs will earn you one point, red ones are worth four.
You can claim a reward from any trainer with your hanky points.

o: How often can I do this?

pages.x: How often can I do this?
The number of hanky points you can claim for depends on your dedication to the art. At the moment, you can claim hanky [amount] points' worth of training per week.
Which activities give which handkerchiefs?
Our pickpocketing trainers, safes and easy chests carry blue hankies; red hankies can be found on the coshing trainers and behind harder locks.
Bye for now.
How many hanky points do I have?
I'd like to claim a reward for my hanky points.
Bye for now.
Not interested, thank you.
Give your fingers a workout on my dummy safes, if you'd like, although there's nothing in 'em but hankies. Got to store them somewhere.

conversations.section: In the Thieves' Guild / Inspecting a safe before learning about safe-cracking / After A Guild of Our Own, with space in backpack

pages.x: You'll come across safes like the one next to me in a few places. They've often got 'portable' valuables inside.
Fatal flaw of safes is that their lock mechanisms are really loud.
If you listen, you can hear the tumblers clicking when you get 'em in the right place. But I'm sure a thief of your calibre will have 'em open in no time.
Although, without a stethoscope, you might find it harder to hear the tumblers clicking on more intricate safes.
See, there are different difficulties of safe that'll test your thieving abilities to increasin' degrees.
Got all that?
I think I've cracked it.

o: The trainer hands you a loot bag and a stethoscope.

pages.x: What's the loot bag for?
When you loot safes, you'll automatically swipe the contents in the bag. Loot bags make stuff easy to carry, less suspicious and they're incredibly fashionable.
You got any more questions?

o: What do I do with the items I steal?
Do you know where I can find the high-level safes?
pages.i: What would you like to know?

pages.x: Other than training your sleight of hand and acquiring wealth? Well, you will be able to earn Pilfer Points, I suppose.
Fill up that bag with any amount of loot, then take it over to Robin at the entrance and he'll fence it for Pilfer Points.
Then visit Dodgy Derek's shop to spend them on his downright dirty deals. He has some sweet items, like a shock absorber.
It'll stop you getting stunned when you're caught stealing from pockets.
Ah, good question! The problem with stolen goods is that selling them to general stores will get your fingers chopped off, if the courts are feelin' mean.
Thankfully, at the Thieves' Guild, we offer our fencing services. You've proven to be a heck of a thief, so you get full access.
Simply speak to Robin at the entrance, and he'll sort your stolen goods problem. Although, he will take a cut. Literally, if he doesn't like you.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Task 1 / Start

pages.x: Muahahahahahahaaa!
Erm, excuse me?
Bwahahaha muah muah ahahahahahahaaa!
Are you okay? Can I get you a doctor...or like a priest or something?
Ahaaa! I see you were not terrified by my elaborate evil laugh!
Oh that's what you...erm I mean no...not really.
Then you my good friend are brave and stout of heart. You do not balk in the face of true nightmarish terror!
I'm not entirely sure that's what you were showing there...
Haha you shrug off the nightmare with a burning courage.
Oh is that what the itching sensation is?
SILENCE!!!!
Oh brave and mighty hero, for you I have...A QUEST!!!!!
Is there really a need for all the drama?
You, oh brave one, must go out into the dark and dangerous world and there you must perform a terrifying task.
A task that makes grown men tremble in absolute fear. For you must...
KILL
TEN
RATS!
...seriously? Not even firebreathing dragon rats of death?
Lord no, what do you think I am; a monster? Just kill ten rats and come back to me to claim your prize.

conversations.section: Unaligned

pages.x: You look like a skilled adventurer. Would you like to join the forces of the holy Saradomin?
Yes! Where do I sign up?
I'm pleased to see there is still some good in the world!
You can find the forces of holy Saradomin by finding our recruitment officer in our camp. It's to the north of the battlefield by Lumbridge.
You will be able to find out more about the skills we need there, although everyone has something to offer.
I thank you for your support. Know that our lord looks kindly on his followers.
Maybe. Why should I join you?
Because we fight to defeat evil! For years, the power of Saradomin has kept the forces of Zamorak at bay.
But now, with the return of Zamorak, the weak and the helpless are more vulnerable than ever.
Saradomin's forces are the barrier preventing chaos and death from reigning over the world!
We need all the help we can get. Whether you're a fighter, a fisher, a woodcutter or a miner, you can help tip the battle in our lords favour.
To join the forces of good and drive evil from the land, travel to the battlefield at Lumbridge, and talk to the recruiter in the north camp.
Great! I'm on my way!
That's great news! I know that with your help we will keep the evil of Zamorak at bay.
No way! I support Zamorak!
It truly pains me to see you sell your soul to evil.
It's not too late for you. You can still join the forces of good, if you head to Saradomin's camp at the north of the battlefield instead.
I don't want to get involved.
How can you not take part? Zamorak is an evil that must be stopped at all cost.
Please, for the vulnerable and the powerless in the world, you must side with us to defeat Zamorak!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hey, new fish! Welcome to Waiko! Have a copy of our tourist brochure!
You're enthusiastic!
Of course, Waiko is great, and we love western tourists!
Any questions? I'm here to help! Or read the brochure!
You should talk to Rosie in Waiko market - she's our ship chandler.
Buy some supplies from her, and then you'll be able to head out on an expedition on your own boat!
She's even generous enough to give you a handful of supplies every day for free!
And if you want to claim an uncharted island as your own, you'd best talk to Boni, also in Waiko market. She's looking for help with a little project.
Of course! There are a couple of basic amenities here on Waiko...some bamboo around the market area and some fishing spots on the south dock.
If you're after trickier fish to land, though, you should head to Whale's Maw. There's some tortles to hunt there too, so I've heard.
These are all only basic resources, however. They're pretty good to sell for chimes, but they're not great experience.
But if you head out to explore the uncharted islands, you'll be able to gain some really nice experience, and better resources worth more chimes.
Better still, if you're able to gather a wider range of resources, you can spend some extra effort to turn them into commodities, which sell for even more chimes!
There's plenty of dangerous fauna, monsters and people out in the uncharted islands.
But it sounds like Aminishi might be your sort of speed.
Last I heard, there was a Death Lotus assassin out that way...you should talk to them for more information.
Hey, if you're ever looking for work you should talk to Sojobo in Waiko market.
His contracts are a good way to learn the ropes, while also earning some chimes and experience.
But I'm sure if you ask around, there'll be a bunch of other odd jobs you can pick up too!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hmm? What's that, young [man/woman]? What can I do for you?

o: I don't know, what can you do for me?

pages.x: Hmm, well, mmm, do you have a family crest? I keep track of every Gielinorian family, you know, so I might be able to find yours.
I'm also something of an, mmm, a painter. If you've met any important persons or visited any nice places I could paint them for you.

o: Can you see if I have a family crest?

pages.x: A family crest, mmm? So, what is your name?
Player.
Mmm, Player, let me see...
Would you like a portrait or an, mmm, a landscape? Or a map, maybe?

o: The Prince and Princess of Miscellania

pages.x: Mmm, well, see you some other time maybe.

conversations.section: During The Bird and the Beast / Armadylean / Runite token

pages.x: You have gained favour with Armadyl. How can I help you?
How's the battle going?
Can you tell me about the gods?
I have questions about you.
Please, ask.
Who are you?
Where are you from?
Why do you follow Armadyl?
How is it you survived the aviansie's destruction? (After asking anything else)
A god named Zamorak decided that the God Wars had gone on long enough. He used the Stone of Jas and levelled an entire continent, creating the Wilderness.
The vast majority of our tribe was wiped out in the explosion.
Armadyl assumed that no aviansie remained. We assumed that our god had fallen. We were both wrong.
It would be many years before Armadyl returned to Abbinah to discover those who had escaped the explosion - children of the deserters, the sick and the infirm.
What happened after the God Wars? (After asking anything else)
Back to the present.
I have a question about my orders.
You are doing well so far. Keep the energy coming in on our caravans, so we can ensure victory. Armadyl thanks you for your efforts.
Continue to spread the word of Armadyl. Be involved in our quest for freedom.
I have no more questions.
May Armadyl guide us to freedom.

conversations.section: In the White Hole, after Gower Quest

pages.x: Well go on then. You don't want to wait around here, do you? It's just a mostly featureless room.

o: Can you explain this place again?
I'd rather stay here for a bit.

pages.x: It's Behind the Scenes!
-PLACEHOLDER- hilarious placeholder dialogue here. Wait, what? Why did I say that?
It's the editing. There's no one checking the dialogue, so you just spew any old rubbish.
-PLACEHOLDER- the player still doesn't understand. Yuck! That feels horrible!
Don't worry, you've probably gotten it out of your system now. You may still find yourself saying some pretty weird things though!
So, what is this place?
I'll break it down for you. You're from RuneScape, right?
I'm from Gielinor.
Sure, big rebranding exercise, world building, but same thing. Sometimes in RuneScape things change. People change how they look. New stuff appears. Old stuff disappears.
I never noticed this happening.
You're part of the system, see, you don't see it happening. Take Rat Pits, you remember Rat Pits?
No. What's Rat Pits?
It was a minigame, and it was broken, and no one played it, so it got removed. Now for you it's like it never existed.
But what does that have to do with this place?
Well when something gets removed from the world, or before it gets added, this is where it goes. We call it Behind the Scenes.
Look, just think of it as like the afterlife. Afterlife-slash- theme-bar.
So it's full of dead people?
Close enough. You go on in. You'll either figure it out or go mad from the trying.

conversations.section: Before Love Story / After speaking to the other bank guard / Without stew in backpack

pages.x: Hello?
Ssshhh! What do you want?
Well, it's not every day you see a man up a tree.
I'm trying to observe a suspect. Leave me alone!

o: This is about the bank robbery, right?
You're not being very subtle up there.
Can I do anything to help?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: This is about the bank robbery, right?
Yes, that's right. We're keeping the suspect under tight observation for the moment.
Can't you just... I dunno.... arrest him?
I'm not meant to discuss the case. You know what confidentiality rules are like.
Fair enough.
You're not being very subtle up there.
I'd be doing a lot better if nits like you didn't come crowding around me all day.
But your legs are hanging down!
Go away!
Please yourself!
Can I do anything to help?
That's very kind of you. I'd rather like a nice bowl of stew, if you could fetch me one. I don't get many meal breaks.
You want a bowl of stew?
If you wouldn't mind...
I'll think about it!

conversations.section: Game modes

pages.x: Greetings Player! Would you like to change you game mode before you leave for the mainland?

o: Tell me about the game modes available to me.
I'd like to change my game mode.

pages.i: Which game mode would you like to learn about?

pages.x: In standard mode you play RuneScape as originally designed, playing alongside others with no special rules or restrictions!
You can freely trade and team up with other players as you desire.
As an Ironman you must be self-sufficient, making and using your own resources.
You won't be able to trade with others, access to event rewards is limited, and multiplayer gameplay such as minigames may be limited.
As a Hardcore Ironman you'll play with the same restrictions as regular Ironman, but with the added danger of PERMA-DEATH!
Dying in this mode will remove your Hardcore status and you'll continue as a regular Ironman.
In Group Ironman you play with the regular Ironman rule-set within a group of 2-5 players, working collaboratively to achieve your goals!
Certainly! Your current game mode is: [Standard/Ironman/Hardcore Ironman/Group Ironman]. What would you like your new game mode to be?

pages.i: Are you sure you want to change your game mode to: Standard?

pages.x: Very well, I have changed your game mode to: Standard!

pages.i: Are you sure you want to change your game mode to: Ironman?

pages.x: Very well, I have changed your game mode to: Ironman!

pages.i: Are you sure you want to change your game mode to: Hardcore Ironman?

pages.x: Very well, I have changed your game mode to: Hardcore Ironman!

pages.i: Are you sure you want to change your game mode to: Group Ironman?

pages.x: Very well, I have changed your game mode to: Group Ironman!

conversations.section: After Housing of Parliament

pages.x: Hello, Player!
Hi Tyton.
Is there anything I can do for you?
What's the history between the owls and the City of Um?
You'll have to be more specific than that.
Well, did Death create you? How long have you been around?
As far as I can remember, my siblings and I have been around since the before the inception of Um. Thus I would presume we were not creations of Harold.
How were you created, then? What is your purpose?
That is a much larger existential question that I am unable to answer.
My personal theory is that we were appointed here upon the creation of life, to oversee the many events of the Underworld. But knows.
That's understandable. Do you ever get bored of the Underworld?
Speaking for myself, no. The Underworld is vast, with a never ending flow of new life passing through.
It's definitely not the worst place to be stuck in for eternity, I suppose.
What do you think of Deryn?
Hmm... Yes, Deryn is a rather kind soul to spend her time in Um looking after my siblings and I.
Before her, we were left to fend for ourselves. Which wasn't an awful way of living by any means - there's food and water aplenty in the Underworld.
I do enjoy feeling pampered, though - gourmet food with a fresh bath, right on my doorstep.
Nevermind.
Farewell.

conversations.section: During the event

pages.x: Greetings festival goer!
Greetings!

o: Can I help you with anything?

pages.x: What is going on here?
You mean you don't know? Why do people turn up to these types of festivities without knowing what they're doing here...?
They could end up getting themselves into all sorts of mischief!
Am I getting myself into mischief?!
Oh, of course not! This is a perfectly normal festival! Just don't stand too close to the fire!
Welcome to the Wintumber Warmer! We celebrate the end of the long cold months and welcome in the turning of the seasons! I enjoy this time of year.
It helps me to remember that the long, warm days are not too far away!
I do enjoy a bit of time at the beach in the summer.
Me too friend!
Join me in celebrating the Wintumber Warmer by taking part in the activities around the crater. You can help Chad and Evey to build lanterns and summon fire spirits.
And if you're feeling more adventurous, I think Emmet and Sera are looking for some willing... volunteers to try out fire breathing and dancing.
There really is something for everyone!
Wonderful!
Can I help you with anything?
Goodbye.
See you around.

conversations.section: After Fate of the Gods

pages.x: I'd like to talk about Zaros returning

pages.i: Tell Wahisietel that Zaros is back?

pages.x: So...I have some news for you. Which do you want first: good or bad?
Good. Always good.
Okay, so, I guess you'd think it was good news that...Zaros has returned.
What? Could it really be true, after all this time?
It is; I was there. In fact, if not for my aid, he'd not have been able to.
Hmm, thanks to your new status as World Guardian, no doubt...
This is very good news indeed. I thank you for the bringing of it.
And the bad news?
Sliske has been excommunicated - he's no longer a loyal supporter of Zaros.
That's hardly news, let alone bad news!
How was Zaros?
I do wonder why it is that I am finding this out from you, however.
Azzanadra didn't tell you the plan?
He did not... I must contact him about this.
I'm sure he has his reasons
I give you knowledge, in exchange for the knowledge you gave me...

o: Wahisietel hands you a reward lamp.

pages.x: Actually, never mind.

conversations.section: What do we know so far? / With Ritual of the Mahjarrat started and The World Wakes completed

pages.x: So, what do we know of the Mahjarrat?
Well of course now you know I am myself a Mahjarrat, but I'm happy to remind you of what you know of us.
We are powerful with a strong aptitude for magic including the ability to change our form and look like other creatures.
There are a number of Mahjarrat active in the world.
Jhallan, who you helped to hibernate in the north, was weaker than most Mahjarrat. He was not present at the last ritual.
There is Zemouregal, who controls many zombies, including the once great hero Arrav. Zemouregal seems to have a penchant for attacking Varrock.
He was also present at the death of Guthix in an unsuccessful effort to kill Guthix in the name of Zamorak.
Enakhra is a female Mahjarrat and follower of Zamorak. She is a rival of Akthanakos, who is a follower of Zaros.
Enakhra also tried to kill Guthix in order to gain favour with Zamorak, but she did not succeed in her plan.
There is General Khazard, who owns territory around Port Khazard and the Fight Arena.
There is Azzanadra, who you freed from a pyramid he was trapped in and who then taught ou how to use lot a of useful magic.
Later in your travels, you met Azzanadra again. He was disguised so that he could restore the Zarosian temple under the digsite without arousing too much suspicion.
Once the temple was complete it formed a communication link between Azzanadra and Zaros.
So, although Zaros has not physically returned, he is able to command those loyal to him once again. It seems that the stage is set for a rather dramatic act, no?
You also met Azzanadra at the death of Guthix. He was proposing to wake Guthix, with the other Zarosians.
There is Lucien, who is looking particularly dangerous and powerful, even for a Mahjarrat.
First, he gained control of the Staff of Armadyl and now he has the Stone of Jas, which could be the most powerful artefact known to Gielinor.
It's possible he even has aspirations to become a god.
There is also Sliske. A mysterious Mahjarrat who killed Guthix. It is possible he may have gained power from this, but we do not know for sure.
Many Mahjarrat follow the evil god Zamorak. The wiser among us follow Zaros.

conversations.section: NovtumberFest / When talked to / After the first time

pages.x: What can I do for you?

o: I'd like to help with your research.
Explain to me what's going on again.

pages.x: Would you like to help with my research?
Well that's disappointing.
What are you doing?
Why, I am currently researching wolpertingers, fascinating creatures they are!
What is a wolpertinger?
That's the beauty of it! Is it a rabbit? Is it a wolf? Is it something else? That's what I aim to find out!
Now let me tell you, there are 2 different types of wolpertinger.
Light wolpertingers and dark wolpertingers.
If you zap a light wolpertinger with a light zap it will be sent safely back to the spirit plane!
Same as if you zap a dark wolpertinger with a dark zap it will also be sent safely back to the spirit plane!

o: This would give you Summoning XP.

pages.x: However, if you get these the wrong way round the poor wolpertingers will be slain on the spot!

o: This would give you Slayer XP.

pages.x: Well that's disappointing.

conversations.section: Historical dialogue / Standard dialogue

pages.x: Good day to you, Player!

o: What can vis wax be used for?
Can you help me with the machine?
How did you know my name?

pages.x: Why, my boy, I am Wizard Goldberg: world-renowned inventor!
Give me a lever long enough, a fulcrum on which to place it, some bellows and maybe a few tubes, and I could assemble a machine to move the world!

o: Goldberg seems to lose himself in this thought.

pages.x: As long as the peacock kept hold of the spanner...
Um... Wizard Golberg?
Oh, right, yes... This is my latest invention: the Rune Goldberg Machine! Which I believe has the potential to help us unravel the mysteries of magic!
So how does it work?
Well, I haven't quite unravelled the mysteries of the machine itself yet, so I'm letting everyone take a crack at it.
This is my latest and most fabulous invention: the Rune Goldberg Machine! It will take your ordinary, unremarkable runes and turn them into purest vis wax!
I'm sure it has plenty of uses, my boy! I'm told it can make your auras last longer, if that's something you have trouble with.
It's highly prized by challenge masters for its rich waxiness. They'll let you change or extend your challenges in exchange for a good dollop of the stuff.
It can even be used to increase the amount you can gather from divine locations - really! Using one simple trick discovered by a housewife! That is to say, my wife.
Hrrrrm... She's a fickle machine, so what worked for your friends yesterday may not work for you today. I do know that the top slot seems to work the same for everyone...
And there's a fair chance you know someone who'll have the same experience with the middle as you... But the bottom is a mystery that you alone can solve.
Why, I used my Name Goldberg Machine, of course!

conversations.section: Unaligned

pages.x: Aha! I see a new recruit for the army of Zamorak.
Yes! Where do I sign up?
I knew it! You should go to the south side of the battlefield in Lumbridge, and talk to the officer there.
You can sign up, and fight for the winning side - ours!
And if you don't want to fight, we also need skilled gatherers of all types.
Don't delay. We need all the help we can get!
Maybe. Why would I join you?
Because we're the strongest!
Zamorak is the most powerful of the gods, and soon Saradomin will fall before our might. You can be part of that victory.
Everyone can play a part, from the weakest to the strongest, and from the warrior to the woodcutter. All welcome!
To join us, you need to go to the south side of the battlefield in Lumbridge and talk to the recruiter.
I'm on my way!
Praise be to Zamorak! I look forward to the day we defeat Saradomin!
No way! I support Saradomin!
You would side with the weak and worthless Saradomin? Then I pity you.
But it is not too late for you to join the winning side. Zamorak is all-powerful, and soon all of Gielinor will see!
I don't want to get involved.
You are uninterested? This battle will touch everyone.
And when Zamorak is victorious, it will be too late for you to seek scraps from his table.
It's not over yet! You can still join the mighty Zamorak, if you head to the south side of the battlefield.

conversations.section: First time / Talking to Acting Guildmaster Reiniger for the first time

pages.x: Are you here to sign up with the Archaeology Guild? We've just recently received some serious funding, and we're in need of as much help as we can get.
Maybe. Why would I want to become an archaeologist, though?
You want the sales pitch, right? Need a reason to get down in the dirt with the rest of us working schmoes?
Well, I'm sure one of these four core aspects of archaeology will at least get you to give it a shot: wealth, power, fame and stories!
Wealth is the easy one. Not only will you find artefacts with their own inherent value, we also have a healthy trade going on between guild members.
Any materials you excavate, you can sell to other archaeologists!
Power comes in the form of any magical relics you discover in your career.
I have no doubt an adventurous sort such as you could gain great value out of increasing your power!
Fame comes in the form of being the first to discover something of note or importance.
There's more than one way to become a world-renowned archaeologist, and it isn't all just about being the most experienced of us!
And finally, the stories.
As an archaeologist, you will uncover long forgotten tales of people and places from the past, events lost to time and rediscover things both mysterious and wonderful!
Well, I'm sure at least one of those motivates me! Do I need any qualifications?
Those can come later. I'm sure we can start you off on the basics and you can learn on the job.
Great. So, er, what are the basics?
First off, you're going to need some tools!
Those tools I just handed you will cover most of your needs - uncovering excavations and restoring damaged artefacts, mostly.
However, we've been developing a new tool to do the actual excavation - strong enough to dig out materials quickly, but delicate, for when you need to be careful around an artefact.
Take this bronze mattock to start with...

conversations.section: Talk-to

pages.x: Hello? I'm Player.
Hello, Player.

o: Can I access my bank account?
(If the confirmation was previously disabled:) Enable barrier confirmation.
(If the doors were not previously kept open:) Can you keep the doors to this chamber open for me?

pages.x: Who are you?
Ashuelot...Ashuelot Reis, and I'm sorry.
I've been through more than many can imagine, waiting here, guarding our mistake...ensuring it never returns to full strength.
Can you turn the confirmation check for the barrier back on?
One second... done.
Can you keep the doors to this chamber open for me?
Why would you want to return here so freely?
Certainly not to open that large glowing door.
I want to fight Nex.
This is a pointless crusade.
But I know I cannot stop you.
I would need a substantial offering to be sure you are dedicated to this cause.
Bring me 10,000,000 coins, a set of Ancient Ceremonial Robes and the frozen key you used to enter this place.
That's all, thanks.
Guthix guide you, Player.

conversations.section: At the Dragonkin Laboratory / When talked to after having completed Temple of Aminishi

pages.x: Oh, hello again, Player. I heard you freed the guardian spirit of Aminishi from a terrifying curse. Very heroic, you did a great thing!
What are you doing all the way out here, Bryll?
I've heard rumors of more misdeeds carried out in this area. Some horrible, torturous experiments. So I was scouting the place out.
I just managed to fix the lift mechanism that goes down into the ruins. Maybe you could go explore for me? Perhaps with a group of others.

o: What can I get for exploring here?

pages.x: Lots of dragons. I wasn't down there for long, so I just grabbed what I could.
I haven't been able to go very far in but I could see a vast cavern filled with ruined buildings and volcanic currents.
The place is abandoned, apart from the wild creatures. I can't tell when they left, though. Magmatic activity is unpredictable.
It might have been inhabited recently or be totally ancient.
Did you spot anything significant?
Hmm, in the distance there was something that looked like a huge magic shield. I could only see it from certain angles. Perhaps it's protecting something valuable?
Do be careful if you get close.
To be honest I don't think I could handle it alone. I was hoping you'd offer to travel deeper inside.
I was quite cautious, made sure I wasn't followed. Even brought a camouflage potion. We should be safe around here, but be careful if you head back west.
Some people are likely to try and kill you out there.
Well you'll be able to train your Dungeoneering skill some more by defeating monsters down there. I'll award you some reward tokens for taking out the powerful ones too.
You can spend them on some of Marmaros's stock back at Daemonheim. I've heard a couple rumors about some powerful combat techniques too.
Perhaps there's some record of them here.

conversations.section: Barbarian Assault / After agreeing to sign up / Talking to him

pages.x: Hi...I mean, Player reporting, sir!
Straighten that back when you talk to me! You want my help?

o: Sir! Can we do some training?
Sir! Could I change my current wave?

pages.x: Sir! Can we do some training?
Again? Very well. Listen closely this time!
Sir! Could I change my current wave?
Nah, sounds boring.
Boring? You'll get nowhere with that kind of attitude! Drop and give me ten!

o: Maybe next time. I need to go wash my hair.

pages.x: Maybe next time, I need to go wash my hair.
You'll do as I say!
Arrrghhh. Okay, okay!
Sir, yes sir!
Good to see you've learned some respect. Make it five.
Yes sir!
But I already did!
You did?
Sir, yes sir!
I don't trust you in the slightest. Do as I tell you!

conversations.section: After completing the Barbarian Assault tutorial

pages.x: I believe you might be able to reward me for my progress in this arena?
Well, that depends upon your skill levels for each role. What's your name, soldier?
Player, Sir!
Okay. What exactly do you want to know, Player?

o: Can I trade some of my points?
What points do I have so far, sir?
Could I have a 'Queen Help' book?
Could I change my current wave?

pages.x: Can I trade some of my points?
Of course.
What points do I have so far, sir?
Let me check... You have: x Attacker Honour Points, x Defender Honour Points, x Collector Honour Points, and x Healer Honour Points.
Could I have a Queen Help book?
By all means.
Could I change my current wave?
I can change it down to wave 1 and you're currently on wave x. I'll give you a ticket for use on the wave x door, so you can change your wave back to that room.

o: Yes, reset my wave to one.
No, I want to stay on wave x.

pages.x: Yes, reset my wave to one.
Very well.
No, I want to stay on wave x.
That is all, sir.
Very well, on your way.

conversations.section: After Housing of Parliament

pages.x: Hello, love!
Hi Deryn!
What can I help you with today?
So, what made you want to take care of the owls here in Um?
Well, back in my life, I was in charge of looking after the terrorbirds in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.
When my time had come to part with the living world, I realised I wanted to have a bit of change in death.
One lifetime of terrorbirds is enough for anyone, I'd imagine.
Now, don't get me wrong, terrorbirds are lovely creatures!
I truly enjoyed spending my life with them, but there was a whole variety of jobs out there that I was yet to try.
So... you became a keeper for a different bird instead?
It's not what I was expecting, either! But once I arrived in Um, and I found that the poor owls had no one to look after them, I couldn't say no!
Do they need anyone to look after them? They've been surviving for quite some time before you came along.
I'm sure they were surviving just fine, but, as with anyone, the dears needed a bit of love and attention. So I was more than happy to step up.
I guess it was meant to be.
I guess so!
Can you tell me about owl tracking?
Bye for now.
Farewell, dear!

conversations.section: When talked to during Birth by Fire

pages.x: Thank you for heeding my call, human.
It's hard to ignore a demon stepping out of a bonfire.
I have been sent as an emissary of the Queen of Ashes, and require any and all help.
What is it you need?
Many interesting embers have been turning up in this world, and my Queen wishes to analyse their properties.
Collect as many burning embers as possible and bring them back to me.
Sounds simple enough.

o: What do you plan to do with these Burning Embers?
How long will you be around for?

pages.x: A failed experiment. Considered unworthy. Incredibly angry. Redeemed by Fire.
It sounds like you've got a pretty large grudge against someone.
That's not even the half of it.
Some questions are best left unanswered, human.
Like 'What's your relationship with Zaros'?
Yes, like that one.
My Queen noticed this world appear in the heavens as if it had been revealed from behind a curtain. Last year she felt an increase in fire energy in this location.
She had her pyradins spend a year preparing to use that energy. With it, she could bring me through the planes, in the hopes that the energy would build up once more.
You worked an entire year in the hope that the energy might return?
I did not personally; my task is to act as scout and herald for my Queen; to seek worlds that are ready for her Enlightenment, and deliver messages between those who are already Enlightened.
Without a continuous source, all fire comes to an end. I can only last here for the amount of time my Queen's strength allows me. Be sure to collect my embers quickly!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Do you work here?
Yes, I work as a forester for the McGrubors! Let me guess: the lederhosen gave me away, right?
Something like that. What does your job entail?
What? Where? How many tails?
Excuse me? No, I mean what do you do here?
Oh! Er...sorry. I look after the place - plant and fell trees, check them for disease, look after the local wildlife...and hold back the tide of the pheasant incursion.
Sounds simple enou-
Wait - run that last one by me again.
Pheasants! I kill them - they're pests, see.
Pests? Really? Are you sure you're not thinking of pigeons?
Pigeons, pheasants - what's the difference?
Actually, there's a very big diff-
Exactly! They're as bad as each other...plus these ones are mutating.
Mutating?
Some have got more tail feathers than others.
Maybe some have just lost a few fea-
Giant mutated pheasants from the Void, planning the destruction of my lovely forest!
But they're tiny! You're...you're just a bit mad aren't you?
Mad? No. 'Freaky', maybe, but not mad!

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: My name is Holstein, emissary of the Godless. I am here to teach you about them.
If you wish, you can declare your support for the Godless, and I have some jobs you can do.

o: Can you tell me about the Godless?
I want to declare my support for the Godless!

pages.x: My name is Holstein, and I am a wanderer by nature. I have travelled the world and seen much.
I have seen the devastation of the Wilderness; I have seen the corruption in Morytania; I have seen the cold, crystalline walls of the elf city of Prifddinas.
I have seen as the gods returned and immediately set to claiming lives and lands. One, I have already seen fall.
All of this brings me to believe one thing: we do not need the gods. So, I am here as the emissary of the Godless - those who follow no god.
What do you want to know about the Godless?

o: Why should I join the Godless?

pages.x: The Godless are a group of like-minded individuals, striving for a world where there are no gods; no 'supreme beings' fighting for dominance.
We may not be as strong as the gods alone, but together we believe we can rise up and cast them from this world. We are our own protectors!
The Godless represent those who are dissatisfied with the gods. We do not want to be mere pawns of some greater power.
By joining with the Godless, you too can cast off the shackles of the gods, and be free to follow your own path.
We of the Godless want a world without gods. We have seen the strife they have wrought, and we see no future on that path. Bandos has already fallen. Gods can die.
We can be free of them!
Good! On behalf of the Godless, I welcome you.
Please, take this banner to show your support. I have a gift for you.
It is a book of stories and other accounts, pertaining to the gods and their followers - as well as some of our own. Read it.
It is important that you understand what we are up against. The book is not yet complete, however. When you complete some jobs I will give you more pages.

conversations.section: Upgrading necromancy equipment / Tier 80 / Tank / Before having received the uncharged spiritbound hammer

pages.x: So, you want to upgrade to tier 80.
First off, I'll need some more souls in this soul urn.
The urn will only accept souls from killing monsters assigned as your Slayer task using necromancy, or completing greater communion rituals.
I need 150 Slayer task souls, or 30 greater communion souls.
I also need you to recharge this special hammer of mine, with some powerful soul energy.
Powerful, eh? Do I need to defeat an elder god? An average god? A demi-god?
Er, not exactly. Just some of their followers.
Oh.
Powerful followers, though! I was thinking of the four generals in God Wars Dungeon.
Defeat them, and then charge up my hammer with residual energy from their altars. It depletes quickly after their defeat though, so you'll have to be fast.
Fast as lightning, noted.
And last but not least...
A pie?
A pie!
But not any old pie...
A redberry pie!
I was wondering how long it would take for you to ask for one.
I've exercised a lot of restraint by trying the other pies first, but I think it's time.
Now here's your list.

conversations.section: In the Grand Library of Menaphos / Before Pharaoh's Folly

pages.x: Hi, can I help you?
What is this place?
Keep your voice down! This is a library!
*whispers* What is this place?
I just told you, this is a library. Well, what's left of one anyway.
When he's not ruling the land, the Pharaoh likes to let off some steam with a good old-fashioned book burning.
We've lost far too much, including all of the Menaphite history, sociology and adult romance.
He's not a complete barbarian, however, and has been burning by issue number, so we still have a complete set.
Kind of considerate, really.
Suit yourself!
Who are you?
Keep your voice down! This is a library!
*whispers* Who are you?
I am the watchful protector of the literary realm, Kohnen the librarian.
There comes a time when jewels cease to sparkle, when gold loses its lustre, when the throne room becomes a prison and all that is left is love for a good parse through quality census data.
Suit yourself!

conversations.section: Castle Wars

pages.x: Good day! How may I help you?

o: What do you have for trade?

pages.x: What is this place?
This is the great Castle Wars arena! Here you can fight for the glory of Saradomin or Zamorak.

o: Really? How do I do that?
What do you have for trade?

pages.x: Really? How do I do that?
Easy! You just step through one of the three portals. To join Team Zamorak, pass through the red portal. To join Team Saradomin, pass through the blue portal.
If you don't mind which team you're on, pass through the green portal - that's the Guthix portal - and you'll end up helping to balance the teams out.
Are there any rules?
Of course - there are always rules. Firstly, you can't wear a cape as you enter the portal. You'll be given your team colours to wear while in the arena.
You're also prohibited from taking non-combat items in with you. So, you should only have equipment, potions and runes with you.
Secondly, attacking your own team or your team's defences isn't allowed. You don't want to be angering your patron god, do you?
Other than that, just have fun and enjoy it!
Great! Oh, how do I win the game?
The aim is to get into your opponents' castle and take their team flag. Then, bring that back and capture it on your team's flag stand.
What can I win?
Everyone will gain a Silver Castle Wars ticket, regardless of the score. The winning team will receive two Gold Castle Wars tickets.
In the event of a draw, everyone will get one Gold ticket each. Tickets can be traded in with me for various rewards.
Can we talk about ammunition?

conversations.section: In the Black Guard HQ in western Keldagrim / After Birthright of the Dwarves

pages.x: What can I do for you, Player?

o: So you're still head of the Keldagrim Black Guard?
I want to talk about the Red Axe spies.

pages.x: So you're still head of the Keldagrim Black Guard?
I am. I was having trouble with the responsibility at first, but the Supreme Commander says I've grown into the job.
I want to talk about the Red Axe spies.
Thanks for your help with that, Player.
At first I was annoyed that Veldaban would send a human to judge dwarves, but perhaps only an outsider could have judged them fairly.

o: What do you think of my choices?
Where do you send dwarves when they're exiled?
How do the executions take place?

pages.x: What do you think of my choices?
What do you want me to say? Is your conscience troubling you? Do you want me to tell you that you made the right choice?
As the king's agent you were empowered to judge the prisoners however you saw fit. From a legal standpoint, whatever you did was correct.
Decisions like that come with the territory, I'm afraid. No one said they were going to be easy.
Where do you send dwarves when they're exiled?
They're forbidden to enter lands controlled by Keldagrim. A lot of them seem to end up to the south of Yanille.
How do the executions take place?
A dwarf sentenced to death is taken to the mines outside the city and a Black Guard cuts off their head with an axe.
It may not be a perfect system but at least it's quick.
I should go.
It was good to see you again, Player.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Dialogue 5

pages.x: Hi!
Hmm... 3rd Age... No, no... maybe 4th...
Hello?
Yes, that's it, just like that. Mustn't forget the map either... hmm... what else?
HELLO! Are you there?
Oh, hello there. Sorry, was a bit engrosed in updating this display. I've just been out questing and thought I'd stop off here you see. It's quite rewarding too.
Yes, well, no need to ignore me.
No offence intended, my dear [chap/girl]. Just very interested in this history stuff, that's all.
Okay. Have you seen the Natural History exhibit in the basement?
Oh, yes, marvellous isn't it! I particularly like the wyvern, very interesting considering they've never found a live specimen.
And to think they could possibly have been flapping around at one time!
A bit like the crazy gnomes and their gliders. Have you seen the model they have upstairs?
Yes, very intricate isn't it? Worrying to think some people risk their lives in them! You wouldn't catch me up in one.
Had a chat with Jacques while I was up there, the art critic... he's a bit funny in the head.
That's not very nice!
Well, he thinks he's going to get an entire portrait gallery to himself!
Who knows, the Museum just got really big and appears to have cash. They might entertain him with his very own floor - we'll see.
I guess so. Wonder what poetry he'll come up with then! Still, I must get on with this display. See you around I hope!
Bye!

conversations.section: At Mill Road Mill, north of Ardougne / Before The Chosen Commander

pages.x: Oh, hello. What do you want?
Who are you?
I'm Milton the Miller of Mill Road Mill. I'll give you one guess what I do for a living.

o: You're a knight who is also a culinaromancer?

pages.x: You're a miller?
And they say common sense is dying out.
You're an undercover White Knight?
Very funny.
You're an evil culinaromancer?
Very funny.
You're a knight who is also a culinaromancer?
Hah, yes. They call me the Knight of the Living Bread.
What is this place?
It's a windmill, you idiot.
How do I mill flour?
You go upstairs, put some wheat in the hopper and pull the lever, then the milled flour comes out here.
Then you keep doing that all day, every day, because it's the family business and you have to stay in the family business.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: In Jatizso

pages.x: Hail the conquering hero!
Heh. Thanks - I was pretty heroic even if I say so myself.
Is there anything I can do for you?
Tell me more about Jatizso.
Tell me more about Jatizso.
Jatizso is a small Fremennik town, which is far less closed to the world than other Fremennik tribes.
We maintain trade links with many powers in the world and have moved beyond some traditions to take advantage of modern advances.
We do, however, continue to 'enlighten' our neighbours in Neitiznot. Unfortunately, some of the Islands are infested with trolls.
We should really be trying to deal with the trolls, but the King tends to get a bit preoccupied with his cousin, the Burgher of Neitiznot.
Tell me more about the King of Jatizso.
Tell me more about the King of Jatizso.
Ha! Our benevolent King Gjuki Sorvott IV. He doesn't have much of an opinion about anyone, apart from his cousin Mawnis who rules the other Island.
He hates him with a passion that can occasionally be quite scary.
You might be able to talk to him if you help out around Jatizso. Don't expect much in the way of gratitude though.
Can you ferry me to Rellekka?
Can you ferry me to Rellekka?
Sure.
No, I'm fine right now.
No, I'm fine right now.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hi. Are you one of the returned townspeople?
Why, yes. You must be the brave adventurer that Maisa told us was seeking our return.
I guess so.

o: I would like to buy some of your produce.
Why were you stuck in Menaphos?
It was nice to meet you.

pages.x: Why were you stuck in Menaphos?
Well, it all started the day that the plagues broke out here.
I had gone into Menaphos in the morning to get some flour and chocolate powder and, when it came time for me to return, the gates were shut.
So the guards wouldn't let you back?
No, not at first. I actually didn't want to return. I didn't want to come down with the plagues so I stayed.
What happened then?
Well, word must have traveled back to the slaves that their fellow slaves in Sophanem no longer had to work and so they rioted.
That must have been scary.
It was, but Coenus, chief gate keeper of the city, stamped the revolt down fairly fast...and quite brutally.
If the revolt was stamped out, why are the gates not open?
No, it was only really stopped in the Imperial and Merchant districts of the city. There is still trouble brewing in the Worker and Ports districts.
Now, if you wouldn't mind, I'd rather not dwell any further on the past. Can I interest you in my goods?
No, thanks.
It was nice to meet you.

conversations.section: After bringing him a cup of tea for the first time

pages.x: Hello, who are you?
Hello, I am the panning guide. I'm here to teach you how to pan for gold.
Excellent!
Let me explain how panning works. First, you need a panning tray. Use the tray in the panning points in the water and then search your tray.
If you find any gold, take it to Terry in the Exam Centre. He will calculate its value for you.

o: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

pages.x: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?
Of course! Let's see now... Trowels are vital for fine digging work, so you can be careful to not damage or disturb any artefacts.
Rock picks are for splitting rocks or scraping away soil.
What about specimen jars and brushes?
Those are essential for carefully cleaning and storing smaller samples.
Where can I get any of these things?
Well, we've come into a bit more funding of late, so there should be a stock of each of them in the Exam Centre's tools cupboard.
We also hand out relevant tools as students complete each level of their Earth Sciences exams.
Anything else?
If you need something identified or are not sure about something, give it to Terry. He's the archaeological expert in the next room.
Ah, okay, thanks.
Thank you!

conversations.section: Talk-to / With the little book o'piracy or having completed Rocking Out

pages.x: Hello there! Can I sew ye somethin' tegether?
What do you mean?
Well, ye see it works like this; I can sew yer eye patches onto yer pirate hats or pirate bandanas.
Just pirate bandanas mind ye, I hate the feel of snakeskin. (Shudder)
It costs 500 gold te do it, and 600 gold te get them separated.
Okay, why does it cost more to get them separated than put together?
Wear and tear on scissors.
On another note, I also sew crab claw gauntlets on to pirate hooks, highwayman masks to black cavaliers, and mime masks to black berets, if ye have them with ye.
So, do ye have anything ye wants doin?
Yes please!
Now, do you want to be sewing items together or separating them?
I'd like something sewn together.
Aye, pick out what items ye be wantin' sewn together.
I need something separated.
Aye, aye. Just use yer item on me and I'll see if I can separate them.
No.
Fair enough. See you around!

conversations.section: At the tower north of Falador / Before Grim Tales (58 Thieving required)

pages.x: Hello there!
I say! Where on Gielinor did that voice come from?
Uh, hello there! Can you hear me?
Why yes. Yes I can. My word. Is that...is that one of the gods? Guthix perhaps? Saradomin?
No, no. I'm not either of them.
Egad! You're not...Zamorak...are you? I mean, uh...begging your pardon of course, my Lord. No offence intended!
Ha ha! No, I'm speaking to you through the pipe here! I'm at the bottom of your tower.
Oh. Oh I see! Oh, yes. How clever! Remarkable idea! However did you think of that? Good show, old bean!
Who are you?
Rupert the Beard. At your service, old fruit.
Rupert the Beard?
Yes, old turnip. On account of my wonderfully long bearded chin, you see.
So what are you doing up there exactly? And how come you talk so strangely?
What am I doing? Well, I guess I'm stuck in a matter of speaking. Dear me, yes! I'm stuck. And I speak in the King's speech, I'll have you know.
Really? Which king?
Which K...? Why, THE King old spud! THE King! Only one worth mentioning in my opinion.
I see. Well is there anything I can do to help you up there?
Hmmm. No, no, I can't think of anything at the moment. I'm a bit stuck. Let me know if you get any ideas though.
I'll do my best!

conversations.section: In Taverley / With partial completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters

pages.x: What can I do for you young 'un?
Hey there, can you tell me something about this Sanfew Serum, like how do I make it, and what does it do?
Certainly. It was after all, my creation, and mine alone. If anyone should know how to make it, it should be me!
Can't fault that logic!
Ok, essentially this potion is a mixture of a cure poison and restore stats all rolled into one! Very hand for the adventurers with an eye on conserving inventory space.
Ok, I'm sold... How do you make it?
Well, it's very easy really. You take a standard super stat restore potion. Add some ground unicorn horn. Then, add some snake weed from the island of Karamja.
Finally, add some nail beast nails. You can only get these from the
area of Morytania, specifically, if you go deep in the Mort Myre swamp.
How do you mean, deep into the Mort Myre swamp?
Well, most adventurers avoid the deep Mort Myre swamp, whereas the Paterdomus trek and the Burgh de Rott trek take you through the most interesting areas.
These areas often allow the quickest, but potentially more dangerous
routes, through Mort Myre. This is where you're likely to encounter a nail beast.
Are they very dangerous?
They can be pretty dangerous. They'll defend for a long time, then attack suddenly and seemingly without warning, landing three vicious attacks at once.
This can be pretty lethal. However, the nail beasts can be damaged by
the Sanfew Serum itself... it's very bizarre that a potion made from their claws should have such a pronounced effect on them.
Ok, that’s very helpful. Many thanks for your assistance.

conversations.section: First time dialogue

pages.x: Alright. You look like you could help.
What with?
I'm trying to perform a study on some wandering spirits, but I don't have the budget to travel much in search of them.
You seem the inquisitive type, plus you have your own ship from what I can gather.
Okay, how would I help, and what's in it for me?
I'm studying entities I call kami spirits - they're these floating spectral things that appear to be wearing masks.
For each new specimen you bring me, I can impart some of my knowledge to you.
And if you can help me collect one of each type, I'm sure we can work out something more rewarding.
How do I catch them?
You'll need a jar of some sort, and probably a net too. Although they are spirits, their masks make them easy to catch.
Would an impling jar work?
I don't know; what's an impling? Maybe just give that a try and you tell me.
Will do. How many types I hunting for?
Honestly, I couldn't tell you. Maybe you could keep track of them in a journal or something. What I do know is that there are two kinds.
Some you will only find on populated islands - those are quite common and easy to catch. They're used to living creatures and less skittish.
And then there are those only found in the uncharted islands - they'll be more difficult to catch.
I call them orokami to differentiate them, but they're basically the same as bakami.
Any questions?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Any questions?

o: Can I toggle my kami spirit reward?

pages.x: That's what I'm trying to figure out. So far, I've determined that they are spirits of some kind.
Considering their tendency to be animalistic, my leading theory is that they are the wandering spirits of deceased sea monsters.
Are they all creatures of the sea, though?
From what I've witnessed so far, no.
There are bird-like ones, and mammals, and then some really strange ones, and mammals, and then there are some really strange ones too.
You know, though, that there are more 'monsters' in the Wushanko Isles than live in the sea. My theory is that they are all connected somehow.
Though it's true, we do have a lot of water here, so perhaps that's why we predominantly find sea monsters.
Well, that's just my name for them. It's sort of a joke, but I discovered them, so I got to name them!
You might well already know the word 'kami' - it's sort of our word for...well, it can mean a lot of things - spirits, gods - but we mainly use it when referring to sea monsters.
But the word 'baka', that again can have many meanings - idiot, silly - but I see it in this case being closer to 'mischievous'.
So, 'bakami' means 'idiot gods'?
That's losing the nuance. It's more like 'mischievous spirits of sea monsters'...though they aren't all sea monsters, and some seem friendly, others dangerous.
Mostly, they're quite benign, though.
'Orokami' means much the same thing, though there is a slight difference. Whatever bakami are, orokami are the same but 'more' in some way.

pages.i: Which would you prefer from catching kami?

pages.x: Alright. From now on, any kami spirit you catch, however you catch 'em, will earn you triple the usual experience!
Alright. From now on, any kami spirit you catch barehanded will earn you twice the normal loot! It won't work for opening kami jars, though. That'd be cheating.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up

pages.x: Hello again! And what might I be able to do for you today?

o: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I'm done talking to you, now!

pages.x: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
But, of course! Just have a look at my map.
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I can tell you about the state of the beacons in either direction, up to the last fires that are lit.
I could probably tell you about the other beacons as well, but I'd need the help of a macaw.
A macaw?
Yes. Macaws have the ability to fly high into the air and see things that are much further away.
They are also highly intelligent and can be trained to provide the exact information I'd need for a complete overview of the beacon network.
How's it going?
Very well, thank you. We're ever so grateful for your help in testing the beacon network.
Oh, it was no big deal. You're doing most of the hard work, standing watch like that.
To be honest, I'd intended to become an 'Arcanist', but due to an administrative error, I ended up being put forward as an 'Arsonist'.
Go figure.
Still, things worked out for the best. It's a great honour to play such an important role in protecting the kingdom.
I'm done talking to you, now!
Goodbye, then. Stop by again if you're in the neighbourhood - it's nice to have the company.

conversations.section: During The Bird and the Beast / Armadylean / Dragon token

pages.x: Ah, one of Armadyl's most loyal supporters. We are delighted to see you. What can we do for you?
How's the battle going?
Can you tell me about the gods?
I have questions about you.
Please, ask.
Who are you?
Where are you from?
Why do you follow Armadyl?
How is it you survived the aviansie's destruction? (After asking anything else)
What happened after the God Wars? (After asking anything else)
My ancestors returned home to Abbinah from Gielinor. They were deserters.
My people formed the same tribes as before, but lived as Armadyl wanted them to live: at peace.
We survived, long enough for Armadyl to find us again. He had been roaming the universe, mourning us. He returned to Abbinah and realised that we lived.
The celebrations lasted for a full year.
We are fighting to end the war between gods. What happened to us cannot happen to anyone else.
Back to the present.
I have a question about my orders.
I have no more questions.
May Armadyl guide us to freedom.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Dialogue 5

pages.x: Hi!
Hmm... 3rd Age... No, no... maybe 4th...
Hello?
Yes, that's it, just like that. Mustn't forget the map either... hmm... what else?
HELLO! Are you there?
Oh, hello there. Sorry, was a bit engrosed in updating this display. I've just been out questing and thought I'd stop off here you see. It's quite rewarding too.
Yes, well, no need to ignore me.
No offence intended, my dear [chap/girl]. Just very interested in this history stuff, that's all.
Okay. Have you seen the Natural History exhibit in the basement?
Torrcs: Oh, yes, marvellous isn't it! I particularly like the wyvern, very interesting considering they've never found a live specimen.
And to think they could possibly have been flapping around at one time!
A bit like the crazy gnomes and their gliders. Have you seen the model they have upstairs?
Yes, very intricate isn't it? Worrying to think some people risk their lives in them! You wouldn't catch me up in one.
Had a chat with Jacques while I was up there, the art critic... he's a bit funny in the head.
That's not very nice!
Well, he thinks he's going to get an entire portrait gallery to himself!
Who knows, the Museum just got really big and appears to have cash. They might entertain him with his very own floor - we'll see.
I guess so. Wonder what poetry he'll come up with then! Still, I must get on with this display. See you around I hope!
Bye!

conversations.section: Talk to / If the player isn't a Player Moderator / In Ardougne

pages.x: Hear ye! Hear ye! Player Moderators massive help to RuneSc-
Oh, hello citizen. Are you here to find out about Player Moderators? Or perhaps would you like to know about the laws of the land?

o: Tell me about the Rules of RuneScape.
Can you give me a handy tip please?
Toggle Ring of Life teleport location
Tell me about the Achievement System.
Could I buy a spare of the reward?
I'd like to change my teleport point.

pages.x: Very well: the Achievement System is a collection of deeds you may wish to complete while adventuring around the world.
You can earn special rewards for completing certain achievements; at the very least, each is worth a cash bounty from Explorer Jack in Lumbridge.
Some also give items that will help complete other achievements, and many count as progress towards the set for the area they're in.

o: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
How do I claim these rewards?

pages.x: Tell me about the set reward for this locality.
For completing the Ardougne set, you are presented with a cloak.
This cloak will become increasingly useful with each difficulty level of the set that you complete.
When you are presented with your rewards, you will be told of their uses.
How do I claim the rewards?
You need to complete all of the Tasks in a set of a particular difficulty, then you can claim your reward.
Some of the Ardougne set's Tasks are simple, some will require certain skill levels, and some might require quests to be started or completed.
To claim your Ardougne set rewards, speak to Doctor Orbon in East Ardougne church, Aleck in Yanille, or myself.
I'd like to change my Watchtower Teleport point.

conversations.section: After The Feud

pages.x: I don't have time to talk right now! Ali Morrisane is paying me to hand out these flyers.

o: What is there to do here?

pages.x: Who is Ali Morrisane?
Ali Morrisane is the greatest merchant in the east!
Were you paid to say that?
Of course I was! You can find him in the north edge of town.
What are the flyers for?
Well, Ali Morrisane isn't too popular with the other traders in Al Kharid, mainly because he's from Pollniveach and they feel he has no business trading in their town.
