I think they're just sour because he's better at making money than them.
The flyer advertises the different shops you can find in Al Kharid.
It also entitles you to money off on your next purchase in any of the shops listed on it. It's Ali's way of getting on the good side of traders.
Which shops?
What is there to do round here?
I'm very busy, so listen carefully! I shall say this only once.
To the south is the busy and wondrous market of Al Kharid, and to the south are the ruins of the Duel Arena, now known as Het's Oasis.
If you're here to make money, there is a mine to the south. Watch out for scorpions, though, they'll take a pop at you if you go too near them.
To avoid them, just follow the western cliff as you travel south.
If you're in mood for a little rest and relaxation, there are a couple of nice fishing spots south of the town.
Thanks for the help!

conversations.section: When talked to

pages.x: Hey there, what can I do for you?

o: What do you do in the Wizards' Tower?
Do you know if I could make a bigger essence pouch?

pages.x: I'm an apprentice at the Wizards' Tower. I'm here to share knowledge of the Runespan and help others within their travels.
You can buy various things from me that should aid you within the Runespan.
I have runesphere and yellow wizard teleports which will allow you to get around easier.
I can also provide you with the master runecrafters outfit should you be ready for it.
Lastly, I have a range of altar teleportation tablets that can be used to take you directly to the centre of the mysterious ruins containing rune altars!
Do you know if I could make a bigger essence pouch?
In theory, yes!

o: What would I need to make it?
I lost some of the parts.

pages.x: Where could I make it?
At an altar, of course! Only something like that should have the binding energy to create such an item.
What would I need to make it?
Powerful materials, that's for sure.
You could possibly repurpose a Wicked hood as the basis of the pouch - I happen to have a Hungry hood I could sell you for that purpose.
Of course, you'd probably also need the power of other essence pouches, too.
Something that taps into dimensional energy like that would definitely need a protective sleeve of some kind, perhaps made from some strong types of leather...
Oh! You'll need a way to bind it shut, too.
I've heard talk of a magic thread that was spotted when crafting runes after entering the altar ruins directly, which could work.

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander, before The Mighty Fall / At Zanik’s Room in Dorgesh-Kaan

pages.x: Hello, Player.

o: What have you been up to?

pages.x: What have you been up to?
I crossed the river into Morytania; the whole land was so gloomy and depressing.

There was a whole castle full of strange creatures, and a swamp… I found this nice little town… Or at least I thought it was nice… But when I was in the bar I accidentally spilt someone’s drink, and they all turned into wolf-men!
I spent some time in Keldagrim. Some of the people were nice, but I didn’t like the city so much. Everything was so industrial and it was all controlled by corporations.
I ended up hanging out with this dwarf who ate a lot of kebabs. I don’t quite remember what happened after that. I think I got a bit drunk!
I went and talked to Juna again, but she wouldn’t talk to me. She still says I should have helped Bandos take over Dorgesh-Kaan.
She says I had no right to go against my ‘destiny’. She thinks that gods should always get what they want, just because they’re gods, and that mortals just don’t matter.
I didn’t realise she thought such hateful things.
We used to be such good friends… Back when the city was still cut off, I used to sit with her for hours, listening to her stories of the surface and just imagining what it was like.
I can see the surface for myself now, but still, I’m going to miss that.
I visited Varrock the other day. It’s such a huge city, isn’t it? Even bigger than home! There were so many people!
I met a gypsy who said she could foresee the future, but she couldn’t see mine!
I visited the Kharidian Desert. I’ve never seen such a big expanse of empty ground! After growing up in these confined caves, it was amazing!
Just the yellow ground and the blue sky, and me in the middle. I found a ruined city where there was a man made out of clay.
He said he was left over from the God Wars and he said you had repaired him.
Goodbye.
Goodbye Player. See you soon.

conversations.section: The Bird and the Beast / Bandosian / Gold faction token

pages.x: Your courage in battle has been recognised by Bandos. How can I help you?
How's the battle going?
Our warriors out there are too weak. We're at a stalemate with the Armadylean forces. Show them the strength of Bandos by wreaking their convoys.
Can you tell me about the gods?
Bandos is the strongest of all warriors. When he wins battles, he doesn't win by margins, he wins by great distances. He is a master strategist.
He can turn certain defeat into a rout. And the troops die, knowing they supported the great god Bandos.
The devices I create are used by Bandos himself, and I am proud to serve him in the ultimate victory.
Armadyl's under the impression that the gods can live in peace. Sounds like madness to me. War thrives - that never changes. Armadyl has only failed in the past.
He doesn't understand what it's like to win. Do you want someone on the throne who has never tasted success?
Once Bandos defeats him, there'll be no place for his weakness in this world.
Guthix did all he could to dodge war. If he was so strong, so ancient, then why did he only delay the other gods? He must have known the storm he was brewing.
People see him as great, but I see him as a coward. The weak always die eventually.
I have questions about you.
I have questions about my orders.
Protect our caravans as they gather energy. Smash the Armadylean caravans. Build defenses along the roads. Show the power of Bandos to those who are unconvinced.
I'm hoping we get more recruits like you.
I have no more questions.
Then go join the battle! For Bandos!

conversations.section: In Varrock Palace, before River of Blood

pages.x: Please only talk to the King if it's important. He has a heavy burden to bear with the running of his Kingdom.

o: How did you come to be an advisor to King Roald?}}

pages.x: Apologies! Allow me to introduce myself: my name is Aeonisig Raispher, special advisor to King Roald on spiritual matters.
Special advisor on spiritual matters? What does that mean?
It means that some decisions the King has to make might have unforeseen repercussions on the nation's spiritual sensibilities.
My duty is to ensure that Saradominist ideals are not stomped underfoot.

o: How did you come to be an advisor to King Roald?

pages.x: My main function is to ensure that King Roald is apprised of all options, especially those that favour the righteous followers of Saradomin.
But surely the King should be able to make his own decisions on what's best for Misthalin?
What an interesting perspective you have! Totally unworkable of course, but interesting nonetheless.

o: How did you come to be an advisor to King Roald?

pages.x: I took my religious and combat training in several parts of the known world. I've also fought despicable beasts in the wilderness in Saradomin's name.
Needless to say I have great experience in the ways of the world and am an invaluable aid to his lordship's decision-making process.

o: How did you come to be an advisor to King Roald?

pages.x: The King of Misthalin, like any great leader, always requires the best advice and the best advisors.

He very often summons occasional advisors to help him in certain situations, but it was felt by the Church of Saradomin that a full time advisor on religious matters was needed to ensure fair treatment of Saradomin's followers.
How come he doesn't have an advisor for any other religious denominations?
Because I simply won't stand for it, that's why! Now, enough of your impertinent questions. I have work to do!

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / After Diamond in the Rough

pages.x: Welcome! It is good to see you again. How can I be of service, friend of Al Kharid?
Though I met Ozan only briefly, I could tell that he has a good heart.
He has a sharp tongue too...but he is not lacking in responsibility or honour.
But I find upon my return that he took the Kharid-ib against my father's wishes, and to rescind my father's last order would be to dishonour him.
So, as things stand, Al Kharid must view Ozan as an traitor to be arrested upon sight.
Personally, I hope it does not come to that. In fact, if he were ever to return the Kharid-ib, I would welcome him home as a brother.
My father did not tell me all of the Kharid-ib's secrets, but he did tell me enough to know its true value to Al Kharid.
It may seem harsh to you that he would value it above even his own son's life, but I understand his reasons.
Of greater concern to me is that the Menaphites, and Amascut, not only have the diamond, but also know something of it.
We cannot rely on Ozan alone to return it. Osman is also doing what he can and, when the time comes, I hope we can rely upon you again too.
As a prisoner, I was privy to much that my kidnappers spoke of. I am convinced this is all part of some wider Menaphite plot.
And I now believe that, even during the war, their primary goal has always been to obtain the Kharid-ib.
Now that they have it, the gods only know what their next step will be.
I shall attempt to maintain the peace as long as possible...but I have assigned Osman to look into this matter further. We will have answers.
Yes, it is the most troubling aspect of all of this. That the Devourer herself would directly intervene in such a way terrifies me.
Since the end of the God Wars, the history of the desert is rife with reports of her destructive tendencies.
And now she is behind my kidnap and the theft of the Kharid-ib. I only hope that whatever she is up to can be stopped in time, because whatever it is, it won't be good.

conversations.section: Using the red strange glowing orb on the statue / Before using the orb on Merethiel

pages.x: I see you.
Everything you've done.
Everything you are...
You are nothing compared to me...
This world... This weak world still shakes with my influence even years later...
You do not know the power I've awoken...
Who are you?

o: As you speak the orb glows more intense and begins to hurt.

pages.x: I am the wind that whips at your skin.
I am the earth that will claim your bones.
I.. I don't understand.
You wouldn't.
Be still player name.
Pain...
Fear...
Let me go!
I can feel it coursing through you.

o: As the last words pierce your ears, you feel the orb go ice cold.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Welcome, adventurer. Have you come to hear a tale, or to share one?
My name is Artiefax. I am a teacher and storyteller who keeps the written and oral histories of our people, as my father did before me.
I've recently become interested in collections of artefacts from ages past.
These are not false idols or treasures to be coveted. They are the bearers of tales, and lessons, long forgotten.
That's a beautiful way of looking at it.
Occasionally the past is beautiful. More often it is sordid, violent or tragic. Many stories the past offers are far from pleasant.
But they have much to teach us nonetheless.
Do you want to view my collections or discuss them?

pages.i: What would you like to do?

pages.x: Tell me more about your collections.
Word travels of a land seldom visited. Havenhythe.
Within it lie the remnants of a people who venerated Guthix, as we do, in an age long passed.
From the little I've gleamed they fell astray, debasing the beliefs and values they once held dear.
I would see the artefacts left by these people and learn their tale, so that it may be shared with my people. Thus, we can avoid repeating their mistakes.
After this, these pieces of history shall be returned to the earth, as it is meant to be.
A noble aim. I'll help you if I can.
Farewell.

conversations.section: Talking to Azibo

pages.x: Hi there!
Hi, Azibo.
Want to see my spinning plates or kites? Want to check out my range of party items? Or did you want an item back?

o: I'd like to check my items, please.
Can you check my bank for items?

pages.x: Spinning plates?
There was a mix-up some years back with a man who lives in Draynor - something about 'dragon plates' being confused for armour.
Wow, a kite!
You're not the first to say that...
Can I have one, please?
Well, I suppose I did order more than I need... It's yours for the bargain price of 100 coins.

o: That's a bargain! I'll take one.
No, thanks, I don't want one.

pages.x: That's a bargain! I'll take one.
No, thanks, I don't want one.
Party items, you say?
Yes, I have all sorts of stuff - confetti, bubble makers, fireworks, firecrackers and some mugs! Take a look!
Sure thing, let me just see what you're missing.
Sure thing, let me see what I can take off your hands.
I'll look through items that I will hold onto, items that could go into a costume room in your house and junk items.

conversations.section: In Taverley

pages.x: Hello there.

o: What’s that walking next to you?

pages.x: Hello. Who are you?
My name is Bettamax, I’m a botanist in training.
What’s a botanist?
Someone that studies and identifies different plants and their properties.
What are you studying?
Currently nothing. I’m waiting for Astlayrix, my mentor, to come back from the herblore habitat.
Habitat?
Oh, it’s fascinating. There are all these new creatures and plants and, well, I’m probably not the best person to explain it…
If you want to go see for yourself, I have a small stock of these weird teleport-bag things. They’ll take you straight there.

pages.i: Would you like to buy one?

pages.x: Maybe another time.
What’s that walking next to you?
Oh, that’s Wilbur. He’s a jadinko.
What’s a jadinko?
I have no idea.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hey again, how can I help you?
Could you tell me about The Drop?
Of course! The Drop is an interactive trivia game. You'll be asked a series of RuneScape themed questions.
Answer every question correctly and you'll bag yourself a nice reward. Each time you play, Jagex will donate £1 to charity, up to a whopping maximum of £34,500!
Great, thank you!
Are there any rewards involved?
Of course! If you answer all of the questions correctly, you'll bag yourself the 'Apart Together' title. You'll also bag yourself some prismatic stars and lamps.
Additionally, just for participating, Jagex will donate £1 to charity, up to a whopping maximum of £34,500!
Great, thank you!
Could you give me some more information about charity?
Of course! I'm Charity, I spend a lot of my time... Only joking! Jagex will be making a donation of £100,000 to our mental health charity partners.
Players can help meet this goal by entering The Drop! For each participation, £1 will be donated to charity.

o: Yes, take me to the newspost.

pages.x: Goodbye.
Bye for now.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / After giving him a cave eel

pages.x: Hi, what you doing here again? You want something?

o: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I'm done talking to you, now!

pages.x: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Well, have look at my map, then. But hurry up.
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
Hmm, me have sharp eyes, can see very far. Can tell you all about lit beacons in both directions from here. But, little flappy macaw can see much further still.
Flappy macaw?
If you brings Crate a little flappy macaw, I tell you anything you want to know about ALL de beacons!
Macaw can fly high into air and see long distance. They smart enough to report about things very much far away.
How's it going?
Hmm, pressure of job very great, but I strong and eyes are sharp. They only pick very important trolls for this sort of job.
You must feel very proud.
Of course. But, having so many trolls respect me and having so much work to do make me very, very hungry.
Hmm, must be difficult.
Oh, it is. Someone like you could never understand.
I'm done talking to you, now!
Hmph.

conversations.section: Activating the grim gem

pages.x: What is it mortal? Time is ticking.
How am I doing so far?
I have requested that you collect souls from the following: [Boss name]. I require X more before your task is complete.
Can you give me any hints?
What do you want from me?
As you are no doubt aware, I am Death. The Reaper, the Collector of Souls, or any other name civilisations have given me.
My task is to retrieve the soul from a dying creature, enabling its passage to the underworld.
So what do you need me for?
There is an imbalance in the harmony of life and death. There is far too much... life. My eyes have been on you in this age, Player, as have the eyes of many others.
You appear to have the skills I require to bring balance.
So you want me to kill stuff?
If you wish to put it so indelicately, yes.
Great! When do I start?
Immediately. I have already tasked you to collect souls from the following battle: [Boss name]. You have yet to bring me X souls.
Where are you?
You may find me in my office, a portal to which may be accessed south of Draynor Manor.
Nothing, thanks.

conversations.section: Before The Dig Site / Talk to option

pages.x: Hello there.
Good day; what can I do for you?
What do you do here?
I am involved in various stages of the dig, from the initial investigation to the installation of the mine shafts.
Oh, okay, thanks.
I'm not sure...
Well, let me know when you are.
Can I dig around here?
You can only use a site you have the appropriate exam level for.

o: I am already skilled in digging.

pages.x: Appropriate exam level?
Yes, only persons with the correct Earth Sciences certificate can dig here. A level 1 certificate will let you dig in a level 1 site and so on.
Ah, yes; I understand.
I am already skilled in digging.
Well that's nice for you. You can't dig around here without a certificate though.

conversations.section: After completing Fate of the Gods but before completing Battle of the Monolith

pages.x: Hello again.
Greetings. I await the return of my Lord Azzanadra and of our god. I do not know why, but I feel this spot has some significance...

pages.i: Tell Eblis that Zaros has returned?

pages.x: About that...
What? What is it?
Yeah, so...Zaros IS back.
Really? Where? You'd better not be joking!
He's...actually, you know, I'm not sure where. I'd assume at Senntisten Temple.
Are you sure? What did he look like? Is he coming here?
Positive - I helped make it happen. He looked strong...divine... I think he'd rather the other gods didn't know he was back, though.
Of course. I...I shall not tell a soul. You're definitely sure? Yes, of course you are.
Surely it is only a matter of time now before Lord Azzanadra returns to us with new instruction.
Actually...about that...
What? What is it?
Oh, er, never mind.
You know, I think you're right - there does seem to be something special about this spot. There's an abundance of anima and divine energy in the area.
Perhaps some remnant of the Zaros-Kharid war?
Maybe?

conversations.section: Before learning about glassblowing

pages.x: Hello adventurer, welcome to the Entrana furnace.
Would you like me to explain my craft to you?

o: Yes please. I'd be fascinated to hear what you do.
No thanks, I doubt I'll ever turn my hand to glassblowing.

pages.x: Yes please. I'd be fascinated to hear what you do.
I'm extremely pleased to hear that! I've always wanted an apprentice. Let me talk you through the secrets of glassblowing.
your nets sometimes when you're fishing, on Karamja island or at the Piscatoris Fishing Colony in the nets there.
To turn seaweed into soda ash, all you need to do is burn it on a fire. Feel free to use the range in my house for
that; it's the one directly west of here.
Next we collect sand from the sandpit that you'll also find just west of here, there are others located in Yanille and Shilo Village.
There are many things you can use the molten glass for once you have made it.
Depending on how talented you are, you could try turning it into something, like a fishbowl, for example. If you'd like to try your hand at the
fine art of glassblowing you can use my spare glassblowing pipe. I think I left it on the chest of drawers in my house this morning.
Alternatively I am always happy to buy the molten glass from you, saves me running about making it for myself.
That sounds good. How much will you pay me?
Tell you what, because you've been interested in my art, I'll pay you the premium price of 20 gold pieces for each piece of molten glass you bring me.
No thanks, I doubt I'll ever turn my hand to glassblowing.
Ok, suit yourself. Nobody seems to be interested in the skilled crafts these days.
If you should change your mind, come back and talk to me.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / Having completed the Stronghold of Security

pages.x: Hi. What you want?

o: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
I'm done talking to you, now!

pages.x: Could you look after this beacon for me?
Can you tell me about other beacons?
Yes. Have a look at my map.
Is it possible to get information about beacons that are further away?
Hmm. My eyes good. Can tell you about all beacons in either direction, as long as they lit.
I could tell about the other beacons as well, if I have help of macaw.
A macaw?
Yes. Macaw can fly high into air and see long distance. They also very smart creatures.
Macaw can fly into air and then report back about whole beacon network.
How's it going?
Very, very quiet. No danger in sight.
That's great!
On contrary. Then when danger is greatest! Nothing more dangerous than danger one can't see or hear.
Now, unless you have good questions, becone. I must watch and listen.
I'm done talking to you, now!
Then leave me be! I have more important things to do than listen to you continue speaking.

conversations.section: First time dialogue

pages.x: Can you teach me about the grand exchange?
I most certainly can, but you'll get more complete and entertaining information if you speak with Brugsen Bursen who is standing to my side.

o: I want the basics from you.
I like entertainment, I shall go speak with Brugsen.

pages.x: I want the basics from you.
Let's begin, then.
Let me describe the process in four steps:
Step 1: You come here with items to sell or money to spend.
Step 2: Speak with one of the clerks, at the desks in the corners of the building. They will help you set up your bid.
When you're setting up a bid, we'll show you a guide price for each item. This is just a suggestion, though: you can offer any amount you like.
Step 3: The clerks will take the items or money off you and look for someone to complete the trade. This may be very fast, or it could take several days.
Step 4: When the trade is complete, we will send you a message. You can collect your stuff by talking to the clerks or by visiting any banker.
There's plenty more information about the Grand Exchange, all of which can be found out from Brugsen Bursen, the guy with the megaphone.
I would suggest you speak with him to fully get to grips with the Grand Exchange. Good luck!
I like entertainment, I shall go speak with Brugsen.
As you wish.
I'm not interested in either!
Okay, bye!

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander

pages.x: Hello, Player.
How do you like it here?
I very happy. Oldak not shout at me or tell me do stupid things. And he not care what colour clothes I wear.
What are you doing here?
I Oldak's assistant!
At first I think it wrong for me to do magic, but then I think, maybe Big High War God want me to show magic to Dorgesh-goblins and that why he let me do it.
What do you think about what Zanik and I did?
Chosen Commander fulfil prophecy. She kill false Big High War God, so now goblins can worship real Big High War God.
This means we have victory over world and live in peace. It spiritual victory.
You're deluded.
I not mind that you not believe. Oldak not believe either but that not matter, we still friends.

conversations.section: Telling your story to Gwir / After Within The Light

pages.x: Arianwyn called for me once again. Thorgel, a dwarf I met in the temple, had sent word of the temple releasing some sort of energy.
It was clear Arianwyn knew this was going to lead somewhere, so, after a few tasks, he was disguised and we went to investigate together.
Where did this investigation lead?
Well, with Arianwyn's insight, it led to me being energised in a similar way to the crystal I used to restart the temple's defences.
And this was safe?
I survived, if that's what you mean. The energy wasn't lethal, but it did somewhat...transport me?
Transport you where?
Into the light itself. The elves who built that temple must have been powerful, indeed. There was a whole other section in there with more light switches.
So what did these switches do?
After I had figured out how to activate the switches, I finally managed to open the massive door in the room.
It led to a corridor, which had unfortunately been the victim of a large cave-in.
Was this corridor still within the light or was it in the real world again, so to speak?
A great question. Either it was still within the light or it served as bridge between the Temple of Light and somewhere else.
What makes you think that?
A body - there was a body in there. It was a dead elf messenger who must have perished in the rockslide.
The report that he was carrying is where I learned of Prifddinas's fate.
This I have heard, everyone is talking about it! The revelation that the city was reverted to crystal form...an entire city!
Indeed, and right now there are miners working to clear that cave-in so we can work towards restoring the city, once all threats to it are removed.

Your yelling about Lumbridge has to be unbearably effervescent, I presume?

YIPPEE!

You know me too well.

conversations.section: Dialogue / After The World Wakes

pages.x: I would like to talk about Guthix's death.
I cannot say it is something I wish to think about.
Sorry Juna, but we cannot ignore it. I just wanted to ask some questions.
I'd like some advice about being a Guardian of Guthix.
Guthix chose you as a Guardian because he could already see it in you.
You were chosen to be one of us because you showed not only a great talent, but also an understanding of balance, and the potential to be much more.
With Guthix's death, and the knowledge he imparted to you, he clearly intends us to become an army against the young gods.
You should think on what he told you; remember his intentions when giving you his power. He wants you to lead the defence of this world.
Surely the other Guardians can help? Where did they go?
Of course. We will be by your side whenever you need us, but in the mean time we must all continue our previous duties.
I cannot leave these caves unattended, Death cannot abandon his role... Guthix may be gone, but that does not mean we should abandon our posts.
What do you think will happen now?
We have already seen it begin. Saradomin has already returned.
The others will come. Nothing has changed, Player, they will be as determined and greedy as they were thousands of years ago.
We are on the brink of another God Wars. If we do not act, the world will be ravaged. Guthix is not here to stop them, this time. It is up to us.
How are you feeling?
It is very difficult to speak about. I can't believe...
I'm sorry, I'm not ready to discuss this with anyone. It's too painful.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge during the 25th Anniversary celebrations

pages.x: Hello, what are you doing here?
Celebrating the anniversary, but also mourning all that we have lost.
This past ten years has been filled with trying times and sad stories.
It has felt to me like the world was thrown out of balance, ever since...
You don't have to say. I've felt it too. I think we all have.
It was the return of the gods - that started right here with the Battle of Lumbridge, which caused that crater right above where my nest is.
People have been fighting among themselves ever since, split into factions, and their hearts overtaken by greed.
The Tears of Guthix have been weeping heavily ever since, and I with them...
But one cannot remain lost in grief forever, and it is finally starting to feel as if the mood is shifting.
Very true.
That is why I came to visit - both to honour the past, but also to look to the future, and what better time to reinvent oneself than an anniversary? Change is coming.
What changes?
Did you not see the crater has gone? It has not just healed, it has been rejuvenated!
It is not just the crater either. I have heard many stories of positive change across our world.
And even here, you can see disparate people rejoining hands - old friendships are renewed.
Their joy, too, is palpable. It no longer feels that everyone is in it for themselves. Greed is giving way to generosity.
True, there are many wounds to heal, and many friendships to be rekindled, but it truly feels like hope is returning to Gielinor once again, and balance with it.
You know, I think you're on to something. Here's to the future!

How do you know these things?

I listen to the earth, commune with the anima. I know what lies ahead.

There is an enormous pool of anima hidden within this place, world guardian. A supply of Gielinor's lifeblood so great it has come to be known as 'the Heart'.
Access to the pool has proved elusive indeed. It is what the generals here have been fighting for all this time.
Each of them have come so close, yet they are further than they can realise while they still stand against each other.

A sigil is needed to step through the threshold. A sigil that was broken into four pieces long ago.
Now those pieces lie in the hands of each general. Still together in this place, yet separated by four clashing armies.
It is you who must reunite them, Player. Slay the generals and take back the sigil pieces from their lifeless bodies.
When the entrance reveals itself - as it soon will - you will need the complete sigil to enter.
Tread lightly, world guardian.

conversations.section: What do we know so far?

pages.x: So what information do we have compiled so far?
The Mahjarrat are powerful creatures with a strong aptitude for magic including the ability to change their form and look like other creatures.
There are a number of Mahjarrat active in the world.
Jhallan, who you helped hibernate in the north, seems much weaker than I'd expect the Mahjarrat to be.
You spoke of a Rejuvenation Ritual, perhaps he was not present at the last ritual.
There is Zemouregal, who controls many zombies, including the once great hero Arrav. Zemouregal seems to have a penchant for attacking Varrock.
Enakhra is a female Mahjarrat and follower of Zamorak. She is a rival of Akthanakos, who is a follower of Zaros.
There's General Khazard, who is currently wandering the Shadow Realm.
There is Azzanadra, who you freed from a pyramid he was trapped in and who then taught you how to use a lot of useful magic.
Later in your travels, you met Azzanadra again. He was disguised so that he could restore the Zarosian temple under the Digsite without arousing too much suspicion.
Once the temple was complete it formed a communication link between Azzanadra and Zaros.
So, although Zaros has not physically returned, he is able to command those loyal to him once again. It seems that the stage is set for a rather dramatic act, no?
There is Lucien, who is now looking particularly dangerous and powerful, even for a Mahjarrat.
First, he gained control of the Staff of Armadyl and now he has the Stone of Jas, which could be the most powerful artefact known to Gielinor.
It's possible he even has aspirations to become a god.
There are many more Mahjarrat with names like Bilrach, Kharshai, Sliske and Wahisietel. Some more powerful than others. Many seem to follow the evil god Zamorak.
Others seem to follow another, more obscure god of debatable alignment called Zaros.
They all seem to be preparing for a forthcoming Ritual, where one of them will be killed.

pages.x: What do you think of the Wizards' Tower?
It's interesting. I don't understand the first thing about magic, but it's still interesting.
They handle it so differently from how Oldak does. He's just trying things out on his own. Sometimes they work, but more often they don't and he tries something else.
Here, the wizards have hundreds of years of tradition to draw upon. They can do so much more than Oldak...
but I get the impression they don't really understand what they're doing, some of the time.
What are you doing here?
Well, I came here to get some books for Oldak. He's been in touch with some of the wizards here through letters, so I wanted to see what this place was like for myself.
Then, when I got here, old Wizard Traiborn asked to look for something called a 'thingummywut'. I looked all over but I couldn't find it.
I'm starting to think it doesn't exist.
There's no such thing as Thingummywuts; Wizard Traiborn is mad.
Haha! I thought as much.
The Thingummywut is definitely around here somewhere.
Oh, well, I'll keep looking then.

conversations.section: Burthorpe / Talking to Turael / At the start

pages.x: 'Ello, and what are you after, then?
Well, you've come to the right place.
I like how you think! You've come to the right place.
Then you've come to the right place!
I'm a Slayer master. I train adventurers to seek out and defeat specific monsters. I'll identify suitable targets and assign you a quota.
Burthorpe is surrounded by dangerous creatures. Are you eager to battle monsters for fun, heroism, and profit? Then Slayer is the skill for you!
Trolls are the real enemy in Burthorpe, but you'll need food and armour to survive against them. You should prepare before risking your life in combat.
This is the last adventurer they sent me. He fought the trolls without armour or food. Don't be him. In combat, you'll need to eat to live.
Rabbits are a good source of food, and they make a cute noise when they die. Go kill some bunnies!
Burthorpe is surrounded by dangerous creatures. Trolls to the north, wolves to the west, goblins in the east...
And don't even get me started on the Guthix-damned rabbits.
We're in the eye of the storm, and it's the duty of the Order of the Slayer Masters to keep that blood-shot eye wide open.
CUTE? Hah! The little blighters are voracious vermin. The Burthorpe rabbit population is out of control.
It's your ecological and civic duty to slay as many 'bunnies' as you can. Plus, it's fun. Go on; try it!
You can bank your items at the bank booth to the south-west of me.

conversations.section: Dialogue

pages.x: Hi.
Greetings young one. What wisdom do you seek?

o: What do I have to do in this room?
Got any tips that may help me?

pages.x: In this room you will see various cupboards. It is your task to search the cupboards to find items to turn into gold using your low or high alchemy spells.
You must deposit the money in the receptacle at the end of the hall in order to receive your Alchemist Pizazz Points, otherwise the money will be taken from you as you leave through the portal.
This money is used for the upkeep of the training arena as well as magic shops all around Gielinor.
Keep an eye on the costs of each item as these will change from time-to-time, as will the location of the items.
Occasionally one of the items will be indicated as costing no runestones to convert to money.

You will get magic experience from casting the alchemist spells, as well as 1 Alchemist Pizazz Point for every 100 coins you deposit, and 10% of the coins you deposit will be given to you as you leave.
Keep in mind that you will not be able to take more than 1000 coins back out with you.
You must remember to keep an eye on the various costs of the items.
If you watch the movements of the other players, you might be able to guess which are the best places to visit.
You will get 1 Pizazz Point for every 100 coins, so if you have 190 coins, why not get an extra 10?
I see.

Oh, and a word of warning: should you decide to leave this room by a method other than the exit portals, you will be teleported to the entrance and have any items that you picked up in the room removed.
And that includes gold coins, for which you won't get any Pizazz Points for!
Use what you've learned, young one.

conversations.section: Conversation 2 (Burthorpe Castle)

pages.x: Hello there! How is it going?
Uh... we're not supposed to talk while we're on duty.
Oh, sorry, I didn't realise...
You know what; It's not your fault. I might as well have a chat.
I mean, this is supposed to be a secure military installation, you know? That's why they told us not to talk.
And then they went and wedged the front doors open and put a ladder of all things up along the wall!
Do you have any idea how many people I've almost shot when they peek over the wall there?
There is a war on! We could be knee-deep in trolls any second now! What are they thinking?
It does seem a little odd...
Tell me about it. Next thing you know they'll build one of those house portals up here.
Then we'll have adventurers and householders popping out across the ramparts for a stroll, kids playing with the cannons...
I can see it now... 'Oh Mr Archer, Could you and your friends be dears and move? We have a dinner party at seven and you're ruining the ambiance.'
'Do you mind if we put up some hanging baskets? Only this parapet is frightfully grim'.
Well, so long as things don't get that bad, you'll be all right, right?
Yeah, well, we can but hope.
Whoops, looks like I've been spotted. See you about, ok?
Yeah, good luck!

conversations.section: In the Merchant district of Menaphos, after The Jack of Spades / First time claiming the journal

pages.x: Hello there, outsider, come talk; not too loud, though!
What is it?
I was wondering if you could help me. I work at the Grand Library, and we have lost some of our records recently.
Lost them? How did that happen?
Shhh! Not so loud. Well, you see, the authorities have been clamping down on almost everyone recently. They confiscated a lot of the collections in the library.
Our most important collections lost were...
Our prized collection of Kharidian insects, both old and new.
The old preserved in amber from the days when these lands were filled with forests; the new that irritate us on a daily basis.
The priceless Jewels of the Elid collection, comprising of numerous precious mineral samples, and some completely unique gems which we managed to smuggle out of the library.
In our haste we managed to lose track of some of them.
Some can be replaced with fresh samples, but the unique gemstones will need to have their current holders tracked down.
OK.
And the register of honored cats of the Feline Order of Menaphos. We will need to regain the signatures of each of the cats on this list.
What? Why are you looking at me like that?
Nothing, how can I help?
Here, take this journal. I've put some suggestions for locating all the things in there.

pages.x: Hey, Dave! You know you're not allowed to use the exchange.
What? Why?
You know why!
Let's say for the sake of argument that I don't. Could you explain?
Because last year you bought all that shadow dye! You don't even own anything tough enough to withstand it. You dissolved three of your poor mum's dresses!
Oh, uh, I'm very sorry about that. But look, I really need some runes.
What for?
I need to stop a friend from making a terrible mistake I'll get blamed for.
Okay Dave, seeing as it's you. What kind of runes are you after?
Do I look like I'm made of money?
Actually, yes.
Well, yes, I suppose I sort of do. But I won't be able to afford any more nice suits if I just hand out law runes left and right.
Oh, I don't have any earth runes I'm afraid. You might try speaking to one of the bankers though. I think I heard something about a competition.
Yes, I have a few air runes I might be able to spare for you. I want something in return though.
What?
I really need something to drink. Be a mate and go fetch us one, would you?

conversations.section: After Swan Song, in the Piscatoris Fishing Colony

pages.x: Hello! What can I do for you?

o: How are things going for the Colony?
You know all your doors get stuck open?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: How are things going for the Colony now the trolls have all gone away?
Well, it's been fairly quiet around here, but there's always repair work to keep us busy.
Catching plenty of fish?
Oh yes, lots of them. Their population's been swelling ever since you wiped out the trolls in the area. They've hardly got any natural predators now.
Oh... I suppose that's good...
I was just wondering what you're doing.
Franklin's got me fixing this wall. You did a pretty good patch-job, but it could do with some work.
I'm not surprised - iron sheets won't last any time at all with all that salt water around.
Yes, that's right. I'll probably get Arnold to order some fancy protective paint from the dwarves.
Good luck with that.
You know all your doors get stuck open?
Yes, the salt does terrible things to the hinges. I've been meaning to deal with them, but I never seem to get around to it.
Fair enough.
Nothing, I'm fine.
Enjoy your fishing.

conversations.section: Before A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains / First time

pages.x: Hello, can I help you at all?

o: What do you do around here?

pages.x: What do you do around here?
Oh, I'm the resident healer. My name is Nuff, Fairy Nuff. Who are you?
My name is Player.
Pleased to meet you, Player. As I was saying, I'm the healer in Zanaris. I graduated over 200 human years ago. Look, there's my Advanced Healing Certificate on the wall.
I never go anywhere without it. It's my job to look after the sick, wounded or dying fairies around here.
Of course, fairies being magical by nature, not many of them get hurt, so I don't normally have much to do.
What about healing humans? Lots of adventurers must get hurt fighting the Otherworldly beings.
Yes, they do. Silly isn't it? I do use my healing magic on humans sometimes, but I don't like them attacking our other guests, so I charge them for the service.
How much do you charge to heal someone, then?
Well, the gold that you humans are so fond of has no real value in Zanaris, so I ask my patients to pay me in gems.
I will heal 40 life points for an opal, 50 life points for either a sapphire or a piece of jade, 70 life points for an emerald or red topaz, 90 for a ruby and 110 for a diamond.
Only 110 life points for a diamond? Doesn't that seem a bit steep?
Maybe to you, but you'd be surprised how many adventurers are willing to pay those prices.
No thanks. Just looking around.
Okay. If you want to know anything, just ask.

conversations.section: Anniversary island

pages.x: Good to see you sweetie!
You're looking well as always, Fame.

o: Why did you move the statues?
What are you planning to do next?

pages.x: I loved the garden that Pete and I made for the fifteenth anniversary celebrations, and I wanted to make sure that it was preserved.
It was so gorgeous, and the world deserves to keep beauty like that.
And, there was the lovely serendipity of the Arc, and all of these new islands, so I knew just what I had to do.
I claimed one as my own and got the statues shipped over here. So they can spend the rest of time in this glorious atmosphere and so everyone can enjoy them.
Don't they look lovely?
Absolutely. It's quite the setting for them.
Well, darling, why wouldn't I be? Don't you just love the atmosphere?
Every star has to have their bolt-hole, their little piece of tranquillity where they can truly be themselves. This is that place for me. My little haven.
So you're staying here?
Well, if my public calls for me, I will of course answer them, it's only right. But for now, this is my home.
It's tiring having so much talent, so I'm taking this time to recuperate so I can come back at full capacity.
Feel free to visit me from time to time, sweetie, your company is always welcome. But, yes, I shall be here until I am completely reinvigorated.
Break a leg, sweetie!

conversations.section: Talk to / After having completed the Archaeology tutorial

pages.x: Hi, I'm Associate Helen! Want me to dig the dirt on soil?
You really need to work on your jokes, but sure.
Great! First up, you should know that each site has a unique soil, but functionally they all work the same.
What are the different soil types?
Well, Kharid-et has ancient gravel. The Infernal Source contains fiery brimstone, and Everlight has saltwater mud.
You'll find aerated sediment up at Stormguard, and down in the Warforge is earthen clay.
How do they differ?
Only in what you might find in them when putting it through the screening station here.
Where you got your grubby little mitts on the soil determines which materials and artefacts you might find when screening it.
Soil can contain artefacts?
Well, artefacts tend to be large, and soil mostly contains materials and other smaller finds...but you can rarely find a figurative diamond in the rough.
I suppose the other thing you should know is that all soils are tradeable, so don't feel like you have to get your hands dirty.
I'm sure there are plenty of interns out there happy to do it for some extra credit.

pages.x: Fishing is more than a method of gathering food. It's more than a profession. It's a way of life!

Well, what it's really about is maintaining the natural balance and that.
See, trees in Gielinor grow pretty wicked fast, and without us to trim them we'd soon be overrun!
'Course it doesn't hurt that you get useful logs in a wide variety of qualities that you can use for making stuff, or even setting light to, if that's your thing.
When you chop down trees, all you're left with are useless logs. BURN THEM TO RELEASE THEIR FIERY HUMOURS!

You just put your sticks together AND STEAL THE POWER OF THE FLAME FROM THE GODS THEMSELVES!
The world is filled with flammable objects straining for release! Join me - we can rebuild this world in flames!
Cooking is how you turn all of your fine but inedible ingredients into something you can eat. Eating is important, especially when you've been wounded in battle.
You'll find a lot of food items in the world. Cook everything you find! Cook things that seem like no one would ever eat them.
The only way to get better at it is to practice. So cook all the fish you catch, all the potatoes you grow, and your skill will improve.
Better cooks make better food, but of course you need better ingredients. Fishing and farming can help you with that.

o: Achieve 99 in all your skills to earn the coveted Max Cape!

conversations.section: 15th year anniversary party garden

pages.x: Hey!
Hi! I'm Party Pete. Welcome to the 15th Anniversary garden!

o: Tell me more about the buff.
How long does this party last?

pages.x: It's a party! RuneScape has hit the big 15 so I'm throwing it a birthday party nobody will forget!
Even if they get too carried away with the party spirit?
Even then. This is a party for the ages!
The party spirit is contagious. Just have some food from the tables, or have some of the cake, and it will give you the party spirit too!
It's a 5% buff for all skilling that you do in the party area for the following 24 hours. Just click it again after the 24 hours are up to reactivate the bonus!
It certainly seems to have worked on you!
Yep. Groovy isn't it?
There are lots of fantastic rewards to go alongside the celebrations! Pop 15 balloons for a snazzy extra, and 50 balloons for a present that'll go with a bang!
Get the party spirit buff, from eating from the party tables, and unlock another present, this time a tasty one!
That all sounds good! Anything else?
Collecting statues also gives you special rewards, when you have collected 4, 8, 12, and 15. Keep your eye out for special unlock messages!
Also, you can get cool things from the balloons, like party hat fragments, starts, lamps and gold, and the chance to unlock a statue!
Not everyone has the party stamina that I have, but we're partying hard until the end of January.
The statue portals can be found until the end of the year, though, so keep hunting!

conversations.section: After Birthright of the Dwarves / When spoken to with a Catspeak amulet

pages.x: Insolent dwarves! How dare they deny me my heritage? I am King Tiddles XIV, rightful king of all cats!

o: Do you have any cat followers?
Can you tell me about the Red Axe?

pages.x: There's a king of cats?
Can you not tell by my resplendent coat? Clearly I am a superior feline and deserve to rule.
Do you have any cat followers?
Not yet, but only because these dwarves refuse to support me!
If they would herd all the world's cats into my throne room as I have told them to, I would soon claim my rightful place!
Can you tell me about the Red Axe?
Incompetent servants, whom I have discarded! Hreidmar's plans showed promise at first, but he let himself be foiled at every turn by a human adventurer!
After his first setback, he made a tactical retreat into smelly, dusty caves. Luckily he saw his error and built a more lavish home for me to live in.
When the dwarves in his company threatened to leave, he transformed them into chaos dwarves!
He was right to punish them of course, but chaos dwarves are impolite and never gave me treats.
He kept on with his pointless experiments. First chaos dwogres, and then chaos giants, although he ever learned to control them.
He did keep them away from the palace though, no doubt out of respect for me.
In the end he abandoned his quest to make me king of cats, and gave up!
Eventually the Black Guard attacked the palace and rescued me so I could pursue my destiny.
Their only mistake was to assign this imbecile as a servant rather than someone competent!

pages.x: Hello!

This is intolerable! I already have plenty to drink, so why would they send a serving [lad/lass] up to see me without my food!

Such impertinence! Inform the head of this establishment that I want you to be dismissed immediately!
But...I don't work here.
What's that? You won't do it? Egad, do you not know who you are dealing with, whelp? I'll tan your hide!

By the gods, you're a fiery one! Never have I been so insulted by a lowly servant...
Repeat after me...
What?
I...don't...work...here.
I...Don't... Dash it all, you scoundrel! Why didn't you tell me you didn't work here?
I did...several times.
Fetch the head of this establishment! I will have your job for embarrassing me!
It's like watching a highly obese dog chasing its pudgy tail.

conversations.section: In East Ardougne market

pages.x: Hello, dearie. Would you like some of my lovely baked goods?
No, thank you.
How lovely - I do like a good natter!
So, how's the sandwich business treating you?
Oh, I can't complain! Well, I could - this market stall is a bit of a step down from the tea shop I used to own.
Oh, why? What happened?
I had to sell up to settle my court fees.
Why would you need to pay court fees? You must be the friendliest person I've ever met!
That's kind of you to say, love...but as nice as I might seem, I do have a bit of a short fuse. All I did was to put one of my baguettes in that gentleman's breadbasket!
That doesn't sound so bad.
Well, it doesn't...until you realise that by 'breadbasket' I mean his stomach...and by 'put in' I mean repeatedly bash with violent force and murderous intent!
And all because he took a pie when I'd only offered him a sandwich!
When you put it like that...
You'd at least think it would give me reputation enough to stop the thieving beggars around here pinching from my stall!
But no - I'm still seen as that lovely old sandwich lady, wouldn't hurt a fly. So you'd best not steal from me or I'll knock your loaf off!
No, ma'am!

pages.x: Hello. How can I help you?

o: Can you give me any farming advice?
Can you tell me how to use the loom?

pages.x: Can you give me any farming advice?
Yes - ask a gardener.
Can you tell me how to use the loom?
Well, it's actually my loom but I don't mind you using it, if you like. You can use it to weave sacks and baskets in which you can put vegetables and fruit.

o: What do I need to weave sacks?
What do I need to weave baskets?

pages.x: What do I need to weave sacks?
Well, the best sacks are made from jute fibres. You can grow jute yourself in a hops patch. I'd say about four jute fibres should be enough to weave a sack.
Thank you, that's very kind.
What do I need to weave baskets?
Well, the best baskets are made with young branches cut from a willow tree.
You'll need a very young willow tree, otherwise the branches will have grown too thick to be able to weave. I suggest growing your own.
You can cut the branches with a standard pair of secateurs. You will probably need about six willow branches to weave a complete basket.
Thank you, that's very kind.
Thank you, that's very kind.
I'm okay, thank you.

pages.x: Hey there traveller! I don't suppose you're allowed through those gates are you? If you are then I may just have a job for you.

Menaphite coins! These beauties are all over the places beyond these walls. If you can bring 'em back to me, I can reward you!
That sounds like a good deal to me.

o: Can't you just go and collect them yourself?
How long will you be around for?

pages.x: Can't you just go and collect them yourself?
Ah, I should have guessed you would ask that. The short answer is no, they cast me out! I was once a citizen of Menaphos but I am no longer allowed within those walls.
It's not something I really want to talk about.
Sorry to hear that, from what I heard it's a beautiful city.
Oh you don't need to tell me!
What do you do?
Nowadays I travel around in search of interesting items, and then I trade them with travellers like yourself.
I've got some pretty interesting offerings that I know are of a specific interest to a few people within Menaphos.
How long will you be around for?
Not too long as I'm a busy guy, I have things to do, people to trade y'know?
I'll be around for a little while though as I need a good bunch of Menaphite coins before I'm ready to move on.
One of my clients needs a large chunk of them for their own reasons that I will not go into.

pages.x: Thank you for helping us, adventurer. I really thought I was going to die, but you saved us.
Since you're here, adventurer...could I ask for your advice?
Of course.
The murders in the abbey made me think about what I want to do with my life.
I've been here since I was a child, and I thought I'd spend my whole life here, but now I'm not sure I want to.
I could leave and become a secular musician, travel the world...

What do you think I should do, adventurer?
You should leave the abbey.
Thank you, adventurer.
You should stay.
Thank you, adventurer.
I can't decide for you.
Of course. I suppose I'll stay here and think about it.
Not right now.

conversations.section: Post-release / Talking to before fighting Telos, the Warden

pages.x: Ah, you are the one I have seen. The one who must save us.
You may not know me, but I know you. It is you I have seen in the waters, Player.
How do you know my name?
I have come to know many things, world guardian. I alone know what you must do.
Who are you?
I have been called many things. 'Seer', 'clairvoyant', 'soothsayer'... Common folk do not understand my gift.
I listen to the earth, commune with the anima. I know what lies ahead.
And also what lies beneath. What stirs below... You are the one who must defeat it.
Oh yes, the great tree of crystal and bark and anima. Risen from the depths beneath.
The war raging on here has triggered a reaction. The rumbling, the clanging...the screams.
I feel it on the winds. I sense it in the stone. The earth has woken.
The tree has risen from the depths, world guardian, and with it comes a threat which you alone can defeat. You must strike first.
Me? How do I defeat it?
You must step into the Heart through this threshold. Steel yourself against what lies within, you may be Gielinor's only hope.
Return to me once you have faced the threat that lies within. I shall be waiting.

A bucket of compost, eh? I might have one spare... tell you what, I'll sell it to you for 35 gp if you like.
A rake.

A watering can.
