conversations.section: First task / Talking to Johanhus Ulsbrecht at the Exam Centre / First time

pages.x: It is all starting to make sense to me now!
What is?
Oh hello World Guardian. It's about time someone around here listened to me. Recently I uncovered an enthralling mystery.
It seems that there are caches of First-Age armour buried across Gielinor. I am now very close to discovering their location and solving this mystery.
What has drawn you to this mystery?
The armour was crafted in honour of the Elder Gods, the first and most powerful divine entities.
Their power is unrivalled by all the other weak gods you see around here these days. Myself and my fellow H.A.M members believe that they are the answer to our problems.
They will sweep clear the land of all impurities.
Since becoming aware of them, we have been working tirelessly to learn more. Ultimately, we wish to gain their favour.
Why would you want to do that? They're trying to destroy us all.
Of course they aren't. I am sure they will spare their loyal followers.
That's doubtful... How are you planning to get their attention anyway?
Surely discovering and returning this lost armour to its former glory would do just that. Also, my robes are looking rather tired.
This is an excellent opportunity to refresh my look.
Hmm... I'm really not sure that's a great-
Anyway, I must get back to work.

conversations.section: In Keldagrim marketplace / Standard dialogue

pages.x: Oh no, not another human... what do you want then?
Oh, do you get humans here often?
Not that often, no, but sometimes. Of course, since you people are too big for dwarven clothes, they typically don't stay very long.
Why don't you make bigger clothes then?
What'd be the point? Besides, I don't make these clothes myself.

o: I still want to buy your clothes.
So do you have any quests for me?

pages.x: Who makes these clothes then?
Oh, my sister, she lives in Keldagrim-East. Has a little stall on the other side of the Kelda.
If she only worked a little harder, like me, she wouldn't have to live in the sewers of the city. Shame really.
The sewers? Your sister lives in the sewers?
Keldagrim-East, such a ghastly place. Not civil, polite and clean like we are in the West.
Uh-huh.
So do you have any quests for me?
Quests? Why would I have any quests?
Oh, just anything to do would be fine.
No, not right now... maybe I'll have something for you to do later, but nothing at the moment.

conversations.section: Before agreeing to cook for Gianne

pages.x: Hello.
Well hello there. Are you hungry? If so you've come to the right place. Eat green, eat gnome cuisine. My waiter will be glad to take your order.
Thanks.
On the other hand, if you're looking for some gnome cooking training, this is also the place to be. My son Lufty is looking for staff at the moment.

o: Ok, I'll give it a go.

pages.x: No thanks, I'm no cook.
In that case, please eat and enjoy.
Ok, I'll give it a go.
Well, that's great. I'm Aluft Gianne, owner of this restaurant, and you are...?
Most people call me Player.
Really? Sorry, how rude of me. It just takes a little while to get used to the funny names you humans have.
Of course if you're going to work for me I'll have to see what you're like first. Here, take a look at our menu.

o: Aluft hands you a cook book.

pages.x: When you've had a look at the book, come back here and I'll let you prepare a few dishes.
Okay then.

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Children can't sleep / Task #3

pages.x: Now, my youngest son, he recently lost his teddy bear.
You want me to find him a new teddy bear?
No, no. I may not look like it, but I am quite skilled in crafting. I plan to make him a new one if you could get me the materials.
What do you need?
I need [number] [item] to make it out of.
So, could you get [number] [item] for me?
That will suffice.
What do you know about [item]?

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.
Nevermind.
Nevermind.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Come and warm your soul with freshly baked goods from 'Lev's Baked Delights'!
Our cakes are so good, even The Great Wolf herself couldn't resist one! And there are no ghosts, ghouls or spectres to be seen.
Can I buy something?
What tickles your fancy?
What was that about ghosts, ghouls and spectres?
Ghosts? Who said anything about ghosts? There are no ghosts here.
No rattling, in the dead of night. No cries of pain, ringing in the back of your head. No whispers, warning you about the monster approaching from the east.

o: A loud pinging noise echoes across the bakery.

pages.x: What was that?
I, err...think it came from your oven.
Oh, the scones are ready!
Goodbye.
Please, don't leave. Don't leave me alone with the whispers.
Come again?
Thanks for visiting. Don't be a stranger!

conversations.section: Talk-to / Normally / After completing the Visions of Havenhythe quest

pages.x: Good day to you!
Hello there!

o: Could I buy a beer, please?

pages.x: Could I buy a beer, please?
Sure, that will be two gold coins, please.
How's things?
Not good! The demand for Braindeath's drain-scouring solution has dropped completely off.
Wow! It must have been one of those marketing peaks you hear about.
Whatever it was, I'm now in a 10-year contract to stock that old jackal's noxious swill.
You wouldn't want some, would you?
Oh, okay.
Sorry. Not right now.
Pah! I should never have listened to you.
Bye, then.
Come back soon!

conversations.section: In the Laughing Miner pub in Keldagrim

pages.x: Hello. Do you need any help with brewing?

o: What do I do once my ale has matured?
Can you sell me any ale yeast?

pages.x: How do I brew ales?
Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick.
Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.
How do I brew cider?
First you'll need some apples. You'll need to crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush.
Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.
What do I do once my ale has matured
Well, once you've got a full vat of the good stuff, just turn the valve and your barrel will fill up with eight pints of whatever your chosen tipple is.
Mind it's an empty barrel, though.
Can you sell me any ale yeast?
Nothing, thanks!

conversations.section: After Missing, Presumed Death

pages.x: Brassica Prime!
Why are you still here?
Can't a cabbage just relax and enjoy the scenery for once? I like the feel of this cushion on my leaves.
You know what this place is missing though? A cabbage patch!
Why didn't you flee when the dragonkin attacked?
Everyone knows cabbage beats fire. I had nothing to worry about!
Erm, I think it's the other way round...
A bit of fire couldn't hurt me. A roasted cabbage is a delicious cabbage, and deliciousness is power!
Will you try to win the Stone of Jas?
You mean the Cabbage of a Thousand Truths? Hah, I - BRASSICA PRIME - have no need for such devices. I command the power of highly concentrated nutrients.
There is no greater force in all of creation.
Why didn't you talk to the other gods?
Other gods? I am the god of all cabbages, what other gods do you speak of?
The ones who were here before... Saradomin, Zamorak, Bandos-
Oh, the fleshy giants! They had assembled to meet the all mighty cabbage, Brassica Prime!
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Barbarian Assault / Before agreeing to sign up / Talking to him

pages.x: Hello. What's this place?
Why you wretched Son-of-a-Big-Nosed-Warty-Smelly-Goblin! How dare you speak to a commanding officer like that?
I...err... What?
Stand straight! Chest out, shoulders back!
Okay, okay.
You'll address me as captain!
Yea...yes, captain!
Better. Now what is a low-life, pathetic excuse for a human being doing sniffing around my arena?
Exploring, captain. Looked like a chance for combat, sir!
And you think you have what is necessary to take on the Penance? No chance.
With respect, captain, I don't understand what this place is.
You really are useless, aren't you? Very well, make the most of this because I don't suffer idiots easily! This is the Barbarian Assault arena.
You want to sign up with us?
Sir, yes sir!
Then listen closely.

conversations.section: In the Thieves' Guild / Talking to him / Before Buyers and Cellars

pages.x: Hello there.
Greetings. I'm Robin, the Guildmaster's assistant.
Now, what can I do for you?

o: How long have you known the Guildmaster?

pages.x: Yes, I've never heard that one before.
Still, it's not so bad...
If I hadn't been mocked for my name as a lad, I might never have decided in a fit of ironic pique to learn how to rob from the rich and give to the poor.
Are you the poor in question?
Well, I was.
Having given myself the goods stolen from several rich people, I'm now of limited but comfortable means.
Now, what can I do for you?
Oh, some time now.
We started in business together when he was a con artist, talking people into handing over their hard-earned valuables with lies and vague promises of reward.
Obviously, that's all behind us now.
Now, what can I do for you?
Bye for now.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge

pages.x: Dooooom!
Where is this doom?
All around us! I can feel it in the air, hear it on the wind, smell it...also in the air!
Is there anything we can do about this doom?
There is nothing you need to do my friend! I am the Doomsayer, although my real title could be something like the Danger Tutor.
Danger Tutor?
Yes! I roam the world sensing danger.
If I find a dangerous area, then I put up warning signs that will tell you what is so dangerous about that area.
If you see the signs often enough, then you can turn them of; by that time you likely known what the area has in store for you.
But what If I want to see the warnings again?
That's why I'm waiting here!
If you want to see the warning messages again, I can turn them back on for you.
Do you need to turn on any warnings right now?
Ok, keep an eye out for the messages though!
I will.

conversations.section: In Al Kharid / Standard dialogue

pages.x: Greetings, friend. I am a manufacturer of leather.

o: Can I buy some leather then?
What can you tell me about Ali Morrisane?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Can I buy some leather then?
I make leather from animal hides. Bring me some cowhides and I'll tan them into soft leather for you.
Leather is rather weak stuff.
Normal leather may be quite weak, but it's so easy to craft that anyone can work with it.
Alternatively you could try hard leather. It's not so easy to craft, but I only charge 3 gp per cowhide to prepare it, and it makes much sturdier armour.
I can also tan snake hides and dragonhides, suitable for crafting into the highest quality armour for rangers.
Thanks, I'll bear it in mind.
What can you tell me about Ali Morrisane?
I wouldn't mind him setting up shop, but he's brought others in.
Two of them came here and said they were going to put me out of business if I didn't listen to them!
Hah, as if they think they could threaten me with a hammer and a pair of scissors.
What will you do about the threats?
The other shopkeepers and I won't give in to their threats. Osman's also told us that he'll make sure we're protected.
I'll keep tanning leather for people like you to make into clothes and armour.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Go away! I'm meditating!

o: I've come to repossess your house.
(After The Restless Ghost) I've lost that ghostspeak amulet you gave me.
Can you tell me about the crater?

pages.x: I said go away!
Okay, okay. Sheesh, what a grouch.
On what grounds?

o: Repeated failure to make mortgage repayments.
I don't know, I just wanted this house.

pages.x: What? But I don't have a mortgage - I build this house myself!
Sorry, I must have got the wrong address. All the houses look the same around here.
What? What houses? This is the only one. What are you talking about?
Never mind.
Oh, go away and stop wasting my time.
There were enough people clattering around my house before, and then Zamorak decides he wants a war camp right next to my hut.
At least Zamorak has gone now, but he's left his camp littering my swamp.

conversations.section: Before Throne of Miscellania

pages.x: Hello.

pages.i: What would you like to talk about?

pages.x: Good day. What are you doing?
I'm weeding this herb garden. It's hard work! I also sell a few gardening supplies.

o: What do you have for sale?

pages.x: Good luck with that.
Thanks.
What do you have for sale?
At the moment I'm selling garden rakes and iron sickles. They're 15gp each, if you'd like one?

o: I'd like an iron sickle, please.

pages.x: I'd like a rake, please.
I'd like an iron sickle, please.
No, thank you.
What are iron sickles for?
I can't think of anything just now. But you can buy one if you like!
What do people think of me around here?

conversations.section: In New Varrock / Before Mummy Returns

pages.x: I've lost them. I've lost all of them!
First it was Fluffs, my beloved feline friend. She'd been purring by my side for almost a decade.
There was nobody here to help, so I sent my eldest sons, Wilough and Shilop, out to search for her.
That was the day the demon came...my poor boys. When the red terror burst up through the floor of the square, they were the first to be taken.
After the...the funeral, I was very upset. I shouldn't have gone into the city, not with the demon still about, but I was so lonely.
I only left the house for a short while. I made sure that my children Philop and Kanel were well fed, and the door was securely locked.
I'd barely stepped foot in the square when the dead marched on Varrock. The city guard sealed the gates to try to keep them out.
They wouldn't let me go back for my little Philop and Kanel. By the time the gates fell and the battle was over, it was already too late.
My home was a smoking ruin, and my boys were nowhere to be found.
After the necromancer took over, I moved into this building, since I had nowhere else to stay. I adopted one of the stray dogs, trying to fill the emptiness in my soul.
I've loved him and petted him, but he's changed, bless him. He tries to bite me, and only eats raw meat.
Oh but I don't want to bother you with the troubles of a silly old spinster and her tragic past. It's not like there's anything you can do to help.
What is it you were wanting?
Selling? Well, I could offer you a warm meal, or some nice, yummy chocolate cake. Cooking's how I keep myself occupied nowadays...
Oh...you're leaving so soon? I do love a bit of company. I've been so lonely...

conversations.section: After the beginning of 14 January / At Falador Park / With catspeak

pages.x: Squeak!
That's an odd noise for a cat to make. Shouldn't you be meowing?
HA! Shows what you know! I'm not a cat. I'm a guinea pig!
How did you come to that conclusion?
The facts are very clear. I am called Guinea Pig, therefore I must BE a guinea pig!
It's really very simple. I'm surprised you're struggling with it. You must be quite slow.
How about this? If I can convince you you're a cat, will you come and look after the oasis for me?
Haha! If you can prove the impossible, then sure!
Okay, if you're a guinea pig how come...
Look, I am talking to you. Which I can only do because I can speak to cats!
Not rodents, not dogs, not pigs, not horses, cats!
If you were a guinea pig, I would only hear squeaking. But here we are, having a rather confusing conversation.
My whole life is a lie.
You're right. I...I am a cat. I shall head to the oasis...to consider this truth.
Squeak...

conversations.section: In the City of Um / Not wearing a bedsheet or ectoplasm-covered bedsheet / First time only

pages.x: What a silly thing to say. Of course I'm glowing, I'm a ghost! Also because owl poop...
Hazelmere! You're all glowing!
Probably forgot all about me soon as I died.
Oh, right. I forgot your ability to read minds. It's very confusing.
Yes, yes, they told me. They do just stand outside, you know? Good job honouring them, I suppose.
I've met the other heroes who fell trying to stop Lucien.
Not really, but I knew what I was getting into. The others knew the dangers too
I'm sorry about what happened to you all. Lucien was stopped, if that's any consolation.
I know. But I didn't save you so you could take up the dark art of necromancy.
I've had to turn to necromancy to take on this new threat. It's a danger to you, the others...everyone in Um!
Oh, fine, I'll let you off the hook. Just don't turn evil on us.
I was strongarmed into it! Rasial MADE me his new apprentice; it wasn't my choice!
*sigh* And I suppose you want to rope us all into dealing with this new threat.
You know...it's going to take a LOT to defeat Rasial...
Fine, we'll help.
So what do you say? Are my heroic friends up for one more mission to stop an evil necromancer?

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Get your festive wares here! Accepting Christmas spirit only!

o: How can I earn Christmas spirit?

pages.x: What do you sell?
Many old festive rewards. You name it, I've got it.
Santa hats? Christmas crackers?
I haven't procured those yet. But, I can do you one better...
Yes?
With a wand that shoots Christmas puddings!
As well as icy-themed weapons, a snowman outfit, and more!
How can I earn Christmas spirit?
Many ways. You can help out with some of the activities around the village, such as making snowballs, or chopping fir logs.
You might also see some of my teeny siblings around the world. Grabbing them out the air will give you some too.
Thanks!
Maybe another time.
Hurry back! They're available for limited time only!

conversations.section: During and after Heart of Stone, in the Lumbridge church graveyard / Receiving the Helmet of Trials

pages.x: Glad you came by. I've got something for you. You're one of the most accomplished heroes I've ever seen.
You've done things I can scarcely imagine, and I've lost count of the people who owe you their lives.
If there is any justice when history is written, your name will be among the greatest heroes of old. With Arrav, with Camorra; with Robert the Strong.
I've talked to some people at the Legends's and Heroes' guilds, and we've created a special prize for you.
Think of it as a token of recognition from the whole adventuring community.
Thank you, Xenia, This is an honour.
The honour is mine. You truly are an outstanding hero. I know with you on the scene, the world is in safe hands. Farewell, adventurer.
I don't feel like i deserve this.
I know how you feel. I've felt the same way for a lot of my adventuring career. There's always so much more to do - challenges to face, injustices to right.
A hero's work is never done. Don't let that blind you to what you've already achieved though. Thinking about what you've accomplished so far can be a source of strength.
Remember that. Farewell, adventurer.
About time I got some recognition
Ha ha! I see you didn't get where you are today by being humble! Well, if anyone has a right to be proud of himself/herself then it's you.
I can't wait to see what you do next. Farewell, adventurer.
I don't want your stupid helmet.
Oh. I just thought that... Oh, well, never mind, then.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Can I help you?
I help the main man over there. He can get a bit cantankerous. Every now and then he'll just start attacking people without warning. I act as a sort of home help...
How do you mean, home help?
Well, sometimes he'll fly right off the handle and just start, you know, 'raising the dead' to do his 'bidding'.
That kind of activity is just so anti-social, so it tends to attract a lot of hero types, you know!
Yes, yes, I know the sort. Full of themselves, aren't they?
Exactly! They come in shouting 'Have at thee!' and 'Death to you, evil one!' It's all a bit too dramatic for me, to be honest.
Anyway, he'll often end up getting killed, then nothing gets done around the house while he's awaiting his mortal return.
Mortal return? Sounds interesting.
Well, it's kind of interesting the first few times, but it's like falling off a bike...
What, you graze your knees a lot?
I was going to say that you soon get fed up with it. I guess it's one of those perks of the job, though, the ability to raise yourself from the dead.
You'd think he'd do better things with a gift like that, but all he does is get angry at people who come into his house without being invited, and then he's off again 'raising the dead'.
Thank you.
Okay. Please don't upset the boss while you're here.

conversations.section: City Quest / Children can't sleep / Task #3

pages.x: Now, my youngest son, he recently lost his teddy bear.
You want me to find him a new teddy bear?
No, no. I may not look like it, but I am quite skilled in crafting. I plan to make him a new one if you could get me the materials.
What do you need?
I need [number] [item] to make it out of.
So, could you get [number] [item] for me?
My appreciation.
What do you know about [item]?

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.
Nevermind.
Nevermind.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / With the little book o'piracy or having completed Rocking Out

pages.x: Whadda ya want?

o: I wanted to know where you got that harpoon hand.

pages.x: Whadda ya got?
We gots grog and we gots food. Here, take a look.
Nothing! Honest!
Then stop takin' up me floor space!
I wanted to know where you got that harpoon hand.
Yer new in town aintcha?
Newish certainly.
Well, if ye wants te hear the story, here goes.
See, I was walkin' along the docks one day, and this fierce storm blew up.
All of a sudden I turn an there, bearin' down on me is this albatross...
Sorry to interrupt, but I would just like to clear something up.
What? I was just gettin' to the good bit.
When I said 'I wanted to know where you got that harpoon hand', I meant where did you get it made, or buy it from?
If ye don't wants to hear the story then I ain't gonna tell ye!

conversations.section: Rune Capers / After the event

pages.x: Well, that was another successful Cape Festival, I hope you enjoyed our Es-cape-ades!
... Well, I'm going to go on ahead.
... Like a hat.
HAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!
OHOHOHOHOHOHOHOHO!
HAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!
Ha...ha...Oh...
Doug! Write that one down! I have an idea for a new festival!
Hahaha...

o: You take this opportunity to slowly back away and take your leave.

conversations.section: Talk to / After having completed Kili Row

pages.x: Hello Player, what can I do for you today?

o: Talk about active equipment upgrade task.
Show me the hard Underworld tasks I can do.
Can I claim any rewards from you?

pages.x: I'd like to know more about equipment upgrades.
Equipment upgrades... What would you like to know about them?

o: How can I learn more upgrades?
How can I apply the upgrades I've learned?
Where can I get the materials needed?

pages.x: How can I learn more equipment upgrades?
How can I apply the equipment upgrades that I've learned to my necromancer's equipment?
It's simple. You'll just want to take your necromancer's equipment to my soul forge that's just over there. It will tell you what materials you'll need.
Do you need me to give you directions to the soul forge?

o: No thanks, I can find it myself.
pages.i: Would you like directions to the soul forge?

pages.x: Where can I get the materials needed to upgrade my necromancer's equipment?
The main things you'll need are ensouled materials - cloth, thread, and bars. These come in lesser, normal, and greater variants.
As I taught you, you'll be able to get ahold of these by performing ensoul rituals on various items from the overworld, to imbue them with necromantic energy.
It's worth mentioning that to ensoul bars, you'll first need to smelt a variety of metals together in a furnace.
Some upgrades may also need necromancy runes, which you can get by runecrafting impure essence to the northeast of Um, or through trading with other players.
Nevermind.

conversations.section: Upgrading necromancy equipment / Tier 60 / Before having received the soul urn

pages.x: It's time for tier 60 then!
As always, you'll need to gather some souls in this soul urn.
The urn will only accept souls from killing any monster that is at least level 70 using necromancy, or completing greater communion rituals.
I need 50 monster souls, or 10 greater communion souls.
I also need some more things... And yes, one of the things is a pie.
A garden pie!
The meat pie you got me a while back was lovely, but I'd like to try out the vegetarian option this time.
Fair enough, the Lumbridge cow population is getting a bit sparse. What else?
Nothing as ridiculous as flippers this time, I hope...
No no, not to worry! I just need you to take this device and use it on an ankou.
It's a device I fiddled with that measures what kind of necromantic magic is being used on them. You might need to use it on a few to get what's needed...
I think 10 should do it.
I suppose that sounds more purposeful than flippers.
Ok. So, 50 souls, a garden pie, and... something from ankou.
And that's it! Don't forget your list.

conversations.section: If the tree is dead

pages.x: Blimey! You gone an' done it!

o: Will there be another Evil Tree?

pages.x: Who are you?
Me? Oo's askin'? I ain't nobody but a leprechaun, innit.
You sound a bit different from other leprechauns...
That's bein' on account a' the fact I was raised by imps, innit. Luvverly chaps, imps. Right geezers.
Anyways, I came across this 'ere root on me wanderin', so I got you geezers wif long legs to 'elp me out.
Turns out, I gots a wee bit a'bovver, though, on account of it has gnashin' teef and thrashin' roots!
So I gots you lot to 'elp me out by choppin' and burnin' the arboreal nightmare down!
What's that thing nearby?
That? That's an 'Evil Tree', matey.
It's a cunnin' geezer, and starts out lookin' like an innocent sapling.
Later on, though, ooh! It grows into a frightenin' beast, all lashin' roots and 'Look at me nasty teef!'
Some of 'em, I heard from a mate of a mate, are easier to kill than others.
That's the funny thing. They seem to appear every coupla' hours all around the world. Strange, innit?
The spirit trees know where they are; ask them if you're keen to help.

[number] [item]?

conversations.section: First time encountering Mephisto

pages.x: Oi you! I'm stuck.
That's a bad thing?
Yes...
What happened?
Me and the boys were playing some 'Luncheons & Flagons', see. I'm a 14th level Human Innkeeper!
During the campaign, one of the teleport spells went a bit...awry, and I ended up here!
You lost me at 'Luncheons & Flagons'.
Shut up. It's a fun game! Well, if you play the 5th Age Edition anyway. They made the Chef class overpowered, and I don't like all the new rules they ad-
Okay, stop.
Look, just help me out, please, I'll make it worth your while!
What do I need to do?
It's a binding spell, like a hex or whatever, if you meddle with it, you'll figure out...probably. Reckon you can solve the binding spell?
I could try...

o: Attempt to solve the binding spell?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello. Do you need any help with brewing?

o: What do I do once my ale has matured?
Can you sell me any ale yeast?

pages.x: How do I brew ales?
Well first off you need to fill the vat with water - two bucketfuls should do the trick.
Then you'll need to put in two handfuls of barley malt - that's roasted barley by the way.
After that you'll be putting your main ingredient in - this will decide which ale it is you're brewing. There should be some good guides around with recipes in.
Lastly you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.
How do I brew cider?
First you'll need some apples. You'll need to crush them using this cider-press - four apples should make a full bucket of apple-mush.
Take four buckets of mush and fill up the vat.
After that you pour a pot full of ale yeast in, which'll start it off fermenting. Then all you have to do is wait for the good stuff.
What do I do once my ale has matured?
Well, once you've got a full vat of the good stuff, just turn the valve and your barrel will fill up with eight pints of whatever your chosen tipple is.
Mind it's an empty barrel, though.
Can you sell me any ale yeast?
Nothing, thanks!

conversations.section: Wearing the Camulet

pages.x: Hello, camel.
The name's Mostafa.
Lovely? I wouldn't call it lovely. Sun's hot, sand's hot and my feet are killing me.
Oh. Um... Well, can't you lie down in the shade or something?
Shade? Around here? And you try lying down with a ton of granite on your back.
Terrible. These panniers chafe something rotten and I have a pain all down my left side.
Oh dear, that sounds nasty. Can't you take them off?
Of course not. No thumbs.
Won't Aligra take them off?
Certainly not - I'm the only way he's going to shift that lot of rock.
Horrible. I didn't ask to haul rock around. No one consulted me.
That's terrible! How did you start?
I was just sitting there, contemplating the problem of writing out my proof to the twin prime problem without thumbs and then WHACK!
I get this halter and whopping great panniers stuck on me and - before I know it - I'm loaded down with rock!

conversations.section: After 1 October

pages.x: Greet god, young Herr/Fräulein!
Greet god? What a strange way to greet someone.
It's a common Oktoberfest greeting, my friend. Don't worry, it's a welcoming one. What can I do for you?
Who are you?
Pretzel Bert, and it's a pleasure to meet you! Who might you be?
Player name. Nice to meet you too.
What are you doing here?
I've been employed by the Varrock Tourist Office to sell pretzels and spread word of Oktoberfest. Grundgüttiger, I couldn't think of a better job!
What is Oktoberfest?
Oktoberfest is a huge, traditional festival where a special beer called oktoberbrew is sold. We also organise multitude of events for anyone to take part in.
Best to check the forums if you want information on how to get involved.
How did Oktoberfest begin?
Oktoberfest has centuries of tradition behind it.
Beer festivals have always been held at this time of year, so the beer can be drunk before the new brewing season starts.
Oktoberfest is based on a festival that was originally held for the wedding of Queen Therese and King Ludwig, ancestral regents of my people.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello there!
Oh, er, hello. What do you want?

o: What can you tell me about Al Kharid?
So, what do you do here?

pages.x: What can you tell me about Al Kharid?
There's not much farming land around here. Only that little patch outside.
Can you give me any advice on farming here in the desert?
Like I said, I only know about cactuses...
Just tell me about cactuses, then.
First you have to weed the patch using a rake.
Can you give me any other advice?
Not really. I've not done much farming recently.
Well, can you at least sell me any gardening tools or seeds?
Sorry. They haven't been delivered yet.
So, what do you do here?
I'm going to set up a shop selling farming implements. That patch out there may be small, but it's all we've got.

conversations.section: Resting Lich Place

pages.x: Following in the footsteps of Orcus, I see. And just what do you hope that this will achieve?
If I can find your tomb, I might find a way to stop you!
Would that be the tomb for my mortal remains? Remains decayed ages hence, in a tomb now utterly filled in with dirt? At least Orcus was timely...
Fine, then tell me about Orcus.
He sought me out to devour my remains. It's a chthonian thing; he sought to absorb my knowledge and power. Unfortunately for him, the reverse is what happened.
I greeted him as a fellow necromancer, the first of our kind on this world after my own rise. He taught me of the primordial elements and of Erebus.
The revelation both scared and angered me. Scared for what this other realm would do to ours. Angered at Guthix for keeping such a dark secret from me!
If only Guthix had told me, I could have...
Could have what?
Ah, but that is a revelation for another time.
Fine, then what happened to Orcus?
The same thing that happens to all necromancers who seek me out. I take them under my tutelage, build them up and set them loose on the world.
Then, once they have surpassed my own knowledge in some way, I wring out all of their secrets, then obliterate them.
And that's what you're doing with me? Just waiting for me to learn something you don't?
In part. Do not worry; you have yet to learn anything I have not known for many lifetimes. And you will learn nothing of value here...
...So do not disturb me like this again.

conversations.section: After doing the Grand Exchange tutorial

pages.x: Hey there.
Why, hell to you too, my friend.

o: You look like you've travelled a fair distance.
I'm trying to find the prices for logs.
Sorry, I need to make tracks.

pages.x: You look like you've travelled a fair distance.
What gave me away?
I don't mean to be rude, but the face paint and hair, for starters.
Ah, yes. I'm from Shilo Village on Karamja, it's a style I've had since I was little.
Then tell me, why are you so far from home?
This Grand Exchange! Isn't it marvellous! I've never seen anything like it in my life.
My people were not pleased to see me break traditions to visit such a place, but I hope to make some serious profit. Then they'll see I was right!
So, what are you selling?
Logs! Of all kinds! That's my plan, at least. Nature is one thing my people understand very well.
I'm trying to find the prices for logs.
Then you've come to the right person.
Sorry, I need to make tracks.
Okay, nice talking to you!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Welcome to the Magic Guild Store. Would you like to buy some magic supplies?

o: Can I buy a skillcape of Magic?
I've noticed there are a couple of versions of each skillcape.
I've mastered this skill. Is there anything else?

pages.x: Yes please.
Yes! We, the skill masters, have crafted new versions of all skillcapes! We felt like it was time for a change.

o: Yes, I would like to wear the [new/old] version of the skillcape.

pages.x: Would you like to wear the [old/newer] model for just this cape, or for the Quest Cape and all of the skillcapes you own?

o: I would just like to change the Magic skillcape.
I would like to change all my skillcapes.

pages.x: No problem, you will now use the [older/newer] model for your Magic skillcape.
No problem, you will now use the [older/newer] model for all of your skillcapes!
Great! I'm glad you're still enjoying the [old/new] version!
There is something...though I have kept it a secret for a very long time. It is something that can only be worn by a true master.
Not even I can wear it - that's how hard it is to achieve.
You say you're a master. Stand straight, let me take a look at you...
You...really have mastered it. What an honour! It would be my pleasure to sell you a Magic master cape.

pages.i: Buy Magic master cape for 120,000 coins?

pages.x: No thank you.

conversations.section: After Love Story

pages.x: Why are you bothering me, human? I laboured in the mines for ninety years, and I want a bit of peace now that I'm retired.

o: Tell me about your life as a miner.
I need another copy of your diary.
Can you give me any free stuff?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Tell me about your life as a miner.
You want me to talk about mining, huh? Ahhh, I remember swinging my pickaxe hour after hour, day after day, down in the dark and damp mines.
Old Saggy-face, the supervisor, would be there with his sharpest pickaxe, looking out for slackers to impale. Of course, the trolls got him in the end.
Poor old Saggy-face. We'd found a tribe of trolls roaming the tunnels: huge trolls from the mountains.
Saggy-face tried to take them on single-handed, and they ripped his head clean off his shoulders.
Fortunately, we had that mad human, Dissy, staying in the city at the time. He drove those trolls right out of the mines with his magicks.
Dissy, huh? Was his full name Dionysius?
All human names sound the same to me. Here, I've got my old diary from that time. Take it and read all about those days.
Can you give me any free stuff?
Bah! In my day, people worked for a living, and anyone who wouldn't work got a short, sharp shock with a pickaxe. That's how it was. Ahhh.
So that's 'no', then?
Go away!
Sorry, I'll leave you alone.
Good!

Do you want to start your fire-breathing performance?
No.
Yes.
Of course! They won't stop talking to you, but they'll stop telling you if they think you're being repetitive or not.
Do you still want me to stop them?
No.

conversations.section: Dialogue / First conversation

pages.x: A lot of bad things must have happened here.
You don't know the half of it, pal!
Argh! Y-y-you're a talking pile of bones!
And you're a talking bag of gas. You gonna listen to my story or what?
No need for insults. What's your story, then?
Captain Cora - that was her name. She's the one who did this to us. Trapped our minds in our bones, cursed us to this eternal torment.
This musta been, like, twenty years back now. Just showed up one day, how'd you do, then cursed us like that was nothing.
Then what?
She left. We didn't chase her, though - didn't feel like it. Didn't feel much of anything from that day on.
Then slowly, one by one, we all just died...but somehow also kept on living. Then we started decomposing, yet still here in our heads. Now we're all just bones.
Yet you can still think and talk? And feel?
Don't feel nothing, mate. Like I said, haven't in a long time. We're all just stuck here, not moving on, not going anywhere.
That's horrific. I mean, you Skulls pirates are reprehensible, but still.
I know, right. She must have learned some serious necromantic magic. She could at least have just turned us into normal zombies.
Then we could at least have carried on our piratical ways. This is just cruel.
Leave me to my torment, mate.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Greetings automaton. What can I do for you?

o: Anything I can do around here?

pages.x: About those core memories...
What's going on here?
Why do ask a question that you already know?
We are here to preserve Guthix's deepest memories. We are the archivists of his most important knowledge.
Anything I can do around here?
Automaton, are you malfunctioning? Everything must stay contained within this hall.
The memories must be stored in the jars. Those can be found in the storage room to the east of here.
Once contained, the full jars should be deposited on the far side of this hall.
The butterflies carry a blessing of recollection. This blessing will recall memory shards on occasion.
There are remnants of memories left that should also be contained, but as they have faded they aren't a priority.
The chamber can be unpredictable at times, so you must be ready, should anything happen.
Oh right! Yeah I remember now.
Good. You're not malfunctioning after all.
Nothing, thanks.

conversations.section: Talking to Wall

pages.x: Hello.
What you want tiny?
I just wanted to know where a troll gets a dinosaur skull?
What you talkin' bout human, dat no 'die-nose-or skull' dat special roof fingy.
Right... Where did you get it?
I'm building a house...
Me get it from spooky in um... whats dat place up top called again?
Um?
Yeah me get it from spooky in um.
Needed new roof and spooky wanted some of clothes he found.
Where could you possibly have found clothes in here?
Me killed silly neck-o-dancer that come in 'ere.
I said 'no dancin on my neck' mista neck-o-dancer but he still tried some silly 'oogabooga' on me.
Found the clothes on it after I murdered it to death.
Right... I... Have to go...
Bye bye odd tiny-fing.

conversations.section: Interacting with the creepy doll

pages.x: What are you doing to me? What is this dark sorcery?
That just seems to happen to people when I shake this doll. I don't know why.
And you keep doing that? Why would you keep doing that?

o: I'm not sure to be honest.

pages.x: We are stood upon the back of a destructive force unlike any other, the world eater herself! This is not the time to mess with cursed dolls!
You clearly cannot be trusted with such a dangerous artefact!
MY doll! You have no idea how much effort it will take to get another one of those!
Good! I'm glad! I hope you don't get another!
Can't you at least give me something to replace it?
Fine! If you really want, you can have some of the spare safety apparatus.

o: Wizard Chambers hands you what is very clearly a fishbowl.

pages.x: This is very clearly a fishbowl.
It is not a fishbowl, it is a protective helmet! That one was worn by my former assistant, Apollo.
Then doesn't Apollo need it?
Not any more, no... Apollo has completed his mission.

conversations.section: World Event 3, second teaser: introduction

pages.x: Have you heard the news?
What news?
A huge astrological object is hurtling towards us! It's so big it'll shatter the planet into tiny pieces if it hits!
What!?
I know right! It's great!
Erm, come again?
I've been waiting for this moment my entire life! Don't bother with all that astro nonsense they said. Astronomical research is a dead end they said.
Well look who's laughing now! I can't wait to see what it actually is!
So let me get this straight. A world-annihilating entity is barrelling through space straight for us and you're fine with that?
Of course, why wouldn't I be? I finally get to put all of my astronomical theories into practice.
But we're all going to die!
Nah, we'll be fine. The world is full of heroes that will want a bit of the glory associated with stopping this cataclysmic event, yourself included I bet.
You do your job, I'll do mine eh?
You're crazy!
That's what all of the other wizards said. But now look at me!
An apocalypse waiting to happen and all that stands between us and utter destruction is my 'pointless' research!

conversations.section: In the Wizards' Tower

pages.x: Ello young thingummywut.

o: Teach me to be a mighty and powerful wizard.

pages.x: A thingummywut? Where? Where?
Those pesky thingummywuts. They get everywhere. They leave a terrible mess, too.

o: Er, you just called me a thingummywut.
Tell me what they look like and I'll mash 'em.

pages.x: You're a thingummywut? I've never seen one up close before. They said I was mad!
Now you are my proof! There ARE thingummywuts in this tower! Now, where can I find a cage big enough to keep you in?

o: Er, I'd better be off, really.

pages.x: Oh, okay, have a good time and watch out for sheep! They're more cunning than they look.
That's a pity. I thought maybe they were winding me up.
Don't be ridiculous. No-one has ever seen one.
They're invisible, a myth, or a figment of my imagination. Can't remember which, right now.
Wizard, eh? You don't want any truck with that sort. They're not to be trusted. That's what I've heard, anyway.

o: Oh, I'd better stop talking to you then.

pages.x: How dare you? Of course I'm a wizard. Now, don't be so cheeky or I'll turn you into a frog.
Cheerio then. It was nice chatting to you.

conversations.section: Post-quest dialogue, before Heart of Stone / Receiving the Helmet of Trials

pages.x: Glad you came by. I've got something for you. You're one of the most accomplished heroes I've ever seen.
You've done things I can scarcely imagine, and I've lost count of the people who owe you their lives.
If there is any justice when history is written, your name will be among the greatest heroes of old. With Arrav, with Camorra; with Robert the Strong.
I've talked to some people at the Legends's and Heroes' guilds, and we've created a special prize for you.
Think of it as a token of recognition from the whole adventuring community.
Thank you, Xenia, This is an honour.
The honour is mine. You truly are an outstanding hero. I know with you on the scene, the world is in safe hands. Farewell, adventurer.
I don't feel like i deserve this.
I know how you feel. I've felt the same way for a lot of my adventuring career. There's always so much more to do - challenges to face, injustices to right.
A hero's work is never done. Don't let that blind you to what you've already achieved though. Thinking about what you've accomplished so far can be a source of strength.
Remember that. Farewell, adventurer.
About time I got some recognition
Ha ha! I see you didn't get where you are today by being humble! Well, if anyone has a right to be proud of himself/herself then it's you.
I can't wait to see what you do next. Farewell, adventurer.
I don't want your stupid helmet.
Oh. I just thought that... Oh, well, never mind, then.

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander, before The Mighty Fall / At Tzhaar City

pages.x: Hello, Player. I didn't think I'd run into you so far from home.
Or maybe I should call you... JalYt - something-or-other - Player.
I am JalYt-Xil-Zanik!

o: What are you doing in Tz-Haar?
What do you think of the TzHaar?

pages.x: What are you doing in Tz-Haar?
I have been fighting in the fight caves, i haven't gotten to the end yet though. They say there's some huge creature called TzTok-Jad.
I have reached TzTok-Jad.
You have, what's it like? Wait, wait don't tell me. I am gonna find out for myself!
I haven't reached Tz-Tok-Jad either.
Well we'll see who gets to him first. Ha, ha ha!
What do you think of the TzHaar?
It's fascinating. It's an underground city, but it's totally different from home.
Even though I grew up in Dorgesh-Kaan, I can see how it's an artificial place. Goblins are from the surface originally, just like humans.
The underground is a hostile environment and we have to came it.
But these Tzhaar... they belong underground. They're creatures of rock and fire, born out of the volcano, so a city down here is totally natural for them.

conversations.section: Before The Tourist Trap

pages.x: Hello Effendi! I am Al Shabim, greetings on behalf of the Bedabin nomads.
Who are you?
I am Al Shabim Effendi! I am the leader of the Bedabin peoples!

o: What is there to do around here?}}

pages.x: Good day Effendi!
What is there to do around here?
Well, we are all very busy most of the time, tending to the pineapples. They are grown in a secret location, to stop thieves from raiding our most precious prize.
What is this place?
This is the home of the Bedabin. We're a peaceful tribe of desert dwellers. Some idiots call us 'Tenti's', a childish name borne of ignorance.
We're renowned for surviving in the harshest desert climate. We also grow the 'Bedabin ambrosia.'...
A pineapple of such delicious sumptiousness that it defies description.
Take a look around our camp if you like!

o: What is there to do around here?

conversations.section: Settling in at the base camp

pages.x: Look at this place...
Yes! We can work with this. It is strong, defendable and gives us some high ground.
Of course, Mr. Mordaut is going to need a base of operations to keep everyone focused on the mission so we should focus on that first.
Are you willing to help me out? You look like you can handle yourself from what I've seen so far.
As soon as I set my eyes on you, I knew it would be useful to have you around. Yes, let me explain what you need to do...
Look up there, the top of this temple would make the perfect place for us to establish some kind of Town Hall.
Somewhere where we can help run this camp and ensure everyone is cared for properly.
As you know, just getting here - building the boat, breaking through the storm wall, navigating past those... things - it has all been a trial in itself.
However, we always knew we were going to need to figure out a more permanent way of surviving.
I spotted some resources we could use to build up the base on the way here. There was wood, vines, leaves, stone, hides and clay.
Thankfully, King Roald gifted us a number of workers who will assist us in gathering what we need.
I am in charge of the workers; talk to me at any time to get them gathering different resources.
Remember: we need at least one worker assigned to gather wood, vines and stone.
Oh dear. What a disappointment. I hope you realise that we're all in this together. If you change your mind, please let me know.

conversations.section: Bandosian

pages.x: Hello there. How can I help?
What can I do here?
They call me the record keeper, and I keep this war ticking over.
I keep track of the plans to upgrade our forces. I'm also in charge of hiring fighters to bolster our number.
Since it'll be you out there doing the killing, I need your advice on both. I'll have no fighters to choose from - and new upgrades - every five days.
We'd also like your input on overall strategy, which you can check on the strategy board over there.
I'd like to give directions for the next upgrades.
I'd like to see the options for hiring mercenaries.
Tell me about yourself.
I was born in Rellekka. Yes, you think it's strange for a Fremennik to be for Bandos rather than Guthix.
But I'll tell you this much: the only balance a daggermouth ever respected is the balance of an axe. Everything about the life of our people comes down to one thing.
Strength. It is through force of arms and strength of will that we survive, day to day.
Let the other Fremennik follow what's left of Guthix if they will. I'm for Bandos and his one undeniable truth.
Nothing for now, thanks.
Off you go, then.

Dragon Bitter and Greenman's Ale, oh and some cheap beer.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: What is it?

o: Where did you get those weapons?

pages.x: I'm here because I'm not welcome in this world.
What happened?
Hmph, why are you so interested?
Ah... I'm just a curious sort, I suppose.
When you're dealt a bad hand in life, sometimes you have to cheat at the game.
Someone close to me had to die. I won't say any more.
Oh... I'm sorry for prying.
Isn't it obvious? This is our base of operations.
Alright, alright. You could be less hostile about it.
Don't ask stupid questions.
We know how to handle ourselves. Some, we took from tresspassing outsiders, the rest are spoils from the beasts of these lands. You shouldn't underestimate us.
That's a fancy staff...
Hah, isn't it? Heart torn from the firey wyrms you can find north of here, mounted on an old staff we picked up near the icy northern coast.

conversations.section: At the Grand Tree (Ta Quir Priw) / Before The Grand Tree quest

pages.x: Hello, human. Welcome to Gnome Air.

Glough has ordered that I only take gnomes.
How much for a one-way to Varrock?
I can't take you anywhere.
How come?
I would, but Glough has told me not to take humans.
Never mind.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / If the player does not have a Witchwood icon

pages.x: Be ye mad? There be Horrors in this cave!
What do you mean?
Have ye ever heard of the sort of evil, flesh-eatin' horrors that dwell in the darkest pits of the world?
The sort of dark, sanity-breakin' THINGS that cause the livin' to drop to their knees and weep for the fate of all creation?
Well, have ye?
Yes, I think I've killed a few of them as well.
Well, that's okay then.
But, ye'll need a Witchwood Icon from a slayer master if ye want te go in these caves and live.
Why?
Well, ye see them Jungle Horrors? Well down in the caves there be Cave Horrors.
They are bigger, badder, meaner, and have a howl that freezes the blood in yer veins.
Wearin' earmuffs or a helmet won't work, cos them masks they weear make the sound magical. Only thing that works is wearin' a Witchwood Icon.
That is, o'course, if we can see them, cos if ye don't have any light down there then yer likely te be picked te bones by the insects before the Horrors get ye.
I see, thanks for the warning.
Yer welcome.

conversations.section: South of Keldagrim / Before Between a Rock...

pages.x: Hello!
What?
I said hello!
Hello!

o: Why are you firing a cannon at a wall?

pages.x: Who are you?
Why, I'm Dondakan, of course!
Why are you firing a cannon at a wall?
I can't tell you!
Why not?
Bit noisy here, isn't it?
Cozy? No, not really, it's damp and cold!
No! I said it's noisy!
Then stop shouting!
Goodbye!

conversations.section: Easter events since 2024 / Talk to / Normally

pages.x: Happy Easter, Player, and welcome to the Blooming Burrow!
Our celebrations are in full swing - there's plenty to explore and help out with!

o: Do you have a quest for me?

pages.x: Is there anything new to do in the Burrow this spring?
Ayah has spotted some more spies above the burrows to the east. Speak to her just past the beehives if you want to help investigate.
Consider me !
What's going on here?
Many things! You can find my numerous nephews scattered around the burrow, each offering a different activity.
My nephew Fizzy Bunny needs some help wrangling some escaped chocolate bunnies.
You can also help out my factory, the Egg Plant, by mining some chocolate, and smithing some foil.
More recently, my brother Rich has been looking for eager sailors to test out his new carrot boats, and my other brother, Sticky, is looking after the Burrow's bees.
Stewy, Gooey, and Chewy, could also use a hand... But I'd need you to help me out first before I grant you access to the factory line.
The activities will reward you some skilling experience and spring tokens. You can exchange spring tokens with Gummy Bunny, for some lovely springtime rewards!
My nephew Nougat Bunny has also set up a bunch of egg hunts for you adventurers this year! You should talk to find out more about it.
Lovely! It sounds like there's a lot to help out with, then.

conversations.section: After doing the Grand Exchange tutorial

pages.x: Hello, little boy.
I would appreciate it if you didn't talk to me in such a manner. I'll have you know I'm an accomplished merchant.

o: Can you help me out with the prices for ores?
I best go and speak with someone more my height.

pages.x: Calm down, junior.
Don't tell me to calm down! And don't call me 'junior'.
I'll have you know I am Farid Morrisane, son of Ali Morrisane, the world's greatest merchant!
Then why are you here and not him?
My dad has given me the responsibility of expanding our business here.
And you're up to the task?
What a grown up boy you are! Mummy and daddy must be very pleased!
Look mate - I may be young, I may be short, but I'm a respected merchant around here and don't have time to deal with simpletons like you.
Can you help me out with the prices for ores?
That's easy. Been doing that since I was three.
I best go and speak with someone more my height.
Then I shall not stop you, mister. I've got too much work to do.

conversations.section: In Al Kharid

pages.x: Hello! Have you come to sample my marvellous wares?

o: Yes, I'd like to see what you have.
Perhaps. Your stall has some odd-looking stuff; what are they for?
Can I have a treasure chest?

pages.x: Perhaps. Your stall has some odd-looking stuff; what are they for?
I have the finest of items for those who would find their own things to do. Would you like to see them?
But what are they for?
Although the world has many things to do, some people like to play games of their own.
I sell them the tools to keep track of time, mark out places and routes, decide things randomly, even to hold great ballots of their group.

o: I don't think this is for me.

pages.x: These tools, are they complicated?
No, mister/madam, they are not complicated.
I have a book that explains them, should you need.
I don't think this is for me.
That is a shame. I shall be here if you change your mind.
No thanks.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Ah hello, friend! I was eggcitedly eggsamining my egg incubator, but that is no eggcuse for rudeness.

o: Why are you talking like that?

pages.x: I am Galgalar: eggsalted tender of eggs and incubator eggstraordinaire.
My eggquaintance Salusan and I are here after our unfortunate eggspulsion from Iaia. We seek to eggsact our place in your world.
She has eggstravagant ideas about dragon riders becoming dino-riders.
I merely wish to eggspand my eggsperience as an eggcellent egg hatcher. Salusan's more of a weapons eggspert.
The Potterington supports our coeggsistence. I assume running such a large operation eggsausts her.
Talking like what? Could you be more eggsplicit?
You keep making egg puns. Or do I hear a regional ilujankan accent?
Eggscent? I don't have an eggscent.
The deggsterity and fleggsibility of my vocal chords is one of my most veggsing features.
The elders told me it was how they knew I would eggcel at incubation, though.
I'm not sure if that makes more or less sense...
See you neggst time!

conversations.section: Talk-to / After completing A Guild of Our Own (miniquest)

pages.x: Ah, Player, there you are. How is the shadowy world of crime doing up there?
Very shady, thank you.

o: Can we try out that testing dummy again?
How's the guild coming along these days?

pages.x: Our vault is built, we've got a man on the inside of the banking network and the living quarters are finished. Thanks to you, we've got a guild to be proud of!
Anything else I can do for you?

o: Can we try out that testing dummy again?
How's the guild coming along these days?

pages.x: So what's new around here?
Look at this glorious guildhall I have caused to be! Our own bank, our own banker... Have you met Pinsworth?
What's a Pinsworth?
Oh, he's big into bank security, but the Bank of Lumbridge fired him, so he's our man now.

o: I've got some items for you here.

pages.x: We are always on the lookout for limited-edition items to add to our collection. If you bring me any such items, I will make sure the Thieves' Guild rewards you well.
It can be anything from an antique painting, a collector's coin to some shiny jewellery.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge / Before claiming a herald cape

pages.x: Hello there, dearie! How can I make your Lumbridge day even more wonderful?
Hello to you too! What do you do here?
I'm the Lumbridge herald, my dear! It's my job to make Lumbridge a lovely place to be.
You need a parade? I'll arrange it! You need a fancy banner? I can do that too! You need a herald cape...
Herald cape? What's that?
Why, it's the latest and greatest thing in Lumbridge attire. We provide you with a lovely Lumbridge cape to wear around, for nothing!
And if you've been particularly handy around the area, we'll show you how to customise it into something more fabulous!
In fact, I hear that other cities, like Varrock and Falador, are also offering herald capes with their own special designs!
Naturally, our Lumbridge capes are much nicer.
Can I interest you in taking a cape?
Sure, I'll take it!
Wonderful! Let's take a look at the customisations we can do...
No, thanks.
Oh, gosh. Well, drop by again if you change your mind, sweetheart.

conversations.section: In Burthorpe

pages.x: You need to make things. Leather. Pottery. Every piece you make will increase your skill.

o: Tell me about Crafting and other artisan skills.
Tell me about the skills menu.

pages.x: Crafting is the most versatile skill by far. You can make leather armour, pottery, jewellery and even glasswork.
If you ever get as good as me, you'll be able to perform extraordinary feats like making armour from the hides of dragons!
Fletching is about making bows and arrows. The better you are at it, and the better the quality of your materials, the better the result.
Every bow and every arrow you make will increase your skill.
If you expect to spend any time as an archer you'll want to ensure you have the arrows you need.
Most people have no appreciation for how many arrows an army goes through every day. We could really use your help re-supplying them.
Smithing is all about making weapons. And armour!
The better you are at smithing, the higher the quality of the metal you can work with and the better the resulting items are.
Every bar of metal you smelt and every metal item you smith will improve your abilities.
As well as being able to make gear directly, some of the most powerful ancient relics need an expert smith to reassemble their fragmented parts.
Burthorpe's militia need to be kept well supplied with arms and armour. It falls to smiths to meet that need.

o: Achieve 99 in all your skills to earn the coveted Max Cape!

conversations.section: Before The Fremennik Trials / In Rellekka / Talk-to

pages.x: What do you want from me outerlander? It is our policy not to associate with those not of our tribe.

pages.i: What would you like to ask about?

pages.x: Where is your chieftain? I find it highly discriminatory to refuse to talk to someone on the grounds that they are not part of your tribe.
I don't rightly understand your speech outerlander, but my loyalty is with Chieftain Brundt.
He resides in our long hall; it is the large building over there, you should speak to him for he speaks for us all.
So what are you doing here?
This should not concern you, outerlander. I am awaiting other Fremenniks to join me on an expedition to Waterbirth Island.
It is a small crescent-shaped island just north-west of here, outerlander.
We have many legends about it, such as the tale of the broken sky, and the day of the green seas.
The reason I am travelling there is more serious Fremennik business, however. I doubt an outerlander would be interested.
As you wish. Come and see me when your bloodlust needs sating.
Hey, I have to say, that's a fine looking hat you are wearing there.
It is actually a helm, outerlander, but the sentiment is appreciated nonetheless.

conversations.section: After Underground Pass

pages.x: Hi there, you okay?
Ooooh, my head ...I'm fried.
What's wrong?
Too much of this home brew my friend. We make it from plant roots, but it blows your head off. You don't wanna put it near any naked flames. Want some?
Okay then.
Here you go... Hic!
Ha ha! I warned you - it's strong stuff. Have a good meal; it may sober you up a bit.
No thanks.
Your losh... Hic! Well maybe a good meal? I could part with some food for a few coins.
Okay then.
75 coins pleashe.
No thanks.
Well come back any time.

conversations.section: Keldagrim

pages.x: Hello there, human! Come in, come in!
Hi, nice to see you!
Tell me, what brings you here?
Well, first I came to this city just for the adventure and excitement, but then I knocked over this statue, you see.
Well, I didn't really knock it over myself, I was on this boat.
A boat! Fascinating, go on!
Yes, well, this boatman was a bit rubbish, or there was something wrong with the ship, I don't know. And then I got arrested by the Black Guard.
Not the Black Guard!
Yes, and they took me to this Veldaban person, who pretended to be really angry but actually he was really nice and he asked me for my help.
So here I am, helping to rebuild the statue.
And after a whole lot of running around, I finally managed to get the statue to be rebuilt.
Such an interesting tale!
Now how did you come to be in Keldagrim again?
Never mind.

pages.x: Hi! What can I get you?

o: What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: What ales are you serving?
Well, we've got Asgarnian Ale, Wizard's Mind Bomb and Dwarven Stout, all for only 3 coins.

o: Can I have a Dwarven Stout?
I don't feel like any of those.

I'll try the Mind Bomb.

I don't feel like any of those.
What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?

Drop a gold coin into asgarnian ale and you'll get this weird golden ale that the dwarves seem to love, I think they're genetically attracted to gold.
Thanks, I won't forg...err.. misplace it, this time.

Ha! You may not have been on my side, but you certainly earned your title...
Look - I don't like you, and I'm guessing you don't like me. I don't regret my actions, but...
if you see Ozan, please tell him I'm sorry.

conversations.section: Upgrading necromancy equipment / Tier 70 / Tank / Before having received the soul urn

pages.x: Alright, so you want to upgrade to tier 70.
Of course, I'll need some more souls in this soul urn.
The urn will only accept souls from killing dragons using necromancy, or completing greater communion rituals. I need 100 dragon souls, or 20 greater communion souls.
This time, I'd also like to try a fish pie.
Back when I was living, fish pies were one of my favourites. I'm curious if they taste any better now that I'm dead.
Ok, soul urn and pie. Standard. What's the last thing you need?
Am I that predictable?
A little.
Well, the last thing I need is some necroplasm. Necroplasm from the original Barrows brothers, specifically.
How can I get it?
Firstly, you'll need some greater necroplasm. Around 20 for each brother should be enough.
Once you have that, take it to their crypts. The energy from their sarcophagi should be enough to transform the necroplasm.
But... I don't want the individual brothers' necroplasm. You'll need to find a way to combine them into a singular necroplasm.
That sounds doable, I think.
Perfect. Here's the list.

conversations.section: Upgrading necromancy equipment / Tier 80 / Power / Before having selected the task

pages.x: Right. You want to learn tier 80, power armour.
So, as it's power armour, I won't need you to gather me any souls.
Phew.
Instead, you'll need to defeat Nex and the Queen Black Dragon!
So much for an easy task.
First of all, I'm in need of 5 Zaryte fragments. You should be able to get these from Nex.
Second of all, I'd like 5 tortured soul essences. I believe the Queen Black Dragon will possess these.
Poor souls.
Another thing to note, is that they'll probably only drop the things I need if you defeat them with necromancy.
Probably?
Almost certainly, according to my research...
A definite guarantee would be appreciated, before I charge in all gung-ho.
Well, we don't always get what we want in life. Or the afterlife.
...And that should be all I need! Here's the list.

conversations.section: Upgrading necromancy equipment / Tier 90 / Power / Before having selected the task

pages.x: So, now we're onto tier 90, power armour.
This time you won't need to fill up any soul urns for me.
Instead, I need a few items which will require some challenging tasks.
I'm up for anything.
That's the spirit!
To start with then, I need a piece of greater ensouled cloth, dripping with venom.
Using the cloth on the corpse of Araxxi should be sufficient.
The next thing I need is a fragment of anima. You should just be able to get one of these from defeating either Vorago, Telos, or Solak, with necromancy.
A piece of cake.
Really? Well, I still need one more thing...
A special pie infused with the power of the gods, which I can only get by defeating Zamorak?
I wish!
But no. The last thing I need is some ulthven necroplasm, which you'll be able to get from defeating the Ambassador with necromancy.
I hope this upgrade is worth it.
Maybe. Before you go, here's the list.

conversations.section: After Between a Rock...

pages.x: Welcome to the Keldagrim library, human traveller!

o: an you tell me more about the library?
What do you know about impenetrable rocks?

pages.x: What do you know about impenetrable rocks?
You're confusing me, what rock exactly are you talking about?
The big one in the mines south of the city. Dondakan's big rock.
I see, I see.
I heard there was a demon inside there that you banished.
Yes, what exactly does that mean anyway?
There are some demons that we cannot see properly as mortals. They also cannot be fought with normal weapons.
But sometimes these creatures manifest themselves in a solid form in our world. Their avatar.
When you defeat an avatar, you defeat the actual demon behind it. But they don't die, they are banished to where they came from originally.
Does that mean I will have to deal with this demon again some time?
Doubtful. He will grow stronger and stronger over time, but that's a process that will take a thousand years at least.
Even dwarves don't live so long.
No, we won't see him again and the mines are safe to dig for gold now. Of course, that might lead to other problems eventually...

conversations.section: Summer Skill Off / Before the event / Talk to

pages.x: Hello! Hello. Hello!
Hey?
Yes! YES! You're here! You're actually here!
I am indeed here.
You know where you need to go?
The Spectacular Summer Skill Off.
Lumbridge Crater!
But not now.
No.
Later!
Monday!
Go there on Monday!
We'll be waiting.
What just happened?

pages.x: Hello!
What you want, Bentnoze?
Then who did say something? Who that?
It's Player! I'm talking to you by magic!
Hello, Player!
Bentnoze, [he/she] is here! I hear [him/her] in head!
Me not crazy, Bentnoze! [He/She] talk to me by magic!
You shut up Bentnoze! You stupid! You just jealous Player talk to me not you!
Shut up Bentnoze! You stupid!
SHUT UP!

conversations.section: After Observatory Quest / Before receiving the jug of wine

pages.x: Hi assistant.
Wait a minute.
What's your real name?
My real name?
I only know you as the professor's assistant. What's your actual name?
Patrick.
Hi, Patrick, I'm Player.
Well, hello again, and thanks for helping out the professor.
Oh, and, believe it or not, his name is Mambo-duna-roona, but don't tell him I told you.
You made that up!

Thanks very much.
No problem. Scorpius would be proud.
Sorry?
You may want to check out the book on the table, and perhaps look around for a grave...

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Slayer master / Task #1

pages.x: I'm ready for a change in career.
Oh, really? How can I help?
Well, I really want to be a Slayer master, though I could do with some practice.
Alright, give it your best shot.
Greetings, adventurer! It is I, the Slayer master!
How was that?
Yeah, that was great, but you have to tell me what you want me to slay.
Oh, right!
Adventurer! I need you to slay...uh...
I need you to slay...[number]...[monster]?
Cheers, love!
Where could I find [monster]?

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Oh, well, maybe someone else will pop along.

conversations.section: On Ape Atoll

pages.x: What do you want?
Oh, nothing in particular really.
Well stop distracting me then. I'm meant to be guarding this sacred statue from the temple of Marimbo.

o: Where is the temple of Marimbo?

pages.x: Where is the temple of Marimbo?
You're not from around here are you?
Actually I'm not. I'm a visitor from foreign lands.
Very well, the temple is to the east of the village.
What is the statue of?
It's of Marimbo, you cretin!
Ah yes. How stupid of me not to see the likeness.
I'll be back later.
I wouldn't count on it.
What?!
Oh, nothing.

conversations.section: November 2018 / When talked to

pages.x: What do you want?
What's wrong?
Sorry, I'm just frustrated about this 'internship'. My brother won't listen to any of my ideas, and he's only in charge because he's older!
Not to mention making me follow adventurers around like a pet...
What happened to the fanmail?
Ah yes, the first of my many improvements to the postal service. I simply glued all the fanmail to the parcels. Now we just have to deliver the parcels.
Ah, so you just found parcels and fanmail from the same people and bundled them together. Clever!
From the same people, that would have made more sense...
Got any interesting rumours?
I don't read people's mail, you can't prove anything! I mean, er, I haven't heard any rumours recently.
Would a few coins jog your memory?
Well if you were to hand me a few coins I might remember something...
Anything I can help with?
Well, if you could find some bone hurting juice, I may have an idea... MWAHAHAHAHAHAHA Anyway, I have no idea where to find such a thing.

conversations.section: In the Thieves' Guild / Talking to him / Subsequently

pages.x: Hello there.
Ah, Player. I'm doing classes on picking pockets, if you're interested.

o: Give me a few pointers, then.
How many hanky points do I have?

pages.x: Oh, we use them to keep track of our members' training regimen. Blue handkerchiefs will earn you one point, red ones are worth four.
You can claim a reward from any trainer with your hanky points.

o: How often can I do this?

pages.x: The number of hanky points you can claim for depends on your dedication to the art. At the moment, you can claim [number] hanky points' worth of training per week.
Bye for now.
You can give it a try with myself or my colleagues, although we've not got anything but hankies.
Picking a pocket is a simple thing, really.
Just act casual, keep your fingers loose, and be sure you can take a beating if you're spotted.
Most people don't take kindly to someone running a hand through their belongings, and they'll give you a good whack if they catch you at it.
Thank you for that stunning revelation.
You can give it a try with myself or my colleagues, although we've not got anything but hankies.

conversations.section: While obelisk is active, subsequent conversations

pages.x: So, will you help us gather more raw shards?
Well, there's no risk to your physical form or items in this realm. Your body stays here, so you can't really die.

o: What are the limits on this mental focus you speak of?
Any other effects inside the spirit plane?
Any limitations on what I can take with me?

pages.x: What are the limits on this mental focus you speak of?
Well, Pikkupstix says it is quite mentally exhausting to maintain your focus on staying in the spirit plane, so you can only do so for a limited time and only once per week.
Hmm, okay, so I'll need to work quickly.
You'll find that you can only have a maximum of sixty raw shards on you at a time. Pikkupstix says it's because they have a draining effect on your mental focus.
Any other effects inside the spirit plane?
Well, you won't be able ot go running around willy-nully in there. Take your time and conserve your run energy. At least, that's what Pikkupstix teaches.
But that won't affect me when I get out?
No, not at all.
Any limitations on what I can take with me?
Not really, but physical enhancements will not benefit you in the spirit plane at all, so nothing is actually needed. It's all about the mental focus you have.
No, thanks.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Can I 'elp you, monsieur?

o: Why do you work in a fishing colony?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: You've got an interesting accent!
Oui, I 'ave perfected zis accent for when I worked for my father in Ardougne.
He is a baker in ze market, and 'e believes ze customers will think ze bread of higher quality if it is made by a foreigner.
And does that work?
Perhaps. I do not care for ze bread; it is ze fish zat shall be my future.
Good luck with that!
Why do you work in a fishing colony?
Ahh, it is because I love ze sea. Ze rushing waters, ze endless horizon - it is beautiful! Also, I like ze fresh fish.
It seems like rather hard work - can't you just get a beach house on Karamja?
Zat, I am afraid, is not for me an option. Besides, I 'ave read of ze island of Karamja - it is full of ze big green spiders, and I like zem not!
Fair enough.
No thanks, I'm alright.
Ahh, farewell.

conversations.section: In the Exam Centre / After The Dig Site

pages.x: Hello there! I heard all about your big find; well done!

o: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?

pages.x: Can you tell me more about the tools an archaeologist uses?
Of course! Let's see now...
Trowels are vital for fine digging work, so you can be careful to not damage or disturb any artefacts.
Rock picks are for splitting rocks or scraping away soil.
What about specimen jars and brushes?
Those are essential for carefully cleaning and storing smaller samples.
Where can I get any of these things?
Well, we've come into a bit more funding of late, so there should be a stock of each of them in the Exam Centre's tools cupboard.
We also hand out relevant tools as students complete each level of their Earth Sciences exams.
Anything else?
If you need something identified or are not sure about something, give it to Terry. He's the archaeological expert in the next room.
Ah, okay, thanks.
Thank you!

conversations.section: Talk to / At the tannery, before starting Finding Tali

pages.x: Oi! Haven't you heard of knocking?
Sorry, I thought your shop was open.
A new face? Don't see many of those round these parts.
I should be the one apologising. Shouldn't 'ave shouted at you like that. Just got a lot going on, you know?
What's the matter?
It's my kid, Tali.
She went wandering off yesterday. Never came home. I'm worried something fierce.
She's a good kid. Got her 'ead screwed on right, and she's nearly fully grown. Doesn't feel right reprimanding her for wanting some independence.
But she shouldn't be camping out in the Highweald forest on her own. It's not safe.
Why haven't you gone looking for her?
It's a difficult time for us. Have a feeling I'm the last person she'd want to see right now.
Last time she went hiking through the Highweald alone Adam practically chewed her ear off. Don't need 'im getting involved again either.
She said she was going to explore the ruined watchtower by the passage into the mountains. If you're 'eaded that way, would you mind keeping an eye out?
I'll let you know if I find her.
Thanks, mate. Appreciate it.

pages.x: Now that you've shown your dedication. I have a secret to tell you.
Allow me now to tell you a deep secret about the Dragonkin...something that will chill you to your very core!
Finally! Something worthy of my talents!
Many centuries ago, the Dragonkin went out into the world and...
Noooo...no...noo! I can see that look in your eyes...don't do it!
...set a task, just for you...
No...don't you even think about it!
For you...mighty warrior...must...
I. WILL. END. YOU!
KILL
You...
TEN
Mother...
RATS!!!!!!
I can only use Quickchat.

Because I invented the Log Canoe!
Log Canoe?
Yeash! Me and my cousins were having a great party by the river when we decided to have a game of 'Smack The Tree'.
Smack the Tree?
It's a game where you take it in turnsh shmacking a tree. First one to uproot the tree winsh! Anyway, I won the game with a flying tackle.
The tree came loose and down the river bank I went, still holding the tree. I woke up a few hours later and found myself several miles down river.
And thatsh how I invented the log canoe!
So you invented the 'Log Canoe' by falling into a river hugging a tree?
Well I refined the design from the original you know! I cut all the branches off to make it more comfortable. I could tell you how to if you like?

Can I access my bound and stored items?
