conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello there, love. Alright?

o: Could I ask a personal question?
I better be going. Things to do.

pages.x: Oh, I can't complain, Portmaster. The adventurers and captains who turn up here every day keep my busy. Mind you, John was here last night. Drunk of course.
Shouting something about sailing one of the ships eastwards. Bless him. I'm glad you're here. We've needed someone to sort this place out for a long time.
For the past few years its felt like we've been trapped in cobwebs and shadows. With you here, it feels light again.
You want to know about the tentacles, right?
Er - yes.
Oh, dont blush, little octopus. You see there's an afflication in the east, no one knows the cause of it, but some of us are born with gills, tentacles, even fins.
One poor man had flippers; meant he couldn't wear shoes.
You'd reckon looking like this we'd have some special powers, like that siren sulking around the docks, but you'd be wrong.
I can swim better than most, sure, but that's about it. Of course, there's many folks who are distrustful of us. They call us sea orphans, which says a lot.
And some are more than just distrustful. The Purists in the Scythe region hate us with a real passion.
They spread lies about us, beat us up, kill us when they get the chance, scare mothers into drowning us at birth. No one does much about them. Cruel folks, them Purists.
Ah...sorry, love. You don't want to hear me prattle on.
You take care, now.

pages.i: What would you like to say?

Well, we've got Asgarnian Ale, Wizard's Mind Bomb and Dwarven Stout, all for only 3 coins.

I don't feel like any of those.

pages.x: One Asgarnian Ale, please.
I'll try the Mind Bomb.
Can I have a Dwarven Stout?
I don't feel like any of those.
What can you tell me about dwarves and ale?
Oh it's you again. Forgotten the secret already?
No... I just... misplaced it.
Mmmmm... the secret is in the gold.
Drop a gold coin into asgarnian ale and you'll get this weird golden ale that the dwarves seem to love, I think they're genetically attracted to gold.
Thanks, I won't forg...err.. misplace it, this time.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello there!
I'm a little busy at the moment. What is it?

o: What can you tell me about Al Kharid?
So, what do you do here?

pages.x: What can you tell me about Al Kharid?
Oh, it has wonderful weather.
Wonderful? It's hot and dry all the time!
Not quite as hot as back home.
Where's home, then?
Oh, it's a town to the south of the pass, called Pollnivneach.
So, what do you do here?
If I had cloth, patterns and customers, I'd be a tailor. As it is, I'm a tailor with nothing to do.
The silk merchant won't even sell me any silks, because he doesn't trust me!
Anything I can do to help?
No, no, it's all being dealt with.

conversations.section: Second task / Returning to the Curator and asking about A Cultist's Journey

pages.x: Have you found Johanhus yet?
Yes. Johanhus has found a cache of First-Age armour in the Feldip Hills. Strangely it's in surprisingly good condition...
How interesting. Perhaps this suggests that it is not simply armour, but a product of the raw, elemental magic left behind by the Elder Gods' acts of creation.
He was also rambling about dreams
Fascinating. I wonder whether these items were created by early mages, inspired by visions caused by the magical fallout that saturated the world during the First Age.
If some of that magic lingers in them, it could explain why Johanhus is having some colourful dreams. We will never truly know of course.
But Johanhus is making a bold, and rather ignorant assumption by claiming that the armour was created for humans who worshipped the Elder Gods.
Of course the elemental nature of the armour could well mean that it is associated with the Elder Gods.
But it would be delusional to assume that they would want - or even acknowledge - worship. Especially from humans.
After all, to the Elder Gods we're little more than a glitch in creation.
Johanhus seems to believe that the Elder Gods will think he is special... He has decided that it is a good idea to wear the armour!
The man is a fool. Did you learn anything else?
He claimed that he was too busy to talk to me further.
Very interesting... I wonder what he is planning next. I'll be seeing you again soon, I'm sure.

conversations.section: Second task / Talking to Johanhus Ulsbrecht at Feldip Hills / First time

pages.x: Behold! At last, I have discovered the armour.
I can see that...
Isn't it incredible? Now I will surely be noticed by the Elder Gods!
Um... I'm not sure the Elder Gods are interested in you. Or anyone, for that matter.
If they believe I am showing them my devotion, they will begin to take notice and respect me. Soon they will realise what a great ally I'll be to their cause.
The monsters that occupy this land will be no more.
Hold on, didn't you say this armour was from the First Age? How is it so pristine?
Armour devoted to such powerful entities must be built to last. Nothing but a few scratches here.
Right...
Anyway, I do not have time to stand around and chat to you, World Guardian, I have so much to do.
Like what, exactly?
I don't have time to explain. The dreams were... amazing. Such vivid images. I'm still trying to make sense of them.
Um...
Farewell, World Guardian!

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / After Pharaoh's Folly

pages.x: Welcome! It is good to see you again. How can I be of service, friend of Al Kharid?
I hear Ozan has had quite the turn of fortune, now that the succession of Menaphos has been decided.
Earning Leela's favour? He's a lucky man. I wish him well.
Regardless, until the Kharid-Ib is returned, Al Kharid's view on the matter remains unchanged.
The day it is returned - particularly by Ozan's own hand - is the day he will be welcome in this city again.
So Osman finally met his match. It brings me no joy to learn of his fall.
To think that this is the same man my father trusted with his life - the man he trusted with my life! He would turn in his grave to hear of this.
It troubles me that Leela let him disappear. An ill omen, if ever I've seen one.
With Amascut drawing ever closer, the last thing the desert needs is a viper lurking in the dunes.
Though, regardless of that danger, I ought to acknowledge Leela's succession.
It's strange to think of her as Pharaoh. She and I were children in this palace only yesterday, it seems.
Should we survive the Devourer, I hope to meet Leela again in person, Emir to Pharaoh. Perhaps our cities can be friends once more.

pages.x: I am exhausted because my children are unable to sleep at night.

My oldest son is too afraid to sleep because of the [monster].
Would you be able to go and find some [monster] and thin their numbers?
Seems a little excessive... How many would I need to deal with?
Could you kill [number] [monster] for me?

conversations.section: Talk to / After Secrets of Amberfell

pages.x: Lovely to see you again, dear. To what do I owe the pleasure?

o: Can you tell me more about your homeland?
How much do you know about Morytania?
Can you tell me about yourself?

pages.x: What's your plan now?
My plan?
Well, we defeated the Sanguine heart. We saw off the plague in Amberfell. What's the next move?
Ah, I see!
I will continue my research into the nature of the Sanguine. I intend to make use of Inanna's knowledge to see how far it has spread, and its effects on the land.
And, of course, to investigate what others of my kind are doing here.
In the meantime, I hope to see you more. I do so enjoy having an ally here.
You consider me an ally?
Why, yes. If you must know...
Yes?
I do admire you.
Your work. I admire your work here, with these people. It is admirable.

conversations.section: At Stormguard Citadel Dig Site

pages.x: Oh, Armadyl, I wasn't expecting to see you here.
I had to see this place again for myself.
Do you mind if I ask...um...this place doesn't really fit with how the world views you.
You refer to the weapons of war, yes? This place began with lofty intentions of of alchemical study and to enrich the lives of my followers.
It was only later into the God Wars, when tides had turned and alliances had frayed, that thing became so desperate.
'If you desire peace, cultivate justice',so goes the saying... To protect my own people from the ravages of war required us to be able to defend ourselves.
War was not something we sought out, but it came to us, nonetheless. I would not sit idly by and see my people suffer and die at the hands of others.
Yet the path it took us on led to ruin regardless.
Stormguard is not my deepest regret, even though it cuts deep, but it is my greatest lesson.
Could you tell me more about this place?
I could...
Will you?
No, I don't think I will.
Besides, I would not wish to rob an archaeologist of the joys of their journey of discovery.

conversations.section: At Senntisten Temple / After The World Wakes

pages.x: Isn't Sliske Zarosian? It didn't look to me like he was trying to avoid bloodshed.
We may be united in our devotion to Zaros, but Sliske and I are not one and the same.
We had many centuries to discuss the possibility of discovering Guthix's location; so we had plenty of time to argue what should be done.
We were not all united. My brothers, Wahisietel and Akthanakos, agreed that Guthix did not need to die.
Sliske disagreed; sometimes I think just for the sake of disagreeing. However, he did eventually align with the majority.
We couldn't quite believe our luck when it was you who discovered the entrance to Guthix's chambers.
Our plan had not extended beyond letting the others exterminate each other before we stepped in.
Sliske came to you and proposed our view; we believed he truly agreed with it.
Of course, you should never believe anything Sliske tells you.
So what happened after that?
The next part of the plan; Sliske released Nex from her icy cage while I notified Char. It felt momentous; Zaros' true followers, together again.
But then Sliske disappeared. This isn't unusual, of course. Besides, we didn't have time to chase him down. We arrived at the chambers, and well...you saw the rest.
Sliske was lying to us the whole time. He never believed Guthix should live.
What will happen to Sliske?

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Friend's son slowly dying / Task #3

pages.x: Oh no...
What?
I am...hopeful. I worry that you have given us hope, only for the sands to snatch it from us.
No matter. I will take this brief moment of solace for what it is.
A good idea. How else can I help?
We have everything we need. If you still want to help: while we've been caring for the young boy, we've neglected our daily duties.
Getting hold of [number] [item] should be sufficient.

o: I don't have time right now.

Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

Nevermind.

pages.x: Who are you?
My name is Ex Sea Captain Barfy Bill.
Ex sea captain?
Yeah, I bought a lovely ship and was planning to make a fortune running her as a merchant vessel.
Why are you not still sailing?
Chronic sea sickness. My first and only voyage was spent dry heaving over the rails. If I had known about the sea sickness I could have saved myself a lot of money.
What are you up to now then?
Well my ship had a little fire related problem. Fortunately it was well insured. Anyway, I don't have to work anymore so I've taken to canoeing on the river.
I don't get river sick! Would you like to know how to make a canoe?

pages.x: Hello.
Hello?
'ello mortal.

Can you tell me what the people on the stands next to you are wearing?

pages.x: I stole this armour from the wights of the Barrows Brothers. I raided through their tomb in Morytania, battling the brothers and the many creatures along the way.

o: Can you direct me towards these Barrows?
Can I ask you about something else?

pages.x: Of course, let me mark it on your map for you.
The guy to the far left is in armour worn by the famous Zarosian ranger, Pernix. He would have picked that up in an icy dungeon that we call the God Wars Dungeon.
The God Wars Dungeon is good hunting: the generals of the gods are a real challenge and defeating them is worthwhile.
The lady in the centre is wearing full steel plate armour. This armour is made by the many smiths across RuneScape.
The guy on the right is wearing black dragonhide armour. This armour is made by crafters from hides of slain black dragons.

o: Can you direct me towards the God Wars Dungeon?
Can I ask you about something else?

pages.x: Of course, let me mark it on your map for you.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Welcome to the Golden Scarab Inn! Come take a load off before you go on your next adventure.

o: Could I buy a beer, please?
What is there to do in the Ports district?

pages.x: Could I buy a beer, please?
Sure, that will be two gold coins, please.
Well, there is this one drink we sell that's a little 'out there'. It's called Squeck Juice.
Oh, will it help with my thieving?
Not in the least. Want to try it? It's 10 gold.
No, thanks.
This is the waypoint to the rest of the world - we have ships that can sail you anywhere you need to be, whether that is to take you on a new adventure or to help you escape trouble.
Of course, you're happy to hide out here anytime you want.
The Golden Scarab has a renowned reputation for keeping our mouths shut if the Imperial guard come asking questions.
So don't be shy, tell me your secrets.
Take care, sailor.

pages.x: So you've plucked up the courage to come and confront that girl!
That I did, that I did!
And?
She turned out to be really nice! She's joining us to become a pirate!
Really? And you're not sceptical about this? You know, after what she did last time?
She---has---no---spell---on---me.
Huh? Why are you talking like that?
Like what?
Like someone else was talking for you. Are you sure she hasn't put a spell on you again? Did she wave a watch in front of your face?
You know, tell you to look deep into her eyes?
She---has---no---spell---on---me.
I think you've been hypnotised. I wonder what happens if I click my fingers?
*Cluck* *cluck* *bwaarrk*
Oh dear. Oh well, I'm sure you'll learn one day.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue after The Firemaker's Curse / Without having completed The Temple at Senntisten, The World Wakes or Fate of the Gods / At 91 Firemaking and above

pages.x: Are you ready to begin?

o: Could you show me how to do it, again?

pages.x: Yes!
Get on with it then.
Could you show me how to do it, again?
As a child, I learned the basics of fire building and control, but Zaros taught me something new.
You can get great worth from your fires if you create them in specific patterns, and have the right knowledge.
I have constructed the grid behind me to train this skill. You will find the patterns I use in my journals.
For example, the basic square.
Or the spiral.
Of course there is one pattern, very close to my heart, that I did not write down.
I will give you a set amount of time to make as many arrangements as you can, and will reward you for each arrangement made.
Use this side as a base, as I did in my examples, so I can see your patterns properly.
Are you ready to begin?

conversations.section: After Carnillean Rising

pages.x: That wine was amazing. I slept right through Philipe's fight with the wolf.
Wow!
I've a little business proposal for you. Some of my friends heard about the magical wolf.
If you can go to the wolf's den, kill it again and bring me it's skull, they'll pay handsomely.

o: What would you like to say?
Tell me more about your friends.

pages.x: Pretty difficult, yeah. She can cast spells, like you saw, and her pups are there to help her.
Knowing them, it'll be potion ingredients or magical supplies. That's what they're into.
They're chaps with chaotic inclination and druidic talents, if you know what I mean. There are loads around Ardougne.

o: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Shhh! Look: they just want to do fancy rituals, and a Cave Wolf Matriarch skull will help them out. Okay?
Knock it off, will ya?
That wine was amazing. I slept right through Philipe's fight with the wolf.

conversations.section: Foreshadowing / Attempting to open the door to Closure's room

pages.x: Excuse me, can I help you?
Oh, this door is locked.
You mean the door to my personal space? My bedroom?
Wait, do ghosts even need sleep?
Somehow, I think you are missing the point.
Adventurers might get away with invading people's homes and going through their things, but I don't want you rifling through my drawers.
There might be a clue scroll in there.
There isn't.
Do ghosts even own underwear?
'And so Player decided to be incredibly rude and presumptuous with the person who would be writing his life-long biography.
Clearly, this was not his finest hour, but rather just one more entry in a long list of inappropriate actions.'
I'll stop. I apologise. Just, please stop passive-aggressively writing my biography...

conversations.section: Standard dialogue before Sheep Herder

pages.x: Hello.
How do you feel? No heavy flu, shivers, nausea or loss of appetite?
Uh... no... I feel fine...
How about nightmares then? Are you experiencing any problems with especially scary nightmares?
No... not since I was young.
Good, good, I had to make sure. This plague really has an incredibly fast contagion rate. It spreads faster than the common cold!
The plague? Tell me more.
It came from the west somewhere. It is extremely quick spreading, and utterly deadly.
What are the symptoms?
It varies slightly from case to case, but usually abnormal nightmares and flu-like symptoms, progressing as you succumb more.
Eventually, it results in the presence of a thick black tar-like substance secreted from the nose and eyes.
Okay, I'll be careful.
You do that adventurer. You do not want to become infected by the plague.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge / Case 1

pages.x: Hello there, can I help you?

o: Are there any quests I can do here?}}

pages.x: This is the town of Lumbridge my friend.

o: Do you know of any quests I can do?

pages.x: Aye, not too bad thank you. Lovely weather in Gielinor this fine day.
Weather?
Yes weather, you know.
The state or condition of the atmosphere at a time and place, with respect to variables such as temperature, moisture, wind velocity, and barometric pressure.
Not just a pretty face eh? Ha ha ha.
What kind of quest do you seek?
No it's not!
No you're right. I have nothing to back that up.
Fool! Leave me alone!

conversations.section: Talk to / After completing Guys and Dolls

pages.x: Hey, Doyle. So, how does this pumpkin order thing work?
All you've gotta do is harvest pumpkins from the patches in front of me and deposit them in the harvest cart right here.
You can hand in parts of the order as you go or wait until you've harvested everything in the order.
You'll get a nice bit of experience when the order is completed, and a bonus if you do it all in one go!
Are those crows still hassling you?
They are - every time a pumpkin gets harvested, there they swoop in looking for seeds. Their eyes are bigger than their bellies!
You can shoo them away easy enough, but it's hard work one at a time.
I can scare them all at once, but every time I do I'll need a minute to recover.
However, once a crow has been scared away from a patch a new pumpkin will grow in it. So it's gotta be done.
Sounds simple enough - harvest pumpkins, shoo crows away, and fill Dolly's order by putting pumpkins in the harvest cart.
Anything else I should know?
Oh, yeah! There's a compost bin in the corner opposite the harvest cart. You can trash any pumpkins you don't want in there.
Might help for making room for different ones, or just when you've finished for the day.
Also, you can get random Halloween stuff while harvesting, but you'll get the experience mostly from completing orders.

conversations.section: By the dock, after completing the Archaeology tutorial

pages.x: How can I help you?

o: How's the new recruit training going?
Can you remind me about the basics of archaeology?

pages.x: How's the new recruit training going?
Great! Thanks for asking. We've had a lot of new recruits through here lately.
There's an endless amount of history out there that we still need to uncover, which means we need all the help we can get.
Can you remind me about the basics of archaeology?
Not a problem at all, it's quite simple really. You'll need to get yourself a mattock and then head out to an area you wish to excavate.
We have a couple of camps set up that focus on some pretty big areas of our history. These dig sites are full of untold mysteries.
There are some smaller excavation sites out there too, just scattered throughout the world.
Using your mattock you'll be able to dig away and uncover materials and artefacts.
You'll want to try and restore any artefact you manage to discover as they're worth a pretty penny to the right person.
You can check out the collectors noticeboard near the main building if you're interested in seeing who's interested in what.
In exchange for your hard work you'll find yourself rewarded with chronotes which can be spent to assist you on our archaeology journey.
Whils you're out in the field, make sure to take notes in your journal of anything you find.

Player.

conversations.section: In Varrock Palace Garden / Without the requirements for Garden of Tranquillity

pages.x: What's going on here? I see a lot of farming patches with nothing growing in them.
No, one has just had them installed. One has had the most marvelous idea to bring renewed happiness to one's own dearest husband.
One? I'm not sure I understand you-
Oh dear - the common classes, oh how they fill one with intolerable levels of exasperation, I swear to be most true.
Ri-ight ... if you say so, my lady. I'll be off then, if you don't mind-
Yes, be off with you, before I call the guards.
No problem, sorry to have bothered you.
Peasant - WAIT!!!
Are you speaking to me?
Who else would I be speaking to, you funny little [man/woman]? Of course you.
Well for a moment there I thought there was a dog around here somewhere...
Oh yes, sarcasm - how amusing. No, no, peasant - I have a question to ask of you, and you are required to answer.
Well, seeing as you put it so nicely...
Do you know of anyone who might have some degree of horticultural experience?

conversations.section: While Dungeoneering / Talking to the Enigmatic hoardstalker

pages.x: Wanderer, your movements are as uncertain as a fledgling in first-flight. Are you lost?

o: Do you have a riddle for me?
Can you open the door for me?

pages.x: Do you have a riddle for me?
I do. Here it is:
Give me the answer not in words but with an object.
Who are you?
Like all gorajo, I have no name; instead, I have a path. I have chosen to be a naabe hoardstalker.
My tribe required a mental trial to be given at this door. I am to stop the unclear of mind from passing into danger.
Can you open the door for me?
I am capable of opening the door, ahnanai.
Well, go on then!
Ah, you wish to skip to the end, like a wolf stalking prey. Naabe, it is not that easy. You must prove your clarity of thought with a trial.

conversations.section: Attempting to enter the fortress without wearing the uniform

pages.x: Hey! You can't come in here! This is a high security military installation.

o: I don't suppose you're open to a bribe.
Who does this fortress belong to?

pages.x: I might be new here, but I certainly don't recognise you.
You're not even wearing proper guards' uniform!
Well, you can see me wearing it. It's an iron chainbody and a bronze helmet.
Of course, the officers have elite black plate armour, but that's not something we grunts can dream of...
Hmm, I wonder if I can make that or get some in the local towns...
What was that you just muttered?
Oh, nothing important.
Go away. You're getting annoying.
If I had a penny for every well-meaning adventurer who tried to bribe their way into this fortress...
I could hang up my uniform and retire!
This fortress belongs to the Black Knights, also known as the Kinshra.

conversations.section: At the farm north of Lumbridge

pages.x: What are you doing on my land?

pages.x: What, on my land? Leave my livestock alone!

Fred!
...flee! Oh, woe is me! The shape-shifter is coming! We're all...
FRED!
...doomed. What?
It's not a shape-shifter or any other kind of monster.
Well, what is it, [boy/girl]?
Well, it's just two penguins... disguised as a sheep.
Have you been out in the sun too long?

conversations.section: Historical dialogue / Al Kharid jetty

pages.x: You want passage to Daemonheim?
Well, don't stand around. Get on board.
Well, be on your way then. Leave me in peace!
Yes, the icy peninsula far to the north of here.
Ice, snow, harsh winds...
...and no sand or swamp sludge, clogging up every orifice.
Are you done with questions? Can we go now?
Grumpy? I should kill you where you stand!
But that wouldn't help with this damned humidity.
I need the snow in my boots, the sea wind stinging my face...
That's why I want to leave. Are you ready to go to Daemonheim?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hey it's the hero! Wow, you're amazing! How on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely - you've done a great job!

Is there anything I can do to help out?

How do you like your town?
It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.
What's happening around here?

Is there anything I can do to help out?

I for one am very pleased to have met you.

A diamond? Are you crazy?

I haven't brought my diamonds with me.
No tax, no entry.

First we collect a pile of gems and then we get a spider to spin 'em into a long web, we light the jewels by imbuing each one with a little bit of magic.
So you're telling me fairylights are made out of gems?
That's right, how else could we make 'em twinkle so beautifully?

conversations.section: Green with hat / Conversation 1

pages.x: Hello.

Wednesday
Saturday. You big folk really aren't the quickest!
Thursday
Saturday. You big folk really aren't the quickest!
Friday
Saturday. You big folk really aren't the quickest!
Saturday
Correct. You can go now.
I don't know.
Saturday. You big folk really aren't the quickest!

conversations.section: When speaking to the goebie named Shauny

pages.x: Look at the sky! Isn't it amazing? And the sea! Isn't it brilliant?
Are you okay?
Oh yes, very much so. I have a wonderful family, Thuk has just invited me into his clan...
Did you mean Thok?
Everyone is being so nice to me and making me feel so welcome. People are just so lovely.

Sorry?
The Ahhhhhk, in the Eastern Lands.
Ohh...
I am never going to forget Gielinor.
I'm glad you liked it. What are you going to tell the other goebies about it?

conversations.section: Telling your story to Gwir / After Mourning's End Part I

pages.x: So, you say Eluned spoke to you following the consecration? I imagine it was her who brought you back to Arianwyn?
Yes, but how did you know?
Well, this is a bit more recent, so I hopefully have the facts already.
That should save me a bit of talking, so I'll help by making sure you've got accurate information.
Great! So Arianwyn told you of the mourners being dark elves in disguise, working from their outpost in West Ardougne.
Correct, but the outpost is, in fact, underneath Ardougne, not in it.
Oh, thanks, let me just make that change. Okay, so you got your hands on a mourner outfit and infiltrated the outpost.
Yes, I did, where I met the head mourner.
I've got here that it was he who told you of their plans, saying they were overstating the threat to Lathas so that he would grant them control?
Exactly. With Lathas in fear of the Underground Pass, he was happy for them to somewhat rule West Ardougne, fake the plague and wall it off.
Unfortunately, this was precisely what they wanted: time and space to dig about below.

Indeed, they were digging, and after I had proven myself by continuing their efforts to fake the plague, the head mourner finally trusted me enough to inform me they were searching for an ancient elven power source...
Something that could speed the return of their 'Dark Lord'.
This source of power presumably being the Temple of Light...

conversations.section: Telling your story to Gwir / After Roving Elves

pages.x: Next I...
Ah, yes, I actually stopped to help Islwyn. He revealed to me that he is the grandson of Glarial.
Gracious Glarial.
Yes, I know the elves value her so. Islwyn was happy to hear that her final resting place was the waterfall Baxtorian had chosen, but her grave was not consecrated.
So you performed said consecration? That's very noble of you to fulfil Islwyn's wishes. Glarial, indeed, rests in peace - if only she had Baxtorian to rest with her...
You speak in a riddle of sorts. What exactly happened to Baxtorian?
Our great king of old, the most powerful of us all - he had such power.
When he returned to his home in the east to find Glarial missing - after years of searching for her - he entered the waterfall, never to appear again.
Wait, he entered it and never came out? So where is his body?
A sound question; where indeed?
Well, that was what happened. After the consecration, Eluned, who travels with Islwyn, was ready to task me again.

conversations.section: After doing the Grand Exchange tutorial

pages.x: Hello!
What? Oh, hello. I was deep in thought. Did you say something?

o: Do you know much about the prices for armour and weapons?

What sort of things are you selling?
Good old armour and weapons! My people - dwarves, you understand - are hoping I can trade with humans. Are you selling items here also?
I have already, yes.
Then good luck with your future bids!
Do you know much about the prices for armour and weapons?
Most certainly. My area of expertise.
I didn't say anything at all.
I thought you at least said, 'Hello'. I must be going mad. Do you think I'm going mad?

conversations.section: Talk-to / After Tribal Totem

pages.x: It's a fine day to be out in the garden, isn't it?

Days like these make me glad to be alive!

o: So... do you garden round the back, too?

pages.x: So... do you garden round the back, too?
That I do!
Doesn't all of the security around the house get in your way then?

Whose middle name?

Do you need any help?

conversations.section: Without level 99 Firemaking

pages.x: Can I help you at all?

o: Do you have anything for trade?
What is that cape you're wearing?

pages.x: Who are you?
My name is Ignatius Vulcan. Once I was - like you - an adventurer, but that was before I realised the beauty and power of flame! Just look at this...
Stare into the flame and witness the purity and power of fire! As my attraction to flame grew, so did my skills at firelighting.
I began to neglect my combat skills, my Mining skills and my questing. Who needs such mundane skills
when one can harness the power of fire? After years of practice I am now the acknowledged Master of Flame! Everything must be purified by fire!
Okaaaay! Err, I'll be going now. Umm, get better soon.
Do you have anything for trade?
What is that cape you're wearing?
This is a Skillcape of Firemaking. I was given it in recognition of my skill as the greatest firemaker in the lands! I AM the Master of Flame!
Hmm, I'll be going now. Keep a sharp look out for those men with their white jackets!
No, thanks.
Okay, keep the fire burning.

My appreciation.

No matter. I will take this brief moment of solace for what it is.
A good idea. How else can I help?
We have everything we need. If you still want to help: while we've been caring for the young boy, we've neglected our daily duties.
Getting hold of [number] [item] should be sufficient.

Oh, yes, Movario...
Oh...er, well, sorry, I'm not really supposed to divulge client details. Times are tough enough as it is; I can do without losing customers because of my gossiping!
Sorry.
You're in luck: here you go, but look after them this time.
Okay, thanks.

conversations.section: Talking to Markus / Without a Slayer assignment for a Slayer Tower monster

pages.x: Can I interest you in a job? I'll pay you for your work.

o: What would you like to say?
What sort of job are you offering?

pages.x: My name's Markus. I used to run a trading company in Falador, but now I'm a warrior, fighting the evils of Morytania.
Actually, I've found that fighting isn't really my thing, so I'm hiring people to do all that stuff for me.
If you're interested in doing some combat yourself, I'd be happy to give you a job. I can pay you.
I'm hiring people to kill the monsters in this tower. I'd do it myself, but I've found that fighting isn't really my thing.

Alternatively, I bought myself some books about combat, but they're too technical for me, so you could have one as your payment.
Incidentally, if you already have an assignment from elsewhere to kill creatures that can be found within the tower, do come and see me.
Fulfil your task within the tower, and I'll give you a special contract that'll work in tandem with it, and give you an additional reward on top.
So would you like a job now?
Excellent. Take a look at my contracts and see which one you'd like to do.
Alright, but come back if you change your mind. I can pay you for your work.

pages.x: Hey there!

Can I interest you in a currency doubler? It'll mean you get double token drops for the rest of the event!

Would you like to have a look at the store?

Could I help with that? Where is it?

conversations.section: While obelisk is active, first conversation

Who?
The other druids; Pikkupstix will be most upset.

Can I help?
You want to help us get shards?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / At the Falador Party Room / Player

What's so funny?
Just a joke that he told me. Care to hear it?

2 Parrots sit on a perch. One says to the other 'Can you smell fish'? Hee heheee he ho ho.

Sigh. 2 Parrots sit on a perch. One says to the other 'Can you smell fish'? Hee heheee he ho ho.

ARGH!! 2 PARROTS. ON A PERCH. SMELLS FISHY.
No, still lost. Is one of them a penguin?
You're doing it on purpose now aren't you? Please leave me alone!

pages.x: Welcome to my humble abode. What can I do for you?
Up at the Rogues' Castle, you mentioned a business. What was that about?
Ah, yes, I run...what do you call it? Something of a little jewellery business.
So, if you happen to come across any unenchanted gold jewellery, I'll gladly take it off your hands for a decent sum of coins.
Only gold jewellery?
Correct. I'm not buying anything that isn't beautiful, bright gold. My...eh...clients are picky about that.
I have some right here.
Good, good, just hand it over and I'll see what I can give for it.
Alright, I'll remember that.
Nothing.

conversations.section: In the Desert Monkey Colony / While wearing a monkeyspeak amulet

pages.x: Welcome to Chimpish Airways: the premium monkey carpet station for a monkey in a hurry.

o: What does Ali Morrisane think of this set up?
I'd like to see what's lost and found.

pages.x: I'd like to travel.
Of course, all travel is free for you from this hub. Where would you like to go?
What does Ali Morrisane think of this set up?
He came here, with a monkeyspeak amulet, and accused us of stealing his carpets.

A deal?

What's up with your assistant?

I thought humans were supposed to be cutesy and full of energy; if anything, he's driving away business.
I've got to go.
On behalf of Chimpish Airways, we hope to see you soon.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Hello there, adventurer. What brings you to me today?
I'm Salusan, though most call me Sal. Most of my life I have made weapons for the warriors of Iaia.
Recent events encouraged me to relocate, rapidly.
I see opportunity in this place, though. I am much less bound by the expectations of my people.
On my travels around Anachronia, I witnessed the majesty of the dinosaurs on the island.
I often dreamed of one day becoming a dragon rider on my homeworld.
Do you think we ilujanka could ride dinosaurs too?
It's no more far-fetched than anything else I've seen going on this Potterington brand expansion.
My thoughts exactly.
I feel a kinship with these beasts. Potterington has allowed me some claws-on experience with them here.
Maybe one day I could convince some of them to fight alongside me.
Farewell.

conversations.section: After Within the Light and before Plague's End

pages.x: Hello, you look new here. Welcome to the Death Guard!
Death Guard? Nah, mate, I'm just a hired hand - a cleaner, ya know?
You're not...you know?
You're not an elf under that gasmask?
Elf? Nah, mate: human. You're talking like there's some sort of mass conspiracy going on.
Would you believe me if I said there was? What if you could take that gasmask off and be completely safe?
Nice try! 'Hello, you look new here' - that ol' routine, eh? 'Take yer mask off,' you say. 'It's perfectly safe,' you say.
Then, 'BOOM', Scotty gets the plague...and you'll steal my business!
You think I'd try to kill you just to become the new janitor?
Of course! Everyone's trying to move in on us! You shoulda seen the fiasco when we were working some waiting rooms for a guy called Mandrith.
Every other guy was coming at us with a dragon dagger!
Yet you live to tell the tale?
What can I say? This old broom's as lethal on people as it is on trash.

conversations.section: After One Piercing Note

pages.x: Hello again, adventurer.

o: Why didn't you tell Abbess Benita who the killer was?

pages.x: How are you doing?
Oh, I'm fine. The clock is running smoothly.
Why didn't you tell Abbess Benita who the killer was?
You're the adventurer. You solved the mystery and defeated the killer. It was better that she should hear it from you.
There's a saying: a stopped clock is right twice a day.
Well, I don't like that saying. A clock ten minutes slow is never right, but it's a lot more useful than one that's stopped.
What are you getting at?
What I am getting at is, perhaps it's better for someone to have the wrong time, if that's what keeps their clock going.
It's better than setting the clock right but having it stop.
You think it was right for me to lie?
I think that you were the mechanic, and it was your decision how best to fix the clock.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: In the Black Guard HQ in western Keldagrim / After Forgiveness of a Chaos Dwarf and before Birthright of the Dwarves

pages.x: I hope you're pleased with yourself, human. Your escapades have cost me my best officer and made me a laughing stock in the Palace.
I'll have to work hard to restore the Consortium's confidence in the Black Guard.
Now, was there anything else you wanted to talk about?

o: You need to deal with the Red Axe!

pages.x: You need to deal with the Red Axe!
We dealt with that in the Consortium meeting, human! I do not have the resources for an assault on the Red Axe stronghold. Now, leave me alone!
I am Bisi. I am the Supreme Commander of the Black Guard.
The Black Guard has many regiments across the dwarven realm. All the Commanders of those regiments report to me.
Oh yes, I helped Commander Lawgof once, in his fight against the goblins.
That's good to hear.
Now, was there anything else you wanted to talk about?
I have no news for you, human.

conversations.section: In eastern Keldagrim / Standard dialogue

pages.x: What'you want?
Do you-
What? Speak up, I can't hear you!
Uhm... I'm just looking for some pickaxes! Do you have any?
Do I have any pickaxes? Do I? Of course I do, this is a pickaxe shop, isn't it!
Do you-
What? Stop mumbling!
I want a quest!
I don't have any lousy quests... I've got someone who's helping me already! Well, I say helping... he takes his merry time to do his chores, my son does.
Then perhaps I can help in some way?
Pfft, I doubt it... maybe when my son fouls up again, but not now.
Nothing really.
Then clear off!

conversations.section: In the Orthen Oubliette / Standard dialogue

pages.x: Where did Zaros go?
Your predecessor has damaged the oubliette and released Raksha.
My predecessor?
The purple deity. He told me of your coming.
He told me of your strange new species.
He told me you can survive in this environment.
You must enter the inner chamber and stop Raksha.
Do you need anything else?
Wait, who are you?
I am the Keeper, the caretaker of the oubliette.
I maintain the apparatus that sustains and imprisons Raksha, the prisoner of this place.
I have maintained this vigil for many centuries, and the seals have never been broken until now.
Do you need anything else?

conversations.section: Normal dialogue

pages.x: How are you today?
Great, thanks! If you bring me some teeth, I'll offer you a fair price for them.

o: What sort of teeth and what price do you pay?
Where can I find the teeth you're after?

pages.x: Bring you some teeth?
Yes, soldier, you heard me. The fairy economy is based on the appropriation of teeth - they're very valuable to us.
If you bring me the right kind of teeth, I'll give you gold in return.
What sort of teeth and what price do you pay?
Specifically, we're looking for kebbit teeth, suqah teeth, 'old' teeth and, finally, monkey dentures.
And prices?
Oh, yes, prices...
Kebbit teeth are quite common, so we only pay one gold for those; monkey dentures are not that in demand, so we only pay 50 gold; suqah and 'old' teeth will fetch you a hefty 2,000 gold each.
Where can I find the teeth you're after?

You can get kebbit teeth from hunting, I believe; suqah teeth you'll have to investigate yourself; old teeth you can gain from archaeological excavation areas; monkey dentures you'll also have to research yourself.
Okay, thanks.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Dialogue 3

pages.x: Hi there!
Hello, what are you doing here?
Oh, just taking a look at these displays. I'm a bit of a history buff.
Really? Tell me something I didn't know!
Well, did you know that Bob the Cat is... no, no... you'd never believe me anyway.
He's what? Tell me!

o: (If the player has not completed A Tail of Two Cats:)
(If the player has completed A Tail of Two Cats:)

pages.x: No, no. Couldn't possibly ruin the surprise.
ARG! Tell me!
If you really want to know, go talk to Unferth in his house in Burthorpe.
He's a very famous hero! Robert the Strong!
Oh, yes, I knew that.
Oh, I thought I was going to surprise you.
Nope, but thanks for sharing.

conversations.section: In New Varrock

pages.x: Ho there, loyal thrall to Zemouregal. How can I help you?

o: Are there bots in this world?

pages.x: The name's Craig Forrester. I'm in charge of Bot Wars: the finest Bot-vs-Bot experience this side of Water Mountain.
Bot Wars? You get bots to fight each other?
Oh yes! The arena's owned by Melzar, and we have hudnreds of people coming to watch. Fun for all the family!
Even Zemouregal turns up. He's a big fan. He's building his own bot for battling, I believe.
I would invite you, but the league finished last week. Sir Jump-A-Lot was crowned champion, if you're interested.
His defeated enemies are mounted next to me. Impressive, no?
'In this world?' I like it, very dramatic. I might add that to the end of everything I say.
'Come see bots fight other bots, in this world!'
Oooh, that's good. Anyway yeah - we have bots.
Melzar makes them, and everyone watches them fight. They used to call him Mad Melzar, but look at him now.
He's Multi-Millionaire Melzar now - in this world.
See you around, then.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hey it's the hero! Wow, you're amazing! How on earth did you manage to tackle those two juvinates and Gadderanks? And the town is lovely - you've done a great job!
You're more than welcome.

o: How do you like your town?
Is there anything I can do to help out?

pages.x: What do you do here?
I'm Victor. I may be just a kid, but I'll duff you in! You don't look that tough to me!
How do you like your town?
It's just perfect, thanks so much for your efforts.
What's happening around here?
Oh, not much really, we're all still hiding from the vampyres and eking out a living from this terrible place, hopefully soon we'll be strong enough to make the journey to the temple on the Salve.
Is there anything I can do to help out?
Not as far as I know, we have some basic amenities now which is so very useful, we're all incredibly grateful to you.
I've never really seen or known a hero before, so I have nothing to compare one to, but I suspect in most people's judgement, you would be one!
I for one am very pleased to have met you.
Okay, thanks.

conversations.section: The bookcase / The Great Labour

pages.x: In their effort to achieve perfection, the masters created every single world in the universe.
The masters created world after world from sacred clay, each an improvement on the last, born from the essence of their beings. The first worlds were primal and chaotic.
The masters tore them asunder, and cast the discarded clay into the abyssal void. The masters were dissatisfied with the work of their bare hands.
They created tools - artefacts of power - to wield as they sought perfection in their creation. They hungered to create the most perfect of worlds.
The masters toiled for aeons. The masters travelled through the formless void, creating world after world. The masters improved their technique.
They created precision tools, and abandoned their inferior prototypes on the failed worlds.
In time, Ful created the Elder Kiln: an artefact that manufactures living implements. At the site of the last few worlds, she planted the Elder Kiln beneath the surface.
Sacred lava flowed through sacred clay. The TokHaar awoke. Forged by the Elder Kiln, we worked to fulfil our masters' plan.
The TokHaar-Hok heard the masters, and conveyed their orders. The TokHaar-Ket, the TokHaar-Xil, the TokHaar-Mej, the TokHaar-Hur obeyed.
As the TokHaar spread out across each forming world, we TokHaar-Hok increased in number, to carry the words of the masters to every corner of the world.
When our work was complete, the masters looked upon their creation, and were dissatisfied.
The TokHaar returned to the sacred lava, and Ful tore the Elder Kiln from the imperfect world.
The masters started anew, hoping that with their next project they would achieve perfection.
The TokHaar improved with each attempt, becoming more effective instruments of the masters. We laboured. We obeyed. We served our great purpose. It was glorious.

conversations.section: With Wilough's red envelope

pages.x: Greetings, Player.
Hello! What can I do for you?
I'm here to deliver a letter to you from Wilough.
Oh! Splendid! Let's have a look.

o: The Wise Old Man opens the envelope and begins to read the letter.

pages.x: What a lovely...
Oh...
Oh no.
What is this language!?
What the heck is steamed ham!?
Youngsters these days have no respect!
Alright... on with you then.
I'm sorry.

conversations.section: Valentine's Day Event / Before the event / First day

pages.x: Times by the three, and carry the nine...
Excuse me?
Oh sorry, I didn't see you there. How can I help?
Who are you?
My name is Deedit. I'm a wizard. A pretty good one at that I'd like to think, although recently I've been branching out.
Branching out? What are you doing?
Oh yes, I'm dabbling in a bit of invention. Have you heard of it? Jolly interesting subject.
So many possibilities.
Goodbye.
What are you doing?
I'm having a little scout around. This seems like the perfect area for a bit of an experiment.
Give my new idea a bit of a whirl. Just have to choose the right spot.
Well, time waits for no man, not even a wizard.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Inside the Wizards' Guild

pages.x: What are you doing bothering me? Don't you think some of us have work to do?
I thought you were here to help?
Well... I am, I suppose, anyway... we're very busy here, hurry up, what do you want?

o: What is there to do in the Wizards' Guild?
What are the requirements to get in the Wizards' Guild?
What do you do in the Guild?

pages.x: What is there to do in the Wizards' Guild?
This is the finest wizards' establishment in the land. We have magic portals to the other towers of wizardry around Gielinor.
We have a particularly wide collection of runes in our rune shop.
We sell some of the finest mage robes in the land and we have a training area full of zombies for you to practice your magic on.
What are the requirements to get in the Wizards' Guild?
You need a magic level of 66, the high magic energy level is too dangerous for anyone below that level.
What do you do in the Guild?
I'm the Grand Secretary for the Wizards' Guild, I have lots of correspondence to keep up with, as well as attending to the discipline of the more problematic guild members.
Ok, thanks.

conversations.section: First task / Returning to the Curator and asking about A Cultist's Journey

pages.x: Have you spoken to Johanhus yet?
Yes, I have. Johanhus believes that he has uncovered a mystery.
He believes that there are caches of First-Age armour dedicated to the Elder Gods buried somewhere in the world.
He thinks he is close to finding out where and intends to go and recover the armour.
Incredible. There is no evidence of humans worshipping the Elder Gods throughout recorded history.
If he's correct, he may have blundered upon a find of actual historical significance.
I'm not sure he cares about that much. He believes that if he finds the armour then the Elder Gods will recognise him and bestow him with their favour.
Why would he want that?
He believes that they are going to solve all of H.A.M's problems...
The fool. The Elder Gods are vast, primordial beings whose only concern is the pursuit of perfection in creation.
Why would such beings care about being worshipped, and why would they see humans as special? Clearly, we are going to need to keep a very close eye on him.
Not that it should be too difficult, he seems to leave a trail of evidence wherever he goes, which I am sure to hear about from somewhere.
I'm sure I'll be needing your help again soon.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue after Darkness of Hallowvale

pages.x: Well, I guess so.

o: I'm lost, can you help me?
Do you know about the Myreque?
(whisper) Do you know about the Myreque?

pages.x: What do you do here?
I was playin', but den da flapsies came so I was hidin'. Don't want da flapsies to bit me.
I'm lost, can you help me?
Urm, well I fink we're in sector [one/two/three/four/five/six]. Not sure what else to say. I'm only a kid ya know!
Do you know about the Myreque?
Err, me dad says I'm not allowed to talk about that. Do you have any sweets?
No, sorry, but please can you answer my questions?
(whisper) Do you know about the Myreque?
Err, no! I'm not allowed to say any thingies about dem; but they're the good 'uns what can help us.
Okay, thanks.

conversations.section: Talk to / On a member's world

pages.x: What can I help you with adventurer? Armour? Abilities?

o: I'd like to see your store.
What rewards do you have to offer?

pages.x: There are many items and abilities I can offer you in exchange for any anima fragments you may have collected while exploring the worlds beyond the portals!
We've devised a couple of new techniques I could teach you. Bladed Dive can help you chase down your enemies.
Salt the Wound will help you take down larger foes and even improve your Dazing Shot.
We also have a few techniques to improve your Slayer routine. Slayer's Insight increases your slayer experience gain by 10% for 30 seconds.
Kuradal's Favour allows monsters in Kuradal's dungeon to respawn instantly for 30 seconds, and Aggression will force all nearby monsters to instantly attack you.
I'm also offering slayer contracts, which can be completed within Shattered Worlds, granting you slayer experience as you progress.
You may wish instead to requisition one of our suits of armour. Or perhaps a helpful slayer mask.
The last thing I have on offer is a little strange. A strange creature has wandered out of the portal and into our world.
We've determined that it should be harmless, and the commander has tasked me with finding it a home. The creature appears to be prone to... changing.
Changing?
Changing.

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Collector of curiosities / Task #1

pages.x: I am a collector of curiosities, and I currently have the greatest collection of [item] in all of Menaphos!
Well, I did...
What happened?
Another collector has arrived in the city and their collection is dwarfing mine.
How many more [item] do they have?
I've heard they have [number] more [item] than I do.
So, if someone were to bring you [number] [item], you would have the greatest collection again?
Yes! Would you do this for me?
That will suffice.
Where could I find [item]?

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.

conversations.section: Adventure begins / Starting out / Talking to Gudrik

pages.x: I need to talk to you abut something very important, [laddie/lassie].
What's the matter?
I had a dream – a vision! The world was on fire. All of Gielinor was consumed in flames! When I awoke, I knew I had to come and get you. You're special, [laddie/lassie].
You have talents and abilities beyond those of ordinary folk. Gielinor needs heroes, now more than ever. That's why you have to come with me to the mainland.
Once we're there, I'll guide you to places where you can put your talents to use. But before we set off, we'll need to prepare you for the journey ahead.
You're going to need some food and a decent sword, for a start – that rusty old blade of yours wouldn't cut a load of bread!
Right you are, [laddie/lassie].
Gudrik's the name. Bane of the baneful and defender of the defenceless.
Proud member of the Society of Intrepid Adventurers, and three-time winner of the Beard of the Year award.
You take a knock to the head or something? We're in Ashdale, far from the shores of the mainland. Where else would we be?
We need to prepare you for the journey to the mainland.
Our destination is the harbour, but first we need to get you some food, and that means heading down to the fishing spot.

conversations.section: Fishing / Talking to Hendrik

pages.x: Saradomin's blessing upon you, my friend.

o: What can you tell me about this place?

pages.x: Well I was about to do a spot of fishing, but then I heard what sounded like fighting. Is everything alright?
There was a zombie attack.
Zombies? Is Ashdale? I've never heard anything like it! Was anyone harmed?
You came to the rescue, eh? I might have known. You always did strike me as the courageous type. Still, I've never known something like that to happen in Ashdale.
Let's hope it's not a sign of worse to come.
Glad to hear it. Let me know if the situation changes, won't you?
Since it was founded, Ashdale has become something of a refuge, a place for people who want some peace and quiet. Let's hope it stats that way.
Saradomin is one of the beings that first brought life into Gielinor. Most of us who live in Ashdale have taken Saradomin as our patron.
He stands for truth, justice, and – above all – order.
Saradomin watch over you, my friend.
Have you seen him?

o: What is that outfit you're wearing?

pages.x: Who are you looking for?
The Easter Bunny! It's that time of year and I expected him to be here.
Oh no, I haven't seen him for a few years. This is a celebration of Guthix instead.
Driven into hiding, eh? I guess that's a good thing!
What happened between you two? Most people like the Easter Bunny - he brings chocolate eggs and-
Not just any eggs. MILK CHOCOLATE EGGS!
Sorry, am I missing a problem here?
What about all the people of the world who are lactose intolerant? What about the pain and suffering he bought upon those who suffer from this ailment?
That's what this is about? You're hunting the Easter Bunny because you're lactose intolerant.
Yes! And so far so good. If you do see him though, let me know immediately. For now let me keep watch and everyone will remain safe!
This? Why, this is my Yolk Breaker outfit. Perfect attire for hunting the Easter Bunny!

conversations.section: At Senntisten Temple / After Ritual of the Mahjarrat

pages.x: Player, you fought bravely during the ritual. I am pleased that Lucien is no longer among our number.
Yes, but only to be replaced by an even larger threat. At least Lucien only wanted to rule over this plane; the dragonkin want to destroy it!
Yes, it is troubling... I am sure you will do all you can to prevent that.
Will you help?
Maybe, I don't know. I have certain other priorities right now. When my plans have come to fruition it will be easier to deal with such enemies.
What about Jhallan? I feel bad for him; I mean, I was the one who helped him to hide under the ritual site.
You do like to get involved, don't you?
It seems strange that you would be concerned when your race is so short-lived. It is the Mahjarrat way that the weak serve the strong.
While he was not my own choice, we would have all died long ago without the sacrifice of others.
We Zarosians may be fewer in number, but our day will come again, mark my words.
Speaking of Zarosians, after you left...Sliske tried to turn me into one of his Barrows wights, but took one of my friends instead.
I have no control over his actions. Even alongside other Mahjarrat, he's always been...different.
While I would rather not lose him as my ally, I would not begrudge your revenge, though I doubt you will find him unless he wishes to be found.

conversations.section: Conversation

pages.x: RARRRRRRR!
They fear me! I am the LORD OF BONES AND THE LORD OF BONES FEARS NO BEING, FOR I AM MADE OF BONES ALREADY!
Go on, try me... What could possibly strike fear into me.
A dog?
*gulp*
Or perhaps a trip to the famed Ectofuntus temple's bonecrusher?
*GULP*
Or perhaps... worst of all...
You catch a whiff of bruning Marrentill on the breeze... and then you see it. Someone training prayer on an altar, guilded with stunning gold leaf...
They turn, and see... YOU. BAM.
You find yourself snatched up and atop the altar, ready to be sacrificed to the gods for some soul to earn a bit of knowledge of prayers.
Make it stop. MAKE IT STOP!
At once, M'lord.

conversations.section: Before Love Story / Subsequent times / After viewing the recording

pages.x: Yes?

o: The robber in the recording looked familiar.
Can I see that recording again, please?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: The robber in the recording looked familiar.
Oh, you recognised him too?
Yes, and I can tell you where he lives!
Thanks, but we already know where to find our suspect.
So are you going to have him arrested?
We're certainly keeping an eye on him. I'm afraid I can't give you any more details about the case.
Fair enough.
Can I see that recording again, please?
I'd like you to pay me 50 gp first.
Sorry, I don't want anything.
Ok.

conversations.section: Talk-to / Normally

pages.x: Can I help you?

o: Any hints where I can go adventuring?

pages.x: I'll have a pint of beer please.
Ok, that'll be two coins please.
Any hints on where I can go adventuring?
Ooh, now. Let me see...
Well there is the Varrock sewers. There are tales of untold horrors coming out at night and stealing babies from houses.
Sounds perfect! Where's the entrance?
It's just to the east of the palace.
Heard any gossip?
I'm not that well up on the gossip out here.
I've heard that the bartender in the Blue Moon Inn has gone a little crazy, he keeps claiming he is part of something called a computer game.
What that means, I don't know. That's probably old news by now though.

conversations.section: Talk-to / With a keg of mead before making a delivery to Rusty Anchor during The Need for Mead event

pages.x: I was wondering if you could give some feedback on this mead?
Where was it brewed? Who's the brewer?
I have no idea where it was brewed but the brewer is called Leslie.
I'm not trying anything they make, ever again. Not after last time...
What happened last time?
That's not for you to know.
Actually, you know what, hand it over. Let me have a look.
Whoa! Don't tip it all away.
I'm doing a justice to Gielinor by ensuring no one else has to drink this.
Okay then...
Mr. Grumpy...
What did you say?!
Bye!

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / First time dialogue

pages.x: Hello, Player! Back for more, are you?
Well, King Roald did say that you could use some help giving the entire beacon network some serious testing.
Could we ever! There are fourteen beacons in all, spanning the south and west borders of the Wilderness.
What we really need is for someone to try to keep alight as many beacons as possible, all at the same time.
I should warn you: it's not as easy as it sounds - some beacons are harder to light than other and there may be burning issues you have to resolve before you can access each beacon.
The more testing we do, however, the more prepared we'll be in case of adversity.
If you're interested in helping, I suggest you plan a route and then give it a trial run or two, just to make sure that you can get where you need to go and you have everything you need.
It requires some specialist skills, but you'll be well rewarded. Not to mention the job satisfaction.
You are not only doing a great service for the southern kingdoms, but...
But?
But what could be better than spending every moment of one's life starting BIG, LONG LINES OF FIRE!
Uh, Blaze?
Ahem. Sorry. So, yes. Do you have any burning questions for me?

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Do you want to go on a trip to Karamja?
The trip will cost you 30 coins.

o: (With a ring of charos (a) equipped:) Or I could pay you nothing at all...

pages.x: Yes please.

o: (If you have completed the Karamja easy tasks:)

pages.x: Wait a minute, didn't you earn Karamja gloves? Thought I'd seen you helping around the island. You can go on half price - 15 coins.
Or I could pay you nothing at all...
Mmmm, nothing at all, you say...
Yes, why not - jump aboard then.
No, thank you.

conversations.section: In Keldagrim / The resting Keldagrim conductor

pages.x: Wot you want?

o: I'd like to buy a ticket.

pages.x: What is this place?
Can't you see I'm 'aving a li'l break?
Now that you mention it, yes.
Where can you take me?
Can't you see I'm 'aving a li'l break?
Now that you mention it, yes.
I'd like to buy a ticket.
Can't you see I'm 'aving a li'l break?
Now that you mention it, yes.
I have to go.
Then why did ya waste my time?

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Hello.

o: Where do you take all this ore?
Why do you use bones to build with?

pages.x: How's the mining going?
Where do you take all this ore?
To the town of Dorgesh-Kaan, deep in the caves.
Why do you use bones to build with?
Well, our legends say that on the surface there was a substance called 'wood', which grew out of the ground in towers.
But we cannot get wood here, so we can only build with stone, bone, and iron.
The only bones long enough are those of the fearsome giant frog!
Oh, right.
Giant frogs aren't fearsome!
Perhaps not for a mighty adventurer like you, but we think they're terrifying!

conversations.section: At Seers' Village Courthouse, after King's Ransom / Before accepting the first case

pages.x: Ah, it's you. Anna Sinclair's famous Defence lawyer.
Well, I don't know about famous...
Indeed, perhaps infamous is better.
I'm glad you stopped by. We have had quite an influx of cases since you last came to work.
Feel like stepping into that courtroom again? I've got an easy case to get you back into the swing of things.
Sure. I'd be glad to.
Great! I'll explain what you need to do. I'm going to assign you a case. You'll then get to choose whether you prosecute or defend it.
Once we've sorted that out, you can get background information and case reports from
the filing cabinet next to me. Read them and, when you're ready, head downstairs to the courtroom to start the trial.
Okay, I've assigned you a case. An alleged mugger (level: 6) is on trial for mugging someone in Edgeville.
No thanks.
Too bad. Well, come back when you're interested.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / Before giving him a cave eel

pages.x: What you doing here? No one told Crate to expect visitors!
I'm helping King Roald test the fire beacon network.
Hmph, no one tell me about it. But, while you here, maybe you could be of use.
How so?
I very hungry. Want some lava eel. You bring some to me.
What? I'm not an errand [boy/girl]! I'm here to help test these beacons.
We talk about that later. For now, me hungry. You bring some lava eel for me or not?

o: Fine, I'll bring you some lava eel.

pages.x: Fine, I'll bring you some lava eel.
Good. And hurry. It matter of great importance.
Sure.
Keep dreaming!
Then begone, before I lose temper.

conversations.section: In Varrock

pages.x: Welcome to Varrock Museum!

o: Do you know where I could find any treasure?
Talk about the master quest cape.

pages.x: Have you any interesting news?
Yes, we have an expedition underway at a rather interesting island to the north of Morytania. We believe that it may be of archaeological significance.
Oh? That sounds interesting.
Indeed. We're looking for qualified archaeologists to travel there to assist the expedition.
Would I qualify?
Do you know where I could find any treasure?
Look around you! This museum is full of treasures!
No, I meant treasures for ME.
Any treasures this museum knows about it goes to great lengths to acquire.
I notice that you have acquired a new cape.
Oh this? The design was donated to the museum as a symbol of the spirit of adventure and the pursuit of knowledge. Would you like to purchase one?

conversations.section: During In Search of the Myreque

pages.x: Hey, what're you doin' here?

o: I've come to help the Myreque. I've brought weapons.
I don't have to answer to you!
I'm lost, can you show me the way out?

pages.x: I've come to help the Myreque. I've brought weapons.
I don't have to answer to you!
You do if you know what's good for you!
No reason.
Come on... speak up! I may be able to help you. However, you's gotta know that you's trespassing and that, by rights, I should slap you around a bit.
You know: just like as a warning.
I'm lost, can you show me the way out?
You got yourself in here, now get yourself out. And quickly, if I were you.
I have to go.
Sure... be on your way, stranger.

conversations.section: In Draynor Village / Claiming Treborn

pages.x: Howdy there, partner.
Hi, Diango.
Are you here to recall memories long forgotten?
Yes.
Well there was a video released recently about the year ahead in RuneScape, maybe you can find the answer from that.
Okay.
No.
Memories long forgotten?
Yes, I managed to capture something North-West of Eagle's Peak, I can give it to you if you like...
There's just a small matter of the secret code, and then it's yours...
Are you here to recall memories long forgotten?

conversations.section: Talk-to / With a catspeak amulet / Before All Fired Up

pages.x: Hello, cat. What on earth are you doing here?
Oh, I'm looking after this beacon for King Roald.
How's that going for you?
All's well, life is peaceful, the flowers are blooming, the birds are singing, and it's the most lovely of days today.
Wow, you seem very pleased about things!
I am! I'm so happy, I can't help but wag my tail and bound about recklessly!
It's nice to have such a high purpose in life and to have earned the trust and affection of such a noble human as King Roald.
Wait - you're a cat right? Not a dog in disguise?
Uh, by 'wag my tail' I meant...um...'purr really loudly'. And, just for the record, I'm, uh, thoroughly indifferent to humans. And aloof. I'm very, very aloof.
That sounds more like it.
Say, you won't repeat what I said before, will you? I wouldn't want any more marks on my cat license.
Don't worry, moggy; your secrets are safe with me.
Purrrrrrr!

conversations.section: After Gunnar's Ground, at the Leptoc manor / Before engraving the ruby bracelet

pages.x: Come in, my friend, come in! There is another matter I could use your assistance with.

o: I want to talk about something else.}}
I don't have time right now.

pages.x: I have some more jewellery for Gudrun and I need your help to engrave them.

o: I want to talk about something else.
I don't have time right now.

pages.x: A magnificent ruby bracelet.
That's a shame. Maybe you can try again another time.
What can I do for you?

o: This is a very large house.
I'd like to see the poem you wrote for Gunthor.
I seem to have mislaid my swanky boots.

pages.x: Every morning I wake to sunshine and birdsong! Life is marvellous!
I know! I don't know where Gunthor would have got such a thing. Maybe Gudrun has some idea.
I seem to have mislaid my swanky boots.
Goodbye!

conversations.section: Without tea in backpack

pages.x: Hello dearie! What can old Elsie do for you?

o: Can you tell me a story?
Can you tell me how to get rich?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: What are you making?
I'm knitting a new stole for Father Lawrence downstairs. He could do with something to keep his neck warm, standing in that draughty old church all day.
Can you tell me a story?
Maybe I could tell you a story if you'd fetch me a nice cup of tea.
I'll think about it.
Can you tell me how to get rich?
Well, dearie, I'm probably not the best person to ask about money, but I think the best thing would be for you to get a good trade.
If you've got a trade you can earn your way, that's what my old father told me, Saradomin rest his soul.
I hear people try to get rich by fighting in the Wilderness north of here but that's no way for honest folks to earn a living!
So get yourself a good trade, and keep working at it. There's always folks wanting to buy ore and food around here.
Thanks for the advice.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge / Post-quest dialogue / Claiming the cash reward from the yeti dung, if the player doesn't tell Explorer Jack the truth

pages.x: I let those stones thaw, making a very smelly discovery.
I'm sorry.
You knew about it?
I did. When I exited the cave with the 'stones' I met some snow imps, who let me into a secret.
This whole quest was a prank on you, as they judged you nosy, greedy and annoying. It was meant to teach you a lesson.
They didn't leave me much choice but to complete their plan.
Haha, that's a good one, chum! I suppose I deserve it. Nosy, haha!
Glad to see you're taking it lightly.
Eh, I've got good news! While you were gone, I managed to sell them to a wandering witch for a goodly sum.
She identified it as yeti dung, and said it was a key ingredient in some very advanced ancient potions.
Really?
Yes indeed! I've kept some of the money for you. There you go.
Thank you!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Now you look like someone who goes to a lot of fancy dress parties.
Errr...what are you saying exactly?
I'm just saying that perhaps you would like to peruse my selection of garments.
Or, if that doesn't interest you, then maybe you have something else to offer? I'm always on the lookout for interesting or unusual new materials.

o: Okay, let's see what you've got, then.
(After Eagles' Peak:) Could you make another bird costume for me?
I think I might just leave the perusing for now thanks.
(If you do not have suitable fur in your inventory:) Can you make clothing suitable for hunting in?
(If you have fur in your inventory:) Could you make anything out of this fur that I got from hunting?

pages.x: Okay, let's see what you've got, then.
Could you make another eagle costume for me?
Certainly, if you can supply the materials. I'll need appropriate feathers, swamp tar and some yellow dye. It'll also cost you 25 gold pieces.
I think I might just leave the perusing for now, thanks.
Can you make clothing suitable for hunting?
Certainly. Take a look at my range of made-to-order items. If you can supply the furs, I'll gladly make any of these for you.
Could you make anything out of this fur that I got from hunting?
Certainly. Take a look at my range of made-to-order items. If you can supply the furs, I'll gladly make any of these for you.

conversations.section: In Taverley / After Let Them Eat Pie

pages.x: Ruined! I'm ruined!
What's the matter?
Don't interrupt my woe!
Ahem... Ruined! Oh woe is me!
First I lose my spices, and then that blubbery whale Rolo goes and gives away all the food I could've used to buy some more!
I'm going to starve in the gutter; my clothes taken by footpads and my body heaped into a pauper's grave!
Oh come on, I'm sure things aren't that bad.
Hmm, now you mention it.
I know, I'll just stop paying my workers so much, and drop the quality of the goods I sell.
If I keep firing people and charging through the roof for my wares I'll soon be back to normal!
Uh...
Thank you, uneducated and filthy stranger. You may have saved my life!
You're... welcome.

conversations.section: Summer events / When talked to

pages.x: Welcome to my new rebuildathon!

o: What do I need to do here?
What do I get for helping?

pages.x: Simple really. Choose a sandcastle you want to help build and start working on it.
I've got some visiting dignitaries mind so it's worth trying to impress them while they're here to get a better reward.
It's hot work mind, so if you get too hot you might want to find yourself an ice cream to cool off.
Straight down to business, eh?
Help me build these sandcastles and you'll get some Construction XP.
If you take note of the visiting dignitary then you'll get a greater reward for impressing them with your work.
My name's George, and I'm the foreman of this project.
Bit of a change from my previous work - helping to rebuild Lumbridge after the battle - but this looks to be just as challenging.
Really? They just look like sandcastles - how hard can they be to build?
Are you questioning my building abilities?
Let's just say they're more advanced than your regular sandcastle - I've got the blueprints, you just focus on the building.

conversations.section: After The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Shhh! I'm waiting for the show!
What's on the bill?
There's a performance of an epic from olden times tonight! The epic of Bukalla!
Bukalla?
He was a famed slayer of daggermouths in olden times. It's a very inspirational song.

o: Sounds interesting! Maybe I'll stick around.

pages.x: Sounds boring.
Well, you're missing out on a glorious piece of history.

conversations.section: In the Gnome Village Dungeon / After The Prisoner of Glouphrie

pages.x: Hello, Player. Did you come to tell me about Gramps?

o: Actually, I came here for Glarial's pebble.

pages.x: Player! I can't thank you enough for getting Gramps out of that pickle! You can't imagine the trouble you would have been in if anything had happened to him.
Can't believe you left that letter in a book.
It's okay, Golrie. It all worked out in the end. Although, I'm fairly certain your granddad hasn't given up with his plans to bring down Glouphrie and Arposandra.
Keep an eye on him and make sure he doesn't go and do anything silly, will you?
Mum will help with that, don't you worry. I'll keep doing what I do. You know, cataloguing and stuff.
I heard your mum's staying around the village now, to train as a tree whisperer. Your mum is full of surprises.
Yeah? Well, your mum...
Naah, just kidding!
Anyway! Thanks again, Player! I'll see you around!
Bye!
Actually, I came here for Glarial's pebble.

conversations.section: After Birthright of the Dwarves

pages.x: Who you? Grunsh think Grunsh remember you, but Grunsh not sure.

o: I'm no one you know. Goodbye.

pages.x: You don't remember me?
Grunsh think maybe you kind to Grunsh once...but Grunsh forget.

o: Chaos dwarves? Hreidmar? The Red Axe?

pages.x: What do you remember?
Grunsh not remember very much. Other ogresies, they say Grunsh arrive one day, they say Grunsh look very tired and sad.
They say Grunsh go into cave, say magic-type wordsies, then go to sleep.
Grunsh not remember any of that. Grunsh just remember he wake up in cave. Grunsh not remember what happen before.
But Grunsh happy in Gu'tanoth, living with ogresies, Grunsh eat chompy bird and get into fights! Life good!
Grunsh think best not try to work out what happen before. But Grunsh have feeling maybe you kind to him once, so Grunsh want say thank you.
Chaos dwarves? Hreidmar? The Red Axe?
Those things sound nasty and far away. Grunsh just simple ogre, Grunsh not know about those things.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: What are you doing here?
I'M ON SHOUTING DUTY!
No need to shout.
I'M SORRY I'VE BEEN SHOUTING INSULTS SO LONG I CAN'T HELP IT!
Who are you insulting?
THE TOWER IN NEIZINOT. THEY SHOUT INSULTS BACK.
Err, why?
THE KING TELLS US TO.
Your King is a strange person.

o: Oh well, I'd better get going

pages.x: Can I watch? I'm curious.
IF YOU LIKE!
Oh well, I'd better get going

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Other dialogue

pages.x: Can I help you?
Can I go upstairs?
Yes, citizen. Before you do, I am instructed to give you one final piece of information.
Should you find a player who acts in a way that breaks one of our rules, you should report them.
You can also right-click a player to examine them, and use the 'report' button on the top left of the examine interface.
Or you can simply click the 'Report an issue' button in your chat window and then the 'Report Player' button. You will then be shown the following screens:
If you used the 'Report' button you’ll see the first page, simply click a line of chat the player has said. Then click 'Next'.
For offences other than botting or bug abuse you can only report players who have spoken recently.
On the following page, click on the offence that the player has committed.
Finally, you’ll be given the option to temporarily ignore the player you’ve reported. That will last until you next log out.
Okay. Then what?
That's it! It really is that simple and it only takes a moment to do. Now, you may enter the training centre. Good luck, citizen.
Thanks!

conversations.section: Novtumberfest / At a Wolly? event / Requesting hint

pages.x: I have lost Wolly, my wolpertinger, have you seen him?

o: What can you tell me to help me find him?

pages.x: I love wolpertingers, they are just so cute!
Yeah they are! How many do you have?
Too many to count, you can never have too many wolpertingers.
I guess that's cool... what do you call them?
Wolly.
All of them?
Yeah, what else would you call a wolpertinger?
But anyway...
Can you help me find Wolly?
What can you tell me to help me find him?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue, in the Worker District of Menaphos

pages.x: Hi!
Hello, traveller. How may I be of assistance?

o: What's a monk doing in a place like this?
Which monastery do you come from?

pages.x: What's a monk doing in a place like this?
Menaphos is a wondrous place full of beauty and splendour, but its beauty is tarnished by its misguided faith.
The people here worship the Menaphite Pantheon and not the divine radiance of the glorious Saradomin.
So I am here to save their souls, by bringing them the wisdom of Saradomin.
Really?
It beats being stuck in the monastery!
Which monastery do you come from?
I belong to the monastery north of Falador.
You're a long way from home.
Yeah, I miss the guys.

conversations.section: Combining / First hand of glory

pages.x: Who is this? Who is messing with things they don't understand again?
What just happened? I just looked at this hand and then your voice was in my head?
I'm using the Player Contact spell. This is Player, isn't it? I should have known. This is Aris, by the way.
What? What's a player? I'm confused?
Perpetually. And you are also messing around with a hand of glory! Those can be dangerous in the wrong hands...
You know what I meant!
Okay, so what can I use this hand for and how can I make it safe?
The safest use for a hand of glory is to use a Ring of Luck on it. Anything else and the universe could explode. I mean, it could anyway.
Add any luck ring, got it!
