Did I say 'any'? No, I specifically said 'Ring of Luck'. You have to take baby steps with these things.
Universe. Exploding. Gotcha.
If you find multiple hands of glory, then maybe you can start to slowly build up which tier of ring you use...

conversations.section: Combining / Third hand of glory

pages.x: Aris, are you there?
Who is this? I'm...busy!
It's Player. I was expecting you to contact me about this hand of glory.
I wasn't planning to - you should have figured this out yourself by now. Do you need me to hold your hand for everything?
Oh, right, sorry.
It's just that you contacted me for the first two hands...
A Ring of Fortune. Use a Ring of Fortune. Now, can I get back to my soaps?
Soap?
Not 'soap', 'soaps'. They're a bit like dramat- You know what, never mind.
Okay. Sorry again. Bye!
No, I think she's gone.

conversations.section: Interactions / Interaction 1

pages.x: Hello!
HELLOOO!

o: The scarab seems to be ignoring you.

pages.x: HELLLOOOOOOOOOOO?
This better be worth breaking my vow of silence for. What do you want?
What do you call a psychic scarab?
*sigh* I don't know. What do you call a psychic scarab?
A for-chitin teller!
Really. Disrupting my peace and quiet for that?
Well, I thought it was shell-arious.

o: The scarab goes back to ignoring you.

pages.x: Tough crowd.

conversations.section: In the Grand Library of Menaphos / After Pharaoh's Folly

pages.x: Hi, can I help you?
What is this place?
Keep your voice down! This is a library!
*whispers* What is this place?
I just told you, it's a library. The greatest hub of literature and learning in the desert.
Now we have a Pharaoh who shows the proper respect for history, this venerable institution will soon return to its former glory - I'm sure of it.
Though my requests for extra funding haven't yet been answered. Something about the dread Devourer coming for our souls?
Anyway, I'm sure once that's all sorted, the great restocking can begin.
Suit yourself!
Suit yourself!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Praise Seren for sending you, human. You are the saviour of our city.
Can you tell me about yourself?
I am merely another traveller on the journey to enlightenment. It is a road few dare walk, but the light of Seren shall show us the way.
Who I am is not important. Nor indeed my origin. To focus on what we were inhibits our potential to become something more.
Can you tell me about Clan Hefin?
Where other clans build or fight or destroy, clan Hefin looks inward.
We contemplate the physical and spiritual world, and meditate upon the wisdom of Seren.
We strengthen our bodies and minds, that we may be enlightened by her grace and the beauty of her spirit.
Can you tell me about Clan Hefin's skills?
We seek to cleanse our minds in prayer, and hone our bodies through agility exercises.
We welcome all who crave enlightenment, and provide for their physical and spiritual needs.
Why not leap atop a serenity post, and meditate in unity upon the wisdom of Seren? I think you will find the experience quite edifying.

conversations.section: In Shilo Village

pages.x: 'Ello, and what are you after then?

o: Do you have anything for trade?
I am here to discuss any rewards I might be eligible for.

pages.x: Do you have anything for trade?
I have a wide selection of Slayer equipment; take a look!

o: How do I earn co-op points to spend on rewards?

pages.x: You'll gain co-op reward points if you complete at least half of your contribution to a task with a friend.
That means you need to be in a group for most of the time you're working on your task, but it doesn't matter if your friend beats you to the majority of kills!
You'll still have been in a group for most of your contribution, so you're still entitled to a co-op reward point.

o: Where can I use the co-op food and potion rewards?

pages.x: The rewards can be used in most of the areas we commonly send you to to complete your tasks.
Er...nothing...

conversations.section: Death / Talking to Sir Vant

pages.x: The town of Lumbridge, although quite small, is packed with things to do.
You can always refer to your Quest Journal if you aren't sure what to do next or are stuck on a task.
Now, then. If you should be unfortunate enough to die on your adventures, you will return to Lumbridge Castle and your health will be restored.
I'm sure that won't happen, though.
Do I lose anything?
Normally, you will keep your three most valuable items. The less valuable items will fall on the floor, protected by a gravestone so nobody else can pick them up.
If you can return in time, you may be able to pick these
items up.
Oh yes, before you go. RuneScape is a curious place, as it seems to love interrupting and surprising you.
You might find that you are cutting a tree, only for it to wake up and stop you! Keep your wits about you
and you should be fine.
Really? That sounds pretty scary.
There's no need to worry. This kind of thing only happens occasionally and they can often lead to a reward.

conversations.section: Outside a heist entrance / Afterwards

pages.x: Hi, Liara. So, how can I assist?
What are heists exactly?
On the surface, very simply just a specific target ripe for burglary. I make sure to only target joints that are either long-abandoned or inhabited by the unscrupulous.
That way, you aren't hurting anyone that doesn't deserve a bad day?
Precisely, the has a code of honour to uphold!
Then, I nick anything of value not bolted down - plus a couple of things that are - using every technique in the book!
So, like pickpocketing, picking locks, coshing, safecracking and the like?
Exactly! But try not the get caught, else you'll lose out on some of the loot you've *ahem* appropriated so far.
Then, when I make my escape, I fence the loot in order to help fund the Guild's altruistic activities.
They're a tour de force of triumphant thievery, a rush of relishable robbery, a smorgasbord of satisfy-.
Stealing is fun!
It certainly has its merits. Though, remember the golden rule: only ever from people that deserve it!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: What's that ladder next to the altar for?
An...archaeological dig. Yeah, a dig.
Why?
Next to a Chaos Altar? That's a bit odd. Can I go down and have a look?
Well...I suppose. See, we found this ancient altar, but it was pretty broken so the Z.M.I. sent some of its researchers to try and repair it.
How'd that work out for them?
Pretty well - only one died. Still, They got it working...sort of. This ancient technology can be tricky.
What do you mean, 'sort of'? Altars either work or don't work.
This one works, just not as you'd expect. You put pure essence in, but get random runes back. Some of them we don't even know how to craft!
Sounds like a pretty good deal. Can I give it a go?
I don't think so. The mages don't like outsiders going in; they'll probably attack you.
They only patrol the short path, though, so if you used the long path, through a tunnel near the entrance, you'd probably be safe.
Thanks.

conversations.section: Entering the dungeon for the first time

pages.x: Halt there! Ahead of here lies only death.
What's in there?
Unnatural creatures. There is a power in there that chills me just thinking about it.
Just stood here, I can feel it creeping over me; it makes me just want to up and abandon my post and run back to my family.
It can't be that bad. Can I just take a look?
Hmm, yes, you do look like you can handle yourself, but you can't go in there just yet.
These creatures do not fall as normal beasts do, they exist on the boundary of life and death. So the priests say, anyway.
There is an item, though - the feather of Ma'at. They may look like normal feathers, but they contain some magic...or perhaps a curse, I do not truly know.
With a feather upon you, these creatures will fall to your blows.
Where can I get these feathers?
There are two places. The first is from me - you didn't think they would leave me to guard without them, did you? I can sell them to you, of course, for a cost.
However, if you would like to collect them yourself, I hear that the workers have been recovering them from the tombs below Menaphos.
If you were able to gain access to Menaphos and its tombs, then I'm sure you will be able to find some down there.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Do you want to buy a lamp, surface-dweller?

o: Can you fill a lamp with oil, please?
How do the lamps around the city work?

pages.x: Yes please.
No thanks.
Suit yourself.
Can you fill a lamp with oil, please?
You can do that yourself! Just put some swamp tar in the lamp oil still here and then use the lamp on the still.
How do the lamps around the city work?
They work by our very own Dorgeshuun magic!
Sometimes they don't work very well, though. The light orbs blow and they have to be replaced.
If you ever see a lamp that's gone out, you can fix it by replacing the light orb.
You can make new light orbs out of glass, and use a piece of wire on them to add the filament.
There's a machine in the south of the city that makes the wire you need.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello there!
You seem rather cheerful. Is there anything you're after?

o: What can you tell me about Al Kharid?
So, what do you do here?

pages.x: What can you tell me about Al Kharid?
Well, it's hot and full of sand.
Anything else?
Don't ask me, I'm not from around here.
So where are you from?
A town to the south of the Shantay Pass, called Pollnivneach.
So, what do you do here?
Not very much, at the moment. I came from further south to set up a smithy here...
...but we still haven't set up the shops, so we have no customers yet.

conversations.section: After The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Shhh! I'm waiting for the show!
What's on the bill?
There's a performance of an epic from olden times tonight! The epic of Bukalla!
Bukalla?
He was a famed slayer of daggermouths in olden times. It's a very inspirational song.

o: Sounds interesting! Maybe I'll stick around.

pages.x: Sounds boring.
Well, you're missing out on a glorious piece of history.

conversations.section: Bringing him a cup of tea for the first time

pages.x: Ah, you read my mind - I could murder a good cuppa right now. If I can have that cup of tea, I'd give you permission to pan here. What do you say?

o: Give the panning guide a cuppa?

pages.x: Ah! Lovely! You can't beat a good cuppa! You're free to pan all you want.
Hello, who are you?
Hello, I am the panning guide. I teach students how to pan in these waters.
They're not permitted to do so until after they've had training and, of course, they must be invited to pan here too.
So, how do I become invited?
I'm not supposed to let people pan here unless they have permission. Mind you, I could let you have a go if you're willing to do me a favour...
What's that?
Well, to be honest, what I would really like is a nice cup of tea!
I've some here that you can have.
Ah! Lovely! You can't beat a good cuppa! You're free to pan all you want.

conversations.section: Talk to / Whale's Maw

pages.x: Calm down, Steven. You're not having any fish, you get fed too much as it is.
And I do wish you'd stop 'dropping feathers' down the back of my coat.
Wow, your seagull actually drops feathers?
Er, no. It's a euphemism.
They ain't feathers.
It's poop.
Yes, I got that, thank you.

conversations.section: West of Lumbridge Castle

pages.x: Glory to Saradomin, the rightful victor of the Battle of Lumbridge!

o: What is that armour you're wearing?

pages.x: You don't know?
The Battle of Lumbridge was an epic battle fought between the noble god Saradomin and the wicked pretender god Zamorak.
Zamorak came through a portal in Lumbridge and immediately began destroying everything around him.
But then, the mighty Saradomin appeared and intervened, protecting us all.
Locked in a stalemate, each summoned their mighty armies and waged war across Lumbridge.
They were locked in vicious battle for ten weeks, before Saradomin finally emerged victorious, leaving Zamorak broken and defeated.
This armour? Why it is the armour of the dedicated warriors of Saradomin.
Brave followers of Saradomin were given this armour when they had earned enough recognition with his army.
During the battle you could have claimed this from the quartermaster, if you fought for Saradomin.
Other than that, it is only borne by from devout Saradominst warriors in the God Wars dungeon.
The vile Zamorakian forces have similar - though far more sinister - armour that can be taken from Zamorakian warriors in the God Wars Dungeon.

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Do you want to go on a trip to Karamja?
The trip will cost you 30 coins.

o: (With a ring of charos (a) equipped:) Or I could pay you nothing at all...

pages.x: Yes please.

o: (If you have completed the Karamja easy tasks:)

pages.x: Wait a minute, didn't you earn Karamja gloves? Thought I'd seen you helping around the island. You can go on half price - 15 coins.
Or I could pay you nothing at all...
Mmmm, nothing at all, you say...
Yes, why not - jump aboard then.
No, thank you.

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Do you want to go on a trip to Karamja?
The trip will cost you 30 coins.

o: (With a ring of charos (a) equipped:) Or I could pay you nothing at all...

pages.x: Yes please.

o: (If you have completed the Karamja easy tasks:)

pages.x: Wait a minute, didn't you earn Karamja gloves? Thought I'd seen you helping around the island. You can go on half price - 15 coins.
Or I could pay you nothing at all...
Mmmm, nothing at all, you say...
Yes, why not - jump aboard then.
No, thank you.

conversations.section: Talk to / After Visions of Havenhythe

pages.x: It's an honour to have you visit our shrine again, blessed of The Great Wolf.
Is there anything I can help you with?
I was hoping you could tell me more about Inanna.
Of course!
Inanna is benevolent, nurturing and patient. Stepping in to protect her children when the need arises while providing them the distance to thrive independently of her.
She provided guidance to our ancestors when they first arrived here. Every Wendlewicker and their family has a unique history with and connection to her.
Even my brother and I have differing philosophies, despite both tending her shrine.
What are your beliefs?
Inanna is more than a mere messenger of the gods. She is a deity in and of herself.
She is the one who lives among our people and safeguards our lands, while asking nothing of us in return.
The other gods crave worship, while The Great Wolf is selfless and humble. That is why she and she alone deserves my reverence.
I understand. Thank you for sharing that with me.
You are very welcome. May Inanna watch over you, my friend.

conversations.section: In Al Kharid

pages.x: Do you want to buy any fine silks?
How much are they?
3gp.

o: No, that's too much for me.

pages.x: No, that's too much for me.
2gp and that's as low as I'll go. I'm not selling it for any less. You'll only go and sell it in Varrock for a profit.

o: No, really, I don't want it.

pages.x: 2gp sounds good.
No, really, I don't want it.
Okay, but that's the best price you're going to get.
Okay, that sounds good.
No, silk doesn't suit me.

conversations.section: When talked to / After obtaining the task list

pages.x: Hello, have you come to help?
Maybe? What do you need?
Great, I could do with some help with a few jobs I've been given.
How many are there?
There are eight tasks, and if you help me with those, I'll find a special reward for you.
What do I need to do?
Well I was trying to make some special flour in the nearby windmill for RuneFest but the controls seemed to have got jammed?
Want me to take a look?
That'd be great. Perhaps some combination with the levers might do the trick.
Try moving them up and down a couple of times, then left and right a couple of times.
Is that it?
It might be, who can say. Let me know what happens.

conversations.section: Dialogue / First conversation

pages.x: Ha! Looks like some 'Skulls' still live in this fort.
No need to make a joke of it, buddy - that's just mean. We're people too ya know!
Argh! Oh no, wait, I'm not shocked any more.
Wow, I can't even creep people out these days. Thanks a lot, that's all I had going for me.
Fine, what's your story then?
Me, I was so proud - I'd only just passed the gang's initiation! I was gonna be a pirate like my dad before me, and my dad's dad too.
But then SHE came along and ruined it. I wasn't even born when whatever happened to her, er, happened to her. It ain't my fault!
Who was 'she'?
That's just it - I had no idea? Never seen her before. Says she was the khan of Goshima's lieutenant.
Says she'd earned her freedom and came back here to exact revenge on us Skulls.
I'd done nothing, buddy, like I said. Told her that too, but she didn't care, then 'zap'!, she turns me into this.
That's just, like, really unfair, ain't it? I didn't even get a chance to kidnap and ransom people. Not cool.
I'm too depressed to talk about it.

conversations.section: In Al Kharid

pages.x: Who are you and what do you want?

o: Can I have some sq'irks please?

pages.x: None of your business! I go where I like and do what I like.
Not in my house. Be gone!
I'm here to kill you!
I think not!
Can I have some sq'irks please?
What do you want them for?
Someone asked me to bring them some.
Who?
You find yourself compelled to answer truthfully: Osman.
In that case I'm sorry, you can't. I have had a falling out with him recently and would rather not oblige him.
I'm just passing by.

conversations.section: Talk-to / On the first time during the fourth task

pages.x: Bee, over here!
Bzzzz?

o: : Aw, look at your big old face!

pages.x: Stop it, tell it what you think!

o: : You've always been my least favourite!

pages.x: Nice!
Bzzzzz?

o: : You sound like a yak when you sleep!

pages.x: Boom!
Bzzzz.

o: : You don't even know the difference between nectar and pollen.

pages.x: Bz...
Nice one!

conversations.section: At Musa Point / Talking to him / Normally

pages.x: Ay-uh, 'tis a grand day for the fishin'. Will ye be wantin' to exchange yer fish for banknotes?

o: Okay, exchange all my fish for banknotes.
Who are you and why are you here?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Ahhh, when I were a young'un my name were Nigel but, these days, folks mostly call me Stiles.
Long time ago, in Draynor Village, there were three brothers who'd exchange yer stuff for bitty bits o' paper, like these new-fangled banknotes we've got today.
Niles, Miles an' Giles they called themselves.
They be long gone, like the golden days, but they were an inspiration to me, so I took this trade myself, an' I changed my name to Stiles.
But why are you here, in this place?
The smell of yon bananas were drivin' me scatty, so I can't go too near the fishing spots.
A tough-lookin' geezer callin' himself a slayer master tried to give me a nosepeg once, but I bain't wearin' one o' them things. Ol' Stiles has a tender nose.
So, would ye like me to exchange yer fish now?
Which fish can you exchange?
Ahhh, ol' Stiles has banknotes for yer lobbies, yer swordies and yer tuna. 'Tis a grand service I be offerin' here, and nary a penny do I ask in return.
No thanks.

conversations.section: After partial completion of The Feud / First-time dialogue

pages.x: Hey there!
Did you see the way I distracted that guy? Man I'm one smooth operator!
Ya you were good alright.
So where's my money?
Don't play stupid with me, I'm better at it. Where's my money?
Oh that money! I don't think you deserve it!
Liar, thief!
How observant of you!
Give me my money!
Make me!
You'll be sorry!
Here you go, thanks.

conversations.section: After The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Shhh! I'm waiting for the show!
What's on the bill?
There's a performance of an epic from olden times tonight! The epic of Bukalla!
Bukalla?
He was a famed slayer of daggermouths in olden times. It's a very inspirational song.

o: Sounds interesting! Maybe I'll stick around.

pages.x: Sounds boring.
Well, you're missing out on a glorious piece of history.

conversations.section: On Daemonheim Peninsula / Using Thok on Wood on him

pages.x: What you want with Thok?
I found this book of yours by rummaging in Balthazar's Raffle, it was at the bottom of a barrel!
Book did not sell as well as Thok want. Showing book off to people, I punch everyone who say book was stupid.
Then weaklings who chop tree with axe start to hate Thok too. They say I take all trees so they have nothing to cut. So I punch them too.
After Thok punch weaklings, green people who hug trees say Thok not think about trees feelings.
They say Thok no care if a tree not want to become place where beer goes, I punch them as well.
Thok not stupid, Thok king of make stuff with trees!
How do you make furniture? I don't see a workbench around here and I'd be very surprised if the Housing Agency allowed you to own a house.
Thok pick up tree and smash tree over knee until Thok is happy.
I'm not sure how that works.
Thok think of what to make and smash on knee until it is made. It not hard, just need to find tree. Here Thok show-
No no no Thok, that isn't necessary. Thank you for whatever that conversation was.
Thok happy to see book again, Thok no punch you this time.

conversations.section: In Tai Bwo Wannai / After Tai Bwo Wannai Trio

pages.x: Ah, [Adventurer/Explorer/Wayfarer/Nobody], welcome back to Tai Bwo Wannai.

o: Is there anything interesting to do here?
I've been doing some work around the village.

pages.x: What do you do here?
It should be clear to anyone that I am the chief of Tai Bwo Wannai. I ensure that things run smoothly in this village.

o: Is there anything interesting to do here?
I've been doing some work around the village.

pages.x: Ok, thanks.
Is there anything interesting to do here?
Yes Bwana, plenty of interesting things to do. Firstly you could make an effort to tidy the place up a little.
Equip yourself with a machete and start cutting down the jungle that seems to be growing all around here.
Go and have a chat with Murcaily for information, he's tending the hardwood grove to the east of here.
I've been doing some work around the village.
That's good Bwana, I would hate to think that you were just being lazy while you're in my kingdom!
I'm just passing through.

conversations.section: At the Herblore Habitat / Asking "What tools can you store?"

pages.x: Ah, 'tis a foine day, to be sure! Can I help ye with tool storage, or a trip to Winkin's Farm, or what?
What can you store?
We'll hold onto yer rake, seed dibber, spade, secateurs, waterin' can and trowel - but mind it's not one of them fancy trowels only archaeologists use.
We'll take a few buckets an' scarecrows off yer hands too, and even yer compost and supercompost. There's room in our shed for plenty of compost, so bring it on.
Also, if ye hands us yer Farming produce, we might be able to change it into banknotes.
We can also store some of the potions that help keep this 'ere habitat running smoothly. Only 3-dose potions, mind: we're not going to look after your empties.
So, do ye want to be using the store?

o: What do you do with the tools you're storing?
No thanks, I'll keep hold of my stuff.

pages.x: Yes, please.
What would you like to store?

conversations.section: Talk-to / With a keg of mead before making a delivery to The Pick and Lute during The Need for Mead event

pages.x: Welcome to the Pick and Lute! How can I help you?
I've come from the brewer, Leslie. They were wondering if you could try their latest batch of mead?
Leslie, you say? Not heard from them in a while.
Still meddling with all things bee, are they?
They sure are. I'm sure their mead is delicious too.
Well, I can see the seal on the keg isn't broken, so hand it over.
Oh nice. Yes, that's great. Could use some improvements in the overall flavour though.
How much water was added during the brewing stage?
No idea...
Well, pass this on to Leslie. There's too much water and it's diluting the flavour.
The biggest problem here though is the intensity. I think Leslie needs to change up the food they feed to their bees.
Richer food will bring out richer flavours.
I'll pass that on.

conversations.section: Talk to / If the player isn't a Player Moderator / In Draynor Village, before Vampyre Slayer

pages.x: BEWARE THE VAMPYRE, EVERYONE IN BY NIGHTFALL...
Oh, sorry for shouting right at you.
Hello citizen. What can I do for you?
What did you mean about 'Beware the vampyre'?
Our village is plagued by a vampyre that lives in the manor to the north. One of the citizens - Morgan I think - is trying to find a vampyre slayer to rid us of him.
Hmm, maybe I should speak to him.
You could go there yourself and see! It's not far to the east of here. If you look to the north you can see where Saradomin stood, fighting the demons of Zamorak.
And to the south, you can see where Zamorak stood, summoning great spells to attack the Saradominist forces!
It was a titanic battle, swinging one way and then another as they struggled for supremacy.
But, after months of fighting, Saradomin gained the upper hand, and crushed the forces of Zamorak.
Saradomin was ready to strike the final blow, but Zamorak escaped with the help of his remaining forces.
Saradomin left at that point, ready to regroup to prove his supremacy amongst the gods.

conversations.section: In Edgeville / Claiming the varrock hard task set for the first time

pages.x: I've completed all the Hard Tasks in the Varrock set and, let me tell you, it wasn't an easy job.
I can imagine! I expect you'll be wanting a reward for your hard efforts, eh?
Yes, please.
I'm happy to say that you've done well, so I will reward you suitably for your work.
Great! Thanks.
I have upgraded your Varrock armour so you now have a chance to double your bars when smelting, ores when mining and progress when smithing rune, orikalkum and necronium.
I have watched your progress with interest and have sent word to the Cooking Guild, west of Varrock.
They have a prestigious bank there which you will be allowed entrance to, as of now, if you are wearing your Varrock armour.
I can also change your Varrock Teleport spell so that it takes you to the Grand Exchange, if you'd find that more convenient.
Well done on completing all of the tasks set before you, Player.
This magic lamp should help you with your skills. I trust you already know what should be done with it.
Wow, thanks!
Now, if you should happen to lose that armour, you may come back to me to reclaim it.

conversations.section: After Missing, Presumed Death

pages.x: I'd like to ask about what happened at the Empyrean Citadel.
Do you still see Sliske as a Zarosian?
I do not. That snake has betrayed us for the last time. After murdering Guthix I was disappointed in him, but now I have lost all hope.
It has always been his way to act alone; spending his days in isolation, always plotting and scheming. But now I fear he has lost his mind.
His actions do seem to indirectly benefit Zaros, but if he really is loyal he will have some serious explaining to do.
Are you in contact with Zaros?
Unfortunately my lord has not seen fit to contact me, no. He keeps his communication to an absolute minimum, choosing only to liaise with Azzanadra.
I do not take it personally though. He must keep his communication routes hidden, and his plans even more so.
I can feel him watching, adventurer. It will not be long before he makes his return.
Will you try and obtain the Stone of Jas?
I have no interest in the power the Stone of Jas provides. I leave the hunger for ascension to the Zamorakians. So blinded by their own selfish needs...
If Zaros expresses a need for the stone, I will of course commit my focus to obtaining it. Perhaps it will factor into my plans.
For now though I prepare for the Empty Lord's return. He still has many followers who will rally to his side.

conversations.section: After The World Wakes

pages.x: I'd like to talk about Guthix's death.
What happened with Sliske?
Well, he has always been...different. He is slippery; always lurking in the shadows.
You can never quite be sure what he is intending, but you can always guarantee his actions will either benefit himself or Zaros.
While he betrayed us, he was still working for Zaros. Just in the way he thought best. And of course, in the way he felt was the most entertaining.
In any case, it is still a good outcome. If not what we had planned.
What do you envisage for the future?
Zaros' return, of course! With the edicts gone, we can set so much in motion!
So what's stopping Zaros coming back straight away?
Zaros is intelligent. It is wise to first devise a plan, observe any enemies, calculate the risks...
What do you think of Saradomin's return?
What a display that was. Typically Saradomin; always trying to make an impression, show everyone what he can do. He flaunts his power and leaves himself open.
Wiser gods keep their cards close to their chest; a hidden strength can take an opponent by surprise. That is why Zaros will have the upper hand.

conversations.section: First time informing about Jhallan / Unknown conditional

pages.x: So this is your place?
Humble but homely, I think. It suits me well. How good to see you again!
You told me how to thaw out the Muspah. I thought I should keep my part of the bargain.
Oh! So you have some information for me? I must record this!
To start with, the Muspah wasn't what it appeared to be.
It turned out to be alive all along, and once I'd freed it, it... changed.
It told me it was a Mahjarrat. It was quite a shock to suddenly see its head was a skull.
The Muspah creature was a Mahjarrat in disguise?
Yes, he's called Jhallan. He was incredibly weak and wanted to hibernate under the Mahjarrat ritual site.
I found him somewhere peaceful and put him back to sleep. Apparently the ritual will rejuvenate any Mahjarrat nearby.
We know where to find him again, should we ever need to.
Well, that creature in the ice has given me much to think about.
I've started to research these Mahjarrat; I'm worried they may be a threat to us humans. We need to collaborate to gather as much information as possible.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / After reaching Woodcutting level 99

pages.x: Wow! It's not often I meet somebody as accomplished as you in Woodcutting! Seeing as you're so skilled, maybe you are interested in buying a Skillcape of Woodcutting?

o: I've noticed there are a couple of versions of each skillcape.
Can you help me with the sentinel outfits?

pages.x: No, thanks.
Okay. Come back to me if you change your mind.

o: I think I have the money right here, actually.
I've mastered this skill. Is there anything else?

pages.x: I know where to find you if I change my mind.
Excellent! Wear that cape with pride my friend.
There is something...though I have kept it a secret for a very long time. It is something that can only be worn by a true master.
Not even I can wear it - that's how hard it is to achieve.
You say you're a master. Stand straight, let me take a look at you...
You...really have mastered it. What an honour! It would be my pleasure to sell you a Woodcutting master cape.

pages.i: Buy Woodcutting master cape for 120,000 coins?

pages.x: Yes! We, the skill masters, have crafted new versions of all skillcapes! We felt like it was time for a change.

conversations.section: In City of Um / Talk to her

pages.x: No.
No what?
No to whatever it is you were thinking of asking me.
But...
Look, I'm dead, I'm tired, I'm burnt out, and I'm overused. I need a break.
Even becoming an site manager might have been a stretch too far.
Can't help, won't help. Sorry.
Wait, not even helping me to take out Rasial, the evil necromancer?
Not even.
I'm just playing darts and having a drink.
So, please...just let me rest in peace.
Bu-
In peace.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Greetings traveller.

o: Can you heal me? I'm injured.
Isn't this place built a bit out the way?
How do I get further into the Monastery?

pages.x: Can you heal me? I'm injured.
Ok.

o: Abbot Langley places his hands on your head. You feel a little better.

pages.x: Isn't this place built a bit out the way?
We like it that way actually! We get disturbed less. We still get rather a large amount of travellers looking for sanctuary and healing here as it is!
How do I get further into the Monastery?
I'm sorry but only members of our order are allowed in the second level of the monastery.

o: Well can I join your order?

pages.x: Well can I join your order?
Oh, sorry.

conversations.section: Burthorpe / Talking to Turael / Before cooking meat or fish

pages.x: Do you want to cook meat or fish?

o: I want to fish and cook crayfish on a fire.
I want to cook rabbit on a range.

pages.x: The nearest fishing spot in Burthorpe is to the south of us. Go cook yourself some fish to eat in combat!
Remember, you're less likely to burn food cooking on a range. You can use the range in my house to the south-east.
Mountain trolls are hard as rocks, and half as smart. They're always hungry, but trolls just don't seem to understand we don't like being eaten.
Trolls even name themselves after the first thing they eat - or the noise we make when they eat us.
Trolls will eat literally anything, but people taste much better than rocks. And the mountains are mostly rocks.
So when the trolls raid Burthorpe, the imperial guard make sure it's the trolls' last meal, or die trying.
Why didn't the trolls eat the 'last action hero' over there? Did he taste as bad as he smells?
Ah, yes. The chosen one, of many. I pulled him out of the cave as an example for the next adventurer that came along. How's that working out for you?
I'm not dead yet.
Keep it up. You may even make a habit of it.

conversations.section: In Draynor Village / Using 50 Shades of Dye on her

pages.x: Someone bought my book! Have you checked out dye number 42? It's my favourite!
I haven't had a chance yet, I'm sorry.
That's OK, every dye I've ever made is in that book. There really is quite the mixture.
So you can make every dye? That is fascinating.
It's no trouble really. You'd be surprised at what you can whip up with a little woad leaf and some redberries.
I'm fairly certain that I could make any type of dye with a blindfold on! Comes in handy when I'm chopping the onion for a dye.
Are there any new dyes that you can make for me from your book?
I'm afraid not. As part of the book contract, I wasn't allowed to make any more of the dyes from my own book.
It's a shame really. I was doing a bit of redecorating and wanted to recolour my grain storage to a nice shade of red.
So that would then be a red room of grain?
Precisely.
I'll, uh, leave you to it.

conversations.section: After constructing the tier 1 Town Hall / First time

pages.x: Excellent! We did it! The first signs of civilisation on this forsaken place.
The Town Hall is just one of the many buildings you can help build.
I'm sure there are several people, yourself included, that could do with a safe haven building for them on the island.
As you do so, each building will grant you various benefits to make life here a bit easier here on the island.
Come visit me if you want to view the perks for constructing and upgrading each building.
We're also going to need more space for workers and resources in the future so we should ensure we're building Sleeping Quarters and a Storehouse when we have the chance.
Doing so will help us gather resources quicker and build more of the base camp.
Before you go, one of the workers found this: some compacted resources. If you return them to me I can add them to our stocks. Let's take a look to see what it gives us.
I better head up to the Town Hall now and prepare for Mr. Mordaut's arrival.
Wait... what should I do?
You're an adventurer, aren't you? How about you explore the island and see what you can discover?
You could also talk to the others here in the base camp to see what else you can learn.

conversations.section: After Violet is Blue, in Yeti Town

pages.x: I'm bored!
Why don't you go have some fun?
NO! Tell my parents to take me home!
I don't think you'd want that. This is a time to be with your family and friends. Go on, have some fun, you won't regret it.
I regret talking to you.
Listen here. Your parents went through a lot of effort to get you here. The least you could do is try to look like you're having fun!
I don't want to!
Ooh look at me! I'm the yeti that's too cool for the festival! I'm so awesome and cool and everyone else sucks.
...why are you being so mean? You...you bully! Mummy! They're picking on me!
I'm not sure that was my best moment...
I didn't like you anyway!

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Children can't sleep / Task #2

pages.x: Ever since she was a little baby, she has been unable to sleep without [item].
Right. Why [item]?
Yes, I know it's a bit strange, but [item] were the only thing that would help her drift off.
So, please, if you could get [number] [item] I would greatly appreciate it.
That will suffice.
Do you know where I could get [item]?

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.
Nevermind.
Nevermind.

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Collector of curiosities / Task #3

pages.x: Could you perhaps do one more tiny job for me?
Does it involve [item 1] or [item 2]?
No, of course not!
Really?
Yes I promise, I need [number] more [item] for my final collection!
This is the last time I ask. I promise.
[number] [item]?
You're a good person.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue after Swan Song

pages.x: Ah, you come back! What you want from Arnold, heh?

o: Can you open my bank account, please?
I'd like to check my Bank PIN settings.
I'd like to see my Collection box.
Nothing, I just came to chat.
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Would you like to trade?
Ja, I have wide range of stock...
Nothing, I just came to chat.
Ah, that is nice - always I like to chat, but Herr Caranos tell me to get back to work! Here, you been nice, so have a present:
A cabbage?
Ja, cabbage is good for you!
Um... thanks!

conversations.section: Departure / Ready to leave Ashdale

pages.x: This boat will take us to the mainland. Just use the gangplank to climb aboard.

o: There's something I'd like to ask first.

pages.x: Just climb aboard the boat. I'll be right behind you.
Alright, [laddie/lassie] – fire away.

o: Can you tell me more about Morwenna the Cruel?
How did you lose your arm?

pages.x: Just climb aboard the boat. I'll be right behind you.
She was an evil necromancer who terrorized Gielinor during the Fourth Age. She died hundreds of years ago ... but someone must have brought her back.
As for why she came here, I think it might have something to with the fact that I, sort of ... plundered her tomb, back in my adventuring days.
Hey, don't look at me like that! How was I to know she'd come back from the dead?
It happened year ago. I was exploring the Kharidian Desert and accidentally disturbed a kalphite hive. Vicious wee blighters, those kalphites.
They swarmed me, and – well, you can see the result for yourself. It makes opening jars a challenge, I can tell you that.
We defeated Morwenna the Cruel and equipped you for the journey ahead. All that's left to do is board the boat for the mainland.

conversations.section: Saying goodbyes / Talking to Sarah

pages.x: Looks like you saved the day.
Thanks, rhubarb face.
Thanks apple face.
Thanks, monkey features.
Hah, good one. So what's next for the hero of Ashdale?
I'm going to the mainland.
Oh, so you're leaving us? What a relief. Ah, you know I'm only joking. Truth is, I'll miss you. It won't be the same without you around.
What about you?
Some people are born for greatness, pumpkin head. The rest of us have to play the hand we're dealt. For you, the future lies over the sea, far from Ashdale.
But I'll always be here if you want to come and visit.
Goodbye.
Bye for now.

conversations.section: Rellekka / Talk-to / After The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Hello again Askeladden.
Hey buddy! That ain't my name no more! My new Fremennik name is Larravak! What's yours?
My Fremennik name is [Fremennik name].
Ha! Ain't as good as my name buddy! So what can I do ya for?

o: Ask for a new pet rock

pages.x: Yeah, sad that. I heard he's dead. Sounded like a good guy.
One day I'll be a hero just like him!
So, Askeladd- sorry, Larravak; What is there to do around here now that we are both Fremenniks?
I guess you could do a bit of shopping. We got fresh fish at the docks, and some armour and weapons at Skulgrimen's place.
Okay, thanks.
Can I have another pet rock? I lost mine...
Sure thing buddy! I'd say take better care of this one, but it's just a rock! I have hundreds of them! Go wild!

conversations.section: At the Clan Camp / Normally / If the player is in a clan without a citadel

pages.x: You! Yes, you! Do you have a clan? Are you a high-ranking member? Can you procure followers for me?

pages.x: Hi, Player. What can I do for you today?

pages.x: So, how's business?

If you have the skill to care for it, you can catch a baby platypus and raise it as a pet.
They need special care, so you can't have more than one at a time, and you can't catch one if you are unable to care for it.
If you do manage to catch one, try feeding it raw fish. They seem to love that.
Thanks for the info!

conversations.section: At the Power Station, after Perils of Ice Mountain

pages.x: Hello again!

o: I still don't understand why Ice Mountain was heating up.

pages.x: I still don't understand why Ice Mountain was heating up.
No, I suppose I never did get a chance to explain it. It's something I learned from the druids of Guthix. It's about the balance of the atmosphere.
Sunlight causes the world to heat up but, normally, excess heat radiates upwards into the sky and away from RuneScape. So, the land remains at a constant temperature.
Different gases trap heat more or less well. The smoke from the dragon power station trapped heat very well, more so than normal air.
You've had a taste of what would happen if the gases increased. Plants would die - except it wouldn't just be Monastery roses, it would be crops people needed to eat.
Creatures would lose their habitat and go extinct - not just vulnerable icefiends, but all sorts of creatures.
Heat would make water expand and ice melt, so sea levels would rise, and that would mean coastal cities flooding, as well as drowning underground cities like Keldagrim.
If it were to go unchecked, it would mean the end of dwarven civilisation. Human civilisation too. Thank Saradomin you stopped it in time.
How is the windmill doing?
Quite well, actually. It looks like my estimates were all correct and the wind here is quite enough to power Nurmof's machine.

conversations.section: Dialogue / Before One Small Favour

pages.x: Hello! Don't get in the way around here, we've got a lot of work to do!

o: Hello there, what are you working on?
Is there anything I can do?

pages.x: Hello there, what are you working on?
Well, it's quite exciting...we're extending the glider network to include the Feldip Hills so that people can come and look at these curious ogres.
They are impressive creatures aren't they... quite mystified they are by the technology we gnomes have invented.

Well, people will be able to visit this area once construction has finished by using the most advanced network of glider routes in the whole of Gielinor... in fact...
the only network of glider routes!

Ok, thanks.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Ah, human! Welcome to Mazcab, our home.
Hello... Erm, how do you know I'm a human?
We watched you battle the great beast Tuska through the world window. We've been eagerly awaiting your arrival on our planet!
Now you're finally here, we were hoping you'd be able to lend us your aid.

o: What do you need help with?
What is there to do here?

pages.x: The airut have invaded our planet and enslaved our people. We aren't strong enough to fight back on our own.
If you're willing to help you'll find plenty of goebies around here that are in need of aid.
I'm glad you ask! There are plenty of places for you to explore. Village Kanatah is to the east and Otot is in the northwest.
You'll need to go through Nemi forest to reach it.
Directly to the north is where most of the airut have settled around our sacred temple.
If you want to gather a group and fight the most powerful of them, that is where you should go.

conversations.section: Anachronia / Talking to before starting mining / First time

pages.x: What are you doing over here?
Hello! I'm thinking about making a small garden here.
This rock catches all the light from the sky! If we can say goodbye to the big rock, the ground here will make the perfect planting patch!
What do you want to plant?
Cactus!
What a surprise!
It has to be where the rock is?
Yes.
Obviously.
I see. I could mine through that thing for you.
Can you bring me some magic logs? I'll start making a patch perimeter and you can smash the rock!

Yes. Hence the word 'thermal' as a descriptor. How terribly observant of you.
Heat come up from belly of de ground, make you feel lots better when you swim in it.
What do you mean?
Oh, it simple! You feel poisoned, you feel diseased or you just take beating in battle, just take bath in de hot water and you feel all better in no time.
It easy to notice effect if you just try it out - but maybe you human types not smart enough to notice things much.

What we saw on the way here... they were anything BUT fossils!

pages.x: You're right; there is more to this island than meets the eye.

Focus on your mission and everything will be okay.
I really hope you know what you're talking about.

I want to ask about something else.

o: I want to ask about something else.

pages.x: Goodbye.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge / Historical dialogue / After the Lumbridge Rebuildathon

pages.x: Good day to you! Welcome to my fishing shop. Between the Battle of Lumbridge and the rebuildathon, my shop has endured through interesting times.

o: Can I see your fishing supplies?

pages.x: It got turfed out by Saradomin of all the things, but looking at it now, you wouldn't be able to tell!
Foreman George and his men have done a sterling job and rebuilt it from scratch.
Anyhow, back to business!
My fishing shop used to be located over where the god Saradomin set up his camp for a battle to defend Lumbridge from Zamorak.
I was minding my shop as usual - selling bait and buying fish, nothing special - and there was this almighty noise, and the ground began to shake.
I ran outside just in time to see poor Explorer Jack run out of his house too, and it practically caved in behind him!
'Course, the old fellow was a bit shocked, to say the least! Fair shook up he was. I helped him up as best I could with the ground moving like it was.
It was chaos! Soldiers running everywhere, as even the castle walls fell!
My house fell down while I was helping Jack back to his feet. Had I not helped, I'd have been caught inside, and I wouldn't have fancied my chances!
Anyway, I shan't speak ill of Saradomin, after he crushed Zamorak like that. It all turned out alright in the end.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge / Historical dialogue / During Stage 1 and 2 of the Lumbridge Rebuildathon

pages.x: Look at those guys work! They'll have my shop fixed before I know it!

o: Have you got any supplies left?

pages.x: It got turfed out by Saradomin of all the things!
Since the war it's been a ruin, but Foreman George's men are doing good out there, rebuilding it from scratch!
It's shaping up really well, too! I could watch these guys work all day.
But back to business! I still have a few fishing supplies, if you're interested.
Yes, it was during the battle of Lumbridge. Saradomin decided that my shop was in the way of his camp.
Since then, I've been out here in the street, trying to peddle what's left of my wares.
I should probably not speak ill of Saradomin now, after he crushed Zamorak like that.

o: What exactly happened to your shop?
Can I see what you have?

pages.x: Yes, I salvaged some supplies from the wreckage, so I can still buy and sell fishing supplies.

Can you give me any tips on fishing?
Do you have any fishing bait?

o: (If the player already has fishing bait in their inventory:)
(If the player dropped the fishing bait on the ground:)

pages.x: Don't you already have some? Try looking in your backpack.
Don't you already have some? Try looking on the floor.
Saradomin is one of the beings who first brought life into Gielinor.
Most of us who live in Ashdale have taken Saradomin as our patron. He stands for truth, justice, and - above all - order.
Saradomin watch over you, my friend.

I'll handle the minutiae of the site management and you can focus on uncovering ancient secrets from the Second Age.
This is the ancient city of Senntisten, the centre of power for the vast Zarosian Empire of the Second Age.
Right now it's a war zone. With the forces of the Elder Gods gathering against us, it's hard to perform the delicate work that an archaeological dig requires.
But there's still so much to discover here! We can try to understand what life was like for the citizens of the Empire.
We can perhaps learn about the rituals and trappings of the ancient Zarosian religion.
We might even uncover forgotten techniques and secrets to improve our daily lives.
The possibilities are endless.
See you around, boss.

Fair thee well.
Why do you have so much wool in your store? I haven't seen any sheep anywhere.

What do you trade for it?
Rope of course! What else can we sell? Fish would go off before it got so far south.
Where does all this rope go?
Err, I don't remember the name of the place very well. Dreinna? Drennor? Something like that.

conversations.section: Dialogue / In your POH

pages.x: Soft-thing! How dare you approach the queen of the kalphite?
I killed you, remember?
Yes you killed the queen, but by now another will have risen up! One kalphite may die but the hive goes on!
The kalphite race grows stronger everyday, and our young feed on the blood of the soft-things that invade from above!
Someday we will overrun the world again and all soft creatures will die.
But we will reserve the worst fate for those who have killed a queen and hung her head in their house.
We will lay eggs in your brain and you will not die until it explodes and a million kalphites emerge to make a grand hive of all the world!
You don't scare me!
Your pitiful misplaced confidence is irrelevant. You will all die!
Please don't kill me!
Ha ha ha! It is too late for pleading now, pathetic mammal! Your fate is sealed!

conversations.section: In Al Kharid / Talking to him

pages.x: Would you like to buy a nice kebab? Only one gold.

o: I think I'll give it a miss.
What do you think of Ali Morrisane?

pages.x: What do you think of Ali Morrisane?
I don't like him. He makes all these claims about being the best salesman in the world, and he even has some thugs that he's hired to threaten us.
One of them came round here and threatened to cut my head off if I didn't cooperate with them!
I've also heard some rumours about them from my friend Isma'il in Pollnivneach...
What sort of rumours?
Apparently he has men there as well, who have also been threatening people.
And it's said that they even intend to steal from the ruler of Al Kharid himself!
Really?
That's what I've heard. Anyway, are you sure you wouldn't like a kebab?

o: I think I'll give it a miss.

conversations.section: In Taverley / After Let Them Eat Pie

pages.x: I saw it. I saw all of it...
Saw what?
You don't know! You'll never know what I saw!
The colours...all the colours...and sometimes NONE of the colours...
The darkness came to me then...with the stench, it protected my mind.
But the darkness is still there. The smell...The smell of it will never, ever fade...
Well...isn't this a bit over the top from seeing Rolo get a little ill?
A little ill? A little ill?
The gods themselves wept tears of blood at the things he brought to light. Things that never should have been!
I...see. Well, I'll leave you to your mind babbling now. Have fun!
No! Don't leave me! It will come back for me!
Bye! Going away now! Have fun!

pages.x: The next supplies I require are a load of [item].
Right. Why [item]?
The thaumaturge tells us that we need [item]. We didn't think it wise to argue.
Right. If this... thaumaturge thinks that a [item] could help, then I guess we should search for [item].
I will make the preparations while you are away; is it a reasonable request?
My appreciation. I shall write another stanza depicting your kind deed...

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Maybe someone else will cast a rope into this gaping void...
Maybe someone else will cast a rope into this gaping void...
Maybe someone else will cast a rope into this gaping void...

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Crocodile Tears

pages.x: *braaak*
Met with Crondis, greedy Crondis.
Brought her a croc ice!
Brought her a croc ice!
Brought her a croc ice!
Brought her a croc ice!
Brought her a croc ice!
That joke got old quick! Bored now.
She spat something up! Disgusting, gross - kill it with fire!
I'm talking about you now.
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: Cavern of Tainted Memories / Talking to

pages.x: Hello there my darling! I seem to have uncovered a special cavern in my quest to further my divining knowledge!
What makes this cavern so special?
It appears to be home to a certain kind of rare wisp. They have been corrupted with the evil memories of the world.
However it isn't all doom and gloom. It turns out these wisps can be harvested for a type of essence that can be cleansed and forged into some rather lovely weaponry.
That sounds pretty awesome!
Quite. But I can't just be allowing this precious resource to be harvested unchecked. We don't know whether it is finite or not.
I will allove you a short period of time in there in each day. If you bring me a cavern entry token, I'll allow you in again!
If you don't want to receive Divination XP from the cavern, I could give you a bundle of other rewards instead.

o: Would you like to receive Divination XP or mystery rewards?

pages.x: Very well. You will now receive Divination XP whilst you are in the cavern.
Very well. You will now receive some mystery rewards when you leave the cavern.

conversations.section: In Lumbridge

pages.x: Hello there.
Hello, I suppose. I'm Lachtopher. Could you lend me some money?
Lend you money? I really don't think so. Don't you have any of your own?
I spent it all and I can't be bothered to earn any more.
Right, and you want my hard-earned money instead? No chance!
You're just like my sister, Victoria. She won't give me any money.
Your sister sounds like she has the right idea.
Yeah, I've heard it all before. 'Oh,' she says, 'It's easy to make money: just complete Tasks for cash.'
Well, if you want to make money...
That's just it. I don't want to make money. I just want to have money.
I've had it with you! I don't think I've come across a less worthwhile person.
I think I'll call you Lazy Lachtopher, from now on.

conversations.section: After King of the Dwarves

pages.x: You can go into the Lava Flow Mine if you want now, human.

o: Is the mine up and running again?
Tell me more about the Lava Flow Mine.

pages.x: Did the wounded miners recover?
Three of them recovered. I'm afraid one was too badly wounded. If it wasn't for you, though, they'd all be dead.
Is the mine up and running again?
If it wasn't, we wouldn't be standing here. Everything in the city relies on it - heat, water circulation, even clean air.
The central boilers have been breaking more often since the incident, but we've been keeping on top of the repairs.
Tell me more about the Lava Flow Mine.
It's where the city gets most of its power. We've tapped into a magma vent, and we use its heat to power the steam machinery that runs the mine carts.
The mine's been running for nearly a hundred years. The Consortium had it built to provide power to all the city's new industries.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Ranged combat / Talking to Sir Vant

pages.x: There! That should keep the dragon quiet for a bit.
Well done! You did it.
You did it too. I don't think that dragon will be coming back any time soon.
You can never tell.

Not yet. What should I do next?
Well, I wrote all the tasks in your Quest Journal. Feel free to do them in any order - you could always explore Lumbridge and see what you want to do next.
I am feeling quite weak and weary though, so I'd really like some crayfish.
What will that do for your health?
Like a crayfish, you are wet behind the ears. Food heals you!

o: I'd like to know about something else.
I'll go get you some crayfish.

pages.x: I'll go get you some crayfish.

conversations.section: In Barbarian Village

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Welcome, surface-dweller, to the Dorgesh-Kaan marketplace! Are you here to sell your exotic surface foods?
Yes!
How can I sell food?
Most of the people wandering around the market want to buy food. Since the passage to the surface opened up there's been a craze in exotic food from up there.
To sell something, simply use a piece of food on one of the gourmets in the market, then name your price, and the gourmet will tell you how many they are interested in buying for that price.
If you want a rough idea of how much something will sell for, show it to me and I'll try to estimate.
But you should also take into account the gourmet's reactions when naming your price. If someone likes the look of a food, they will pay more for it.
Also remember that the novelty of new foods quickly wears off. If people have been eating a lot of something lately, then they won't pay as much for it.
If someone especially likes your food then you might even start a craze for it! If there's a food that's in fashion like that, then the gourmets will pay more for it.
Are you selling anything?
Goodbye.

Certainly [sir/ma'am]! Coming right up! That's two coins, please.
Can you dance, Megan?
Can I dance?!
CAN I dance?!!
Dance with me Megan!
Do you have any news?
Not at the moment. I've heard that the known world is expanding as new places are discovered.
These are exciting times indeed!
Never mind.

Is there anything I can do to help out?

What's happening around here?

I for one am very pleased to have met you.

conversations.section: Talking to Mod Raven atop the hourglass tower in the City of Um

pages.x: It is strange to be here. They do know I'm not dead, right? Someone has told them?
I mean...this is the Underworld?
True, it is the perfect place for a snack. The souls here are delicious after all.
So rife with precious suffering, how I adore it.
I miss you Raven.
That's a lie and you'll burn for it.
But I miss you too...
I'm glad you're gone.
Who are you again? Do I know you?
Anyway, enough idle chatter. There are lost souls here and I have a shiny new spoon.
Dinner time!

conversations.section: Non-random NPC dialogue / Oneiromancer

pages.x: Oneiromancer!
What? Ah, very bright of you contacting me this way.
Yeah, thought I'd make use of the new spell to ask a question.

o: Can you change my spell book back to the standard one?
Can I tell you a joke?

pages.x: Oh, I do like jokes, go ahead.
What do you call a crazy moon?
A crazy moon... Hmm, I don't know. What?
A luna-tic!
Ahahahaha!
Hahaa!
Hahahaha!
Okay, okay. It wasn't THAT funny.

conversations.section: Random NPC dialogue / Al Kharid Camel

pages.x: Hi there!
Why, helloooo!
A camel?
Well this is grand, darling. How nice it is to make your acquaintance!
Thank you. Nice to meet you too.
Wait a minute. How am I talking to you without a camulet?
My dear, I'm a camel; how should I know?
Hmmm. I suppose this spell must tap directly into your mind, so there's no need for language to get in the way.
I think I am somewhat confused.
May one ask how you contacted me?
I'm just using one of the Lunar spells.
Oh my, oh my. These youngsters today and their new-fangled gadgets!

conversations.section: Subsequent conversation / All birds found / First time

pages.x: Skreeeee! Have you found any more birds yet?
Yes, sixteen! Here, take a look!
Skreeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee!
Skreeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee!
... Are you okay?
You've done it! These are all the birds I ever found in the Arc! Thank you, thank you, thank you! Skreeee!
No problem!
Please take this beautiful specimen as a reward!

o: You have unlocked a new pet!

pages.x: Skreee!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Oh, hello! I was just trying to discover the properties of these magical stones you call 'runes', and trying to make some devices to harness their power.
Oh, it's terribly exciting! Let me explain...
The only thing I've been able to make so far is this. I call it the moving-over-distance sphere.
Well, I was experimenting with these blue runes, the ones you call 'law' runes. They have a strange property of being able to move instantly from one place to another.
I know; I couldn't believe it either!
I found that whenever I prepared powdered law runes in a certain way and then threw them on the ground, I would appear somewhere else in the city.
I asked Zanik to test it, and she said that wherever she was in the caves, even if she went to the surface, whenever she smashed the sphere on the ground she would appear back in the city!
I can see how it might be useful, but I wish I knew more about how it worked...
Goodbye!
Oh, er, goodbye. Now, where was I...

conversations.section: On Ice Mountain / After obtaining the Ice Mountain Elder Chronicle

pages.x: Can you impart your wise knowledge to me, Oracle?
Wen the cold wind blows.
Don't you mean 'when'?
Who?
No, when.
At the end of things.
What? I'm lost.
As are we all.
Never mind.
You know, I preferred your older prophecies.
Would you like to hear one?

o: No, I'm not in the mood.

conversations.section: At the Divination camp / Using a memory on her / During the 25th Anniversary celebrations task

pages.x: Ah, the memories...
And the energies, chronicles and wisps...
Very droll.
But you are right, we should not dwell on the past so much.
Perhaps you are here for me to divine your future...
Well, seeing as I'm here.
Hmm, let me see... You will stand tall and fight back against powerful gods, yet end up triumphant!
Um, all of that is in the past.
Hmm, let me see... You will complete a series of seemingly random, nostalgic tasks in exchange for a shiny reward!
Sorry, no, that's the present.
Hmm, let me see... You will get an elbow in the ribs from an irate diviner.
Ah, no! Please, spare me from my terrible fate!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Are you hunting animals, then?
I'm exploring the region for the good of the gnome people.
You're not tracking down huge beasts to kill - you look equipped for it.
Well, if I find anything interesting I'll try and bring it back to the King. That might include animals, I suppose.
I'd rather not kill it, though - most animals are more useful alive.
How would you get it home, then?
Never underestimate the ingenuity of a gnome, friend.
Have you found anything else interesting around here?
I've heard strange rumours about something the locals call the Broodoo.
I haven't quite worked out what they are but they seem to be some sort of undead whose ghastly fate depends on the way they were killed.
I think they may be sacrifice victims - but I'm not sure why they are sacrificed. Either way the locals seem to be very scared of them.
That's interesting. Thanks.

conversations.section: When spoken to normally

pages.x: What's up doc?

o: Tell me about your task list
What do I need to get for this prescription?
I've got some ingredients for the prescription.

pages.x: Tell me about your task list.
Yes... there's plenty of tasks you can do for me...
If you can finish the tasks on the card I'll make sure you're rewarded... appropriately.
I do like being rewarded appropriately.
Yes... I'll show you how to be just like me...
I've lost my task list.
What do I need to get for this prescription?
Yes... Have a look at my list...
Goodbye.
You'll be back...

conversations.section: Historical dialogue / Before completing the test

pages.x: Hello, Professor.
Ah, hello again. How may I help you?
What is this place?
This is the Misthalin Training Centre of Excellence.
It is where bold adventurers, such as yourself, can come to learn of the dangers of the wide world and gain some valuable experience at the same time.
What can I do here?
Here you can take part in the Player Safety test: a set of valuable lessons to learn about staying safe.
Yes, please.
Not right now, thanks.
Very well. Come back and see me again if you change your mind.

conversations.section: Before Royal Trouble

pages.x: Hello.
Er...Hello, Your Majesty.
Have you come for a particular reason? I am a busy Queen, you know. I had to attend the opening of a new orphanage this morning.
Yes, I...
And this afternoon I shall be receiving the Embassador of Karamja and accompanying him on his week-long tour of Etceteria.
Er, I...
Then this evening we shall be putting on a grand ball! All of the kingdom's nobility will be present!
If I m...
Oh, who am I kidding...nothing ever happens here. I always wanted to be a princess when I was a girl. If I'd been told it would be like this, I wouldn't have bothered.
Your Majesty!
Yes? Did you want something?
...actually, no.

I thought this acne potion might help ease your spots.
Ok let's give it a go so.

Oh stop being so soft.
Well?
Well what?
Did it work?
Well...umm...no.
What? You intolerable, insufferable idiot. I've just burned out my eye for no reason? I would say get out of my sight but that's not far enough away.
Sorry I was just trying to help.
Scram or I'll give you something to feel sorry about!

Like my fellow guardians I am part of the arena and live to ensure its safe running.
I see.
Can I trade my Pizazz Points, please?
Got anything else I can buy?
Well, we do stock a special book that you may be interested in, which provides a comprehensive guide to this training arena. It costs 200gp; would you like one?
Thanks, bye!
Use what you've learned, young one.

conversations.section: At Port Sarim Jail / Talking to Rick Turpentine

pages.x: Stand and deliver?

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: What are you doing?
I used to roam the lands robbing travellers and giving the loot to anyone I liked. It was such a happy life, and I didn't really do much harm.
Suddenly they've decided that wealth redistribution is a crime, so they've stuck me in here with a stupid mugger. We even have to take turns using the bed!
I still shout 'Stand and deliver' at people, but it doesn't really work so well from in here.
That's really sad.
You could cheer me up by shooting the mugger. I like it when people shoot the mugger. I like it when people shoot the mugger, even though he always comes back.
Hahaha, you're locked up.
No need to rub it in!
I'm leaving now.
I guess I'll be here next time you come by.

conversations.section: After Spirits of the Elid

pages.x: Come one, come all, buy my amazing choc ice invention here! Chocolate on the outside. Iced cream on the inside.
Oh I also have some chocolate left over from making choc ices which I'm selling too.

o: Cool, I'd like to buy some.
(After Crocodile Tears) Do you sell croc ices?
How do you stop your icy snacks melting?
How's business, now that the curse has gone?
(After Do No Evil) Made any more chimp ices?

pages.x: Do you sell croc ices?
Why, yes I do! I've just recently started stocking some for a customer near Menaphos.
I have to warn you, though - they are VERY moreish. They are so delicious, it's hard to stop at just eating one.
Though, you should be aware you'll have to deliver them by foot. Any sort of magical interference and they'll melt.
How's business, now that the curse has gone?
Ohh as good as ever.
The people of Nardah seem to have taken well to the taste of chocolate and iced cream combined and, with the curse gone, all my friends are much happier too, so it's all good.
Made any more chimp ices?
Ah, no. I sold the intellectual property rights to a group of desert monkeys: non-rectangular shapes are more of a headache than they're worth.

conversations.section: In the Draynor sewers

pages.x: Hello.
You ssshould not be down here...
Who are you?
My name isss unimportant... I live only to ssserve my massster.
Um... Okay then.
Why are you down here?
Thisss isss where I belong... Beingsss sssuch as myssself cannot abide in the light... It is in the darknesss where we find our homesss...
Uh... Okay then.
Can I use your anvil?
Of courssse you may... I have very little ussse for it nowadaysss...

Grrreetings frrriend! Welcome to my worrrld famous food emporrrium! All my meats are so frrresh you'd swear you killed them yourrrself!

What? Why, what else would you want to eat? What kind of lycanthrrrope are you anyway?
...A vegetarian one?
Vegetarrrian...?
Never mind.

Cooked food? Who would want that? You lose all the flavourrr of the meat when you can't taste the blood!
Can I buy some food?
Cerrrtainly!

conversations.section: Clan Cup

pages.x: Hello there! Do you wish to participate in a special Clan Cup for your clan?
What's this about?
This is a special competition where I'll track all Clans who wish to dedicate time to this competition!
For this particular Clan Cup you'll be required to skin as many dinosaurs in Anachronia as possible!
How do I take part?
If you wish to take part without a Vexillum, feel free to select the 'Clan Cup Functions' option on the trophy in Clan Chat!
Now on to the competition...
You'll have 1 hour to set the highest score you can, the top ten members for your clan will constribute to a clan total which will be compared against the other clans!
What can we win?
If your clan finishes in the top ten for the entire competition, expect some goodies including a boost to that avatar of yours and more!
My fellow scribes will be in touch to arrange prizes, should you finish in the top 10!
Thank you!

You should escape while you can.
Oh, I wasn't trapped here. I could have left at anytime. You should escape now, though.
Oh, that's okay. It's not so bad here.
You do know where 'here' is, though, don't you?
Of course - this is ScapeRune! It's a sort of mirror dimension to your world... but like one designed by someone who didn't fully understand the word 'opposite'.
Believe me, I used to want for nothing more than to escape, but Evil Bob... well, he's not so bad; he's grown on me.
He lets me explore the island sometimes, he strokes my hair...
... plus I should be getting my new litter tray soon!
I think you might have been here too long. You've become conditioned to your - um - conditions.
Maybe so, but at least I'm happy now. How many people can truly say that?
Farewell!

I've recently been exploring the Eastern lands - very easterny, I have to say...
Right...
Rumours had it of a fantastically large lobster around these parts. I naturally rushed to see what the fuss was about.
Oh, you mean Clawdia?
Yes, Clawdia was it's name! A friend of mine called Shuma came along. He's a great whaler! Wait, no... his name's Hubbub.. he's hunting something called Shuma. A whale.
Wait, is that right? Come on Carlos, keep it together!
What did Hubbub find here?
You know Hubbub? No way - me too! He just left after helping me find a claw of a giant lobster called Clawdia! I cooked it up right away. Care to try a piece?
Sure, I'll try anything once.

There's a few magic lamps, which should help you with your skills. I trust you already know what should be done with them.
Wow, thanks!
Now, if you should happen to lose that armour, you may come back to me to reclaim it.

Give me a lever long enough, a fulcrum on which to place it, some bellows and maybe a few tubes, and I could assemble a machine to move the world!

o: Goldberg seems to lose himself in this thought.

pages.x: As long as the peacock kept hold of the spanner...

Had?
Well, yes... It turns out she wasn't quite the success I'd dreamt her to be, so I've taken her out of action.
This is my latest invention: the Rune Goldberg Machine! Before I took her out of action, she was able to turn unremarkable runes into purest vis wax!
She was always a bit temperamental... Some runes worked better than others. Anyway, she's no longer in use, sorry.

o: Can you show me how to get there?

Let's go.
Happy hunting!

conversations.section: At the Artisans' Workshop / Normally

pages.x: Welcome. What brings you to the home of the artisans?

Artisans are a collective of skilled smiths who work towards upholding quality as their principle ethos.
Smithing can be seen as a coarse, unloving undertaking...bashing out platebodies as quickly as you can. It's not like that here.
Recently, we've opened our doors to humans. Some of our stauncher members aren't happy about this, but if you work hard I'm sure you'll earn our respect.
Tell me more about yourself.
I built the furnace that rather dominates this room. Took me four and a half years; carved the rock myself. If you need any pointers on how to use it, talk to Egil.
I don't do much actual smithing any more. I mainly potter around the workshop, helping where I can.
I've got to go.
Ah, take care.

conversations.section: First cutscene

pages.x: The dragon told me the voyage would be treacherous but I have never seen a storm like this one.
The sea is primordial. It is ancient, and vast, like a thing from another time. The sky is angry. I can feel it.
If not for the Stormbreaker's powerful magical wards, we would be torn apart.
From the deck I hear the island calling to me.
'Turn back. Turn back. I do not want to be found. I should not be found. Turn back.'
This must truly be the very end of the world. Cut off from everything.
The sort of place I have been seeking all my life.
A place of solace.
I think the storm is finally breaking.
At last we can catch a glimpse of this barren rock...

What? Aren't you going to help me then?
Oh heavens, no! Surok has a frightful temper at times - and you probably did something to deserve it anyway.
Surok is a traitor to Varrock and is wanted by the Varrock Palace Secret Guard!
Well I don't know about any of that, but I do know that I haven't been paid yet and until I get paid, I'm doing nothing further.
I don't think he's coming back, you know.
He'd better, or I'll be contacting the palace to make a formal complaint!
I...I see. Well, good luck then.
Thank you. Goodbye!

I train my skills here upon its foul brood, to prepare myself for the fight ahead!

Ah, you did not come prepared [Fremennik name]?
I have nothing to spare, but my equipment grows weaker under the onslaught of the daggermouth spawns!
I will trade you a finely cooked shark if you have a replacement for my helm, my shield or my blade...

pages.x: Waaaaaah!
Hello there, what are you doing?

...I just appeared here. I think the tree is magic!
Well, looking across the shore I can see a tree of the same type. Perhaps if you climb it again it will teleport you back over to your brother.
Waaaaaaaah!
I'm scared of climbing, though!
Hang on a second, you got in this mess because you climbed a tree. But you're scared of climbing?
Waaaaaaaah!
I'll stay put for now.
Suit yourself.

Yes, I'm grateful to be alive, but don't expect me to be jumping for joy.
Why don't you leave?
I'm a known exile! No reputable ship will take me as a passenger, even if I could afford their fee. If I tried to go anywhere on foot I'd be killed by ogres or bandits.
Can you tell me more about the Red Axe?
They sent us to Jatizso to keep an eye on the Fremenniks there, in case they formed an alliance with Keldagrim.
Grundt and I didn't know anything specific about the Red Axe's plans.

hee, I probblie schoodn' 'av anuva drinkie right now. But dis dwarven beer ish kind of moreish after the fiff pint.

I yousht to be a tesht pilot yoo know. I reeel hero.
But I loscht my bottle. Scho I now ffind scholiss in the bottle.

Naaah, I realished I woz scared ov heightsh.

Hello there! Are you interested in buying one of my special team capes?

If you and your friends all wear the same team cape, you'll be less likely to attack your friends by accident, and you'll find it easier to attack everyone else.

Tell me about your previous jobs.
For millennia I have served and waited on the mighty Demon Lords of the Infernal Dimensions.
I began as a humble footman in the household of Lord Thammaron, and for several centuries I was the private valet to Delrith.
I have also worked in the Grim Underworld, escorting the souls of the dead to their final abodes.

As fun as tumbling through pocket-dimensions sounds, I'll stay put.

Ah, so that's how everyone can have a house without them cluttering up the world!

pages.x: Welcome, fellow mercenary, welcome.

o: Can you assign me a bounty?
How many bounties do I have available?
Can you tell me more about your bounties?

pages.x: I assign bounties to fellow mercenaries like yourself. This is a war, you see, and there's killin' to be done.
The deals I cut with the faction representatives here mean you can pick one to do your bounties for, earning reputation with them in return.
What does a bounty entail?
Well, killin' of course. One hundred kills of the faction I assign you, to be precise, but if you kill their general it counts as twenty-five!
You pick the faction you fight for, I pick the faction you fight against, then away you go. Happy hunting.
So why are you even here in the first place?
I'm a mercenary, much like anyone else in this war-torn place. 'Course I have my own nefarious agenda, but that's for me to know.
Happy hunting.

They're cute little creatures, aren't they?
Purrrrr!
My children have always been popular with Adventurers. They have inherited their father's adventurous spirit.

Well, you could flap your mouth about while making words into a sentence.
Oh...you are so lower class. I've become used to dealing with better people than you since I became fabulously wealthy.
Thank goodness I have my pomander of expensive spices, your odour was beginning to make me feel light-headed.
Hey!
I'm sorry, I can't hear it when poor people are upset. Toodle-pip.

conversations.section: Before Between a Rock...

pages.x: Welcome to the Keldagrim library, human traveller!

Quite like the name myself.
The books in this library have been collected for many centuries now, through various generous donations.
You'll find books dating from many different eras as well, such as the Era of Kings, the Rise of the Consortium and the Era of Prosperity, our current era.
How do these eras correspond with the Ages of the world?
Oh, they are quite different, and most of them take place in the Fourth Age.
Since we dwarves hid underground for a long time to sit out the wars that raged above the ground our history books differ slightly from those written by humans.
Thanks for the information!
