Most outlanders are confused by our beliefs. From what I understand there is a great deal of conflict between the followers of different gods on the mainland.
That's putting it lightly.
Thank you for sharing this with me.
It is nothing. Go in peace, friend.

conversations.section: Talk-to / Normally / Before Dealing with Scabaras / First-time dialogue

pages.x: Hello.
G'day, mate. I'm Simon. Simon Templeton. Who are you?
I've been contracted to retrieve artefacts from the top of this magnificient pyramid.
So, why are you down here and not up there?
Well, it's me back...an old injury I picked up in Sophanem has come back to haunt me.
I was working for Varrock Museum, but the gold they gave me wasn't even enough to pay for the carpet rides, let alone any decent equipment.
But that was a long time ago... I can't even lift a chisel right now. There's no way I can climb all the way up there.
Hang on a second... You look like you're pretty agile and up for a challenge. How about you retrieve them for me?
I'll tell you what. I'll give you 1,000 coins for every artefact you get for me.
I'll see what I can do.
Good on ya, mate!

conversations.section: In New Varrock / After Dimension of Disaster: Demon Slayer

pages.x: I don't know how you've managed to get that sword so dirty after just one use.
I know I'd take better care of it, but even though it's a family heirloom, I'm not worthy to wield it.
About that, what happened with you and the trials?
You should know - you've been through them too! Didn't you find them difficult? What trials did you face?

pages.i: What will you tell Sir Prysin about the trials?

pages.x: I sobered up a drunkard, aced a pop quiz and was pretty much just handed the third trial.
And that whole thing with the coughing I found VERY uncomfortable. I still have flashbacks about that.
I performed an exorcism on a legendary vampyre hunter, after braving a dark cave that was home to a savage beast.
Then an animated grimoire posed me a raft of near impossible questions, all of which I had to answer.
Finally, I had to place my faith in another to guide me towards my future. I was entirely at their mercy.
I hassled a bunch of spirits until they were so annoyed with me that they just gave me the sword to get some peace and quiet.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Hey Spring Cleaner.
Hey [Player], did you know... BEHIND YOU, LOOK OUT!
What?
Haha, made you look!
Hey Spring Cleaner tell me something interesting.
72.1% of statistics are made up.
The chances of getting a dragon pickaxe on your next Chaos Dwarf kill is 5000 to 1.
Hey Spring Cleaner tell me something funny.
I got scammed by someone the other day, you could say he cleaned me out.

conversations.section: In Keldagrim

pages.x: Do you want to buy any stone for building? Or gold leaf?

o: What kind of stone do you sell?

pages.x: No thanks.
What kind of stone do you sell?
A few kinds. Limestone, of course. Here in Keldagrim we're surrounded by the stuff so I can practically give it away!
You'll be able to build some kinds of furniture out of that.
Marble is much better, of course, but it costs a lot for me to get hold of it. You can make some beautiful pieces of furniture out of that.
I also sell gold leaf, which can be used to decorate furniture made of marble or mahogany.
Then for the very special furniture I sell these magic stones.
Only the most skilled builders can work them, but they can create a few amazing pieces of furniture with them.
So, do you want to buy anything?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Are you one of the returned citizens?
Why, yes. You must be the adventurer who Maisa talked to us about?
That would be me. Now, can you help me?
Probably not; I'm a stone mason and have little to offer an adventurer.
You know what would be brilliant?
I don't know.
Could you make some granite armour or alter granite armour to better fit me?
I'm adraid I can't do that, sorry. In the blazing desert sun, granite armour isn't very popular so I haven't had any experience of working with it.
Once the place is a bit less chaotic, however, I will try to think of ways you adventurers can help. Who knows what I'll come up with.
Should I come back soon, then?
I wouldn't hold my breath. I'm thinking it will be months before I have work for you rather than a few days.

conversations.section: Talking to the hunter or trying to passing by without answering him going to the abbey for the first time

pages.x: Hey, are you going to the abbey?
The abbey?
The Abbey of Saint Elspeth? It's the only place that path leads.
Well, if you're heading to the abbey, you should keep your ears open. Their music is famous all over the world.
I can hear 'em sometimes, when the wind is right. Times like that, I don't mind I'm not catching any strykewyrms.
Yes.
Well, if you're heading to the abbey, you should keep your ears open. Their music is famous all over the world.
I can hear 'em sometimes, when the wind is right. Times like that, I don't mind I'm not catching any strykewyrms.
No.
Well, you're going the wrong way, then. The only place that path leads is the abbey.

conversations.section: After Mining and Smithing rework

pages.x: Hey what's going on here?
You make burial armour for fallen ancestors.

o: How can I make burial armour?
What's up with the suits of armour?
What do I get from this?

pages.x: Dwarves die lots. Miners crushed by rocks. Warriors stabbed by goblins. Smiths get black lung.
To honour our dead, we build them armour so they can keep on working in afterlife.
You smith full set of adamant armour (or better). Helm, body, legs, gauntlets and boots. Then you upgrade each piece until it is best.
Then smith them into burial armour set at burial anvil. It is simple. But slow. Like wife of Suak! Or you are lazy. You buy fully upgraded armour.
You smith burial armour set. Suak does not like the lazy smith.
Suak not so smart with words, but good with hammer.
Dwarves not buried with armour will be unable to make way to afterlife. They come here. We give them burial armour. They go. Suak thinks they pass on.
To build armour for our beloved dead. An honour. Great experience for you. For helping our dead, you earn respect of Suak.

conversations.section: Viewing memories / Juna

pages.x: I am sorry Juna. I have lied to you. I have been your idol, your god, your father. But I am the reason you are alone. It was a choice you see.
It had to be one world or another and I chose the other world. Numbers. Pure numbers. There were more of them, then there were of you.
As cold a reason for genocide as any other. So, I placed the lure on your world, a fountain of delicious anima for the blind beast to sniff out.
She destroyed your world, it was my fault. Another world lived because of that sacrifice, cold comfort though that may be. I wanted to save more of you.
So I grabbed two eggs, you and your sister. I thought that perhaps if I could save a family it would be my absolution.
I would have saved more, but the beast was on your world so fast, faster than I had dared think possible. So I saved you and your sister. Two eggs.
The last of their kind. I thought I could save you. I thought all you needed was me to look after you, but only you hatched. Only your egg survived.
I couldn't bear the shame of you knowing. So I hid your sister. Buried her lifeless egg where no one will ever find it. And I never told you about her.
Each time we meet I yearn to ask for your forgiveness. But then I see the look in your eyes. I see the standard to which you hold me.
The hope, the faith, the love you have for me and my courage crumbles. I am so proud of you Juna. You are like a daughter to me, I hope you know that.
And if you find this message, I pray that one day you can forgive me.

conversations.section: Viewing memories / Sword of Edicts

pages.x: Enough! My intention to be forgotten is futile if other gods fill the void in the hearts of mortals.
This is not the fault of gods, but the folly of mortals to be meek and unquestioning.
While I spend all my will stalling the inevitable end of mortality, while I wasted my time protecting them from inevitable destruction, they instead dash their own lives on the altar of worship.
Such futility - it must stop! Mortal life is brief enough as is.
It should not be wasted in servitude to power, in worship of false idols, in the hopes of a reward beyond death. When will they learn that life itself is the reward?
It should be treated as such, spent in joy and discovery, in time with loved ones, in the betterment of self...
The petty tribal rivalries of so-called gods are nothing but a distraction, and one I must try to remove.
I shall evict the gods and their influence from this world, even though maintaining a barrier to keep them out will split my focus.
As a result, I shall not be able to delay the inevitable for anywhere near as long as I had hoped. The elders will wake anew.
But better for mortals to realise their end is nigh and start living their lives, fighting for it themselves, than me mollycoddling them and gifting them limitless time in which to act as sheep.
They are blinded to this truth of this reality by their own folly. If allowing their end to come sooner will force them to open their eyes, then so be it.

conversations.section: In port

pages.x: Ecstatic to see you again, darling.
How are things?
I wonder if you could help me.
I am yours for eternity.
Do you prefer to work alone?
How's the life of the occultist?
A blood ritual here. Fighting demons there. Oh, it can be SO dreary.
But don't play coy, I've heard you're no strange to the arcane arts yourself. Your knowledge of runes is second to none.

o: Meet the Occultist Only if she was not your first adventurer.

conversations.section: In the Miscellania and Etceteria dungeon

pages.x: Good day, [sir/madam].

o: What are you doing down here?

pages.x: What are you doing down here?
We're extending the cave so more people can live in it.
These Miscellanians aren't so bad. They appreciate the benefits of living underground.
...such as?
Not getting rained on, for example.
Did you do anything about that monster Donal was talking about?
It's been taken care of.
Glad to hear it. Now we can get on with excavating.
Good day.

conversations.section: At Mudskipper Point / While having Imcando mattock pieces in inventory

pages.x: A tingling in my Imcando toes! Is that really what I think it is?
Yes! You've come across a very rare thing. Some unforged Imcando metal. Do you mind if I take a look at it?
It won't be easy, though. As well as the pieces, I'll need a dragon mattock, and one million coins for the time.
And a redberry pie, of course.

o: I have those things with me now.

pages.x: Lets get to work.
...and then once you bind these two pieces together with some flux to prevent the metal from oxidising. You've made yourself a tool the dwarves would be proud to weild.
Thank you, Thurgo.
With all the ancient sites that have been uncovered lately, it only feels right to equip the best archaeologists with the tools and means to uncover the secrets of our ancestory.
If you can find enough of these rare Imcando metals, I can teach you how to create a such a tool for yourself.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Dialogue 4

pages.x: Hello.
Hi there. So much to see here!
Yep, could be looking all day! Updated any displays yet?
Yes, I just learned more about some priestly warriors and a staff of the gods.
Sounds fun, how did you do that?
Ahh, I'm big on quests me, love questing. So when I've done one, I check here with 'Historian' Minas to see if I can help the Museum out with some information.
Sometimes they already know it, or don't want to know and sometimes it earns me a reward or two.
That sounds really good. Perhaps I should do the same!
You should, as well as everything else there is here in the Museum. Did you know they have a really fun-looking display down in the basement? I love monkeys.
I'll check it out. Got to get going now, nice talking to you.
Have a good day!

conversations.section: Before One Piercing Note

pages.x: Greetings, traveller!

o: What are you doing at the abbey?

pages.x: What were you singing about?
Ah...it's a song about someone I knew, a long time ago.
What are you doing at the abbey?
One of the sisters here, Sister Anna, she passed away recently. I knew her before she joined the abbey, so I've come to pay my respects.

o: How did you hear about Sister Anna's death?

pages.x: How did you hear about Sister Anna's death?
I have my ear to the ground. Even a religious order isn't completely cut off from the world.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue after The Fremennik Isles

pages.x: Hello, Vanligga!
Oh, hello [Fremennik name]. Always good to see a friend. Hmm, I suppose I can trust you, since you have done me a favour in the past. Can you keep a secret?
Of course.
Well as you probably already know, all yak meat and yak products are banned on this island - orders of the king.
That King has some very strange attitudes.
Well, I have a contact on the other island. Are you interested in obtaining some produce?
Yes, please.
No, thanks.
Well, any time you need black market yak produce, you know where to come.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello!

o: I want to join the orb project!

pages.x: I want to join the orb project!
You can speak to Wizard Acantha or Wizard Vief if you want to join a particular team. Or if you like I could assign you to whichever team has fewer members.

o: Please assign me to a team.
I'll talk to one of the wizards.

pages.x: Please assign me to a team.
I'll talk to one of the wizards.
Okay!
Never mind.

conversations.section: In Port Sarim / Before Pirate's Treasure

pages.x: Welcome to my food store! Would you like to buy anything?
Yes please.
No, thank you.
What can you recommend?
We have this really exotic fruit all the way from Karamja. It's called a banana.

o: Hmm, I think I'll try one.
I don't like the sound of that.

pages.x: Hmm, I think I'll try one.
Great, you might as well take a look at the rest of my wares as well.
I don't like the sound of that.
Well, it's your choice, but I do recommend them.

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander, before The Mighty Fall / At Stealing Creation

pages.x: Hello, Player.

o: What do you think of the mystics?

pages.x: What are you doing here?
Well, I wanted to check out these mystics that people have talked about, and their portal to another world.
They won't let me go through their portal to see the other world, though. The Head Mystic talked about how the holy ones were angry with me or something.
Well, never mind, there's plenty to see in this world.
What do you think of the mystics?
They worship the ghosts in the wilderness - ghosts left over from the God Wars. Did you realise that?
They seem to think the God Wars was a time of glorious battles, where everyone was heroic and brave.
I think if they could, they'd go back to that time...or they'd start a new war here.
I know a bit about war - I've had the War God in my head, after all - and I don't think these mystics would be so fascinated by war if they were in a real one.

conversations.section: Third task / Talking to Johanhus Ulsbrecht in the cathedral / First time

pages.x: Aren't they incredible? It is an honour to be in the presence of such beauty. I can already feel a connection with the Elder Gods forming.
How did you get in here looking like that? And why have you been telling people that we are working together?
I didn't tell them that we're working together, I just mentioned that I am your close associate.
But WHY would you say that?
Well, I had to make it clear that I am no threat... And please keep your voice down. Show some respect!
I had heard rumours, but I had no idea they would be so mesmerising.
You need to leave.
I am not going anywhere. You may leave if you wish.
Look, I have more pressing matters to attend to and do not have time to argue with you. No one here is going to let you do any real harm, but just stay out of the way.
Oh, and don't wander out onto the battlefield. You'll die.

conversations.section: City Quest / Friend's son slowly dying / Task #3

pages.x: Oh no...
What?
I am... hopeful. I worry that you have given us hope, only for the sands to snatch it from us.
No matter. I will take this brief moment of solace for what it is.
A good idea. How else can I help?
We have everything we need. If you still want to help: while we've been caring for the young boy, we've neglected our daily duties.
If you could obtain gear for climbing for us, you would allow us another day's peace.
Getting hold of [number] of [item] should be sufficient.

o: I don't have time right now.

pages.x: Wonderful.

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / New product / Task #1

pages.x: I've had a brilliant idea for a new product I can sell in the city. It is so brilliant that it would be a bad move to share with you what it is...yet.
I could tell you if you helped me out by sourcing what I'll need to create my invention!
What do you think? Could you please bring me [number] [item]?
I just want to thank you.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: It's fine. Everything will just go up in smoke...
It's fine. Everything will just go up in smoke...
It's fine. Everything will just go up in smoke...

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / War effort / Task #1

pages.x: I've been tasked to procure supplies for the war effort.
Who are we- Who are YOU at war with?
All will be revealed. First up I need [number] [items]. Can I rely on you?
I just want to thank you.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: It's fine. Everything will just go up in smoke.
It's fine. Everything will just go up in smoke.
It's fine. Everything will just go up in smoke.

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Awaiting delivery / Task #2 / Afterwards

pages.x: The next supplies I'm missing are a load of [item].
...and they still haven't arrived yet?
Could you get me some to tide me over for now? About [number] [item] should do.
That will suffice.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.
Nevermind.
Nevermind.

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Awaiting delivery / Task #3

pages.x: Seeing as you're so resourceful, I wonder if you could save me a trip around the city...
Go on…
Are [number] [item] too much to ask for? Will you find me some?
That will suffice.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.
Nevermind.
Nevermind.

conversations.section: In Jaldraocht Pyramid

pages.x: And... just like that. It's painless. Almost without sensation.
What?
The way this altar tampers with your mind.
I've spent years learning one set of spells, and then in an instant they're gone, and these other ones are there in their place. So easily...
Modern spells...
Ancient spells...
Modern spells...
Ancient spells!
If only there were some way to hold both sets of spells in the mind at once. Or to work out how to use this mind-rewriting effect...
Anyway, I've got work to do. I'll see you around, Player.

conversations.section: First conversation

pages.x: Not good. Not good at all.
What isn't?
Your shell, it won't do.

o: The armoursmith wiggles a hammer in the direction of your stomach.

pages.x: The Airut will crush it, their hounds will shred it and the desert will cook it.

o: How do you suggest I improve my shell?
I think my shell will do fine, thank you.

pages.x: Mazcab is old, hides many secrets, I have fragments of these secrets. Bring me Teci, I make them into a better shell for you. Maybe you find your own Mazcab secrets.
Maybe they form better shell than I make. Until then, come to me.
I think my shell will do fine, thank you.

conversations.section: Rellekka / Talk-to / Before The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Hello there.
Hey there, buddy. You're an outerlander, huh? I'm not really supposed to talk to you.
Why not?
I dunno buddy. Some stupid tradition or other. We're always told not to talk to outerlanders unless the Chieftain has allowed it.
The Chieftain? Who is that?
His names Brundt, buddy. He's a real boring guy. You can find him in the long hall there.
Can you take me to see him?
Sorry buddy, I'm not allowed into the long hall. Don't worry, he's easy to spot. He's the one in the fancy helmet. Oh, and he only has one eye.
He's a cyclops?
Nah, nah, nah... He just wears an eyepatch! Well, see ya around buddy!

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Do you want to use the balloon? Just so you know, some locations require special logs and high Firemaking skills.
No.
Who are you?
I am Assistant Le Smith. I used to work as a glider pilot, but they kicked me off.
Why?
They said I was too full of hot air.
Do you want to use the balloon?
No.

conversations.section: After Fragmented Memories

pages.x: How is the professor doing?
Which one?
Well, the salamander professor is fine, happily just exploring and gorging on insects. Keeps them off the team while we work, very helpful.
More so than Professor Alfredo was in that body.
And the actual professor?
Oh, he's a cutie! His little salamander face is full of expression! You can almost see Alfredo's mannerisms in him, but he's just too cute to take seriously.
Honestly, I've never liked him more.
Well, we'll get them swapped back eventually...I think we've discovered all there is here for the moment.
While in the device, the professor mentioned lingam stones and a door near a dragonkin head stonework piece somewhere around the temple to the south-east of Anachronia.
Don't rush on our account! Perhaps that's the lead we need to follow for our next mystery!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Do you want to use the balloon? Just so you know, some locations require special logs and high Firemaking skills.

o: Could you tell me how to make an origami balloon?
Could you combine my cap and goggles?
Could you replace some items for me?

pages.x: No.
Could you tell me how to make an origami balloon?
First, use the papyrus on the ball of wool. The papyrus is folded into an origami box and the yarn will support the heat source.
Next, add the unlit candle to the balloon structure. It will act as the heat source.
Now you have an origami balloon!
If you use your origami balloon with any dye, you can change the colour.
You can release the balloon and watch it float in the air, just use a tinderbox on it.
There you go! You look like a true airship pilot now.

conversations.section: After Love Story

pages.x: Yes?

o: The robber in the recording looked familiar.
Can I see that recording again, please?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: The robber in the recording looked familiar.
Oh, you recognised him too?
Yes, and he's admitted that he did the robbery!
The amount of evidence against him makes that almost unnecessary.
So are you going to have him arrested?
I believe the staff of the Wizards' Tower have taught him a lesson, and they're ensuring he doesn't cause any more trouble in future.
The revenue we've received from people watching the recording has adequately covered the cash stolen from the bank, so the Bank of Gielinor is satisfied.
Fair enough.

conversations.section: Normal dialogue

pages.x: Good day. How may I help you?

o: I'd like to access my bank account, please.
I'd like to check my PIN settings.
I'd like to see my collection box.
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: What is this place?
This is a branch of the Bank of Gielinor. We have branches in many towns.

o: Didn't you used to be called the Bank of Varrock?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: And what do you do?
We will look after your items and money for you. Leave your valuables with us if you want to keep them safe.
Didn't you used to be called the Bank of Varrock?
Yes we did, but people kept on coming into our branches outside of Varrock and telling us that our signs were wrong.
They acted as if we didn't know what town we were in or something.

conversations.section: In Varrock / With a keg of mead before making a delivery to Blue Moon Inn during The Need for Mead event

pages.x: What can I do yer for?
I've been sent here to see if you'd be interested in trying and giving some feedback on this mead. I have an entire keg for you.
More mead from Leslie? They just don't give up!
Yeah, they were hoping you'd have some constructive feedback on this latest batch?
Let me have a try.
Hmm...
Better than the last batch...
Something isn't quite right though...
Yer, there's a nasty after taste. I wouldn't stock this.
Okay, I'll let them know. Thanks.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello.
Good day to you, brave adventurer. Can I get you a refreshing beer?
Yes please!
Ok then, that's two gold coins please.
No thanks.
Let me know if you change your mind.
How much?
Two gold pieces a pint. So, what do you say?

conversations.section: Talk-to / With a keg of mead before making a delivery to Jolly Boar Inn during The Need for Mead event

pages.x: Can I help you?
Leslie has sent me here to ask if you could give some feedback on their latest batch of mead.
For Leslie, happily!
I wasn't expecting you to drink it all.
It's the best way.
I somehow doubt that.
That was pretty good though!
The intensity is right. The flavour is good but it just tastes too weak!
I know they're always after perfection. This is good, but not perfect!
Thanks, I'll let them know.

conversations.section: Historical / Standard

pages.x: Hello. Do you want me to make some planks for you or would you be interested in some other housing supplies?

o: What kind of planks can you make?
Can I buy some housing supplies?

pages.x: What kind of planks do you want?
I can make planks from wood, oak, teak and mahogany. I don’t make planks from other woods as they’re no good for making furniture.
Wood and oak are all over the place, but teak and mahogany can only be found in a few places like Karamja and Etceteria.
Nothing, thanks.
Well, come back when you want some. You can't get good quality planks anywhere but here!

conversations.section: Talk to / Before Extinction

pages.x: Can you hear that?
Listen.
I can only hear the waves?
Exactly! The peaceful sound of water.
The sound makes me feel calm, peaceful and untroubled.
It is quite nice.
It's also lovely to get a break from my brother. I found this tree that transports anything that climbs it over to that island across the shore.
I asked him to climb it for some fruit and *poof*. He vanished. Allowing me to get my peace and quiet for the day.
If you want to get across, just climb the tree and you'll teleport too. Really handy for getting places quick!
Thanks!

conversations.section: As the player's chosen director after The Giant Dwarf / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here are your bars!

o: The Director replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Guthix be praised!
I am well pleased with your work, Player!
You are a true asset to the Blue Opal!
You never fail to satisfy, Player!
I will get my secretary to send this to the trade floor at once!

o: If the player received the task from complaining about the trade floor guards:

pages.x: I'll have a word with the guards. They won't be watching you for the next ten minutes.

conversations.section: As the crew of Sarim's Revenge / Waiko

pages.x: Captain, while we're docked, I'll see about getting some repairs done.
Anything you need from the markets, Evie?
How about some information on my brother's whereabouts? This isn't a holiday.
You're all about business, aren't you?
I'm Kinshra. Discipline is why we're a better fighting force than those stodgy White Knights.
I'm surprised, then, that the Black Knights let you leave to search for your brother.
Er, yeah, about that...
Actually, it's nothing. Forget I said anything.
Evie?
I said forget it.

conversations.section: In Brimstail's cave / After The Eyes of Glouphrie

pages.x: Hello adventurer, what can I do for you?

o: I've been investigating another watcher in the Tree Gnome Village.
I need to mine some rune essence.

pages.x: Hello, just wanted a chat.
It's always a pleasure to catch up with another mage! Especially one who has helped me so much!
I've been investigating another watcher in the Tree Gnome Village.
And, as a consequence, I've found an underground cave complex full of warped terrorbirds and tortoises.
It seems to be underneath Arposandra or, at least, a city with gnomes in that use talking terrorbirds as guards.
Wow! You've really found Arposandra.
I think so, though I can't get in. It's all blocked up. But I'll find a way...eventually.
Well, good luck!

conversations.section: As the player's chosen director after The Giant Dwarf / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here are your bars!

conversations.section: In Servants' Guild

pages.x: Good day, sir. Would sir care to hire a good butler for [number] coins?

o: Tell me about your previous jobs

pages.x: What can you do?
I can fulfill all sir's domestic service needs with efficiency and impeccable manners.
I hate to boast, but I can say with confidence that no mortal can make trips to the bank or sawmill faster than I!
Tell me about your previous jobs.
From a humble beginning as a dish-washer I have worked my way up through the ranks of domestic service in the households of nobles from Varrock and Ardougne.
As a life-long servant I have naturally suppressed any personality of my own and trained myself never to use the second person when talking to a superior.
I have usually worked in the large households of the aristocracy, but now that such a large number of private persons are building their own houses I decided to offer them my services.
I must respectfully decline, sir.

Or I could pay you nothing at all...

conversations.section: After Kennith's Concerns

pages.x: Hello again, Caroline. Are you all rested after your ordeal?
Yes, I'm feeling much better, thank you. Kennith is doing well out on the platform too.
I'm glad to hear it. I hope he's behaving himself!
Oh yes, Bailey has him at work trying to clear the platform of the sea slugs. He's even started writing letters to Kimberly!
Really? How has she reacted to that?
I don't think she's quite ready to forgive him yet, but I don't think Kennith is ready to give up either. To tell you the truth, I think he's smitten with her!
Who'd have thought it!
Yes, that's quite a revelation. Well, I hope it works out for him. I might go out to the Fishing Platform to visit him sometime soon.
Oh, I think he'd like that - he's always talking about you!
I'll do my best.

conversations.section: After As a First Resort

pages.x: Hi, human.
Hi, ogre.

o: Can you tell me about this salt-water spring?

pages.x: Can you tell me about this salt-water spring?
Yeah, sure, human! De water flows fast from underground. When you bathe here, it make you flow fast overground for long, long time.
Flow fast?
You know, flow on your feetsies. Fast-like. Quick, like a bunny!
Are you talking about running?
Yeah, run, flow - same thing. Have bath here, it not matter how heavy you are, how much you carry - you can flow long time!
Thanks, that's good to know.

conversations.section: Foreshadowing / Closure's Study

pages.x: No cutting in line! Did you not see the other souls waiting to see me?
Oh, I'm sorry, this is important and I'm in a bit of a rush. It's literally a matter of life and death.
Those are the only such matters I deal in. Your troubles are no more important than those of the souls here who have been waiting longer than you.
About that... Why are these others here?
Ah, I see. I imagine you defeated these foes some time ago, and are confused why they are here now.
All who die find their way to me, but time works slightly differently here. Their past might be your future.
It helps me with the huge task I have set myself, which is to write the stories of all who die.
Stories have a tendency to intertwine, even in my waiting area for some reason, and history is not without a sense of irony.
Those you do not know, you will come to know in your future. Regardless, they were here first. I will get to you in time.
Until then, please make use of the facilities in my waiting room. Read a book or something. There are plenty to choose from...

conversations.section: During the lost sword of King Raddallin event / Giving her the letter from King Raddallin

pages.x: Th-this can't be right! We knew Raddallin and Valzin were associates at the beginning of his reign but this suggests that even at the end they were still friends.
This just can't be! The people of Falador, the White Knights, none of them are ready to hear this... This will change history, and who knows what will happen next.
Just look at the fighting that's happening right now. If we allow the Black Knights to be legitimised then this whole region could fall into a new civil war.

o: That's not your place to decide.

pages.x: Yes, yes, thank you for agreeing with me.
It goes against everything I stand for but I feel this letter must be preserved and kept private until we can be sure people are ready to hear this.
And it's your place instead? To risk hundreds of lives for some heroic vision of the world?
I'm sorry but in this case I feel this letter must be preserved and kept private until we can be sure people are ready to hear this.
I thank you for your assistance in recovering these items. Feel free to keep the sword, maybe it's best that it stays lost for the peace of Falador.
Thank you for all your help!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Welcome to the Mining Guild. Can I help you with anything?

o: What have you got in the guild?

pages.x: Ooh, it's WONDERFUL! There are orichalcite, runite and coal rocks, all exclusively for people with at least level 60 mining.
What do you think? We smelt it into bars, smith the metal to make armour and weapons, then we exchange them for goods and services.
I don't see many dwarves selling armour or weapons here.
No, this is only a mining outpost. We dwarves don't much like to settle in human cities. Most of the ore is carted off to Keldagrim, the great dwarven city.
They've got a special blast furnace up there - it makes smelting the ore so much easier. There are plenty of dwarven traders working in Keldagrim.
Anyway, can I help you with anything else?
Can you help me with the gemstone golem outfits?
No thanks, I'm fine.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

What do you have to offer?

pages.x: Why do you live so close to the trolls? Isn't it dangerous?
Well, I suppose I do keep getting captured by the trolls and thrown in prison...But they always release me in the end, I'm far too old and skinny for their tastes.
In any case, this is my home, and I'm not leaving it. And this area has the tastiest goats!
What do you have to offer?
The chef's recommendation for today is mountain goat stew. I'll give some stew in exchange for logs for my fire. They're hard to come by around here.
Your loss!

If you manage to excavate any artefacts, I'd be willing to give you some Spooky tokens in exchange.
I can also impart a bit of my knowledge of prayer on you, as well as some more Spooky tokens, in exchange for any ancient remains you find whilst working within the Hollow.
*yawn* I'd very much like to lay them to rest if you bring me a full set.
Bye.

So, you're just picking the flax for fun? You must really like flax.
'Like' the flax? I don't just 'like' flax. The GLORIOUS flax is my calling, my reason to live. I just love the feeling of it in my hands!
Erm, okay. Maybe I can have some of your spare flax?
No. I don't trust outsiders. Who knows what depraved things you would do with the GLORIOUS flax? Only locals know how to treat it right.

Bless you.
What's going on here?
Pestilence asked me to look into ways of recruiting more underlings - uh, I mean members - into the clan.
I thought that perhaps offering a fast way here for potential applicants would help sign them on, so I drew this little summoning circle.
It's powered by the candles around the edge - the more that are lit, the more potent and efficient the spell.
*sniffle* If you fancy helping I could pay you in Spooky tokens for every guest you summon - consider it your commission.
Farewell.
*sniffle* Bye bye.

conversations.section: After As a First Resort

pages.x: Hi, human.
Hi, ogre.

o: Can you tell me about this copper-coloured pool?

pages.x: Can you tell me about this copper-coloured pool?
Yeah, it red!
Yes, I can see that.
Then why you ask, silly human?
Well, it's hard to explain. I just sense a strange energy coming from this pool. Do you know anything about it?
Oh, well, it called de 'Bandos pool' round here. It s'pposed to be special-special. It hard to explain to human creature like you. Maybe you need talk to auntie Seegud.
She explain good about these things.

conversations.section: In Sophanem / With a cat in the bank

pages.x: Good day.
You have the feel of a cat person about you. Do you look after one?

o: Yes, but I don't bring it to harsh places like this.
Yes, but I've left mine in the bank.

pages.x: Yes, but I don't bring it to harsh places like this.
A pity; they can be of great help in some adventures. I would like to talk to your cat. Would you bring it to me?
I might, but I have a few things to sort out first though.
No, you are mistaken.
Really? I'm generally quite good at knowing these sorts of things.
Yes, but I've left mine in the bank.
What? That's no place for a cat!

conversations.section: After being asked to bring a spicy flower but before attempting to give one / Using items / Cave nightshade

pages.x: You found the spicy flower!
Me knew you were good zomboe.
Now give it 'ere.
Well here goes nothing.

o: You throw the nightshade into the ghost troll's mouth.
It passes straight through the troll.

pages.x: Aww, me can't enjoy nuffin no more.
I'm sorry, is there anything I can do?
No, no point.
I... Guess I'll leave you to it.

conversations.section: After unlocking the spirit tree

pages.x: If you are a friend of the gnome people, you are a friend of mine. Do you wish to travel, or are you here to ask about the evil tree?

pages.i: What would you like to ask about?

pages.x: You can travel to the trees related to me. Where do you wish to travel, whisperer?
I can help you find the where it will spawn, but my knowledge outside of the anima mundi is limited.
It can be found close to a [location] (See Evil Tree#Locations with hints for list of locations).
It is an abomination of nature that must be destroyed as quickly as possible.
We do not know where it will appear, but, when it does, you should go to it immediately and help out!
Goodbye.
Nothing, thanks.

conversations.section: At the mountains east of the Poison Waste / Standard dialogue / If there is no Evil Tree

pages.x: If you are a friend of the gnome people, you are a friend of mine. Do you wish to travel, or are you here to ask about the evil tree?

pages.i: What would you like to ask about?

pages.x: You can travel to the trees related to me. Where do you wish to travel, whisperer?
I can help you find the where it will spawn, but my knowledge outside of the anima mundi is limited.
It can be found close to a [location] (See Evil Tree#Locations with hints for list of locations).

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello old bean.

o: Can you teach me about canoeing?

pages.x: My name is Tarquin Marjoribanks. I'd be surprised if you haven't already heard of me?
Why would I have heard of you Mr. Marjoribanks?
It's pronounced 'Marchbanks'! You should know of me because I am a member of the royal family of Misthalin!
Are you related to King Roald?
Oh yes! Quite closely actually. I'm his 4th cousin, once removed on his mothers side.
Er... Okay. What are you doing here then?
I'm canoeing on the river! It's enormous fun! Would you like to know how?

conversations.section: Player-owned port

pages.x: Hello. Can I assist you?
How are things?
I wonder if you could help me?
If you ever need help, do not hesitate to ask.
Do you prefer to work alone?
How's the life of an architect?
An architect has to consider both function and aesthetics: we have to balance strength with beauty; form with function. Each building is a new puzzle.

conversations.section: Viewing memories / Aagi

pages.x: In time, you might come to see my choice to die as a selfish act, but I am decided.
I have prepared for this for centuries, ever since you visited me and I became aware of my fate. But if the mortals are not ready now, they never shall be.
Maintaining the Edicts has taken too much of a toll. And I cannot stall things forever. I am so very tired.
I will leave you with a fighting chance, a glimmer of hope, but you will have to find your own way, World Guardian.
Use the power I shall bestow upon you, the knowledge in these caches and the guidance of my guardians.
If you should fail, then at least the afterlife should welcome the fallen for a time, until that too fails.
When I see you at my end, I shall tell you I wish to be with my wife and daughter in death.
However, the truth is that I gave up my right to that a long time ago - unwittingly, but unequivocally.
And though I know I shall never see my Aagi or Fraji again, I have lived long enough without them. In this place, I shall leave my strongest memories of them.
Perhaps they too can help you in some way. I have knowingly left you with a great burden, World Guardian. I hope you can find it in your heart to forgive me.

conversations.section: Standard

pages.x: Woah! Don't sneak up on me like that!
How are you doing, Carlos?
I could use your help.
You need something sliced, diced and cooked? I'm on my way!
Do you prefer to work alone?
Do you like cooking, Carlos?
I love to cook. You get to work with a big pot and stir things in without being accused of witchcraft and cursing people!
I have to go.
Oh, I'll see you around port then. Farewell!

conversations.section: Standard

pages.x: How may I serve you, naabe?/Good day, challem.
How are things going?
About your voyages...
I am ready to carry any burden you would hand me.
Do you prefer to work alone?
How are your burdens?
They hang heavy on my shoulders as always, but my shoulders are strong, as they should be, for I am a worldbearer.

o: Meet the Exile Only if she was not your first adventurer.

conversations.section: Inside Asuran Arsenal

pages.x: Proceed no further. This facility is restricted.
What is this place?
Experimental weapons facility zero-zero-one.
Ah, of course.
Why can't I go any further?
Only dragonkin are authorised for entry. You may not pass.
Good luck with that.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue, in the player-owned-port

pages.x: Greetings! Can I help you?
How are things going, Reginald?
I'm in need of someone with your skills.
Tally ho! What are we waiting for? Let's get to it!
Do you prefer to work alone?
How is the hunting going?
Mother loves the trophies I send her. If I accidently have fun wrestling a mountain lion to the ground, then all the better!

conversations.section: After As a First Resort

pages.x: Hi, human.
Hi, ogre.

o: Can you tell me about this copper-coloured pool?

pages.x: Can you tell me about this copper-coloured pool?
Yeah, it red!
Yes, I can see that.
Then why you ask, silly human?
Well, it's hard to explain. I just sense a strange energy coming from this pool. Do you know anything about it?
Oh, well, it called de 'Bandos pool' round here. It s'pposed to be special-special. It hard to explain to human creature like you. Maybe you need talk to auntie Seegud.
She explain good about these things.

conversations.section: In the Burthorpe mine

pages.x: Burthorpe needs weapons, and we miners provide the ore used to make them. You want to help out?

o: Tell me about the skills menu.

pages.x: Mining is the source of all the metal in the world. Without mining, there'd be no tools, no weapons, no industry at all!
Get your pick and swing it at some rocks! The more you swing, the better you'll get.
The better you are at mining, the better the ore you can mine. Better ores are much more useful and much more valuable.

o: Tell me about the glowing rocks.

pages.x: When mining, a nearby mining rock will occasionally glow. Mine that rock for a swing of extra damage, and therefore faster progress.
Occasionally when mining, you'll find an untradeable geode: sedimentary, igneous, or metamorphic. Crack open the geode to find a reward inside.

o: You can get igneous geodes from members' core rocks.
They also have a rare chance to yield a valuable metamorphic geode.
Achieve 99 in all your skills to earn the coveted Max Cape!

conversations.section: Talk to / Before sacrificing the fire cape

pages.x: Let us talk...

o: Last time I was here, you spoke about a battle?
I'd like to speak more about you and your kind.

pages.x: The skirmishes we engaged in when you were last here were entertaining, but not a stretch for our capabilities.
A real challenge is all we desire...
We heard that the TzHaar compete for a cape composed purely of fire...
Beasts have wondered in here and we have melted their being into us. Some of these beasts fought in what you call 'The Fight Cave'.
Okay. Go on...
Someone who possessed such a cape would be worthy of our challenge.
Go on.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Dialogue 1

pages.x: Hello!
Hi, have you seen the Dig Site displays?
Yes, good aren't they! Have you done the quest?

o: (If the player has not completed The Dig Site)
(If the player has completed The Dig Site)

pages.x: Not yet.
Oh you should, it lets you get into that bit where they clean the finds, and you can join in!
Sounds fun, I should probably check it out.
Yes, I did it all.
Did you know after the quest you can get the teddy bear back by stealing it from the female student?
I shall have to try that sometime.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue, after TokTz-Ket-Dill

pages.x: You need help, [Title]-[Caste]-Player?
Are you not [Title]-[Caste]?
Well, yes, I suppose I am...
Then you [Title]-[Caste]!

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / Giving her a white fruit

pages.x: Hello, traveller! Look, I hate to be rude, but is that the aroma of White Tree fruit I smell?
It might be.
You wouldn't happen to have one on you going spare, would you? I'm utterly exhausted and could really use a pick-me-up.

o: Of course; I brought one just for you.
Sorry, I can't help you right now.

pages.x: Of course; I brought one just for you.
Thank you ever so much. I can't tell you how much I was craving White Tree fruit.
Glad to help.
Should I ever be able to repay the favour, just let me know.
Sorry, I can't help you right now.
Ah, well. It costs nothing to ask.

conversations.section: I have more information about the Mahjarrat / Enakhra's Lament

pages.x: I encountered a pair of Mahjarrat called Enakhra and Akthanakos. Enakhra had imprisoned Akthanakos in the form of a creature called a "boneguard".
The imprisonment spell seemed to require her constant supervision, though.
I ended up breaking the deadlock and now they say they're headed to the north to continue their fight there.
Why would they be heading to the north before resuming their fight, I wonder? I guess it's something to do with the ritual.
It seems unusual that they were embroiled in such a fight outside the Ritual, anyway.
Apparently they've always been rivals, but it seems they also had religious differences. Enakhra is a follower of Zamorak and Akthanakos follows a god called Zaros.
A Mahjarrat following Zaros? Interesting.
So, you've heard of Zaros?
Yes, there are some reference to him in ancient texts that I have run across.
From what I gather, he once had followers who were fiercely loyal to him; what has become of him now, I don't know.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / Before completing the Grand Exchange tutorial

pages.x: Hello there. I was wondering if you could help me out...
I suppose I could, but I must admit, I feel a bit intimidated talking to someone who looks so brave and adventurous.
Are you being serious?
Oh, quite serious. I don't feel we have enough in common for me to even begin to be able to have a conversation with you.
So, ignoring the fact that we are, in fact, having a conversation at this very moment, are you saying that you'd help me out if... we shared some interests?
That's exactly it.
So, what are you interested in, then?
Well, perhaps if you learned more about the exciting world of trade and commerce, I'd feel more able to talk to you.
You are a very strange individual.
That sort of comment doesn't help, you know.

conversations.section: Talk-to / Before All Fired Up

pages.x: So, what are you up to, this fine day?
Oh, just tending this fire.
What fire? I don't see any fire.
Oh, it is not lit yet.
So, you're just standing here, watching an empty fire pit?
Of course not. When tending a beacon, it's much more important to watch your surroundings than to watch the fire itself.
It is?
Of course. One must be constantly vigilant for any sign of danger. In fact, talking to you is distracting me a bit from duties to the kingdom.
I'm afraid I'll have to say goodbye now.
Oh, right. Sorry.

conversations.section: As the player's chosen director after The Giant Dwarf / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here are your bars!

o: The Director replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Guthix be praised!
I am well pleased with your work, Player!
You are a true asset to the White Chisel!
You never fail to satisfy, Player!
I will get my secretary to send this to the trade floor at once!

o: If the player received the task from complaining about the trade floor guards:

pages.x: I'll have a word with the guards. They won't be watching you for the next ten minutes.

conversations.section: In Port Sarim / After Pirate's Treasure

pages.x: Is it nice and tidy round the back now?

o: Yes, can I work out front now?
Yes, are you going to pay me yet?

pages.x: Yes, can I work out front now?
No, I'm the one who works here.
Yes, are you going to pay me yet?
Umm... No, not yet.
No, it's a complete mess.
Ah well, it'll give you something to do, won't it.
Can I buy something please?
Yes, of course.

conversations.section: As the player's chosen director after The Giant Dwarf / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here are your bars!

o: The Director replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Guthix be praised!
I am well pleased with your work, Player!
You are a true asset to the Yellow Fortune!
You never fail to satisfy, Player!
I will get my secretary to send this to the trade floor at once!

o: If the player received the task from complaining about the trade floor guards:

pages.x: I'll have a word with the guards. They won't be watching you for the next ten minutes.

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander, before The Mighty Fall / At Oo'glog

pages.x: Hello Player, isn't it beautiful here? It's so peaceful!

o: It's full of mud and ogres!

pages.x: Yes, I like it.
I am glad you like it too. Most of the humans here pass through so quickly. They don't stop to look around.
Its full of mud and ogres!
And? What's wrong with mud and ogres? Oh, never mind. I think it's something humans don't appreciate so much.
I think this place is especially peaceful for goblins and ogres and other...you know...other Bandos races. Races from Yu'biusk.
I think that this place must be like Yu'biusk. Not like it is now, but like it was before Bandos destroyed it.
Mud, plants, cool water - it's just like Grubfoot described.
So it moves something deep inside us. It feels like home.

conversations.section: Fourth task / Talking to Johanhus Ulsbrecht at Nodon Front

pages.x: World Guardian, what is it that I have stumbled upon here?
It is rife with monstrous abominations, yes, but more than that...
There is so much violence. And it's merciless. Indiscriminate.
Nobody is being spared. Nobody at all.
Do you see now? The Elder Gods don't want your worship, and they would think nothing of wiping you, all of humanity and every race on the planet out.
If we are to survive, we need to unite against this threat. That means not just humans - it means everyone.
This is not what I expected at all. Not what I wanted at all.
I am getting out of this awful place. Good luck to you.

conversations.section: Using a A 'Durzag & Goebbana' catalogue on Acca Kanatah

pages.x: Ah you found it! I have been seeking this for some time, Player.
Finally, I can order the newest rock covering that I have been longing for.
Embroidered with the finest Mazcab silk, finished with eeligator saliva - it is truly the greatest accessory any goebie should ever need.
So... do I get anything as a reward? Will you be telling all of the goebies of my heroic deed on this day?
Absolutely not, human! No-one can know that an Acca wears Durzag and Goebbana, no matter how high quality and reasonably priced their fashion is.
This must stay between you and me, [sic]
Not even a single goebie?
No!
Kanatah's secret, it does have a certain ring to it.

conversations.section: Burthorpe / Talking to Turael / After slaying the rabbits

pages.x: Well done slaying those rabbits! How do you feel?

o: Good. I'm ready to slay something else.
I hated it. Please don't make me kill bunnies again.
Can I kill more rabbits? That was fun!

pages.x: That's the spirit! I have a tougher assignment for you, but you'll need melee armour and more food to take into combat. Let's get cooking!
Don't worry! I have a tougher assignment for you, but you'll need melee armour and more food to take into combat. Let's get cooking!
Of course! You can never slay enough rabbits.

o: Now I am become Death: the Slayer of Bunnies!
Be vewwy vewwy quiet. I'm slaying wabbits!

pages.x: Yes, yes. Very amusing. Now hop to it.
(whisper) Yes...very amusing...now hop to it.
Slayer's pretty amazing, isn't it? Profitable, too! Now go forth, and reduce the surplus population!

conversations.section: City Quest / Friend's son slowly dying / Task #2

pages.x: Good, thank you so much.
Now that's done, we need the next block of supplies.
The next supplies I require are a bunch of [item].
Right. Why [item]?
The thaumaturge tells us that we need [item]. We didn't think it wise to argue.
Right. If this... thaumaturge thinks that a [item] could help, then I guess we should search for [item].
I will make the preparations while you are away; is it a reasonable request?
Wonderful.

conversations.section: In Al Kharid / Using an Al Kharid flyer on him

pages.x: Hi! I have this money off voucher!
Oh! Err .. unfortunately it seems to have expired yesterday!
But I only just got it from Waseem the Leaflet dropper!
I'm sorry, there's nothing I can do.
But you're the one that had them printed!
Look, I had those printed to win over the local traders. They weren't too pleased with the money off voucher, but I promised them I would repay their losses.
So that would be why they're all out of date then?
I don't know what you mean!
Anyway, before you go, take a look at my wares.

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Awaiting delivery

pages.x: I've been awaiting a delivery that contains some [item 1] and some [item 2].
I urgently need the [item 1], but folks on the pier say that there's no sign of the ship for miles.
That will suffice.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.
Nevermind.
Nevermind.

conversations.section: In the Wizards' Tower / Talk to / During the 25th Anniversary celebrations task

pages.x: Hello, Archmage Sedridor. Might I ask a question about the Lodestone Network?
Why, of course. How may I be of assistance?
Do you think lodestones have improved everyone's lives or taken away a little bit of its magic?
Hmm, a peculiar question. They are the height of convenience! They have done wonders for world trade.
No doubt, they have spared many ex-walkers untold amounts of foot injury.
Ah, but true...when does one take the time to casually stroll these days, to take in the sights and the sounds?
What wonders we miss when when convenience is at the fore...
Indeed, life should be somewhat 'bumpy', for you cannot have the highs without the lows. Thank you for reminding me of such.
You know what, I think I'LL go out for a walk soon.

conversations.section: Food and healing / Talking to Ned

pages.x: What do you want?
You may think you're some kind of warrior, wandering around with that sword of yours, but you don't fool me.
I saved the villagers from a zombie attack!
Hah, zombies? Don't be ridiculous. There's never been anything like that in Ashdale, and there never will be!
I'm catching fairies with an invisible net! What's it look like I'm doing? I'm sitting here by the fire trying to enjoy some peace and quiet.
Don't play the fool with me, young [man/miss]. You know full well who I am! There's only one Ned Swarbrick on this island, and that's me.
My family has been in Ashdale since the very beginning, and don't you forget it!
Hmph.

conversations.section: Waterbirth Island / Talk-to / After The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Hi buddy! Or do ya want me to call ya [Fremennik name] now?

o: Ask what Askeladden is doing here
Ask for a new pet rock

pages.x: Askeladden, what on Gielinor are you doing up here? And by the way, the name is Player.
Sure thing, buddy!
I was down in that cave killing daggermouths! It was fun! But then I got thirsty, so came up here for a bit of a rest...
Hey buddy, I'll tell you what, if you got any kegs of beer on ya, I'll buy them off ya for 700 gold coins each!
If ya found any animal parts killing daggermouths I'll trade ya for them too!
Can I have another pet rock? I lost mine...
Well it's sure a weird place to ask for it buddy, but I have hundreds of them! Go wild!

conversations.section: 2026 / After completing quest

pages.x: Oh, hey Ayah-
Sssh! You're going to get me caught when I'm so close!
These spies have got to go!
Sabotaging the rabbits in amazing disguise is my thing!
Once they're gone. I'll take over the Easter Bunny's kingdom, dispose of this dairy contraband, and begin my lactose-free empire!
Are you still not over that?
For now my hatred of dairy is merely an undercurrent of internal rage. Until these posers are dealt with...
So go on then. Pick their pockets and get rid of any information they're getting on these 'sweet little bunnies.'
Take any Spring Tokens you find as payment.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After The Hand in the Sand / First-time dialogue

pages.x: Bert! Good news!
Arrr...Good news always be handy.
They arrested Sandy for the murder of the wizard and the sand pit now refills itself!
ME JOB! I'VE LOSTED ME JOB! 'ow c'n yer say tha' be good news?? Me wife'll tear me limb fr'm limb!
Don't worry, the Wizards are going to pay you a large pension so that you can retire...
Bu' wha'll I be doin' wit' me day now! I be lovin' tha sand.
What will you do with your day? Well... You could build sand castles with your own two hands!
I din't think so... bu' iffen yer ever need someone ta haul buckets o'sand 'round. ye be lettin' me know Player, I's can help yer!
Wow! That would be great! Buckets of sand direct to my bank everyday, you say? That's great!

conversations.section: In Port Sarim

pages.x: Welcome to the magic emporium.

o: Talk to Betty about The Hand in the Sand.

pages.x: Zavistic told me what a good job you did. If you want some more pink dye, I have made up a batch and you can have some for 20 gold.
No thanks, Betty. Good luck with the shop. I might be back for some dye later.
Thanks, Player. See you soon.
Yes, please!
Sorry, I'm not into magic.
Well, if you see anyone who is into magic, please send them my way.

conversations.section: Location-specific dialogue / Lumbridge

pages.x: Hi Bob. I didn't think I would ever see you round here. Long way from home isn't it?
Yes, but the fish round here are oh so tasty! And there's nobody who can make a good old fashioned seafood gumbo like the Lumbridge cook!
Gumbo?
Oh yes, an old recipe passed down from generation to generation of cooks. But this might be the last generation since the Duke's current cook doesn't have any children.
Ah, I will have to ask him for the recipe then.
Oh, I wouldn't do that if I were you, he's very sensitive about his gumbo responsibilities.
I'm sure that if you're a good enough fisherman and cook the knowledge will reach you one day.
OK, I shan't bring it up with him. Cheers for the chat Bob.
No problem. Just make sure you bring me some of you ever get the chance to make it. I love that gumbo!

conversations.section: Wisdom / Wisdom 22

pages.x: Do you like dogs?
Yes!
Me too. Care to swap recipes? I have a rather unique hotdog sauce.
Bob, you’re a bit messed up really aren’t you.
No, I just know what I like. Besides, it was a joke.
A joke? I doubt the dogs are laughing.
What dogs? I have already rid this place of dogs. Have you ever seen one?
Yes actually. I heard there are a few wild dogs about here somewhere.
Right!! Fellow cats, prepare for war!!

conversations.section: In the Dwarven Mine / Talking to him

pages.x: Hello traveller.

o: Hello there, what's going on back here

pages.x: Hello there, what's going on back here?
Just taking a break. This section of the mine was stripped of ore long ago.
I'll leave you to it then, farewell.
Why are you called Boot?
I'm called Boot, because when I was very young, I used to sleep, in a large boot.
Huh, was that comfortable?
I don't remember much from back then, but apparently I didn't complain.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: What can I do for you?
Can I rest here?
I suppose.
What are you doing here?
Oh... I lived in Meiyerditch. The Vyrewatch forced me to play music here. They did not enjoy it, of course, but they liked to see me suffer.
Even in death, I am forced to remain.
That's very sad.
That's all, thanks.

conversations.section: After Birthright of the Dwarves / Spared

pages.x: None of the companies will accept me as a member! I'm a highly skilled trader, and they shut me off just because I worked for the Red Axe!

o: I spared your life. You could be more grateful.
Can you tell me more about the Red Axe?

pages.x: I spared your life. You could be more grateful.
Everyone in Keldagrim sees me as a traitor! I'll never be accepted into dwarven society again. No more dwarven food, dwarven clothes, dwarven drink!
Yes, I'm grateful to be alive, but don't expect me to be jumping for joy.
What will you do now?
I can't get a job as a trader or manager because of my association with the Red Axe. My only option may be to become a...
...manual labourer!

conversations.section: After Family Crest / With the unimbued family gauntlets

pages.x: I hear you have brought the completed crest to my father. I must say, that was awfully impressive work.
I believe your father mentioned you would be able to improve these gauntlets for me...
Yes, that is correct. I can slightly alter these gauntlets to allow you some of my skill at preparing seafood by making them cooking gauntlets.
When you wear them you will burn lobsters, sharks and swordfish a lot less. It will be a permanent modification however, so make sure this is what you want.

o: Yes, please do that for me.
I'll see what your brothers have to offer first.

pages.x: Yes, please do that for me.
I'll see what your brothers have to offer first.
As you wish. Let me know if you change your mind.

conversations.section: After Icthlarin's Little Helper

pages.x: Hey there, how're you holding up?
Well, I suppose things could be worse, though I really did have my hopes up. I thought you could fix things up.
I suppose that makes two of us.
Well, I've got a business to run here. I can't keep feeling sorry for myself for ever.
Are you in need of any willow logs at the moment, or any other wood for that matter?
Sorry, no. I've recently worked out a decent supply which bypasses the grey economy.
Grey economy?

conversations.section: Dialogue

pages.x: Need something, [sir/ma'am]?

o: How do I change my clan permissions?

I'd like to change my citadel's chat visibility settings.

pages.x: You can access your clan settings by clicking on the 'permissions' tab in the 'clan settings interface', accessible from the clan list.
Pick a rank from the list on the left and a category from the top to see what permissions each rank has, and click an option to toggle it on and off.
Remember, however, that you can't alter the permissions for any players of your own rank or higher, and that some options can only be accessed by those with administrator access or higher.
Also, the chat category works slightly differently to the others, in that you set the minimum rank to talk or kick, rather than setting permissions for each rank individually.
Would you like to know more about a specific category?
The admin category lets you change the permissions for all administrative actions within your clan.This includes recruiing, accessing the clan citadel and keep, and leading Rated Clan Wars.
