pages.x: So, what's your story? What do you do here?
I love it out here!
I came here to make money and catch big fish, but I stayed for the peace and the calm the ocean brings to my mind and the camaraderie amongst the people here.
This collaborative spirit inspired me to start combining parts of jellyfish for the other fisherfolk. I want to do my part to turn this place into a fishing utopia!
Don't you ever get seasick on these platforms?
Never! To me, it feels as if I'm cradled soothingly by the ocean, night and day.
Not sure my stomach agrees...

conversations.section: After Family Crest / With the unimbued family gauntlets

pages.x: Hello again. My family now considers you a hero.
Your father tells me you can improve these gauntlets for me...
And right he is at that. Although my skill with Death Rune magiks was not great enough to defeat Chronozon, I am adequately skilled at Chaos Rune magiks.
If you give me your gauntlets I will bestow upon them some of my power, and make any bolt spells you wish to cast more effective.

o: I shall see what options your brothers can offer me first.

pages.x: That sounds good to me!
I think I'll check my other options with your brothers before committing myself.
I doubt they will offer anything as useful as my magical boost, but as you wish.

conversations.section: In the tunnel near Lumbridge Castle cellar / Talking to him

pages.x: Hello, surface-dweller.

o: Can you show me the way to the mine?
Can you show me the way to the water mill cellar?

pages.x: Who are you?
Mistag posted me here when surface-dwellers started visiting the mine. If you have business in the Dorgeshuun mines I will guide you through the tunnels.

o: Can you show me the way to the mine?
Can you show me the way to the water mill cellar?

pages.x: Can you show me the way to the mine?
Can you show me the way to the water mill cellar?
Of course!
Maybe some other time.

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Beneath Scabaras' Sands

pages.x: *braaak*
Bug attack!
Found Scabaras, finally!
Osman's arrogant! Who knew? Tried to kill a god!
Amascut's angry! Attack coming!
Nice knowing you...
Not!
*raaawwwwk"

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Icthlarin's Little Helper

pages.x: *braaak*
Sophanem is full of plagues!
Talked to wanderer! Talked to sphinx!
Raided a tomb! Defiled a corpse!
Mind control! Mind control!
Like that'll hold up in court!
Wanderer was Amascut. Fooled again! Fooled again!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: Upgrading necromancy equipment / Tier 30 / Before having received the soul urn

pages.x: What can I help you with?
I'd like to learn more equipment upgrades, please!
Let's get started then! The next step is to learn the tier 30 upgrade.
What's the maximum tier I can upgrade my equipment to?
You can upgrade it every 10 tiers until it's tier 90. For tiers 70, 80, and 90 I can also give you the option of power armour, or the standard tank armour.
But let's not get ahead of ourselves just yet!
Right, so where were we... Tier 30.
Similar to when I taught you the first upgrade, I'll need you to take this soul urn and fill it with some souls.
This urn will only accept souls from killing trolls using necromancy, or completing lesser communion rituals. I need 25 troll souls, or 3 lesser communion souls.

conversations.section: At the entrance to the Warriors' Guild, after While Guthix Sleeps / Without requirements to enter the Warriors' Guild

pages.x: You can't come in. You're not enough of a warrior.
And a gnome called 'Laidee' is?
Are you being heightist?
No, I'm laughing at your name!
You really shouldn't do that. I'm what's stopping you from entering the Guild, and it's not really warrior-like.
What's to stop me just stepping over you?
I promised Ghommal that anyone unworthy would not gain entrance to the Guild. I will stick to that. Plus...you'd regret it.
Okay, you win.

conversations.section: Woodcutting / Talking to the Woodcutting Tutor / With the logs

pages.x: Well done! You have some logs. Did you know there are many different types of trees?
Oh? Tell me more.
Well, around here you mostly get plain trees, but there are oaks, willows, and further afield you can find maples, yews and even a magic tree!
Of course, you'll be wanting better axes to cut down these trees, but that will come with time and Woodcutting experience.
I suppose you'll be wanting to make a fire with those logs you got?
Yes I was. Sir Vant is tired and cold having fought the dragon, so I am going to make him a fire. The thing is, I'm not sure how.
It's no matter. You should visit the general store to buy yourself a tinderbox. Usually I have a stock to give to people but, what with the barricades, I've run out.
The tinderbox you buy from the shop will enable you to
light a fire.

conversations.section: Random event (Historical)

pages.x: I'm so sorry to drag you away like that, but I need your help.
What do you want?
I've put the wrong coffins into these graves.
I need you to pick up the coffins and put them in the right graves.
If you need to free up some space in your inventory, just store things in the mausoleum and I'll take them to the bank for you.
Okay, I'll get right on it.
How am I getting on?
Okay, let's have a look...
Wonderful! That's taken care of all of them.

conversations.section: At the Khazard Battlefield

pages.x: Move into position lads! eh? Who are you and what do you want?
Who are you then?
Lieutenant Schepbur, commanding officer of the new Armoured Tortoise Regiment.
There's only two tortoises here, that's hardly a regiment.
This is just the beginning! Gnome breeders and trainers are already working to expand the number of units. Soon we'll have hundreds of these beauties, nay thousands!
And they will not only carry mages and archers but other
fiendish weapons of destruction of gnome devising. An army of giant tortoises will march upon this battlefield and rain the fire of our wrath upon all our enemies!
Nothing will be able to stop us!
Oooookayy...... I'll leave you to it then....

conversations.section: In the Thieves' Guild / Subsequent dialogue

pages.x: What can you teach me?
I'm the locks and traps trainer. Need any advice?

o: How many hanky points do I have?
I'd like to claim a reward for my hanky points.

pages.x: You have collected [no hanky points yet/(number) hanky points]. You may claim the reward for up to [number] more hanky points this week.

o: I'd like to claim a reward for my hanky points.

pages.x: I'd like to claim a reward for my hanky points.
Bye for now.
Bye for now.

conversations.section: With catspeak

pages.x: So. Come to seek my wisdom? Or perhaps you wish to make a deal? I am so good at deals. I can get you anything.
You want power? Pfft, power is the game of kittens, I can make you a pharaoh, an emperor, even a god! It would be trivial.
Power flows so easily, if you know where to look.
Ahh, but perhaps you seek power of the arcane variety. Knowledge, the greatest force anyone can wield. I can give you secrets. I can teach you forgotten knowledge.
I who was apprenticed to the High Magister Oreb, master of souls.
I who have read all the books in the Grand Library of Menaphos.
Promise me your soul. Surrender it to me and I will teach you all of these things. I will give you power beyond your wildest dreams.
Yeah, I’ll get back to you.
It’s only your soul, you’ll barely miss it.

conversations.section: Dialogue

pages.x: Hello?
Moooooo.
Hey, I know you can talk!
Moooo.
Stop ignoring me!
Look, mate. Leave me alone!
You talked! You talked!
Moooo.
I think I'll have some beef tonight.

conversations.section: In Varrock Square / Talking to him

pages.x: Greetings, citizen.
Good day to you.

o: I'll let you get on with it, then.

pages.x: How's everything going today?
Fairly uneventful so far. Varrock's not the hotbed of crime that Ardougne is, after all.
I'll let you get on with it, then.
Stay safe, citizen.
I'll let you get on with it, then.
Stay safe, citizen.

conversations.section: After The Fremennik Isles

pages.x: It makes me proud to know that the helm of my ancestors will be worn in battle.
I thank you on behalf of all my kinsman, [Fremennik Name].

o: (If the player has lost the Helm of Neitiznot:)

pages.x: Ah yes, about that beautiful helmet...
You mean the priceless heirloom that I gave to you as a sign of my trust and gratitude?
Err yes, that one. I may have mislaid it.
It's a good job I have alert and loyal men who notice when something like this is left lying around and picks it up.
I'm afraid I'm going to have to charge you a 50,000GP handling cost.
Please be more careful with it in future.

conversations.section: After Birthright of the Dwarves / Meike / With the Consortium in power and Veldaban abdicated

pages.x: Hello again, Player.

o: How do you think the Consortium is doing now?
Have you heard from Veldaban lately?

pages.x: How do you think the Consortium is doing now?
They're back to their old ways. It could be worse, but...it's disappointing.
After what happened you can bet the company leaders are thinking of ways to prevent another loss of their power.
I doubt I'll see the monarchy permanently restored in my lifetime.
Have you heard from Veldaban lately?
Yes, he's been in touch. I invited him to join us here, but I think he's more comfortable on the other side of the city. Too many company leaders live over here, I think.

conversations.section: After Birthright of the Dwarves / Meike / With the Consortium in power and Veldaban abdicated / With Drunken Dwarf III as king

pages.x: Hello again, Player.

o: What do you think of the new king?

pages.x: What do you think of the new king?
He *is* the new king. I was there when they went through the records, and there really is no doubt this time.
I suppose one of the strengths of a monarchy is that each heir is trained for their role from a young age. You're not going to get that with a restored monarchy.
But even so, I wish it had turned out to be someone who hadn't spent their whole youth wandering the world in a drunken daze!
I'm sorry about Veldaban's death.
It's sad...but I know if there had been a way for you to save him, you would have done it.

conversations.section: Dialogue

pages.x: Hello there.

o: Do you have a spare pick?
How do you get out of here?
What is it that you're mining?

pages.x: Where are we?
What, you can't tell from your surroundings that you're in a mine? You must have been hit hard on the head to not notice that.
What do you do here?
Do you have a spare pick?
Sure, got one here you can use.
How do you get out of here?
What is it that you're mining?

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Awaiting delivery / Task #1

pages.x: I've been awaiting a delivery that contains some [item 1] and some [item 2].
I urgently need the [item 1], but folks on the pier say that there's no sign of the ship for miles.
Thank you.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Let me guess, you're worried about associating with me? Of course. Just like the others.
Let me guess, you're worried about associating with me? Of course. Just like the others.
Let me guess, you're worried about associating with me? Of course. Just like the others.

conversations.section: At the mill northwest of Lumbridge

pages.x: Hello, adventurer. Welcome to Mill Lane Mill. Can I help you?

o: What can I do with the flour I mill?

pages.x: I'm Miss Millicent Miller, the Miller of Mill Lane Mill. Our family has been milling flour for generations.
Don't you ever get fed up with flour?
It's a good business to be in. People will always need flour.
This is Mill Lane Mill, source of the finest flour in Gielinor, and home to the Miller family for many generations.
We take wheat from the field nearby and mill it into flour.
Flour is ideal for making tasty cakes, pies or delicious bread. I'm not a cook so you'll have to ask a cook to find out how to bake things.
You could also sell it on the Grand Exchange in Varrock for a profit! Likewise, if you need flour and do not have time to make it yourself, you can buy some there.

conversations.section: Officer training / A.R.M.S. Command Centre / Talking to Junior Cadet Mal

pages.x: This is the A.R.M.S. Command Centre for Mobilising Armies. Our mercenaries are all war heroes.
They desire money, adrenaline, combat and glory to such a degree that they'll fight for anyone.
We set this centre up to make the best use of their qualities, launching dangerous missions to outlying islands in search of treasure and fame.
Fair enough. So, what are all these buildings used for?
First, there is the recruitment room, where you can recruit and manage your army.
With an army, you'll be ready to proceed to the briefing rooms where you wait to join Mobilising Armies games.
The special unit tent's where you can purchase special units to aid your squads.
Finally, there's the officer tower. Through victory, you can climb the floors and claim the rewards that you are due.
[missing]

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Greetings traveller.

o: Can you heal me? I'm injured.
Isn't this place built a bit out of the way?
How do I get further into the monastery?

pages.x: Can you heal me? I'm injured.
Ok.
Isn't this place built a bit out of the way?
We like it that way actually! We get disturbed less. We still get rather a large amount of travellers looking for sanctuary and healing here as it is!
How do I get further into the monastery?
You'll need to talk to Abbot Langley about that. He's usually to be found walking the halls of the monastery.

conversations.section: In West Ardougne / While not wearing full Mourner gear / Talking to a Mourner (non-attackable)

pages.x: Hmmm, how did you get over here? You're not one of this rabble. Ah well, you'll have to stay. Can't risk you going back now.

o: I haven't got the plague though...

pages.x: So what's a mourner?
We're working for King Lathas of East Ardougne trying to contain the accursed plague sweeping West Ardougne. We also do our best to ease these people's suffering.
We're nicknamed mourners because we spend a lot of time at plague victim funerals, no-one else is allowed to risk the funerals.
It's a demanding job, and we get little thanks from the people here.
I haven't got the plague though.
Can't risk you being a carrier. That protective clothing you have isn't regulation issue. It won't meet safety standards.

conversations.section: Linking a clue to a character / During investigating the murder of Simon Bullace / Princess / Amulet of Spanielspeak

pages.x: Hello, Princess.
Talking! You're talking! Please, help!
Father ate strange smelling meat and now he's not moving. Sad. Confused.
We think somebody poisoned him. I know it won't bring him back, but I'm trying to find out who did it.
Why would anyone hurt father? He gave the best treats. And belly-rubs. And pats!
I'm not sure. I don't suppose you've seen anything suspicious. Anything that could be a clue?
Lots of suspicious things around! Things buried, strange smells, strange people. Show you! Show you!
Lead the way.

o: Select Princess and she will point you in the direction of a potential clue.

conversations.section: Non-random NPC dialogue / Larry/Chuck / Chuck (after Hunt for Red Raktuber)

pages.x: Hello there.
Greetings, voice in my head.
I wanted to talk to you about the penguin spies all over the world.
What about them?

o: I'm having trouble find the penguins. Can I have a hint?

pages.x: I've found more penguins.
More? Hmm, interesting. How many have you found?
I've found X penguin[s] this week.
Never mind.

conversations.section: Random NPC dialogue / Aris

pages.x: Hello.
Because I can tell the future.
Um?
That is the answer to your next question.
But how did you know what I would ask?
Because I can tell the future.
Ah, that's very clever.
Thanks. Oh - and be careful in the Wilderness. Tonight is not your night.
Cheers!

conversations.section: Random NPC dialogue / Hakeem the Sandsweeper

pages.x: Hello there! Who is this?
Hakeem.
Hakeem who?
I'm Hakeem the Sandsweeper.
You sweep sand?
Certainly do! I'm the best darn sandsweeper this side of the Lum.
There's more of you?
We have a union, mate! There's always sand to sweep.
Indeed. Um, I have to go.

conversations.section: Random NPC dialogue / Lumbridge Cow

pages.x: Hello?
Moooooo.
Hey, I know you can talk!
Moooo.
Stop ignoring me!
Look, mate. Leave me alone!
You talked! You talked!
Moooo.
I think I'll have some beef tonight.

conversations.section: As the crew of Sarim's Revenge / Waiko

pages.x: Oh, hey, have you met Boni yet? She sells all sorts of things in Waiko market.
You know each other? What sort of stuff does she sell?
Well, she's not part of my pod, but we did train to be seasingers together on Tuai Leit. She's nice, you'll like her!
Just don't stare at her eyepatch. There was an accident during our training involving some whale blubber, a rotten old cork and a narwhal. She's still embarrassed by it.
What sort of stuff does she sell?
She's in with all the traders here, and can get you better deals with them, and she carries an array of souvenirs and cosmetic items for tourists.
She also sells experience lamps, if that's your thing. Oh, and just a few specialist
items...
I expect she'll have even more to choose from in a few months, too, from what she tells me.

conversations.section: During Mega May, at Player-owned ports / Talking to Jemi / Thereafter

pages.x: Hi, it's so cool to see you again!

o: What can you tell me about yourself?

pages.x: Well, I was about to go on one...but I could use a little advice if you're up for it. I'll give you some of the treasure I find as a thank-you!
Sure, ask away.
Not just yet.
You...you want to know about me? Oh, good Guthix! It's like all my dreams came true at once!
Well, my name's Jemi - I mean, I think I told you that already - and I'm an adventurer. Well, I mean I'd like to be an adventurer.
At the moment I'm more of a novice adventurer...but I'd like to be more.
OK!

conversations.section: Talking to Niamh / After completing A Christmas Reunion / During a Christmas event

pages.x: How are you doing, Niamh?
HI Player!
SORRY, indoor voices! Indoor voices.
I'm doing some deep meditation right now. Pixies are prone to overexcitement, which can be not-so-helpful when we're trying to perform intricate tasks like crafting toys.
I haven't seen any accidents happen so far.
The rest of the pixies have much more experience than me, so they've learned to get it under control for the most part! Except for when a snow impling wanders in.
We love those little guys.
Maeve has been teaching me some breathing techniques, so hopefully I can be just as cool and collected as everyone else in no time!
Well, good luck with that!

conversations.section: In the Dwarven Mine

pages.x: Greetings and welcome to my pickaxe shop. Do you want to buy my premium quality pickaxes?

o: Are your pickaxes better than other pickaxes, then?
How is the wind power station working out?

pages.x: No, thank you.
Are your pickaxes better than other pickaxes, then?
Of course they are! My pickaxes are made of higher grade metal than your ordinary bronze pickaxes, allowing you to mine ore just that little bit faster.
How is the wind power station working out?
Very well, thank you. I had been worried about supply cutting out when the wind drops, but Bordiss has installed some kind of device to store power for those times.
It's far less smelly than the old power station, too!
It almost makes me want to go for a walk on the surface, and few things make an old dwarf like me want to go to the surface!

conversations.section: Before Birthright of the Dwarves

pages.x: That's odd, isn't this the office of the Red Axe?
No, quite clearly this is not. Can't you see the banner?
Hmm... it looks like some kind of orange flame.
Very clever, yes. That's us, that is. The Orange Flame.
But what are you doing here?
The Red Axe has committed treason. They have departed the city. We have clawed our way up from the rabble of the minor companies.
We're now wealthy enough to trade on the Trade Octagon.
Need any help with that at all?
That is a scandalous suggestion! Get out of here!

conversations.section: During tier 41 of Journey to Iaia / First time

pages.x: Greetings Player, what brings you here?
Hello Otavea. I've been sent to make sure you and your people are doing okay, under the circumstances.
That's much appreciated Player. There has been some trying times recently.
But there is hope on the horizon for our people, with new land for us and new generations in the future.
Speaking of. I'm in the process of running supplies from the mainland to the island you refer to as Anachronia.
Some of my ilujanka have began integrating into life on the island. Apparently rearing some mighty creatures, and 'pruning' some of the local fungi!
I have Luke the Gurh here with me. Could you put together a nice dish for him to eat? He's been working hard and needs to keep his energy up.
Just mix this redcane together with some fresh vegetables, that should perk him up!
On it!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Upon catching all god jadinkos for the week / Talking to Papa Mambo afterwards

pages.x: Heh heh heh. As you have caught all the special jadinkos, I's be giving you this extra special gift.

o: Which skill would you like to improve?
I'd like to improve my Farming.
I'd like to improve my Hunter.
I'd like to improve my Herblore.
I'll need to think about it for a moment. I'll come back when I've chosen.

pages.x: I'll need to think about it for a moment. I'll come back when I've chosen.
As you wish, but do not take long.
I'd like to improve my [Farming/Hunter/Herblore].
You be finding that the shaman clothes give you greater...experience, shall we say, for growing plants, finding jadinkos and making juju potions.
This gift will only last for half an hour, though.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Good day, good day. Come to admire the new parrot aviary have we?
It's very nice.
Isn't it just?
When did you add it?
Just recently. It would have been sooner, but some wretch thought it would be amusing to replace their drinking water with vodka.
The vet had to nurse them back to health for weeks!
What do you feed them?
Well, fruit and wheat mostly. I try to give them a balanced diet, but their favourite treat is pineapple chunks.

conversations.section: Livid Farm / Talk-to / With a witchdoctor camo outfit piece and without Mambo's potion before having drunk it

pages.x: Oh, hi. I heard word from Papa Mambo.
Oh? Yes, I've done some work down there on Karamja. How did you hear from him?
Lokar went to barter for some more seeds-
I doubt 'barter' is the correct term for it, but go on.
Apparently, Papa Mambo keeps talking about a great farmer called [Player] and he's really impressed with the way they have been managing the Jade Vine.
Hurrah for me!
It gets better. He handed Lokar a strange vial, which I'll now pass on to you! Apparently, it'll help increase your knowledge of Farming.

o: Pauline hands you a strange-looking vial.

pages.x: Thanks!

conversations.section: Farmer's Market / After feeding the rabbits

pages.x: Now what?
Now we wait...
Wait for what?
Well, we need those rabbits to reach adulthood, so we can use them as breeding stock to make more bunnies...and then bunnies equals monies!
How long will that take?
Well, you can either come back in around [number] minutes or...I know a way to kill some time, if you'd prefer...

pages.i: Advance time until rabbits reach adulthood?

pages.x: Time flies when you're having fun!
That was a lot more fun than I was expecting!

conversations.section: Starting out / Talking to Granny Potterington / First time (With requirements)

pages.x: Hello, random person wandering onto my farm. By any chance, do you know how many beans make five?
Wait, this is some sort of saying, isn't it? I think I might have heard this one... Something about two beans, half a bean, and another bean and, er...
Eh, close enough, I guess. You look like your fingers are at least a little bit green. You'll do.
Do for what? Wait, what did I just get myself into?
You are now my official farm hold partner. Get to work, [lad/lass]!
What just happened?
Just trust me, this'll be good for you. You can start by grabbing old Jack.
Jack?
Yeah, he's the old yak out back, baroo-ding by the breeding paddock - pick him up and bring him to me.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / At the Varrock Library / Player

pages.x: HEY PETE, WHAT ARE YOU DOING HERE?
Shhhh! It's a library you know!
Oh, sorry! So, what's new?
Not much, just doing some research on Dwarvern Culture.
Did you know that Keldagrim was originally constructed by a long lost clan who embraced the power of magic, and used it to aid with glorious buildings like the royal palace?
Really??
Yes. They even stayed down there for 1000 years or more, in a time they call 'The age of Kings'.
WOW!
Shhhh! That's enough history for one day I think!

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Hello. So you're just a private?
Show some respect! It's more than you'll achieve.
I beg to differ. I'm in perfect shape!
Prove it!
How?
Give me five star jumps!
Five sit-ups!
Run on the spot!
Okay. Maybe you have what it takes. Best you speak with the captain.

conversations.section: Historical dialogue / After completing the test

pages.x: Hello, Professor.
Ah, Player. How's the test going?
I think I've finished.
Excellent! Let me mark the paper for you, then.
Hmm. Uh-huh, yes, I see. Good! Yes, that's right.
Excellent! Allow me to reward you for your work. I have these two old lamps that you may find useful.
Also, there is an old jail block connected to the cells below the training centre, which have been overrun with vicious creatures.
If you search around the jail cells downstairs, you should find it easily enough.
Now, your rewards.

conversations.section: In Al Kharid / Talking to her

pages.x: Do you want to buy any armoured skirts? Designed especially for ladies who like to fight.

o: No, thank you, that's not my scene.
What do you think of Ali Morrisane?

pages.x: No, thank you, that's not my scene.
What do you think of Ali Morrisane?
He's a shifty man. Brought several men from his home town to try to set up shops here, or so he says.
But if they're just setting up shop, why does he need to send them around to threaten us?
One of them came here, waved his hammer around dangerously, and said things would be worse for us if we didn't join them!
What will you do about it?
I'm not going to let those thugs run me out of this town. So I'll just keep selling armoured skirts here. Would you like to buy any?

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Hello.
Hmmph.

o: What do you do around here?

pages.x: What do you do around here?
I wheel, I deal, I keep the money moving by offering prizes for hard earned spooky tokens.
What sort of stuff do you sell?
Hmmph. Costumes, weapons, prizes. Even some legitimate clan confections if you've got enough tokens.
Goodbye.
Yeah, yeah.
Hello there! Are you interested in buying one of my special team capes?
What do team capes do?
If you and your friends all wear the same team cape, you'll be less likely to attack your friends by accident, and you'll find it easier to attack everyone else.
They're very useful in Clan Wars and other player-vs-player combat areas where you might come across friends you don't want to harm.
So would you like to buy one?
No thanks.
No thanks.

conversations.section: Before Spirits of the Elid

pages.x: Come one, come all, buy my amazing choc ice invention here! Chocolate on the outside. Iced cream on the inside.
Oh I also have some chocolate left over from making choc ices which I'm selling too.

o: Cool, I'd like to buy some.
How do you stop your icy snacks melting?}}

pages.x: No thanks, I'm not interested.
How do you stop your icy snacks melting? The middle of the desert is the last place I'd expect to see ice.
It's quite a surprise, isn't it, my friend?
I actually have this special magic box of ice, which I bought for a princely sum from a strange man while adventuring in lands far away.
He said it is imbued with some sort of powerful ice
magic which keeps it cold all the time. I had never seen any ice magic before. It's clearly very rare and powerful, so I felt I had to buy it.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello.
Hello, traveller. Have a look at my latest range of gnome fashion. Rometti is the ultimate label in gnome high-society.
Really.
Pastels are all the rage this season.

o: Okay then, let's have a look.

pages.x: I've no time for fashion.
Hmm...I did wonder.
Okay then, let's have a look.

conversations.section: In the Miscellania and Etceteria dungeon

pages.x: Would you like to try some fine Miscellanian ale, your Royal Highness?
Well I say Miscellanian, but it's actually brewed on the mainland.
Would you like to try some anyway?

o: What's it like living down here?

pages.x: Yes, please.
No, thank you.
What's it like living down here?
Business is booming!
Now, if only I hadn't taken a loss to the beer I sold to those teenagers.

conversations.section: In Taverley / After Eadgar's Ruse

pages.x: What can I do for you young 'un?

o: Did you say you needed more goutweed?
I have some more goutweed for you.
ave you any more work for me, to help reclaim the circle?
Actually, I don't need to speak to you.

pages.x: Did you say you needed more goutweed?
I don't need any more goutweed for the ritual, but it's still quite difficult for me to get.
If you ever come across some, bring it to me; I'll exchange it for some other herbs.
I have some more goutweed for you.
Ah, good. Here are some herbs in exchange.
Have you any more work for me to help reclaim the stone circle?
Well, not right now I don't think young 'un. In fact, I need to make some preparations myself for the ritual. Rest assured, if I need any more help I will ask you again.

conversations.section: In Taverley / Before Druidic Ritual

pages.x: What can I do for you young 'un?
So... I've heard you druids might be able to teach me Herblore...
Herblore eh? You're probably best off talking to Kaqemeex about that; he's the best herblore teacher we currently have.
I believe at the moment he's at our stone circle just north of here.
'Course he's just the best teacher. You don't need him to show you how it works. Not like in my day.
Back then you had to go running all over the place before you so much as learned how to wipe muck off a leaf.
Still, that's what the kids are all like these days. No time to stop and listen to a teacher.
With their 'rune armour', and their 'chilly-chompers' and their loud music...
Uh... thanks?

conversations.section: At Brimhaven Dungeon entrance / Talking to Saniboch

pages.x: Good day to you bwana.

o: Can I go through that door please?
Where does this strange entrance lead?
I'm impressed, that tree is growing on that shed.

pages.x: Can I go through that door please?
Where does this strange entrance lead?
To a huge fearsome dungeon, populated by giants and strange dogs. Adventurers come from all around to explore its depths.
I know not what lies deeper in myself, for my skills in agility and woodcutting are inadequate.
Good day to you too.
I'm impressed, that tree is growing on that shed.
My employer tells me it is an uncommon sort of tree called the Fyburglars tree.

conversations.section: City Quest / Crop pests / Task #1

pages.x: Those pesky [monster] are eating my crops!
Well, that is a problem. Anything I can do to help?
Yes, I have a plan.
I believe if we coat the crops with some sort of disgusting mixture it will deter them.
Yeah, that seems reasonable.
First of all I need [number] of [item]. Could you get these for me?
You’ve done well.
Where could I find [item]?

conversations.section: After Tuai Leit's Own

pages.x: Thank you for your assistance in trying to cure my friend.
How are things going?

o: Is there anything for me to learn?

pages.x: We convinced the original necromancer to remove her curse not only from him, but many others who were affected by it.
She did so by tearing a piece of paper that was stuck on a jiangshi's forehead.
Poppycock! What drivel. I'm sure there must be some sort of physical or spiritual explanation behind all of this superstitious mystical twaddle.
Next you'll be trying to convince me of the benefits of homeopathic medicines, as if tigers' dangly bits ever did anyone any good.
Excuse my disbelief, though - I am most pleased that your friend has recovered.
Is there anything left for me to learn?

conversations.section: Talking to Shauna / After completing A Christmas Reunion / During a Christmas event

pages.x: You know, this workshop is much nicer than I was anticipating, based on the horror stories I'd heard.
Horror stories?
Oh yes. My dad Fionn would tell them around the bonfire in the Harvest Hollow, about his old days working in Diango's previous workshop.
Let's just say you would NOT want to have been around if Slim Louie and Fat Rocco found out that you painted a bauble the wrong colour.
Dad said even Diano had a nasty streak, like he was possessed by greed! I can't imagine.
Oh, yeah. I remember having to battle marionettes with him to get him to snap out of it.
Quite surprising that Santa still invited him here after that, really.
He seems to be fine now, though. And Cait's doing a wonderful job as union representative for us. Unlimited hot chocolate and gingerbread yeti breaks!
Living the dream!

Take a look.
No thanks.
Ok, well, if you change your mind, do pop back.
Didn't you once sell Silverlight?
Silverlight? Oh, Sir Prysin of Varrock explained that was a unique sword and told us to stop selling it.
If you want Silverlight and don't have it, you should speak to Gideon Bede.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Halt, adventurer! Go no further! Mortal, wormy peril lies within this cave!

o: Don't worry, I eat peril for breakfast.

(After Song from the Depths, if the player has destroyed their Remora's necklace:) I don't suppose you've seen a necklace lying about?

pages.x: Wormy indeed! The most unsightly, ghastly and smelly worms you could imagine have suddenly risen from a hidden network of underground caves!
But fear not! We, the Falador White Knights, have been officially dispatched on a mission to deal with this slithering menace!
I am the famous Sir Rebrum: hero of justice extraordinaire and destroyer of all things evil!
I know you'd love to hear about all my adventures, but I'm on duty here.
Most impressive! Carry on, then.
Why, yes I have! The Raptor passed by earlier. He said you might need it.
Why, yes I have! The Raptor passed by earlier. He said you might need it.

conversations.section: At the Daemonheim camp / Talk to / Unlocking Thok It To 'Em (saga)

pages.x: Greetings, Player. It's so nice to see you again! Have you come to hear a story?

pages.i: Tell Skaldrun about the badly scrawled note?

pages.x: I found this illegible note on the floor. Mean anything to you?
Oh, yes, I recognize that story!
This is a tale of daring heroism, staggering displays of strength and skill and, most importantly, a mighty Fremennik warrior called Thok.
Oh...and his brother Marmaros is in it too.

o: No, I'd like to discuss the dig site.

pages.x: No, not just yet.

conversations.section: At the Daemonheim camp / Talk to / Unlocking Thok Your Block Off (saga)

pages.x: Greetings, Player. It's so nice to see you again! Have you come to hear a story?

pages.i: Tell Skaldrun about the rock and twine bundle?

pages.x: I found this...thing...while exploring. I have no idea what it's for.
Oh my, it's magnificent!
In fact, it does remind me of a tale, one that involves the search for a lost weapon and two mighty brothers, Thok and Marmaros.
Perhaps you should hear of their earlier exploits first before I tell this tale.

o: No, I'd like to discuss the dig site.

pages.x: No, not just yet.

conversations.section: After Icthlarin's Little Helper

pages.x: Hi!
What do you want?
What's wrong?
Word has it that you very nearly spoiled our fun!
What, you're upset that I tried to put the high priest's soul to rest?
So that we could get back to work again? What makes you believe that he even deserves such a burial?
Doesn't everyone?
What, even those that gain through the blood, sweat, tears and misery of others?
I was just trying to help and, as it turns out, I've not achieved not a whole lot.

conversations.section: At Vorago's Borehole

pages.x: Fancy meeting you here, Player. Such a coincidence! Such a small world! But alas, you meet me as I am leaving.
The big paperweight, Vorago, and I have already finished our chat... if you could call it that. I will save you the dull and inevitable question.
I am here because he has killed a god, Tuska. So, I have invited him to my Big Game. Vorago will join Armadyl.
They both gain the chance of seizing the Stone of Jas, because they have both killed gods.
Hmmm, I wonder if there will be the opportunity to kill one bird with two stones?
I grow a little restless, to be frank. Things are going rather slowly. I feel I may have to speed things up.
Very little. But he will be at the Big Game. To defend Gielinor and the lifeforce of the world. I paraphrase, of course.
A delight as usual.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / Giving him a davy kebbit hat

pages.x: Oh, kebbit hat! That exactly what I always wanted. It would be perfect thing to keep wind out of hair.
What hair? You don't have any hair!
Are you going to give it or are you here to taunt me?

o: Sorry, I just brought it here to taunt you.

pages.x: Thank you very much. It fit like dream! My ears so warm now.
Glad you like it. It suits you to a 'T'.
Very grateful. I in your debt, human.
Sorry, I just brought it here to taunt you.
Harrumph. It good thing my ears too cold to hear you or I'd get real angry.

conversations.section: Talk to / During the "check in with the doc" task in Oasis Restoration event

pages.x: Hi!
Hi. How can I help?
Are you all okay, after - you know - the Duel Arena collapsed?
Oh quite. We've all been through much worse.
Really? Like what?
Well...there was...the pineapple incident.
What happened there?
We do not talk about it. EVER! I still hear the screams when I dream.
The horror! The sweet sticky horror!

conversations.section: After Tai Bwo Wannai Trio

pages.x: Hello, Tamayu, first son of Timfraku.
Stranger, why you have returned?
I'm just passing through.
Using your new found poison I have been creating spears. Would you like to buy some?
Yes.
No.
As you wish, stranger.

conversations.section: In Varrock

pages.x: Greetings friend. I am a manufacturer of leather.

o: Can I buy some leather then?
pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Can I buy some leather then?
I make leather from animal hides. Bring me some cowhides and I'll tan them into soft leather for you.
Leather is rather weak stuff.
Normal leather may be quite weak, but it's so easy to craft that anyone can work with it.
Alternatively you could try hard leather. It's not so easy to craft, but I only charge 3 gp per cowhide to prepare it, and it makes much sturdier armour.
I can also tan snake hides and dragonhides, suitable for crafting into the highest quality armour for rangers.
Thanks, I'll bear it in mind.

conversations.section: Talk-to

pages.x: Oh, hello. Have you got something you want preserving?
Yes please.
Give it to me to look at then.
Not right now.
Well, you go kill things so I can stuff them, eh?
What?
If you bring me a monster head or a very big fish, I can preserve it for you so you can mount it in your house.
I hear there are all sorts of exotic creatures in the Slayer Tower -- I'd like a chance to stuff one of them!

conversations.section: At the Void Knight Outpost, before Quiet Before the Swarm

pages.x: Hi, how can I help you?

pages.i: What do you want to say?

pages.x: Who are you?
I'm Terry.
Are you a Void Knight?
No. I want to be. My father was, but when he died fighting the pests, my mother forbade me from joining up.
What is this place?
This is the Void Knight Outpost. The Void Knights keep us all safe from the pests that are trying to invade. You should talk to one of them if you want to know more.
I'm fine, thanks.

conversations.section: Player-owned port bar

pages.x: What do you want?
How are things going with you, Ling?
I'm in need of someone with your skills...
Certainly. I would never turn down a chance to practice my skills.
Do you prefer to work alone?
How's the life of an assassin?
Not too different from yours, I'd imagine. We are both skilled killers, are we not? You know what a heavy burden that can be, but by only killing the deserving...
Well, that can help.

conversations.section: In the Orthen Oubliette / Post-kill dialogue

pages.x: We did it!
Thank you.
Is the supply of energy likely to be restored?
No. Kerapac's device was destroyed.
How?
Dramatically.
Then Raksha will likely not stir again.
He and I will sink once more into slumber.
Do you need anything else?

conversations.section: In Bar

pages.x: Good day. May the light of Saradomin guide you.
How are things, Tomlin?
I need something done, Tomlin.
Certainly, I'm the man to get it done.
Do you prefer to work alone?
How's the life of a missionary?
Our lives are not that dissimilar. We are both devout followers of the gods, although I'm not sure we follow the same one.
Whatever your faith, I can't help but admire your devotion. Your dedication to prayer and worship is inspiring.

conversations.section: After Koschei's Troubles

pages.x: Hey, Thorvald! Is everything okay here?
No, everything is not alright! Koschei turned out to be a powerful being known as a Mahjarrat! I heard arguing and popped my head down to see what was going on!
Saw the whole thing!
Yes, it's true. He's your friend, so I don't think he is a threat to you.
That's not what I am worried about.
Then what is the matter?
Who am I going to get to test the young Fremennik warriors now? No one else will volunteer to be attacked every day!
Maybe you should take his place: dress like him and fight in the trial. Since it is only a test of bravery, you can stop when they have proven themselves.
Ah, I see how you got Peer the Seer's vote now! You are wise indeed. Let's keep this little...arrangement between us.

conversations.section: At Mudskipper Point / After Birthright of the Dwarves while having Imcando pickaxe pieces in inventory

pages.x: A tingling in my Imcando bones! Can it really be...
Yes! You've found part of an ancient Imcando pickaxe! May I take a look at it?
It won't be easy, though. As well as the pieces, I'll need a gilded dragon pickaxe, and one million coins to buy other materials.
And a redberry pie, of course. Smithing makes me hungry!

o: I have those things with me now.

pages.x: I have those things with me now.
Excellent! Let me get to work.
An Imcando pickaxe?

conversations.section: Talk to / Conversation 1

pages.x: Hello? Is anyone there?
Ah, bonjour madam/monsieur!
You seem familiar?
I am - or at least I was - the Magnificent Monty: daredevil extraordinaire of the greatest flea circus in the lands.
You probably recognise me from my moustache. It's okay, I get it a lot.
Wow! What are you doing here?
I have left the circus - I had done it all: leapt through flaming rings, dived from the top of the Wizards' Tower, slew the King Black Dragon with my bare hands.
I started a new life here and so I came here to risk it all on the Stony Sea.
Impressive.

conversations.section: After River of Blood

pages.x: Hi, how are things in Meiyerditch now?
Better than they were, that's for sure. The vyrewatch have all cleared out and we're not tithed any more. It's still a slum, though. Life is still pretty hard here.
At least, whoever's in charge now is trying to improve things, though. Food and water are still pretty scarce, but it feels like it's getting better on that front too.
And then there's the people being returned. Family members long thought to be lost are coming home.
Do you know much about the new leaders?
Not much, really. Apparently, one of the Drakans is still in charge, but with all these improvements around here, I find that hard to believe.
There's a rumour going around that the fabled Queen Efaritay has returned to kick the vampyres out. And yet others that the Myreque won and now they're in charge.
The truth is somewhere between all of those things.
Good to know, thanks.

conversations.section: After Love Story

pages.x: Psst! My surveillance mission is complete, but I'm stuck in this tree. Can you chop the tree down, please?

pages.i: What would you like to say?

pages.x: Okay, I'll do that. Mind your legs.
Oof! Ouch! Owwie!
Yeow! Yeeowch! Yeeeouch!
Thank you so much! Please accept these coins as a sign of my gratitude.
Cheers!
Sorry, I'm busy.
Come again soon. I'm not going anywhere.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Oh! Hello, little bug. I don't often get visitors. What brings you here?

o: Are you related to the moai on Waiko?

pages.x: My name's Tuai Leit, but you can call me Sparkle.
I can, but I'm not going to.
Oh, Waiko. I love the sound of his voice. He's so dreamy.
No, we're not related. And he's married, the poor fool...to Aminishi, that ugly crone.
So you don't know where I could find any of their children?
Sorry, sweetie, can't help you there. They've not returned my calls lately. I hope Waiko is alright.
I bet Aminishi told him not to talk to me anymore. Jealous old cougar.

conversations.section: Magic / Talking to the Magic instructor / First time

pages.x: Good day, newcomer. Your journey is nearly at its end.
My name is Terrova. Before you leave for the mainland, I'm going to tell you a little about [Magic/Magic]. Let's start by opening your [spellbook/spellbook].
This is a list of your spells. Casting spells increases your [Magic/Magic] skill, and consumes runes, which you carry in your backpack.
You create runes with the [Runecrafting/Runecrafting] skill.
With a low [Magic/Magic] level, you can cast only the simplest spells, such as [Air Strike/Air Strike]. You must wield a magic weapon to cast combat spells.
You'll begin your adventure in [Burthorpe/Burthorpe], in the kingdom of [Asgarnia/Asgarnia].
The [Burthorpe/Burthorpe] imperial guard need an adventurer like yourself to defend the principality from [trolls/trolls] invading from the north.
I'm going to deactivate the protective spells around this island so you can [Home Teleport/Home Teleport] to [Burthorpe/Burthorpe] using the [Lodestone Network/Lodestone Network].
If you ever get lost, you can freely teleport to a lodestone you have discovered.

conversations.section: After As a First Resort

pages.x: Hi, human.
Hi, ogre.

o: Can you tell me about this stinky, green spring?

pages.x: Can you tell me about this stinky, green pool?
What you mean, stinky? It smell delightful!
Um, right. Semantics aside, can you tell me anything about it?
Oh, yeah, it very nice place to have bath. You smell pretty and mum say it refresh the soul.
What do you mean?
Well, it a bit confusing, but mum say that dat taking bath here is as good as goin’ to altar.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After All Fired Up / Before giving her a white fruit

pages.x: Hello, traveller! Could I impose on you for a moment?
What is it?
Well, I'm supposed to be looking after these beacons, but I'm utterly exhausted. Constantly scanning the horizon is hard work.
I've heard that the fruit from the White Tree can pep one up a bit. Is there any way you could bring me one? I'd be eternally grateful.

o: Sorry, I'm busy at the moment.

pages.x: I'd be happy to help. The safety of the kingdom is paramount, after all.
Thank you very much. I'm worried that if I carry on on this state, I might miss something important.
Sorry, I'm busy at the moment.
Ah, well. It costs nothing to ask.

conversations.section: In Keldagrim / After Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf / Without having completed Between a Rock...

pages.x: Hello, Player. What can I do for you?

o: Why don't we go for a beer and a kebab?
Do you have a quest for me?

pages.x: Why don't we go for a beer and a kebab?
Not now, Player. I'm on duty.
Do you have a quest for me?
There's nothing you can help me with.
If you really want something to do, I suppose you could help my father Dondakan with his mining problem.
He's been at it for years and hasn't got anywhere, though, so I don't know how much you'll achieve.
Nothing.

conversations.section: First time informing about Jhallan / After The Temple at Senntisten

pages.x: You told me how to thaw out the Muspah. I thought I should keep my part of the bargain.
Oh! So you have some information for me? I must record this!
To start with, the Muspah wasn't what it appeared to be.
It turned out to be alive all along, and once I'd freed it, it... changed. It told me it was a Mahjarrat.
It was quite a shock to suddenly see its head was a skull.
The Muspah creature was a Mahjarrat in disguise?
Yes, he's called Jhallan. He was incredibly weak and wanted to hibernate under the Mahjarrat ritual site.
I found him somewhere peaceful and put him back to sleep. Apparently the ritual will rejuvenate any Mahjarrat nearby.
Well, we know where to find him again, should we ever need to.
Hello there! Are you interested in buying one of my special team capes?
What do team capes do?
If you and your friends all wear the same team cape, you'll be less likely to attack your friends by accident, and you'll find it easier to attack everyone else.
They're very useful in the Wilderness and other player-vs-player combat areas where you might come across friends you don't want to harm.
So would you like to buy one?

o: Redirected to William's Wilderness Cape Shop

pages.x: No thanks.

conversations.section: Attempting to place a cannon on Zolarea

pages.x: Player? What are you doing?
Rosalina? How are you talking to me?
The contact spell. We've been through this.
I'm not sure that's how it works, but okay.
So, what were you doing?
Just, er, setting up this cannon here... I wanted to check out those meteorite cannonballs...
Really? After all the hospitality the star sprites showed you, and you're taking to shooting their planet?
I expected better of you. If any harm comes to just one of them...
No, ma'am. I'll take the cannon down right away.

conversations.section: Varrock

pages.x: Hello.
... whassup?
Are you alright?
... see... two of you... why there two of you?
There's only one of me, friend.
... no, two of you... you can't count...
Whatever you say, friend.
... giant hairy cabbages...

conversations.section: After Plague City, before Plague's End / While not wearing full Mourner gear / Conversation 1

pages.x: Hello, how's it going?
Life is tough.

o: Yes, living in a plague city must be hard.

pages.x: Yes, living in a plague city must be hard.
Plague? Pah, that's no excuse for the treatment we've received. It's obvious pretty quickly if someone has the plague.
I'm thinking about making a break for it. I'm perfectly healthy, not gonna infect anyone.
I'm sorry to hear that.
Well, ain't much either you or me can do about it.

conversations.section: In the Port Sarim jail / Talking to him

pages.x: Whut you want?

o: Sorry, thought this was a zoo.

pages.x: What are you in for?
Me not sure. Me pick some stuff up and take it away.
Well, did the stuff belong to you?
Umm...no.
Well, that would be why then.
Oh, right.
Sorry, thought this was a zoo.

conversations.section: Exchange mole bits / With mole bits / On a members' world, with the Falador hard tasks complete

pages.x: If I'm not mistaken, you've got some mole bits there! I'll trade them for bird nests, if you like. I also see that you're a shield holder; a champion of Falador, eh?
I'll throw some special seeds into the bargain.

o: Yes, I will trade the mole claws.
Okay, I will trade the mole skin.
Can I trade the mole nose?
I'd like to trade all three.

pages.x: Yes, I will trade the mole claws.
Okay, I will trade the mole skin.
If you don't plan on using those seeds, some of the other gardeners may be interested in them.
Can I trade the mole nose?
I'd like to trade both.
I'd like to trade all three.

conversations.section: Before mining the big sandstone boulder / When talked to / First time

pages.x: What are you doing over here?
The Pharaoh, along with a number of other benefactors, would like a cactus patch over in this corner.
Of course the location had to have a giant sandstone boulder sat on it...
Yeah...
Tell you what. If you construct the cactus patch for me, I'll let you use it to practice your farming skills.
Sounds fair. I could mine through that thing in no time at all.
Before I let you get started, Bring me 12 Acadia logs, and I'll work on a basic plot perimeter.
Only 12?
12 Acadia logs is fine. I'm not crafting the Dominion Tower!

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander, before The Mighty Fall / At the Champion's Guild

pages.x: Player! You're a member of the Champion's Guild too? This is great!

o: How did you become a member of the guild?
What do you think of the guild?

pages.x: How did you become a member of the guild?
I had to do a quest to prove myself. I had to slay a monsterbut the monster was the easy part! The hard part was getting there; everyone had lost the map.
What do you think of the guild?
It's alright, but I wouldn't want to stay here long. The Guildmaster never goes out on adventures , he just stands and greets people.
The champions downstairs aren't much better. They asked me to be the 'Cave Goblin Champion but I wasn't interested.
I don't want to spend all my time sitting and waiting for excitement to come to me. I want to get out there and find it!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / When using the right-click call-Over option

pages.x: Durrrr...
Hey! Come over here!
Who? Me?
Yes, you!
Give me a moment...I can't move that fast.
Why not?
I used to be a magician's assistant until the accident...
What accident?
Looook...

conversations.section: Fourth task / Returning to the Curator and asking about A Cultist's Journey

pages.x: Have you been to check on Johanhus yet?
Yes. I found him cowering at the edge of the Nodon Front.
It became all too apparent to him that humans were as much at risk as anyone.
He got a bit frightened, and decided to head on home.
I don't think he likes the Elder Gods much any more.
I see... We are fortunate that Johanhus is such a coward and a weakling. He has so much anger and hatred, but without any courage.
Let us hope that no-one with actual drive and courage adopts the mantle of the Elder Gods.
Thank you for all your help investigating this for me. It will surely make a great addition to my archives.

conversations.section: After One Piercing Note

pages.x: Welcome back, adventurer.

o: Is there anything I can do here?

pages.x: How is the abbey?
We're struggling, but not with anything dramatic. After the news of what happened got out, it's not surprising that we've had fewer applicants.
Hopefully things will return to normal in time. If not - well, there's nothing you can do.
Is there anything I can do here?
You're welcome to use our scriptorium to make your own illuminated copies of the Book of Saradomin. Use your book on the book-making stand to start.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: First conversation

pages.x: Ah, another human! Let me get a good look at you.
My, my... What a strange race you are. So tall and soft. Yet you present yourselves as our saviours.
Yes, I am Player. The saviour of your down-trodden race!
I am Player. I have come to offer my help, if you need it.
I am no saviour, I am Player. I come to your planet in search of its treasure.
Hm, is that so? Well, Player, we have much to discuss. I am the Acca of Kanatah, the wisest of this village. I can see you have questions, let us converse.

conversations.section: Offering a relic

pages.x: Is there something you wish to discuss, human?
Those relics are of great cultural significance to my people.
I can't afford to pay you for them, but if you were willing to part with them, I'd ensure that goebies everywhere knew that we were indebted to you.

o: If you hand over your relics, you will gain X reputation with the goebies.
Trade your X relics for X reputation?

pages.x: Thank you human. From all goebies, thank you.
Very well human. I wish I could compensate you adequately.

conversations.section: Gnome cooking training / Toad crunchies

pages.x: Hi, Mr Gianne.
Hello, Player. So what did you think of the book?
I'm not too sure about toad's legs.
They're a gnome delicacy, very tasty. Chicken tastes like toad's legs you know. You'll love them. If I give you what you need, can you make me some Toad Crunchies?
I'll give it a go.
Thanks.
The dough is made according to a secret family recipe. If you need any more, I suggest you speak to Hudo the grocer. He's very reliable.
Let me know how you get on.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: I can't believe that I've been made to wait so long.
What are you waiting for?
I have been waiting for an audience with the King for days!
Well, he's clearly a busy man.
Bah! I think he's just trying to insult the gnome nation, by making me wait. The cheek of these humans.
Just because they're vertically challenged they think they can ignore us.
I'm not ignoring you.
Hmm. I should be thankful for small mercies, I suppose.

conversations.section: At the Dig Site before departure / Talking to Laniakea

pages.x: A pleasure to meet you, Player.
I'm sorry, I don't think we've met.
You are right, we have not. But I have heard an awful lot about you.
My name is Laniakea and I am from the Order of the Slayer Masters.
King Roald reached out to the order for someone to help accompany you and a few archaeologists on this journey.
Pleasure to meet you Laniakea.
Is that so.
If you feel ready, board the boat and we begin at once.

conversations.section: On the beach at Anachronia / Talking to Laniakea

pages.x: Quite a sight, it's very interesting to see there is architecture here.
I certainly was not expecting that, it all looks well built so that excites me.
Why is that exciting?
Well Player, it means that there is or was once civilisation here. What secrets do they have? What knowledge do they possess that we do not?
More importantly, what new creatures or plantlife live here? They could yield types of poisons for me to toy with.
We should press on, Player. The beach does not feel very safe for now, we should bring a small party inland to find an area of relative safety to make camp.
Sounds like a good idea.
Of course.

conversations.section: Northeast of Varrock / Recruiting Anna as an Archaeology researcher

pages.x: Oh, hello, Guildmaster. I have a request... Could I sign up for your research team as a professor?
I thought you were independent of the museum and the guild.

Historically, yes, but due to the recent injection of funding, me needing a steady wage at the moment, and also that I think you'd be a good person to learn from, this seems like a good time to go legit.
I have lots of field experience, as you know.

pages.i: Recruit Anna as a research professor?

pages.x: Sure thing, Anna. Welcome aboard!
I won't let you down.
Hmm, let me think about it...

conversations.section: Talking to Aoife / After completing A Christmas Reunion / During a Christmas event

pages.x: Hi, Aoife! Can I help you out here with anything?
You sure can! I'm in charge of making sure the hot chocolate doesn't go bad.
Does it go bad that easily?
Easier than you'd think! There's a certain art to it.
Every so often, I'll call out which ingredient needs adding to the cauldron. That might be sugar, chocolate, milk, spices, or even firewood to keep the pot hot.
You can find everything nearby in the kitchen.
Otherwise just make sure to keep stirring!
Sounds easy enough. I'll get started!

conversations.section: In Burthorpe

pages.x: So many runes...
Are you alright?
Oh! Don't worry. I'm trying to learn about runes from Mistress Carwen. It's a fascinating subject!

o: What can you tell me about Runecrafting?

pages.x: There's so much to talk about! I'm just learning the ropes though. You'd be better off talking to Mistress Carwen.
As part of my duties I do help her by selling runes. Would you like to take a look?
Sure thing. If you ever need to get that magic flowing, don't be shy - come see us!

conversations.section: At lodestones / When talked to

pages.x: Player, just the person we're looking for. The Archaeology Guild is looking for new recruits.
Oh? Tell me more.
We've just recently received some serious funding, and we're in need of as much help as we can get.
Some of the core aspects of Archaeology are wealth, power, fame and stories.
Interested? I can take you to the campus right now to talk with the Acting Guildmaster, if you'd like?
If you'd like to make your own way there, you can find the Archaeology campus to the east of the Varrock lodestone.

conversations.section: Relics / Sacrificing the mortal cup / Interacting with the mysterious monolith / With the relic

pages.x: Amazing! You weren't pulled inside the monolith!
Wait! That was a possibility?
Um... Well, that's how Guildmaster Tony vanished. I probably should have been clearer about that part...
We've made it off limits to the rest of the guild's members...but there was something about how that relic drew you to it and how confident you were.
I just had a feeling things would work out this time...and look, I wasn't wrong.
Wow. How many interns have you been through?
I'm sorry, okay, don't judge me. We've been accident free since Tony's disappearance.
Anyway, let's see if you can tap into the monolith and access the power that relic contained.

conversations.section: After Desert Treasure

pages.x: Hello there.
Hello again.
Did you find any signs of that treasure yet?
Not as such, but I unleashed a powerful demon from its tomb in return for unbelievable magical power.
So no gold then?
Not as such, no. Sorry about that.
Aw... I was hoping to go abroad on holiday this year.
Maybe I'll go check out Karamja next, I hear there's treasure to be found there...

conversations.section: Food and healing / Talking to Digory

pages.x: Hello there!
Digory Popplewell, at your service! I must say you're looking very well, my friend – very well indeed!
Yes - and why not? The sun is shining, the air is sweet, and the sea is as blue as a maiden's eyes. A fine time to be alive, wouldn't you say? Haha!
There was a zombie attack!
Zombies? Hah, you certainly have a vivid imagination, my friend. Everyone knows you don't get things like that in Ashdale!
What am I doing? Not very much! Doing things is very bad for your health, you know. That's why I make it a policy to do as little as possible.
Goodbye, my friend!

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Do you want to use the balloon? Just so you know, some locations require special logs and high Firemaking skills.
No.
Who are you?
I am Assistant Brock. I serve under Auguste as his number two assistant.
Do you want to use the balloon?
No.

conversations.section: When talked to

pages.x: Hey there, can I help you?
Who are you?
I'm a runecrafting scholar in training, and currently an assistant to Cat.
What are you doing here?
These dunes have started to appear across Gielinor. I've been tasked with finding and removing them from the world.
I thought it would be a simple task, however every time we clear one, another pops up somewhere else!
Sometimes I wish I had super powers, at least that way I could have these removed in no time at all.

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Do you want to use the balloon? Just so you know, some locations require special logs and high Firemaking skills.
No.
Who are you?
I am Assistant Marrow. I'm working here part time while I study to be a doctor.
Do you want to use the balloon?
No.

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Do you want to use the balloon? Just so you know, some locations require special logs and high Firemaking skills.
No.
Who are you?
I am a serf. Assistant Serf to you! Auguste freed me and gave me this job.
Do you want to use the balloon?
No.

conversations.section: Talk-to option

pages.x: Do you want to use the balloon? Just so you know, some locations require special logs and high Firemaking skills.
No.
Who are you?
I am Stan. Auguste hired me to look after this balloon. I make sure people are prepared to fly.
Do you want to use the balloon?
No.

conversations.section: First time dialogue, or when golden rocks are toggled off

pages.x: Hey, you seem resourceful! Would you like to help me with a little project?
I need someone to help me track down all the parts of the statue that's supposed to sit on this plinth.
When the city was reverted to seed, the statue must have been compromised. The parts could be anywhere by now!
Great! From now on, while you're training any of the elf clan skills, you might find a golden rock.
If you find two rocks from the same skill, bring them here and add them to the statue plinth.
You don't have to find them all in Prifddinas. They could be anywhere, and found doing almost anything related to the clan skills.
And if you ever want to stop finding golden rocks, talk to me again and I'll do that for you.

conversations.section: After Family Crest / With the imbued family gauntlets or without any of the gauntlets / Talk-to option

pages.x: I have received word from my father of your assistance to our family in this matter. You have my thanks for restoring our honour.
Not a problem.
Yes well... Is there anything I can help you with?

o: Can you change my gauntlets for me?
Player: Can you change my gauntlets for me?

pages.x: No thanks.

conversations.section: After Kennith's Concerns

pages.x: Hello, Bailey, how are you doing? Is Kennith causing you any problems?
Hello again, Player. Don't worry about us; we're doing fine.
I've been living over here with these sea slugs for a long time - I'm not going to have any problems with one little child.
Are you sure? You know he can be quite a handful.
You worry too much! Kennith and I are getting on fine. In fact, he's helping me control the sea slugs.
Together we might even be able to drive the dratted things off this platform.
I'm glad to hear it! Anything that can help defeat the sea slugs is worthwhile.
We can but hope.

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Friend's son slowly dying / Task #1

pages.x: The teenage son of a good friend of mine is slowly dying. Now it is not the time to let the sands take him from us.
I appreciate it!

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.
Nevermind.
Nevermind.

conversations.section: Banker on Etceteria

pages.x: Hi there, can I help you with anything?
Is this a bank?
Why yes, what else would it be? Anything else?
Do you get many customers?
We're the only bank on these two islands, so business is pretty good. Anything else?
I'd like to access my bank account, please.
I'd like to check my PIN settings.
I'd like to see my collection box.

conversations.section: Day 6

pages.x: The slime is no more!
We couldn't have done it without your help!
Always happy to help!
Hey, Barry?
Yes?
Thanks for all the memories, we're really going to miss you.
It's been a crazy few days alright, we'll not be forgetting that anytime soon. You take care of yourself Player.
Thanks Barry.

conversations.section: Keldagrim

pages.x: Do you mind? You're in my home.
I'm sorry, should I have knocked?
Very funny, human.
We can't all live in plush houses, you know. But that doesn't mean us mining dwarves don't work hard.
Where do you do your mining?
Normally the coal mine to the north. We need a lot of coal to keep our steam engines going, you know.
Can I do a bit of mining there as well?
I'm not sure, but as long as no one notices I don't think anyone is going to care.

conversations.section: Fort Forinthry / Talk to / Not building the Grove / For the first time before talking about Oak

pages.x: Hello Bill, how is everything?
Good, good. Those new outer fortifications have been holding up well and nothing new has come up since we got those in place.
Although actually...
Yes Bill, is something wrong?
A visitor arrived earlier today to speak with you.
I see, well if the guards allowed them in, then that doesn't seem too concerning?
Yes, your grace, but since they arrived they've been very fixated on the tree outside the chapel.
Hmm, I see. Thanks Bill, I'll go see what they're so interested in.

conversations.section: Highest reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here are your bars!

o: The Director replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Guthix be praised!
I am well pleased with your work, Player!
You are a true asset to the Blue Opal!
You never fail to satisfy, Player!
I will get my secretary to send this to the trade floor at once!

conversations.section: High reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Wonderful! I will personally oversee that it goes to the trade floor on time!
Well done, well done!
I knew you were the right human for the job!
Thanks, I will make sure the director hears of your expeditiousness!
You're always reliable, Player!

conversations.section: Low reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: How unusual for you, but it is appreciated nonetheless.
The Blue Opal is pleased that the trust it put in you has not been put to shame after all.
That is quite a pleasant and unexpected surprise.
Perhaps I was wrong about you after all...
Thanks... I suppose.

conversations.section: Medium reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: I have to admit, I was worried for a moment, but I'm glad to see you came through for us.
I am happy to see that the trust we put in you has not been in vain.
And not a minute too late as well. Well done.
The Blue Opal recognizes your performance.
That's good to hear, thanks.

conversations.section: Wisdom / Wisdom 6

pages.x: Nothing interesting happens.
Eh? That's hardly useful.
Ahh, but you see. It does all sorts of wondrous things.
Like what?
Well it's more to do with what happens when you hear that being said. You see, something interesting happens somewhere else.
So what you're saying is that if nothing interesting happens to me, then something interesting is happening for someone else that IS interesting?
Yes, that’s about it.
OK…I see… I think.

conversations.section: Before Tower of Life

pages.x: Hi there.
A'up, how's it gowin'?
Not bad, thank you.
What are you building here?
Nowt at moment. We're on strike!
You're on strike? Whatever for?
Those strange alchemists are up ta somefin', best go ta one ov 'em.
Oh, okay.

conversations.section: Highest reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here are your bars!

o: The Director replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Guthix be praised!
I am well pleased with your work, Player!
You are a true asset to the Brown Engine!
You never fail to satisfy, Player!
I will get my secretary to send this to the trade floor at once!

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Wonderful! I will personally oversee that it goes to the trade floor on time!
Well done, well done!
I knew you were the right human for the job!
Thanks, I will make sure the director hears of your expeditiousness!
You're always reliable, Player!

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: How unusual for you, but it is appreciated nonetheless.
The Brown Engine is pleased that the trust it put in you has not been put to shame after all.
That is quite a pleasant and unexpected surprise.
Perhaps I was wrong about you after all...
Thanks... I suppose.
