pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: I have to admit, I was worried for a moment, but I'm glad to see you came through for us.
I am happy to see that the trust we put in you has not been in vain.
And not a minute too late as well. Well done.
The Brown Engine recognizes your performance.
That's good to hear, thanks.

conversations.section: Before Ritual of the Mahjarrat

pages.x: Hey there!
Urgh.
What's wrong?
I've been checking out local tourist destinations and somehow I ended up in the Misthalin Training Centre of Excellence; I've spent the morning eating the professors' chocolate cake.
So you're saying you slithered, like a serpent, into the school kitchen and ate the professor's personal snack?
You're a disgusting criminal, aren't you?

conversations.section: On Lunar Isle

pages.x: Hi.
And you're wanting what now?

o: Can you take me back to Rellekka please?

pages.x: Can you take me back to Rellekka please?
I'll take you as far as Pirates' Cove. You'll have to find the rest of the way back yourself.
So we're here?
Yep. You're free to explore the island. Be careful though, the Moon Clan are very powerful, it wouldn't be wise to wrong them.
Thanks, keep that seal of passage close.

conversations.section: First time

pages.x: Hey, I'm Charity. For a limited time only, I'll be the host of the interactive trivia game, The Drop!
Sounds great! How does it work?
You'll be asked a series of RuneScape themed questions. Answer every question correctly and you'll bag yourself a nice reward.
Each time you play, Jagex will donate £1 to charity, up to a whopping maximum of £34,500! I know what you're thinking. Why are they giving all of that money to me?
... Anyway, how do I take part?
I'll announce each time The Drop opens. You'll then have 2 minutes to join before the game starts.
Thanks!
Talk to me again for more information, or use the 'Quick join' option to jump straight into the game!

conversations.section: In Varrock / Historical dialogue prior to 13 February 2017

pages.x: Spare some change, guv?

o: Is there anything down this alleyway?

pages.x: Is there anything down this alleyway?
The ruthless and notorious criminal gang known as the Black Arm Gang have their headquarters down there.

o: Do you think they would let me join?

pages.x: Thanks for the warning!
Don't worry about it.

o: Player: Do you think they would let me join?

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello, little fluffy wuffy bunny wabbit. Where's the tea party going to be?
Hello?
Skippety skoppety. Yes, Mrs Badger, I'm going to make some wongleberry jam.
Mrs Badger? What's a wongleberry?
Don't worry, Mrs Badger, I'm sure he'll be a good rabbit. Otherwise he won't get his birthday treat.
I'm not sure I want to know this.
Wongleberry and buttercream trifle with sparkly sparklegums on top! Wongliscious.
Wongliscious indeed.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Hello, welcome to the Civic Office of West Ardougne. How can I help you?
Who is through that door?
The city warder Bravek is in there.
Can I go in?
He has asked not to be disturbed.
I'm just looking thanks.

conversations.section: 2017 Halloween event / Starting out / After the first meeting

pages.x: Okay, so what do I do and where should I start?
To start yourself off, I would suggest you search around Edgeville for a restless spirit. You'll know it when you see it.
Once you have helped five ghosts to move on, return to me and I shall reward you for your efforts.
After which, there are four MORE ghosts to fine, and then you may assist me with one final task for an additional reward.
And as for what to do, that will vary depending on the story the ghost wishes you to know. Simply talk to them and figure it out.
Your quest journal has hints that point towards their last known locations.
Oh, so I'll need a way to talk to ghosts too?
Typically, one might, but while assisting me, you will inherently understand the ghosts I seek. Consider it a perk of the job.

conversations.section: In Yanille

pages.x: Who goes there? Friend or foe?

o: Why is this town so heavily defended?

pages.x: Friend.
Ok good to hear it.
Foe!
Oh righty...
Why is this town so heavily defended?
Yanille is on the southwest border of Kandarin, Beyond here you go into the Feldip hills which is major Ogre territory. Our job is to defend Yanille from the ogres.

conversations.section: After Sheep Herder and before Plague's End / While not wearing full Mourner gear

pages.x: Hello again sir.
Well hello again adventurer! How are you today?
Fine thank you. And yourself?
MUCH better now that I don't have to worry about those horribly discoloured sheep spreading the plague.
Although we still have plenty to worry about!
Like what?
Well, you never know what will happen. Not so long ago two gods turned up in Lumbridge and started fighting.
I'd hate to think of that happening here! Have you seen how they left the castle?

conversations.section: Historical dialogue

pages.x: Welcome to Varrock Museum!

o: Do you know where I could find any treasure?
Talk about the master quest cape.

pages.x: Have you any interesting news?
Yes, we found a rather interesting island to the north of Morytania. We believe that it may be of archaeological significance.
Oh? That sounds interesting.
Indeed. I suspect we'll be looking for qualified archaeologists once we have built the transport we need to get there.
Would I qualify then?

conversations.section: Talking to Fred Swarbrick

pages.x: What do you want?
Hmph!
I'm catching Davio with an invisible net! What's it look like I'm doing? I'm sitting here by the lake and trying to enjoy some peace and quiet.
Eh?
There's only one Fred Swarbrick on this island, and that's me. My family has been in Davendale for generations, and don't you forget it!
Hmph.

conversations.section: Talking to Mayor Druss Daven

pages.x: Wanderer! I saw you arrive from my humble mansion on the hill! I'm Mayor Daven of Davendale, but you can call me Druss.

o: You spotted me, but not the trolls?

pages.x: Trolls? Bwa-ha-ha! Imagine a troll - a mountain troll! - trying to swim to our little island. You almost had me there.
Trolls? Hardly, my good friend! It's why my ancestors moved here. Mountain trolls can't get us here. Not across miles of water.
Lovely to meet you too! Such manners are rare, don't you find?
Hmm, that's odd. Perhaps it was Martin, the fishmonger. You see him wearing big waders on his way to the beach sometimes.
Now, join me in the centre of Davendale, and I'll give you the grand tour.

conversations.section: Talking to Mayor Druss Daven at Davendale Square / First time

pages.x: Welcome to Davendale Square. Perhaps we could persuade you to stay with us.
That fair mansion on the hill is mine.
It's been standing since the Fourth Age, don't you know.
Great gods. Are those trolls?
You can probably tell that Davendale is out of its depth.But I know this village. We get things done. We just need to be shown how.
Inspire us. Fight the trolls near my mansion. My daughter, Zafir, will lend you our family's sword. Once we've seen how it's done, Davendale will rally behind you.
Inspiration doesn't have to come from combat. You could choose to cook fish for the wounded to eat. I've sent Martin to the lake, to collect them.
Either task, Combat or Cooking, will raise our fighting spirit. Choose one, or choose both!

conversations.section: Before Recipe for Disaster

pages.x: What are you doing in my house?

o: I want to use your kitchen.

pages.x: I'm just wandering around.
Would you mind wandering out of my house?
I want to use your kitchen.
I suppose you can, but try not to make a mess.
Give me all your money!
I haven't got any money!

conversations.section: First conversation

pages.x: Hello there. I don't think I've seen you here before.
Oh, Dondakan's employed me recently. He needs a ship to take all his gold to the city.
The city? Can you take me there?
There is only space on my boat for two things... me, and the gold. But if you want, I can take your gold ore to the city and bring it to the bank.
That's a good service! Will it cost me anything?
Only a little bit. One piece of gold ore for every shipment, and one piece of gold ore for every five pieces of ore on top of that.
So... if I had ten pieces of ore, how much would you take?
That would be three pieces. One for the shipment, two for the load. Seven pieces would go into your bank account. So, are you interested?

conversations.section: Miners near mining sites for Doric and Son

pages.x: Hello, boss. No need to check up on me. I'm working hard on keeping Doric & Son fully stocked in ore.
Oh, you know; I can't complain. I have a pickaxe and there's plenty of ore. What's to complain about?
Thank you, will do. Mining's what I do; can't get enough of it. Point me to some ore and I'm there.
Oh, yes. I've seen plenty of exciting things around here today.
Does most of these exciting things involve rocks?
Of course. Every rock is different and it's a wonder to see what comes from each one.
If you say so.

conversations.section: Leaving the tutorial / Talking to Vicendithas / First time

pages.x: Excellent. See how it feels, that strange crackle as it tries to siphon knowledge out of the air?
Now we need to give it something to feast on, to allow its potential to manifest.
That's where this comes in.

This incubator will flood that effigy with cosmic energy allowing it to transform into a more or less complete effigy and the excess energy from that process I can use to capture fragments of my father's knowledge in my own effigy.
We both benefit.
Before we can do that though, we'll need to power up the machine. This won't be simple, you and I will need to work together to get this up and running.
There are a number of valves which modify the energy flow within the incubator. I'll need to monitor the incubator and I will shout out what valves you need to pull.
Turn the [Colour] valve.

conversations.section: Dialogue

pages.x: Ooh, I'm all dizzy...
Why's that?
Well, watching that wheel go round and round and round...
and round and round and round...
Looks like you need a bit of a rest.
and round and round and round again...
See you around!
Very funny.

conversations.section: Wintumber Warmer / During the event / Talk to

pages.x: Uh... Hello there.
What are you doing here?
Chad said that they needed some help running the celebration so I tagged along.
What's going on around you then?
Oh! We're summoning pretty fire spirits using special fire stones.
That sounds like a lot of fun.

conversations.section: Dialogue

pages.x: Hi there.
Hey.
Why, I'm an esteemed farmer and tree surgeon, Farmer Jimbo! People from far and wide request my help in healing and protecting their farming endeavours.
I've even had requests from kings and queens before!
Goodbye

conversations.section: In the Miscellania and Etceteria dungeon

pages.x: Good day, sir.
What are you doing down here?
Shoring up the walls.
What does that do?
Stops them falling down.
Oh, I see.
Aye. If you want to chatter, you'd better talk to Thorodin over there. I'm working.
Okay then.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Ready to head back?

o: No, I'll stay a little longer.

pages.x: Although, saying that, I wouldn't mind getting my hands on that beastie in the pool. She'd make a meal fit for a kingdom.
I might need a bigger rod though!
There's great fishing to be had here. The tropical trout are frisky, but just the thing for cooking up a tasty summer treat.
Those ships are feisty ones! They're looking for something to fight.
If you have any battleships you can pit them against one of the pirate ships but beware, the pirates never lose!

conversations.section: Before Throne of Miscellania

pages.x: Hello.
Good day. What are you doing?
I'm selling flowers, 15gp for three. Would you like some?
Yes, please.
Thank you! Here you go.
No, thank you.

conversations.section: At Gertrude's House / With a cat in the bank

pages.x: Hello Fluffs.
Purrrrr. So, you can talk to cats now?
Yes, I got this amulet from a Sphinx.
Well, I should thank you for finding my kittens that time. I have a terrible time keeping track of them and I never know how many Gertrude has managed to sell.
They're cute little creatures, aren't they? I've got one in my bank.
You've put one of my children in your bank?
It's fine in there, honest!
Hisss!

conversations.section: Interact / Conversation 3

pages.x: Hello there.
Hello to you too. Isn't it a wonderful day?
It seems very nice, yes.
Not nice! It is wonderful!
If you say so...
NO! I'LL GNAW YOU GOOD! SAY THAT IT'S WONDERFUL! NOW!
Okay, okay! It's a wonderful day.
Yah! Wonderful days are nice!

conversations.section: After King of the Dwarves / Using a gilded pickaxe on Foreman Jaak

pages.x: Do you want me to remove the gold from that pickaxe?
Yes, please.

o: Foreman Jaak removes the gold from the pickaxe.

pages.x: There you go. Now you can mine without hurting everyone's eyes.
No, thanks.
Well, keep that thing away from me, then. I can't stand the...tackiness.

conversations.section: After Death Plateau

pages.x: Hello, Freda.
Hello there. I heard from some of the boys in town that you really gave those trolls a thrashing!
You keep it up. Every little helps.
I will!
Anything else you need?

o: Aren't you afraid of the trolls up here?
Can I buy some Climbing boots?

pages.x: I don't see why not. Let me see what I've got in your size.

conversations.section: After asking how to help

pages.x: Hello.
Hey there! How is the work coming?

o: Could you remind me what I have to do?
Do you have a knife I can use?
Do you have a hammer I can use?
It's not going too well, I'm afraid.

pages.x: It's going great!
Wonderful! Keep up the good work.
It's not going too well, I'm afraid.
What kind of attitude is that? You need to work harder, that's all.

conversations.section: In Port Sarim

pages.x: Welcome! You can buy fishing equipment at my store. We'll also buy anything you catch off you.

o: I want to find out how to catch a lava eel.
I've lost my oily fishing rod.
Let's see what you've got then.

pages.x: Lava eels, eh? That's a tricky one, that is. You'll need a lava-proof fishing rod.
The method for making this would be to take an ordinary fishing rod, and then cover it with fire-proof blamish oil.
So where can I fish lava eels?
Taverley dungeon or the lava maze in the Wilderness.
Let's see what you've got then.
Sorry, I'm not interested.

conversations.section: Before Ghosts Ahoy / With an amulet of ghostspeak

pages.x: All visitors to Port Phasmatys must pay a toll charge of 2 Ectotokens.

o: I would like to enter Port Phasmatys - here's 2 Ectotokens.
I'm not paying you Ectotokens just to go through a gate.

pages.x: I would like to enter Port Phasmatys - here's 2 Ectotokens.
I'm not paying you Ectotokens just to go through a gate.
Sorry - it's Town Policy.
Where can I get Ectotokens?
You need to go to the Temple and earn some. Talk to the disciples - they will tell you how.

conversations.section: In the Tree Gnome Stronghold / On the advanced route

pages.x: Wow, nice to see experienced people taking it to the next level of training.
Thanks. So this is the advanced route the other gnomes are talking about?
It sure is. You've already made the climb up here, now all you need to do is run across this sign here.
Seriously?
Oh yes, totally. When you've made it across, look for the swings to get to the northern section.
When you land from them, try to vault the branches into the pipe and you should slide out to the finish line!
And will I still have my legs intact when I've done all this?
Yes. Of course.

conversations.section: Speaking to the male gnome traveller

pages.x: Hello there! What're you doing in the city?
Why do you want to know?
I was just wondering. I thought this was a dwarven city, not a gnome city.
It's not a human city either, but you're here all the same.
Fair point.
Anyway, we're here to do some business with one of the companies of the Consortium. Getting supplies for our people back at, er, the Grand Tree.
What kind of special supplies do the dwarves have that you need then?
Oh, nothing special, nothing special I assure you... it's just that the dwarves have everything in large supplies.

conversations.section: In the Tree Gnome Village, after The Prisoner of Glouphrie / First time dialogue

pages.x: Thanks again for aiding me in my father's rescue, Player. While he gets back to full health, I've decided to stay in the Tree Gnome Village and care for him.
I thought I'd use the time to train up as a tree whisperer. If you have any spirit tree seeds, then I can keep them for you.
I study them as part of my training, and you can get them back whenever you need them!
Uncle Bolren also allowed Belmondo to establish a gilder route to the village.
Belmondo won him over with stories of his landing in the Galarpos Mountains and they've become fast friends since.
Bolren's no longer worried about having a flightpath so close to the village - as long as Belmondo's operating the line, of course!
I get all the men of my life close to me: my dad, my husband, my son and even my uncle!
Lucky lady, right?

conversations.section: In the Tree Gnome Village, after The Prisoner of Glouphrie / Subsequent dialogue / Without any spirit seeds stored with Golrana, or in backpack

pages.x: Hey, Player! Have you come to bring me some spirit tree seeds? I'll keep them for you.
How very unlike an adventurer! It's appreciated, of course.
Dad's well; he's upstairs, recovering from his ordeal in Arposandra, and he's already planning the next step of his revenge, bless him.
We visit mum's grave every weekend, too.
Golrie's back in the cave, and I'm holding back his allowance until he's organised it all.
My training's going well; the spirit trees quite like me, although they tell me that you are a great whisperer yourself.
I'm starting to think that perhaps - but only perhaps - you may be as good an adventurer as me. And that's about it!
Glad to know it's all going okay. I'll see you later.

conversations.section: Highest reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here are your bars!

o: The Director replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Guthix be praised!
I am well pleased with your work, Player!
You are a true asset to the Green Gemstone!
You never fail to satisfy, Player!
I will get my secretary to send this to the trade floor at once!

conversations.section: High reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Wonderful! I will personally oversee that it goes to the trade floor on time!
Well done, well done!
I knew you were the right human for the job!
Thanks, I will make sure the director hears of your expeditiousness!
You're always reliable, Player!

conversations.section: Low reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: How unusual for you, but it is appreciated nonetheless.
The Green Gemstone is pleased that the trust it put in you has not been put to shame after all.
That is quite a pleasant and unexpected surprise.
Perhaps I was wrong about you after all...
Thanks... I suppose.

conversations.section: Medium reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: I have to admit, I was worried for a moment, but I'm glad to see you came through for us.
I am happy to see that the trust we put in you has not been in vain.
And not a minute too late as well. Well done.
The Green Gemstone recognizes your performance.
That's good to hear, thanks.

conversations.section: After As a First Resort

pages.x: Hi, human.
Hi, ogre.

o: Can you tell me about this mud pool?

pages.x: Can you tell me about this mud pool?
Dat my favourite pool, dat is! It nice and sticky mud, very warm and comfy. It de muddiest mud around!
The muddiest mud?
Plus, if you lie in de mud for a while, it much easier to sneaky-sneak hunt de creatures. De mud, it cover your awful human stink!
Huh! I'll have to try that sometime.

conversations.section: In the Port Sarim jail / During the Port Sarim Invasion / Afterwards

pages.x: Right then, so, how can I help out?
There's a bunch of stuff you can help us out with.
First and most obvious, you can take out the Skulls' landing parties.
My guards are doing what they can to keep them outside of the jail, but they need support from more experienced fighters.
Jed's ship is pounding the prison. Do what you can to repair the old lighthouse tower - if that thing falls it'll collapse the whole prison.
We also have a cannon up on the roof. If you have any experience in making things explode at a distance, you might want to muck in with that.
And of course, that cannon needs feeding with ammunition.
There are some portable furnaces and a mixing table on the jail roof, so if you can smith us some cannonballs or mix black powder, that'd be a big help.

conversations.section: If sided with the Guardians / After Desperate Measures

pages.x: Kerapac has been dealt with. He is no longer a threat to Gielinor.
And the staff?
I didn't see it, but I believe it is now, once again, in the possession of its creators.
Armadyl has it?
I think you should ask Armadyl for more information on the current situation.
I'm afraid the stakes are much higher than they were when it was only Lucien you had to worry about.
Be of good cheer! With Armadyl's victory over the vile and vicious Bandos, his power waxes mightier than ever.
He will prevail in the end - whatever comes - and usher in a new era of peace.

conversations.section: If sided with the Guardians / After The Bird and the Beast

pages.x: I met Armadyl, he's returned to Gielinor!
He's back?!
Yes, I saw him with my own eyes. The other gods have returned too, they were all gathered at the Empyrean Citadel.
Armadyl's seat of power! This is... Wonderous news! What of the staff, adventurer?
The staff has changed hands, it's now in the possession of Sliske.
Once again the staff is held by a Mahjarrat, this is grave news. I am sure Armadyl will find a way to remove it from his clutches.
Be of good cheer! With Armadyl's victory over the vile and vicious Bandos, his power waxes mightier than ever.
He will prevail in the end - whatever comes - and usher in a new era of peace.

conversations.section: Talk to / Normally

pages.x: Oh *omnom* hi Player!

o: How can I get spring tokens?

pages.x: How can I get spring tokens?
*omnom* Various activities around the Blooming *om* Burrow will offer spring tokens as a reward for helping out!
You could work at the factory for a while *omnomnom*, or check out the chocolate mine, the foiling station, or the chocolate rabbit burrows.
*omnom* Oh, and there's carrot boating and beekeeping too! *omnom*
Bye, Gummy!
Bye *omnom* bye!

conversations.section: After completing Guys and Dolls

pages.x: How're those coloured logs working out for ya?
The variety of colours is doing wonders for my pale complexion!
I can see that...through you. So, what can I do here to help?
Well, you were always free to bring and burn your own logs. You can get spooky tokens and other Halloween stuff while doing so, because I'm generous like that.
But seeing how you helped me out, you are also welcome to make use of Dolly's coloured logs too, so you don't need to bring your own.
I've placed baskets containing each of the five different log colours around the edges of the bonfire. Burn whichever you like!
Though, if you move around to match the logs you're burning to the current colour of the bonfire, it'll be more rewarding.
Right, so when the bonfire changes colour, I move to burn the logs that match that colour. Well, that sounds simple enough. Thanks, Guy!

conversations.section: Having your story told back to you / Regicide

pages.x: Not your finest hour in the history books...
Unfortunately, you were led to believe Iorwerth to be on the side of good, and you learnt of explosives, which you used to kill King Tyras.
Ah, yes, not my greatest moment, indeed.
Maybe not, but at least the truth came out.
As you came to report this news to King Lathas, Arianwyn intercepted you, revealed the lie and how it was good in a way, as you had earnt the trust of King Lathas.
This would allow you
to infiltrate deeper into this conspiracy than any elf could.
Need help with anything else?

conversations.section: In the Miscellania and Etceteria dungeon

pages.x: Welcome to Miscellania's first clothing store! We sell clothing made especially for Fremenniks and Dwarves.
Can I help you with anything, your Royal Highness?

o: I'd like to look at what you have for sale.
What's it like living down here?

pages.x: I'd like to look at what you have for sale.
No thank you, I'm fine.
What's it like living down here?
It's very spacious down here. One of the dwarves said that the caves go on for miles!
The only problem I find is that the lighting's not very good, which means I make mistakes when cutting cloth.

conversations.section: In West Ardougne, after Plague City and before Plague's End / Without full Mourner gear equipped

pages.x: How did you get into West Ardougne? Ah well you'll have to stay, can't risk you spreading the plague outside.

o: I haven't got the plague though.

pages.x: So what's a mourner?
We're working for King Lathas of East Ardougne trying to contain the accursed plague sweeping West Ardougne. We also do our best to ease these people's suffering.
We're nicknamed mourners because we spend a lot of time at plague victim funerals, no-one else is allowed to risk the funerals.
It's a demanding job, and we get little thanks from the people here.
I haven't got the plague though.
Can't risk you being a carrier. That protective clothing you have isn't regulation issue. It won't meet safety standards.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue after Swan Song

pages.x: Hiya Hermie!
Ah, Player! How's the fishing going?
Still working on it. How's the Colony?
Flourishing, now that the colonists are coming back! Soon all the finest restaurants will be serving monkfish!
It's a pity those skeletons you brought here haven't gone away again, though. They're in the dormitories, which is rather annoying!
So please take a little time to kick 'em around a bit.
Oh, and please don't call me Hermie.
Whatever you like, Hermie!

conversations.section: In Keldagrim marketplace / Minitask dialogue

pages.x: Hello! I’ve got a little quest for you, are you interested?

o: No, quests are dull and boring.

pages.x: Yes, I love quests!
That’s the spirit! Now, what I need is [item]. And I need them within [number] minutes as well.
Not much of a quest, but I’ll do it. Just [item] in [number] minutes.
No, quests are dull and boring.
Don’t be so dismissive, you didn’t even hear what I wanted to ask you!
I don’t want to! I just want to kill things!

conversations.section: Before Witch's Potion

pages.x: What could you want with an old woman like me?
You look like a witch.
Yes, I suppose I'm not being very subtle about it. I fear I may get a visit from the witch hunters of Falador before long.
Nothing, thanks.
I'm looking for work.
Hmmm... Perhaps you could do something that would help both of us.
Would you like to become more proficient in the dark arts?

conversations.section: On Entrana / Having lost the ice gloves from Heroes' Quest

pages.x: Many greetings. Welcome to our fair island.

o: Have you seen a pair of ice gloves?

pages.x: By which you mean the pair of mythical gloves you stole from the cold dead body of the Queen of the Ice?
Er...
The gloves that you acquired to aid you in plucking the Entranan firebird? Another victim of your murderous nature, I should add.
The ice gloves that, from context, I would assume you have lost, if not carelessly discarded?
Those ice gloves, yes.
One of my monks found these gloves. If only to spare this world from further carnage, I return them to you.

conversations.section: After As a First Resort

pages.x: Hi, human.
Hi, ogre.

o: Can you tell me about this mud pool?

pages.x: Can you tell me about this mud pool?
Dat my favourite pool, dat is! It nice and sticky mud, very warm and comfy. It de muddiest mud around!
The muddiest mud?
Plus, if you lie in de mud for a while, it much easier to sneaky-sneak hunt de creatures. De mud, it cover your awful human stink!
Huh! I'll have to try that sometime.

conversations.section: At the Void Knight Outpost, before Quiet Before the Swarm

pages.x: Hi, how can I help you?

pages.i: What do you want to say?

pages.x: Who are you?
I'm Jessika. I'm a mage from the Wizards' Tower, doing research on pests.
What is this place?
This is the Void Knight Outpost. For some reason there is a disturbance in these islands and pests come through portals. I'm studying those portals.
You should talk to one of the Void Knights if you want to know more.
I'm fine, thanks.

conversations.section: City Quest / Crondis is angry / Task #1

pages.x: The magnificent Crondis has been angered by [monster]. She requires a blood sacrifice and a tribute.
First, go and kill [number] [monster].
What have the [monster] done to anger the almighty Crondis?
You don't need to know. Will you go to kill them?
My appreciation.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.

conversations.section: City Quest / War effort / Task #3

pages.x: Now is the time you have been waiting for, soldier! The killing!
We will finally vanquish our dreaded enemy, the [monster]!
What?
Yes, kill [number] [monster] in the name of the Pharaoh himself!
My appreciation.

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Nevermind.

conversations.section: Sitting in the Long Drop chair / After A Clockwork Syringe but before Pieces of Hate

pages.x: What'll it be?
A Long Drop.
Ye sure?
Aye, drop me...
Take a seat.
Er, nothing?
Then stop tryin' te take up me table space!

conversations.section: After Family Crest / With the imbued family gauntlets or without any of the gauntlets / Talk-to option

pages.x: Hello again. My family now considers you a hero.
Maybe because… I am.
Yes well... Is there anything I can help you with?

o: Can you change my gauntlets for me?

pages.x: Can you change my gauntlets for me?
No thanks.

conversations.section: Dialogue / During the ornate bowl upgrade

pages.x: Tell me a...wait one moment.
What's the matter?
I feel that you possess great skill; great enough to gain the full power of the tears.
Use your great skill to make a more ornate bowl. The pattern will come to you as you work.
Bring the bowl to me, and you can use it to collect the tears to gain the full power they hold.
Now, tell me...a story...
Very well. Return soon...

conversations.section: City quest dialogue / Friend's son slowly dying / Task #1

pages.x: The teenage son of a good friend of mine is slowly dying. Now it is not the time to let the sands take him from us.
My appreciation. I shall write another stanza depicting your kind deed...

pages.i: Would you like to abandon this city quest?
Are you sure you wish to abandon this city quest?

pages.x: Maybe someone else will cast a rope into this gaping void...
Maybe someone else will cast a rope into this gaping void...
Maybe someone else will cast a rope into this gaping void...

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / A Tail of Two Cats

pages.x: *braaak*
Bob the Cat, stuck up a tree!
Kissing N-e-i-t-e!
Took Bob to Sphinx! Cleaned out Unferth!
Robert the Strong! Robert the Strong!
Spray cats with water! Stinking cats!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Desert Treasure

pages.x: *braaak*
Killed four beasties! Stole their diamonds!
Freed a dangerous prisoner!
All for a new spellbook!
Talking of Ancients...
...you're getting on a bit!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Diamond in the Rough

pages.x: *braaak*
Stole my diamond again!
Played around in Kalphite poo!
Saved the Prince! Saved the Prince!
Old Khoochak reckons...*braaak*
...that you shoulda drowned in quicksand!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Enakhra's Lament

pages.x: *braaak*
Build a statue, find a temple!
Two Mahjarrat in a stalemate!
You let 'em both free, stupid!
Enakhra! Akthanakos!
You've got a face like a camel!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Missing My Mummy

pages.x: *braaak*
Raided a pyramid!
But did good for a change!
Restored the tomb! Rebuilt the mummy!
Bet you still stole something, though!
Mummy too wrapped up in things to care.
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Our Man in the North

pages.x: *braaak*
Made noise in a library, you heathen! Stole a book!
Jabari unhappy! Jabari assassin!
Osman is Pharaoh! Osman is traitor!
Nothing bad to say about you for once.
Other than you stink.
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Smoking Kills

pages.x: *braaak*
Sumona's twisted. Save her sister!
But she just wants you dead!
Big smoking dungeon!
Banshee mistress! Banshee mistress!
Hope she gets you next time!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Spirits of the Elid

pages.x: *braaak*
Drought in Nardah! Wayward Nardah!
Restored shrine to Elidinis!
Genie in a bottle! Rubbed it right way!
Turned the water back on!
You're a sole-less golem killer!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Stolen Hearts

pages.x: *braaak*
Stumbled across kidnapping!
Broke into my palace!
Stole my lucky diamond!
Killed the Emir! Killed the Emir!
Naughty naughty naughty!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / The Golem

pages.x: *braaak*
Found a demon dimension!
Repaired a damaged golem!
Washed its brain! Washed its brain!
Bet you broke it in the first place!
Did you go back to steal the gems?
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: In Al Kharid Palace / Tourist Trap

pages.x: *braaak*
Crying lady at Shantay Pass!
Her daughter taken as slave!
Ana in a barrel! Ana in a barrel!
A mine full of tourist slaves.
But you only saved one, lazybones!
*raaawwwwk*

conversations.section: Talking to her to complete "Potion For a Lady"

pages.x: It's good to see you again, Player. Prifddinas is more beautiful than I ever imagined. What can I do for you?
Ah, I see you have a super melee potion there. Can I have it?

o: Give super melee potion to Lady Meilyr?

pages.x: There you go, but don't lose it. That's the only one! I'm happy to share Clan Meilyr's secrets with you, Player. However, I must ask for a fee.
Okay, but if you change your mind I'll give you something in exchange. I'm happy to share Clan Meilyr's secrets with you, Player. However, I must ask for a fee.

conversations.section: Talk-to / After The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Hello there.
Ha! Stupid human! You no get any golden apples! Even though me much like stone soup!
Can I please have some more golden wool?
Me will sell you some golden wool, but me not sell you any golden apples!
How much for the golden wool?
Me want 1000 coins! You pay or go!
You no pay, then you go! You no get any golden apples!

conversations.section: After Forgiveness of a Chaos Dwarf

pages.x: Are you interested in dwarven mining? If you're an experienced miner, you might appreciate a tour of the Lava Flow Mine.
I'd like the tour.
Alright. Are you ready now?
What's the Lava Flow Mine?
It's where the city gets most of its power. We've tapped into a magma vent, and we use its heat to power the steam machinery that runs the mine carts.
Goodbye.

conversations.section: Adventure begins / Talking to Sir Vant

pages.x: My word! You scared me there, friend. I have no idea where you came from, but you have fantastic timing. You see, I have come across a dragon.
A dragon?
Oh yes. It's not usually a problem. After all, I am a White Knight!
I just haven't really had time to prepare: food, runes, legions of other White Knights - those sorts of things.
You didn't prepare for facing a dragon?
It's not as if I woke up with a dragon-slaying urge! I was on my way through Lumbridge when it started attacking. It's a rather large, three-headed variant. Very rare.
So, what can I do?
You can keep back - it's returning!

conversations.section: Combat / Talking to Sir Vant

pages.x: I think we have found a job for you, whoever you are. Here, take this sword and shield.
I think the value of this property has slumped a little.
A little? It's got a huge dragon in it!
I'm sure the owners had no idea when they bought it. It would take an interesting individual to deliberately build a cellar in a dragon's den.
I believe this dragon has been asleep for a while - at least as long as it has taken Lumbridge, the town above us, to be established.
Something must have roused the dragon - a large noise, tail cramp, the smell of damsels.
Don't worry, the goblin is stunned, so it can't hurt you at the moment. You should know something about basic combat before tackling it.
Now, I have to keep watch for the dragon.

conversations.section: During The Fremennik Trials / Trying to enter the backstage without enchanted lyre

pages.x: Get lost, outerlander. Performers only past this point.
But I am a performer!
Oh, really? So where's your instrument?
Um... I'm an acapella bard?
Oh, really? You won't mind singing me a quick song then.
That was a pile of tosh. Get lost, outerlander. You're a bard like I'm a goblin. Do I look stupid to you?
Well, actually...
I said, get lost.

conversations.section: At the mountains east of Poison Waste, after The Path of Glouphrie

pages.x: So, I think I've found an entrance to Arposandra.
I found this hatch and I saw what looked like talking terrorbird guards in there, but they ran away and I can't open the door to get in.
Talking terrorbirds? There must be some strange magic being practised in there. Though, that doesn't really prove that it is Arposandra.
Well no, but who else, other than gnomes, would go to the effort of making terrorbirds talk?
I agree, but I think you'll need more than that to persuade any gnomes that we've found the legendary lost city of Arposandra.
So far, we've only found some rather dangerous sewers, some rather warped creatures and a
couple of talking terrorbirds. Everyone will think that we're insane.
I'm used to that, but we do need to find a way in.

conversations.section: Speaking to Luthas again

pages.x: Have you completed your task yet?

o: What did I have to do again?
No, the crate isn't full yet...
So where are these bananas going to be delivered to?
That customs officer is annoying isn't she?

pages.x: What did I have to do again?
There's a crate ready to be loaded onto the ship. If you could fill it up with bananas, I'll pay you 30 gold.
No, the crate isn't full yet...
Well come back when it is.

o: Player: So where are these bananas going to be delivered to?

pages.x: I sell them to Wydin who runs a grocery store in Port Sarim.

conversations.section: Talking to Maeve / After completing A Christmas Reunion / During a Christmas event / Without a marionette

pages.x: How does crafting marionettes work exactly?
It's a multi-step process. You'll need to start with taking some dry fir wood from the crate in the corner.
Step one is to carefully carve the wood over at the carving bench. Once you've crafted its head, torso, arms, legs, and a handle, it'll be ready for painting.
Step two is to paint the marionette over at the painting bench. Then lastly, step three is to assemble your marionette handle and body over at the finishing bench.
Once you're done, hand any marionettes you've made over to me.
That's quite an involved process.
We're experts at our craft here, Player! Only the best marionettes are allowed to leave this workshop!

Such beautiful sounds.
But then... but then....

conversations.section: Farmer's Market / After curing the rabbit

pages.x: Oh, and don't forget to give them a little food. It's the best thing for keeping your animals healthy and happy, which in turn makes them more likely to breed.
The health and happiness of an animal will also determine how much experience you get when you gather from them, so you want to keep them in tip top shape.
How do I feed animals?
You can interact with a trough to see what food sits in each category.
You can do that from outside of a pen, if you prefer, or you can climb over the stiles to get into each pen and do it that way.
You'll see that foods are grouped into categories, and each animal will only eat certain categories of food.
For instance, your rabbits will happily eat any fruit, vegetables or flowers.
Though, if a trough contains some fruit, shall we say, you can't also mix in food from a different category. You'd have to get rid of the fruit first.

No, never. I run a humane animal farm here. Treat 'em with love, find 'em good homes.

pages.x: Hi there. I was wondering if you could help me out.
Sorry. Can't hear you. My ears too cold and my feet hurt.
How does your feet hurting stop you from hearing?
Am glad I can't hear - you sound very annoying.
Right. So, say I were to bring you - oh, I don't know - a nice, warm hat to cover your ears. Then would you be able to hear me?
If it were nice, warm, furry kebbit hat made by Frawd the ogress. Those very good to look at AND very warm.
You're not very subtle, you know.
What? Sorry. Ears too cold to hear you and all.

conversations.section: Talk to / Normally

pages.x: Hi!
Hi. How can I help?

o: Do you see a lot of injured fighters?

pages.x: Can you heal me?
Of course!
Do you see a lot of injured fighters?
Do you come here often?

conversations.section: First time

pages.x: Excuse me?
What do you want? ...Oh, wait. I know! You're probably just like all the others, aren't you? After some fancy spell or potion from me, I bet!
What? No! At least, I don't think so. What sort of spells do you have?
Hah! I knew it! I expect you want my Aphro-Dizzy-Yak spell! Want someone to fall madly in love with you, eh?
That spell sounds very interesting, but I didn't mean to disturb you!
Well, I see that you do have some manners. I'm glad to see that you use them. Now, if it's all the same, I am very busy at the moment.
Unless you want something specific, please come back another time.
Yes, of course. Goodbye!

conversations.section: In eastern Keldagrim / Minitask dialogue

pages.x: My no good son must be down the pub again, drinking away all our money instead of getting one simple item from the market for me. Now, I have another errand.
Perhaps you will be more useful?

o: I don't work for rude people.

pages.x: What's it about?
I'm in need of some raw supplies. Get me [item] and be quick about it! I need them within the next [number] minutes!
Hmm, [item] in [number] minutes, that sounds about alright.
I don't work for rude people.
You're just as bad as my son, or worse!

conversations.section: In eastern Keldagrim / Minitask dialogue / Talking to Tati without the item

pages.x: Where're my [item]? My son could've gotten them faster!

o: I've had enough of this wild goose chase.
I'm still trying to collect them.

pages.x: I've had enough of this wild goose chase.
Why you useless little human! I should thrown you in the Kelda! With a lump of granite attached to your feet!
Ha, who are you calling little here?
Get out!
I'm still trying to collect them.
Try a little harder! I don't have all day you know!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: What do you want?
If you want friendly, go back to Waiko and talk to Sharkborne.
We ran his big mouth out of Whale's Maw for good reason, you know. Too damn cheerful.
I'm catching salmon with an invisible net! What's it look like I'm doing? I'm sitting here by the fire and trying to enjoy some peace and quiet.
Eh?
There's only one Ted Swarbrick on this island, and that's me. My family has been on Whale's Maw for generations, and don't you forget it!
Hmph.

conversations.section: At Waiko / With The Architect unlocked in player-owned port

pages.x: Hello, Lidylla!
Oh, you gave me a start! I had my nose in my work.
Hello, Portmaster. You are here visiting Waiko. Why are you here visiting Waiko? It's odd seeing you outside of your port.
How are the quakes here these days?
Still frequent and, despite my best efforts, still damaging.
Can I help at all?
Perhaps you could, just not yet. I'm working on a plan as we speak, but it's not quite ready yet.
Once it is, I think you would be a capable pair of hands to see it put into action!

conversations.section: Viewing memories / Cres

pages.x: How do you choose who to sacrifice? The caching of my knowledge is a task of great importance to the future survival of existence.
But the being I select to fulfill this task is doomed. I know they must sacrifice all to complete their work - their humanity, their will, their peace beyond death.
I know already when and how they will fall into oblivion...and yet there is no other way.
The forbidden secrets of this universe and beyond must be recorded while I still live, so that they can be metered out only when the time is right. The Great Revision.
The Broken Needle. The Shadow Breach. If that knowledge is lost, all things shall end. Not just life. Not just the universe. Everything.
Time and space, and life and death... I suppose death is the fairest way to choose.
I shall request Harold to deliver the next suitable candidate to me, instead of to the Underworld.
They will have no choice but to become one of my guardians, and to perform this task for me...for everyone.

conversations.section: Viewing memories / Seren

pages.x: I loved her, even though I knew it was a lie. Not real love. Not the love I felt for Fraji. But love all the same. Something. Is it wrong to have latched on to that?
To that strange power she possessed? Not to fight it, but to know it for what it is and accept it all the same? An illusion of connection.
A facsimile of my heart in exchange for all of hers? Because I know she loved me. Genuine, true, beautiful love.
The love that only the eternal can know, a love spanned the rise and fall of empires. A beautiful lie. But I liked the lie.
It was better than the loneliness of the truth and, really, could I ever find something better? So I lied to her. I kept lying to her.
For centuries I whispered sweet promises I never really meant and spoke of eternities together, even though I knew our time was finite.
Then the time came when I had to cast them all out and on the day I was grateful that it was a lie. I let me turn cold to her suffering, turn away from her misery.
I cast her out and thought that would be the end of it. She chose another option. A way to be with all the people she loved. Even me. It really was a beautiful lie.

conversations.section: After The Fremennik Trials

pages.x: Hello again, [Fremennik name]. I suppose you want a drink? Or are you going to try another scam with that terrible Askeladden again?
Scam? Oh... You mean his promise not to come in here anymore?
Yes. Yes I do. I should never have trusted him not to come in here, even with that written promise. Anyway, do you want a drink or not?

o: (After Hero's Welcome) Can I ask about V?

pages.x: He was a great hero to our people. Why couldn't they have gone for one of the bad gods, like Zamorak or Saradomin?
No thanks.
Okay then.

conversations.section: At Mudskipper Point / After Song from the Depths while having a coral crossbow in inventory

pages.x: You! May I take a look at that coral crossbow?
This is amazing engineering! Your crossbow could become extremely powerful if we added the right components onto it.
Unfortunately, judging by the materials, the flames you'll need to forge these components together will need to be extremely hot; far beyond anything any conventional forge could produce.
You'd probably need an ancient
dragon from the legends to produce a flame hot enough!
In the meantime, I can perform a basic assembly of these components if you'd like; it won't be usable as a weapon until you expose it to extreme heat, though.

conversations.section: At Mudskipper Point / While having Imcando hatchet pieces in inventory

pages.x: A tingling in my Imcando fingers! Is that...
Yes! You've found part of an ancient Imcando hatchet! May I take a look at it?
It won't be easy, though. As well as the pieces, I'll need a dragon hatchet, and one million coins to buy other materials.

o: I have those things with me now.

pages.x: Excellent! Let me get to work.
It's an ancient dwarven artefact, isn't that exciting enough?
An hatchet will be far better at cutting trees than a dragon hatchet, that's for sure.

conversations.section: In Tai Bwo Wannai / After Jungle Potion

pages.x: Trufitus sent me.
Trufitus Shakaya? What news does he send?
Trufitus has communed with the gods. Your village was never cursed and your people are free to return.
Bwana, do you speak the truth?
Yes, I helped Trufitus gather ingredients for a commune potion.
Then it must be true.
I cannot thank you enough for what you have done so far.

o: Your gratitude is all I deserve.
Well, some gold would be nice.

conversations.section: In Tai Bwo Wannai / Before Jungle Potion / Talking to him again

pages.x: You again! Only a fool would ignore my instructions.

o: Well there's a simple explanation for that...
Not so much ignore as disregard...

pages.x: Well there's a simple explanation for that...
I said: begone!
Not so much ignore as disregard...
I said: begone!
What instructions??
I said: begone!

conversations.section: Before Love Story / Before speaking to the other bank guard

pages.x: Hello?
Ssshhh! What do you want?
Well, it's not every day you see a man up a tree.
I'm trying to observe a suspect. Leave me alone!
What's this all about?
Haven't you heard? you'd better go and talk to the other guard, the one by the bank door. He'll tell you all about it.
Go on, ask him what's wrong with the bank wall. He loves when people ask him that.
Okay, if you say so.

conversations.section: First conversation

pages.x: Greetings, friend! The spirits have answered our prayers. You have come to help us, yes?

o: Yes, I have come to lend you my aid!

pages.x: Then the spirits still hear us! You are certainly a strange looking saviour, but we are grateful for your arrival.
Oh, so you have did not hear the call of the spirits? Still, it matters not. They work in mysterious ways.
Oh, sorry, I must have been mistaken. Please come back if you change your mind!
Here in Kanatah we're doing everything within our power to survive. The Airut attack the village almost daily, but we're gradually learning their patterns.
If you're willing to help us rebuild and fight back you would gain favour with the Elders. They would likely see fit to reward you!

conversations.section: Casting NPC Contact

pages.x: Hello?
'Ello, who's that?
I'm Player. I'm using magic to communicate with you.
Bizarre. Go on then, what do you want?
I need another assignment.
You're still hunting [assigned creature]; come back when you've finished your task.
Er... Nothing...

conversations.section: In his cell in the Black Knights' Base / Before claiming the dusty key

pages.x: Thank you for rescuing me! It isn't very comfy in this cell.

o: So...do you know anywhere good to explore?
Do I get a reward for freeing you?

pages.x: Well, this dungeon was quite good to explore...until I got captured, anyway. I was given a key to an inner part of this dungeon by a mysterious cloaked stranger!
It's rather tough for me to get that far into the dungeon however. I just keep getting captured!
Would you like to give it a go?

o: No, it's too dangerous for me too.

pages.x: I don't blame you!
Well, not really. The Black Knights took all of my stuff before throwing me in here to rot!

conversations.section: After the bonus experience trading period

pages.x: Hello there, are you interested in buying items with your credits?

o: I would like to trade in some bonus experience.
I would like to buy something.

pages.x: I am a trader of sorts. I can take your bonus experience and offer you compensation in the form of various rare objects.
Does it hurt?
Not at all! I get your bonus experience and you can get experience of your choice in return - or, if you prefer, you could have some rare items.
How does it work? What are you doing with the experience your take?
That's not for you to know. I'm not going to be around forever, so make good use of the offer while I'm in the area!
I am no longer trading, but you can still spend the credits you have earned.

conversations.section: Before Birthright of the Dwarves

pages.x: What do you want, human?
Ehm, anything on offer?
Can you wield a warhammer? If not, then go away.
Of course I can.
I can, but I won't.
Yeah, right.

conversations.section: I have more information about the Mahjarrat / Temple of Ikov / Aiding the Guardians

pages.x: I met a strange person called Lucien - I believe he was a Mahjarrat. He certainly looked similar to Jhallan.
He was trying to steal a powerful artefact called the 'Staff of Armadyl'.
He wasn't actually all that strong, I managed to just about defeat him in combat, but he escaped before I could finish him off.
Hmm, this is quite interesting. From what I've heard of Mahjarrat, I wouldn't have expected him to be such a weak foe.
I guess the fact it's not long until the Ritual means they are weakening a bit.
It doesn't seem to have stopped him getting up to some mischief, though.
The Staff of Armadyl, you say? I've heard of Armadyl; an obscure deity from around the Third Age.
Very interesting that a Mahjarrat would be after an artefact attributed to him. Sounds like it might be powerful.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Are they here? Are they there? Are they elsewhere?
Are what where?
This gate's sisters...
I didn't know gates had relations.
Oh yes. This one here: she is calm and boring. She stays here all the time.
She doesn't like to move, but her sisters are fidgety and refuse to stay in the same place for more than half an hour.
So, where are the, errr, fidgety sisters at the moment?
Oh well. I don't know what you humans call these places. Let me show you.

conversations.section: Historical dialogue / Normal dialogue before 17 February 2025

pages.x: Welcome back to my retreat, Project!

o: Can you tell me about yourself?
What do you want me to do?
Can you explain the rewards to me?
I would like to purchase some rewards.
Can you warn me when I'm trying to reattune a portal?
Can you decant some potions or jellyfish for me?
Can you sell me some Challenge Gems?

pages.x: Can you sell me some Challenge Gems?
Of course, Project! How many do you want?

pages.i: How many would you like to buy?

pages.x: None, I have changed my mind.
Never fear, you know where to find them now Project. Anything else?

conversations.section: In Keldagrim marketplace

pages.x: What can I interest you in? Need any pipes? I make very sturdy pipes.
No, not really... what kind of shop is this anyway?
Why, it's Wemund's Wrench Warehouse. Wemund, that's me. I don't really sell just wrenches, you know, I sell anything related to the maintenance of dwarven steam machines.
Sometimes I do repair work as well. Or I send my assistant.
Who's he then?
Oh, he's right over there... used to work in the mines to the south, poor lad. Made a bit of a mess of things I believe. So what'll it be then?
Got any ship engines to repair?
Thanks, but I don't think your services are required.

conversations.section: After Purple Cat (miniquest)

pages.x: Oh, hello.
Let's talk about purple cats.

o: Can you make my cat purple?
Can you remove the purple from a cat?

pages.x: Can you make my cat purple?
Can you remove the purple from a cat?
I'm afraid that once the spell is cast, it's cast for good. I haven't figured out how to undo the purple yet.
Ah, right. Hmm.

conversations.section: After Purple Cat (miniquest) / Using a regular cat on her

pages.x: Could you make this cat purple for me?
I can, but I should warn you: I can make cats purple, but I don't know how to change them back. It's a permanent change! Is that okay?

o: Yes, please make my cat permanently purple.
No, I think I'll hold off for the time being.

pages.x: Yes, please make my cat permanently purple.
There you go! Oh, such a beautiful colour.
Thank you.
No, I think I'll hold off for the time being.
Okay. If you change your mind, let me know.

conversations.section: At the entrance to the Werewolf Agility Course / Talking to him / With the werewolf outfit equipped

pages.x: What's beneath the trapdoor?
That's none of your business, human, and I'll never tell.
I'm not a human, I'm a werewolf.
You can tell by my...errr....stunningly fluffy tail.
You smell of human...and your tail is attached by a peg.
Erm...woof?
Har har har.
I guess I deserved that.

conversations.section: At the entrance to the Werewolf Agility Course / Talking to him / Without the ring of Charos equipped

pages.x: What's beneath the trapdoor?
That's none of your business, human, and I'll never tell.
Oh, come on - I'm only curious.
If it wasn't my duty to stand here and guard our agility course from the likes of you, I would be relieving you of your life right now.
So it's an agility course, then?
No ... yes ... oh blast - you didn't hear me say anything, right?
No problem. Can I come in?
No, human - it's werewolves only.

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here are your bars!

o: The Director replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Guthix be praised!
I am well pleased with your work, Player!
You are a true asset to the White Chisel!
You never fail to satisfy, Player!
I will get my secretary to send this to the trade floor at once!

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: Wonderful! I will personally oversee that it goes to the trade floor on time!
Well done, well done!
I knew you were the right human for the job!
Thanks, I will make sure the director hears of your expeditiousness!
You're always reliable, Player!

conversations.section: Low reputation / Handing in a task

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: How unusual for you, but it is appreciated nonetheless.
The White Chisel is pleased that the trust it put in you has not been put to shame after all.
That is quite a pleasant and unexpected surprise.
Perhaps I was wrong about you after all...
Thanks... I suppose.

pages.x: I've completed your task! Here is your ore!

o: The Secretary replies with one of the following at random:

pages.x: I have to admit, I was worried for a moment, but I'm glad to see you came through for us.
I am happy to see that the trust we put in you has not been in vain.
And not a minute too late as well. Well done.
The White Chisel recognizes your performance.
That's good to hear, thanks.

conversations.section: Talk to

pages.x: Hallo.
I'm Wilhelm, I've travelled from a far off land. It's a land known for its tulips and windmills. We also have a strange liking to the colour orange.
To celebrate these past 10 years of prosperity, I have brought with me a delicacy known as stroopwafels. I will stay around for a week handing out boxes of stroopwafels.
Oh they are so delicious, you just can't stop eating them. A stroopwafel is two thin waffles with a flavoured filling in the middle.
Ever since coming to these lands I've made some experiments on the fillings. You should give all types of flavours a taste.
Tot ziens.

conversations.section: After using the guidance 9 times

pages.x: I'm getting tired of guiding you to Rellekka, you know, Player. My boots are wearing out.

o: Oh, come on, just one more time?

pages.x: Oh, come on, just one more time?
Fine, I'll guide you there, Player. But this is the last time.
Fine! Don't bother.
Fine! I won't!
Fine!

I will get my secretary to send this to the trade floor at once!

I am happy to see that the trust we put in you has not been in vain.

The Yellow Fortune recognizes your performance.

conversations.section: Before the destruction of Duel Arena / Conversation 5

pages.x: Hi!
I could've 'ad 'im!
Er...
I was robbed!
Right.
It was rigged, I tell you!
Uh-huh.
Leave me alone.

conversations.section: After The Chosen Commander, before The Mighty Fall / At the Ranging Guild

pages.x: I'll show these stuck up archers, I'll show 'em all!

o: What are you doing in the Ranging Guild?
What do you think of the Ranging Guild?

pages.x: What are you doing in the Ranging Guild?
I am going to prove myself! I am going for the record! They made fun of me, they said crossbows weren't as good as "real" bows!
Well they won't be laughing when I hold the ranging competition record!
What do you think of the Ranging Guild?
Would you believe they wouldn't let me in at first? They said a goblin would never make a decent archer. Well I showed them... with seven bullseyes in a row!
A goblin with a crossbow is more fancy than their longbows and throwing axes any day!

conversations.section: Upon ringing the bell outside the Wizards' Guild / After completing The Hand in the Sand

pages.x: What are you doing... Oh, it's you... sorry... didn't realise... what can I do for you?

o: I'm here about the sicks... err Zogres
I have a rather sandy problem that I'd like to palm off on you.

pages.x: Don'y you worry about Sithik, he's not likely to be moving from his bed for a long time.
When he eventually does get better, he's going to be sent before a disciplinary tribunal, then we'll sort out what's what.
Thank you for your help with all of this.
Ooohh, no thanks required. It's I who should be thanking you my friend...
your investigative mind has shown how vigilant we really should be for this type of evil use of the magical arts.

o: What is there to do in the Wizards' Guild?
What are the requirements to get in the Wizards' Guild?
What do you do in the Guild?

conversations.section: On Braindeath Island / Trying to open the gate

pages.x: Arr! Tryin' ter get away eh? Well ye'll never sneak past me, I'm the best lookout this crew has ever seen!
Hey you! Look over there!
Who's that making faces behind you?
Oh my! Is that a genuine 3rd Age Diversion?
Is that your distraction?
Who is that behind you?

conversations.section: First conversation

pages.x: Good day human. I was told of your fortuitous arrival. Please, allow me to welcome you to the city of Otot!

o: Thank you, I'm Player, and you are?
City? It's a collection of about seven tents!

pages.x: I am the proud Acca of this marvellous city! Here, we rebuild our civilization! Here, we preserve our culture!
Sorry human, I'm a bit excitable about what we've preserved here. Now, is there any way I may be of service?
I know! It's wonderful, isn't it? I am the proud Acca of this marvellous city! Here, we rebuild our civilisation! Here, we preserve our culture!
Sorry human, I'm a bit excitable about what we've preserved here. Now, is there are way I may be of service?

conversations.section: In Keldagrim marketplace / Minitask dialogue

pages.x: I ehm… find myself in some slight trouble, human. I was wondering if you were busy?

o: What do you need help with?

pages.x: What do you need help with, exactly?
I need some clothing equipment for my sister. But hurry up! I will need [item] before [number] minutes are up.
Hmm, [item] in [number] minutes, that sounds about alright.
I’m incredibly busy, yes.
Pfft, I’m sure you are!

conversations.section: Historical dialogue prior to 13 July 2026 / If the player doesn't own a house yet

pages.x: Do you need Construction help?

o: Tell me how I can get my own house.

pages.x: See there were these wizards, right, and they needed more living space. So they figured out a way of making it so that stuff doesn't take up any room.
I don't really understand it myself, but now everyone can have their own two acres and it's all easily accessible right here.
Yeah, somewhere to hang your hat. Your roots. Your castle. A home of your own.
A fine magical house right here in Rimmington will set you back a mere 1,000 coins. You can always move the portal somewhere else later if you want.
(Note: Alfred says 'Taverley' instead of 'Rimmington' in his voiceover.)

conversations.section: Standard dialogue / Long-haired one

pages.x: Yeah?
Hello.
Whassup?
So...are you here to give crafting tips?
Dude, do I look like I wanna talk to you?
I suppose not.
Right on!

conversations.section: In the Miscellania and Etceteria dungeon

pages.x: Good day, [sir/madam].

o: What are you doing down here?

pages.x: What are you doing down here?
I'm waiting for my shift, of course. We can't dig all the time, you know.
I'm also researching the links between the Fremenniks and the Dwarves.
I've found that we have some mythology in common.
Good day.

conversations.section: When talked to

pages.x: Oh hello there! Exciting times are approaching... or possibly approached.
The museum has finally obtained the funding to start digging into the history of Gielinor. Quite literally.
Soon the guild will be opening at the Varrock Dig Site and the door to the past will be flung wide open!
You should give it a look yourself. An accomplished adventurer like you, why I bet you'll be a natural!
You'll need quite the skill to dig deep into the earth and uncover the ancient secrets.
And I bet there'll be plenty of strange and wonderful discoveries you could make to enhance your adventuring!
Give it a look, the Archaeology Guild will be coming to the Varrock Dig Site soon!

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: It's all very white round here, isn't it?
Well, it is the White Knights' Castle.
I think it would all look better in pink. At least then I wouldn't be squinting all the time.
Yes, but then they'd have to become the Pink Knights. I think they'd have problems recruiting then.
You're probably right. Maybe brown, then.
I think that may be worse...
Bah, humans have no sense of style...

conversations.section: In Burthorpe

pages.x: Hi there! Are you interested in helping with a new discovery?
What is it?
Since the beginning of the Sixth Age, a strange energy has been appearing throughout Gielinor.
My sister, Orla, has set up a camp beside the Lumbridge crater as a base for research! They're always looking for volunteers to help.
If you're interested, you should definitely pay her a visit.
Simple! Teleport to the Draynor Village lodestone, then run south and you should find the camp on your left.

conversations.section: Guild / Talking to Acting Guildmaster again

pages.x: Excellent! You can upgrade your soil box capacity as you advance through qualifications.
Now you have nearly everything you need to get out there and start excavating.
The final thing is to give you this journal.
All archaeologists should have a journal to make notes on their travels, but it also has some other handy features.
Checking in on your overall progress and getting you back to the guild quickly are just a couple of things it can do.
Feel free to stick it in your pocket whilst you're out and about, you never know when it might come in handy.
And without further ado, I'm pleased to welcome you as a new intern to the Archaeology Guild. Please accept this certificate of qualification.

conversations.section: Standard dialogue

pages.x: Good day traveller. You are far from home, what brings you here?
I am a wandering [hero/heroine], I come here in search of adventure.
Sounds ghastly, I just want to live in peace.
Unfortunately without people like me, peace doesn't last for long.
True, but then again most adventurers cause as much trouble as they put right.
You've got a point there... Hmm...
Well, good day traveller. And always do the right thing.

conversations.section: Confrontation / Talking to Sarah

pages.x: I'm glad you're here. Something weird is happening inside the church.
Like what?
I don't know. There was a sound, sort of like a thunderclap, and then the sky went all strange. It seems to be focused on the church.
Don't worry, I'll deal with it.

a much greater threat to the rest of Gielinor.

conversations.section: Having your story told back to you / Within The Light

pages.x: Well, Arianwyn called for your assistance once again. After a few tasks, he had a disguise and you both left to investigate.

You then went into the light itself.
After you worked out how to activate some switches there, a massive door opened in the room that led to a corridor, which had unfortunately caved-in.
There was a dead elf messenger there who must have perished in the rockslide. It was his report that revealed Prifddinas's fate to us all.
The city was reverted to crystal form...an entire city!
Need help with anything else?

conversations.section: Telling your story to Gwir / After Mourning's End Part II

pages.x: The Temple of Light was the next part of my quest. I investigated the area and found a crew close to the entrance.
I assume they perished at the hands of the shadows?
Indeed. To this day the mourners still have not found it. I tell them I'm still looking for the missing crew, but hopefully they will never find out the real situation.
Well, I don't think they will. I've got it documented already that you yourself restarted the temple's safeguards and defences to make it secure once more?
I'm happy to say you are correct; the temple's safeguards are intact. I can't see the mourners being a particular threat now, unless they find some other source of power.
Of course, and they won't even be trying to find another source until if and when they discover the temple and find themselves unable to penetrate its defences!
So the Temple of Light's defences are active - it is secure and the mourners are weakened without them even knowing it. What happened next?

Elves sing to their crystals and they form into the desired shape.

Either talk to an elf or find some other way to sing to the crystal. If this came from Oaknock, he must have found a way...
Thanks, I'll have a look round Oaknock's old workshop. I can have a chat with Brimstail while I'm at it! Thanks!

Wow - that does sound interesting.

Why not to prison?

Over the years, I've had to sell off my land to keep myself afloat, not that the buyers used it mind.

First, we'll need to buy back the deeds to one of these old animal pens.
Plus we'll need a couple of baby rabbits to kickstart our new venture - one boy, one girl.
Those beans we got should be just enough. Here, let's take a look at the farmers' market...
